Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
The units of the Delhi Police, including the Crime Branch, Special Cell and the police of 15 districts participated in the operation, which lasted until 6 pm on Thursday, he said.
As per the police chief ‘s directions, all deputy commissioners of police (DCPs) and Station House Officers were directed to take action under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS), and Excise and Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (Copta) acts. Each police station was given a target of issuing 200 challans, said an officer.
The officers were asked to take maximum preventive action under Section 107/150 and 107/151 of CrPC, along with action under 65 DP Act.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In the previous ‘Operation Kawach’ held on November 14, the police conducted raids at 907 places and arrested 700 people across 15 districts. The police teams had identified 64 hotspots where narcotics were being sold in Delhi and seized around 870 gm of heroin, 244.8 kg of ganja, 16.1 gm of cocaine, and 434 grams of MDMA. They arrested 14 people under the Arms Act and recovered six country-made pistols, nine live cartridges, eight knives, and 15 stolen motorcycles.
The police had also detained and arrested the associates of multiple gangs, including those led by Lawrence Bishnoi, Neeraj Bawana, Kaushal Chaudhary, Tillu Tajpuriya, Kala Jatheri, Manjeet Mahal and Kapil Sangwan.

headline: AAP MLA Amanatullah Khan questioned by Delhi Police after court grants interim protection from arrest
description: As the Delhi Police questioned Amanatullah Khan, his supporters gathered at the Jamia Nagar Police Station.
content:
The Delhi Police Thursday questioned Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)’s Okhla MLA Amanatullah Khan for over two-and-a-half hours in a case where he allegedly obstructed the police from arresting a proclaimed offender.
Khan appeared at the Jamia Nagar Police Station with his lawyers after a Delhi court granted him interim protection from arrest in a case. The court directed the police to record his questioning on a CCTV camera.
The court also questioned the Delhi Police on why they had gone to arrest Shavez Khan, the alleged proclaimed offender, when he was on anticipatory bail. Additionally, the court asked the police about the lack of video evidence of the MLA’s intervention and the alleged subsequent assault of the police officers.
Police sources said they are trying to verify whether Shavez received anticipatory bail. On the court’s observation that the police could have used their phones to record the incident, a source said, “Officers were overwhelmed by 20-25 people attacking them. It was the last thing on their mind to pull out their phones and begin recording… nearby CCTV cameras were not working at that time.”
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
Khan was expected to arrive at the Jamia Nagar Police Station at 5 pm amid the heavy presence of the Rapid Action Force (RAF) and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF). As news spread of Khan’s arrival to the station, the traffic began coagulating as cars, bikes, e-rickshaws, and auto-rickshaws slowed down, hoping to catch a glimpse.
Khan’s supporters, too, were present at the scene, however, with strict instructions to not shout slogans and to not “become emotional”, according to a member of Khan’s team. As Khan arrived to much clamour and noise, a member of his team, Mohammad Sajid said, “Let’s see what the police ask him… He hasn’t done anything wrong.”
“Amanatullah came to rescue the man because he was being harassed by the police… Only two men in plain clothes were there who were questioning him… Shavez was out on bail…the MLA only went to help him out because he heard one of his people was being targeted by the police,” Sajid added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Before he went in, he told us it won’t take more than 15 minutes… Lagta hai chunaav jeetne ka SHO sahab unko tahey dil se mubarakbaad de rahein hain (looks like the SHO wants to congratulate him for his electoral victory),” said Mohammad Iqbal.

headline: Centre deploys Pralhad Joshi, Mann his minister Khuddian for talks with farmers in Chandigarh today
description: Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has assigned Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khuddian, Chief Secretary KAP Sinha, Special Chief Secretary Anurag Verma and DGP Gaurav Yadav to attend the meeting scheduled at 5pm.
content:
A 28-member delegation of farmers, including Jagjit Singh Dallewal and Sarwan Singh Pandher, will attend a meeting to be held on February 14 (Friday) with the Centre to resolve their issues, including legal guarantee for MSP.
The central team will be led by Union Minister of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution Pralhad Joshi. He will be accompanied by Devesh Chaturvedi, Secretary Agriculture, Farmers Welfare, Government of India as per an invite received by Punjab government from the Centre.
Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Chouhan, whose son is getting married Friday, will not be participating in the meeting.
Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann has assigned Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khuddian, Chief Secretary KAP Sinha, Special Chief Secretary Anurag Verma and DGP Gaurav Yadav to attend the meeting scheduled at 5pm at Mahatma Gandhi State Institute of Public Administration Punjab (MGSIPA), Sector-26, Chandigarh.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
The invite came hours after state Finance Minister Harpal Cheema said that the state government had not revived any invitation for the meeting. “The Punjab government has not got any information about the meeting so far. We do not know what they want to do on whether they want to include us in the talks or not. We will wait. If we are invited, then the Chief Minister will take part in the talks,” Cheema had said while talking to media after Cabinet meeting.
The meeting comes after four rounds of dialogue between the Centre and the agitating farmers that were held in February last year. CM Mann had then attended the meetings on February 8, 12, 15 and 18 last year, but talks had remained inconclusive. At that time, the central panel comprised three union ministers — Arjun Munda, Piyush Goyal and Nityanand Rai. The farmers had rejected the Centre’s proposal of buying pulses, maize and cotton crops at MSP by the government agencies for five years.
Dallewal, the Samyukta Kisan Morcha (non-political) convenor whose indefinite fast entered 80th Thursday — also the day the stir at the Shambhu and Khanauri borders completed a year — said he will attend the meeting.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Earlier, Pandher, convenor of Kisan Mazdoor Morcha, addressed a ‘mahapanchayat’ at the Shambhu border. He said said the government of India should bring a concrete solution to the farmers’ issues.
“Holding an agitation is not our wish. We will fight till a legal guarantee to MSP is given,” he said, asking the Punjab government to convene a session of the Vidhan Sabha to reject the draft of the National Policy Framework on Agricultural Marketing.
Farmer leaders at the mahapanchayat said they will observe the first death anniversary of farmer Shubhkaran Singh on February 21 at Balloh village in Bathinda. Shubhkaran had died during a clash at Khanauri border when protesters tried to march towards Delhi on February 21 last year.
A joint statement issued by the SKM (non-political) and KMM said a 28-member delegation of both the forums will participate in the meeting with the Centre. Prominent farmer leaders, who will be part of the delegation, are Abhimanyu Kohar, Kaka Singh Kotra, Sukhjit Singh, P R Pandian, Arun Sinha, Lakhwinder Singh, Jaswinder Longowal, M S Rai, Nand Kumar, Balwant Singh Behramke and Inderjit Singh Kotbudha.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On January 18, a delegation of senior officials from the Union Agriculture Ministry, led by joint secretary Priya Ranjan, invited the representatives of the two forums for a meeting to discuss their demands on February 14 in Chandigarh. In the letter, it was stated that a meeting with the ministers of the government of India and the Punjab government regarding the demands of the farmers’ unions had been convened.
Meanwhile, one more farmer died at Khanauri border, taking the toll in one year to 43, said Pandher. “This is the cost of protest, which we have paid in one year,” he said, reiterating that a group of farmers would resume its foot march to Delhi from the Shambhu border on February 25 if the Centre does not find a “suitable solution” regarding their demands in the meeting.

headline: Shinde to set up own coordination centre to monitor projects; CM Devendra Fadnavis has his war room
description: Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar also runs a project monitoring unit to track projects that fall under his guardian ministership and falling within departments handled by him and his party leaders.
content:
In a move that may see infratructure projects reporting to multiple authorities, at least three bodies headed by top three Mahayuti leaders — the chief minister and two deputy chief ministers — will monitor the development of various projects across the state.
Even as Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis already runs a war room from Mantralaya that monitors all the ongoing infrastructure projects across departments, Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde is in the proces of setting up a coordination centre to monitor the implementation of ongoing infrastructure, housing and planning projects.
Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar also runs a project monitoring unit to track projects that fall under his guardian ministership and falling within departments handled by him and his party leaders.
“This is not a war room, but a coordination centre. It aims at providing necessary administrative support to the ongoing projects with the deputy CM’s (Shinde) office. This will not interfere with the existing war room work,” said an official related to the developments.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
After Delhi election, lesson for all parties: Listen to the ground
Shinde holds Urban Development and Housing portfolios and both these departments have undertaken a number of big infrastructure projects, such as redevelopment, Metro, projects undertaken by municipal corporations, etc. The planned centre will coordinate  between departments, monitoring progress reports and resolving administrative problems to speed up projects.
The Chief Minister’s war room at Mantralaya monitors all the ongoing infrastructure projects across departments as well as implementation of big industrial projects. War room meetings are held to monitor progress of projects and speed up their implementation.
Fadnavis has also decided to monitor the implementation of socially important schemes from the war room, such as Jalyukta Shivar 3.0, while Shinde’s coordination centre is an addition to the already existing monitoring platforms.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
For few weeks now, Shinde has been keeping distance from government meetings. While he did not attend a war room meeting two weeks ago, on Tuesday, he did not attend the review meetings of several metropolitan region development authorities chaired by Fadnavis. These authorities fall under Shinde’s Urban Development Department.

headline: Torres case: Ukrainian national says no role in case, career will be spoiled if kept in jail
description: The Torres brand, run by Platinum Hern Pvt Ltd, allegedly offered high-returns investment opportunities to investors and later duped them.
content:
Ukrainian national and actor Areman Garuh Ataian arrested in Torres Ponzi scheme case on Thursday approached the sessions court seeking bail claiming that he had no role in the case and his “whole career will be spoiled” if kept in jail.
Ataian, 48, was arrested by the  Economic Offences Wing (EOW) of Mumbai Police on January 29 for his alleged involvement in helping other Ukrainian masterminds in the Torres ponzi case.
The Torres brand, run by Platinum Hern Pvt Ltd, allegedly offered high-returns investment opportunities to investors and later duped them.
Ataian, the sixth person to be arrested in the case, was sent to judicial custody  by a magistrate court on February 3 and was lodged at Arthur Road Jail.
As per police, Ataian’s name had cropped up in the case during interrogation of Tausif Reyaz alias John Carter, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of Platinum Hern.
The EOW had claimed that Ataian has been living in the city for last 10 years without any valid documents and was responsible for helping Ukrainian national accused in the case to settle down in the city and providing them logistical support.
Ataian, who has also worked in some Hindi movies, claimed in his plea that his “whole career will be spoiled” if kept in jail,
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The plea stated  he was falsely implicated in the case and that his name was not mentioned in the FIR.
Some Ukrainian nationals had approached him regarding setting up a jewellery store in Mumbai, and he arranged a meeting between them and Tausif Riyaz, the plea said.
It added that Ataian was neither an employee of Platinum Hern or Torres, nor its director or promoter and was not related to activities of the firm.
The plea further said that Ataian had cooperated with the investigating agency and will continue to do so  and as per remand report, he had no role in the alleged scam, therefore “no purpose will be served by putting him behind the bars.”
The court will hear the plea in due course.

headline: ED arrests 2 in Fairplay illegal broadcasting of IPL matches
description: The arrested accused Chirag Shah and Chintan Shah, as claimed by ED, have played key role in the alleged crime and were closely linked to the main accused of the case, agency sources said.
content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) arrested two more people on Wednesday in connection with the alleged money laundering linked to Fairplay, an online platform allegedly involved in the illegal broadcasting of IPL matches and various betting activities.
The arrested accused Chirag Shah and Chintan Shah, as claimed by ED, have played key role in the alleged crime and were closely linked to the main accused of the case, agency sources said.
Both were remanded to ED’s custody for two days by a special PMLA court on Thursday.
In 2023, the Nodal Cyber Police in Maharashtra had filed an FIR against Fairplay Sport LLC and others on the complaint of Viacom18 Media Pvt Limited under relevant sections of the Indian Penal Code, the Information Technology Act and the Copyright Act for causing loss of revenue of more than Rs 100 crore.
Suspecting money laundering, the ED initiated a money laundering investigation by filing a separate enforcement case.
During the investigation, the agency said it found that Krish Laxmichand Shah, the “key person” behind Fairplay, has registered various companies such as M/s Play Ventures N V and M/s Dutch Antilles Management N V at Curacao, M/s Fair Play Sport LLC, M/s Fairplay Management DMCC at Dubai and M/s Play Ventures Holding Limited at Malta for Fairplay’s operations.
While Fairplay is being operated from Dubai, ED last year searched the premises of individuals who provided technical and financial management support services to the platform.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
ED probe earlier revealed that the purchase of high-value immovable or movable assets in India by the persons involved, amounting to more than Rs 100 crore.
Earlier, the ED had carried out search operations on four occasions and seized or frozen movable assets to the tune of over Rs 200 crore.

headline: Punjab buckles under farmers’ pressure, defers stamp duty on land transfers among blood relatives
description: The stamp duty on the transfer of land among blood relatives was eliminated in 2014 by the SAD-BJP government in Punjab.
content:
Buckling under pressure from farmer organisations, the Punjab government has deferred a plan to impose stamp duty on property transfers to next of kin, choosing not to discuss it in the cabinet meeting on Thursday.
“A direction to defer the agenda was given to the Department of Revenue and Rehabilitation by Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Wednesday evening. The department was asked to put it on hold,” said a source.
On Wednesday, Balbir Singh Rajewal of the Samyukta Kisan Morcha warned that farmer organisations would oppose the stamp duty “tooth and nail”.
The government did not want to give farmers any reason to protest against it, the source added.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
I want to enjoy remaining years of my cricket career like a child: MS Dhoni
What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
As Rekha Gupta is appointed Delhi CM, the 4 big challenges she will face
The cash-strapped government had decided to impose a 2.5 per cent stamp duty on the transfer of property among blood relatives. As per the proposal, direct transfers from parents to children (sons and daughters) and grandparents to grandchildren would require a stamp duty of 1 per cent, while all other transfers, including those between brothers, sisters and spouses, would incur a stamp duty of 2.5 per cent.
Official sources had said the stamp duty would have generated a few crores of rupees in revenue for the government. “The transfer of property among blood relations has many takers as it does not have any duty. We observed that parents transferred property to their children’s names, and the same property was transferred back. This transfer was shown as a sale deed to mortgage it in a bank for a loan. At least 25 per cent of sale deeds were found to be among blood relatives. The revenue staff was busy dealing with these transfers. With the government now levying stamp duty, only serious transfers will be made,” a government official had said.
It remains to be seen whether the government will take up the agenda in the next cabinet meeting or if it has been postponed indefinitely.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
It was in 2014 that the stamp duty on the transfer of land among blood relatives was eliminated, by the SAD-BJP government. According to a government notification dated May 7, 2014, no stamp duty was chargeable on instruments pertaining to the transfer of immovable property by an owner during their lifetime to any of their blood relations (i.e., children, grandchildren, brothers and sisters). Transfers between spouses were also exempt.

headline: Padma Shri-winning Karnataka folk singer Sukri Bommagowda passes away
description: After she lost her husband to alcoholism when she was 16, Sukri Bommagowda also took up social activism.
content:
Renowned folk singer and Padma Shri awardee Sukri Bommagowda, fondly known as Sukrajji, passed away Thursday morning at her home in the Badageri village of Karnataka’s Uttara Kannada district.
She had been receiving treatment at a Manipal Hospital for the past few days.
A revered figure in the Halakki community, Sukrajji was often called a “walking encyclopaedia” for her efforts in preserving its rich folk traditions. She had memorised nearly 5,000 folk songs and played a vital role in various social movements. In the 1980s, Akashvani recorded hundreds of folk songs sung by her, ensuring her legacy would endure for future generations.
One of her most impactful contributions was her fight against alcohol addiction in Ankola and nearby areas in the Uttara Kannada district. Through folk songs and speeches, she spread awareness about the harmful effects of alcohol on individuals and families.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
I want to enjoy remaining years of my cricket career like a child: MS Dhoni
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Her activism was deeply personal — she lost her husband Bommagowda to alcohol addiction at 16. She witnessed the devastating impact of alcoholism firsthand, which fuelled her commitment to social causes.
Her contributions earned national recognition when she was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2017. She was also honoured with the Nadoja Award and the Rajyotsava Award by the Karnataka government.
Sukrajji believed in a simple, nature-friendly life, a message she shared with the hundreds of schoolchildren who visited her home in the Badageri village of Ankola taluk during educational tours.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On February 6, despite her illness, Sukrajji sang a song for health officials who had come to conduct a routine body checkup.

headline: Politicians across party lines, netizens hail PM Modi for wearing Himachal’s Kulluvi cap during his France visit
description: Kulluvi cap was also part of the Indian contingent’s attire during the inaugural ceremony of the ongoing 9th Asian Winter Games 2025 in Harbin, China.
content:
Leaders from both the ruling Congress and the Opposition BJP have praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for wearing a Himachali cap, better known as the Kulluvi cap, during his recent meeting with French President Emmanuel Macron.
Netizens on social media also lauded the prime minister’s gesture, using hashtags such as #HimachaliCap, #ProudMoment, and #ModiFrance.
Vikramaditya Singh, Congress leader and Himachal PWD & Urban Development Minister, shared a picture of PM Modi wearing the Himachali cap with Macron on his Facebook account. He wrote, “Our political and ideological differences exist and will continue in the future, but when the Prime Minister wears a Himachali cap during his international visit, we feel proud as Himachalis.”
Vikramaditya Singh, son of six-time chief minister Virbhadra Singh and current Himachal Congress chief Pratibha Singh, further said, “We hope that the central government will assist the state government in light of the massive financial losses suffered due to the disasters of previous years.”
BJP Dharamsala MLA Sudhir Sharma also shared pictures of PM Modi wearing the Kulluvi cap during his visit to France. Sharma wrote, “Himachal’s identity during the PM’s France visit: PM Modi was seen wearing a Himachali cap during his France visit, showcasing a glimpse of Indian culture and tradition. This is not only a proud moment for Himachalis but also a reflection of India’s rich heritage.”
Netizen Naveen Sharma wrote on social media, “It is not the first time when PM Narendra Modi was seen wearing the pride and identity of Himachal: a Kulluvi cap.”
Himachali Kulluvi caps were also part of the official attire of the Indian contingent participating in the ongoing 9th Asian Winter Games 2025 in Harbin, China. Indian athletes, coaches, and administrative officials took part in the march past wearing Kulluvi caps during the inauguration ceremony on February 7.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A round cap with a flat top, the Kulluvi cap has a band of colourful embroidery with intricate patterns on its front. The cap’s back, which covers the head, is mostly made of local woollen yarn, though sometimes it is crafted from cotton or other lightweight materials.
The Himachali cap has historical ties to Kinnaur and spread to other parts of Himachal Pradesh through the princely states of Bushahr and Kullu. The weaving style and materials used for these caps vary from region to region.

headline: How a concert and a meditation session saved Osho disciples on Feb 13
description: The commune, visited twice by David Headley, may have been the original target.
content:
“A bunch of people swear that they owe their lives to my performance. When that bomb exploded at 7.15 pm on the 13th Feb 2010, I was just about to go on stage, while they were sitting in the audience, a comfortable half-kilometre from where they might well otherwise have been,” says Chinmaya Dunster (74) a renowned sarod player.
Born in the United Kingdom, Dunster became an Osho disciple in 1982 and moved to India in 1989. In 1990, the man who had been inspired to learn the sarod after attending an Amjad Ali Khan concert in Delhi, founded a band with Prem Joshua at Pune’s Osho International Meditation Resort. An active environmentalist who performed concerts to foster awareness for saving ecosystems, Dunster was doing exactly that at the Osho centre on February 13, 2010 when the German Bakery blast happened.
The event was a benefit concert he had arranged to raise funds for solar lighting in the Himalayan village of Jhuni. “The band was ready to go on stage when suddenly we heard from afar an ominously deep and rumbling boom. Probably another gas cylinder exploding somewhere… we re-assured each other. But just as we were about to play the hostess frantically signally to me. When I went to her she whispered in my ear that there has been a bomb at the German Bakery and that’s all we knew,” recollects Dunster in a blog he wrote in 2017 on the night that changed everything.
As he realised that no one else seemed to have heard about the blast he decided to go ahead with the concert. ‘”The Show Must Go On’ reverberated in my head and without further hesitation I got back on stage, picked up my sarod and gave the cue for the opening number,” he says.
Dunster admits though that he doesn’t remember much of what he played that night. But the memory of the police sirens and the ensuing chaos, once the one-hour performance ended and people got to know what had happened, has remained entrenched in his mind.
Speaking to The Indian Express from UK Dunster, who decided to drive off early in the morning to join his partner Naveena and new-born daughter Koyal in Goa says, “The extraordinary sight at 4 am when I drove off Koregaon Park is indelible in my memory. The roads were absolutely deserted. No human being was there in any direction. It was grey and smoggy. I felt like I was the last person on the planet. It was like trying to escape a destroyed city.
Another thing really remarkable to remember was the sense of doom that maybe this is the beginning of something far worse.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Over the next few weeks though Dunster received many calls and mails, – ‘You saved my life, man! I had been planning to go to the bakery as usual, but went to your gig instead…..’ they all said.
The gratitude was understandable. The blast happened at 7.15 pm. Every day the Osho centre’s gates would close at 6.40 pm for the evening meditation. Many who did not want to join the meditation would typically slip off to catch some coffee and conversation at the Bakery just down the road that was very popular with Osho disciples. That day a lot of that crowd decided to stay back for the concert. “The number of casualties ended up containing just three Osho sannyasin names,” says Dunster.
“Yes the timing of the blast saved many Osho followers,” agrees Ma Sadhana, spokesperson of the Osho centre. “It happened when we also had our white robe evening meditation and a lot of people hence were inside the meditation resort and not at the bakery,” she adds.
While between the concert and evening meditation many sanyasin lives may have been saved, the blast did forever alter the way the Osho commune functioned. And it was not just because of its proximity to the site. Soon after the blast it emerged that David Headley, a Lashkar-e-Toiba operative and an accused in 26/ 11 had planned the German Bakery bombing. Headley had twice visited the Osho commune in 2008-2009.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“The Osho commune could have even been the original target, given that Headley had come here twice and surveyed the place. But because we have CCTVs and our own security making it difficult to bring in bags unchecked, the target must have shifted to another place with international tourists,” says Sadhana.
Security was immediately enhanced at the commune and the height of the bamboo walls raised considerably. A permanent police post just outside the lane, barricades on the road and a scanner at the gate were other preventive measures that have now become the norm at the centre – a marked departure from its earlier relatively easier access.
Or as Dusnter says,” The outside world had invaded our little haven and would not be going away…”

headline: Invest Karnataka 25: First phase of Tumakuru’s Industrial Smart City to be completed by 2026-end: Minister Piyush Goyal
description: PM Modi laid the foundation stone of South India’s first industrial corridor project at Tumakuru, spread over 8500 acres under the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC).
content:
At Invest Karnataka 25, the three-day Global Investor Meet (GIM), Union Commerce and Industries Minister Piyush Goyal on Wednesday announced that the first phase of Tumakuru’s Industrial Smart City project is set to be completed by the end of next year.
The smart city, covering a sprawling 8,000 acres, has already begun operations under the innovative ‘Play and Plug’ model – an industrial infrastructure concept designed to provide ready-to-use facilities, reducing setup time and costs.
“In the past year, the government has allocated Rs 11 lakh crore for infrastructure development. The first phase, spanning 1,736 acres, is expected to be completed by the end of 2026,” the minister said.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone of South India’s first industrial corridor project at Tumakuru, spread over 8500 acres under the Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC), in February 2023.
The Central Government, through the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT), and the state government, through the Karnataka Industrial Area Development Board (KIADB), have jointly taken up the development of the industrial township at Vasanthanarasapura, spread across 8,500 acres in three phases in Tumakuru district through the project’s Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV).
The CBIC project includes the development of industrial townships at three nodes: Krishnapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), Tumakuru (Karnataka), and Ponneri (Tamil Nadu). The Tumakuru node has been prioritised for development, with an area of 1736.20 acres identified as the priority development area.
The first phase of the project is expected to generate employment opportunities for approximately 88,000 people and attract investment of around Rs. 7,000 crore over five to six years, triggering growth and prosperity in the region.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The project will be a mixed-use development comprising land uses like industrial, institutional, residential, commercial, green spaces, etc. making it a completely self-sustainable and resilient smart industrial city. This project is aimed at facilitating investments, fostering innovation, enhancing skill development, and building the finest manufacturing ecosystem. Target sectors are food products, textile and apparel, electronics, auto and auto components, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, engineering, general manufacturing etc.
Goyal also said on Wednesday that with the continued cooperation between the Central and State governments, India would become a $30 trillion economy by 2047. He emphasised that the Central Government would fully support Karnataka in realising its economic potential.
‘Invest Karnataka’ awards presented to 15 firms
During the GIM Invest Karnataka 25, Goyal presented the ‘Invest Karnataka’ awards to 15 businesses that have made significant contributions to the state’s economic and industrial growth. Additionally, he unveiled the ‘Karnataka Success Stories’ compilation, which highlights the state’s industrial achievements.
Minister Goyal highlighted India’s growing reputation as a hub for investment, emphasising the country’s strengths, including its democracy, demand, population, digitalisation, and diversity. He mentioned that India would soon see the development of 75 new airports, flight connectivity to 120 cities under UDAN-2, 114 waterways, doubling the existing number of ports, and 50 new tourist destinations. The initiatives will also benefit Karnataka, he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“India’s export trade has reached $800 billion, with Karnataka playing a pivotal role in this achievement. The Central Government has earmarked Rs 20,000 crore for innovation, Rs 74,000 crore for the semiconductor mission, and Rs 2 lakh crore for industry incentives under the PLI scheme,” he said.
Piyush stated that Karnataka would lead the way in deep-tech, fintech, and future industries in the coming years.
The Global Investors Meet will conclude on Thursday.

headline: AAP MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh says it’s time to replace Bhagwant Mann as Punjab CM: ‘Must set our house in order’
description: The reason behind AAP’s Delhi debacle is the bad governance in Punjab, AAP MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh said.
content:
Punjab MLA Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, the Aam Adami Party’s (AAP’s) poster boy during its 2022 election campaign in the state, said on Thursday that he believed it was time to replace Bhagwant Mann as the chief minister, adding that he had conveyed his reasons to the party.
Singh’s statement comes in the backdrop of AAP’s dismal show in the Delhi Assembly elections and a subsequent meeting between national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and the party’s Punjab leadership in the national capital.
“I did not go to the party MLAs’ meeting in Delhi. That meeting was not held to raise any demands…it was more like a one-way communication from the higher-ups. I marked my attendance over the phone and conveyed my concerns,” Singh said. Kejriwal told the AAP leaders in Punjab at the meeting that winning the 2027 elections in the state was of utmost importance.
“I have been demanding to change the Punjab CM. I have given the reasons to party. We want to call a meeting of party MLAs so that they can elect a new leader. We are MLAs, and it is our right to elect the leader of the House,” Singh said.
“In my view, the reason behind the Delhi debacle is the bad governance in Punjab. One more reason is the Congress in Punjab is taking it for granted that they will form the next government in the state. Even the BJP has been gaining confidence that it will be able to win Punjab in 2027. So we must set our house in order. I can only tell you this. I have given the rest of the feedback to the party,” Singh said.
Also Read | Opposition finds fresh ammo in Kejriwal-Punjab MLAs’ meet: ‘split, mid-term poll imminent’
A 1998-batch IPS officer who was once the inspector-general of Punjab Police, Singh, the Amritsar North MLA, was among the high-profile AAP faces before its victory in the 2022 Assembly elections.
Dissatisfied with the then Captain Amarinder Singh-led Congress government’s stand in court over the 2015 sacrilege cases, Singh had opted for premature retirement from service soon after the Punjab and Haryana High Court on April 9, 2021 quashed the probe report filed by the Special Investigation Team he had led into the Kotkapura firing case. His resignation sparked events that led to the ouster of Captain Amarinder Singh as the chief minister a few months later. Later, Singh joined AAP, and Arvind Kejriwal pushed his image to promise justice in the sacrilege cases.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
After AAP’s defeat in Delhi, Singh posted on Facebook, “It is time for introspection. I was deeply saddened by AAP’s defeat in Delhi, especially the personal defeat of senior leaders, which is extremely painful. Particularly when Congress leaders are rubbing salt into the wounds. This is a clear reflection of poor governance in Punjab.”
Also Read | Kejriwal puts chatter to rest: Mann to remain Punjab CM
“In cases like sacrilege and the Kotkapura-Behbal Kalan firing, the government system deliberately protected the guilty, even after the main culprit confessed his crime at Sri Akal Takht Sahib—an outcome of my investigation that proved true,” he wrote.
“There is apathy and insensitivity in government institutions towards public work, along with open corruption and exploitation of the public in districts and municipal offices,” he said, alleging that gangsters have been joining AAP and mocking honest police officers.
“These are just some examples of poor governance in Punjab that I have already highlighted, especially during my meeting with Madam Sunita Kejriwal in August. Due to my domestic circumstances—especially the sudden and untimely death of my wife—I have not been very active in politics. Yet, seeing all of this is painful. Although time has passed, introspection must be done soon. I am fully committed to strengthening the party and upholding the principles of Swaraj,” he added.

headline: Tughlakabad Fort protected area’s physical demarcation to be completed in 3 weeks, HC told
description: The court has been hearing a bunch of petitions, one dating as far back as to 2001, over the issue of removal of encroachments in Tughlakabad Fort.
content:
After years of stalemate, Kalkaji sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) informed the Delhi High Court on Wednesday that in consultation with the Archeological Survey of India (ASI), physical demarcation of the Tughlakabad Fort protected area shall be completed within three weeks.
This, after the ASI, through its counsel, informed HC that the physical demarcation is yet to be carried out.
A division bench of Chief Justice D K Upadhyaya and Justice Tushar Rao Gedela had on Tuesday pulled up the authorities for the delay in completing the physical demarcation despite the court’s repeated orders to remove encroachments from the protected area.
The court has been hearing a bunch of petitions, one dating as far back as to 2001, over the issue of removal of encroachments in Tughlakabad Fort.
Last December, the HC had recorded in its order, “…it is apparent that for one reason or the other, the physical demarcation has not been conducted so far, for past several years, which we consider to be necessary to address the issue of rampant encroachment in the area.”
It had asked the SDM as well as the additional director general of ASI to join the proceedings on the next date of hearing “to assist this court for resolution” of the issue.
Kalkaji SDM Anuj Bharti, appearing before the court on Wednesday, said that he was posted at his current jurisdiction only last November and was thereafter engaged in duties related to the Delhi polls.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Bharti assured the court that its order directing for a physical demarcation of the area will be completed. “It won’t take much time now, we can get it done in a week… Maps have already been prepared by tehsildar… coordinates are available.”
The bench recorded Bharti’s statement, noting that “in consultation with ASI, the physical demarcation of the area shall be completed in three weeks”.
The HC will hear the matter next on March 26, when it also directed that a report regarding work done on the matter related to physical demarcation be submitted before the court.
The issue of encroachment in Tughlakabad Fort area had earlier reached the Supreme Court as well. In 2016, the SC had recorded that “repeated orders are passed to the effect that there would not be any further construction in the protected monument”, which means ASI has to take action for removal of unauthorised construction as also encroachers from the public land. However, the encroachments had continued.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In an order issued in April 2023, the HC had recorded that ASI had already served 1,248 notices towards various structural encroachments within the fort.
As the court order had recorded, the ASI is in complete control of the area in question. However, since various state departments passed the buck over removal of the encroachments, the HC had in May 2017 constituted a committee — comprising various state departments — to conduct a survey of the area and take appropriate steps for removal of encroachments.
However, in April 2023, the ASI had expressed its “helplessness” in removing the encroachments on account of “non-cooperation of other departments”, including MCD and GNCTD.
In August 2023, the court was also informed that about
100 bigha of land has already been freed from encroachments and a wall is being built around the area.

headline: Court pulls up CBI for not handing all documents to Sandip Ghosh
description: On hearing the charges, the special CBI judge reprimanded Ghosh’s counsel, saying: “We’re not here to see faults of either side... This isn’t a political platform where you can raise your voice. You cannot talk like this against an agency. Give in writing.”
content:
The counsel of former principal of RG Kar Medical College and Hospital, Sandip Ghosh, on Monday accused the CBI of not providing all the documents related to the chargesheet in the case of alleged financial irregularities at the state-run hospital during the tenure of his client.
Ghosh, currently in jail, is one of the accused in the case.
In a submission before the trial court, Ghosh’s counsel Joseph Rauf said: “The CBI is always misguiding and misrepresenting the court. They have to give all the documents and statements of the witnesses. They haven’t done that. Documents that were filed here on the first day were 70%. But the next day, the CBI said all the documents had been given.”
“Why are material facts suppressed by the CBI? Some registers were not given. The CBI should be issued show-cause notice. The CBI has not given copies. It has suppressed our emails,” the lawyer told the court.
On hearing the charges, the special CBI judge reprimanded Ghosh’s counsel, saying: “We’re not here to see faults of either side… This isn’t a political platform where you can raise your voice. You cannot talk like this against an agency. Give in writing.”
The CBI’s counsel, on the other hand, accused Ghosh’s counsel of “always complaining”. “He is having problems. No one else has had problems. We will provide the documents,” the CBI’s counsel told the court.
The judge then reprimanded the CBI, directing the central probe agency to provide the documents immediately.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Where are your scanned copies? If the scanned copy is ready with you, provide it right now. Ask your representative (CBI) to bring the documents,” the judge told the CBI counsel.
The court ordered the CBI to provide the deficient documents to the counsels of the accused by 4 pm on Monday by email and in pen drive. Last Friday, the Calcutta High Court gave two days’ time to Ghosh and four other accused to go through the documents submitted by the CBI after taking cognisance of more time required
to go through the “voluminous documents”.

headline: Due to lack of birth certificate, can’t deny one from taking part in sports events: Delhi High Court
description: It was hearing a plea moved by basketball players against the Basketball Federation of India's (BFI) rule regarding verification of age, which had the potential to exclude underprivileged children from events organised by it.
content:
Not having a birth certificate due to socioeconomic backwardness can’t be the sole reason to deny a person the opportunity to compete in sports events, the Delhi High Court has ruled.
It was hearing a plea moved by basketball players against the Basketball Federation of India’s (BFI) rule regarding verification of age, which had the potential to exclude underprivileged children from events organised by it.
In his order dated January 27, Justice Sachin Datta said, “This court cannot be oblivious of the fact that on account of socio-economic backwardness, it may not have been feasible in some cases, to obtain birth certificates/other documents evidencing the age of the person within certain years from the date of birth. However, merely for this reason such persons cannot be denied the opportunity of competing in sporting events.”
State-level basketball players Deepak Jain (from Uttar Pradesh), Chandini (from Maharashtra), and seven others had approached the HC on multiple occasions against BFI’s rules on age verification, which they thought were “illegal” and “arbitrary”.
In regard to the basketball nationals held last May, the BFI had stated that the Age Verification Committee or Medical Board will on May 7, 2024, determine the eligibility of players to participate in the event. “Please advise your players to bring birth certificates issued by the Municipal Corporation/Registrar of Birth and Death obtained in the year of their birth or within five years of their birth and their Aadhaar card…,” it had added.
The point of contention for the petitioners was the requirement for the aspirants to provide birth certificates obtained within five years of their birth. The petitioners are attached to Noida-based Dribble Academy Foundation, which teaches underprivileged children to play basketball.
Advocate Amartya Bhushan, who represented the petitioners before the HC, said: “For national-level events, advertisements are published in the media regarding age eligibility rules well in advance. However, for district-level events, the rules are made public two or three days before the tryouts. Most children don’t have the resources to challenge these rules, especially on such short notice.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“The BFI wanted to curb age fraud… but it put people from underprivileged sections in the same bracket as fraudsters” he added.
The BFI had made several changes in the age verification process. In 2019, the rule stated that a player should have a birth certificate obtained within five years of his birth. Every subsequent year, the BFI reduced the requirement by one year. Thus, a player who was eligible in 2019 with a birth certificate issued within five years of his birth was not eligible the subsequent year when the criteria was birth certificate issued within four years.
In their plea, the petitioners maintained that the age verification method “unfairly deprived (underprivileged children)… solely due to lack of access to proper documents verifying their age”. This was on account of the children’s backward/socio-economic conditions, they said.
Further, they sought that the ‘National Code against Age Fraud in Sports’, issued by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, be adhered to. As per the code, a medical examination is mandatory when a sportsperson for the first time participates in any age-restricted competition.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The BFI, meanwhile, cited before HC lack of facilities to follow the requisite process to determine the age of players.
The court said: “…it is hardly open to (BFI) to cite the cost/s of test as a impeding factor. Unfortunately, the counter-affidavit filed on behalf of (BFI) does not even advert to, much less deal with, the hardship that will be caused to sportspersons, such as the petitioners… who will be deprived of participating in basketball events despite being otherwise qualified, competent and proficient, simply for want of an age certificate obtained within certain years from the date of their birth.” It added that “no cogent explanation” was given by BFI on why the ‘National Code against Age Fraud in Sports’ was not being followed.
Speaking to The Indian Express, Jain said, “Due to this rule, I missed my opportunity to compete at higher levels. However, with this restriction now removed, I am excited that I will finally be able to participate in state and national-level tournaments. This change opens new doors for many.”
Pradyot Voleti, the founder of Dribble Academy Foundation, said, “The parents of such children are electricians, plumbers and migrant labourers. For them, playing at competitive levels help them get admissions in schools and colleges… it even helps them get government jobs.”

headline: India won’t be viksit if it doesn’t largely reduce number of people staying in villages: Montek Singh Ahluwalia
description: Former Planning Commission deputy chairman Montek Singh Ahluwalia also says that if India witnesses 8% economic growth for the next 20 years, it will be led by the private sector and likely to begin in the South.
content:
Recommending that state governments improve urban management by empowering city administrations, particularly in places like Bengaluru, Montek Singh Ahluwalia, a former deputy chairman of the Planning Commission, said on Wednesday that more states should be carved out to increase the number of cities in the country.
“If India is to grow at 8 per cent, then the urban population has to grow larger. I think you have to recognise that India will not be viksit (developed) if it doesn’t largely reduce the number (of people) staying in the villages,” he said in Bengaluru.
Ahluwalia made these remarks during an interaction on “Resilient Pathways: Charting India’s Economic Growth Amid Global Challenges” at the state government’s Invest Karnataka 2025 meet alongside economist and author Salman Soz.
Ahluwalia emphasised that making a city liveable involved more than just attracting corporate investment. “There is a whole lot of urban management that has to be done. And there, Bengaluru has not done what it should be doing. Now that it is on the global map, the first thing that should be done is that the Bengaluru city government should be made hugely more efficient,” he said.
Also Read | ‘Rapid growth sees excess bank loans. It’s common… As boom ends, there is stress… But must it last 6 yrs?’
Ahluwalia said that city governments in India lack sufficient power. “Constitutionally, any state government can empower lower levels of authority as much as it wants. The constraint is not how to do it; the constraint is whether anyone wants to do it,” the economist said.
Advocating more urban centres, Ahluwalia suggested that tier-II cities should be developed into metros. “The only case it happens is when new states are carved out… If you did that, instantly there would be political willingness to create two or three new cities,” he said.
If India grows at 8 per cent for 20 years, it will be private sector-led and is likely to begin in the South, Ahluwalia said. “And then you will have those regional issues. If the country is to grow at 8 per cent and the South grows at 9 per cent while the North grows at 7 per cent, politics should be able to handle it,” he added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
While acknowledging that the slower population growth in the South compared to the North could be beneficial, he warned that it would lead to increased migration. “Lower-end jobs will be filled with people coming from Bihar, Orissa and so on. That is a huge structural change which will have all kinds of consequences,” he said, calling for discussions on the issues accompanying economic reforms.

headline: Military Intelligence and Pune Police bust fake Army recruit racket
description: Probe revealed that the suspect identified as Mohit Ramsingh Dhami (31), was approaching aspirants from poor financial background from Uttarakhand, Punjab & Maharashtra.
content:
IN A joint operation with the Southern Command Military Intelligence, Pune City Police have arrested a 31-year-old man who was allegedly running a fake Army recruitment racket and was giving forged appointment letters after taking money from aspiring youths from Maharashtra, Punjab and Uttarakhand.
A specific intelligence input was shared with the officials from Bundgarden police station by the Southern Command Military Intelligence regarding a suspect who was running a fake recruitment racket. Probe revealed that the suspect identified as Mohit Ramsingh Dhami (31), was approaching aspirants from poor financial background from Uttarakhand, Punjab & Maharashtra.
“Investigation revealed that Dhami approached aspirants claiming he had contacts and could ensure recruitment. He asked for Rs two lakh from each candidate and promised them jobs in the Army. He also gave them fake appointment letters with forged letterheads and stamps. We are now probing how many candidates he has cheated till now.” said a police officer.
Multiple cases of fraudsters posing as Army personnel or claiming contacts in the armed forces have been unearthed by the police in collaboration with the Souther Command over the last few years. These cases have been reported from Pune, Nashik, Ahmednagar districts in which imposters posing as Army officers or personnel, wearing Army uniform and claiming contacts with insiders have been arrested. In the context of the presence of several key defence establishments in these districts, such cases of impersonation pose a serious threat to security, officials have said.
The investigators in these cases have recovered forged documents like the identity cards, appointment letters, character certificates, service certificates and even tax deduction certificates, bank documents identifying the suspects as Army officers along with fake seals and letterheads of Army establishments in some cases.

headline: Three held for posting ‘objectionable’ comments about women’s panel chief Rupali Chakankar
description: According to police officials, the picture and the comments were posted on Facebook between October 22, 2024, and December 28, 2024, after which one of the office-bearers of the women’s commission filed a police complaint.
content:
Three persons were arrested for allegedly posting objectionable comments about Maharashtra State Women’s Commission Chairperson Rupali Chakankar on Facebook, police said Wednesday.
According to the South Cyber Cell of the Mumbai Crime Branch, a picture of  Chakankar  was uploaded on a Facebook page “Rajkaran Maharashtraache” to target her , following which other users of the platform began posting obscene comments under it.
According to police officials, the picture and the comments were posted on Facebook between October 22, 2024, and December 28, 2024, after which one of the office-bearers of the women’s commission filed a police complaint.
A case was then registered under relevant sections of the BNS, and an accused, identified as Babasaheb Shinde, was arrested on January 8.
Later, two others, identified as Avinash Pukle (30) and Aakash Dalve (30), were arrested from their respective residences in Solapur, Wednesday. Meanwhile, a court here granted bail to  Pukle and Dalve after furnishing bond of Rs 15,000.

headline: Pune DGGI uncovers Rs 1196 crore GST fraud
description: The release said the investigation involved searches in Pune, Delhi, Noida and Muzaffarnagar and revealed a sophisticated network of bogus companies engaged in fraudulent Input Tax Credit (ITC) transactions.
content:
THE   (DGGI) Pune Zone, has uncovered what they claimed was a “massive GST fraud amounting to Rs 1,196 crore.” A statement issued by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) issued on Wednesday evening said one person has been arrested in this fraud so far.
The release said the investigation involved searches in Pune, Delhi, Noida and Muzaffarnagar and revealed a sophisticated network of bogus companies engaged in fraudulent Input Tax Credit (ITC) transactions. “The accused had set up shell entities with no legitimate business operations, generating fake invoices and E-way bills to create a facade of genuine trade. However, these E-way bills had no RFID movements associated with them, confirming the absence of actual supply of goods. The fraudulent network facilitated the availing and passing of fake ITCs worth Rs 1,196 crore,” the release read.
The arrested individual is a director of a private limited company in Muzaffarnagar. The investigation uncovered that a cartel maintained a database of addresses, identities, email IDs, and phone numbers, which were strategically rotated to obtain new GST registrations and evade detection. “The newly created firms had directors or proprietors selected from this repository, allowing the fraudsters to sustain their illicit activities,” the release read.
During searches at multiple locations, officials recovered original invoices, financial records, company stamps, and seals, indicating centralised control over multiple shell firms. The investigation has so far identified 20 such fictitious companies with no genuine business activity. Authorities have also frozen one bank account linked to a fraudulent entity, with further investigations underway.

headline: Recruitment process begins for 666 vacant teaching posts in govt medical colleges
description: In the current academic year, nine new government medical colleges have opened across the state, adding 900 new student seats.  This increase has also led to a rise in total vacant teaching positions.
content:
The recruitment process to fill 666 out of the 1,600 vacant teaching posts in government medical colleges across the state has started through the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC), said sources from the Directorate of Medical Education and Research (DMER).
“These posts include 428 lecturers, 167 associate professors and 71 professors for government medical colleges. Even as it does not cover all vacant posts yet, it is a major relief for government medical colleges currently managing with contractual teachers,” said an official from the DMER while adding that this includes vacant posts in existing government medical colleges along with additions from the nine new ones which started in the state in this academic year.
In the current academic year, nine new government medical colleges have opened across the state, adding 900 new student seats.  This increase has also led to a rise in total vacant teaching positions.
Details of 666 posts have been sent to MPSC for recruitment which will include a thorough process.
“All new government medical colleges saw full admission in the first year itself. This proves the demand for government medical colleges among aspirants as it is a more affordable choice than learning medicine in private medical colleges. Deans of the new government medical colleges are currently given authority to appoint contractual teachers to meet needs,” the official added.

headline: Gujarat anti-graft bureau gets full-time director after 4 years as ADGP Piyush Patel is appointed to the post
description: The post of Director of the Gujarat ACB has been substantially vacant since the superannuation of DGP Keshav Kumar in 2021.
content:
The Gujarat government on Wednesday appointed Additional Director General (ADGP) Piyush Patel the Director of the Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) in the state.
The 1998-batch IPS officer, who had gone on central deputation in 2023, had been awaiting posting for the last couple of months now after being repatriated to his home cadre after serving as Inspector General (IG) of the Border Security Force (BSF), in November 2024. He was repatriated early on the request of the Gujarat government.
Before his posting at the BSF, Patel was the IG of Surat Range when he was promoted to the rank of ADGP.
Notably, the ex-cadre post of Director of the Gujarat ACB was, on Tuesday, downgraded from DGP to ADGP to accommodate this appointment.

The post of Director of the Gujarat ACB has been substantially vacant since the superannuation of DGP Keshav Kumar in 2021.
The post has been held as additional charge by DGP Sanjay Srivastava while he was Commissioner of Police (CP) Ahmedabad City Police till his superannuation in 2023. He was followed by ADGP Rajesh Brahmbhatt, who held additional charge while posted at the State Intelligence Bureau.
ADGP Anupam Singh Gehlot was then given charge during his stint as CP of Vadodara City Police. In late 2023, ADG Shamsher Singh was given the additional charge of ACB while at the post of DGP (Law and Order).

headline: Maharashtra PWD minister seeks Rs 10,000 cr to clear pending dues of contractors
description: Contractors in the state have gone on strike from February 5, stopping all ongoing infrastructure works alleging that payments worth Rs 89,000 crore from different departments have allegedly not been paid since July 2024.
content:
State Public Works Department (PWD) Minister Shivendraraje Bhosle Wednesday said that he has sought Rs 10,000 crore to be released at the earliest for contractors who have been on strike for a week over pending dues.
“I have spoken to the Chief Minister and Finance minister. Both are positive regarding the demands raised by contractors. The department is positive about our demand of Rs 10,000 crore to be released at the earliest. It will help paying dues of the contractors,” said state’s PWD minister Shivendraraje Bhosle.
According to the PWD department, around Rs 18,000 crore is needed in the current fiscal to sort out the issues of the contractors.
Contractors in the state have gone on strike from February 5, stopping all ongoing infrastructure works alleging that payments worth Rs 89,000 crore from different departments have allegedly not been paid since July 2024.
Among the alleged Rs 89,000 crore dues of the contractors include Rs 46,000 crore from the PWD, Rs 18,000 crore from the Jal Jeevan Mission under Water Supply and Sanitation department, Rs 8,600 crore from the Rural development department, Rs 19,700 crore from the Irrigation department and Rs 1,700 crore from the works done under DPDC, MLA fund and MP fund.
Bhosle accepted that there are certain issues regarding the payment to contractors.
“However, the dues are not from the past one year alone. Some dues are from the previous years as well,” he said, adding that major chunk of payments is of road and bridge works.
“These are district-level works where small contractors are suffering. We understand their problems and we are working towards solving those,” Bhosle said, adding that total of around Rs 18,000 crore is needed in the ongoing fiscal.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The minister, when asked about large number of work orders issued in the poll year, said, “Now, it was an election year and the works orders were issued in greater numbers. But we are sure that it will be sorted out.”

headline: 2 men with links to Canada-based gangster Arsh Dalla held in Punjab’s Fatehgarh Sahib: Police
description: The police identified the accused as Sahil and Gurkirat Singh and said that they were working for Canada-based gangster Arsh Dalla through an inmate in Patiala jail.
content:
The police in Punjab’s Fatehgarh Sahib district said on Wednesday that they have busted Canada-based gangster Arsh Dalla’s network and arrested two people. Five country-made .32 bore pistols along with five live cartridges, a scooter and two cell phones were recovered from the accused, the police added.
According to Ravjot Grewal, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Fatehgarh Sahib, a Crime Investigation Agency (CIA) team arrested Sahil and Gurkirat Singh from Sirhind on Tuesday and booked them under the Arms Act.
Gurkirat had returned from Malaysia in May 2024 after staying there for a year. He and Sahil were working for Dalla through Tejbir Singh, alias Sabu, an inmate in Patiala jail, the SSP said, adding that Sabu was an associate of Dalla. Designated a terrorist by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in January 2023, Dalla has over 70 cases registered against him in India.

Tejbir was in jail for murder and illegal arms-related cases and was involved in several criminal activities in Amritsar, Grewal said. Earlier, he was booked in an arms case in Amritsar and a murder case in Jagraon in Ludhiana district. Tejbir and Sahil are close associates who stayed in the Siripura locality of Amritsar, the SSP added.

“The accused were supplying arms to execute criminal activities but police intervention prevented a major incident. Tejbir Singh has been brought from Patiala Jail for further interrogation, which is expected to reveal crucial information. Currently, all three accused are in police remand,” the SSP added.
