headline: Custody plea: Delhi HC seeks response from Uganda High Commission, FRRO on bringing orphaned infant to court
description: Ugandan mother of 18-month-old baby died of HIV infection
content:
The Delhi High Court has sought response from the High Commission of the Republic of Uganda and the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) in a petition seeking production of an 18-month-old infant whose 27-year-old Ugandan mother, unlawfully trafficked to India, died due to HIV infection.
The petition has been moved by an NGO, Manobal Foundation, which provides assistance to victims of human trafficking, through advocate Utkarsh Singh.
The petition notes that the deceased mother was brought to India under false pretences in November 2022, with her visa valid until November 2023. She ended up overstaying after becoming a victim of human trafficking “and had to endure inhumane conditions” until her rescue by the Manobal Foundation.
She had subsequently submitted an application for an exit permit on January 11.
However she was hospitalised on January 17 and three days later, died due to her HIV infection. At the time of her hospitalisation, she had entrusted the custody of the child to one Namakula Dooren for the period she was in the hospital.
Ever since the mother’s death, it was found that Dooren had handed over the infant’s custody to another woman, one Jackylin Nakayima alias Julie. Nakayima then refused to hand over custody of the child to the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) as is required if a child is orphaned. The same was informed to the Ugandan Embassy, Department of Women and Child Development and Children Welfare Commission through an email.
In an order by the division bench of Justices Prathiba Singh and Dharmesh Sharma on January 27, the court recorded, “Further, allegations have also been made by the Petitioner NGO that various foreign nationals are residing in Delhi, who are forced into human trafficking since these individuals are not being given the requisite exit permits after their visas have expired.”

Following the NGO’s submissions, the court issued notice to all the respondents including the two women who allegedly had custody of the infant at various point of time, Uganda High Commission, the state through the police, Child Welfare Committee and WCD department, FRRO and district child protection unit of New Delhi.
The court has posted the matter for next hearing on February 7.

headline: Sharjeel Imam, 6 others move Delhi High Court seeking stay on release of ‘Delhi 2020’
description: After the petitions were filed over ‘Delhi 2020’, the Delhi High Court sought a response from the Centre and CBFC.
content:
Delhi riots accused Sharjeel Imam and six others moved the Delhi High Court Thursday, seeking a stay on the release of Delhi 2020, a film purportedly based on the Northeast Delhi riots, slated for release on February 2.
Justice Sachin Datta sought a response from the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) and the Centre through its Ministry of Information and Broadcasting as well as the production house Visual Birds Studio as well as BJP IT Department head Amit Malviya in two of the three petitions.
The third petition — by the Independent candidate Umang — was not listed on Thursday, and is expected to come up on Friday.
The first petition was moved by five people — two victims of the riot, Sahil Parvez who lost his father and Mohd Saeed Salman whose mother was burnt alive, and three accused in the riots case including Akil Ahmed, Sonu and Tasleem Ahmed (who is still in jail). They are seeking quashing and setting aside the CBFC certification of the film and a direction that it is not be released till the criminal cases involving the petitioners are finally disposed of.
Advocate Mehmood Pracha, appearing for the petitioners, told Justice Datta the release of the film will “completely prejudice both accused and complainants in the cases” pertaining to the Delhi 2020 riots and added that the film is in “direct contravention of the Cinematograph Act as well as the Contempts of Courts Act.” Pracha added, “You (respondent filmmaker) can have your political objectives and aims but not at my expense.”
Sharjeel Imam’s petition seeks a pre-screening of the movie for the court as well as to direct the Centre to postpone its release until the trial in the larger conspiracy case of Delhi riots, in which he is accused, is completed. Imam is also seeking the court’s direction to the various respondents to take down all pre-release material such as posters, images, trailers etc until the trial’s completion.
Advocate Warisha Farasat, representing Imam, told the court, “I’m one of the accused who is being shown front and centre in the trailer, not once but several times…the law actually supports us…we have to balance right of freedom and expression and a clear exception is carved out…arguments on the charge (against Imam) are going on, and bail is before this court (Delhi HC)…Time is of essence… Let this court direct a viewing of the film”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The court issued notice to the respondents in the two of the petitions, and directed the Centre, CBFC, and the production house to “come with instructions, ready to argue the matter tomorrow”, posting the matter for Friday in light of the urgency pressed for by the petitioners.
The third petition, by Umang, an Independent candidate from the Rajinder Nagar constituency, has sought a stay or ban on the release of Delhi 2020 in cinemas, on television, and on OTT platforms, and an order to remove the trailer of the film from YouTube and other social media platforms. He has also sought the revocation of the film’s certification under the Cinematograph Act, 1952, and action against the filmmakers and others responsible for launching the film and sharing videos, which he said has the potential to create communal disharmony.
Umang is also seeking direction to the Election Commission of India to investigate the complaint filed by him in this regard and take appropriate action against violations of the Model Code of Conduct (MCC).
Citing the violation of MCC as well as the Cinematograph Act, Umang’s petition submits, “The timing of the film’s release is critically coincidental with the upcoming Delhi Assembly Elections scheduled for 05.02.2025. headline: BPO employee murdered by colleague: Pune police issue SOP for safety of women employees
description: The SOP recognises the fundamental right of women to a safe and secure working environment, free from all forms of violence and discrimination.
content:
In the aftermath of the murder of a 28-year-old accountant working for a multinational business process outsourcing (BPO) firm in Pune by her colleague, the Pune city police have issued Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to be followed by the police and private firms to prevent such incidents. The SOPs primarily focus on safety of women employees and has pointers on safety audits, access control and communication, among other issues.
Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar made the announcement about the SOPs while interacting with representatives from the Information Technology (IT) and other corporate sector companies from Magarpatta City about their various safety and security concerns and other issues faced by them. The interaction was organised under the purview of the seven-point action plan given by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis for better functioning of government departments.
Referring to the murder of BPO accountant Shubhada Kodare, Kumar said, “After analysing and assessing the situation we have chalked out a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on what the police and the companies need to do to ensure that there is no chance of recurrence of such an event. The SOP has been laid out based on what transpired and what were the sequence of events leading to that incident on January 7.”
The SOP recognises the fundamental right of women to a safe and secure working environment, free from all forms of violence and discrimination. It aims to ensure the safety and well-being of women employees in all workplaces across Pune city.

Man held for raping 12-year-old girl on way to school in UP’s Bulandshahr, search on for his mother
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Among the provisions of the SOP is establishment of security committees: Every establishment with 10 or more women employees shall mandatorily constitute an internal committee to address issues related to women’s safety. The committee shall comprise representatives from management, women employees, and a designated officer for women’s safety.
On security audits, the SOP states that all Senior Police Inspectors of Pune City shall conduct regular security audits of establishments with significant female employees. WhatsApp groups should be created at the police station level of HR heads and security heads of such establishments along with in-charge inspectors and Chowky Incharges. Audits shall assess physical security measures including lighting, CCTV coverage, access control, emergency response protocols, and awareness programs for employees.
On access control, companies are to ensure proper access control by use of equipment like X-ray bag scanners, metal detectors. Random checking of vantage points, dark alleys, parking areas to ensure women safety shall be conducted by the management.

On communication and collaboration, WhatsApp groups are to be set up with company security heads and HR heads to facilitate rapid communication and coordinated responses to security concerns. The senior inspectors of local police stations must ensure that the response is quick and concerns are addressed expeditiously.
On CCTV coverage, the respective Assistant Commissioners of Police in coordination with ACP (Wireless), company IT teams and local police station staff shall conduct comprehensive checks on the CCTV coverage of all establishments. Regular audits be conducted of transportation services employed by companies to ensure the safety and security of women employees during commute. This includes background checks of drivers, vehicle maintenance, and GPS tracking.
Each company shall conduct regular interaction sessions with women employees to assess their concerns and fears, particularly regarding late night travel. Mechanisms shall be established to address individual concerns and provide necessary support.

headline: Having lost Rs 290-crore Central aid last year, Punjab plans to bring in maize as part of crop diversification plan
description: The Centre had rolled out a plan last year under which Punjab farmers were to get Rs 7,000 per acre for planning any crop other than paddy as a part of CDP; the amount got lapsed.
content:
Months after the Rs 290-crore grant meant for Punjab under crop diversification plan (CDP) of Centre got lapsed due to the delay in rolling it out for the state farmers, the Punjab government is not taking any chances this time and is formulating a plan before the kharif sowing season sets in.
The government is now consulting experts from Punjab Development Commission (PDC), set up in September 2023 as an independent action-based think tank, so that the Central grant of Rs 7,000 per acre for farmers as part of crop diversification plan (CDP) for the 2025-26 fiscal does meet its goal.
Additional Chief Secretary (Development) Anurag Verma on Tuesday held a meeting with experts from PDC and officials of the agriculture department and sought suggestions on how the Rs 7,000 per acre could be given to the farmers.
Sources said the discussions revolved around cultivating monsoon (Kharif) maize as an alternative to paddy. “We are now formulating a policy. We have discussed maize and cotton. We will be able to make an offer to the farmers in the coming days,” said an official.
Also Read | Punjab farmers usher in a ‘silent revolution’ by diversifying agriculture through horticulture
Maize is being used as packaged fodder for cattle, meant to be supplied to Rajasthan and Gujarat, and also to produce bio-ethanol. Several units for preserving and packaging the fodder have been set up across the state. The government is planning to bring in private players to tie up with farmers to supply them maize for bio-ethanol plants.
The kharif season in Punjab is the period between the second half of May and mid-November.
The Centre had rolled out a plan last year under which Punjab farmers were to get the amount for planning any crop other than paddy as a part of CDP. Paddy was, however, included in the plan at the insistence of the Punjab government. But the benefit of the plan could not be given to the farmers.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The state government has a huge challenge staring itself in the face of reducing the area under paddy this Kharif season. Last year, the area was at an all-time high at 32 lakh hectares.
The area under cotton had dwindled drastically to a mere less than one lakh hectares last season, which is an all-time low recorded history in the state. Two years ago it was 1.79 lakh hectares. Cotton used to have a huge area in Punjab till 1980, and 1990s when it witnessed up to 7.58 lakh hectares area. A strategy for increasing the area under cotton cultivation was also sought.
Last year the department of agriculture could not formulate a policy as the state leadership was busy with the Lok Sabha elections that was scheduled between April 19 and June 1, 2024. Paddy transplantation starts in Punjab in mid-June. Before that it takes a few weeks for the farmers to sow the seeds and prepare nurseries.
Samyukta Kisan Morcha’s (Political) Balbir Singh Rajewal had raised the issue of lapsing of Rs 290 crore in a recent meeting with Punjab Agriculture Minister Gurmeet Singh Khuddian asking him to explain why the grant could not be given to the farmers.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Also Read | Seeds of change: Transition to high-value crops like strawberry, dragon fruit helps Punjab farmers earn Rs 5-6 lakh per acre
An issue of seed subsidy on wheat, costing the Centre and state Rs 20 crore (60:40 share) annually was also discussed at the meeting. The government has been paying Rs 1,000 on every quintal of seed purchased for up to 5 acres of landholdings. It was discussed that this subsidy should rather be paid on seeds of alternative crops to pull the farmers out of paddy-wheat monoculture.
“The withdrawal of this subsidy is a political issue. The decision is to be taken by the political leadership. We can only suggest,” said an official.
The state government is already facing an issue of lifting of paddy. During the last Kharif season, the farmers had faced problems with lifting of paddy as there was no space to store it due to lax movement of paddy out of godowns in the state. Some farmers had complained that they had to take a cut of Rs 200 on every quintal of paddy procured. “The farmers are also wary of growing paddy this season. They know there is no space. They would like to diversify. Just that we have to come out with a plan. We will have to do it aggressively this year,” said an official.
The government will have to take charge fast. The farmers start harvesting wheat in the first week of April. After the procurement, the preparation for sowing of paddy nurseries begins.

headline: Karnataka High Court issues interim stay on central order barring ex-judge P N Desai from govt appointments
description: The central order came months after Justice P N Desai, who had retired from the Karnataka High Court, was appointed to investigate the alleged MUDA land scam.
content:
The Karnataka High Court has issued an interim stay on a November 2024 order by the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions that barred Justice P N Desai, who had retired from the court, from taking up government appointments for three years.
Justice Desai was appointed by the state government as the one-man commission of inquiry to investigate the alleged MUDA land scam in July last year.
Senior advocate Udaya Holla, representing Justice Desai, argued that the retired judge had made a communication on August 14, 2024, to the effect that he thanked the government for his appointment as a member of the Central Administrative Tribunal but he could not take up the role as he had already accepted the assignment of the Karnataka government.
Holla argued that the consent of the selected candidates was required before proposals were sent to the secretariat of the appointment committee. If appointed candidates did not join their posting for thirty days, the procedure is to send a 15-day notice informing of possible debarment, it was further argued.
On Tuesday, a bench of Justice R Devdas issued an interim stay on the Union ministry’s order until the next date of hearing in the matter, February 6.
The court’s interim order said, “Learned Senior Counsel submits that neither the petitioner was informed of his selection nor was a notice issued to the petitioner before passing the impugned order of debarment. Moreover, it is submitted that some of the newspapers are carrying the information that the petitioner has been debarred from further appointment as a judicial member of the Central Administrative Tribunal.”

headline: GRAP III anti-pollution curbs return in Delhi as air quality worsens
description: Delhi's AQI was 365 on Wednesday against Tuesday's AQI of 276.
content:
Anti-pollution curbs under Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) kicked in on Wednesday evening again as the Capital’s air quality deteriorated to the ‘very poor’ category. The development comes after the AQI (air quality index) in the city remained in the ‘moderate’ or ‘poor’ category for nine straight days.
Delhi’s AQI was 365 on Wednesday against Tuesday’s AQI of 276. Calm winds are said to be one of the factors behind the worsening air quality, apart from smoggy condition.
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM), the Centre’s panel on Delhi-NCR’s air quality, has invoked the stringent measures which include hybrid mode for classes up to V; a ban on BS III, and a ban on BS III petrol and BS-IV diesel cars; staggered timings for public offices and municipal bodies in Delhi and a few NCR districts, as well as a ban on demolition work and mining activities.
The situation is likely to persist in the coming days, the CAQM said in its order, citing the forecast by the India Meteorological Department and Indian Institute of Technology Madras.
During winters, the Delhi-NCR region enforces restrictions under GRAP, which categorises air quality into four stages – Stage I (Poor, AQI 201-300), Stage II (Very Poor, AQI 301-400), Stage III (Severe, AQI 401-450), and Stage IV (Severe Plus, AQI above 450).

headline: Clean chit to Haryana IPS officer in sexual harassment case
description: The all-woman SIT finds viral sexual harassment letter ‘baseless’
content:
A three-member, all-women special investigation team (SIT), headed by an additional director general of police (ADGP)-rank IPS officer, has found allegations in a viral sexual harassment letter against a Haryana IPS officer to be “baseless.”

headline: 2014 techie rape-murder: Mumbai Crime branch analysing SC’s judgement, plans to file a review against SC verdict acquitting accused

content:
A day after the Supreme Court passed a verdict acquitting Chandrabhan Sanap, the man arrested by the Mumbai Crime Branch in a rape-and-murder case involving a 23-year-old techie, senior police officials from the department informed that their team is analysing the judgment and trying to understand the grounds on which they could appeal or file a review on the verdict.
A senior police officer confirming the development said, “A deputy commissioner of police police has been assigned to analyse the judgment in detail. We will ascertain the grounds on which Sanap was acquitted, following which we will decide on our next steps.”
Officials from the Mumbai police also alleged that they are trying to understand whether they can file an appeal against the order or if they could ask the Supreme Court to review it.

description: Nayab Saini drank the Yamuna river water as a counter to Arvind Kejriwal for his 'poisoning' comments, demanding that the former Delhi chief minister apologise to the people of Haryana and Delhi.
content:
In a dramatic counter to Aam Aadmi Party chief Arvind Kejriwal’s claim that the BJP government in Haryana was “poisoning” Delhi’s water supply, Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Saini publicly drank water from the Yamuna river.
The act, captured in a one-minute video by news agency ANI, comes as tensions rise ahead of the upcoming Delhi Assembly elections, with the Haryana government now planning legal action against Kejriwal over his comments.
In the clip, Saini is seen paying his respects to the Yamuna River in Delhi’s Palla Village before taking a sip and spitting it out. Then he took another sip and this time he drank it.
#WATCH | Haryana CM Nayab Singh Saini takes a sip of water from the Yamuna River in Delhi’s Palla Village. pic.twitter.com/v1rkJXrcbQ
— ANI (@ANI) January 29, 2025
Saini’s act comes after he escalated his offensive against Kejriwal for his comments, demanding that the former Delhi chief minister apologise to the people of Haryana and Delhi.
“Kejriwal has lost his mental balance seeing his possible defeat in the elections. He should seek an apology from the public of Delhi and Haryana immediately, or we will file a defamation suit against him,” Saini asserted saying the AAP convener has “insulted the land” where he was born.

Rejecting Kejriwal’s allegations, Saini questioned his claims regarding water contamination.
“Kejriwal said ‘the engineers of Delhi Jal Board stopped the (Yamuna) water from coming to Delhi because they came to know that there is a poison in the water.’ How did the engineers determine there was poison? Kejriwal should explain ‘what poison was added and in what quantity?’ If the water was actually poisonous, how many fishes died?” he asked.
Saini also questioned why would the residents poison the water when they worship the Yamuna river.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Election Commission has also stepped in, seeking proof from Kejriwal after BJP and Congress leaders lodged complaints over his remarks.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi also hit out at Kejriwal, calling his statements an insult to the people of Haryana.
“A former CM of Delhi has levelled disgusting allegations on people of Haryana. Due to fear of losing, people from ‘AAP-da’ have got rattled. Are people of Haryana different from those in Delhi? Can they poison the water their own people drink?” Modi said at a rally in Delhi, adding that Yamuna river’s water is consumed by everyone in Delhi, including him.
Delhi elections will be held on February 5 and results will be announced on February 8.

headline: Interview: Looking to raise women officers’ strength in AFMS to 25%, says Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin
description: In an interview with The Indian Express, Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin, the first woman Director General of AFMS, says digital health initiatives are being given top priority at AFMS and AI is being utilised for predictive health analytics and personalised treatment plans.
content:
The Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) is looking to increase its strength of women officers to 25 per cent from the present 21 per cent, said Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin, the first woman officer who took charge as Director General, AFMS, in October last year.
Surg Vice Adm Sarin is in Pune for the 73rd annual Armed Forces Medical Conference being held from January 28 to 30.She inaugurated Indian Council of Medical Research Advanced Molecular Oncology Diagnostic (DIAMOnDS) centre during the conference, apart from a smart lecture hall for postgraduate training at Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC).
DG, AFMS, functions under the Ministry of Defence, and is responsible for all medical policy matters related to the Armed Forces.
In an interview with The Indian Express, Surgeon Vice Adm Sarin said that the organisation offers ample opportunities for young women to take up leadership roles.
The officer was In Pune for the 73rd annual Armed Forces Medical Conference being held from January 28 to 30.
“Priorities include bolstering disaster preparedness, integrating advanced medical technologies, enhancing operational capabilities through mobile and modular healthcare units and enhancing our cooperation with Friendly Foreign Nations,” Sarin said. Excerpts from the interview:
Q: Three months into your tenure as the first woman DG what have been your key areas of focus?
Surgeon Vice Admiral Arti Sarin: It is an incredible honour and privilege to have been bestowed the opportunity to serve as the first lady Director General, Armed Forces Medical Services. This speaks of the highest standards of professionalism and gender neutrality in AFMS. These past three months have been marked by both challenges and opportunities, where I have strived to enhance operational medical readiness, while maintaining the highest standards of healthcare delivery. My focus has been on building a more inclusive, adaptive, and technologically advanced medical service that aligns with the evolving needs of our Armed Forces personnel.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Q: What plans are being taken to upskill medical officers with the latest developments in the field of medicine?
Surg Vice Admiral Sarin: Continuous professional development is critical in ensuring our medical officers remain at the forefront of medical science. We have partnered with leading national and international institutions for augmenting our training programmes. Emphasis is being placed on skill development in conventional fields of medical sciences as well as emerging fields such as personalised medicine, telemedicine, and artificial intelligence applications to facilitate diagnostics and treatment. Regular workshops, CMEs, and exchange programmes are also being enhanced. AFMS officers are encouraged to undertake short-term and long-term training programmes, including PhD to enhance their skills. AFMC has recently conducted a CME on AI in Medicine and we ensure Medical Officers in remote areas also participate through hybrid mode to remain updated.
Q: There are over 400 vacancies of medical officers in the Armed Forces, as per reports. What is the requirement and when will these be filled?
Surg Vice Admiral Sarin: The requirement of manpower is assessed periodically, and the organisation’s mandate is to induct the best human resource to serve our clientele and fulfill various operational needs. Armed Forces Medical College, Pune, one of the premier medical colleges in the country trains medical graduates for serving the Armed Forces. In addition, we regularly conduct interviews for selection of medical officers for AFMS, from other medical colleges too. Regular efforts are underway to attract the best talent in AFMS. Outreach programmes are being organised at various medical institutions to sensitise the medical students about the career opportunities being  offered by AFMS.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Q: Can you elaborate on several research projects that have been taken up along with DRDO and other defence institutions?
Surg Vice Admiral Sarin: Significant progress has been made in research collaborations with Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and other institutions over the years, with exceptional efforts of my predecessors whereby collaborations with Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Indian Institute of Technology (IITs), AIIMS (New Delhi), Department of Biotechnology (DBT), iDEX and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) have been undertaken. Institutionalisation of High Altitude Medical Research Centre, Leh, into an independent research institute and a centralised repository of data generated by various research projects are also on the cards. The areas in which we intend to evolve our existing protocols and innovate are (a) Field Diagnostic Kits for rapid diagnosis and treatment of medical ailments in remote locations (b) Artificial blood substitutes for emergency transfusions and (c) development of AI models for data pertaining to diagnostics in Pathology and Radiology.
Q: How is digital transformation reshaping healthcare and medical training, and what role does AI play in enhancing medical services?
Surg Vice Admiral Sarin: Digital health initiatives are a top priority, with projects like an integrated electronic health record system being rolled out across the Armed Forces hospitals. AI is being utilised for predictive health analytics, personalised treatment plans, and enhanced diagnostics in radiology and pathology. AI-enabled software in diagnostics and pathology which will enable us in clinical decision making, precision medicine, triage, injury prevention are also being worked upon. In medical training, simulation-based learning, augmented reality tools, and AI-driven virtual instructors are being adopted to elevate the skills of our medical personnel.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Q: Are there any programmes tailored for mental health care needs for those in the Armed Forces? What is the burden of stress-related disorders in the Armed Forces?
Surg Vice Admiral Sarin: Mental health care remains a critical focus area in AFMS. Further, AFMS encourages preventive mental health and has instituted several projects towards improvement of mental health and stress related disorders through wellness clinics, adoption of Hub and Spoke model and resilience building workshops. TELE-MANAS cell, a dedicated 24 x 7 mental health initiative tailored for the unique challenges faced by military personnel and their dependents is functional at Armed Forces Medical College, Pune.
Q. You have played a key role in inspiring young women to join the Armed Forces and are an icon of the Nari Shakti initiative of the Government. How do you see women’s participation in the Armed Forces?
Surg Vice Admiral Sarin: The growing participation of women in the Armed Forces is a testament to the Government’s Nari Shakti initiative. Women have played key role in AFMS since the 1950s, while women entered in the other services in the 1990s. 75% of top leadership appointments in AFMS are held by women (for instance Lt Gen Sadhna Saxena, Director General, Medical Services, Army, and Surgeon Vice-Admiral Kavita Sahai, Director General, Medical Services, Navy). Women Agniveers have been recruited in the Navy and the Air Force in various roles, and in the Corps of Military Police in the Army. Women have taken up combat role as fighter pilots in the Indian Air Force since 2016. The National Defence Academy has started admitting lady cadets since 2021, which exemplifies gradual and systematic increment in the role of women in the Armed Forces. Women officers constitute over 21 per cent of the officer strength in the Armed Forces Medical Services, which we are looking forward to increasing to 25 per cent in the times to come. As you are seeing, the organisation offers ample opportunities for young women to take up leadership roles.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Q: Has AFMC got the status of institute of national importance?
Surg Vice Admiral Sarin: Achieving the status of an Institute of National Importance for AFMC remains a key objective and we are putting in our best efforts for the same.

headline: Cinematographers’ meet in Mumbai to shine spotlight on their journey, challenges
description: 'Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham' cinematographer Kiran Deohans and seven others to hold a discussion as part of the ongoing Kala Ghoda Arts Festival at Cama Hall in Mumbai on January 29.
content:
In a recent masterclass, senior cinematographer Kiran Deohans recounted the challenges of lighting a romantic sequence in the song “Inn Lamhon Ke Daaman Mein” from the 2008 film Jodhaa Akbar, starring Hrithik Roshan and Aishwarya Rai Bachchan. He explained that they had to create an elaborate setup to give the impression that the room was illuminated by the reflection of the setting sun. Later in the song, the lighting changes as the crescent moon comes up, and the room is filled with candlelight.
The masterclass by Deohans, who has shot Qayamat Se Qayamat Tak (1988), Karan Johar’s iconic Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001) and others, was hosted by Flare Cinematography Film Festival. Cinematographer Pooja Gupte, who founded Flare with the aim to build a community of cinematographers to share their expertise and help build their skill set, believes that learning about such fascinating experiences, unique challenges and how to manage intricate setups is the idea behind holding such masterclasses and discussions.
In continuation of that effort, Flare was set to host a cinematographers’ meet on Wednesday as part of the ongoing Kala Ghoda Arts Festival at Cama Hall in Mumbai. Cinematographers Deohans, Fowzia Fathima, Siddharth Diwan, Deepti Gupta, Neha Parti Matiyani, Anil Mehta, and Priyanka Singh will take part in the meet.
“While the American Film Institute and various cinema bodies in Europe hold such masterclasses and conversations regularly, we rarely do that in India,” said Gupte, who studied cinematography at Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, Kolkata. Sharing personal experiences, believes Gupte, is a step towards “creating a community and to facilitate skill development”.
One of the major challenges that cinematographers face while working on a big set is to handle the light and maintain continuity. “While an action scene needs choreography, lighting is of utmost importance in a romantic scene,” said Gupte. That apart, one of the biggest teams on a film set belongs to the cinematography department. “So, managing a team is another challenge,” added Gupte.
The cinematographers’ meet at Cama Hall will be held from 4 pm to 6 pm.

headline: Mahisagar: Tribal man dies by suicide; kin blame local administration
description: Family claimed he was made to run from pillar to post for an English copy of caste certificate required for his daughter's appointment in a Central govt job
content:
A 45-year-old tribal man from Ranakpur, a remote village in Kadana taluka of Mahisagar, allegedly died by suicide on Tuesday. His family claimed he took the extreme step because of the “delay in getting the copy of a caste certificate in English” that could have jeopardised his daughter’s recent appointment in a Central government department.
The death sparked off a row with the family members of the deceased alleging that the local administration “made him run from pillar to post”.
On the other hand, the Mahisagar district administration stated that the application was made only 11 days ago as against the stipulated 45-day time set by the government to decide on caste certificate matters.
The body of Uda Damor, a former Gram Rakshak Dal staff, was pulled down from a tree on the outskirts of his village. Police also found a note in his pocket in which he had allegedly blamed the local administration for allegedly forcing him to take the step.

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Death penalty nixed in POCSO case, rapist assaults, kills 11-year-old disabled girl
Kanti Damor, the uncle of the deceased, said, “He had been running from one office to another to get the caste certificate for his daughter, who recently got appointed in the Post Department. Since it is a Central government appointment, it has become mandatory to provide an English copy of the caste certificate. She already has a valid caste certificate in Gujarati. All they needed was an English version but the local office found faults in the application and asked them to bring documents pertaining to a caste issue before 1960. Time had been running out for the girl and he was left with no choice…”
Even as the Kadana police station registered a case of accidental death and sent Uda Damor’s body for post-mortem examination, the family, on Tuesday evening, refused to accept the body until action was initiated against the officers. Sources in Mahisagar district police said that preparations were being made to shift Uda Damor’s body to the mortuary in SSG hospital in Vadodara from the Kadana government hospital, if the family did not accept the body until midnight.
Additional Superintendent of Police, Mahisagar, Vijay Bheda said, “The incident seems to have occurred between 5.30 am and 7 am on Tuesday. Police was informed at 8.25 am. We are verifying the note left behind to ascertain whether he has written it himself. We are also seeking expert opinion. We are investigating the allegation that he was forced to take the extreme step due to an issue with the caste certificate…”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
While Mahisagar District Collector Neha Kumari was unavailable for comment, senior district administration officials have said that an internal inquiry into the matter has revealed that the family had made the application on January 17.
A senior officer of the administration said, “The application in the case was received at the mamlatdar office on January 17, although it was dated January 15. The application did not mention which language they needed the caste certificate in. On examining the documents submitted, among those persons mentioned in the pedhinama (family pedigree), the applicant had not submitted appropriate documents for one person named Kalu Damor. Therefore, the applicant was called to the mamlatdar office to be informed that they can either submit a verified document of the same person or another supporting document of the person’s mother or father.”
The officer added that internal inquiry had revealed that although the applicant (Uda Damor’s daughter) submitted the document asked for by the administration at 5.30 pm on Monday (January 27), the applicant’s father had “passed away a day later”.
“The decision on the caste certificate is pending and as per the government rules, a stipulated period of 45 days has been awarded to decide on the matter and issue caste certificates. In this case, the time lapse between the application and the death of the applicant’s father is 11 days. Therefore, it cannot be connected to the pending application of the caste certificate,” an internal inquiry of the administration stated.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Babu Gala Damor, a local community leader in Ranakpur, said, “Time was running out for the daughter. He (Uda Damor) was anxious and worried that she might lose employment with the Central department if the certificate is not given on time. They (administration) kept sending him back…”

headline: TCS to begin operations in Visakhapatnam in 90 days, says minister Nara Lokesh
description: Nara Lokesh said that TCS setting up a facility in Visakhapatnam would see the port city turning into an IT and technology hub.
content:
Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) will soon set up a facility in Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, Nara Lokesh, state IT and Electronics Minister, told The Indian Express on Wednesday. The process to identify land for the tech company to set up a permanent facility is on, Lokesh added.
“It will be a 10,000-people campus. It may take two to three years to construct a permanent building. To start with, they (TCS) are renting out a building. The company is expected to begin operations in 90 days,” Lokesh said.
Lokesh said this was the beginning of turning the port city into an IT and technology hub.
Innovations like AI and big data are being introduced in the IT sector and necessary cooperation will be extended to start-ups through the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub, Lokesh said. The state government is looking to create at least 5 lakh jobs in the IT sector in five years and is expecting other tech companies seeking to expand to set up their facilities at Visakhapatnam, he added.
Meanwhile, after visiting the World Economic Forum at Davos, Switzerland, Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu said Visakhapatnam will witness an IT revolution once TCS establishes its unit there.
At Davos, Naidu had asked Thomas Kurian, Chief Executive Officer, Google Cloud, to examine the possibilities of establishing a design centre in Visakhapatnam for developing chips used in servers. Naidu also asked Kurian to set up a manufacturing unit in Andhra Pradesh to integrate its server supply chain to make the state the headquarters for server maintenance services.
Google Cloud, the third-largest cloud provider globally, has already established two cloud regions in Delhi and Mumbai. It recently signed an MoU with the Andhra Pradesh government to set up a Data City in Visakhapatnam and artificial intelligence (AI) applications while fostering skill development opportunities for local youth.

headline: Students struggle to reach JEE exam centre in Pune due to traffic
description: An aspirant from Solapur said, "I have walked nearly a kilometer from Ramtekdi road to reach the centre because of heavy traffic."
content:
By Sonali Priya, and Abhijit Sherekar
Students appearing for the Joint Entrance Exam (JEE) Mains in Pune had to struggle to reach their examination centre at Ion Digital Zone in Ramtekdi due to narrow roads and heavy traffic.
Paper 1 (BE/ BTech) of the exam was held on January 22, 23, 24, 28, and the last paper is scheduled to be held on Wednesday. The exam is held in two shifts, morning and afternoon. The Indian Express visited the exam centre on January 24 and 28 to speak to students and parents about the difficulties they faced while arriving at the centre.
The exam centre is located around 1.5km off the Pune-Solapur highway towards the Ramtekdi industrial area, where thousands of students appear in each shift. The road to reach the centre passes through the JCC Colony slum, where a massive number of private vehicles dropping exam takers caused bumper-to-bumper traffic jams. This meant students had to get off their vehicles and walk through the narrow roads to reach the centre on time, adding to stress before an already stressful exam.
An aspirant from Solapur said, “I have walked nearly a kilometer from Ramtekdi road to reach the centre because of heavy traffic.” Similarly, Pratyusha Naik, another aspirant, said, “Due to traffic, my parents parked the car away from the centre so we had to walk around 500-600 metres to arrive at the centre.”
Vijay Pawar, who had come to drop a relative for the exam, said, “I was stuck for at least 30-45 minutes in the traffic. Then I had to park my vehicle and walk to the centre. They should block the movement of other vehicles when the exam is going on.”
A official of the National Testing Agency at the venue said, “Traffic is not our concern. We are responsible for an error-free and smooth conduct of examination. Along with everyone else, we too are facing the problem of increased traffic.”

Deputy Commissioner of Police (traffic) Amol Zende told The Indian Express that more traffic personnel would be deployed for the last day of Paper 1 and for the upcoming Paper 2 to ensure better traffic flow.

headline: At Patparganj poll rally Rahul Gandhi attacks AAP: ‘Sisodia ran away after liquor scam’
description: In Patparganj, Rahul urged voters to back Congress candidate Anil Chaudhary, claiming that the sitting MLA, AAP’s Manish Sisodia, had “run away” after being implicated as the “architect of the liquor scam”.
content:
Crowds thronged the streets of Patparganj and Okhla on Tuesday as Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi addressed Maha Jan Sabhas, rallying support for Congress candidates ahead of the February 5 elections.
In his speeches, Rahul took on Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the BJP, and the AAP. While he accused the BJP of fostering division and promoting a culture of hate and fear, he labelled the AAP as a corrupt party, which has failed the people of Delhi. Reiterating his Bharat Jodo Yatra slogan ‘Nafrat ke bazaar mein, mohabbat ki dukan’, Rahul said, “We don’t want an India of hatred, fear, and violence, but an India of love, harmony, and brotherhood.”
In Patparganj, Rahul urged voters to back Congress candidate Anil Chaudhary, claiming that the sitting MLA, AAP’s Manish Sisodia, had “run away” after being implicated as the “architect of the liquor scam”.
Sisodia, who switched his seat from Patparganj to Jangpura this year, was the Deputy Chief Minister till 2022. He resigned weeks after being arrested by the ED and the CBI in relation to the excise policy case in 2023.

Referring to the Ram Temple inauguration, Rahul said, “At the Ram Mandir consecration, not a single poor person was present. The richest of the rich were invited, but the President, an Adivasi woman, was not present.”
Rahul alleged that Modi was prioritising interests of powerful billionaires over the welfare of the citizens. “(Industrialist Gautam) Adani gets all the airport contracts. GST money doesn’t go to farmers, small shopowners, or street vendors — it goes to the billionaires,” he claimed.
He criticised policies like the Agnipath scheme, arguing that it stripped soldiers of their pensions while enriching the wealthy. Speaking on unemployment, he told the gathering, “You send your children to college to secure jobs, but in today’s India, even a degree doesn’t guarantee employment. Meanwhile, the children of billionaires can dream and achieve anything.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In his address, Chaudhary sought to connect with Purvanchali voters of Patparganj by raising slogans of ‘Chatti Maiyya ki jai’.
In Okhla, asking the crowd to vote for the Congress, Rahul reminded them of the party’s 2024 Lok Sabha performance. “No matter who fears Narendra Modi, we will not. He no longer talks about his 56-inch chest because we have exposed the reality behind their claims of 400-paar, we proved them to be false in the Lok Sabha elections.”
The Congress-led INDIA bloc alliance had won 235 seats, of which 99 were won by the Congress in the 2024 polls.
Okhla Congress candidate and MCD councillor Ariba Khan highlighted AAP’s unfulfilled promises and the lack of development in the constituency.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
She recited Faiz Ahmed Faiz’s poetry — “Ae khak nashino uth baitho wo waqt kareeb aa gaya hai, jab takht uchale jayenge, jab taj uchale jayenge (O downtrodden, wake up, the time has come when thrones will be toppled, when crowns will fall)”.
The two rallies marked Rahul’s second and third appearances in the Capital’s campaign trail, following his January 13 rally in Seelampur. He had then accused both Modi and Kejriwal of making false promises, drawing parallels between the two leaders. The Seelampur rally had also signaled a shift in Congress’s strategy, with Rahul openly opposing AAP, an INDIA bloc ally, after failed alliance talks for the Assembly elections.
However, Rahul’s campaign was disrupted by ill health in the days that followed. He missed four events, including a January 20 rally alongside Congress candidate Sandeep Dikshit and a January 24 rally in Sadar Bazar.
At the Patparganj rally, people climbed up barricades, chairs, and nearby buildings for a glimpse of Rahul, with chants of ‘Mohar lagega haath pe’ and ‘Button dabega haath pe’ echoing through the air.

In Okhla, residents cheered as Rahul made his way to the stage. After the rally, the streets came alive with celebration as supporters danced and waved Congress posters.

headline: Gandhinagar: Upset with his relationship with their mother, two brothers stab mason to death, say police
description: Police said the duo had also planned to kill their mother but were arrested before they could execute their plans.
content:
It was a Sunday. Ratanji Chhanaji Thakor, a mason, left home in Kalol taluka of Gandhinagar district around 8.30-9 am for his job site along with his associate, Jakuji Maganji Parmar.
After a few hours, around 12 pm, Ratanji’s sister came rushing to his son Ajay and told him that his father had been attacked by an acquaintance at his work site. On reaching the spot, Ajay was shocked to see the condition his father was in: blood draining out of his head, his intestines pulled out. He was dead.
Based on CCTV footage, police arrested the two accused the same day – January 26. Identified as brothers Sanjay alias Manga Amaraji Thakor (27) and Jayeshji Amaraji Thakor (23), police said they had killed Ratanji because they were angry about his relationship with their mother.
Police said the duo had also planned to kill their mother but were arrested before they could execute their plans.

The FIR, filed at Kalol taluka police station, based on a complaint by Ajay, stated that Ratanji and Jakuji along with three labourers were working at the site when the two brothers  arrived there.Sanjay first struck Thakor several times on the head till he began bleeding and collapsed to the ground. He then allegedly pulled out a knife and stabbed Ratanji in the head and in  stomach. When Jakuji attempted to rush to the aid of his partner, Sanjay allegedly warned him that he would meet a similar fate. The two men then fled on a motorbike. They were booked for murder and arrested the same day from Kalol town, said police inspector (PI) Unnati S Patel of Kalol taluka police station.
Gandhinagar SP Ravi Teja Vasamsetty said, “The two accused had, after murdering Thakor, also planned to murder their own mother. However, this was thwarted by their timely arrest.”When the police interrogated the accused brothers, they learned that their mother had allegedly been in a relationship with Ratanji for over 15 years. The parents of the accused often used to fight over this issue, police said.
PI Patel said, “The two accused had also planned to kill their mother but after a recent fight in the house, she had gone to her parents’ home around three days before the incident. This, coupled with the arrest of both her sons, prevented her killing.”

headline: The troubled past of Chandrabhan Sanap
description: Chandrabhan Sanap, the man acquitted by the Supreme Court on Tuesday after being found not guilty in a rape-and-murder case, has a history marked by repeated brushes with the law. The court’s decision to acquit Sanap was based on gaps in the prosecution’s case, but his criminal background stretches back years, with multiple FIRs filed […]
content:
Chandrabhan Sanap, the man acquitted by the Supreme Court on Tuesday after being found not guilty in a rape-and-murder case, has a history marked by repeated brushes with the law. The court’s decision to acquit Sanap was based on gaps in the prosecution’s case, but his criminal background stretches back years, with multiple FIRs filed against him before his arrest in 2014.
A resident of Nashik, Sanap led a life filled with instability and frequent conflicts with the law. At the time of his arrest in 2014 for the murder, he was 29 and working as a coolie at various railway stations. His criminal activities ranged from petty crimes like mobile theft and bag-lifting to more serious offenses. Police records show that Sanap had multiple cases filed against him across several locations, including Madhya Pradesh, Nashik and Mumbai’s Gamdevi.
“His criminal activities eventually led to his arrest and a seven-month stint in a Madhya Pradesh jail, prior to his arrest by Mumbai police in the rape and murder case involving the techie,” said an officer involved in the case.
Sanap’s personal life was equally turbulent. He had been married three times—his first wife passed away, and his second wife left him. At the time of the case, he was living with his third wife and their 14-month-old son. After being interrogated by Kurla GRP officials in connection with the case, Sanap chose to relocate to Nashik in 2014. In addition to his work as a coolie, he also worked briefly as a driver.
“He moved to Nashik after being questioned by the police in 2014. It was a decision fuelled by the investigation into the case,” an officer recalled.

headline: Woman claims to be sole witness to Bengaluru Carlton Towers fire to siphon Rs 6 crore, arrested
description: The Bengaluru Central Crime Branch police have arrested the woman’s husband and an associate as well in the case, in which the victim is a businessman who was previously acquainted with her.
content:
A woman has been arrested for allegedly defrauding a businessman out of Rs 6 crore after claiming to be the sole witness of the 2010 Carlton Towers fire tragedy in Bengaluru and that she would get Rs 25 crore from the building’s owner if she withdrew her testimony.
B Dayananda, Commissioner of Police, on Tuesday announced the arrests of Rekha, 38; her husband Manjunath, 40; and their associate Chetan, 35, in the case.
The Central Crime Branch (CCB) police said Rekha, a BSc graduate, orchestrated the scam, while Manjunath, an MBA graduate and businessman, and Chetan, a financial advisor, assisted her in executing the plot.
According to the police, the trio approached the businessman claiming to be a witness to the Carlton Towers fire tragedy, in which nine people died. The businessman was previously acquainted with Rekha, who had presented herself as someone offering loans, the police said.

Rekha allegedly claimed that the Carlton Towers owner’s Rs 6-crore bank deposit had been frozen owing to action by the Income Tax Department and the Enforcement Directorate. To help “release” this amount, the trio asked the businessman for an initial loan of Rs 7 lakh, with assurances of repayment once the account was unfrozen.
“The trio proposed a deal, promising the victim a 2:1 return—offering Rs 2 crore for every Rs 1 crore he invested to help release the money,” a police officer said.
The trio convinced the businessman that the Carlton Towers owner had offered Rs 25 crore in return for withdrawing her testimony in court. Over time, he was manipulated into paying Rs 6 crore for alleged clearance charges and other expenses, according to the police.

Rekha was arrested on January 16 from a paying guest facility near Hoskote. The police said she confessed to the crime and revealed the involvement of her husband and Chetan, following which they arrested Manjunath at the couple’s home in KR Puram and Chetan in Hassan.
Further investigation revealed that Rekha had defrauded several others by offering loans. In one instance, she allegedly extorted Rs 31 lakh from a man through video call blackmail. The police also discovered that she had ignored multiple court summons related to cheque bounce cases.
The police said they uncovered transactions totaling Rs 24 crore between 2022 and 2024 in Rekha’s bank accounts. Investigations into other accounts linked to the accused are ongoing, they added.

headline: D K Shivakumar seeks report from BWSSB on ‘inevitable’ water tariff hike in Bengaluru, cites loss of Rs 1,000 crore per year
description: Bengaluru residents will see their water bills increase for the first time since 2014 if the Karnataka government goes ahead with the proposed hike.
content:
The Karnataka government has sought a report from the Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB) over the proposed “inevitable” water tariff hike in Bengaluru city limits, Deputy Chief Minister and Bengaluru Development Minister D K Shivakumar said Tuesday. If the proposal is implemented, Bengaluru residents will see their water bill increase for the first time since 2014.
“I have directed officials to submit a report on the water tariff hike. A decision will be taken soon,” Shivakumar said following a meeting with Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP), Bangalore Development Authority (BDA), BWSSB and Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA) officials.
As water bills have not been revised for more than 10 years, BWSSB was incurring losses of Rs 1,000 crore per year. “The electricity bill of BWSSB has increased from Rs 35 crore to Rs 75 crore (between 2014 and 2025),” he said, estimating the losses due to non-revision of water tariff at around Rs 85 crore per month.
Shivakumar said that the hike had “become inevitable”. “The Board is finding it difficult to raise funds as banks are refusing to lend loans due to the losses,” he said. Previously, Shivakumar blamed “political reasons” for not revising fares for over a decade.
He said a decision was yet to be made on the quantum of the water tariff hike. “It will be decided after detailed deliberations,” he said. For the poor, he said a token charge of at least one paise per litre would be applied to help BWSSB accurately measure the amount of water supplied to the city.
This was not the first time Shivakumar talked about the impending water tariff hike. In August, while launching the ‘Cauvery Water at Your Doorstep’ campaign, he highlighted that there had been no water tariff hike in the city for years, placing immense strain on BWSSB’s finances.
Defending the water tariff increase, he said, “Our government has reduced electricity tariffs. This situation arises from the rising prices of petrol and diesel. Additionally, employees receive an extra dearness allowance (DA). However, the Board’s employees are currently facing issues due to unpaid salaries.” Asked about the one-time settlement scheme in BWSSB, he said, “It is being deliberated, and I have instructed officials to look into it.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He also stated that the government had set aside Rs 20 crore to provide water to slums and urban poor, but the BJP had stopped that scheme. “We will restart that scheme. The water supplied to the poor also needs to be measured even if a token amount is charged. The water supplied to slums is being misused in many places. We have formulated a plan to collect accurate information on water consumption across the city. Illegal connections must be regularised,” he said.
Shivakumar details preparations for summer in Bengaluru
Shivakumar mentioned that the officials have been instructed to expedite filling up tanks to charge groundwater in the city in the run-up to the summer. “We have instructed officials to ensure there is no water shortage in Bengaluru this summer,” he said.
On the recently inaugurated Cauvery 5th stage water supply project, he said 15,000 new connections were provided following its implementation. “We are providing 20,000 more connections,” he said. According to Shivakumar, many apartment complexes were not taking the Cauvery water connection. “All of them have been told to take water connections mandatorily,” he said.
He also noted, “The government has spent money for public use, but many have taken illegal connections to avoid deposits and fees. The government has taken strong action to prevent illegal connections. Officials are visiting every house and apartment complex to urge people to take Cauvery water connection.”

headline: ‘Why not forgive loans of middle class?’: Kejriwal urges PM Modi to stop loan waivers for BJP’s ‘billionaire friends’
description: Former Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal says income tax and GST rates can be halved, the taxable income limit doubled and GST on essentials abolished if corporate loan waivers are stopped.
content:
Ahead of the Delhi Assembly polls, AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal launched an attack on the BJP-led central government on Tuesday for waiving loans of its “billionaire friends” and demanded a halt to the practice, adding that such a move could transform the country’s economic landscape.
Showing a letter he has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, he told reporters, “Today I wrote a letter to the prime minister on a very important issue. In the letter, I have told the prime minister that the BJP-led central government is spending money from the government treasury on the country’s billionaires. Whichever billionaire friend they want to be kind to, they give him money from the government and waive off that loan in two or three years. In the last five years, the central government has waived loans of 400-500 such billionaires worth Rs 10 lakh crore.”
“On one hand, the poor and middle class of the country are struggling with daily inflation and on the other hand, the entire treasury of the Centre has been opened for 400-500 billionaires. Just a few days ago, it was published in the newspapers that one of his friends had a debt of Rs 47,000 crore, out of which Rs 46,000 crore was waived off. Another one had a debt of Rs 6,000 crore, out of which Rs 5,000 crore was waived off,” he added.
In his letter, Kejriwal called on the prime minister to either pass a law or make a public declaration to end the loan waivers for billionaires. The AAP chief said that stopping these corporate loan waivers could transform the country’s economic landscape. He proposed halving the income tax and GST rates, doubling the taxable income limit, and abolishing GST on essential food items—measures that he said would be feasible if the loan waivers for billionaires are stopped.

Kejriwal highlighted the tax burden on the common man. “A middle-class individual who earns Rs 12 lakh annually is burdened with so many taxes imposed by the central government. They pay income tax, GST, service tax, property tax, education cess, capital gains tax, road tax, and more. When all these taxes are combined, a person earning Rs 12 lakh ends up paying at least 6 lakh in taxes—half of their income—to the government. And what do they get in return? Nothing. Absolutely nothing,” he said.
Kejriwal added, “When such a person sees that despite paying Rs 6 lakh in taxes every year, this money is being funnelled to billionaires, they feel betrayed and deeply hurt.”

headline: Chandigarh tells hotels: ‘Don’t add service charge in bill of customers, it’s voluntary’
description: Restaurants in Chandigarh were reportedly found collecting service charge from customers apart from total price of food items mentioned in menu.
content:
Next time you dine out at a restaurant in Chandigarh, make sure you are not levied service charge in the bill. For, the Chandigarh administration has issued a directive to hotels and restaurants mandating that they shall not add service charge automatically in the bill nor collect it under any other name from consumers.
Restaurants in the Union Territory were reportedly found collecting service charge from customers in addition to the total price of the food items mentioned in the menu and applicable taxes, often in the guise of some other fee or charge. The practice was allegedly followed by eating outlets without informing consumers that paying such charge is voluntary and optional.
“No hotel or restaurant shall force a consumer to pay service charge and shall clearly inform the consumer that service charge is voluntary, optional and at consumer’s discretion. And no restriction on entry or provision of services based on collection of service charge shall be imposed on consumers. Service charge shall not be collected by adding it along with the food bill and levying GST on the total amount,” Chandigarh administration specified.
“Further, It has also been noticed that some customers have been paying tips to the waiters in addition to service charges under the mistaken impression that service charge is a part of taxes,” the UT said in a statement.
As per the guidelines issued by Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, Service Charge cannot be added in the bill involuntarily, without allowing consumers the choice or discretion to decide whether they want to pay such charge or not.
In public interest, Chandigarh administration also sent out a message to people.
What can be done if service charge is levied
In case a hotel or restaurant has imposed a service charge in violation of the guidelines, the administration said that a consumer may make a request to the hotel or restaurant concerned
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
to remove service charge from the bill amount. The person can lodge a complaint on the Consumer Helpline, which works as an alternative dispute redressal mechanism at the pre-litigation level, by dialling 1915 or WhatsApp number 8800001915 or through the NCH mobile app, the Chandigarh administration stated.
Consumers can file a complaint against unfair trade practice with the Consumer Commission, it was specified.
The complaint can also be filed through www.e-jagriti.gov.in for its speedy and effective redressal and submit a complaint to the CCPA by e-mail at com-ccpa@nic.in.
Besides, the aggrieved person can also approach the Department of Food & Supplies and Consumer Affairs and Legal Metrology, UT, Chandigarh, through helpline number 0172-2703956 or email at fcs-chd@nic.in for subsequent proceeding by the CCPA.

headline: ‘Weakness in legs, could not get up’: Patients, their families on Guillain-Barré Syndrome
description: Guillain-Barré Syndrome is a rare neurological disorder in which a person's immune system attacks the peripheral nervous system.
content:
Sharayu Bankar had a bout of loose motion and had to be taken to a hospital when he felt extreme weakness in his legs. The 26-year-old resident of Manik Baug in Sinhagad area, diagnosed with Guillain-Barré Syndrome, was admitted to the hospital for five days.
“I just could not get up and my brother took me to Poona Hospital,” Bankar said.
Bankar got a five-day course of Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IV-IG) and was discharged on January 24. Similarly, Pramod Garud, a lawyer, was grateful his son Harshad, 37, who was diagnosed with Guillain-Barré Syndrome, was able to recover within five days and was discharged from Poona Hospital on January 25.
“My son had fever for a day or two and then weakness. But on January 19, when he did not feel better with medicines and felt a sudden weakness in his limbs, we were alerted and took him to the hospital. Initially we thought it must be a chikungunya viral infection but it was shocking when he simply could not move,” said Garud.
After five days of the medication and physiotherapy, Garud’s son was discharged and was slowly recovering. Bankar too said that he underwent physiotherapy and while his right leg was a little weak, he was feeling much better.
GBS is a rare neurological disorder in which a person’s immune system attacks the peripheral nervous system. Some cases are mild and others can lead to paralysis and can be life threatening, according to doctors. According to Maharashtra health department data, there are 111 persons who are clinically diagnosed with GBS and multiple tests are being conducted to confirm the diagnosis.
Field visits were conducted by National Institute of Virology and surveillance teams from Pune Municipal Corporation at the affected sites. Public health preventive measures like verifying chlorine content of water supplied by water tankers to housing societies was also undertaken. Of 25,578 homes surveyed till January 26, health department officials have identified 146 persons with acute diarrhoea and dysentery.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Patients have been undergoing treatment across 25 hospitals in Pune including 26 at Deenanath Mangeshkar Hospital, 21 at Sassoon General Hospital, nine at Kashibai Navale Hospital, seven at Sahyadri Super Speciality Hospital, Deccan, five at Poona Hospital and Research Centre, and four each at YCM and Bharati Hospital. The remaining patients are scattered across different hospitals.
Dr Sudhir Kothari, consulting neurologist at Poona Hospital and Research Centre, said that some patients have recovered and been discharged. Dr Sayali Kalbhor, senior resident in neurology at Poona hospital pointed out some of the patients were admitted for a week or so and are recovering well.
According to the latest data, authorities at Navale Hospital said 12 patients were admitted. Director Dr Arvind Bhore said that four patients required ventilator support and they were being managed.

headline: BJP councillor’s husband is AAP Kirari candidate, party expels her, four others for ‘indiscipline’
description: All four leaders have been suspended for six years for alleged indiscipline after, senior leaders maintained, “all efforts to make them see reason” and pacify them, failed.
content:
Taking the expulsion route to stamp out rebellion within its ranks, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Monday showed four leaders, including the wife of an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) candidate, the door with days to go for the Delhi Assembly elections.
Former Delhi BJP Mahila Morcha president Poonam Parashar Jha was among those expelled. Her husband Anil Jha, who recently joined the AAP, has been fielded from Kirari. The BJP has termed this a breach of party discipline.
Three other leaders — Vinay Chaudhri, Vikas Tyagi, and Sunil Kukreja — were removed from the primary membership of the BJP for choosing to contest as Independent candidates against the party’s picks from their respective seats.
All four leaders have been suspended for six years for alleged indiscipline after, senior leaders maintained, “all efforts to make them see reason” and pacify them, failed. Following the announcement of Kapil Mishra’s candidature from Karawal Nagar, considered a stronghold of five-time BJP MLA Mohan Singh Bisht, the latter had announced his decision to contest independently from the seat terming the party’s decision “a mistake”. Bisht was, a day later, accommodated as the BJP’s candidate from Mustafabad.
“The party has counseled and convinced innumerable karyakartas over issues ranging from ticket distribution to the fielding of candidates from outside since last month; such leaders have been told that this is a crucial time and the issues that they have brought to notice can always be ironed out later,” a senior leader said. “However, when all such efforts failed in some cases, a decision had to be made. We are also identifying other karyakartas who may have breached party discipline,” the leader added.
Jha, who was with the BJP for over three decades during which she held several organisational posts, said, “I was shocked when I was told (of the party’s decision)…I have been with the BJP since childhood and contested my first election in the year 2002. What is my fault if the AAP reached out to my husband and asked him to join? Now, when the wind is blowing in his favour in the seat (Kirari) owing to his personal connect, I am being penalised for it despite the BJP’s emphasis on mahila sashaktikaran (women empowerment).”
Chaudhuri, who is contesting as an Independent candidate from Shahdara, said, “I was not even told that I was expelled…there is a way to convince someone like me who has been with the party for as many as 12 years if they are having issues. There is no problem that we have with the senior leadership of the party – the PM, the national president or the HM – all this is the doing of the party’s local leaders who are targetting me.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Kukreja, who is contesting independently from Jangpura, said, “No one from the party informed me; I had, in fact, tendered my resignation on December 16 itself because I cannot remain in the party after it decided to field someone who has publicly assaulted BJP workers from the same seat that they have now been fielded from. I will take this matter to court.”
Tyagi, contesting from Rohtas Nagar, said, “I do not care about the party’s decision; I am contesting the elections on my own.”

headline: Rs 1,000 for women in Punjab figures in pre-budget discussions
description: A senior officer said if at all the scheme is implemented in Punjab, it will be only be for non income tax payees.
content:
Ahead of the annual Punjab budget and amid Delhi Assembly elections, where Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) supremo Arvind Kejriwal is promising Rs 2,100 per month for women, a similar promise of Rs 1,000 made in Punjab before the 2022 Assembly elections has now become a key topic of discussion for the upcoming budget.
The Punjab government is currently preparing the budget, which will be tabled in the Vidhan Sabha session next month. Sources in the government revealed that with Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann being questioned by the media in Delhi about whether Punjab would fulfil this promise, pressure is mounting on the finance department to arrange funds for the scheme.
A senior government official said, “Discussions are certainly on. However, we are fund-starved. We are collecting data on income tax payees and other women voters. If at all, the scheme is implemented, it will only be extended to non-income-tax-paying women. However, as of now, it seems impossible. It remains to be seen how much we can pay, but income tax payees will definitely not be included.”
Also Read | In Our Opinion: 5 things to watch out for in the Budget
He added that, in any case, the government would need to allocate funds for this scheme in next year’s budget. “Next year will be the last budget of the current dispensation, as elections are due in early 2027, and we won’t be able to table the budget then. Questions are being raised now, and we are exploring if it can be implemented this year. We are trying hard.”
Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann recently told the media in Delhi that the monthly allowance for women would be rolled out in the next budget (2025-26). “All eyes are on us now,” he said. Mann had previously announced during the Lok Sabha elections in June last year that the allowance would be increased to Rs 1,100 from the Rs 1,000 promised earlier. He claimed that the file related to the scheme was on his table, but he couldn’t approve it due to the code of conduct. He assured that the file would be signed once the elections were over. However, Punjab’s financial constraints have delayed its implementation.
The state’s financial condition remains precarious. The government struggled to pay employee salaries before September 4 last year. Subsequently, it withdrew a Rs 1,500 crore subsidy introduced by former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi, hiked VAT on petrol and diesel, and increased bus fares. Non-payment of the Rs 1,000 monthly allowance was a major issue during the Lok Sabha elections, with voters questioning AAP candidates about the delay.

While the AAP government has improved revenue collection in excise and GST, it has fallen short on its sand mining revenue projections. Before the Punjab Assembly elections, AAP claimed it would generate Rs 20,000 crore from sand mining. However, it has only managed to earn Rs 527 crore over the last two fiscal years—Rs 247 crore in 2022-23 and Rs 300 crore in 2023-24. The projected revenue from sand mining for the current fiscal year is also Rs 300 crore.

Of Punjab’s total budget, 23 per cent is allocated for debt repayment and interest, 57.5 per cent for salaries and pensions, and 25.14 per cent for the power subsidy.
In a recent report on the Fiscal Health Index (FHI) for 2022-23 by NITI Aayog, Punjab was ranked the lowest among all states, with the worst FHI in the country. The report highlighted Punjab’s poor performance in “quality of expenditure” (spending heavily on non-development activities), “fiscal prudence” (reliance on independent revenue generation), and “debt index” (high revenue expenditure on debt repayment).

headline: Valedictory Function of the ‘Paschim Maharashtra Space on Wheels’ Program at COEP Technological University
description: It featured quizzes, poster-making, essay-writing, science exhibitions, and interactive sessions with ISRO scientists, offering students hands-on learning experiences.
content:
The Space on Wheels initiative, a collaborative outreach programme of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and Vijnana Bharati (VIBHA), concluded with a valedictory function at COEP Technological University Auditorium in Pune on Monday.
The Space on Wheels initiative showcased ISRO’s achievements, including models of satellites, launch vehicles, and missions like Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan, and Gaganyaan, while highlighting the societal benefits of satellite applications in navigation, communication, and remote sensing. It featured quizzes, poster-making, essay-writing, science exhibitions, and interactive sessions with ISRO scientists, offering students hands-on learning experiences.
The programme saw over 4,15,520 visitors from across seven districts of Western Maharashtra, including Pune, Nashik, Ahilyanagar, Solapur, Sangli, Kolhapur, and Satara in attendance. The Space on Wheels mobile exhibition showcased ISRO’s technological advancements in space science and provided a platform to educate and engage students, teachers, and the public with interactive exhibits, activities, and competitions.
At the beginning of the programme, the bus Space on Wheels was given a grand welcome in the premises of COEP, with the sound of drums and conch shells. It was also showered with flowers by drones. On this occasion, floral tributes were paid to the statue of M. Visvesvaraya.
Dr Prakash Chauhan, director of National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) and chief guest of the ceremony said, “The visionary dream of Dr Vikram Sarabhai, the father of Indian space science, who had a vision for space science and believed that space science would change the lives of masses, has been fulfilled. Today, all of our lives have been fulfilled.”

Dr Chauhan also highlighted India’s remarkable journey from economic challenges during Sarabhai’s era to becoming a space science leader. He said, “ISRO’s achievements, such as Chandrayaan, have captivated public interest while improving lives through satellite applications in weather forecasting, agriculture, disaster management, and more.” He expressed optimism about India’s future space missions, including Gaganyaan and Venus exploration, underscoring the importance of initiatives like ‘Space on Wheels’ in bringing space science closer to people.
National organisation secretary of Vigyan Bharati, Dr Shivkumar Sharma, stated, “The Space on Wheels programme successfully raised awareness about space science, inspiring curiosity and encouraging questions among citizens. Teachers play a vital role in fostering inquiry and guiding students to find answers. ISRO’s achievements not only reach the skies but also connect deeply with the grassroots.”

headline: Shiv Sena to hold interviews to reconstitute its Mumbai executive ahead of municipal polls
