headline: On ground check: Mann visits 2 govt complexes, assures smooth delivery of citizen-centric services
description: In Mansa, Mann directed the officials concerned to streamline operations, ensure prompt public services, and install high-speed Internet there.
content:
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Tuesday conducted surprise inspections at the newly constructed Cheema Sub-Tehsil Complex in Sangrur’s Cheema and Sardulgarh Tehsil Complex in Mansa, to ensure smooth delivery of citizen-centric services at grassroots level.
During his visit at the Cheema complex, Mann interacted with the people, who responded with lauding his government for focusing on improving the service delivery.
Emphasising that the inspections were only to enhance efficiency, Mann said: “The people of the state are witnessing, for the first time, that a chief minister is visiting government offices to ensure effective service delivery.”
“The state’s top priority is to resolve people’s daily administrative tasks, without any hassle,” the CM said, while directing government officials to perform their duties diligently and ensure that the citizens do not face unnecessary delay in services.
Reviewing the upcoming mela in memory of Sant Baba Attar Singh, the CM also directed the officials to make foolproof arrangements for the pilgrims, while assuring that he would monitor the preparations personally.
In Mansa, Mann directed the officials concerned to streamline operations, ensure prompt public services, and install high-speed Internet there.
Reiterating the Punjab government’s focus on health, education, power, employment, and infrastructure, Mann said that “efforts are being made to rejuvenate the development of the state, which was neglected by the previous administrations”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Due to our efforts, Punjab schools are being renovated, new roads are constructed, youths are hired for government jobs — overall development is visible in every sector,” the CM said, while announcing that a regular tehsildar will soon be appointed at the Sardulgarh complex. He also directed the installation of high-speed Internet to improve office efficiency.
During his visit to an under-construction 20-bedded hospital in the region, Mann said that the project — scheduled to be completed by June 30 — will serve as a key healthcare facility.
Support to US deportees
On the recent deportation of Punjabis from the US, Mann said that the state government supports those affected and will provide them rehabilitation. “We will provide opportunities for them to rebuild their lives, with guidance from young entrepreneurs who have overcome similar hardships,” he said.
Three US military planes (C-17 Globemaster) landed in Amritsar this month so far, deporting Indians as part of the Trump administration’s promised crackdown on illegal migration, with the latest one on Sunday night. The deportees have alleged that despite paying huge amounts to travel agents, they were made to travel to the US illegally, without their knowledge. They now seek strict action against the agents.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On February 5, a US military aircraft carrying the first batch of 104 illegal Indian immigrants — including 33 each from Haryana and Gujarat, 30 (Punjab), three each from Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra, and two from Chandigarh — landed in Amritsar. In the second batch of 116 deportees, 65 were from Punjab, 33 (Haryana), eight (Gujarat), two each from Uttar Pradesh, Goa, Maharashtra and Rajasthan, and one each from Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir. The third batch had 112 deportees, including 44 from Haryana, 33 (Gujarat), 31 (Punjab), two (Uttar Pradesh), and one each from Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh.

headline: Vice-principal and students of Karnataka law college arrested for leaking questions online
description: M V Nagaraj, vice-principal of Basavashree College of Law in Kolar, says he was unaware that the question paper was being sold online by his students.
content:
A vice-principal and two students of a law college in Karnataka’s Kolar city were arrested for leaking a question paper on WhatsApp and Telegram in return for money, the Bengaluru police said on Tuesday.
Commissioner of Police B Dayananda identified the arrested accused as M V Nagaraj, vice-principal of Basavashree College of Law; Jagadish, a student of the college; and Varun Kumar, who is a student of the college as well as the vice principal’s car driver.
According to the police, Nagaraj, who was the custodian of the question paper, received it a week before the examination. He allegedly shared it with Jagadish and Varun, who offered to sell the questions on WhatsApp and Telegram groups.
However, the questions from the Contract-1 exam came to the notice of vigilance squad member Ravindra Rajpoot, who forwarded it to squad chairman Vishwanatha K N for verification. He lodged a complaint with the Bengaluru city police’s Central Crime Branch on January 30.
A police officer said, “During the interrogation, Nagaraj claimed that he had leaked the question paper but not for monetary gain. He said he leaked the question paper to increase the pass percentage of the college and to help some students pass. He claimed that he was unaware that it was being sold by his students.”
“Further investigation is underway to ascertain if anyone else was involved in the leaks,” the police officer added.

headline: Amid deportation By US, HC gives Punjab 30 days to act against illegal travel agents
description: Bench disposes of a plea seeking emigration check posts in all districts of Punjab and an upgraded list of certified agents
content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has asked the Punjab government to decide on a representation seeking action against illegal travel agents duping people by illegally sending them abroad.
A bench of Chief Justice Sheel Nagu and Justice Harmeet Singh Grewal passed the direction Monday (February 17) while disposing of a public interest litigation (PIL) that establishment of “emigration check posts” in all districts of the state, an upgraded list of “certified recruiting agents” and stricter action against unauthorised travel agents involved in “human smuggling”.
The bench directed the petitioner, Advocate Kanwar Pahul Singh, to submit a representation to the authorities concerned, which must be decided within 30 days.
The observed that the matter fell under the jurisdiction of the competent authority under the Emigration Act, 1983, and refrained from making any comments on the merits of the case. “The grievance alleged is of rampant illegal immigrants being sent abroad through illegal means in violation of certain provisions of the Emigration Act, 1983,” the bench noted.
The petitioner, appearing in person, sought directions to the Union of India and others to set up emigration check posts under the Emigration Act, 1983, to streamline the migration process and prevent incidents such as the recent deportation of illegal immigrants from the United States.
He also sought an updated list of certified recruiting agents and permitted foreign employers “in order to prevent people of Punjab from becoming the victim of such con/fake travel agents in future”.
Submitting that the recent deportation of illegal immigrants of India by the USA, caused losses of crores of rupees to the people of Punjab, he urged the court to order a crackdown on illegal travel agents operating in Punjab under the Punjab Prevention of Human Smuggling Act, 2012.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Direct respondents to identify, find and take immediate action against all ‘fake/con travel agents,’ who are not having a license to run business in the territory of State of Punjab,” he contended.
Appearing for the Union government, Additional Solicitor General of India Satya Pal Jain, along with Advocate Dheeraj Jain, opposed the plea.
Advocate Jain contended that many of the immigrants had left the country for European countries on study or tourist visas and then illegally entered the US.
The counsel said the Protector of Emigrants in Chandigarh has forwarded a total of 127 complaints over the unscrupulous agents to the Punjab government for action in the past year. Of the complaints, 57 were received from victims, he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The court, while disposing of the petition, directed that the representation be decided within 30 days. “If done, within a period of 30 days, [the representation] shall be considered and decided by respondents…as expeditiously as possible by passing a speaking order and the outcome shall be communicated to the petitioner,” the court ordered.
Notably, after the first batch of 104 illegal Indian immigrants -, including 31 from Punjab, were deported from the US on February 5, the Punjab Police formed a special investigation team to probe the issue of illegal human trafficking. Two more batches of 116 and 112 deportees arrived on February 15 and 16, respectively. They included 65 from Punjab in the second batch and 31 in the third batch.

headline: Gujarat local body polls: As counting begins, BJP leads from the front
description: As counting for 1,677 seats in 66 municipalities in Gujarat began on Tuesday, the BJP won the Halol and Wankaner municipalities.
content:
Counting commenced for 1,677 seats in 66 municipalities in Gujarat on Tuesday, with with 167 seats out of the total 1844 seats being won uncontested ahead of the February 16 polls.
While the BJP, which has emerged in the lead in at least eight municipalities, won 162 seats uncontested before the February 16 elections, the Congress won one seat uncontested, while other parties won four seats uncontested.
As per the state Election Commission data, the BJP has won 401 seats and is leading in 552 seats. The Congress, which has claimed that it is “fighting against odds” with Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee president Shaktisinh Gohil, alleging that the BJP was using its “might and money power to pressure Congress candidates”, has won 25 seats and is leading in 42 seats. The Bahujan Samaj Party has won five seats, while Independents have won 23 seats so far, as per the data.
As the counting commenced, the BJP was declared the winner in the Halol and Wankaner municipalities. In Halol Municipality in Panchmahal district, the BJP had already won 19 out of 36 seats uncontested. Elections were held for 17 seats, of which five BJP candidates were declared winners early Tuesday morning. The BJP, thus, has retained the Halol Municipality for a consecutive term.
In Kalol Municipality in Panchmahal district, the counting is on for 28 seats in seven wards, with the BJP aiming to retain power.
In Wankaner in Morbi district, 13 candidates were declared uncontested winners at the start of counting. This includes 11 from the BJP and one each from the Congress and BSP. The contest for the remaining 15 seats is on, with the BJP and the Congress seeing a tough fight in the wards. So far, the BJP has won five of the 15 seats while Congress has won four, and Aam Aadmi Party has also emerged as the winner in one seat in ward no. 3 in Wankaner.
In Devgadh Baria Municipality in Dahod district, with 24 seats in six wards, three Independent candidates have emerged winners along with five BJP candidates and one Congress candidate so far.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In Vadodara district’s Karjan Municipality, the BJP is fighting for “pride and prestige” after 16 of its sitting corporators defected to contest as AAP candidates after being denied tickets. Out of the 28 seats that went to polls, a close contest is on, with the BJP leading in 11 seats so far.
In Salaya Municipality in Devbhumi Dwarka district, which has been a Congress stronghold, eight Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) candidates have emerged winners in wards 1 and 2, pulling off a major upset. The Congress in 2018 had managed to wrest power in Salaya after facing a defeat from the BJP in 2013.
In Dwarka Municipality, the BJP panel of four candidates each has emerged winners in wards 1 and 2, while wards 3 and 4 were already won by the party uncontested ahead of the polling day.
In 2018, of the 75 municipalities that went to polls, the BJP had won 47 while the Congress had won 16, with the NCP and the BSP emerging, gaining a majority in one each. Six municipalities saw a coalition, and four municipalities were run by Independents, who formed a board together.

headline: ‘RPF trying to clear overbridge when platform for Kumbh Special changed… this led to a stampede’: Officer’s report
description: According to the RPF officer’s report, after the departure of Train Number 12560 Shiv Ganga Express from Platform Number 12, suddenly there was a crowd of passengers in the station, because of which FOBs 2 and 3 got choked.
content:
What set off the stampede at New Delhi Railway Station on Saturday night killing 18 people was an announcement about a change in the departure platform of a Kumbh Special train to Prayagraj, according to a report prepared by an inspector-rank officer of the Railway Protection Force (RPF).
The inspector’s report will be taken as an input by the RPF which is preparing a final report to be submitted to the two-member high level committee set up by the Ministry of Railways.
“…at around 8.45 pm, an announcement was made that Kumbh Special going to Prayagraj would depart from Platform Number 12, but after some time, another announcement was made that the Kumbh Special would leave from Platform Number 16, due to which a stampede situation arose among passengers,” the officer is learnt to have written in the report submitted on February 16 to his Delhi Zone seniors.
At this time, the report said the Magadh Express was stationed at Platform 14, Uttar Sampark Kranti Express at Platform 15 and a crowd of passengers waiting to board the Prayagraj Express were also present at Platform 14 — all this froze the movement of passengers.
“Upon hearing the announcement, passengers started trying to climb the stairs from Platforms 12-13 and 14-15 via foot-over bridges (FOBs) 2 and 3; and passengers of Magadh Express, Uttar Sampark Kranti and Prayagraj Express were climbing down the stairs. In the midst of pushing and shoving, some passengers slipped, fell on the stairs and got injured; and other passengers started walking over them,” the report said.
When contacted, Himanshu Shekhar Upadhyay, Chief Public Relations Officer (CPRO) of Northern Railways, said multiple departments have been asked to send reports, RPF being one of them. “After receiving reports from all, the high-level committee set up by the ministry will cross-question them and then come to a final conclusion,” he said.
According to the RPF officer’s report, after the departure of Train Number 12560 Shiv Ganga Express from Platform Number 12, suddenly there was a crowd of passengers in the station, because of which FOBs 2 and 3 got choked. “There was a jam-like situation on platforms 12-13, 14-15 and 16 as well,” it said. “After assessing the crowd from FOB2, ASC/ NDLS (Assistant Security Commissioner, New Delhi Railway Station) asked the station director not to sell more tickets and advised caution, fearing more crowds,” a senior officer said, citing the letter.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Further, the inspector asked all on-duty and off-duty staff to immediately reach the three platforms and FOBs. “The station director was asked to order the special train to run immediately when it gets full…,” the letter said. Around this time when the personnel were trying to clear the crowd, the announcement about a change in the departure platform of the Kumbh special train was made.

Explaining the incident, Northern Railways CPRO Upadhyay, said, “Prima facie, it appears that Prayagraj Express was scheduled to arrive at Platform Number 14. Passengers who regularly travel to Prayagraj (reserved passengers) by this train, in addition to other passengers also wanting to travel by this train, led to a massive crowd on the platform, including at the FOB. To manage this, we immediately arranged for another train on-demand for Prayagraj, which was announced to arrive at Platform Number 12. The moment the passengers waiting at Platform Number 14 heard the announcement, they suddenly started moving up the staircase and the FOB. Since the number of people was too large, the FOB was blocked and during this time, a stampede-like situation occurred at the staircase.”

headline: With Korean hotels, restaurants and games, a ‘little Korea’ emerges in Pune
description: Talegaon, home to automobile giant Hyundai, steel company Posco and food business Lotte, among others from South Korea, has brought a steady stream of Koreans to the city
content:
A giant green signboard by the road proudly declares the beginning of Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation’s (MIDC) Talegaon Industrial Area and Floriculture Park.
Below it, as quiet as the community they address, are two small white hoardings with neat Korean inscriptions. It is the first glimpse of a growing Korean presence in this industrial hub.
Talegaon, home to automobile giant Hyundai, steel company Posco and food business Lotte, among others from South Korea, has brought a steady stream of Koreans to the city, whose cultural markers are gradually emerging amid the manufacturing hubbub.
At Hangang resort, where all rooms are booked for Hyundai staff, a ball lies on the grass beside a net stretched between two poles. “This is Jokgu, a Korean game where you hit the ball with your leg only as you pass it back and forth,” says Lee Jun Seo, whose family runs the resort. They are from Seoul and came to Pune around 10 years ago after hearing that there are more opportunities here as a lot of Korean factories were coming up.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Gold medallist female power-lifter dies after 270-kg barbell falls on neck during practice in Bikaner
Priyanka Chopra’s sister-in-law Neelam Upadhyaya says she got skin allergy after haldi ceremony: ‘What on Earth…’
Man convicted of raping 7-month-old toddler in Kolkata gets death sentence
Lee, who was 10 at the time, and his siblings found Indians to be warm and friendly.
Korean Lotte officials at the inauguration function of the Lotte factory (Havmor Icecream Private Limited) at Talegaon MIDC on February 6, 2025. (Express Photo/ Pavan Khengre)
“Korean people are more reserved. If you don’t know them, you are just like a stranger. For Indians, even if you’re a stranger, you must be treated like a friend. Now, when I visit Korea, I feel socialising with people there is difficult since Indians are friendlier,” he says.
Lee studied in a Pune school before going to Seoul for his culinary training.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“In the beginning, a lot of people didn’t even know what Korea was. If I said that I was Korean, they would ask ‘North or South?’. That was a common question. With K-pop, K-dramas being popular, a lot of people are aware of Korean culture. When I go out, people come up to me and the first thing they ask is if I am Korean, rather than, ‘Are you Chinese?’ like it was from 10 years ago,” he says.
There’s Korean food in the kitchens and lunch is staples like a spicy sweet chicken with red sauce and lots of carrots, potatoes and green onion. The restaurant has cabins, besides a common dining space, “because Korean people like their privacy”.
He has to keep the surroundings spotless “because Koreans are very strict about cleanliness”. A major highlight of the space is the gym, which includes pool tables and facilities for golf. In the garden, there are boxes of lettuce for the famous Korean salads, especially the sort that isn’t easily available in India.
A few minutes’ drive away is the SooMooNan hotel, a multi-storeyed guest house that is entirely for the Korean community.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On the ground floor are the clues – pool tables waiting for players. Sharad Gadsing, whose family owned the land, says that Korean professionals prefer to socialise among themselves, possibly because language is a barrier in engaging with their Maharashtrian neighbours.
Nevertheless the Gadsing family and a few Korean guests at the hotel have exchanged food—puran poli for them and Ramen from them.
“What they had asked for, and we provided, was a plot of land to grow salad vegetables,” he adds.
A hotel signboard by the road. (Express Photo)
Once again, there are lettuce and spring onions that the Korean staff at the guest house, mostly bachelors who stay around six months, cultivate and harvest. “They are here, digging and watering every evening after work,” says a local resident.
Restaurants are the most visible sign of a sizable Korean population in Talegaon. The Seoul Store is stocked with Ramyun, miso paste, frozen meats, sauces, oils and products for the kitchen, house and personal care. On weekends, there could be more than a hundred Korean clients buying their week’s supplies. There are also a number of eateries that bear signages in Korean, such as Eden Restaurant and Gung The Palace.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Shubham Gole, civil engineer at Hyundai Engineering and Construction India at Talegaon, works in a team of five Koreans and three Indians.
“We have friendly relations with same aged Korean persons but older Koreans are strict. Every Korean has a defense background so they are punctual with time and commitment. There is a gap between Koreans and Indians due to their soft skills and software proficiency,” he says, adding that 70 per cent of the engineers at the factory are Korean nationals.
Some of these engineers have previously worked at the Hyundai Chennai plant but prefer Pune because of the climate and infrastructure, said Chairman of the Korean Association in Pune Edgar Lee.
Lee also said that around 1,000 Korean nationals currently reside in Pune, spread across factories in areas like Talegaon, Chakan, and Ranjangaon, where the Korean electronics company LG Corporation has its factory.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Just like Lee Jun Seo, the children of Korean workers who have migrated with their families are enrolled in international schools like the Mahindra International School in Hinjewadi. Balewadi High Street and Phoenix Mall in Wakad are the go to spots for the senior engineers who reside in the Balewadi-Baner area, with foods like naan and chicken tandoori being major hits.

headline: UP CM defends Maha Kumbh spending: ‘If Rs 7,500 cr can generate Rs 3.5 lakh crore economic activity, isn’t it a wise investment?’
description: Pushes for religious tourism, says Ayodhya saw number of annual visitors jumping from 2.35 lakh to over 14 crore since inauguration of Ram Temple
content:
Stating that Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj generated employment for “lakhs of people”, leading to “increased incomes and contribution to Uttar Pradesh’s economic growth”, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday defended the government’s decision to spend Rs 7,500 crore for the 45-day religious event that is held once in every 12 years.
“If an investment of Rs 7,500 crore by the Central and state governments can generate economic activity worth Rs 3 to Rs 3.5 lakh crore, isn’t it a wise investment,” asked Adityanath while speaking at a meeting with entrepreneurs at his Lucknow residence.
According to the chief minister, the spending on Maha Kumbh proved “transformative” for Prayagraj as Rs 7,500 crore was spent on building 14 new flyovers, six underpasses, over 200 widened roads, new corridors, expanded railway stations, and a modern airport terminal. “Additionally, Rs 1,500 crore was earmarked specifically for Kumbh Mela arrangements,” he said.
The chief minister claimed that if the number of pilgrims reached 60 crore, the state’s GDP could see a boost of Rs 3.25 to Rs 3.5 lakh crore.
So far, according to the CM, 53 crore people have visited Prayagraj during the Maha Kumbh.
Recounting how an investor expressed interest in setting up a replica of the Dwadash Jyotirlinga made from recycled materials in Prayagraj, the chief minister said: “The investor committed to funding the project with a profit-sharing model of 50-50. The municipal corporation allocated 11 acres of land for the initiative, and I inaugurated it in the first week of January. The organisation invested Rs 14 crore, and within just 21 days, it recovered its investment and earned an equivalent profit. The municipal corporation also benefited from the revenue.”
Citing the “success” of Shivalik Park, Adityanath said that spiritual tourism has immense potential, as demonstrated during Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj.
At the ‘Dialogue with Young Entrepreneurs’, the chief minister also highlighted the inflow of tourists to Ayodhya where Ram Temple was inaugurated last year. “The impact is clear… In 2016-17, when there was no BJP government in Uttar Pradesh, the number of devotees visiting Ayodhya (in a year) was merely 2.35 lakh. By 2024, this number has surged to over 14-15 crore,” Adityanath said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Drawing parallels, the chief minister said that so far, 53 crore devotees have taken a dip at the Triveni Sangam during Maha Kumbh, and “still nine more days are left” for the conclusion of the Mela.
“In the 2013 Prayagraj Kumbh, 12 crore devotees participated over 55 days. In 2019, when Ardh Kumbh took place, the number doubled to 24 crore. This year, during the 45-day Maha Kumbh, 53 crore devotees have arrived in just 36 days,” the CM said.
He also pointed out that the Mela was earlier confined to 1,000 acres earlier. “By 2013, it was expanded to 2,000 acres, and this time, the Mela area has been further increased to a massive 10,000 acres,” the CM said.
Highlighting the logistical efforts to accommodate the surge of people to Prayagraj, Adityanath said: “In just 35 days, 40 routine flights and over 700 chartered flights arrived. The Railways has been operating hundreds of special trains daily, while the State Transport Corporation has deployed a fleet of 14,000 buses to facilitate the travel of people. From January 28 to 30, 15 crore devotees took holy dip. On January 28, around 5.5 crore devotees came, followed by 8 crore on January 29, and 2.5 crore on January 30.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
At least 30 people were killed and 60 others injured in a stampede at the Sangam in the early hours of January 29 after a large number of pilgrims gathered for a holy bath on Mauni Amavasya. While the chief minister has ordered a judicial probe and called it a “conspiracy”, the Opposition has been hitting out at the BJP government, accusing it of negligence and mishandling. The Allahabad High Court is also hearing a PIL which has sought action against responsible officials.
Meanwhile, another stampede took place at New Delhi railway station last Saturday (February 15) as a large number of people gathered to board trains to Prayagraj for Maha Kumbh. At least 18 people were killed in the stampede there.

headline: Chandigarh Municipal Corporation gets a mere Rs 467 crore for development works
description: The MC approves ₹1,079 crore deficit budget, funding gap remains a big challenge
content:
The Municipal Corporation Chandigarh (MCC) has approved a ₹1,079 crore deficit budget for the 2025-26 financial year, highlighting a persistent funding shortfall.
The total budget proposed by the MC stood at ₹2,114 crore, but it is set to receive only ₹625 crore as a grant from the Chandigarh Administration. The corporation plans to generate ₹410 crore from its own sources, mainly through property tax and water bills.
For 2025-26, the MC’s estimated expenditure is ₹1,664 crore, including ₹1,197 crore for salaries, pensions, and other recurring expenses, and ₹467 crore for development projects. However, even the committed liabilities—such as ₹900 crore for staff salaries, pensions, and utility bills—outstrip the available funds.
The MC has approved the budget, hoping to receive funds as per the recommendations of the 4th Delhi Finance Commission (DFC), which suggest a grant of ₹1,704.62 crore from the Chandigarh Administration. However, past trends indicate that this amount is unlikely to be sanctioned.

Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
'Main aisa aadmi nahi hoon': Samay Raina 'breaks the facade' of comedy
Apple iPhone 16e is here with eye on price-conscious customers, has one edge on earlier models
For years, the MC has been passing deficit budgets, regardless of which party has controlled it, but has never received funds as per DFC recommendations. Even previous appeals by the Chandigarh Administrator to the central government for adequate funding have not yielded results.
The financial strain is evident in the current fiscal year (2024-25) as well. The MC had approved a ₹2,325 crore budget with a target of generating ₹633 crore from its own sources, but revised estimates show it could collect only ₹347 crore—less than 55% of its projection.
With no assurance of additional funds, the MC appears set for yet another year of financial uncertainty.

headline: Illegal Bangladeshis have got Aadhar, voter cards, some even pay Income Tax: Calcutta HC judge
description: Recently, police have arrested nine people linked to the fake passport probe
content:
Justice Debangsu Basak of the Calcutta High Court on Monday claimed that all Bangladesh nationals entering India illegally have got Aadhar card, Indian voter card, and ration cards made for themselves.
While hearing a bail plea of a couple arrested in connection with a fake passport case, Justice Debangsu Basak observed: “All those Bangladeshi nationals who are coming to this country have Indian Aadhar card, voter card, ration card. Whether your client pays income tax, I do not know, but there are many Bangladeshis who pay income tax also. The Bangladeshis make fake passports and enter India and then they make Aadhar card, ration card, voter card.”
Dulal Sil and his wife Swapna Sil, who were arrested 13 months ago for allegedly possessing fake passports, had filed the bail plea before the Division Bench of Justice Basak and Justice MD Shabbar Rashidi.
Sil’s counsel told the High Court that the couple came to India in 2010 and had settled in Purba Bardhaman. They have genuine Aadhar card, voter card and ration card and also got a home allotted under the PM Awas Yojana, their counsel told the Division Bench.
Asserting that their clients are “genuine citizens” and didn’t enter the country on fake passports, the counsel said that documents to prove that they are citizens of India are not being provided to the couple.
Sil’s counsel since their client entered India before December 31, 2014, they do not fall under the Foreign Citizenship Act as per section 2 of the law notified in 2019.
Citing the recent deportation of illegal Indian immigrants by the US, Justice Basak said the couple will be granted bail only if they submit documents proving that they are true citizens of the country. “Don’t you see America is deporting back all those who had entered the country illegally. If there is any document proving that they (Sils) are true citizens of India, submit it and they will be granted bail.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Recently, police have arrested nine people linked to the fake passport probe. Among those arrested included Samir Das, a law clerk at Barasat court, who allegedly charged Bangladeshi citizens for procuring fake documents; Abdul Hai, a 61-year-old retired sub-inspector from Kolkata Police’s passport section, among others. The racket, disguised as a travel agency, had reportedly issued at least 73 fake Indian passports to Bangladeshi nationals, facilitating their entry into India.

headline: Writer’s Corner | Fazlul Hasan, the self-taught historian who brought Bengaluru’s past to life
description: Fazlul Hasan’s interest in history was sparked almost by accident, when he stumbled across an ancient carved inscription.
content:
Over the five centuries that Bengaluru has made its mark, its inhabitants have chronicled its history in various ways. But in recent decades, one book has been omnipresent among English publications about the city’s history—Bangalore Through the Centuries. Since its initial publication in 1970, the book has become a treasured possession for book lovers and historians alike, with only 1,000 copies printed. Until recently, obtaining a copy was extremely difficult—after the author, M Fazlul Hasan, passed away in 1991, plans for a second edition had not materialised.
Surprisingly for an author whose history of Bengaluru influenced many subsequent works, Fazlul Hasan was not a formally trained historian; he studied law. His daughter Ameena Shaheen, who retired as the principal of Hasanath College, Bengaluru, said, “He retired as an administrative officer with the City Corporation. He was not taught history at all—it was all his own learning.” She recalled that at a young age, she did not fully grasp the implications of her father’s work. The scope of it became clearer to her during her own study of epigraphy (the study of ancient inscriptions) while completing her master’s degree in Kannada.
Also Read | Fazlul Hasan’s ‘Bangalore Through the Centuries’ relaunched 52 years after original edition ran out of print
Fazlul Hasan’s interest in history was sparked almost by accident, when he stumbled across an ancient carved inscription. “In Sunkenahalli near the Bull Temple there was a place with a mango grove where my relatives used to stay. When he was young, he used to play and saw a stone with an inscription, and he was curious enough to know what was on it… that was the difference between a person with foresight and a normal person. Since then, his studies began,” Ameena Shaheen said.
The second edition of the book was released in 2023, edited by Bengaluru architect Naresh Narasimhan, who was introduced to Fazlul Hasan’s family by actor Prakash Belawadi, a former neighbour. Ameena Shaheen said, “So many people had wanted to republish the book. We had trust issues as we didn’t want it to be too commercialised. Slowly, we met Naresh Narasimhan and were convinced that he would do the job properly.” The book remains mostly Fazlul Hasan’s work, with minor edits made alongside the addition of new photographs. “Every time people say how my father’s book brought about a comprehensive approach towards the study of Bangalore,” she concluded.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

'Main aisa aadmi nahi hoon': Samay Raina 'breaks the facade' of comedy
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Offering a perspective on Hasan’s work at a 2023 event, Narasimhan said, “The book was a labour of love. In an era before the internet, the bibliography of the book had around 223 citations. In fact, most books on the history of Bangalore after the 1970s refer back to this book.”
Even a cursory glance at Bangalore Through the Centuries reveals a work of passion—the author’s vivid descriptions bring history to life, from his accounts of the Marathas and Wodeyars to the time of British rule, in remarkable detail. It is not difficult to see why it remains an iconic landmark in the documentation of the city’s history.

headline: Himachal Pradesh education department limits days of annual sports meets, asks govt schools to effectively utilise teaching days
description: Discontinue the practice of sending students to attend functions of other departments, the Himachal education department tells schools.
content:
Emphasising the effective utilisation of the prescribed 220 teaching days in government schools, the Himachal Pradesh government Saturday issued its annual academic calendar for 2025-26, limiting the duration of the annual sports meet at different levels.
Additionally, the annual academic calendar focuses on curbing the practice of sending school students to participate in various functions organised by government departments and NGOs.
The calendar, issued through the office of the secretary of education, states, “The practice of sending school children to attend various functions, events, programs, rallies, yatras, etc., organized by different government departments and NGOs shall be discontinued. No group of students from any school shall be sent for such events as participants or audience members. In case it is necessary to send a batch or group of students for any such event, prior permission from the concerned Director of Education must be obtained.”
The calendar further states, “However, students shall be allowed to participate in various competitions as a team or individual participants. Only one teacher shall accompany such a team as a coordinator or manager. Meanwhile, schools may organize as many school-level activities (curricular and co-curricular) as needed, provided they do not reduce the teaching days.”
A source said that schools have been instructed to complete activities for events such as Environment Day, World Science Day, and Tree Plantation Day within one hour in the morning, instead of organising different events throughout the day. There are approximately 15,000 government schools in the state, with around 7.5 lakh students.
“According to the National Education Policy (NEP), we have 220 teaching days for every academic year. However, it was observed that teaching days were not being utilised effectively. Various reasons were identified for this, including the prolonged scheduling of sports events throughout the year, the appointment of teachers to sports events despite their non-sports background, and the participation of students in activities organised by other departments and NGOs. Moving forward, sports tournaments for Under-14 students (elementary classes) at the block, district, and state levels will be held from April 27 to April 29, May 18 to May 20, and October 11 to October 12, respectively. Similarly, for Under-19 students (secondary classes), sports tournaments at the block, district, and state levels will be conducted from May 10 to May 12, May 29 to May 31, and October 11 to October 12, respectively,” said B R Sharma, Additional Director of Elementary Education, who was one of the key officials involved in designing the annual academic calendar.
A source said, “Previously, sports events at the block, district, and state levels were prolonged. Only 10 to 20 students from a government school would participate in sports, but the entire school would become engaged in preparations and practice, leading to a significant reduction in effective teaching days.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Meanwhile, separate schedules have been issued for summer- and winter-closing schools, with no changes to school holidays. Winter-closing schools will have a winter break from February 1 to February 11 and a monsoon break from July 21 to July 26. Summer-closing schools will have a six-day Lohri holiday from January 11 to January 16. The results for non-board classes will be declared on March 31, and admissions will begin on April 1. These schools will observe a monsoon break from June 22 to July 29. The teaching-learning process shall commence from the very first day of the academic session.
The government schools in plain areas, including districts Una, Kangra, Solan, and certain parts of Sirmaur (such as Nahan and Paonta Sahib), as well as Sundernagar in Mandi district, fall under the summer-closing category. The remaining schools follow the winter-closing schedule.
Notably, Himachal Pradesh has emerged as a leader in student reading proficiency, according to the 2024 Annual Status of Education Report (ASER), released on January 28 this year. The report highlights significant progress in learning outcomes, infrastructure, and digital literacy in the state’s schools, though challenges remain in stagnant school enrolment and rising dropout rates among older students.
The ASER 2024 report, which evaluated 268 schools in Himachal Pradesh, found that 46.6 per cent of Class 3 students in government schools can easily read a Class 2 Hindi textbook – almost double the national average of 23.4 per cent. This marks a 10-percentage-point improvement since 2022. Himachal also ranked third in reading proficiency among Class 8 students, following Mizoram and Kerala.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Physical Teachers Association raises objection
Lalit Chauhan, President, Himachal Pradesh Physical Teachers Association, has raised concerns about the dates set by the Himachal Pradesh education secretary for sports events. “Scheduling boys’ and girls’ block tournaments on the same date at two different venues is very challenging due to staff shortages,” Chauhan said. He further pointed out that many schools have only one physical education teacher in senior secondary schools, who is responsible for both Under-14 and Under-19 tournaments. Additionally, the orders state that apart from Physical Education Teachers (PETs) and District Physical Education Officers (DPEs), no other staff members will be involved in tournaments. “This raises concerns about who will accompany and manage students during tournaments,” he added. The Physical Teachers’ Association is yet to submit a memorandum to the education department regarding these issues.

headline: Linking MTHL and Mumbai-Pune Expressway: Rs 1,100 crore elevated corridor to be completed by Feb 2027
description: The elevated corridors, with a combined length of 4,958 metres in the Chirle section and 1,700 metres in the Palaspe section, will improve traffic flow and reduce congestion, making the region more accessible and boosting economic growth.
content:
The Rs 1,100-crore elevated corridor project to ensure smooth connectivity between the newly commissioned Mumbai Trans Harbour Sealink (MTHL) and the Mumbai-Pune Expressway will be completed by February 2027, according to the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), which is implementing the project.
The project consist of two elevated corridors — one from the Chirle end of MTHL to Gavan Phata, and another from Palaspe Phata to the Mumbai-Pune Expressway.
The six-lane elevated corridor over the JNPT–Panvel National Highway (NH-348) will be constructed between Chirle and Gavan Phata, including the reconstruction of service roads. A similar six-lane elevated corridor will be built along the Old Mumbai-Pune National Highway (NH-48) in Raigad district, which will also include widening NH-48 to six lanes.
Dr Sanjay Mukherjee IAS, Metropolitan Commissioner of MMRDA, described the project as transformative, emphasising that it will reshape regional connectivity and ease traffic congestion, particularly on NH-348.
“By seamlessly integrating Atal Setu with the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, we are ensuring efficient traffic dispersal and eliminating congestion at crucial junctions, particularly on NH-348, which carries a significant load of multi-axle container traffic from JNPT,” said Mukherjee.
The project being carried out by Gawar Construction Ltd at a cost of Rs 1102.75 crore, is scheduled for completion in February 2027. At present, excavation work is under way, marking the beginning of this significant infrastructure development.
“This initiative is about reshaping the way people and businesses move between Mumbai and Pune. Professionals will be able to work in Mumbai while residing in Pune, significantly enhancing opportunities and quality of life,” said Mukherjee.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The elevated corridors, with a combined length of 4,958 metres in the Chirle section and 1,700 metres in the Palaspe section, will improve traffic flow and reduce congestion, making the region more accessible and boosting economic growth.
This visionary infrastructure development will strengthen Maharashtra’s position as an economic powerhouse and accelerate growth in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region as per the MMRDA.

headline: Immigrants land: 2 from Haryana, Punjab held over pending cases
description: The suspects, who have been identified as Sandeep Singh alias Sunny, a resident of Vikas Nagar in Rajpura, and Pardeep Singh, were detained soon after their flight landed in the evening, police officers said.
content:
Sahil Verma, a resident of Pehowa town of Haryana’s Kurukshetra, was arrested soon after landing in Amritsar on Saturday night in connection with a harassment complaint lodged by a minor girl in 2022. He was among the 116 illegal immigrants deported by the US in the second batch.
Kurukshetra SP Varun Singla said the girl had alleged in her complaint that Verma blocked her way and threatened to kill her. Verma is also accused of harassing her. To evade arrest, Verma allegedly fled the country after paying `38 lakh to travel agents. He lived in Italy for nearly two years and then went to the US via a ‘dunki route’, said police.
The Ludhiana Police on Sunday arrested 26-old-year Gurwinder Singh from the second batch of deportees over pending non-bailable warrants against him in a 2021 snatching case.
Gurwinder,  a resident of Sasrali Colony in Meharban, was detained Sunday morning from his home. A graduate, Gurwinder — the son of a Punjab Police officer — was booked in two FIRs for alleged snatching and theft, said the police.

headline: New Delhi Railway Station stampede: Security upped at key UP junctions, Yogi urges devotees to cooperate
description: An estimated 1.36 crore devotees took a dip at the Sangam in Prayagraj by 6 pm on Sunday, the Maha Kumbh Mela administration said
content:
Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday reviewed the arrangements at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj and appealed to pilgrims and other visitors to make the religious congregation a success by cooperating in maintaining hassle-free traffic movement.
Also, strict security protocols were enforced at the key railway stations in Uttar Pradesh, particularly Prayagraj, Varanasi, Ayodhya, Kanpur, Lucknow and Mirzapur, a day after a stampede at the New Delhi railway station amid large number of people arriving for the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj.
Addressing a climate change convention in the Maha Kumbh area, the Chief Minister said, “Maha Kumbh is a great festival of faith in which people from all over the country and the world are excited to participate in. In such a situation, everyone’s positive co-operation can increase the event’s success manifold.”
Condoling the Delhi stampede deaths, he termed the incident as “unfortunate”. “All devotees are requested not to park their vehicles on roads and instead use the designated parking spaces so that everyone gets an opportunity to take a holy dip at the Triveni Sangam,” he added.
“While doing an aerial survey of the Kumbh today, I noticed that people had parked their vehicles on the road before leaving for a bath at the Sangam despite the availability of parking space. If people park their vehicle at a designated place, there will be no traffic jams on roads,” he said.
Also Read | New Delhi station stampede: Families of 18 who died get Rs 10 lakh ex-gratia, in cash
The everyday footfall at the Kumbh this time was as much as it used to be on Mauni Amavasya on earlier occasions, he claimed, adding this has become the world’s biggest event. On enforcing strict security protocols at the key railway stations in UP, Additional Director General (Railways) Prakash D said, “We have identified holding areas for passengers, as trains have a limited capacity. Platforms too have a limited capacity. The extra passengers coming to the station are kept in the holding areas.
North Central Railway’s Shashikant Tripathi said, “We are strictly adhering to the established protocols, which were successfully implemented during festivals like Mauni Amavasya and Basant Panchami.” At the Prayagraj Junction, entry is restricted to the city side, and passengers are kept in a ‘holding area’ until their train arrives.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In Varanasi, Ashok Kumar from the North Eastern Railway said protocols are in place at Jhunsi and Rambagh stations, where passengers are held in secure areas until their train arrives.
Security at Varanasi Junction was also tightened. Station Director Arpit Gupta said vehicle entry is banned around the station, barriers have been placed at key locations, and security forces monitor the crowd.
Also, security measures were implemented at Ayodhya’s railway stations. Separate entry and exit points were set up for pilgrims, with GRP and RPF ensuring security. In Lucknow, police were deployed at the railway station.
1.36 crore take dip on Sunday: Mela authority
An estimated 1.36 crore devotees took a dip at the Sangam in Prayagraj by 6 pm on Sunday, the Maha Kumbh Mela administration said. According to figures released by the mela administration, the total number of pilgrims who have taken a dip at the Sangam since January 13, when the Maha Kumbh started, has crossed 52.83 crore.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Saturday also saw 1.36 crore devotees taking a holy dip, while on Friday, around one crore pilgrims participated in the ritual, pushing the total number of pilgrims past the 50-crore mark, the administration said.
—With PTI inputs

headline: Gujarat Hardlook: Work in progress as nine municipal corporations undergo urban makeover
description: The nine new municipal corporations announced by the Gujarat government during the 2024-25 budget have been carved out and the state is trying to send them to the election by next year. These new civic bodies take the state’s urban population to over 50 per cent from the current 42 per cent. As the civic bodies find their feet, Parimal Dabhi, Kamaal Saiyed, Aditi Raja and Brendan Dabhi... take a look at the path ahead
content:
In its first state cabinet meeting of 2025 on January 1, Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel-led government gave its sanction to form nine new municipal corporations in Gujarat by upgrading the nine A category municipalities (those with one lakh population and above). Going by the February 2024 budget speech of state finance minister Kanubhai Desai, Gujarat aspires to take the population living in urban areas to 75%.
The new municipal corporations are Morbi, Surendranagar and Porbandar in Saurashtra region; Gandhidham in Kutch district; Vapi and Navsari in south Gujarat; Mehsana in north Gujarat and Anand and Nadiad in central Gujarat. The government has assigned six of the eight existing municipal corporations as their mentors for a year as the plan, say sources, is to hold the first general elections of the new MCs by March 2026. A top official told The Indian Express that the transition process to a municipal corporation has been done ensuring “none of the routine public interfaces with the municipality are disrupted, like getting birth and death certificates and so on.”
Within hours of the decision, the government also appointed new municipal commissioners and the district collectors as the respective executive officers and administrators of the new urban local bodies.
A senior officer of Urban Development Department (UDD) said, “Given the government’s seriousness to ensure that the new municipal corporations find their feet as soon as possible, appointments have also been made on several statutory posts such as town planning officer, medical officer of health, city engineers, municipal secretary, deputy municipal commissioner etc.. for one year.”
The officer added that the UDD is reviewing the status every 15 days to ensure that citizens of the new municipal corporations do not face any hardships during this transition.
Mentorship, a first
Gujarat originally had eight municipal corporations — Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot, Jamnagar, Bhavnagar, Junagadh and Gandhinagar — which were formed in the span of 64 years since Gujarat’s foundation.
According to a top government source, “Junagadh and Gandhinagar — which were among the last ones to be added — took 8-10 years in completing certain tasks. To avoid such delay in the case of these nine urban bodies, the government has introduced the mentorship programme.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Under this, the existing municipal corporations will handhold the new ones and train them in different aspects of urbanisation.“In the major corporations, there are some things that have been streamlined after several years of work. The trial and error that the major cities have gone through to perfect their systems, will be passed on to these new corporations from Day-1 and so they will not have to face the same struggles.
They will just need to modify some processes to suit localised needs,” said another officer.
Leveraging urbanisation
“Six of the existing MCs will go to polls in March 2026. The planning for the new civic bodies is being done in a manner so that they also go to elections simultaneously. Formation of wards is already among the top priority for the new corporations, and meetings are being held with the State Election Commission for the same. Several aspects, including the implementation of reservation in multiple seats of the wards are part of the ongoing plan,” a senior officer of UDD said.
The formation of nine new municipal corporations could be seen as an attempt to make vikas (development) visible under CM Patel.
Senior BJP leader on condition of anonymity
All the new corporations, the officer said, are likely to have 11 to 14 wards. Currently each ward has four corporators, half of which are women. The advantage is that “the people of the city get better facilities of drinking water, drainage, roads, street lights etc.. Also, the cities also get more grants from the centre,” said the senior officer.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The people of these areas, the government added, will also be benefitted in future by projects such as BRTS, Metro and Riverfront.
A senior BJP leader, on the condition of anonymity, told The Indian Express that the formation of nine new municipal corporations could be seen as “an attempt to make vikas (development) visible under CM Bhupendra Patel”.
“When you establish nine new municipal corporations in one go, it creates a political impression that the rural areas are getting developed and there is visibility,” the party leader said. Agreeing with this, a government source said, “Certainly, it boosts the development image of the state. Gujarat is an urbanised state as a whole. But still, it had only eight municipal corporations. Whereas, states such as Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra have bigger number of municipal corporations.”
Tracking the trajectory of new corporations
Mehsana
Mentored by: Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation (GMC)
With a population of over 20 lakh, Mehsana district is spread over 4484.10 sq kms. If one were to visit Mehsana town, sights of JCB machines breaking down encroachments to build roads are common. This Mehsana Municipal Corporation (MMC) is coming up in the district of which Vadnagar — Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s hometown — is a part.The corporation will include areas of Mehsana municipality, 10 surrounding as well as parts of six other gram panchayats, has been divided into two zones and around 13 wards have been identified.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Newly-appointed municipal commissioner Ravindra Khatale said hiring 565 personnel for multiple posts such as engineers, surveyors, town planners, clerks, peons, drivers, fire officials, medical officer of health is among the priorities.Till the posts are filled up, Khatale said, they have hired 60-70 key persons through outsourcing and contractual process for carrying out multiple functions of the corporation. “We did a comprehensive cleanliness drive across Mehsana city and in the neighbouring areas. Whatever legacy waste, garbage dump was lying there (in the city areas), we removed almost all of that,” Khatale said.
The number of vehicles collecting door-to-door garbage is 72 and soon it is going to be around 95.
After doing a cleanliness drive, the MC is now focussing on other developmental activities; one of them is to develop Radhanpur Road and Modhera Road as iconic roads.
For this, the civic body has removed around 500 encroachments clearing around 30 feet space on either side of the two roads. Beautification and utility features such as benches, light poles and so on will make these roads iconic. Former leader of opposition in the outgoing Mehsana Municipality and Congress leader Kamlesh Sutariya, however, alleged that the drive is discriminatory.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“The authorities have removed only shades or some extension of a shop on the footpath. If they are really serious, then they should remove even shops full or partial if they are encroaching upon the road. They have not done that. I don’t know the reason; whether it is because they don’t want to displease some people or are doing this just as a mark of show-off,” Sutariya alleged.
“Also, the corporation should develop not just two roads, but all the roads in the city,” he suggested.
Sutariya also alleged that the people of Mehsana have to wait really long to get birth/death certificates during this transition period.
According to the MMC officials, however, some buildings have been hired to set up two zonal offices, which people can approach for day-to-day services such as birth-death certificates, taxation related works etc..
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Khatale estimates the 2025-26 budget to be around Rs 650-700 crore.The MMC staff has started the department wise training at the GMC and will study their plans for streets and roads and also the Standard Operating Procedures (SOP), said Khatale. He added that a team of top officials of MMC has also visited Surat Municipal Corporation to study the best practices there.
In the pipeline
– Developing an ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system for the grievance redressal
– For the time being, a dedicated helpline number is active
– Underground water, drainage network
– Five new gardens, five new lakes and 10 oxygen parks
Vapi
Mentored by: Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC)
Located on the busy National Highway no 48, Vapi also falls on the route of the upcoming Bullet Train and is a major industrial town, with a substantial population of migrants who work in the GIDC in the town and in neighbouring Sarigam, Umargaon and Bhilad.
Given the heavy industrialisation, and the possibility of accidents the municipality already has its own fire station here.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The new Vapi municipal corporation will comprise the municipality and 11 villages bordering it, taking the total area to 72 sq kilometres and the population to above five lakh.
The immediate challenge for the civic body is hiring new personnel for the new roles. The new municipal corporation has advertised for 50 new jobs for which it got 3,000 applications, municipal commissioner Yogesh Chaudhary told The Indian Express.
“Earlier, there were 99 employees, out of which 47 were cleaning staff. We have increased the strength to 350 permanent employees, consisting of engineers of different branches, town planners, sanitary inspectors, clerks etc.A proposal had been sent to the state government for recruitment. Of the 3,000 applications, we have interviewed some candidates. The rest will be completed next week,” Chaudhary said.
The corporation will also hire 1,000 cleaning staff on contractual basis, and the garbage collection vehicles have been increased to 96 from 48. To begin with, the staff and contractual employees will be trained at the Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC) and later top officials of different departments of SMC will also see the setup. For new offices, properties have been taken on rent, Chaudhary added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In the pipeline
– At least 37 roads have been identified for renovation
– Main roads are to be converted into iconic roads
– Old gardens are to be redeveloped and beautified
– Three new town planning schemes
– Development plan for the 11 merged villages
Navsari
Mentored by: SMC
Being close to Surat, the state government has already tagged Navsari as its twin city. The Navsari Municipal Corporation (NMC) will include the Navsari municipality area and four new villages, covering 58-square-kilometre area and taking the population to five lakh (one lakh higher). The city will be split into east and west zones. The NMC area was earlier under the Navsari Urban Development Authority (NUDA), which already has a draft town planning scheme.
Municipal commissioner Dev Choudhary said, “We will work on drainage lines and drinking water networks in the four new villages. The present strength of NMC is 95 permanent employees, 100 contractual staffers, and 210 cleaning teams. We have proposed 560 more staffers, and the proposal has been sent to the state government. We are hiring 61 contractual staffers for which we have got 2000 applications, and around 250 cleaning staffers.”
Choudhary added,” We are coming up with CCTV networks in entire municipal corporation areas to monitor the activities and also ensure that spitting and littering is not done at public places. The door-to-door garbage collecting vehicles will also be increased, and roads will be resurfaced.”
In the pipeline
– Three to four town planning schemes
– Four new civic centres
– Two flyovers planned to streamline the traffic
Anand
Mentored by: Vadodara Municipal Corporation
Home to the Amul brand and a part of the Charotar region, this municipal corporation is among the few composed of maximum municipalities — Anand, Karamsad and Vidyanagar, and four village panchayats.
Last week, protests had broken out in Karamsad by a local outfit, Sardar Samman Sankalp Andolan Committee, against the inclusion of the municipality area citing that it had “erased the identity” of the town, which was home to Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel. Although former CM Shankarsinh Vaghela and Congress leader Paresh Dhahani joined the protests last week, the ANMC has not faced an obstruction in extended services, said deputy municipal commissioner Nilaksh Makwana. The immediate challenge for the corporation is manpower. Makwana said that the corporation has sent a proposal for hiring about 600 Class I to Class III permanent officers.
Makwana said, “We are still deciding the cadre-wise classification. For the Class IV workers, we will hire as per the instructions of the state government. We are formulating a policy on how Class I officers will be placed in about 20-22 departments in the main office apart from the zonal offices.”
The new MC is divided into east and west zones. “The services for birth, death and marriage registrations were set up within five days. We have appointed registrars and sub-registrars in the zones and also stationed a computer operator and a sub-registrar in the four outgrowth areas of the panchayats that have been included, so as to ensure that citizens can avail of the services without travelling to the main department.”
Makwana added, “Our existing officers are going the extra mile looking after multiple areas for the interim period.” For the iconic roads, the MC has identified the stretch from Chikhodra Chowkdi to Anand Elecon Circle, Grid Chowki to Bhalej, and the Anand-Vidyanagar road, Makwana said.
In the pipeline
– Three iconic roads identified
– Sewage lines to be set up
– Developing lakes and ponds in the panchayat areas
– Storm water drains
Gandhidham
Mentored by: Rajkot Municipal Corporation
Located near Kandla Port, the new corporation just got its new logo after a competition and it was launched on February 12, the 76th foundation day of the city.
“Our first priority was to identify gaps and make sure that there are no interruptions in services such as water, drainage and roads and sanitation during the transition period,” said Mehul Desai, the deputy municipal commissioner (east and admin), of Gandhidham Municipal Corporation (GdMC).
Gandhidham Municipal Corporation has been formed by the amalgamation of the old Gandhidham Municipality (Nagarpalika), the semi-urban town of Adipur and six villages. “People were confused due to the change in systems… so we continued the local talati offices by converting them into ward offices so that other essential services such as taxes and birth and death registration remain unaffected,” said Desai.
Divided into two zones, Adipur town is the western zonal headquarter. There are 13 wards of which eight belong to the former municipality and five gram panchayats have been converted into a ward each. This mechanism has been kept in place during the transition process so that changes in jurisdiction are not immediately jarring for staff and citizens. Desai said, “This is for administrative ease but we will change it later on as we hire more staff and set up the offices. We have hired contractual staff for now but we will conduct regular recruitment shortly.”
Apart from administrative changes, and continuation of essential public works,municipal commissioner MP Pandya carried out a major sanitation drive in the city and beautification works on important crossroads has also begun.
To develop iconic roads, “we required partial acquisition of properties on the edges of these main roads. Here, we got great support from the people. We just did demarcations and sent notices. The people, for the most part, demolished those portions themselves,” says Pandya.
Since the transition process began, teams of two officers or staff from each department of Rajkot Municipal Corporation (RMC) have been visiting both, Morbi and Gandhidham which are being mentored by it, to set up processes and train local officials. This process will end by March 2025. Later on, teams from these corporations will phase wise spend some time in Rajkot to witness first-hand the operations of the major city. Rajkot municipal commissioner Tushar Sumera told The Indian Express, “We will be setting up Morbi and Gandhidham corporations as mirror images of RMC in terms of staff, file procedures, processes and mechanisms. Our primary focus is on training and setting up departments and making sure they have their one-year action plan in place.”
In the pipeline
– Entry points being developed as iconic roads
– Training of senior officers by RMC commissioner

headline: CM Siddaramaiah hails ‘robust panchayat system’ after Karnataka tops ‘Devolution to Panchayats’ rankings
description: The ‘Devolution to Panchayats’ rankings were compiled by the Indian Institute of Public Administration and Ministry of Panchayati Raj.
content:
After Karnataka topped the ‘Devolution to Panchayats’ rankings compiled by the Indian Institute of Public Administration and Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah hailed the development as a reflection of the robust Panchayat system in Karnataka.
In a post on X, Siddaramaiah said that Karnataka was given the top rank in the Devolution Index due to effective financial devolution and timely fund release. “This achievement reflects our commitment to strengthening grassroots democracy. Our Rural Development & Panchayati Raj Department, under Minister Shri Priyank Kharge, has played a key role in ensuring Panchayats have the resources & autonomy to drive rural progress,” he said Sunday.
Siddaramaiah said ‘decentralisation’ was not just a concept, but a “lived reality in Karnataka. A robust Panchayat system means stronger rural development, participatory democracy and inclusive growth.”
