The threats prompted the Indian government to put in place protocols for handling such threats as part of the Bomb Threat Contingency Plan (BTCP).

headline: How women in rural areas of Himachal are living their entrepreneurial dreams
description: State’s Himira website brought 3.5L women connected with 44,000 SHGs together to sell their produce
content:
Jaswinder Kaur from Nalagarh in Solan not only received Rs 60,000 for livestock and non-farming activities from the state government but her income also increased by Rs 20,000 this month.
Megha Devi from Sullah in Kangra has started a small enterprise of making leaf plates thus increasing her monthly income from Rs 5,000 to Rs 20,000. The dreams of Jaswinder, Megha and many others in the state got wings with the Himachal Pradesh government launching an e-commerce website to sell local products (under the name Himira) made by women self help groups (SHGs).
The website, which was launched by CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on January 3, received 1,050 online orders worth lakhs till February 8 from Rajasthan, Kerala Maharashtra, Delhi, Punjab and Haryana among others states.
Jaswinder Kaur from Nalagarh of Solan district proudly displays her products. (Express Photo)
Himira offers natural and handmade products made by women in the rural areas of the state. Approximately 3.50 lakh women across Himachal are connected with Himira through 44,000 SHGs also operated by the women. While Jaswinder Kaur joined the Sainath SHG that produces organic and cow-dung made products, Megha is associated with Shree Ganesh SHG and sells her leaf plates via them.
“Earlier, I was financially dependent on her husband, but now I enjoy my financial stability. With every sale, I see not just profit but the dreams of my children coming to life,” said Megha.
Like Jaswinder and Megha, there are also others who are living the entrepreneurial dream in the hill state. In Keylong of Lahaul-Spiti district, Rigzin Chhoedan leveraged the Kangla Berry SHG to expand her work in agriculture, livestock rearing, handicrafts, and handlooms. Her monthly income has now grown from Rs 4,000 to Rs 25,000.
Megha Devi from Sullah of Kangra district with her plates. (Express Photo)
Anita Devi from Jhamiyat in Hamirpur district once relied on a private job where she earned just Rs 5,000 per month. After joining an SHG and receiving training in mushroom cultivation, her now earns Rs 20,000 per month. “Through hard work and government support, I turned my small savings into a thriving business. Now, I support my family and empower others to believe in their potential,” said Anita.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Shivam Pratap, director of Himachal Pradesh Rural Livelihood Development Department, said that 99 per cent of SHGs are dominated by the rural women in the state. “The state government provides them financial assistance under various schemes for creating infrastructure. All income generated through product sales go to the women. In fact, the government increases the assistance to SHGs that are doing good.”
Elaborating on the process, Pratap said that the first stage of a SHG is Village Organisation (VO), second stage is Block Organisation (BO) and in the third stage Cluster Organisations (COs) of these SHGs were made. “We have women who earned Rs 5,000 to Rs 60,000 depending on the sale and value of their products. For instance, SHGs involved in the manufacturing and sale of desi ghee, wooden craft, woolen clothes etc. earn more than their contemporaries.”
Also Read | How can feminisation of agriculture empower women?
A spokesperson of the Himachal Pradesh Rural Development department said, “Before January 3, people could only purchase the local products at SHG stores, government offices and other designated places. The website has changed the scenario and we are getting a lot of orders. The website features a diverse range of nearly 30 products, from hand-woven Himachali textiles to pure and natural food items. The local women are also getting paid based on the number of products and units they sell.”
Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said that through the digital initiative, nearly 30,000 SHG women now have direct access to livelihood opportunities that were previously unavailable. “The state government is committed to policies that align with the local culture and environment,” he said.

headline: Designed by Jeanneret, teak coffee table to go under the hammer
description: The solid teak wood triangle coffee table with round edges, on three log-type legs had been designed for Jeanneret’s private apartment in Chandigarh.
content:
A teak triangular coffee table designed by Swiss-French architect Pierre Jeanneret is all set to go under the hammer with the reserve price kept up to Rs 5.43 lakh. The auction will be conducted in the Netherlands on 15 February.
The solid teak wood triangle coffee table with round edges, on three log-type legs had been designed for Jeanneret’s private apartment in Chandigarh.
The estimated reserve price has been kept in the range of 4,000 euros – 6,000 euros, which comes to is Rs 3,62,100 – Rs 5,43,150.
Advocate Ajay Jagga, who keeps taking up the issues related to Indian heritage items, has written a communique to S Jaishankar, Union Minister for External Affairs, citing protection of national heritage (Chandigarh Heritage Articles) from being auctioned all over the world.
“In response to my earlier representations on this same topic, the Ministry of Culture took action and asked the agencies like ASI to look into the matter and some action was taken. However, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) is yet to take cognizance of this matter and some remedial measures. So again, I am submitting this communication to intimate regarding the auction of our VIRASAT (legacy) (article from Chandigarh),” he said in the letter.
His letter added that articles are being auctioned regularly in foreign countries without any “resistance” from the Government of India. “It is requested that the Indian embassies in foreign countries must be sensitised about our heritage so that wherever information comes to them, they can at least raise an objection, which may sustain or not, to save the heritage,” Jagga wrote. The advocate went on to say that the ongoing auctions can be stopped only through diplomatic channels and brought back, as they were taken out from the country in an “illegal manner”.
“Moreover, when the Ministry of Home Affairs issued the prohibitory orders regarding furniture items of Chandigarh, putting a STOP on the sale, export, shift, move on these items, how it reached NETHERLANDS, is also a matter of investigation, as to how it crossed the boundaries of India,” Jagga said.

headline: Gujarat Confidential: Divine Journey
description: Parmar, a retired Gujarat-cadre IAS officer of 1985-batch, has also written about his visit to the Maha Kumbh in the GSRTC bus on his official blog on the internet
content: With Maha Kumbh underway in Prayagraj, the choice of mode of travel to the venue is a key question on the minds of devotees who wish to take a holy dip at the Triveni Sangam. And state bureaucrats are no different. A senior state bureaucrat who visited Maha Kumbh recently, after taking multiple flights, said that with soaring air fares, reaching Prayagraj is quite a task. The officer then highlighted the Volvo AC bus service of state-run Gujarat State Road Transport Corporation (GSRTC) for devotees, which also provides accommodation facilities. Highly recommending the bus service as an affordable and quality option for the journey, the officer presented the case of retired IAS officer Punamchand Parmar, who opted for the GSRTC package, visited Prayagraj and “returned happily” recently. Parmar, a retired Gujarat-cadre IAS officer of 1985-batch, has also written about his visit to the Maha Kumbh in the GSRTC bus on his official blog on the internet.

headline: Delhi: Man wanted for shooting at father-in-law arrested
description: On March 18, an FIR under IPC section 307 was registered at Seelampur Police Station when Dileram, a resident of Gautampuri, was shot from behind while walking home
content:
A 34-year-old man who had been absconding for nearly a year in an attempted murder case has been arrested in Delhi, said police on Sunday.
The accused, Prem Pal, was wanted for allegedly shooting at his father-in-law.
On March 18, an FIR under IPC section 307 was registered at Seelampur Police Station when Dileram, a resident of Gautampuri, was shot from behind while walking home. Investigation revealed that the assailant was his son-in-law. Despite medical treatment, Dileram succumbed to his injuries two months later, and Prem Pal had been on the run ever since.
“He knew that the police trace people through mobile phone locations, so he was constantly changing his hideouts and avoided using a phone…The team regularly checked his call data records and online IDs like Facebook, Instagram, Whats App, and bank accounts and further made efforts to trace him…The team had already conducted raids in Ludhiana, Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh to trace him,” said DCP (Crime Branch) Vikram Singh. On Saturday, he was arrested from Sahibabad in Uttar Pradesh.
During questioning, Prem Pal allegedly revealed that he had been married for eight years but frequently argued with his wife, who he believed, prioritised her family over him. Nursing a grudge, Prem Pal allegedly plotted revenge. He procured a pistol and three cartridges, inscribing the names of his wife, father-in-law, and brother-in-law on three bullets.
On the day of the attack, he intended to kill all three but only shot his father-in-law and fled.

headline: UP: FIR over videos on X ‘falsely linked to Kumbh’
description: The police's social media team found upon fact-checking that the video was related to Dhanbad where the local police conducted a lathi-charge on January 1
content:
An FIR has been registered for falsely linking some videos which were being circulated on social media platform X (formerly Twitter) to the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj, police said.
At least 14 such accounts have been identified, they said.
An old video from Dhanbad, Jharkhand, was circulated falsely linking it to the Kumbh, officials said. The posts claimed that the “Yogi Adityanath government’s police were brutally beating devotees searching for their missing relatives in the Maha Kumbh”.
The police’s social media team found upon fact-checking that the video was related to Dhanbad where the local police conducted a lathi-charge on January 1. The administration said this was an attempt to malign the image of the state government and the police and also to incite public discord.
The FIR was registered at the Kotwali Kumbh Mela police station, and legal proceedings have started, the officials said. Efforts to identify and prosecute those responsible for circulating rumours on social media will continue, they added.
The action follows increased scrutiny of social media platforms under the directive of Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police Prashant Kumar, a government statement said.
“The state government has vowed to regularly monitor social media to prevent the spread of misleading content, particularly concerning large-scale events like Maha Kumb,” the statement read.
The administration warned that strict action will be taken against anyone spreading misleading information about the Maha Kumbh.

headline: Torres scam: A month later, six held; 8 Ukrainians, one Turkish still at large
description: Over a month since the Torres ponzi scam was unearthed, there have been arrests, Blue Corner Notices, and seizures. Vijay Kumar Yadav & Sadaf Modak track the developments in the case
content:
On January 6, thousands of investors from Mumbai, Thane, Navi Mumbai, and Mira Road staged protests outside Torres’ jewellery stores in Dadar, Mira Road, and APMC Navi Mumbai after they suddenly stopped receiving their promised interest payments i n various investment schemes in late December, 2024.
Demanding a return of their investments, the investors threatened to break open the safes of the company. Soon,the police stepped in and eventually the same day, Shivaji Nagar police registered an FIR citing a fraud amount of Rs 13.48 crore from 66 different investors.
Mumbai Police’s Economic Offences Wing (EOW) soon took over the investigation. Since then, there have been arrests, Blue Corner Notices, searches and seizures, even as many more investors continue to seek answers.
Also Read | Torres ponzi scheme: Over 10,000 investors duped, fraud amount at Rs 117 crore, say police
Over a month after the complaints began pouring in, the Mumbai Police now claim that there are over 12,000 investors who have come forward reporting frauds worth Rs 125 crore and the suspected Ponzi scheme was being run by the accused company, Platinum Hern Pvt Ltd, which runs the Torres jewellery brand.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Apple iPhone 16e is here with eye on price-conscious customers, has one edge on earlier models
British-Irish woman’s rape-murder in Goa: Behind the conviction that earned investigators a ‘thank you’
The brand had showrooms in six locations in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, including Dadar, Grant Road.
Investors were lured with iPhones, jewellery
The company, incorporated in April 2023, allegedly floated multiple schemes encouraging them to buy jewellery, mainly moissanite stones or American diamonds and offered exorbitant weekly interest rates, with some yielding an annual return of up to 500 per cent.
Initially, investors were lured with incentives such as iPhones, jewellery and other expensive gifts, including branded bags, cars, and apartments. However, the company suddenly stopped paying in the last month of December 2024, causing alarm among investors.
Many investors were seen crying outside the police station as they broke fixed deposits, took out high-interest loans, and even mortgaged jewellery and homes to invest in these lucrative but ultimately fraudulent schemes. Besides Shivaji Park police station, the FIRs were registered by Navghar police in Mira Bhayander, Rabodi police in Thane, and APMC police in Navi Mumbai.
Six arrests
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The police initially arrested three persons — Tazagul Xasatova, an Uzbekistan national, who they claimed were the company’s general manager; the company’s director Sarvesh Ashok Surve and Valentina Ganesh Kumar, the store in-charge. More arrests followed with the company’s CEO Tausif Reyaz alias John Carter, alleged hawala operator Alpesh Khara and an Ukrainian national and actor Armen Atayin, nabbed by the police.
Also Read | Explained: The Torres investment scam in Mumbai, how it operated
Before their arrests, Reyaz and Surve and one chartered accountant Abhishek Gupta, were claiming that they were “whistleblowers”, with multiple emails with identical content sent out to various authorities between December 30, 2024 to January 3, 2025, claiming that the money invested was used to purchase cryptocurrency and other through other means, the money was taken out of the country in a “well-organised cross border operation”, allegedly involving foreign nationals.
Gupta also approached the Bombay High Court seeking protection, claiming that while doing an audit for the company, he came across various discrepancies and flouting of laws.
The police named nine others as wanted accused including eight Ukrainian nationals and a Turkish national and blue corner notices have been issued against them through Interpol.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Police have issued blue corner notice against suspected mastermind Olena Stoian, director of Platinum Hern Pvt Ltd, Victoria Kovalenko, Mustafa Karakoc, Oleksandr Borovyk, Oleksandr Zapichenko, Oleksandra Brunkivska, Oleksandra Tredokhib, Artem Oliferchuk and Iurchenko Igor. Mustafa Karakoc is a Turkish national while the rest are Ukrainian nationals.
The suspected Ukrainian masterminds of the Torres fraud alleged to have sent Rs 200 crore abroad in cryptocurrency form, as claimed in the emails sent by alleged whistleblowers to the police and other law enforcement agencies before the matter came to the public.
Khara was responsible for illegally converting the cash into USDT cryptocurrency, the whistleblower’s emails claimed. EOW investigators found material in the CA Gupta’s contentions and believe that the entire content and findings of the whistleblower’s emails are prepared by Gupta and other accused used it to shield them from action.
Also Read | Torres Ponzi scheme: CEO Tausif Reyaz, who claimed to be whistleblower, arrested from near Pune
The police are also investigating claims that the accused illegally brought significant amounts of gold (25kg) and silver (75kg) into the country, as alleged in the whistleblowers’ emails. The whistleblowers’ emails allege that nearly 60,000 people invested money in Torres.
Tazagul and Valentina, meanwhile, have claimed innocence and maintained that they were just employees of the company and were not involved in the business decisions. The police have also so far found that arrested accused Atayin is a Ukrainian national but had managed to get an Indian birth certificate, which when verified with the civic body was found to be forged.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
An EOW officer said, “There could be more suspects who may be involved in the mass fraud. The investigation is underway. Soon a forensic auditor may be appointed in the case to analyse the financial irregularities that took place at the Torres offices.”
‘Scam destroyed my life’
Meanwhile, the investors continue to struggle and still haven’t recovered from the shock and loss Torres scam has left them in. “I even thought of ending my life. This scam has destroyed my and my family’s life,” said Geeta Gupta, a widower from Sweri.
She added, “I already had suffered a loss of Rs 20 lakh in my life and in a desperate attempt to recover soon, I got trapped in Torres scam and lost Rs 15 lakh. I am forced to mortgage my belongings to pay for the rent of my house. I don’t know how I am going to handle things in future….”
DP Singh, one of the investors, said, “I mortgaged my wife’s jewellery and withdrew cash from my brother’s credit card. Choosing desperate ways to come out from poverty and falling prey to greed, left me poorer.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Another investor said, “I haven’t heard anything from the police yet on the refund of money. I know the legal system takes time, but at least victims investors should be communicated about the case developments or given any assurance.”
A victim investor who lost Rs 20 lakh, on condition of anonymity, said, “My husband is suffering from liver cancer and son is studying MBA. My ailing husband is unaware of the disaster his family is going under. I thought the scheme’s money would help me in taking care of my husband’s treatment, hence I mortgaged my ornaments. After discovering the fraud, I went into depression… We have left with nothing and just hope that we get our money back.”
Advocate Sunny Punamiya, representing victim investors in the case, said, “The victim investors have invested their life savings and pledged the household jewellery to invest in products and schemes floated by Torres. The numbers run in thousands if not lakhs.”
Punamiya, on behalf of investors, filed an application in the court seeking directives to police to get a forensic audit conducted to ascertain the trail of money, to issue arrest warrants against those accused who are still absconding, to identify and attach properties under MPID Act
Advocate Vivek Tiwari who is representing the alleged whistle blower and CA Abhishek Gupta, said, “A month has passed after the mass fraud surfaced, but still the WhatsApp channel of Torres is functional and some investors are still getting assurance that they would soon get their invested money with bonus. This seems to be an attempt from the culprits to distract investors and police from identifying their assets in India or abroad. The police are silent about assets of the accused company and its functionaries in India. The investigators are also silent on what happened to the huge amount Torres had given to landlords as deposit while taking stores on rent.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Besides EOW, the ED is also probing the case and trying to trace the money trail. Both the probe agencies had conducted searches at various locations linked to Torres and its functionaries. The agencies have so far seized and frozen valuables, including cash worth nearly Rs 30 crore.

headline: Gujarat Confidential: Contentious Plot
description: The proposal states that despite reminders, the “buyer” flouted the deadline and did not pay the sum that was due to the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC).
content:
A plot in Vadodara, allotted by way of a public auction in 2020 to a company “backed” by an elected representative of the ruling party, became a matter of heated contention in the Standing Committee meeting of the VMC on Friday. According to a proposal presented before the Committee, the Land Estate (Commercial) department has proposed to hand over the land to the “buyer” after collecting an interest on the unpaid amount that has been due since May 2021. The proposal states that despite reminders, the “buyer” flouted the deadline and did not pay the sum that was due to the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC). Sources said that while VMC Commissioner Dilip Rana proposed to levy an interest rate of 18% on the unpaid amount, members of the Standing Committee from the BJP contended that the interest charged should be 6%. Sources said that a heated argument ensued when Rana mentioned that a lower interest rate would amount to “misadministration” that could attract penalty in any future inquiry. The proposal was deferred by the Standing Committee with the view that it would be put forth at the coordination meeting with MLAs and MPs for recommendation to take further steps to avoid disagreements.
Making a Statement
Hours after the BJP recorded a landslide victory in the Delhi Assembly elections, party leaders in Vadodara grabbed the opportunity to “send out a message” in Karjan, which is among the local government seats to go to polls on February 16. Here, the BJP candidates are up against 16 rebel leaders, who had switched over to the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) last week after being denied tickets. To send out a “strong message”, Vadodara BJP District Unit President Satish Patel was joined by Vadodara city unit chief Vijay Shah as well as other party Taluka Presidents in bursting firecrackers and offering each other sweets at a prominent public junction in Karjan on Saturday. A senior BJP leader said, “It is a thumping win for the party in Delhi after 27 years and that too by uprooting the AAP government, which had been propagating a fallacy all these years. It is pertinent that it has come at a time when the party has suspended 26 rebel leaders in Karjan, 16 of whom have filed nominations as AAP candidates for the upcoming polls. The Delhi loss will weigh heavily on these defectors. The people of Karjan, anyway, have always placed their trust in the BJP.”

headline: Contractual workers of Navi Mumbai civic body to launch strike for equal pay, threatening essential services
description: Around 8,000 workers, covering vital services such as sanitation, water supply, and healthcare, argue that despite their efforts, wage disparities persist, with protests dating back months, including hunger strikes since December.
content:
Thousands of contractual workers in Navi Mumbai, employed by the Municipal Corporation (NMMC), are poised to launch an indefinite strike on February 10, demanding equal pay for equal work.
Around 8,000 workers, covering vital services such as sanitation, water supply, and healthcare, argue that despite their efforts, wage disparities persist, with protests dating back months, including hunger strikes since December.
The strike threatens to disrupt essential civic services, including sanitation, water supply, and healthcare.
The workers have been protesting wage disparities for several months, with some participating in a hunger strike outside the municipal headquarters since December.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
2 men from Karnataka and one from Kerala arrested for leaking Navy secrets to Pakistan’s ISI: NIA
Apple iPhone 16e is here with eye on price-conscious customers, has one edge on earlier models
The strike, led by the Samaj Samata Kamgar Sangh union, emphasizes the urgency of wage parity across municipal departments. “We work across essential services, and if our demands are not heard, we will progressively cease operations,” said Mangesh Lad, the union’s secretary.
NMMC, however, has refuted these claims, stating that it has consistently ensured fair wages, bonuses, provident fund contributions, and other statutory benefits as per the Minimum Wages Act.
The civic body also emphasized that it sought guidance from the Maharashtra government regarding wage parity for contractual workers, but no additional funds were allocated for this purpose by the state.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Following this, the municipal commissioner appointed a special committee, led by an additional commissioner, to examine the legal and financial feasibility of the workers’ demands.
The committee’s report, based on legal provisions and past court rulings, was shared with labour unions, which were then rejected by them.
While NMMC continues talks with union leaders and has pledged to protect workers’ rights, the union remains steadfast, escalating concerns over potential service disruptions.

headline: Child, 3 women killed as dumper truck falls on labourers in Gujarat
description: The dumper tried to make its way through a narrow passage and overturned, falling on a group of labourers engaged in the road construction work, Deputy Superintendent of Police SM Varotariya said.
content:
Three women and a toddler were crushed to death when a dumper truck carrying sand overturned and fell on a group of labourers in Gujarat’s Banaskantha district, police said on Sunday.
The incident occurred at Khengarpura village in the district on Saturday evening when a road construction work was underway, they said.
The dumper tried to make its way through a narrow passage and overturned, falling on a group of labourers engaged in the road construction work, Deputy Superintendent of Police SM Varotariya said.
It took nearly two hours to pull out the women and the child trapped under the truck with the help of cranes and bulldozers, officials said.
The four persons were then rushed to a government hospital where they were declared dead, the officials said.
Also Read | Diamond businessman’s son jumps divider, crashes car into bikes, killing 2 brothers
Jaideep Trivedi, medical officer at the government hospital in Tharad, said four persons were brought dead to the hospital.
The police were informed and the bodies were shifted for post-mortem, he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The deceased have been identified as Renukaben Ganawa, 24, Sonalben Ninama, 22, Ilaben Bhabhor, 40, and Rudra, 2, according to officials.

headline: ‘Trump’, ‘Snake’, ‘America Wala’: Amid US deportations, a look at songs favoured by illegal immigrants
description: Illegal immigrants to the US and other countries in the West are making reels of their journey, set to popular Punjabi songs allegedly promoting ‘dunki’ culture, and posting them on social media.
content:
In August last year, Canada-based NRI Gur Sidhu released a song titled ‘Trump’. More than six months later, the song glorifying illegal immigrants is going viral in Punjab, for all the wrong reasons. With lyrics like “Jattan de puttan nu rok sake na Trump (Trump can’t stop the sons of Jats)”, the song is now being used in deportation reels, along with the message that it seems like the US President has finally caught on.
Sidhu’s song is just one among the many that purportedly promote the illegal immigration route to enter the US and is often used by illegal immigrants who make reels of themselves scaling the wall along the Mexico-US border. Such reels show the immigrants striking their thighs, posing proudly, flashing the victory sign etc.
The song ‘Trump’ has 49 million views on YouTube. “Siddha vajya daran te Subedar tu/Kehnda keenve aaya jatta bina 7 band de/main kiha assi ni embassy vich visa mangya/Jithon lang aaye nahi saukha janda langya/Le ke aaya ni bags vich nave kapde/Sher ud aande 35 footi kandh tapke ((A subedar went straight to my house and asked, ‘How did you come without seven bands (IELTS)?’ I said, ‘We never went to the embassy seeking a visa.’ Where we crossed from, it’s not easy to pass. We did not bring new clothes packed in bags. Lions jump over 35-foot walls to reach their destination,” the song says.
Also Read | Did 33 deportees take legal route to enter intermediate nations? Gujarat cops to probe
“It is as if they won an Olympic medal after climbing the wall. This is to discourage those who follow legal routes….a mafia promoting ‘dunki’ culture is behind promoting such content on social media,” an overseas education consultant from Ludhiana told The Indian Express, speaking on the condition of anonymity.
With a US military aircraft carrying 104 Indians deported for entering the country illegally landing in Amritsar this week, the spotlight is back on the ‘dunki’ route, the treacherous journey across countries that many illegal immigrants choose to reach the US, and the songs allegedly glorifying the practice.
Sidhu, who has roots in Bathinda, released another song in November, ‘Snake’, flaunting the life of illegal immigrants in refugee camps.
Another popular song in such reels is ‘America Wala’ by singers Ravraaz and Ravi Rbs. Released five years ago, the song talks about how illegal immigrants earn more than the ones on study visas.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Kardi je maan tu study vise da. Jatt lake aaya pure 40 lakh ni/Dina vich paani e main game baliye/Bhotiyan main tareekan wala nahi/Haske na kehdi ni 2 numberi/Munda pind vich vajje America wala ni (If you feel proud of your study visa, this Jat has come after spending 40 lakh instead. I will turn the game around in just a few days. I am not the type to go on many dates (court dates of illegal immigrants). Don’t call me a fraud with a smile. In the village, the boy is called ‘America wala’,” read the lyrics.
The song further refers to a boy who spent two months in a refugee camp and paid Rs 18 lakh for the immigration bond (bail in illegal immigration case). Once he got out, he handled his work and sent money to his village every month which is equivalent to the fee of one semester of a study visa student, the song goes on to say.
The songs are just the tip of the iceberg as hundreds of videos on social media – from Facebook pages called ‘America donkey’, ‘USA wale’ etc to several Instagram handles – show how Indians are travelling across countries and entering the US, the UK and Canada illegally.
“Now, things have become stricter in America. Otherwise, such show-off was being done proudly earlier. It was discouraging for genuine aspirants,” overseas education consultant Vinay Kumar Hari, who has offices across Punjab, said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
According to France-based Punjabi NRI Sunny Sandhu, “It is time to make Punjab great and stop running after the American model. People should not follow illegal means. They need to explore opportunities in India. There is so much to do in the field of ecotourism, sustainability, organic farming, agro-based businesses etc.”

headline: DJ faces the music for refusing to exchange money, his pet dog ‘killed’; would-be groom, kin booked
description: ASI Tarsem Singh, who is investigating the case, stated that an FIR for voluntarily causing hurt, wrongful restraint and mischief by killing or maiming animal among other offences has been lodged against the accused.
content:
A would-be groom along with his guests Tuesday allegedly thrashed a DJ (disc jockey), his brother and father over a monetary dispute at a pre-wedding function at Galib Ran Singh village of Jagraon in Ludhiana district.
The accused also allegedly killed the DJ’s pet dog and dumped the carcass in front of his house.
Following the complaint of DJ Dharampal Singh, also from the same village as the accused, the Ludhiana rural police lodged an FIR against the accused identified as Varinder Singh Brar (the would-be groom), his relatives – including Kamal Guri of Galib Kalan village, Amritpal Singh, alias Amba, Davinder Singh of Galib Ran Singh village and Pammi of Talwandi Mallian village, while their four aides are yet to be identified.
Dharampal Singh stated that Varinder hired him to play music at his wedding functions. His brother Satpal Singh and father Darshan Singh came along to help him.
He added that on Tuesday night when the guests were dancing, one of the accused, Kamal, asked for some loose currency from him to throw on those who were dancing. When he refused to exchange money, the accused started abusing him.
Sensing the situation, he left the programme, but the accused intercepted him and thrashed him. Varinder and other guests also joined Kamal in thrashing him, he alleged.
Dharampal alleged that when his brother and father intervened, the accused thrashed them too. The accused later thrashed his pet dog to death and dumped the carcass in front of the house, he alleged.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
His neighbour Manna too was beaten up by the accused, when he came to their rescue. He also alleged that the accused snatched Rs 11,000 from his pocket.
ASI Tarsem Singh, who is investigating the case, stated that an FIR under sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 126 (2) (wrongful restraint), 308 (2) (extortion), 191(3) (rioting), 190 (every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object) and 325 (mischief by killing or maiming animal) of the BNS has been lodged against the accused at Sadar Jagraon police station.

headline: On US deportees’ complaints, 4 FIRs in Punjab, Haryana against travel agents
description: In Punjab, the Amritsar Rural police booked Satnam Singh, a travel agent who allegedly defrauded Daler Singh, (38), a resident of village Salem Pura who was among the deportees,
content:
Police in Punjab and Haryana have registered cases against some travel agents on charges of duping the families of some immigrants who were among the 104 people deported by the US’s Donald Trump administration for entering the country illegally. Separately, Punjab Police also constituted a four-member special investigation team (SIT) to inquire into the issue of illegal emigration and human trafficking.
Of the 104 deportees who landed in Amritsar Wednesday, 33 are from Haryana, 30 from Punjab, and two from Chandigarh. While some of the deportees and their families have since left for undisclosed locations to avoid media glare, most others have shared stories of being defrauded by unscrupulous travel agents who promised legal entry to US but instead sent them through illegal dunki route.
In Punjab, the Amritsar Rural police booked Satnam Singh, a travel agent who allegedly defrauded Daler Singh, (38), a resident of village Salem Pura who was among the deportees,
The police in Haryana also registered FIRs against three travel agents on charges of cheating and criminal breach of trust, acting on the complaints of two deportees and their family members. In the FIR registered at Raja Sansi police station in Amritsar, Daler Singh mention that he used to work as a driver before deciding to migrate to the US for a better future for his family. In 2023, his relative Gursevak Singh introduced him to travel agent Satnam Singh, a resident of village Kotli Khahera, who had promised to take him to the US in a legal way. Daler Singh further said that he raised money to pay the travel agent by borrowing from relatives and friends, besides mortgaging his farmland.
He said that he was taken to Dubai and later to Brazil. He was then taken through the ‘dunki’ route, enduring hardships like passing through treacherous pathways in the jungles of Panama before being arrested by US authorities on January 15.
Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Amritsar Rural, Charanjeet Singh said that Daler’s family pad Rs 60 lakh to the agent in several instalments, including through online bank transfer.
“Daler Singh gave us some proof to support his complaint and those were found genuine upon verification. Following this, an FIR was lodged against Satnam Singh,” the SSP said. Punjab NRI Affairs Minister Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal said that Indians who were deported from the US are not criminals but victims of crime. “Fraudulent immigration agents looted millions from them and illegally sent them to America. Today, I initiated legal proceedings against one such fraud agent,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD

I jumped over a fence in Mexico to enter the US on January 25. However, the US Police arrested me and I was deported,”
Sumit said adding he took Rs 8 lakh from relatives. “To pay the rest of the money, we offered him 1.5 acres of land, and an agreement was made for the same,” he added.

headline: Bombay HC asks BMC if domicile certified required for hawking
description: The petitioners had claimed that while there were 99,435 hawkers as per a 2014 survey, only 22,000 were verified as voters for elections held last year and were told that one of the criteria for exclusion was non-possession of domicile certificates.
content:
The Bombay High Court on Friday sought to know from BMC whether a domicile certificate was required for hawking in Mumbai to carry out business on the streets.
The court posed the question to the civic body while hearing pleas by hawkers’ unions. The petitioners took an exception to Town Vending Committee (TVC) elections held in August, last year, claiming that nearly 77,000 hawkers were excluded, which resulted in only 22,000 featuring in the final list of verified voters.
The petitioners had claimed that while there were 99,435 hawkers as per a 2014 survey, only 22,000 were verified as voters for elections held last year and were told that one of the criteria for exclusion was non-possession of domicile certificates.
“You must have a domicile certificate. We will direct them to frame that policy. Can anybody come and do business in this state without a domicile?” The bench orally questioned and sought to know if the other states had a policy requiring domicile certificates for hawking.

headline: ‘My mother died in Kumbh stampede… now I’m running from one office to another for death certificate’
description: Confusion stems from the fact that the Cantonment Board, Allahabad, has handed over the land to the Kumbh administration for the duration of the event
content:
After losing his mother in the stampede at the Maha Kumbh on January 29, Dhananjay Kumar Gond (24) returned home to Bihar’s Gopalganj — only to be told by the local administration and the police that he needed her death certificate to wrap up the formalities.
He returned to Prayagraj on Monday and has since been making desperate rounds of hospitals and government offices — but in vain.
With little clarity on who will issue death certificates, Dhananjay is one of several family members of stampede victims who have been running pillar to post in Prayagraj. Since the Maha Kumbh is being held in a cantonment area, families and officials say there is confusion about which authority would issue death certificates. The Cantonment Board, Allahabad, has handed over the land to the Kumbh administration for the duration of the event.
Tara Devi (centre) was among 30 who died in the Jan 29 incident
The state government has said 30 people died in the stampede, though an official list is yet to be released. Several hospitals where the dead and injured were taken told The Indian Express they would not share the list of stampede victims who were brought in.
Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has announced a compensation of Rs 25 lakh for each victim’s family.
Amidst the confusion, The Indian Express reached out to officials across departments to determine who would issue the death certificate.
The Prayagraj district administration said the Cantonment Board, Allahabad, would issue them as the land where the incident took place belongs to them. “Since the area where the Kumbh is going on belongs to the Cantonment Board, they would be issuing the death certificate,” said a senior official posted at the office of the Chief Medical Officer, Prayagraj.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Additional District Magistrate, Prayagraj, also said the Board will issue the death certificate.
However, the Board maintained that since the land has been handed over to the Kumbh administration, the responsibility lies with them. “We have handed over our land to the Kumbh mela administration for the duration of the fair, so they have to issue the death certificates,” said the Board’s chief executive officer, Mohammad Sameer Islam.
When contacted, Kumbh’s Additional Mela Officer, Vivek Chaturvedi, said the death certificates would be issued by the Nagar Nigam (Municipal Corporation).
However, the Additional Municipal Commissioner of Prayagraj, Ambrish Kumar Bind, said they are not responsible for issuing death certificates for stampede victims. “I have learned that the hospital where the deceased were taken will be issuing the death certificate,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Chief Medical Superintendent of Swaroop Rani Nehru Hospital (SRN), Dr A K Saxena, said they are unsure of who is responsible for issuing death certificates, but maintained the hospital won’t issue them.  Most of the stampede victims were taken to SRN Hospital.
Dr Santosh Singh, the media in-charge of Motilal Nehru National Medical College, where the postmortem facility is located, said the death certificates would be issued by the Cantonment Board since the deceased were brought dead to the hospital. “We issue death certificates only when a person dies at the hospital during treatment,” Singh said.
However, Islam, the Cantonment Board’s CEO, said the Board will issue death certificates only for persons declared dead by doctors at the hospital operating within the Kumbh campus. Islam said there is just one such hospital operating within the mela grounds, which is managed by their team.
Islam said six stampede victims had already received death certificates from the Board based on reports from that hospital. He added they have no information on who would issue death certificates for victims taken to other hospitals for treatment.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Death certificates serve several purposes, such as filing insurance claims, obtaining government benefits like pension and widow allowance, settling property inheritance, and releasing the deceased from legal and financial obligations.
‘Nothing but struggle’
“I lost my mother, Tara Devi (65), in the stampede. Since then, it has been nothing but a struggle,” said Dhananjay, her son. “On the instructions of authorities in Bihar, I returned to Prayagraj. Since then, I’ve been running from one office to another.”
Tara Devi was at the Maha Kumbh with Dhananjay and some other relatives. “Since many people from our area were going to Prayagraj, my mother wanted to go too and asked me to accompany her. It was my mistake to take her to such a crowded place,” said Dhananjay.
Their relative Saraswati Devi (70) also lost her life in the stampede. Her family is going through the same ordeal. “I was instructed by the local police in Gopalganj to get my mother’s death certificate, but no one here is giving any assurance about when it would be issued. It has been two days, and I am still waiting for clear instructions,” said her son Kamlesh Majhi.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“On Thursday, Prayagraj officials asked me to submit an application with basic details. When I did, an officer at the postmortem house told me an inquiry would be conducted before the certificate is issued. He asked me to return to Bihar and said they would send the death certificate to our residence,” he said.
Twenty-year-old Deepa, daughter of stampede victim Hukum Lodhi from Chhatarpur, Madhya Pradesh, has similarly been visiting various offices in Prayagraj to determine where the death certificate will be issued.
She arrived in Prayagraj with her aunt, Laxmi Devi, to collect her mother’s death certificate. Hukum was among a group of 14 people, including Deepa, who had come to Prayagraj for a ritual bath.
“We returned to Chhatarpur today because in Prayagraj, no one could guide us on where to obtain the death certificate. I submitted an application to the Chief Medical Officer’s office and returned home, hoping for a call soon. I also wanted to confirm whether Hukum is among the 30 people the government has declared dead in the stampede,” said Devi.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Devi recounted that during the stampede, Hukum fell due to the sudden rush and was trampled before anyone could react. In an attempt to save her mother, Deepa also fell and sustained injuries.

headline: Ex-Army Major acquitted of rape of domestic help; Delhi court orders perjury complaint against the prosecutrix
description: The court observed that the prosecutrix's testimony was “full of material contradictions and improvements” and did not “inspire confidence”. “The term ‘aggrieved’ is not confined to the complainant and there may be cases where the accused can be the real sufferer,” ASJ Kumar said in his order.
content:
While acquitting a former Army major (now 38 years old) in a case where he was accused of raping his domestic help in 2018, a Delhi court recently ordered a perjury complaint against the prosecutrix for giving a false statement before it.
“In the present case, it has been proved on record that the prosecutrix (complainant) made a false statement before this court… it would be expedient in the interest of justice that a complaint under Section 340 CrPC of the offence of perjury be sent against her to the Court of Ld. Chief Judicial Magistrate, New Delhi…,” said Additional Sessions Judge Pawan Kumar of Patiala House Court in his order dated January 3.
The court observed that the prosecutrix’s testimony was “full of material contradictions and improvements” and did not “inspire confidence”. “The term ‘aggrieved’ is not confined to the complainant and there may be cases where the accused can be the real sufferer,” ASJ Kumar said in his order.
“The reputation of any person is built over the years and it involves a lot of hard work. It takes one’s lifetime to build a reputation and a few lies destroy the same. In the attending facts and circumstances, the court is of the considered view, an acquittal simpliciter (simply) cannot compensate the agony of the accused, who had to undergo the trauma of trial for such heinous offences based on a false story of rape,” the Judge added.
Advocate Bharat Chugh, who represented the accused, argued in court that the former Army Major was being falsely implicated to extort money from him. Chugh also argued that the prosecutrix changed her statements multiple times and made a false allegation of rape after a nine-day delay.
As per the FIR, the alleged incident took place on July 12, 2018. The same night, the prosecutrix’s husband died by suicide, by hanging himself in the servant quarters which was attached to the accused’s residence.  The prosecutrix had been staying there for the last three months with her husband and two children.
Additional Public Prosecutor Manisha Singh, representing the state, argued that the nine-day delay in registering the FIR was due to the trauma caused by her husband’s death. In her statement recorded during inquest proceedings (judicial inquiry to ascertain the facts of an offence), the prosecutrix stated that her husband died by suicide due to a quarrel with her.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The FIR further alleged that around 10 pm, the accused sent the prosecutrix’s husband to the market to sell an old fridge and asked her to come to his room. On her refusal, the FIR alleged, she was forcibly taken to the room after the accused slapped her.
As per the FIR, the husband of the complainant and the accused got into a scuffle after the former saw his wife being molested. On being pushed by the accused, the complainant lost consciousness and found herself on his bed when she came back to her senses.
Pointing out that no purchaser of an old fridge would be available in the market after 10 in the night, the judge pointed out a contradiction. While in the FIR, the prosecutrix had deposed that her husband went to the market to sell the old fridge, she denied this during cross-examination by the public prosecutor.  Another contradiction noted by the court was this – while in the FIR, it was alleged that after the prosecutrix’s husband left, the accused forcibly took the prosecutrix to his room; in her cross-examination, this was absent.
The court also pointed out that during her examination, the prosecutrix was “silent” about her falling unconsciousness – which is mentioned in the FIR.

headline: On day 8 of hunger strike, Baramulla MP Rashid taken to RML hospital after health deteriorates
description: "The health condition of my father has deteriorated as his hunger strike enters its 8th day. He has been shifted to RML hospital," his son Asrar wrote on X.
content:
Baramulla MP Engineer Rashid was admitted to Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital on Friday — the eighth day of the hunger strike that he began in Tihar Jail on January 31.
“The health condition of my father has deteriorated as his hunger strike enters its 8th day. He has been shifted to RML hospital,” his son Asrar wrote on X.
An official from RML hospital said that Rashid’s condition is stable. “All his parameters are fine, including his blood pressure,” he added.
Citing “lack of representation” for 40% of Kashmiris, and denial of participation in the Budget Session in the Parliament, Rashid – the Awami Ittehad Party (AIP) chief – had late January announced an indefinite hunger strike from Tihar Jail, where he has been lodged since 2019 in a case of alleged terror funding. The hunger strike began on January 31 at 10 am.
“I have not been allowed to join the proceedings of the House even for a single day, thus leaving 40% of the entire population of Kashmir, spread over four districts and 18 constituencies, unrepresented…,” he wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and CJI Sanjiv Khanna on January 30.
“Sir, my options are very limited… I humbly request you to intervene and ensure that I am able to participate in the Budget Session. If that does not happen, I have no option, but to wake and shake the conscience of 140 crore Indians and the institutions of the country. I will go on a hunger strike from January 31, 2025… to remind everyone that my people can’t be deprived of their legitimate political rights in and outside of Parliament,” the letter read.
Rashid, who contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections as an Independent, defeated National Conference vice president and Jammu and Kashmir CM Omar Abdullah from Baramulla constituency by a margin of 2 lakh votes.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“I have a right to know why the people’s mandate is being constantly ignored, bulldozed… and insulted… I am being targeted only for my political beliefs. I am lodged behind bars because of the draconian UAPA, which has been used to silence my voice,” Rashid alleged in his letter.
Inam-Un-Nabi, Chief Spokesperson of AIP, said, “Engineer Rashid Sahib’s decision to go on an indefinite hunger strike is a desperate yet dignified response to the injustice he continues to face. We urge the authorities to respect democracy and allow him to fulfill his duties as an elected MP.”
Tihar Jail officials, meanwhile, said they will follow the prison rules while dealing with such situations. “Prisoners who go on hunger strike shall be warned that no redress of any alleged grievances shall be allowed as long as the strike continues and that they shall be liable to any prison punishment…,” the Delhi Prison Rules 2018 stated.
“It is the duty of the prison authorities to do what they reasonably can to keep prisoners in their charge in good health and to save them from death. Therefore, if a prisoner is likely to cause his own death by continuously refusing to take food, the medical officer may direct that the prisoner be forcibly fed to keep him alive. Forcible feeding shall not be attempted with unnecessary violence,” it added.

headline: NCB seizes Rs 200 crore narcotics from Navi Mumbai, 4 held
description: The NCB recovered the contraband while they were investigating a case over seizure of 200 grams of cocaine which was to be sent to Australia.
content:
The Mumbai unit of the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) seized 11.5 kg cocaine and other narcotic substances worth Rs 200 crore from Navi Mumbai and arrested four persons, officials said on Friday.
The NCB recovered the contraband while they were investigating a case over seizure of 200 grams of cocaine which was to be sent to Australia.
A team under additional director Mumbai Zonal Unit (MZU) Amit Ghawate in January seized 200 grams of cocaine.  The team found that the contraband had been sent by one Navin Chitkar based outside India. It was while investigating the local links that the police found the main accused, who had stashed the contraband at his residence in Navi Mumbai’s Belapur.
An NCB team conducted raids on January 31 and recovered 11.54 kg high-quality cocaine, 4.9 kg hybrid strain hydroponic weed/ganja, 200 packets (5.5 kgs) of cannabis gummies.
Besides the main accused, the NCB also arrested three others in and around Navi Mumbai who were allegedly part of the syndicate involved in supplying narcotics abroad.
An official said that investigation conducted so far revealed that this syndicate is being operated by a group of people based abroad. Some quantities of the seized contraband were sourced from the US to Mumbai and being sent to multiple receivers in India and abroad through courier/small cargo services and human carriers.
The official added that the persons involved in this case are anonymous to each other, using pseudo-names for day-to-day conversations on drug dealing.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Meanwhile, Union Home Minister Amit Shah congratulated the NCB for the drug bust.
“ Bharat crushes drug cartels with zero tolerance. A major breakthrough in Mumbai in seizing very high-grade cocaine, ganja, and cannabis gummies and arresting four people. It is a testament to the success of the top-to-bottom approach to investigation adopted to make PM Shri @narendramodi Ji’s vision for a drug-free India a reality. Congratulations to team @narcoticsbureau on this massive success,” Shah said in a post on X.

headline: Deportation of Indians: Police set up 4-member panel to probe illegal migration from Punjab
description: An officer said that an estimated 20,000 Indians are likely to be deported from the US in the coming days, and that many among these are likely to be from Punjab.
content:
The state police have constituted a four-member fact-finding committee comprising senior officers to inquire into the issue of illegal migration in the wake of the recent deportation of Punjabis from the United States.
Thirty people from the state were among the 104 Indian nationals deported on the C-17 US military aircraft that landed in Amritsar on Wednesday.
Gaurav Yadav, Director General of Police (DGP), informed that the panel will be formed under the chairmanship of Parveen Sinha, Additional Director General of Police (ADGP), NRI; and will include Shive Verma, ADGP, Internal Security; Dr S Boopathi, Inspector General of Police, Provisioning; and Satinder Singh, Deputy Inspector General, Border Range.
The DGP said the fact-finding committee has been directed to take appropriate action against any person found to be involved in committing illegalities and indulging in illegal migration or human trafficking.
Yadav added that the panel has been empowered to co-opt any other police officer in the investigation process and shall maintain coordination with the concerned senior superintendents or commissioners of police, who have been directed to provide all the required assistance and infrastructural facilities to the committee.
As reported by The Indian Express on Friday, based on feedback from those who were deported from the US, the Punjab police plan to launch a targeted crackdown on travel agents who send people abroad through illegal “donkey” or “dunki” routes after promising them a legal way to migrate.
An officer said that an estimated 20,000 Indians are likely to be deported from the US in the coming days, and that many among these are likely to be from Punjab. “With each illegal migrant having paid around Rs 30 lakh to the travel agents, the entire illegal ‘donkey route’ business is worth several hundred crores, if not thousands,” said the officer.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The police added that they have no information on whether other deportees will also arrive in military aircraft. “It could be that this flight was in a military aircraft to put up an ‘effect’ by the US authorities and other flights may be in chartered civilian flights,” an officer said.

headline: Western & Central Railway equip ticket checkers with body cameras
description: Ticketless travel has long been a challenge for railways, with many passengers caught without valid tickets refusing to pay fines.
content:
In a significant move to improve transparency and tackle ticketless travel, Western Railway (WR) has begun equipping its ticket checkers (TCs) with body cameras. The initiative aims to record any inappropriate incidents or disputes that may arise during ticket checks, making enforcement actions more effective and aiding in maintaining law and order.
Ticketless travel has long been a challenge for railways, with many passengers caught without valid tickets refusing to pay fines. These situations often escalate into disputes and, at times, even lead to violent incidents.
To address these growing concerns, WR is taking a proactive stance by providing body cameras to ticket checkers, ensuring better monitoring of these situations. Western Railway currently has around 1,200 ticket checkers in the Mumbai division, which includes suburban train TCs.
Vineet Abhishek, the Chief Public Relations Officer (CPRO) of Western Railway, mentioned that as part of a pilot project, body cameras have already been distributed to a select group of TCs. Over time, the cameras will be rolled out to all ticket checkers in the division.
The body cameras, which function for up to eight hours, will record video footage during ticket inspections. These recordings will be used to take action against passengers who either travel without tickets or refuse to pay the fine, under Section 140 of the Railway Act, 1989.
In addition to the cameras, WR has introduced a Pre-Custody Area at select railway stations for passengers caught traveling without tickets and refusing to pay fines. These areas, located on platforms, are designed to educate passengers on railway travel rules. If passengers still refuse to comply, they will be issued a memo and handed over to the Railway Protection Force (RPF). Pre-Custody Areas have been set up at Borivali and Andheri stations, with plans to expand to other stations in the future.
“The process of providing body cameras to bring transparency to ticket inspections has begun. This will also help deter passengers from traveling without tickets,” said Vineet Abhishek, CPRO, WR. He further added that the pilot project has already shown positive results, with a recovery increase from 20 to 80 percent in fines.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
As per the WR between April to December 2024, they collected over Rs 100 crore in fines from ticketless travelers.
Meanwhile, Central Railway (CR) also initiated a similar project last year. The CR Mumbai division has purchased 50 body cameras for its ticket checkers as part of its pilot project. However, CR officials said that they have submitted a proposal for additional cameras and expansion of the project, as the division has over 1,200 TCs. “The proposal is currently under consideration, as funding for more cameras will be required,” said the official.

headline: Ghaziabad man takes former wife to Haridwar, kills her to avoid paying alimony
description: The Ghaziabad police launched a probe after the woman’s younger sister alleged her former brother-in-law’s involvement in her disappearance.
content:
The Ghaziabad police Wednesday arrested a 42-year-old man for allegedly strangulating his former wife with her scarf, and disposing of her body in a forest in Uttarakhand.
The accused, Virendra Sharma alias Sonu, an electrical contractor, allegedly killed Madhu Sharma, 39, to avoid her paying monthly maintenance ordered by a family court, said the police.
Gyan Prakash Rai, Assistant Commissioner of Police, Modinanagr, said the First Information Report (FIR) was registered after the woman’s younger sister, Manju Sharma, filed a missing person’s complaint on January 23. Manju alleged her sister had left for her boutique in Raj Nagar on January 21 at around 9.30 am, and had not returned home and her mobile phone was switched off.
“Following the complaint, I started my own investigation and tried finding my sister. A neighbour told me that he saw her sitting in a white car with a man and that confirmed that it was her ex-husband. Meanwhile, I also found out about the court verdict and that she was to get a maintenance of Rs 5,40,000 in three instalments and an allowance of Rs 6,000 from her husband,” Manju told The Indian Express.

When they did not listen, I also sat on a dharna outside the police station,” she alleged.
“Ten days into their marriage, Virendra had started assaulting my sister. A year later, she delivered a girl who died 15 days after her birth under mysterious circumstances. In 2003, Virendra had thrown my sister in a forest after assaulting her and then a relative had informed us,” Manju told The Indian Express.
Meanwhile, the police received a tip-off, arrested Virendra from Saunda Road, and also recovered his car, in which he had allegedly taken Madhu to Haridwar. During questioning, Virendra told the police he had married Madhu on December 13, 2002, and separated in 2004.

“The couple was granted a unilateral divorce in July 2014 after years of legal battle. Madhu, subsequently, filed a maintenance case in a Ghaziabad family court. In September 2023, the court ordered Virendra to pay her Rs 6,000 a month and around Rs 5 lakh in arrears,” said an officer.
During the investigation, Virendra allegedly told the police he planned to kill Madhu to avoid these payments, and lured her into his car on the pretext of visiting Chandi Mandir in Haridwar. “Instead of taking the ropeway to the temple, he suggested they take the 3 km trekking route. While returning, about 1.5 km away from the parking site, he strangled her with her dupatta and disposed of the body in the forest and covered it with stones,” said ACP Rai.
“We have recovered the body and the Haridwar police have sent it for an autopsy. We are waiting for their reports, and it will be sent through the proper channel,” Rai told The Indian Express.

headline: Delhi Assembly polls: Turnout dips in key seats, New Delhi & Delhi Cantt among 6 that buck the trend
description: There were only six constituencies that bucked the trend. Delhi Cantonment, the smallest constituency, with just 78,893 voters, saw a massive increase in turnout, going from 45.43% in 2020 to 59.36% this time — a difference of nearly 14 percentage points.
content:
The dip in the overall voter turnout in Delhi — recorded at 60.54% this time, down from 62.55% in the 2020 Assembly polls — is reflected in key constituencies.
There are eight constituencies that saw more than a 4 percentage point dip in turnout, with Karol Bagh leading the pack (6.58 percentage points). The other constituencies that recorded significantly lower turnouts this time as compared to the last elections are Greater Kailash, Chandni Chowk, Model Town and Timarpur (see box).
There were only six constituencies that bucked the trend. Delhi Cantonment, the smallest constituency, with just 78,893 voters, saw a massive increase in turnout, going from 45.43% in 2020 to 59.36% this time — a difference of nearly 14 percentage points.

New Delhi constituency, where former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal is going up against BJP’s Parvesh Sahib Singh and Congress’s Sandeep Dikshit — sons of two former chief ministers — saw an increase of over 4 percentage points.
Security personnel guard a counting station at Gole Market ahead of counting of votes for the Delhi Assembly polls, Thursday. (Tashi Tobgyal)
According to sources in the AAP, reports from the ground have indicated that in some areas, voters from jhuggi-jhopri (JJ) clusters were discouraged from voting.
“There are some constituencies where the party had been campaigning for months in JJ clusters and had been getting a good response. But on the day of voting, several intimidation tactics by the Opposition meant that the turnout from these areas was lower than expected. headline: Interim relief to woman and daughter: Court says prima facie proof of domestic violence against Maharashtra minister, orders monthly maintenance of Rs 2 lakh
description: Apart from the interim maintenance, the court has directed that the minister shall not cause any kind of domestic violence to the woman till the final decision of the proceedings.
content:
NOTING THAT there is prima facie proof of domestic violence, a magistrate court in Mumbai has directed a senior Maharashtra minister and NCP leader to pay an interim monthly maintenance of Rs 2 lakh to his estranged partner and their daughter. The court said that while the minister had denied having any marital relationship with the woman, there is prima facie documentary evidence, including his election affidavit, which mentions their two children, daughter and a son, as his dependents.
“Therefore, it appears that the relations between them are strained and inference can be drawn that as the respondent is denying marital status of applicant no. 1, she is emotionally abused by the respondent which amounts to domestic violence. Therefore, I hold that applicant no. 1 prima facie proved that she has been subjected (to) domestic violence at the hands of the respondent,” the judicial magistrate said in the order passed on February 4.
Apart from the interim maintenance, the court has directed that the minister shall not cause any kind of domestic violence to the woman till the final decision of the proceedings.
The court noted that in 2017, the minister had executed a will, which is a notarised document, where he is accepting that the woman is his first wife and also names his second wife. Another document submitted by the woman to the court was an acknowledgement letter allegedly by the minister, stating that he married her on January 9, 1998. The affidavit submitted to the election commission during the legislative assembly elections in 2024 was also part of the documents submitted to the court. In the affidavit, the minister declared the two children from the applicant as his dependents.
“Thus, from the above said documents it appears that the respondent married applicant no. 1. Now whether the said marriage is legal or not it can be decided on the evidence adduced by both the parties. But from the above said documents the respondent admitted that, the applicant is wife and respondent no. 2 and no. 3 are their children,” the court said, adding that this establishes the domestic relations between the minister and the woman.
A statement by the minister’s lawyer states that the order was passed at an interim stage for maintenance and has no adverse finding against him.
In proceedings filed under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, the woman had claimed that she married the minister in 1998 and they have two children together, a son now aged 20 and daughter aged 19. The application said that they had a love marriage in 1998 and initially stayed in Indore, later in Mumbai and everything was smooth till 2018, after which the political leader’s behaviour began changing. The application claims that he lived outside Mumbai most of the time given his political work and that the woman came to know subsequently that he had married again. The application claims that the minister told her that he had to marry under family pressure and to maintain the family’s reputation, and assured her that she will always be given the status of being his first wife, due to which she did not complain about the second marriage.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The application claims that even though she wanted to live with him in his native place, he never permitted it citing his political career. The application makes allegations that the woman and her mother were assaulted at the behest of the minister and that her sister too was harassed. In November 2020, when she was going towards his native village, she was threatened and stones were pelted at her car by unknown persons, who she said were the minister’s followers. She said that she was also sexually abused by a helpmate of the minister.
The woman had sought relief through interim maintenance of Rs 5 lakh per month and interim compensation of Rs 25 crore from the minister, stating that she has no source of income and has responsibilities of her two children. She said that the minister’s life was luxurious and has lots of land and other properties and investments.
The minister had denied all the allegations claiming that he was never married to the woman and that there is no domestic relationship between them, hence the proceedings are untenable. He also claimed that the woman herself was the director of three companies and has the business of import export, is an insurance agent and also does other businesses. Therefore, it cannot be said that she has no means of livelihood and is entitled to maintenance. The minister has also cited that in 2020 she was restrained by the Bombay High Court from making any statement against him; however, she is violating the order.
The court said that the documents before it show that the woman has an income but considered the lifestyle of the minister. “Considering basic needs of applicant no. 1 and no. 3 (daughter), their income and the lifestyle of the respondent, I am of the opinion that they are entitled to maintenance in the nature of monetary relief, as provided under Section 20 of the Domestic Violence Act,” the court said. It noted that while both the children, named as respondents in the case, are not minors anymore, the son is not entitled to maintenance, while as per law, his daughter is entitled to it until her marriage.

headline: BDA to complete Hebbal flyover works by April 30: Karnataka Dy CM D K Shivakumar
description: Shivakumar also stated that a report will be submitted to Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on funding for Bengaluru infrastructure projects ahead of the state budget.
content:
Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister D K Shivakumar Thursday said the Hebbal flyover ramp will be ready by April 30 and inaugurated in May.
“A parallel road is being constructed near the BDA land at Hebbal flyover, and it must be completed by April 30 for inauguration in May. Contractors have been instructed accordingly. To ease congestion on the Tumakuru-KR Puram Road, BDA, Metro, and BBMP must coordinate efforts. BDA (Bangalore Development Authority) will oversee this project,” Shivakumar said during a press conference at the BMRCL office on Thursday.
Earlier, a 100-day ultimatum was issued by Karnataka Chief Secretary Shalini Rajneesh in January urging BDA to expedite the project. However, BDA officials stated that the construction has been a challenge alongside heavy vehicular traffic at Hebbal, a key junction connecting the Kempegowda International Airport and IT hubs like KR Puram.
The project involves constructing two exclusive lanes to segregate airport traffic from other vehicles.
As part of the ongoing project, two spans of the loop connecting KR Puram to Hebbal are being dismantled, causing temporary road width reductions and disrupting traffic flow. These disruptions have led to long traffic snarls, with traffic from Nagawara, Tumakuru Road, and the ORR service road merging under the flyover. Motorists currently face delays of up to 30 minutes during peak hours while navigating this stretch.
The project also includes the construction of a composite steel girder bridge, which recently received clearance from the railways for span placement above railway land. According to a BDA source, two steel girders measuring 20 metres and 38 metres are being installed to accommodate future railway line expansions planned by South Western Railways and other agencies.
Funds for Bengaluru’s development
Shivakumar also stated that a report will be submitted to Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on funding for Bengaluru infrastructure projects ahead of the state budget. “Since the state budget is approaching, discussions have been held with officials regarding necessary funding for Bengaluru’s development and irrigation projects. A report will be submitted to the chief minister on Friday,” he added.

headline: At BGBS, Mamata Banerjee urges British delegation to establish direct flight connection between Kolkata and Europe
description: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee also expressed interest in fostering a business relationship with Thailand.
content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee urged the British delegation at the Bengal Global Business Summit (BGBS) 2025 on Thursday to consider starting direct flights to Europe from Kolkata, citing the long travel time.
During an international session on Wednesday, she expressed her fondness for London saying, “I have visited so many times, but it is so time-consuming. I am also going to Oxford University in October, I have been invited. I will request you to hold a business meeting and discuss these important matters.”
The Chief Minister’s request comes at a time when discussions are on regarding the addition of more international flights and the upgradation of facilities at the Kolkata airport. An airport official said, “Talks are on regarding the addition of more international flights. Facilities in the airport are also being upgraded.”
Kolkata’s direct flights to London were discontinued on March 20, 2022, with the last flight being that of Air India. The weekly service, which often operated near capacity, was terminated. This service had been reintroduced in 2020 after a 13-year hiatus, initially offering two weekly flights, which was later reduced to one flight per week. Despite recent improvements in passenger loads, the service was withdrawn, leaving Kolkata without a direct European connection. At present, travellers have to rely on connecting flights to reach the US and Europe from Kolkata.
Banerjee also expressed her interest in fostering a business relationship with Thailand. She directly informed the Thai representative at the trade conference about her desire to strengthen these ties. “I want to go to Thailand,” she said, encouraging the Thai representative to organise business summits and invite West Bengal.
After the Thai representative, Thirapath Mongkolnavin, Acting Ambassador of the Thai Embassy in Delhi, delivered his speech, the Chief Minister added, “Thai food is very famous. Do you organize any such business summit there?” Amit Mitra, the Chief Minister’s financial advisor, noted that ASEAN country summits are held in Thailand. Banerjee further shared a personal connection, saying, “I have relatives in Thailand.”
Kolkata is hosting a two-day business summit, BGBS 2025, on February 5 and 6 to attract investments in the state.

headline: Dropped in 2024, Rs 3,984 crore Madh-Versova bridge makes a comeback into BMC budget this year
description: In this year’s budget, the BMC has made a token provision of Rs 19.75 crore for the Rs 3,984 crore cable-stayed bridge project connecting Madh Island with Versova.
content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) much-anticipated cable-stayed bridge project connecting Madh Island with Versova in Mumbai’s western suburbs has yet again found its way to the civic budget this year after it ‘went missing’ from last year’s budget. Pegged at a total cost of Rs 3,984 crore, the civic authorities also made a token provision of Rs 19.75 crore for this bridge in this year’s budget.
The idea of constructing this bridge was mooted in 2015 and tenders were floated in 2019, following which contractors were also finalised. However, the project did not take off as the Union environment ministry directed the civic authorities to come up with a new design that would reduce the impact on the flora and fauna.
A new design was created in consultation with the local fisherfolk communities who had initially opposed the project and sent to the ministry for its approval. It was only last year that the BMC received environmental clearances from the ministry.
“The project is on track now. Two contractors will be executing the work under a joint venture. We issued Letters of Approval immediately after they secured the bids. Next week, we will be holding a meeting with them, following which final work orders will be issued and work can be started,” Abhijit Bangar, Additional Municipal Commissioner, told The Indian Express.

The proposed cable-stayed bridge will pass above the Versova Creek, which is an inlet of the Arabian Sea. Even though both Versova and Madh are located in the western suburbs, there is no direct road connectivity between the two places and people use the ferry service for their daily conveyance.
However, the ferry service remains suspended for four months during the monsoon. Besides this, the only available mode of commute is a 22 km route between Madh Island and Versova through the Western Express Highway (WEH) or S V Road which usually takes 45-60 minutes during peak hours.
The cable-stayed flyover will be 1.5 km long and 27.5 m wide. There will be four lanes on the bridge, with two lanes on each side. Civic officials also maintained that to ensure minimum damage to the mangroves, temporary culverts will be created during construction works.

Although Pardeep was yet to reach home at Jarout village near Derabassi in the district, his visibly distraught family demanded a solution to illegal migration and action against the people who send youngsters abroad by taking huge amounts of money and then leave them at the mercy of the other governments.
