headline: As ‘illegal’ immigrants from US land in India today, Punjab consultants call for action against travel agents behind ‘dunki’ routes
description: Consultants in Punjab said Canada, where many Indians travel through illegal routes, would also deport such migrants.
content:
With the first plane carrying 205 ‘illegal’ Indian migrants being deported by the US scheduled to land in Punjab’s Amritsar Wednesday, immigration consultants called it a matter of self-introspection, and said that travel agents who helped them go to America should be questioned.
According to a Reuters report, the C-17 aircraft carrying 205 Indian nationals left San Antonio, Texas, at around 3 am IST. Sources said they are mostly from Gujarat and Punjab.
Nitin Chawla, executive member of the Association of Consultants for Overseas Studies (ACOS), Punjab, said, “Earlier Canada had deported Indians and now the US is doing…and they have mentioned a list of over 20,000. No doubt, we are welcoming them back home but it is a matter of self-introspection. I strongly feel that those who are coming back should be asked about the people who had illegally sent them so that action can be taken against them. Moreover, the people who went were also wilfully going through illegal ways. Hence, playing the victim card is not justified”.
“Once Canada’s government changes, mass deportation will happen from there as well … rather Canada has been following strict norms for the past many months. The US has followed Canada. Hence, the big question is how India in general, and Punjab in particular, is going to handle this influx. We don’t have jobs for the unemployed here what would happen to those who are coming back,” said Chawla, who is also the director of Kapri Immigration and Consultants.
Also Read | US crackdown fails to deter illegal migration from Punjab, Haryana
Gaurav Chaudhary from Eduplanet, an overseas education consultant based in Ludhiana, said he supports the government’s stand. “As a student visa consultant, I support the Government of India’s stand on the return of illegal migrants, as it reinforces the importance of lawful migration and global compliance. Encouraging legal pathways ensures better opportunities, safety, and stability for aspiring students and professionals.”
Vinay Kumar Hari, from Vinay Hari Education Consultant, said, “Two hundred and five people are coming back and I have heard that over 5,000 more would come back in the days to come. A number of them had crossed over through the Canadian border while many others went through illegal ways. Many parents are also contacting me that their sons have been arrested by the US police and they need help. Now, that they are coming back… it is a lesson for many others to follow legal ways to go abroad.”
Hari said an inquiry needs to be conducted “to find out the mafia behind this illegal immigration”. “As travel agents always have licenses and they always follow legal ways. Those who mint money to send people following the dunki route or other illegal ways are never registered travel agents. They change their phone numbers after a few days”.

He alleged that such “mafia” is run from many cities in the country, including in Punjab, Delhi, Gujarat and other states. “It is not a single person’s job. They take them via charter flights… through jungles and whatnot. It is high time people should understand that they should follow legal ways to move out instead of wasting hard-earned money on illegal ways”.
However, several travel agents told The Indian Express that despite the crackdown by the Trump administration, the demand for migration to the United States remains high, and that people in Punjab and Haryana would continue to enter the US through dangerous, illegal routes.
The “Dunki route” is one such way people use to cross the US-Mexico border through unauthorised paths and travel through countries in Africa and South America to reach Mexico.

headline: After UNESCO panel suspended 3 Capitol Complex projects, IIT-Roorkee gives negative report for 2
description: The three projects that were rejected were holistic development plan for the Punjab and Haryana High Court, construction of sub-terrain at the back of open hand and construction of two floors on the High Court building.
content:
A year and a half after the World Heritage Committee of UNESCO suspended three major projects of the Capitol Complex and suggested a Heritage Impact Assessment again, now the Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee (IIT Roorkee), has submitted a negative impact report for two projects in Sector 1.
After the suspension of the projects, the IIT-Roorkee was tasked by the ministry to carry out the Heritage Impact Assessment report afresh for the three projects that had received suspension. The UT had thought of moving the UNESCO again with a fresh HIA report so that their plea be considered.
The three projects that were rejected were holistic development plan for the Punjab and Haryana High Court, construction of sub-terrain at the back of open hand and construction of two floors on the High Court building.
While speaking to The Indian Express, Chandigarh Chief Engineer C B Ojha said, “We got the HIA done from the IIT-Roorkee and they have given negative impact report for two projects which are holistic development plan for the Punjab and Haryana High Court and construction of two floors on the High Court building.”
He added, “But for the construction of sub-terrain at back of open hand at Capitol Complex, they have given a positive impact.”
The first Heritage Impact Assessment report was prepared by the Mumbai-based consultant — it was positive for all three projects. Later, the UNESCO had in 2023 suspended the projects after looking at the “toolkit”. The World Heritage Committee had suspended citing that these were impacting the OUV – Overall Universal Value. The permanent protection of the heritage is of key importance to the international community.
A senior officer of the Chandigarh Administration said, “The IIT-Roorkee report has specified these projects did not qualify for the heritage impact assessment, meaning they don’t comply with the International Council on Monuments and Sites (ICOMOS) guidelines.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
UT will now re-approach the World Heritage Committee of UNESCO in 2026. The same is said to come up for discussion before the committee in 2027.
What all is in  Capitol Complex
Spread in more than 100 acres in Sector 1, Capitol Complex was the prime manifestation of Chandigarh’s architecture designed by Le Corbusier, with the Sivalik Hills in the backdrop making the sight more serene and grand. The buildings at the complex include the Open Hand monument, the high court, Tower of Shadows, Geometric Hill, the legislative assembly, and the secretariat.
Crores of funds frittered away
Funds worth crores have been splurged in the name of restoration of Capital Complex which has been going on for ages. It has been almost six years that the Chandigarh Administration has been restoring the Capitol Complex. Tenders up to Rs 26 crore were floated only for restoration. Obstructions such as hired consultant leaving the restoration work midway added to the misery.

headline: Delhi Assembly Elections: Most exit polls give BJP edge, AAP says never right
description: These may vary widely from the actual results. In the 2020 Delhi polls, most exit polls got their predictions wrong. Exit polls went wrong in the Lok Sabha elections and, more recently, in the Haryana Assembly polls too.
content:
Most exit polls on Wednesday predicted a sweep for the BJP in the Delhi Assembly elections, while three projected AAP’s return to power, and another two showed a close contest. Interestingly, many of the polls showed that Congress may open its account, after drawing a blank in the 2020 elections.
The exit polls are projections made by election survey agencies based on interviews of voters.
These may vary widely from the actual results. In the 2020 Delhi polls, most exit polls got their predictions wrong. Exit polls went wrong in the Lok Sabha elections and, more recently, in the Haryana Assembly polls too.
Read | Delhi exit polls: How accurate were they in the last three elections?
The exit polls on Wednesday were not linked to television channels. Prominent agencies like Axis My India and Today’s Chanakya said they would release their projections on Thursday.
Arvind Kejriwal and his family members show their inked fingers after casting votes during Delhi Assembly polls. (Source: @AamAadmiParty/X)
In 2020, the AAP won 62 of the total 70 seats, with the remaining eight going to the BJP.
On Wednesday, two exit polls, by Matrize and D V Research, showed a close contest between the BJP-led NDA and AAP. Matrize put BJP+ at 35-40 seats, AAP at 32-37, and Congress at 0-1. D V Research predicted 36-44 seats for the BJP and allies, and 26-34 seats for the AAP.

Six exit polls predicted a BJP victory, including a landslide win by some. Chanakya Strategies said the BJP and its allies were likely to get 39-44 seats, AAP 25-28, and Congress 2-3 seats. P Marq gave the BJP+ 39-44 seats, AAP 21-31 seats, and Congress 0-1 seats.

People’s Pulse put the BJP+ tally at 51 to 60 seats, with the AAP at 10-19 seats, and Congress at 0-1. People’s Insight gave the BJP+ 40-44 seats, AAP 25-28 seats, and Congress 0-1 seats. Poll Diary had similar numbers with BJP+ at 42-50 seats, AAP at 18-25, and Congress at 0-2 seats.
Outside polling booth in CR Park. (Express Photo by Gajendra Yadav)
The JVC exit poll said the BJP and its allies would get 39-45 seats, the AAP 22-31 seats and the Congress 0-2.
Three other agencies, however, predicted the AAP’s return to power. Mind Brink Media said the AAP would get 44-49 seats, BJP 21-25, and Congress 0-1. Wee Preside gave 46-52 seats to AAP, 18-23 to BJP and 0-1 to Congress. KK Surveys and Strategies put the AAP’s likely seat tally at 44 and the BJP at 26.

While the BJP welcomed the exit polls’ projections, the AAP rejected them. “Be it 2013, 2015 or 2020, exit polls have never been right about the AAP. Every time, the AAP has stormed to power with a massive mandate, and this time will be no different,” AAP chief spokesperson Priyanka Kakkar said in a statement.

“We welcome the results being shown by the exit polls but… on February 8, our victory will be more spectacular than what the exit polls have shown today,” Delhi BJP president Virendra Sachdeva said.

headline: Freebies or development — this Assembly elections, East Delhi is divided
description: The Indian Express visited 10 Assembly segments in the East Delhi Lok Sabha constituency – Jangpura, Okhla, Trilokpuri, Kondli, Patparganj, Laxmi Nagar, Krishna Nagar, Vishwas Nagar, Gandhi Nagar and Shahdara.
content:
While both BJP and Congress have conceded the success of AAP’s freebie narrative, East Delhi stands divided — its slum and lower middle class voters favouring freebies or subsidies offered by all the three main parties in fray but its middle class seeking infrastructural development.
The Indian Express visited 10 Assembly segments in the East Delhi Lok Sabha constituency — Jangpura, Okhla, Trilokpuri, Kondli, Patparganj, Laxmi Nagar, Krishna Nagar, Vishwas Nagar, Gandhi Nagar and Shahdara. There is palpable anger among a large number of people, especially the middle class, who live in upscale gated colonies, when it comes to freebies or subsidies offered by the AAP government — free electricity up to 200 units, free water as well as free bus rides for women, among others.
Vineet Kumar Batra, a resident of Delhi Police Apartment in Mayur Vihar 1, which falls under Patparganj constituency, thinks people are not talking about real issues anymore.
Security at a polling station at Jafrabad, Seelampur constituency, in New Delhi on Wednesday. (Express Photo: Praveen Khanna)
“This time, all parties are offering freebies… No party is talking about actual issues – encroachment, clean water, pollution and better roads… But I don’t blame them. They (parties) are also offering what the majority of the people want. People of Delhi have
become blind… they want free electricity but not good roads to walk on and clean air to breathe,” he says.
A 19-year-old resident of the society, Tanasvi, who is voting for the first time, adds, “AAP was in power for 10 years and only made fake promises…”

headline: Ex-SP MLA booked for ‘maligning’ state govt, Kumbh admin
description: Beg also alleged that the administration had failed to make adequate arrangements, leading to dissatisfaction among seers, police said.
content:
THE BAREILLY police have registered an FIR against former Samajwadi Party (SP) MLA Sultan Beg for allegedly spreading “baseless, misleading, and fabricated” rumours against the Maha Kumbh administration and the Uttar Pradesh government.
Police said Beg allegedly made the “derogatory” remarks while speaking to mediapersons.
Beg also alleged that the administration had failed to make adequate arrangements, leading to dissatisfaction among seers, police said.
Shergarh police station in-charge Ashutosh Dwivedi said the police learned about Beg’s statement through social media and an investigation would determine exactly where and when he made the remarks.

Beg has been booked under BNS section 353 (statements conducing to public mischief), 299 (deliberate and malicious acts, intended to outrage religious feelings of any class by insulting its religion or religious beliefs) and 223 (disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant), said the police. The police  also invoked the Information Technology Act against Beg.
Beg did not immediately respond on the issue.
Earlier, the Maha Kumbh police registered an FIR against seven social media account holders for allegedly spreading misinformation by posting an “old video from Nepal and falsely linking it to the January 29 stampede at Maha Kumbh.” A detailed probe is on, police said,

headline: ‘Woke up at 3 am because I was so excited’: Delhi school students volunteer at polling stations during Assembly elections
description: Thousands of students from government schools have been deployed at polling booths during the Delhi Assembly elections 2025.
content:
Class 11 student Puneet woke up at 3 am on Wednesday. He was among the thousands of student volunteers from government schools deployed at election booths to ensure a smooth polling experience as voters across the Capital stepped out to exercise their franchise.
“I am very excited. I am doing this for the first time, and every time someone thanked me for helping them, it made me happy. It feels like I have grown up. It is a big responsibility,” said the 16-year-old as he helped voters at a pink booth at MCD Primary School in Madangir village of the Ambedkar Nagar Assembly constituency.
“Our school sent us, and we will be getting Rs 800 for volunteering today. Three days ago, we trained at Kamla Nehru College. We have to help the elderly and differently abled people. We offer them wheelchairs and also help them cast their vote,” explained Puneet whose father works at a cake-making factory in Haryana.
At Satya Public School in Devli village, Satish Kuhi, 17, and Suraj Patel, 15, carefully matched names on voter IDs with those on the voting slips carried by people in a long queue. They also helped the elderly and differently abled electors.
They were also told to check the voter slips, ensure that people were not carrying their phones inside the booth and provide wheelchair service to the elderly.
The duo from a government school in Malviya Nagar said they were not provided any training beforehand. Even before they started the day’s tasks, they had to face a challenge. “There was some confusion about which school we had to go to. We were first asked to go to one polling booth and then to another. It took an hour before we were able to figure out that this was the school we had to come to. We have been standing here since morning,” said Satish.
Student volunteers Dev and Tushar said that EC officials gave them a lowdown of the entire process at the booth. (Express Photo)
For Dev, 17, a student of Govt Boys Senior Secondary School No 2, Roop Nagar, it was an opportunity to learn a key democratic practice. Keen to cast his vote as soon he becomes eligible, he asserted, “We have become a part of a process that selects the government of a state and there is nothing more exciting than this.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He was deployed at a booth near Kingsway Camp. His schoolmate Tushar Jain, 15, asserted that “the Election Commission officials made us understand the entire voting process and we understood how a ballot is cast.”
It was a learning experience for student volunteer Yogesh too. “We even learned to communicate our names in sign language,” he said.
Jiya (17), Kashish (15), and Vanshika (15) from Sarvodaya Kanya Vidyalaya volunteered at a polling booth in Pitampura Village. The girls said that they opted to volunteer to serve the people.
While Jiya aspires to become a journalist by pursuing mass communication, Kashish and Vanshika said they will opt for humanities at Delhi University. Jiya said she wanted to understand the process of election which is why she took up the role. According to Vanshika, her mother was also participating in the volunteering work which made her opt for it too.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The school students were among the 8,715 volunteers deployed by the Election Commission across 13,766 polling stations in 2,696 locations across Delhi. These volunteers were appointed to ensure a seamless voting experience — providing wheelchairs and support to the elderly and specially-abled voters.

headline: Officials: Preponing of Board dates to help students get more prep time for supplementary and competitive exams
description: The preponing of the exam calendar is a first for the Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board (GSHSEB) since its formation in 1972.
content:
In a first, the Gujarat government will be conducting the Board exams for Classes 10 and 12 in February this year. The tentative dates were announced in October. Usually the exams are held in March when the summer has set in. We explain the reason behind this decision:
Why the early exams
The preponing of the exam calendar is a first for the Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board (GSHSEB) since its formation in 1972. The exams for Classes 10 and 12 have been taking place from February 27 till March 12. Authorities privy to the decision making of early exams this year revealed that this will “give time for early admissions to the students”. Also, with the Board exams winding up early and subsequently the results too being declared early, students will get more time to prepare for the supplementary or the second exams if they have not performed well in the main examination, said the authorities. Further, students preparing for national competitive exams such as NEET (National Eligibility cum Entrance Test) and JEE (Joint Entrance Examination) for admission to engineering and medical colleges will also get more time for preparation, according to the officials.
Student registrations
This year, 14,28,175 candidates have registered for Class 10 and Class 12 (Science and general streams) Board examinations.
This includes a total of 8,92,882 registered students for Class 10,  4,23,909 candidates for Class 12 (general stream) and 1,11,384 candidates for Class 12 (science stream).

Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
According to the information, there is an increase in registration for Class 10 by more than 56,000 this year compared to March 2024. However, in Class 12 — both general and science streams — a slight decline in registered regular candidates has been recorded by the Board. Combining both streams of Class 12, 25,500 less candidates have registered this year against last year.
‘Best of two’ option open
The Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board (GSHSEB) allowing all the students ‘best of two’ options across all streams in October 2024 came as a major relief for Class 10 and 12 students.
In the 2023-24 academic session for the first time, the state education Board had given the option of ‘best of two’ for only Class 12 science stream students where they can improve their results by appearing in supplementary exams conducted in June-July. Between March Board exams and June-July supplementary exams, the students can improve their results by choosing the best of two.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
How many students to benefit
The Gujarat government had claimed that the ‘best of two exam’ initiative to “reduce the dropout ratio of students” is expected to benefit over 2.11 lakh students of Class 10 and 12. The students who have failed in the exams or could not get good results the first time for any reason will get a second golden chance by using the ‘best of two’ option.
Students who have failed or obtained low marks in Class 10 and Class 12 science and general stream will take the supplementary examination, following which the best result among the main or supplementary examination will be considered and the student will be awarded a certificate. The decision will be applicable to students appearing for Board exams in February 2025.

headline: Not sure what went wrong, say kin of those who were sent back
description: Even as the flight from the US, carrying 104 deportees including 33 from Gujarat, landed in Amritsar on Wednesday, family members of many of them struggled to make sense of the events that had swiftly transpired over the last few days.
content:

Even as the flight from the US, carrying 104 deportees including 33 from Gujarat, landed in Amritsar on Wednesday, family members of many of them struggled to make sense of the events that had swiftly transpired over the last few days.
One of them is the father of one of the deportees who is from Central Gujarat. “We are not sure what went wrong and why this deportation… We will know once she gets home. We had been out of touch for a week as she had been mostly confined there for completion of her deportation formalities. It was only three days ago that we heard from her and she told us that she was being sent back…” the man told The Indian Express on condition of anonymity.
“She is traumatised at the experience and the way her name has been flashed all over the news channels since morning,” he added.
“This is a bad experience for us,” said a man from a village in Mehsana; his son and daughter-in-law were deported Wednesday.
Refusing to divulge further details about their travel, he said, “Those who want to go will go regardless of the fact that people are being sent back…”
As per sources, the 33 Gujarati immigrants include 13 people from Gandhinagar district and 10 from Mehsana.

headline: Delhi Decides: 60.44% total turnout, North East Delhi highest at 66.25%
description: The Capital had recorded a turnout of 62.59 per cent in the 2020 Assembly polls, and 58.69 per cent in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.
content:
THE 70 Assembly constituencies of Delhi, where the AAP is seeking a third consecutive term while the BJP is hoping for a comeback after 27 years, saw a total turnout of 60.44 per cent, according to Election Commission data available at midnight Wednesday. Polling started at 7 am and continued till after 6 pm in some areas.
The Capital had recorded a turnout of 62.59 per cent in the 2020 Assembly polls, and 58.69 per cent in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.
On Wednesday, the highest turnout was recorded in North East district, which saw 66.25 per cent polling, while South East district recorded the lowest turnout at 56.31 per cent.
Also Read | Delhi exit polls: How accurate were they in the last three elections?
According to the EC’s district-wise data at midnight, the turnout was 59.09 per cent in Central Delhi, 62.40 per cent in East, 57.13 per cent in New Delhi, 59.55 per cent in North, 60.70 per cent in North West, 63.94 per cent in Shahdara, 58.16 per cent in South, 61.09 per cent in South West, and 60.76 per cent in West.
Among constituencies, North East Delhi’s Mustafabad had the highest turnout at 69 per cent while Mehrauli in South West Delhi recorded the lowest turnout at 53.04 per cent.
While the Capital’s total electorate adds up to about 1.56 crore, there are over 2 lakh first-time voters. A total of 699 candidates contested the elections, the results of which will be declared on February 8. Polling took place at 13,766 stations across the 70 constituencies in the Capital.
In the 2020 Assembly elections, the AAP had won 62 of the 70 seats, with the remaining eight seats going to the BJP.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD

The high-stakes Assembly elections in the Capital saw a shrill campaign, with the AAP, BJP and Congress announcing a slew of poll sops — including for women and the youth — in their bid to outdo each other.
While the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer said polling was conducted in a “peaceful” manner, the AAP alleged that voters were inconvenienced in several of its strongholds. It also accused the BJP of distributing money in many areas, a charge that the BJP denied.
In a statement, the Delhi CEO said: “DEOs and DCPs were made responsible for detecting and responding to any complaints or fake news emerging on social media to nip the misinformation bloom in the bud. The DEOs/DCPs through their official social media platforms gave timely responses to allegations and apprehensions raised on social media.”
“A zero-tolerance approach was adopted towards the use of money power in the elections. Enforcement agencies have made seizures worth Rs 235.78 crore since the announcement of the Delhi elections on January 7. The seizures include Rs 46.48 crore cash, Rs 5.39 crore worth of liquor, Rs 88.36 crore worth of drugs, Rs 88.56 crore worth of precious metals, and freebies worth Rs 6.98 crore from the 11 districts in Delhi,” it added.

headline: Drones to monitor sensitive state board exam centres in Maharashtra
description: Photocopying centres will also remain closed within a 500-metre radius around examination centres, the notice issued by the Maharashtra state board secretary said.
content:
The Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (MSBSHSE) announced Tuesday that it will carry out drone surveillance of sensitive board exam centres in the state.
A facial recognition system will also be employed at the exam centres to confirm the identities of examination officials like the centre director and supervisors, said the notice issued by MSBSHSE secretary Madhuri Savarkar.
Class 10 exams held by the Maharashtra state board will begin on February 21 and will continue till March 17, 2025, and Class 12 exams will be conducted from February 11 to March 11, 2025.
The notice also mentions various other instructions for exam centres. Photocopying centres will remain closed in a 500-metre radius around exam centres and Section 144 will be in place around the area of the examination centre.
District officials must also ensure that all facilities are available at the centre a day before the examinations, it said, adding that cases will be filed under the Maharashtra Prevention of Malpractices Act 1982 in case any illegal activity is detected. Video recording will also be carried out outside the examination centres.
The decisions were taken at a recent meeting attended by state Chief Secretary Sujata Saunik, Principal Secretary of School Education and Sports Department Ranjit Deol, Commissioner of Education Sachindra Singh, all collectors, senior police officials and other officers of the state.

headline: 64-year-old’s car number cloned to use his fastag by accused, case registered
description: It was after contacting his bank and probing a bit that he found that some other person had been using a vehicle on which he put up an illegal vehicle registration number that actually belonged to his car. The senior citizen then approached the local police where an FIR was registered.
content:
A 64-year-old retired man from Ghatkopar was surprised when he received messages from his bank stating his car had crossed toll nakas in Nagpur, Nashik and Karnataka and money was deducted from his fastag account. All this while his Baleno was very much parked in his own society.
It was after contacting his bank and probing a bit that he found that some other person had been using a vehicle on which he put up an illegal vehicle registration number that actually belonged to his car. The senior citizen then approached the local police where an FIR was registered.
On August 25 last year, the complainant received a message from his bank that Rs 155 had been deducted from his fastag account at the Nagpur bypass toll plaza. Over the next few months, there were a total of 12 similar transactions from toll plazas ranging from Nashik, Arjunhalli in Karnataka and Nagpur.
Eventually in December, he wrote to the bank complaining about the issue. Even after that till January 4 this year there were three more transactions made using his fastag. Eventually, the bank wrote back to him saying they had footage of another vehicle that was using the same registration number using the fastag at a toll plaza.
Realizing that someone was illegally using his vehicle’s registration number to use the fastag, he approached the local Parksite police station where an FIR was registered against the unknown vehicle driver on charges of cheating and forgery.
An officer said that they have begun investigation in the matter and are trying to track the owner of the vehicle to place him under arrest.

headline: Making Chandigarh slum-free; policy for elderly’s safety discussed at AAC meeting
description: In the meeting, various inputs were given regarding the start-up policy, skilling- and industry-related issues to boost investment, employment, and entrepreneurship.
content:
Making Chandigarh free of slums and beggars, poor health infrastructure and a comprehensive policy for safety of elderly population and differently abled in the city, were discussed during the first meeting of reconstituted Administrator’s Advisory Council (AAC). The meeting was held under the chairmanship of Gulab Chand Kataria, Governor of Punjab and Administrator of UT Chandigarh at Hotel Mountview on Tuesday. As many as 54 members from various fields participated in the meeting.
Member Dr Sanjeev Bhatia highlighted deficiencies of poor healthcare infrastructure. In the meeting, he specified that civil hospitals in Sector 45, Manimajra, and Sectors 48 remain underutilised, with only 30 per cent of their respective capacities being used. Bhatia said this underutilisation is leading to the entire burden falling on PGIMER, GMCH-32, and GMSH-16.
In the meeting, various inputs were given regarding the start-up policy, skilling- and industry-related issues to boost investment, employment, and entrepreneurship.
The members also gave suggestions for making Chandigarh ‘slum free’, ‘beggar free’ and the need to have a comprehensive policy for the differently abled and also the elderly population residing in the city.

'Main aisa aadmi nahi hoon': Samay Raina 'breaks the facade' of comedy
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Federation of Sector Welfare Association of Chandigarh (FOSWAC) Chairman Baljinder Singh Bittu raised concerns over encroachment and the growing number of beggars in the city. He mentioned that most pedestrian paths have been encroached upon. Some suggestions to enhance public safety, advanced traffic management systems and robust cybercrime prevention measures were also given.
Further, the issues of need-based changes in the dwelling units of CHB, increase in floor area ratio (FAR), revision of building bye laws, conversion of smaller industrial plots etc. to accommodate the ever-emerging needs of the residents of the city were also raised. It was also discussed that the city’s development should be aligned with the changing dynamics and requirements of its citizens.
Further, a number of useful suggestions were also given regarding developing Chandigarh as a hub for education, sports, and medical tourism.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Various initiatives regarding expanding the city’s green cover through increased tree plantation and development of more green spaces were also discussed.
Addressing the council, Kataria stated that “we need to make collective efforts to transform Chandigarh into a modern city, setting a benchmark for urban development, sustainability and citizen-centric governance”.
The administrator also emphasised the need for working together for a comprehensive roadmap for Chandigarh’s growth with focus on community participation in leading the city’s transformation by adopting innovative policy solutions.
Rajeev Verma, Chief Secretary, UT Chandigarh stated that the “AAC is a platform for discussing policy issues and initiatives to enhance administrative efficiency to accelerate the progress of the city”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Sanctity of heritage committee raised
Chandigarh Pradesh Congress President H S Lucky raised concerns over the role of the heritage committee during a meeting. This issue was raised in the backdrop of the query addressed by the Centre over the UT not being a heritage city.
The Centre had on Monday said that Chandigarh has not been designated as a World Heritage City after Congress Member of Parliament Manish Tewari raised a query in Parliament over the city’s status.
In the Advisory council meeting, Lucky asserted that the committee’s purview should be confined to the Capitol Complex; however, it has increasingly become an impediment to resolving various issues affecting Chandigarh.
Lucky further stated that the current composition of the committee often obstructs matters of public interest, underscoring the need for broader representation to ensure a more inclusive decision-making process.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Addressing key civic concerns, he urged the administrator to expedite the resolution of the city’s long-pending issues. He specifically demanded the regularisation of structures outside Lal Dora, arguing that with the integration of villages into the municipal corporation, the very concept of Lal Dora has become obsolete. Lucky strongly advocated for land pooling as the only viable solution to the challenges posed by unplanned development, emphasising that such an approach would not only curb haphazard growth but also serve as a mutually beneficial arrangement for all stakeholders.
Expansion of parking facilities in markets
Certain members in the meeting raised the requirement of expansion of parking facilities in the city markets.
It was specified that while Sector 17 has been a focal point, other markets across Chandigarh also require enhanced parking facilities to address the growing demand.
“To eliminate the problem, multi-level parking structures can be constructed. Dedicated surface parking areas can also be developed to cater to local needs. Also, the establishment of underground parking facilities beneath existing parking zones adjacent to roadways can also be considered. These solutions will help streamline traffic, reduce congestion, and ensure convenient access to market areas for visitors and traders alike,” Kamaljit Singh Panchhi said.
Traders raised the issue regarding 40 booths under new bridge In Sector 17-A and 17-B market. They specified that these booths have remained vacant since 2013, leading to a substantial loss of revenue amounting to crores of rupees. These booths have neither been auctioned nor rented out due to one key issue that they are currently on a leasehold basis with excessively high collector rates.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
It was suggested that auctioning these booths on a freehold basis at reasonable rates should be considered to attract more buyers.
Addition of another floor to single-storey bay shops
The issue of addition of another floor to single-storey bay shops and booths was also raised in the meeting.
It was specified that the current infrastructure markets in Chandigarh has a very limited scope for business expansion, which is very important as of now to accommodate the growing population and to address this issue, it is proposed that an additional floor be allowed to be constructed on the single-storey bay shops and booths in the city, which will be designated primarily for storage purposes.
Traders said that this initiative would provide much-needed relief to small traders by offering additional space without the need for encroachment. Currently, small shops measuring 8 feet x 16 feet often encroach upon verandas and corridors due to insufficient space. Allowing a first-floor addition will eliminate this problem while maintaining orderly market operations.
Farmers’ long-pending demands, water issues
Chandigarh Mayor Harpreet Kaur Babla urged the UT administrator to take immediate action on the pressing issues faced by the residents and farmers of villages in Chandigarh.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
During the AAC meeting, the mayor highlighted the urgent need for regular water connections for residents living outside Lal Dora in 24 villages of Chandigarh. These residents are currently dependent on expensive water tankers, despite having been provided electricity connections.
She urged the Chandigarh Administration to direct the municipal corporation (MC) to amend the water bye laws to facilitate legal water connections.
Additionally, Babla strongly advocated for the implementation of a land pooling policy on the lines of Punjab and Haryana for Chandigarh villages. The proposal, which was unanimously passed by the MC House in 2022, aims to develop approximately 2,900-3,000 acres of land through a structured and legal mechanism. This policy will not only curb illegal encroachments but also provide a win-win solution for both farmers and the administration — ensuring planned urban development while securing landowners’ interests, she said.

headline: Cross-border digital arrest fraud busted, 3 arrested: ‘Over 2 lakh calls made pan-India’
description: Three key players revealing international links to cybercriminals operating from Cambodia, Thailand, and Canada have been arrested as a sophisticated cross-border fraudulent network was busted, said Delhi Police.
content:
For months, thousands of unsuspecting victims across India received calls from what appeared to be government agencies — threatening arrest, legal action, and financial ruin. The only way out? A digital payment. But each victim would eventually realise that these calls weren’t from government officials, after all.
Three key players revealing international links to cybercriminals operating from Cambodia, Thailand, and Canada have been arrested as a sophisticated cross-border fraudulent network was busted, said Delhi Police. The fraudsters used Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP), an advanced technology that allows users to make phone calls and other communication over the internet, to mask their real identities. The arrested individuals had diverse backgrounds. Ajaydeep, a 32-year-old B.Tech and MBA graduate, previously worked for an NGO. Abhishek Srivastava, 34, has experience in computer and CCTV hardware repairs. Ashutosh Bora, 30, is a graduate pursuing a law degree. Police seized over 1,000 SIP numbers and calling terminals from the accused. SIP is a signalling protocol used in VoIP communications, allowing the initiation, management, and termination of voice and video calls over the Internet.
The investigation revealed that SIP trunk services had been fraudulently acquired from Indian telecom providers Jio and Tata Tele Services. That would generate Indian landline numbers which would create an illusion of legitimacy for victims, said police. The police eventually tracked down the IPs of these calls to Cambodia, Thailand and Canada, which were routed to India through the SIP trunking services.
Investigators traced the fraud back to a complaint received on December 19 through the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal (NCRP). The victim reported losing Rs 94,000 after receiving a call from a number that appeared to belong to a government agency. The fraudsters, posing as officials from the CBI and the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), claimed that her mobile number was involved in illegal activities. They threatened her with arrest unless she transferred money to accounts that were later found to be linked to cybercriminals. Following this complaint, an FIR was registered and a specialised police team was launched to look into the matter. “The operation used over 5,000 SIP numbers to make more than 2 lakh calls pan-India…The accused utilised the SIP to facilitate illegal VoIP call termination, enabling cybercriminals to impersonate government officials,” said Outer North DCP Nidhin Valsan.

Apple iPhone 16e is here with eye on price-conscious customers, has one edge on earlier models
British-Irish woman’s rape-murder in Goa: Behind the conviction that earned investigators a ‘thank you’
On January 29, police conducted raids at multiple locations in Lucknow, arresting Ajaydeep and Abhishek Srivastava. A subsequent raid on February 2 in Karnal led to the arrest of Ashutosh Bora. “Ajaydeep acquired SIP service from various providers and rented co-working offices to set up the system with Abhishek Srivastava. After setting up the SIP calling system, access was provided to Ashutosh… Ashutosh facilitated SIP service for cyber crooks abroad, involved in digital arrest, investment fraud, and other criminal conspiracy modules. During questioning, he disclosed his association with Mohammad Ali, the mastermind behind the digital arrest racket…The key accused, Ashutosh Bora, facilitated SIP services for several international cyber gangs,” explained DCP Valsan.
During the raids, police seized multiple electronic devices, including a MacBook, iPhones, Android smartphones, a desktop system, media gateway SIP trunking equipment, routers, auto-dialers, and cloud PBX soft switches.
According to the police, authorities are now working with the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to identify additional victims and track down other members of the international cybercrime syndicate. The investigation is ongoing, and officials are focusing on plugging the technological loopholes that allowed this large-scale scam to operate undetected for so long.

headline: Two arrested for committing thefts to buy drugs
description: On Monday, a tip-off from their sources indicated the accused were seen at Reay Road railway station in Sewri. A police team was dispatched, and Sheikh was apprehended immediately. However, Khan, aware of the police trap, attempted to flee through nearby bushes.
content:
Two persons have been arrested by Mumbai police for allegedly breaking into homes and shops across the city to steal cash and valuables to fund their drug addiction. The police reported that one of the accused received a tip-off about a potential police trap in Sewri and, after a chase, was apprehended aboard a running local train with the help of commuters. The arrested suspects have been identified as Arif alias Rauf Salimulla Khan alias Kubdya (35) and Firoz Farman Ahmed Sheikh (32). The duo is believed to have broken into a shop in Nagpada early on Friday, making off with cash and valuables worth Rs 1.3 lakh.
The case was registered at JJ Marg police station, where investigators managed to gather CCTV footage linking the suspects to several thefts. “The two accused were identified as habitual criminals. Since they were living on the footpath, it was challenging to gather information about them,” said an officer, adding that their drug addiction provided a breakthrough.
On Monday, a tip-off from their sources indicated the accused were seen at Reay Road railway station in Sewri. A police team was dispatched, and Sheikh was apprehended immediately. However, Khan, aware of the police trap, attempted to flee through nearby bushes.
“Our team pursued Khan, with Sheikh already in custody. Khan boarded a running train at Reay Road station, and our team followed suit, apprehending him with the assistance of fellow commuters,” the officer explained.
Following the arrest, additional police personnel were called in, and both suspects were taken to the JJ Marg police station.
The police revealed that the duo is linked to over ten theft cases across the city. “Both
are addicted to alcohol and drugs. To fund their habits, they turned to crime and have become history-sheeters,” an officer said.

headline: Cafe owner’s house heist: Police allowed interim custody of vehicle used by its dismissed constable
description: The Motor Transport Department through its additional commissioner filed an application seeking that a TUV 300, part of its fleet, is in the custody of the Sion police and is lying in the police station premises.
content:
A SPECIAL court in an order on Monday allowed an application filed by the Mumbai police for handing over of its SUV – seized for allegedly being used in a crime by a police personnel – citing shortage of vehicles for purposes like protection of VIPs. The case relates to an alleged heist at a renowned cafe owner’s home in Sion, by the accused who posed as crime branch officials. A police constable, since dismissed, who was arrested in the case, had allegedly used the SUV in the crime.
The Motor Transport Department through its additional commissioner filed an application seeking that a TUV 300, part of its fleet, is in the custody of the Sion police and is lying in the police station premises. The Sion police had seized the vehicle as part of evidence, when it arrested a police constable, Babasaheb Bhagwat, who also belonged to the motor transport department.
The additional commissioner said in the application that vehicles of the Motor Transport Department are used for various purposes like providing protection to VIPs, bandobast duties. It was further submitted that there is a shortage of vehicles in the department and the vehicle lying in a stationary condition at the police station will cause damage and unnecessary loss to the department. The Sion police also gave its no-objection to the interim custody of the vehicle to be granted to the department.
The court said that the evidence showed that the vehicle was allegedly used for abducting a person in the dacoity case and hence it was seized. “If the vehicle is kept pending in stationary condition in the custody of the investigating officer in the premises of Sion police station, it will certainly be damaged and ultimately cause loss unnecessarily to the government,” the court said granting the department interim custody of the vehicle, with various conditions including that it will not be sold or transferred till the conclusion of the trial, nor will its colour, structure will be changed, or it will be destroyed in anyway.
Properties, movable or immovable, which are part of evidence, are seized and are required in the trial for identification by witnesses.
This particular case relates to an offence under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act filed by the Sion police against 11 persons in 2024. The police had claimed that the accused had been part of a criminal conspiracy to rob Rs 72.82 lakh by posing as police officers of the crime branch and under the guise of a raid during elections in May 2024.

headline: Zero tolerance to political extortion in Maharashtra, warns Fadnavis
description: The chief minister made the remarks during an interactive session with Loksatta editor Girish Kuber at the Loksatta Varsha Ved event organised in Mumbai on Tuesday.
content:
In a stern message to political parties, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Tuesday said there will be zero tolerance to extortion in Maharashtra. Strict directives will be issued to the police force to tackle the menace with an iron hand, he added.
Although Fadnavis did not take the name of any politician or political party, he said, “I am not saying political extortion is rampant. But wherever middle-level leaders are indulging in ‘dadagiri’ it will be dealt with firmly. Every political party will also have to come forward to define the line and limits,” he said.
The chief minister made the remarks during an interactive session with Loksatta editor Girish Kuber at the Loksatta Varsha Ved event organised in Mumbai on Tuesday.
While stating that he would complete his full five-year term as chief minister, Fadnavis ruled out partnership with the Shiv Sena (UBT). “The Mahayuti with three alliance partners — BJP, Shiv Sena and NCP — together will give a strong and stable government,” he said.
Dismissing speculations regarding a possible alliance between the BJP and Sena (UBT), he said, “We already are a three-party coalition government. All the benches are now occupied. There is no space left. To the contrary we are already crowded and those amongst us have to be accommodated,” he said in lighter vein.
After the Assembly elections, he said, “Uddhav Thackeray and I may have met a couple of times at official or public events. We have had cordial exchanges. But that does not mean we are going to enter an alliance.”
Responding to speculations that he might soon move to Delhi, Fadnavis said, “My party chose me to lead the state as CM. I will complete a full five-year term and also ensure all the goals set would be accomplished for Maharashtra.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On the landslide victory the BJP received in the Assembly elections, Fadnavis said, “I would attribute it as a collective success where the BJP and alliance partners benefited from each other. Coalition politics in Maharashtra is here to continue for some time. Therefore, when we address our cadre we may talk about going solo in the next elections. But everything depends on circumstances in politics.”
He underplayed the differences within the Mahayuti, arguing, “Both Eknath Shinde and Ajit Pawar are seasoned politicians. We have good understanding which helps in governance. The differences which are often hyped are not related to policies or administrative work.” “There may be some exceptions when it comes to individuals or party level issues,” he admitted, responding to the ongoing power tussle over guardian ministership in Nashik and Raigad districts.
Outlining the roadmap for Maharashtra, Fadnavis said, “The success at the World Economic Forum at Davos with investment of Rs 16 lakh crore showed the state was the most preferred destination amongst global and domestic investors. The investors are confident about our government and its stability.”
“We have initiated reforms towards ease of doing business. A single window clearance through MAITRI portal will remove all the existing hurdles making it investor friendly. Empowering the single and integrated approach for issuing clearance across multiple departments through one window,” he explained.

headline: Pune Inc: How a Pune couple aims to reduce carbon footprint of construction industry
description: The startup, Ready Structures Associates LLP, uses innovative ways to reduce or replace up to 70 per cent of steel reinforcement in concrete while maintaining the same structural strength in construction methods.
content:
A small model of a house sits in the offices of Ready Structures Associates LLP in Pune’s Karve Nagar – a quiet tribute to an innovation for the construction industry. Founded by Shweta Kamble-Ugale and Ravindra Gadre, the startup provides sustainable infrastructure solutions for green buildings and environment-friendly infrastructure.
“Our forte is a patented technology with the potential to make a deep impact on the building construction and infrastructure industry, driving it towards a more sustainable future,” says Shweta Ugale, who is assisted by her husband Tanmay Ugale.
Funded by Startup India and patented in 2023, the innovation is aimed at reducing or replacing up to 70 per cent of steel reinforcement in concrete while maintaining the same structural strength, thereby impacting conventional construction methods. The firm is searching for space on Sinhagad Road to set up a factory where they can scale up the model into a prefab house as a prototype.
Also Read | A strategic step, a boost for social sector — Pune Inc voices its support for Union Budget 2025
“Additionally, the reinforcement can be made using eco-friendly materials such as bamboo and fiberglass, further enhancing sustainability,” says Shweta.
According to the UN Environment Programme, the buildings and construction sector is “by far the largest emitter of greenhouse gases, accounting for a staggering 37 per cent of global emissions”.
“Concrete, by itself, doesn’t have any strength. Every house we stay in, all the roads and so on have reinforcement in the form of steel bars. That is what gives it more strength,” says Tanmay. The company decided to experiment and, while trying multiple combinations, they created one in which they are able to save 70 per cent weight of the steel and achieve the exact strength of regular form.
While the company is squaring up to the challenge of bringing the innovation into the market, they have identified a few sectors for applying the innovation, such as prefabricated houses and other structures, precast walls, roof panels, floor panels, highway trenches, and drain or gutter covers and manhole covers. “Manhole covers are frequently broken by miscreants in search of the steel inside. In a manhole cover, 60-70 per cent of the cost is steel and the rest is concrete. The innovation we have created reduces the amount of steel by 70 per cent or even replaces it with fiberglass or bamboo, among others,” she says.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
She says that, as an architect, she is also concerned about the LEED rating, which is a benchmark for evaluating the environmental quality of buildings. “One of the challenges that architects face is that they do not have many products that have sustainable material or are energy efficient and can come easily under the LEED rating. This is a gap that our technology hopes to fill,” says Shweta.

headline: BMC Khichdi scam: Bombay HC grants bail to Aaditya Thackeray’s aide Suraj Chavan, says trial unlikely to conclude soon
description: As per Enforcement Directorate, Chavan was suspected to have been involved in financial irregularities linked to distribution of ‘Khichdi’ to migrant workers during Covid-19 pandemic.
content:
The Bombay High Court on Tuesday granted bail to Suraj Chavan, aide of Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, booked by Enforcement Directorate (ED) in Khichdi scam involving irregularities worth over Rs 6 crore.
A single-judge bench of Justice Milind N Jadhav directed that he be released on a provisional cash bail of Rs 1 lakh immediately. Chavan is also permitted to provide one or two sureties of the same amount within four weeks from his release from prison.
During the bail period, Chavan is restricted from leaving Maharashtra without permission of the trial court and he shall not influence any witness or tamper with evidence and also inform the ED about his current contact details, the High Court said.
As per ED, Chavan was suspected to have been involved in financial irregularities linked to distribution of “Khichdi” to migrant workers during the Covid-19 pandemic. The ED said Chavan was placed under arrest because he failed to explain the links and did not cooperate in the probe.

Chavan had approached HC after the special PMLA court had rejected his bail plea in September, last year.
He was arrested on January 17, last year and was subsequently lodged at Arthur Road jail (Mumbai Central prison).
Senior advocate Ashok Mundargi, representing Chavan, alleged that there was no case made out by prosecution based on its allegation that lesser weighing food packets were supplied and the bail applicant was merely targeted as he was a political functionary in the then existing political dispensation led by the then chief minister Uddhav Thackeray, with an allegation that Chavan played vital part in procuring work orders.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The court noted that the situation related to allegation of applicant being in an influential position in state “no longer prevails in current dispensation (CM Devendra Fadnavis-led government)”, and therefore, the “apprehension of tampering with evidence can be redressed by imposing appropriate conditions” while granting bail.
Justice Jadhav observed that Chavan has been incarcerated for more than one year and prima facie, the trial of the scheduled offence and consequently Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) offences are “not likely to be completed in foreseeable future.”
The High Court observed that charges are yet to be framed and considered by special court and “there seems no possibility that trial would be concluded in reasonable time” as there are 20 prosecution witnesses to be examined in the case.
“If applicant’s detention is further continued, it would amount to infringement of his fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution of a speedy trial and guarantee of personal liberty,” the court held.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The court also noted that Chavan, who has cooperated with the probe, was not named as accused either in the predicate offence (registered by Mumbai Police) or in ED’s case. It said the trial is not likely to start in predicate offence, and hence the trial in PMLA offence cannot be commenced.
The ED had alleged that Chavan had requested BMC officials to issue work orders to the firm, Force One Multi Services. The HC observed that “if at all it is the prosecution case that there is any illegal act on the part of the vendor (the firm) to provide under-weighing food packets, prima facie, there is no material placed on record through any official document of the MCGM to substantiate this allegation which is clearly evident from the chargesheet.”
Granting bail to Chavan, Justice Jadhav directed him to report to the investigating officer in ED office once in every month on specific date for the first three months and thereafter as and when called. It asked him to cooperate with the conduct of trial and not to take unnecessary adjournments during the same.

headline: Deve Gowda seeks Centre’s nod for second airport in Bengaluru amid Tamil Nadu’s push for one in Hosur
description: Former prime minister HD Deve Gowda made the appeal in Rajya Sabha on Monday. Bengaluru’s Kempegowda International Airport is projected to reach its maximum passenger-handling capacity by 2033.
content:
Emphasising the need for a second airport to meet the needs of Bengaluru, Janata Dal (Secular) MP and former prime minister H D Deve Gowda on Monday requested Union Minister of Civil Aviation Ram Mohan Naidu to approve the Karnataka Government’s proposal for the same.
Gowda’s appeal came during the Question Hour in Rajya Sabha amid the ongoing Budget session after AIADMK MP Thambidurai sought the establishment of an airport in Tamil Nadu’s Hosur.
Gowda said, “The Karnataka government has already proposed the construction of another airport and has discussed the matter with the minister. The situation has reached an advanced stage… I am not opposing what Tamil Nadu is saying, but there is a challenge that needs to be addressed. We must carefully consider how to resolve this issue.”
He added that Karnataka’s plan to build an additional airport should also be taken into account, given the growing demand for air connectivity. “The existing international airport which I sanctioned is struggling to cope with the increasing passenger traffic, and Karnataka is actively considering solutions to meet this demand,” he said.
Also Read | Significance of the new international airport announced in Tamil Nadu’s Hosur
Responding to the request, Naidu said, “Bengaluru airport is getting saturated and busier day by day. There are talks of a second Bengaluru airport. As and when the site gets decided and comes to us for site clearance, we will take it forward.”
Thambidurai had raised concerns over the growing air traffic congestion at Kempegowda International Airport in Bengaluru due to which flights are being diverted to Chennai in times of fuel emergency. He stated that while the demand for an international airport in Hosur is growing, a clause in the concessional agreement prohibiting the construction of another airport within a 150-km radius of Bengaluru airport until 2033 is a challenge. He also requested the Centre to ‘cancel’ this agreement which is hindering the establishment of a new airport in Hosur.
Naidu, in his reply, stated that the establishment of a new airport in Hosur can be done only with an active stakeholder discussion involving the Karnataka government, Tamil Nadu government and the Bengaluru International Airport Limited (BIAL). “The central government has been assisting in this effort but one of the key challenges is the 150-km radius restriction from Bengaluru airport, which makes the situation more tricky,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
According to M B Patil, Karnataka’s Minister for Infrastructure Development, five sites have been shortlisted for the second Bengaluru airport, including Dabaspet, Nelamangala, Bidadi, Harohalli and another new location.
Kempegowda airport is projected to reach its maximum passenger-handling capacity by 2033 and its full cargo-handling capacity by 2040. With the city’s rapid growth and increasing air traffic, a second airport is seen as a necessary step to avoid future overcrowding and delays. Meanwhile, the concessional agreement between BIAL and the civil aviation ministry mandates that no new or existing airport shall be permitted by the Government of India to be developed as, or improved or upgraded into, an international airport within an aerial distance of 150 km of the airport before the 25th anniversary of the airport which would be in 2033.
Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister D K Shivakumar had earlier stated that the new airport must meet international standards and serve as a world-class facility. He cautioned against building a second airport solely to compete with Tamil Nadu’s planned facility in Hosur, which is located near Bengaluru. “We must create an airport with global standards, spread across 5,000 acres of land,” he reportedly said.

headline: Union Budget 2025-26: Mumbai local train services to increase by 10%
description: In addition, improvements to the signalling system are underway to reduce the gap between trains, with plans to decrease the current headway of 180 seconds to 150 seconds, and later to 120 seconds.
content:
Union Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced that the number of local train services in Mumbai will increase by 10 per cent in the near future.
He made the announcement while highlighting major projects announced in the Union Budget that will benefit the state, especially the Mumbai suburban railway network.
Currently, there are 3,200 local train services in Mumbai and the number is expected to increase to 3,500. Mumbai locals are set to become more comfortable and convenient for passengers as railway authorities are working on manufacturing trains with new designs to provide a smoother ride with less vibration and more air circulation.
In addition, improvements to the signalling system are underway to reduce the gap between trains, with plans to decrease the current headway of 180 seconds to 150 seconds, and later to 120 seconds.
Along with expanding the rail services in the state, new tracks, new terminals and extension of existing tracks will be undertaken. A tripartite agreement has been made for the completion of these projects. According to the agreement, the state government, Indian Railways and RBI will collaborate, with the RBI covering the costs incurred by the state government in the joint schemes.

headline: Inquiry process of Kharadi urban property survey on Feb 6 and 7
description: According to information provided by Diwase, the urban survey of Kharadi city, included in the extended area of Pune Metropolitan Municipality, was decided in 2007 but due to technical reasons, the proposal remained in abeyance.
content:
The inquiry process for the Kharadi urban survey is scheduled for February 6 and 7, said state Land Settlement Commissioner Suhas Diwase. Kharadi has approximately 13,300 properties, all of which will be included in the inquiry process.
The detailed survey work was completed in 2023 by government staff as well as a private organization (Mr. Monarch Surveyor Pvt. Ltd). Modern equipment such as drones were employed for an accurate and detailed survey.
According to information provided by Diwase, the urban survey of Kharadi city, included in the extended area of Pune Metropolitan Municipality, was decided in 2007 but due to technical reasons, the proposal remained in abeyance.
The department will use City Survey Enquiry Software (CSES) for the inquiry process. The map of each property in Kharadi village, its area, and the holder will be finalized by visits to the actual site.
Sixty Deputy Superintendents of land records/urban survey officers in the subordinate districts of Pune division and employees of the Pune Municipal Corporation will be carrying out the inquiry process. A notice was issued to 7/12 extract holders in Kharadi about the same on January 20.
After the completion of the process, the finalized records and property cards will be made available online. Diwase said once the survey is over, citizens can get benefits such as geographic information system (GIS)-based maps of the holder’s rights, records, and property cards will be available. A map of the properties with latitude and longitude will be available.
Diwase said the civil rights of the citizens will be protected and procuring loans against properties will be possible as the rights records are prepared in the form of property cards.

Diwase also said that GIS maps will help the PMC in urban planning, disaster management, tax collection, building permits, water supply, encroachment removal and other city planning activities.

headline: AAP & Cong created fake votes for illegal immigrants, says BJP
description: Amit Shah failed to stop infiltrators, AAP retaliates.
content:
With just two days left for the Assembly elections in the Capital, the political war of words escalated on Monday as the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Congress of “manipulating” the electoral system by “creating fake votes for Rohingya and Bangladeshi immigrants” in Delhi. The AAP shot back, saying that the claims were proof that Union Home Minister Amit Shah has “failed to control infiltrators in the country”.
Addressing a press conference, BJP’s national spokesperson Sambit Patra claimed that a JNU research report reveals how Rohingya and Bangladeshi immigrants from Myanmar “have severely impacted Delhi’s geographical infrastructure.”
Patra alleged that the influx of Bangladeshi and Rohingya immigrants has led to a “demographic” shift in Delhi and the city is no longer the same as it was 10 years ago. He also said that these migrants have “unlawfully” taken over job opportunities meant for workers from Purvanchal and other states in the construction sector. “The earnings that should have gone to our brothers and sisters from Purvanchal and other states are now being redirected to Bangladeshi and Rohingya migrants. There is no documentation of this. Behind all this is political protection, particularly from AAP and Congress. By creating fake voter identities, they are manipulating our electoral system,” he claimed.
Patra also accused AAP and Congress of “patronising” and “shielding” these illegal immigrants. Further, he urged voters to consider their children’s future while casting their votes and to recognise those who oppose the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) while allegedly honoring those involved in the 2020 Delhi riots.

headline: RSS held 50K drawing room meetings in Delhi ahead of Assembly polls
description: RSS work in Delhi is divided among eight vibhags (zones), catering to 30 districts and 173 nagars (city, a small unit).
content:
In a parallel manner with the BJP, it was the RSS machinery that was busy campaigning in its own way in the Capital in the run-up to the February 5 polls. According to a report received from its eight vibhags – the zones that Delhi’s RSS unit is divided into – on Monday, nearly 50,000 drawing room meetings have been organised to “educate voters”.
“Our work was focused on educating voters to go to the booth and vote in national interest. But yes, we were asking to vote for BJP, as they are working in national interest,” said a senior RSS functionary from western Delhi.
RSS work in Delhi is divided among eight vibhags (zones), catering to 30 districts and 173 nagars (city, a small unit).
Even before the dates for Delhi polls were announced, each vibhag was asked to hold “drawing room meetings” in small groups in localities, offices, institutions, shopping centres, schools, colleges and other areas.
The RSS had a target to hold 60,000 meetings in all, said sources, adding that pracharaks who work in frontal organisations but have their headquarters in Delhi, were also asked to remain active in Delhi.
At every level (vibhag, district, and nagar), regular meetings were held to take feedback on the drawing room meetings. The last such meeting was held on Monday at every vibhag. Following this, each vibhag pracharak will share data of his vibhag to the prant (state) unit.
After the meeting, one of the prime functionaries belonging to a vibhag told The Indian Express, “In my vibhag, nearly 2,000 drawing room meetings were held by Sangh swayamsevaks and nearly 4,550 by workers of other anushangik (frontal) organisations like Bhartiya Mazdoor Sangh (BMS), Sewa Bharti, Vishva Hindu Parishad, Akhil Bhartiya Shaikshik Mahasangh, Hindu Jagran Manch and units…”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He added that around 53,000 participants, including a large number of women, participated these drawing room meetings.
On an average, over 4 lakh people attended the 50,000-odd drawing room meetings, said sources.
In these meetings, RSS’ ‘panch parivartan (five changes)’ were discussed and voters were asked to vote “for BJP candidates” in the national interest. Issues like environmental pollution, family values, corruption, social harmony and Swadeshi, among others, were also discussed, sources said.
Since the last few years, particularly since the 2014 Lok Sabha polls, the role of RSS has become very crucial for the BJP ahead of every election. In the recent Haryana polls, the BJP won 48 of 90 seats while in Maharashtra, the Mahayuti alliance — comprising BJP, Shiv Sena (Shinde), and NCP (Ajit Pawar) – won 237 of the 288 seats. After the polls, RSS had claimed credit for those victories in particular.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
An RSS functionary said that while they have done a “lot of work in Delhi”, not many efforts have been made to reach out to those who are not part of the fold. “Still, I am sure, our work will help BJP in a big way here.” RSS’s sah-sarkaryawah Arun Kumar, looking after BJP, held meetings in different parts of the city to oversee the work.

headline: Maha Kumbh Mela: No stampede FIR yet, police begin probe by analysing visuals
description: The incident left 30 dead and 60 injured. Hundreds of thousands had gathered at the Sangam Nose for a holy dip when the stampede occurred.
content:
EVEN AS a judicial probe is underway, the UP Police have also launched an inquiry into the stampede on January 29 at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj on Wednesday, analysing images and videos of the area. The incident left 30 dead and 60 injured. Hundreds of thousands had gathered at the Sangam Nose for a holy dip when the stampede occurred.
Uttar Pradesh DGP Prashant Kumar said agencies are analysing related video footage. He said the matter is “under review”. Several photographs and videos purportedly linked to the stampede surfaced on social media.
No FIR has been registered yet for the stampede.
Chief Minister Yogi Aditynath ordered a judicial probe into the matter and said a separate inquiry would be conducted by the UP Police. The three-member judicial probe team is headed by retired Justice of Allahabad High Court Harsh Kumar. The other two are former DGP V K Gupta and retired IAS officer D K Singh.

headline: PCMC chief rules out dismantling BRTS lanes
description: Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Commissioner Shekhar Singh said city gets 'cent percent' treated water
content:
Despite growing opposition, Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Commissioner Shekhar Singh, who is also the administrator of the city, on Monday ruled out the possibility of dismantling the BRTS lanes to allow more space for surging vehicular traffic as per citizens’ demands.
“There is no question of doing away with BRTS lanes. We will never remove them,” the PCMC chief said when asked about the citizens’ demand to remove it, at least on the Pune-Mumbai highway stretch where Pune Metro’s popularity was growing by the day.
Singh said all efforts were being made to strengthen BRTS and the entire public transport system. “There should be more buses on the road, more routes and less private vehicles. We should encourage public buses and discourage private vehicles from coming on to the roads,” Singh said during an interaction with The Indian Express on Monday.
The opposition to BRTS has been growing in Pimpri-Chinchwad, especially after the Pune Metro service was flagged. Citizens have been complaining that the road width has shrunk with BRTS and the Metro occupying one side of the highway stretch and the smart city footpath project being implemented on the other side.
During his interaction, the PCMC commissioner spoke on a range of issues including the way PCMC was handling guillain-barre syndrome (GBS) cases, the city’s expansion needs, water supply, drainage system, growing traffic congestion and garbage disposal system.
Regarding the Metro ridership, Singh said he was confident that as the Metro network expanded, the ridership would increase further.
”When it comes to Metro systems, there is something called the network effect. As the network expands, the ridership grows. As we have four-five more routes, the Metro ridership will grow for sure. We have to make all efforts to ensure last-mile connectivity. Steps have already been taken on that front,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In the wake of the detection of the GBS case in Pimpri-Chinchwad, Singh denied allegations that citizens were not getting 100 percent treated water. ”This allegation is not true. We are treating water cent percent, purifying it and then supplying it to citizens. This is done at both Ravet and Chikhli treatment plants. But yes, I agree that issues might crop up if a drainage line which runs close to the drinking water pipeline develops problems. But to say that we are not treating water 100 per cent before supplying to citizens is not true,” he said.
As for the tankers supplying water, the PCMC chief said the civic administration does not control the private tankers. ”But in view of the GBS cases, we might now intervene and ensure that the wells are disinfected… But I want to stress that the majority of the residential societies do not use tanker water for drinking purposes. There might only be a handful of them doing so… Going forward, we might have to take a call regarding monitoring private tankers,” he said.
The PCMC chief also ruled out the possibility of the civic body taking care of the hazardous industrial waste in Pimpri-Chinchwad-Bhosari industrial area. ”That is looked after by the MIDC which carries the waste to Ranjangaon. PCMC does not interfere with it,” he said.

headline: 6 dead after luxury bus carrying pilgrims from MP falls into gorge in Gujarat
description: Over 24 severely injured passengers are being treated at Surat’s New Civil Hospital. ‘Every week, two accidents occur, and mostly, heavy-loaded vehicles overturn into the gorges,’ said the Malegaon village sarpanch’s husband.
content:
The death toll in the accident of a luxury bus carrying pilgrims from Madhya Pradesh which fell into a gorge in Dang district early Sunday went up to six, with one injured woman succumbing at the Surat Civil Hospital on Monday.
She has been identified as Shantiben Bogha (50) who was from the Shivpuri district, where five others who had died at the spot were also from. They had been identified as the driver Ratanlal Jatav (41), Bholaram Kushwana (55), Guddi Yadav (60), Bijendra Yadav (55), and Kamlesh Yadav (60).
Over 24 passengers who were severely injured were shifted to Surat’s New Civil Hospital on Sunday afternoon, while the remaining were admitted to Shamgham PHC.
The bus, carrying over 42 passengers from Trimbakeshwar in Nasik (Maharashtra) to Dwarka in Gujarat, plunged into a 25-foot-deep gorge after breaking the protection wall near the Forest Department rest house at Malegaon at 4.30 am on Sunday.

An FIR was lodged against the deceased driver for alleged rash and negligent driving.
The local BJP MLA and deputy Chief Whip of Gujarat Legislative Assembly Vijay Patel told The Indian Express that he had made a representation to officials in Gandhinagar “to widen the roads and make corrections in the sharp curve to prevent such regular accidents.”
When the incident came to the notice of Sapurata police, police inspector R S Patel called up the sarpanch of Malegaon village, Tanmayben, and her husband Devram Thackrey and informed them to reach the spot.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Devram Thackrey said, “We have a group of 20 youths of our village who are always ready to do rescue operations. The road climbing down (Ghat areas) from Saputara to Malegaon is quite narrow, and there are even sharp curve turns, as a result of which, we regularly witness accidents of heavily loaded vehicles going from Nashik to Gujarat. We are equipped with rescue equipment, such as bed sheets tied to bamboo sticks to lift injured passengers, as well as vehicles and ropes to go deep into the gorge. After getting calls, our team of 20 youths immediately reached the spot and carried out rescue operations. Before police could arrive, we shifted 20 patients from the spot to nearby Shamgham PHC (Primary Health Centre). Later, within a couple of hours, all the surviving passengers were rushed to the hospital.”
Thackrey said, “Every week, two accidents occur, and mostly, heavy-loaded vehicles (coming from Maharashtra Nasik to Gujarat) overturn into the gorges. We have, many times, complained to the District collector, police officials, political leaders, and others, but to date, nothing has been done.”
One of the travellers, Brijesh Bhargav, lodged a complaint against the deceased luxury bus at Saputara police station on Sunday evening. Police registered offences under BNS sections 281, 125(a), 125(b), 106(1).
Bhargav, in his police complaint, said that around 200 passengers, all from Shivpuri and neighbouring districts in MP (Madhya Pradesh), had been on the religious pilgrimage from December 23 onwards in four luxury buses. He alleged that the driver “lost control over steering.”
