Engineers of the National High Authority of India (NHAI), the District collector, and top police officials reached the spot.
Speaking to The Indian Express, Dang BJP MLA Vijay Patel said, “Regular accidents take place in the 9-kilometre area from Malegaon to downwards. The area falls on the National Highways, and we have been regularly making requests to widen the roads and make changes in the sharp curve areas. I will also make a representation to the state government, and also talk to the higher officials of NH at Gandhinagar on Tuesday.”
Navsari district police superintendent Yashpal Jagania said, “We have deployed GRD guards at different sharp turns, which are accident-prone areas. We have also talked to the highway authorities… The accused bus driver could not see the sharp turn.”

headline: Haryana minister Anil Vij sharpens attack on CM Nayab Singh Saini, releases photos of his ‘detractors’
description: Apart from Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, Anil Vij also slammed BJP president Badoli.
content:
Sharpening his attack on Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, senior Minister Anil Vij Monday released photos of workers who were allegedly with his opponent Chitra Sarwara during the 2024 Assembly polls. In a tough contest, Vij had defeated an Independent candidate and former Congress leader Sarwara with a margin of 7,277 votes.
On Sunday morning, Vij shared a video clip on his X account which has photos of a local BJP leader Aashish Tayal with Saini. According to Vij, Tayal claims to be a close friend of Saini and their numerous photos are available on Facebook. “Those workers who were seen with Aashish Tayal during the Vidhan Sabha polls were also with BJP rival Chitra. What is called this relation? Tayal is still a close friend of Saini, then the question arises who orchestrated opposition to the BJP candidate,” said Vij in the post.
When contacted by The Indian Express, Tayal said he worked for the BJP during the Haryana Assembly elections. “The BJP workers who are seen with me have a lot of photos with Vij also. Some of them are still with the BJP while some of them have deserted the party and went with Sarwara during the polls. The leader (Vij) should see why they deserted the party because he has been a minister for the past 10 years.”
Tayal said he has been with the Bharatiya Janata Party for the past nearly 15 years, and was a district BJP treasurer until recently. “Three to four days ago, I saw a post on social media that I have been discharged from the post. I don’t know the reasons,” Tayal added.

headline: After ‘honey village’, Maharashtra Khadi Board to start first ‘honey park’ in Mahabaleshwar
description: The first ‘Madhache Gaav’ or ‘honey village’ was set up in the Manghar village near the hill town of Mahabaleshwar in May 2022.
content:
After successfully implementing its ‘honey village’ concept, the Maharashtra State Khadi and Village Industries Board (MSKVIB) said Monday it will set up two ‘honey parks’ in the state to start ‘honey tourism’. The first ‘honey park’ will be inaugurated Tuesday in Mahabaleshwar, according to officials.
The Directorate of Beekeeping Industry, under the Board, set up the first ‘Madhache Gaav’ or ‘honey village’ in the Manghar village near the hill town of Mahabaleshwar in May 2022, followed by Patgaon in the state’s Kolhapur district. Officials said since the launch of the ‘honey village’ in Manghar, the village has witnessed more than 1,00,000 visitors every year, and this has significantly increased the income of the villagers.
As part of the Republic Day celebrations, the Maharashtra Government displayed a tableau featuring its ‘Madhache Gaav’ project in New Delhi. The Maharashtra Government has declared that one ‘Madhache Gaav’ will be developed in every district of the state.

“This is the first of its kind initiative to set up a honey park. It will be on the premises of the Directorate of Honey in Mahabaleshwar. It will have at least 30 live honey beekeeping boxes which will be put in three acres of its land,” said Ravindra Sathe, Chairman, MSKVIB.
Sathe said there will be a honey-extracting machine, swarm net, equipment for the production of queen bees, pollen traps, and other items. “This will help in giving a practical demonstration to all those who want to start a beekeeping business. This will be developed into a honey tourism destination. There will be a pilot beekeeping project at the park and create awareness about beekeeping and honey bees,” he added.

The project is being implemented through CSR funding from Everest, a spice company. The funding of Rs 6 lakh will be used to start honey parks in Mahabaleshwar and at Sanjay Gandhi National Park in Mumbai’s Borivali. The Board also plans to create one such park in every ‘honey village’ that it will develop.
“The Directorate of Beekeeping in the state is the only directorate in the country as there is no such directorate in any other state. We want to make it a centre of excellence. We are also organising a state-level conference of beekeepers on May 20 on Honey Bee Day,” said Sathe.

headline: Sunita Kejriwal to Mausmi Gahlot: Meet the spouses of Delhi’s poll candidates on the campaign trail
description: Last year, when the AAP chief was in jail for six months in connection with the excise policy case, it was Sunita who led the party’s charge in the run-up to the Lok Sabha polls.
content:
Mausmi Gahlot has been a busy woman for the past month. A practising lawyer, she has spent at least five-six hours each day attending public gatherings and going door to door to convince people to vote for her husband — former Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Kailash Gahlot. He made headlines last November when he resigned as minister from the Delhi Cabinet, quit the AAP, and joined the BJP the next day. His new party has fielded him from Bijwasan. He has represented Najafgarh for two terms.
Sunita Kejriwal is no stranger to campaigning for her husband, Arvind Kejriwal. Last year, when the AAP chief was in jail for six months in connection with the excise policy case, it was Sunita who led the party’s charge in the run-up to the Lok Sabha polls. The ex-Indian Revenue Service (IRS) officer is back on the electoral field again, attending meetings with RWAs and requesting people to vote for the former CM.
The two women are among several family members of Delhi’s poll candidates who have been working in the background, garnering support, in the run-up to the high-stakes Assembly election on February 5.
Mausmi Gahlot spends at least five-six hours each day on the ground in Bijwasan. Her husband, Kailash Gahlot, has been fielded by the BJP from the seat.

This is Mausmi’s first time aggressively campaigning for her husband, who is up against AAP’s Surender Bharadwaj and Congress’s Devinder Sehrawat.
“During the last election, my younger daughter was in Class 12, so I could not spare much time. But ever since the BJP declared my husband as its candidate from Bijwasan, I have been on the ground…,” she tells The Indian Express.
“I prefer door-to-door campaigning to public meetings because I can interact with people, listen to their problems, and assure them that it will be solved — if they give the BJP and my husband a chance to serve them,” she adds.

She has been focusing on posh colonies such as Vasant Kunj with a key aim to “get people in upscale areas to vote”. She has also covered the slum clusters nearby — Arjun Camp, Shankar Basti, Rangpuri Pahadi — to speak to residents.
“In one such interaction, a woman told me that bus rides are free but drivers often don’t halt for them… she even sustained injuries while trying to flag down a bus. Sometimes, Mausmi says, she also steps in for her husband at public meetings when he is busy with other campaigns or is late and stuck in traffic.
“On such occasions, I tell people that Kailash is a good husband, father, brother, and son… He is passionate about working for the people… I tell them about the good work he has done as a minister in the AAP government and to give him a chance this time, so he can now work for them as part of the BJP government… I also tell them why BJP’s double-engine government is important for Delhi.”

headline: Solving Crime: Falsely arrested for rape-murder of his wife, how a Bengaluru man’s 11-year quest for justice bore fruit
description: Call detail records, brain mapping and luminol tests helped the police crack the 2013 rape-murder of the 43-year-old woman with the arrest of three men, including the former manager of the bank where her husband worked.
content:
A Bengaluru man was falsely accused and arrested for the rape and murder of his wife in 2013, and it took 11 years for the police to nab the culprits after they reopened the case.
After the police filed a closure report in the rape and murder case, he approached the Karnataka High Court seeking directions to reopen it. Following the court’s order, the police launched another probe, and identified the killers using call detail records and brain mapping technology. They found that the man’s former manager at the bank where he worked, and two others were responsible for the rape and murder of the woman.
Speaking to the media in 2022, the bank employee talked about the “traumatic time” when he was arrested for the murder and rape of his wife. “In April 2015, I was unnecessarily called multiple times to the police station in the name of questioning. My daughter, who was in Class 12, used to accompany me. I was being mentally tortured in the name of questioning while my daughter was forced to sit and study in the police station.”
The case is currently in trial, with the police relying heavily on technical and scientific evidence.
woman goes missing, body found in eucalyptus grove
After his wife did not return home after work on February 12, 2013, and her mobile phone was switched off, the bank employee filed a missing person report at the local police station. The body of the 43-year-old woman, who worked at a research firm, was found by some local residents in a eucalyptus grove by the Bengaluru-Doddaballapur highway three days later.
Suspecting it could be the wife of the bank employee, the police asked the man to identify the body. He arrived at the spot and confirmed that it was his wife’s. The post-mortem of the body revealed that the victim had been sexually assaulted.
There was no progress in the case for nearly three years and the police then started suspecting the husband. In May 2015, after summoning him for several rounds of questioning, they visited his house and claimed to have found a few bloodstains on the floor. Based on forensic reports, the police stated that the blood samples found at the complainant’s residence were of his wife. The police arrested him on charges of murder, alleging that he killed his wife at the house and dumped her body in the grove.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
But he was released after spending 73 days in jail as the police could not establish any evidence against him. The police filed a closure report, absolving him of the charges, and the case hit a dead end.
As his wife’s rape and murder remained a mystery, the bank employee approached the Karnataka High Court in 2015 seeking re-investigation and action against the police for wrongly arresting and torturing him.
Decade-old call detail records lead to killers
The court directed the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) to take up the case. Investigating officer Narendra Babu M R, currently Nelamangala rural police inspector, recalled that although the case was reopened, there were no leads until Additional Director General of Police (ADGP) B K Singh discovered something suspicious in the call detail records (CDR).
Another police officer, who was part of the probe, said, “It was clear that the body was brought to the grove from elsewhere. We questioned the family members and friends of the complainant. We also checked those who owned three-wheelers and four-wheelers then. However, the police did not get any leads and submitted a closure report to ADGP B K Singh. While reviewing it, Singh noticed something unusual in the CDR of Narasimha Murthy, a former manager of the bank branch where the victim’s husband had worked.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Deepak, the third accused in the rape-murder case (Express Photo)
The police initially questioned Murthy because he was a family friend of the woman, and the CID had collected his CDR. “On the day the woman went missing, Murthy sent 11 text messages and made several phone calls to a specific number. The recipient’s location indicated that he had visited the grove on the same day the woman disappeared,” the police officer said.
The police also said Murthy knew the victim well, and they were allegedly in a relationship.
The police discovered that the calls were made to Deepak Channappa, who was a snooker trainer at a recreational club where Murthy was in charge of maintenance.
Recalling the breakthrough, Narendra Babu said, “It was probably the last attempt to solve the case. Then, we picked Deepak for questioning, but his responses to our questions were not concrete. We decided to subject him to brain mapping and polygraph tests during which he gave even the smallest details of the crime.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
During the questioning, Deepak revealed that besides Murthy and him, another worker at the club, Hariprasad, was also involved in the crime, the police said.
A police officer said, “On February 12, Murthy picked up the victim in his car to take her to the recreational club. He raped her, probably drugging her, and then Deepak and Hariprasad, who had come at his invitation, also raped her. They strangled her using her shawl when she threatened that she would complain to the police. Later, they stuffed the body in a gunny bag, Deepak took it in Murthy’s Maruti Alto, and dumped it in the grove. Murthy collected updates through messages and calls regarding whether the body was disposed of in an isolated location.”
After Deepak, the police conducted brain mapping and polygraph tests on other accused, too. They later confessed to the crime, as per the police.
While Murthy sold his Alto car after the crime, CID located the vehicle’s new owner. In a stroke of luck for the police, he had not replaced the upholstery of the seats. The forensic team then cut open the backseat, and during a luminol test, they discovered that a portion of the woman’s blood had soaked into the sponge.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Forensic investigators use luminol tests to detect trace amounts of blood at crime scenes. It relies on chemiluminescence, emitting a blue glow when it reacts with iron in haemoglobin. Through a luminol test, a forensic investigator can detect very old bloodstains, even if they are washed away or not visible to the naked eye, said a police officer.
In May 2024, the CID submitted a 1,277-page chargesheet, including statements from 84 witnesses. “This case mainly depends on technical and scientific evidence as the crime occurred more than a decade ago. We are hopeful that justice will be served,” a police officer said.
Asked if the accused were surprised when they went to arrest them, Narendra Babu said they were expecting it. “They were following the developments in the case closely. They knew that someday police would reach them,” he added.

headline: Framing of charges against ex-principal, others to begin soon
description: The special court in Alipore is set to begin framing the charges after the CBI submitted all the relevant documents on prime accused Dr Sandip Ghosh, the former principal of RG Kar Medical College and Hospital and other accused.
content:

headline: 3 more GBS cases in Pune, case count rises to 158
description: Dr Pawar appealing to citizens not to delay treatment if symtoms of GBS surface.
content:
Pune on Sunday reported three new suspected cases of Guillain Barre Syndrome (GBS), taking the case count to 158. Of these, 38 patients have recovered and been discharged from various hospitals.
Dr Eknath Pawar, dean of B J Medical College and Sassoon General Hospital, has appealed to citizens not to panic and immediately seek treatment if they have symptoms.
So far, five suspected deaths of GBS have been reported while of the 158 suspected patients, authorities have diagnosed 127 patients as confirmed GBS cases. State health authorities said 63 serum samples have been sent to the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences, Bengaluru, for Antiganglioside antibodies testing.
Also Read | How Pune’s 6-year-old survived Guillain-Barré Syndrome and came off ventilator support: Know all about his recovery journey
The test is done to detect the presence of these antibodies in the serum that can help diagnose and monitor the progression of these neurological disorders. GBS is a rare neurological autoimmune disorder that produces antibodies which attack the body’s nerves. It is a sequela of either gastrointestinal or influenza-like illness, several experts have said.
While investigations are underway to ascertain the exact cause of the outbreak, several blood and stool samples have been sent for testing to ICMR-National Institute of Virology in Pune. The latest findings show that four samples were positive for campylobacter jejuni infection (which is often transmitted through contaminated food or water), 21 for norovirus, one for EBV while dengue, chikungunya, zika virus and SARS-CoV2 virus was ruled out across a majority of samples tested at the institute.
At private hospitals, doctors have said that samples of some of their patients sent for tests had detected the infection with campylobacter jejuni bacterium.
Meanwhile, according to state health department officials, a total of 31 patients are from Pune Municipal Corporation, 83 from newly added villages in PMC area, 18 from Pimpri-Chinchwad Municipal Corporation, 18 from Pune rural and eight are from other districts. While 38 have been discharged, 48 are in ICU and 21 are on ventilator.
Dr Pawar said five patients in the 21-33 age group diagnosed with Guillain Barre Syndrome were discharged from Sassoon General Hospital on February 1.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Also Read | GBS outbreak in Pune: Private water tanker services found to be supplying contaminated water in city
“A 29-year-old man from Bhimnagar, who had loose motions, developed weakness in both his upper and lower limbs. He was unable to walk when he was admitted to Sassoon General Hospital. After receiving five cycles of plasmapheresis, his condition has improved and he was discharged on February 1,” said Dr Pawar.
Other patients—a 22-year-old woman from Ahilyanagar , another 25-year-old woman from Sinhagad road, a 33-year-old man from Wadgaon Budruk and a 21-year-old man who had similar symptoms, recovered after early treatment and were discharged from Sassoon General Hospital. “We had 28-30 patients and hope to discharge more patients in the next two to three days,” added Dr Pawar appealing to citizens not to delay treatment if symtoms surface.

headline: Nil tax on income up to Rs 12 lakh: Some call it a game-changer, others say it will boost disposable income
description: However, some are confused about the tax they will have to pay if the salary goes beyond Rs 12 lakh.
content:
The announcement by Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in her Budget speech that there would be no income tax payable up to an income of Rs 12 lakh annually has drawn praise from salaried individuals as well as the corporate sector with some calling it a “game-changer”. The move on Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) – whereby the annual limit on rent has been raised from Rs 2.40 lakh to Rs 6 lakh, benefiting small taxpayers receiving smaller payments – has also been hailed.
“Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has proposed sweeping tax reforms for the middle class in the Budget 2025… Those earning Rs 12 lakh will save up to Rs 80,000. For an income of Rs 12 to 25 lakh, the benefit is Rs 70,000 to Rs 1,10,000, which accounts for 25-30 per cent of their tax liability under the current rates.
“This savings on tax will boost discretionary spending of the middle class which will surely boost the economy. The government is targeting to increase the GST (Goods and Services Tax) collection with this Income Tax reform,” Gaurav Bora, a Pune-based stock market expert, told The Indian Express minutes after the Budget was presented.
Echoing a similar view, Anil Pillai, Director, Terragni Consulting, said, “It’s clear that the government is striving for a balance between fiscal discipline and growth stimulation. Notably, the adjustments in personal income tax – particularly the recalibration of thresholds and deduction regimes – aim to ease the burden on middle-income earners while ensuring that higher earners contribute a fair share. This move is expected to bolster disposable incomes for many, although it may also reduce the progressivity of the tax structure.”
Rohit Gera, Managing Director of real-estate company Gera Developments, said, “The changes in personal tax slabs and rebates will significantly boost disposable income, enhancing homebuyers’ affordability. With more disposable income available, buyers can allocate higher amounts toward EMIs, enabling them to purchase larger homes or homes in better locations.”
Gera said dual-income families aiming for homes priced between Rs 80 lakh and Rs 1.25 crore will experience the most significant affordability improvement. “Given that homes typically cost between four to five times annual income, families in this segment would need an income of Rs 16-20 lakh for an Rs 80 lakh home and Rs 25-30 lakh for a Rs 1.25 crore home,” he added.
Pravin Rayate, a salaried employee, said this was the first time that a Union Budget had shown such care for the salaried class. “The income tax waiver for those having up to Rs 12 lakh annual income is certainly a big relief for the salaried class. And this has not been done with an eye on the election. It clearly reflects that the government intends to give genuine relief to the salaried class,” he added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Havgi Ambegave, 21, shop owner, though, is disappointed with the Budget. “I had expectations from this Union Budget that the government would provide tax relief up to Rs 15 lakh. This would have ensured that middle-class people like us, after the 30 per cent tax deduction, would have a decent amount left to cover our expenses such as house rent, electricity bills, and home expenses, and the remaining amount could be invested in some scheme, SIP, or mutual funds. In this budget, the government has provided relief up to Rs 12 lakh, but it should have been extended to Rs 15 lakh.”
“The Rs 12 lakh tax-free income is a game changer, boosting consumption and middle-class savings. With infrastructure, policy reforms, and capital infusion as four growth engines, India accelerates towards prosperity. This is not just a Budget; it is a blueprint for a stronger self-reliant India,” said Kirang Gandhi, Pune-based financial mentor.
However, there is also some confusion among the salaried class whether they will have to pay tax as per the slabs if their salary exceeds the Rs 12 lakh mark. “I am really confused about how much tax I will have to pay if my salary exceeds the Rs 12 lakh waiver mark. What if my salary is Rs 13 lakh? Will I have to pay tax on Rs 1 lakh of Rs 13 lakh? The FM needs to clarify,” said K Dhanavate, a resident of Pimpri-Chinchwad.
Throwing light, retired income-tax officer Sathyan Iyer said, “Under the new tax regime, individuals earning up to Rs 12 lakh annually will not have to pay any income tax. As per the rejig, for people earning more than Rs 12 lakh per annum, there will be nil tax for income up to Rs 4 lakh, 5 per cent for income between Rs 4 and 8 lakh, 10 per cent for Rs 8-12 lakh, and 15 per cent for Rs 12-16 lakh.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“A 20 per cent income tax will be levied on income between Rs 16 and 20 lakh, 25 per cent on Rs 20-24 lakh and 30 per cent above Rs 24 lakh per annum.”
Iyer added there is zero income tax up to an income of Rs 12 lakh per annum, “but if income is more than Rs 12 lakh, tax liability will be calculated from Rs 4 lakh on slab rates.”
Lower class feels ignored
Prashant Tiwari, 46, an artificial flower vendor from Shivaji Nagar, shared his disappointment, “We belong to the lower class… The Budget proposed in the Parliament is only for middle-class people, upper-class people, and all above them, but nothing for lower-class people, why is it so? Every time, the lower-class people are ignored. I sell artificial flowers near the signals at a very low rate. The government should announce some schemes for us.”
Anil Pawar, 73, an auto driver from Wakdewadi, also expressed his frustration, he said, “I have been driving an auto rickshaw for years to take care of my family – my wife and two kids. We live near the New ST Bus Stand in Wakdewadi, and every day is a struggle to manage our daily expenses. I was hoping that this budget would bring some relief for auto drivers like me, but there is nothing for us. No reduction in fuel prices, no support for lower-class people that could have helped us save a little. The lower-class people like us need more affordable healthcare, lower electricity bills, and some tax relief on daily essentials like food grains and cooking gas.”

headline: Ashamed to admit abroad that national capital lacks basic amenities: Jaishankar ahead of Delhi polls
description: "Water, electricity, cooking gas cylinders, houses and health are your right. The people of Delhi did not get their rights in the past 10 years," S Jaishankar said.
content:
Union Minister of External Affairs S Jaishankar Saturday trained his guns on Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and said that during his meetings with foreign leaders, he feels ashamed to admit that people residing in Delhi are deprived of basic amenities like houses, gas cylinders and Ayushman Bharat scheme.
Addressing a gathering of the South Indian community at JLN stadium ahead of Delhi Assembly elections, Jaishankar said leaders in abroad curiously want to know from him about schemes like houses for the poor, free ration, gas cylinders provided under the Ujjwala scheme and various other initiatives in the country. He said that the number of people who have been provided houses in the country is more than the population of Japan, while those getting cooking gas cylinders are larger than Germany’s population.
“I, however, hide one thing… I feel ashamed to tell them that in the capital of India, people don’t get benefits of houses, gas cylinders and the Ayushman Bharat scheme,” the BJP leader said while claiming that these Central government initiatives were not implemented by the AAP government in Delhi.
The BJP’s Sankalp Patra with Rs 2,500 per month to women, Atal canteen and free treatment for the senior citzens above 70 yrs and other benefits were promised under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s guarantee, the external affairs minister said.
Even as the capital should have been a model of the “best things happening in the country”, it lacks all of these for the past 10 years, he said, adding that this will pave AAP’s exit from government on February 5 when the Delhi Assembly goes to the polls.
“Water, electricity, cooking gas cylinders, houses and health are your right. The people of Delhi did not get their rights in the past 10 years. So on February 5, they will decide if this government should remain in power or not,” he said.
AAP, BJP and Congress are locked in triangular contest for February 5 elections, the result of which will be declared on February 8.

headline: Elect a triple-engine govt in Delhi: Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami
description: Encouraging voters to choose BJP candidates, Dhami added, “You have already installed one engine by electing us in the Lok Sabha. Now, you must install another engine in Delhi and create a triple engine in Matiala for better governance and development.”
content:
Addressing a public gathering in Matiala in support of BJP candidate Sandeep Sehrawat, Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami urged voters to elect a “triple engine government” in Delhi.
“For 27 years, non-BJP governments have ruled Delhi, leading to mismanagement. Today, Delhi is suffering from mountains of garbage and a polluted Yamuna. Talking about the central government’s biggest achievements, Dhami said the abrogation of Article 370 and the consecration of the Ram Temple were significant milestones under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership.
On the implementation of the UCC, Dhami described it as a necessary step for a state deeply connected with spiritual and religious traditions. “Uttarakhand, the land of Ganga Maiyya, has taken a historic step by implementing UCC. Now, there is no triple talaq, no halala in Devbhoomi Uttarakhand,” he stated.
Dhami also touched upon issues of law and order, referring to the 2022 Shraddha Walker murder case in Delhi. “We have ensured that such heinous crimes will not be repeated. No one will be able to commit such acts of brutality against innocent girls,” he said.

headline: Gujarat gang of hackers has accomplices in major Indian banks: Crime Branch
description: It said that the accused not only made illicit gains by hacking websites of various companies, but also duped players of online betting platform RummyCircle.
content:
The Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) of Ahmedabad city police that busted a three-member gang of hackers on Thursday, has now said that the accused have accomplices in at least four major corporate banks who helped them crack the alphanumeric code during the transaction process. of a gaming platform. It said that the accused not only made illicit gains by hacking websites of various companies, but also duped players of online betting platform RummyCircle.
Their accomplices, as per the DCB, helped the hackers dupe players of the gaming platform by sending them unique transaction reference (UTR) codes. UTR is an alphanumeric code, which is generated when money is digitally transferred from one bank account to another. DCP (Crime) Ajit Rajian said that the gang members lured the bank employees with money. The names of these banks have been withheld by The Indian Express on request of investigators.
“It has been found that the accused targeted the website of RummyCircle, and a notice will be sent to the online gaming platform,” the DCP added.
The Crime Branch had started an investigation after the websites of PNG Jewellers, and robu.in, an online electronic goods store, were hacked by the accused. They would purchase items from the websites either for free or at nominal prices by using some de-bugging software and tampering with the payment gateway process. The accused would then sell those items at higher rates and make illicit gains. The accused allegedly confessed to having cheated the companies of Rs 7 crore so far.
Following the arrests, investigators found that the accused were also involved in the betting platform scam.
Explaining their modus operandi, an official said: “First, players deposits a certain amount of money in their gaming account. They then redeem this amount to obtain chips and play the game. The modus operandi of the accused was to intercept this process. As soon as a bank transaction was made on the betting app, a bank employee would send the UTR code to the gang members. The accused would redeem the amount deposited by the player and then transfer the same to their own bank account.”
The arrested accused include Vijay Amra Vaghela who used the de-bugging software to hack websites and place product orders. The second accused, identified as Nitesh alias Chotu Sitaram Narayan Madata, used to sell the products. The third accused, Adil Vijay Parmar, was involved in gambling.

An investigator told The Indian Express, “We have learnt that the arrested accused had enticed employees of at least four major banks. The employees would send them UTR codes so that they could intercept transactions on the gaming app. Further investigation is underway.”
During interrogation, the Crime Branch further learnt that the three accused had managed to hack about 10-12 such merchant (e-commerce) websites and officials are now reaching out to them to obtain more details and warn them. Inspector Dipak Dhola, meanwhile, revealed that the gang had attempted but failed to hack the website of Joyalukkas Jewellery.
Investigators also found that some “advanced electronic items ” were purchased by the accused from robu.in at nominal prices. “These appear to be of Chinese origin,” said DCP Rajian, adding that officials are trying to find out what these electronic items were used for.
The remand of the accused is ending on February 2. Officials are likely to seek further remand from the local court.

headline: Union Budget 2025-26: FM Nirmala Sitharaman announces ‘Mission for Pulses’ as import bills soar
description: ‘Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses’ will have a special focus on tur, urad, and masoor.
content:
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman Saturday announced the launch of a six-year ‘Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses’ with a special focus on tur (pigeon pea), urad (black gram), and masoor (red lentil) during her Budget speech.
The announcement came after India’s import bill for pulses witnessed a year-on-year increase on the back of a deficient monsoon.
While welcoming the government’s move, Ganesh Nanote, a farmer from the village of Nimbhara, in Barshitakli taluka of Akola district in Maharashtra, said assured prices for pulses would encourage growers.
Nanote, who is cultivating pulses on seven out of his total 22 acres, said the present mandi prices are around Rs 6,000-6,500 per quintal. “This does not meet the production costs – what we need is surety of prices. The government has talked about procurement through its agencies. However, the quality parameters are extremely tight. They should be relooked,” he said.
India’s pulses imports were valued at $3,275.25 million during April-November 2024, a 56.6 per cent jump compared to the same period in 2023. The country’s pulses imports fell from a peak of $4,243.13 million in 2016-17 to $1,943.89 million in 2022-23. But this was reversed in 2023-24, with imports amounting to $3,746.78 million. The current fiscal (2024-25) could see pulses imports scale a new all-time-high. Domestic pulse production is still largely rainfall-dependent. The poor 2023 monsoon led to lower domestic production and higher imports this year.
Grown mostly in the rain-fed areas of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Rajasthan, pulses especially tur suffer from vagaries of nature. Lower-than-expected yields and low prices have been major issues with pulse growers. India had reported 109.99 lakh hectares of pulse sowing area in the crop year of 2024-25, which was a sharp drop from the 274.94 lakh hectares of 2023-24. In the last five years, the largest acreage was reported in 2021-22 when pulses were sown over 307.31 lakh hectares.
Keeping the spectre of climate change in mind, the Mission has put its emphasis on the development and commercial availability of climate-resilient seeds, enhancing protein content, increasing productivity, improving post-harvest storage and management, and assuring remunerative prices to farmers, noted experts.

headline: Phone calls offering MPSC exam question paper for Rs 40 lakhs: 3 arrested
description: The MPSC is conducting examinations for Group B (Non-Gazetted) Services on February 2 across the state.
content:
Pune city police have arrested three people in connection with a case relating to phone calls asking aspirants to pay Rs 40 lakh in order to question papers for the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC), ahead of the exams.
Police have identified the accused persons as Deepak Gayaram Gaydhane (26), Sumit Kailas Jadhav (23) and Yogesh Surendra Waghmare.
Dr Suvarna Kharat, secretary of MPSC, lodged the first information report (FIR) in this case at the Bund Garden police station on Friday.
The MPSC is conducting examinations for Group B (Non-Gazetted) Services on February 2 across the state. Thousands of students are appearing for the examination.
But, in the last few days, some students from Pune received calls on their mobile phones from a person claiming to be an employee of “Rohan Consultancy” in Nagpur, who offered to provide them with question papers for the scheduled MPSC examination on payment of Rs 40 lakh.
An audio clip of this phone call went viral on social media, causing a major disturbance among candidates appearing for the MPSC examination. To prevent any panic, MPSC’s secretary Suvarna Kharat held a press conference in Navi Mumbai on Friday, saying that no question papers had been leaked.
Kharat also filed a formal complaint with the Pune city police. Subsequently, the crime branch sleuths initiated a probe into it. Based on clues obtained during the investigation, cops arrested Deepak Gaydhane, a native of Bhandara district and Sumit Jadhav of Nashik district, from Chakan area in Pune. Their mobile phones were also seized.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Further probe revealed that Gaydhane and Jadhav are factory workers, who got hold of a list of 24 candidates appearing for the MPSC examination, from one Yogesh Waghmare of Nagpur on January 24, 2025. The duo had then contacted at least two candidates whose contact numbers were mentioned in this list, police said.
A police team was dispatched from Pune to Nagpur to arrest Waghmare. Taking swift action, Nagpur police nabbed Waghmare and handed him over to the Pune cops on Saturday.
Deputy Commissioner of Police (crime) Nikhil Pingle of Pune city police said that so far there is no evidence to show that MPSC question papers may have been leaked.
“An investigation is on to know from where the accused got a list of the candidates appearing for the MPSC examination. We are probing whether they got this information from any coaching classes. We suspect the involvement of more persons in this crime. So far, we have not found involvement of any MPSC staffers in this case,” said Pingle.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Police have booked the accused persons under section 62, 318 (4), 353 (1), 353 (1)(b) of the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita (BNS) for allegedly cheating the candidates and causing fear and panic among a section of society by spreading false information.
Assistant commissioner of police Rajendra Mulik produced the accused Gaidhane and Jadhav before a magistrate court in Pune on Saturday.
Public prosecutor Dilip Gaikwad sought police custody of the two accused for 14 days for further investigation. Police are probing the mobile phone calls and financial transactions of the accused persons. Police suspect the role of an organised group that wanted to cheat multiple candidates. The court remanded Gaidhane and Jadhav to police custody till February 7.

headline: MSU board declines ex-VC’s request for time to vacate official bungalow; varsity reverts to teachers’ contract recruitment
description: A member of MS University’s Board of Management said they also decided to clear the service books of deans which former vice-chancellor V K Shrivastava had not signed since 2022.
content:
Nearly a month after his resignation, the Board of Management (BoM) at MS University on Friday turned down a request by former vice-chancellor V K Shrivastava seeking three months’ time to vacate his official bungalow. The decision comes even as a petition is pending before the Gujarat High Court challenging Shrivastava’s February 2022 appointment to the post.
MSU also resolved to reintroduce the five-year contract system for selected teaching staff that had been discontinued since Shrivastava’s appointment. A member of the BoM said they also decided to clear the “unsigned” service books of deans. The BoM was chaired by Chancellor Shubanginiraje Gaekwad.
Speaking to The Indian Express, a member said, “The BoM resolved that in the upcoming academic year, advertisements will be issued to recruit teachers under Contractual Education Services (CES) for a period of five years with a pay bracket of Rs 50,000-60,000, which had been introduced by V-C Parimal Vyas earlier, and suspended since 2022 when Shrivastava took over. It would attract teachers to the institute and help streamline the process.”
“Since Shrivastava did not sign the service books of deans, thereby withholding increments for no reasonable cause since 2022, the current in-charge V-C would promptly sign the service books and resolve the pending issue across all faculties… It has also been resolved to work on the Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) for professors and teaching staff, who have been denied promotions for the last two years,” the member added.
The BoM also served him a notice to vacate the official bungalow by February 8 when the new Vice-Chancellor will be appointed. “Along with that, he has been asked to also surrender electronic gadgets and services extended to him as V-C of the University. It is a usual practice that an outgoing V-C is given some time to vacate the bungalow, up to one month. Since Shrivastava resigned on January 8, he has already been granted a month to complete the formalities,” the member said.
The BoM comprises the Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, Registrar as member secretary, two selected deans of faculties, head of one department, a teacher nominated by the chairperson, four teachers nominated by the chairperson who are not principals or directors of a recognised institution, an eminent expert from an institute or organisation of national importance nominated by the chairperson, and an industry representative.
The Gujarat High Court is hearing arguments on the question of whether Shrivastava can use his tenure as Vice-Chancellor of MSU for his future applications, as he had resigned pending a petition that challenged his eligibility for the post.

headline: ‘Not allowed to buy house’: Dalit man alleges caste discrimination, FIR registered
description: The FIR, filed at Ellisbridge police station on Wednesday, has named the secretary of the society; a resident; and the owner of the property as accused.
content:
A Dalit man in Ahmedabad has claimed that he was not allowed to purchase a house and was allegedly subjected to “casteist slurs” from people at Gangotri Apartment in Ahmedabad’s Ellisbridge area.
In the FIR filed on the basis of a complaint by Bharat Devshi Vaghera, 45, a resident of Ellisbridge and the owner of a PDS shop, it has been alleged that the sale was called off on the grounds that he belonged to a Scheduled Caste.
The FIR, filed at Ellisbridge police station on Wednesday, has named the secretary of the society; a resident; and the owner of the property as accused. The FIR states that Vaghera, along with his broker friend Mahesh Desai, had gone to visit a flat on the first floor of the apartment.
It says that they had also struck a Rs 60 lakh deal, and that Vaghera had handed the house owner a cheque of Rs 2 lakh. It adds that the process of transfer of ownership had begun and by December 6, 2024, they had also received permission for sale from the office of the Deputy Collector that was necessary since it falls under the jurisdiction of the Disturbed Areas Act.
The FIR also states that Vaghera had the sale documents prepared, but when the two parties met on January 21 this year, the seller asked for some changes to it.
On January 26, the house owner told Vaghera that the president and secretary of the society wanted to have a word with him. Vaghera went to the society to meet them, along with his wife Geeta, where the owner, his wife, the secretary, and a resident were present.

According to the FIR, the secretary of the society told Vaghera, “We are already regretting giving a house to one Dalit. We do not want to give a house to another Dalit so we will not give you the no-objection certificate.” The owner too later changed his mind, it states.

The FIR also states that the secretary of the society later said that the society’s president was in Mumbai.
All three accused were booked under Sections 3(2)(va) and 3(1)(r) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act as well as under Section 54 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, according to the police.

headline: New Delhi World Book Fair 2025 to open today
description: The fair will celebrate 75 years of India’s journey as a republic with a focus on rich literary and cultural heritage of Russia through curated exhibits
content:
With the theme ‘Republic@75’, the New Delhi World Book Fair (NDWBF) 2025, to be held from February 1 to 9 at the Bharat Mandapam, will celebrate 75 years of India’s journey as a republic.
The event will bring together leading voices from diverse cultures, and fields, including literature, governance, technology, art, and cinema. Visitors will be able to interact with leading authors, poets, and translators in vibrant literary discussions. Public figures such as Pankaj Tripathi, Phonsokh Ladakhi, Pushpesh Pant, Shashi Tharoor, Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Govind Dholakia, Kumar Vishwas, Prakash Jha, and Admiral Rakesh Sharma will engage with audiences in their sessions across the nine-day event.

Additionally, the fair will have a dedicated space for young readers with storytelling, workshops, and interactive activities. The B2B Zone and Rights Exchange Forum (New Delhi Rights Table) provide platforms for publishers, authors, and stakeholders to connect globally. NDWBF 2025 will also witness cultural performances celebrating India’s diversity and heritage, a dedicated lounge for published authors, and an illustrators’ zone to showcase the works of illustrators in publishing.
With an aim to highlight the spirit of democracy, inclusivity, and unity in diversity that define the nation’s journey, the Ministry of Education event is organised by the National Book Trust, India.
As part of the Festival of Festivals (FoF), an initiative launched by the National Book Trust, India, in 2024, various book festivals and literary platforms from across the country will come together on a shared stage at NDWBF 2025.

headline: Discharge by STPS: DJB not taking court’s orders on Yamuna seriously, says HC, warns contempt of court
description: The Delhi High Court noted that despite its specific orders to install flow meters at the point of discharge in all 37 STPs, the Delhi Jal Board had ‘not taken the orders seriously’.
content:
The Delhi High Court has expressed ire at the Delhi Jal Board (DJB) for not taking its orders “seriously” over the discharge of effluents in Yamuna. In case of further inaction, the court warned that it “would not hesitate in taking strict and stern action” under the Contempt of Courts Act to ensure that its directives are “properly complied with”.
A division bench of Justice  Prathiba Singh and Justice Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora was dealing with a petition related to the functioning of sewage treatment plants (STPs) on January 28.
Of the 37 STPs, DJB chief engineer Bhupesh Kumar informed the court, flow meters have been installed only at the effluent outlets of 22 STPs. For four additional STPs, the flow meters are expected to be installed by March, the court
was told.
The 37 STPs under the DJB take care of sewage from the domestic and residential areas that flow into the Yamuna River. Industrial effluents are under the jurisdiction of the Delhi State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation (DSIIDC). The submission came as the court noted that it issued specific orders in November 2024 to install flow meters at the point of discharge in all 37 STPs. For 22 STPs, the flow meters had been installed as part of their construction projects, nearly four-five years ago, indicating that no flow meters have been installed following the court’s directions in November 2024.

“This reveals an unsatisfactory position,” the bench noted in its order on January 28. “The issue of STPs is being monitored and has been dealt with by this court since April 2024. In any event since November 12, 2024, no steps appear to have been taken by the DJB for the installation of flow meters… This gives an impression to the Court that the DJB has not taken the orders of this Court seriously and to date, only estimates are being prepared… This position is completely not acceptable to the court,” it added.
“The court is refraining from taking any action against Mr  Bhupesh Kumar (chief engineer SDW DJB) as he has now given an assurance that the estimate for the remaining 11 STPs would be ready and the flow meters shall be installed within a month. If the same are not installed, the court is clear that it would not hesitate in taking strict and stern action in accordance with law, both under the Contempt of Courts Act as also any other law which may be applicable to ensure that the directions of the court are properly complied with,” the bench further said.
The court has also added the DSIIDC as a party to the litigation and directed it to file an affidavit in court, giving details of how many Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs) have been installed or are supervised by the DSIIDC and if any more CETPs are required to be installed to curb untreated water flowing into the river, and whether the CETPs have flow meters and sensors to monitor the effluents discharged into the river.

headline: ‘Where should we go’: Refrain at Kumbh lost-and-found centre
description: Ever since the stampede occurred on the occasion of “Mauni Amavasya” and killed at least 30 people and injured 60, scores of people like Sunil have been making their way to the lost-and-found centre, anxiously looking for their still-missing relatives.
content:
There’s a sudden bustle at the model lost-and-found, or “Khoya-Paya centre”, in Section 4 of the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. At the information desk, Sunil Wadhwa from Madhya Pradesh is waving a photo and Aadhaar card of his mother, Laxmi Bai Wadhwa, missing since the stampede at the Maha Kumbh Wednesday. “We’ve just arrived to look for my mother,” he tells a staffer behind the counter. “Where else should we go, should we lodge a case?”
Ever since the stampede occurred on the occasion of “Mauni Amavasya” and killed at least 30 people and injured 60, scores of people like Sunil have been making their way to the lost-and-found centre, anxiously looking for their still-missing relatives.
It’s still unclear how many are missing. But at this centre — the largest of 10 lost-and-founds in the Kumbh — long queues o people continue to snake its way in, some looking for more recently lost people but most for those lost on the intervening night of January 28 and 29 — the time of the stampede.
Most of those queueing up are men or young boys, looking for lost mothers, wives, daughters, and grandmothers.

headline: Leopard safari to begin soon at Sanjay Gandhi National Park: Ashish Shelar
description: Currently, SGNP hosts tiger and lion safaris. Leopard cubs found in various parts of Maharashtra are brought and reared here.
content:
Maharashtra minister for Information and Technology and Cultural affairs Ashish Shelar announced on Friday that the Sanjay Gandhi National Park (SGNP) planned a leopard safari to attract more tourists.
As part of the conservation gesture, the minister has adopted two lions – ‘Bharat and Bharati’ for a year, taking personal responsibility for their upkeep.
Shelar inspected the Sanjay Gandhi National Park on Friday, along with sub-urban district collector Rajendra Kshirsagar, chief conservator Mallikarjun, deputy director Revati Kulkarni, assistant forest officer Sudhir Sonawane, chief security officer Yogesh Mahajan and other concerned officials.
Currently, SGNP hosts tiger and lion safaris. Leopard cubs found in various parts of Maharashtra are brought and reared here. But tourists do not get to see leopards in their natural habitat. Nearly 30 hectares of land would be required for this purpose.
According to officials, the leopard safari can be started to offer visitors a unique wildlife experience while ensuring a safe and enriched environment for the rescued leopards and their cubs that have been rehabilitated in this park. This will not only enhance tourism but also boost revenue.
The cost of the project is estimated at Rs 5 crore. Every year, 20 lakh tourists visit this national park. Once the leopard safari is introduced, the number of tourists will increase, thereby boosting revenues of the park, informed chief conservator Mallikarjun who made a detailed presentation to the minister.
After going through the presentation, Shelar instructed to immediately initiate the process to start leopard safari and the funds needed will be jointly sourced from the forest department and the district planning committee. He also instructed the district collector to expedite the proposal to bring the initiative to life at the earliest.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Guardian of two majestic cubs – Bharat and Bharati
On Republic Day, two three-year-old cubs ‘Bharat and Bharati’ were brought to SGNP from Gujarat. Shelar has decided to adopt them for a year, personally covering all the expenses for their care and well-being.
Insurance cover for 411 forest workers
According to officials, there are 400 workers in the Sanjay Gandhi National Park, braving extreme weather conditions and direct contact with wild animals. Most of them are tribals. Also, there is a team of 11 workers who are also working to protect both wildlife and human settlements.
After Shelar was informed that they were not insured, he directed officials to provide them immediate insurance cover. Necessary budgetary allocation for their insurance will also be made immediately, said Shelar.

headline: Cash, liquor, drugs worth Rs 194 cr seized ahead of Delhi polls
description: Delhi CEO Alice Vaz said the commission received 5,244 complaints online through the Cvigil app and over 100 complaints offline for violating the Model Code of Conduct.
content:
Valuable items such as cash, liquor, drugs, precious material and freebies worth Rs 194 crore have been seized to date, ahead of the Delhi Assembly polls, reveals data shared by the Chief Electoral Office of Delhi.
Addressing a press conference Friday, Delhi CEO Alice Vaz said the commission received 5,244 complaints online through the Cvigil app and over 100 complaints offline for violating the Model Code of Conduct.
“A total of 1.2 crore monetary value of cash, liquor, drugs, precious material and freebies have been seized at 175 inter-state border checkposts. The total value of seizure made till date is Rs 194 crore… this includes Rs 8.92 crore intercepted by the Flying Squad Team (FST/SST). Further, around 15,65,550 posters/banners and other defacement material were removed by local bodies,” she said.
As per the data, of the total complaints received to date, the highest was from North District (1,049) and the lowest from Shahdara (136).
The Delhi Chief Electoral Office is also gearing up to conduct a smooth election on February 5.
Sharing details about arrangements for polling day, Vaz said 210 polling stations across Delhi will be equipped with upgraded facilities to ensure a seamless and voter-friendly experience.
Moreover, 70 polling stations — one in each assembly constituency — will be fully managed by women staff. Another 70 polling stations will be operated entirely by persons with disabilities to promote inclusivity.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The CEO office also said 6,488 senior citizens aged 85 years and above and 1,051 persons with disabilities opted for the vote-from-home facility.
“To assist voters in finding their designated polling stations easily across multiple booth premises, all District Election Officers will set up polling stations following a colour code. The specific colour code assigned to a particular polling station will be mentioned in the voter information slips distributed to voters. This initiative aims to reduce confusion, minimise delays, and ensure a smoother voting process on election day,” said Vaz.
Data also shows that a total of 21,584 ballot units (BUs), 20,692 Control units (CUs) and 18,943 VVPATS have been prepared for the election and commissioning is completed.
“Mock polls were also conducted in EVMs selected at random in the presence of contesting candidates/their representatives as per the guidelines of Commission… Due to more than 16 contesting candidates in two Assembly constituencies — Janakpuri and New Delhi — double BUs will be used in every polling station,” said Vaz.

headline: Lodha trademark row: Retired SC judge appointed mediator in feud between Maharashtra minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha’s sons
description: Macrotech Developers of Abhishek Lodha has sought an ad interim relief in its trademark infringement suit to restrain HoABL of his younger brother Abhinandan from using the ‘Lodha’ trademark.
content:
The Bombay High Court on Friday appointed former Supreme Court judge Justice R V Raveendran as the mediator to resolve the trademark dispute between Macrotech Developer (formerly Lodha Group) of Abhishek Lodha and his younger brother’s House of Abhinandan Lodha Estate Holdings Private Limited (HoABL). Abhishek and Abhinandan are sons of Maharashtra minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha, the founder of the Lodha Group that is into real estate business.
The court on Monday, January 27, noting that the genesis of the matter appeared to be a dispute between two brothers and it can be put to an end if settlement is reached, had proposed the appointment of a former judge of the Supreme Court as mediator to resolve the dispute.
A single-judge bench of Justice Arif S Doctor has been hearing an interim application by Macrotech Developers of Abhishek Lodha seeking ad interim relief in its trademark infringement suit to restrain HoABL of his younger brother, from using the ‘Lodha’ trademark pending the hearing of the matter.
The origin of the dispute
Abhinandan parted ways with Lodha Group in 2015 and started HoABL and the separation was formalised on the basis of a family settlement agreement in 2017.
Macrotech claimed that due to non-compliance with the 2017 agreement, a new agreement was signed between the two parties in December 2023, which, as per Macrotech expressly prohibited Abhinandan from using a name similar to Lodha.
Macrotech and Digirealty Technologies Pvt Ltd in their suit sought a perpetual injunction against infringing on their registered trademarks and sought through an application an ad-interim injunction pending hearing of the suit. They claimed the infringement by HoABL resulted in the loss or damage provisionally estimated to be more than Rs 5,000 crore due to the use of the ‘Lodha’ by HoABL.

On Friday, senior advocate Janak Dwarkadas representing Abhishek Lodha on instructions from the client submitted that he is willing to make an attempt to resolve the trademark dispute through mediation process.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Senior advocate Darius Khambata for Macrotech suggested that all parties be part of the mediation and not merely the two brothers.
On consent of the parties, the High Court appointed retired Justice R V Raveendran as sole mediator in an attempt for resolution of the dispute arisen between the parties to the suit
“However I clarify that it would be open for parties to place before mediator all such issues that are presently subsisting between them,” it added.
The bench suggested that the mediator at first stage can make an attempt to resolve the dispute between two brothers. “If the two brothers sit down and resolve and if a dispute between two brothers gets settled, everything gets settled,” the judge orally remarked.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“However, this would not in any manner mean that any parties to the suit shall be excluded in any manner excluded from mediation proceedings,” the judge noted.
The bench noted that “it shall be open to mediator after holding first a meeting with Abhinandan Lodha and Abhishek Lodha as to issue appropriate directions for inclusion of all parties in the suit.”
“Needless to state that mediation proceedings are without prejudice to rights and contention to all parties to the dispute,” the court said.
The bench further requested the mediator to ‘expeditiously conclude’ the mediation proceedings, preferably within five weeks. Posting the next hearing in the matter to March 21 to decide on granting ad-interim relief, the HC said that in the event if the mediation is not successful, the replies to the interim application to be filed before the said date.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Needless to say that if the mediator requires extension of period after noticing the mediation is proceeding satisfactorily, the prescribed time can be extended accordingly,” the bench stated.

headline: Jhaadu will wipe out BJP’s dishonesty… don’t waste your vote: Akhilesh Yadav at AAP rally in Delhi
description: “The AAP model of governance is an example not only in the country but also across the world,” he added. “Even BJP is saying they will not stop Kejriwal ji’s model in Delhi... They are so scared of these (AAP’s welfare) schemes...,” said Akhilesh.
content:
Appealing to the people of Delhi to not “waste” their ballot, Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday urged residents “wipe out” BJP and its “dishonesty”. Akhilesh, who was in the city to campaign for his INDIA bloc ally AAP, participated in a roadshow in Outer Delhi’s Kirari with AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal.
Standing atop a tempo, Yadav said AAP has made it clear that it is going to defeat the BJP in the February 5 polls. Brandishing a jhaadu (AAP’s party symbol), he told the crowd, “Do you see this jhaadu… this is going to wipe out BJP’s dishonesty. I appeal to the people here to wipe out BJP. Vote in favour of the broom.”
“Each of your votes should go in favour of the broom… Your vote should not be wasted. To defeat BJP, every single vote should be cast for AAP… the work they have done in Delhi — be it education, health sector or providing 24 hours of electricity — shows they care for you…,” he added.
“The AAP model of governance is an example not only in the country but also across the world,” he added. “Even BJP is saying they will not stop Kejriwal ji’s model in Delhi… They are so scared of these (AAP’s welfare) schemes…,” said Akhilesh.
Addressing mediapersons after the roadshow, Yadav said, “People of Delhi are very smart and will not fall into the trap of BJP.” “The AAP will form the government again in Delhi and BJP will lose all 70 seats,” he added.
The SP chief, however, did not speak about another INDIA bloc ally, the Congress. Despite being part of the INDIA bloc, several key parties — including SP, Trinamool Congress, Shiv Sena (UBT), and NCP (Sharad Pawar faction) — have extended their support to AAP over Congress in Delhi.
Kejriwal, however, accused Congress of collaborating with BJP to defeat AAP in Delhi. At the roadshow, he said: “Congress aur BJP mai inu inu, I love you I love you ho raha hai… be careful… Voting for Congress means you are making BJP win. And if BJP comes to power, Delhi will become hell and all schemes — free electricity, water, bus travel for women, health and education — will be stopped.”

“If you want save Rs 25,000 every month, vote for AAP on February 5 and ensure it gets majority,” he added.
From Kirari, AAP has fielded Anil Jha, a former BJP MLA who had joined the party in the run-up to the polls. He replaced sitting AAP MLA Rituraj Jha. Anil will take on BJP’s Bajrang Shukla and Congress’ Rajesh Gupta.
Kirari, densely populated  with unauthorised colonies, is home to Purvanchalis — a term used to describe migrants from Bihar and eastern Uttar Pradesh in Delhi. The people here mostly belong to the lower middle class and economically weaker sections. Besides, villages like Kirari and Nithari also house a large number of Jats and Haryanvis.
According to residents, the major problems that Kirari faces are water scarcity, poor roads and overflowing sewers.

headline: My city, My vote: ‘Defence Colony is getting crowded… too much construction’, says ex-R&AW head AS Dulat
description: The Indian Express asks eminent citizens, who live and work in Delhi, about the one big issue facing their constituency and what they think should be the top priorities of Delhi’s new government.
content:
Amarjit Singh Dulat (85) joined the Indian Police Service (IPS) in 1965. He then moved to Intelligence Bureau (IB) in 1969, where he served for almost 30 years. At the IB, he headed the Kashmir Group during the turbulent 1990s till he joined and headed the R&AW. After retirement, he was appointed adviser on Kashmir in the Prime Minister’s Office and served in the post from January 2001 to May 2004. He lives in Defence Colony, under the Kasturba Nagar constituency.
Issue concerning the Constituency:
“Defence Colony is getting crowded now… We shifted here seven years ago… now there is a lot of construction going on and the result is that there are too many cars and parking has become a huge problem.
Agenda for Delhi’s new government:
“Delhi should be like it used to be… I’ve known Delhi since 1947… we used to live in Civil Lives and from there to Connaught Place, it was a 10-minute drive. There is overcrowding happening all over Delhi and traffic is a big problem. For instance, if I have to go to from Defence Colony to Gurgaon, it could take anything between 40 mins to 2.5 hours. Once during the monsoon, it took us three hours to get there. Traffic is a big issue in Delhi… Delhi is a peculiar city in that way. Not many people use the buses. And I am told the metro is over crowded.”
“One doesn’t want to say these things but the health business has become a racket. Doctors are not easy to find and hospitals charge a lot… I am a retired government servant and I have some CGHS benefits, but they don’t cover everything. If there is an emergency I have to go to a private hospital nearby which has two wings… peculiarly, one is covered by the CGHS and the other is not… It’s crazy…”

headline: Congress writes to NGT against ‘illegal’ shrimp ponds, seeks action
description: Seeking action by the Tribunal, Naik claimed that such ponds have affected the environment as well as livelihood of people.
content:
Senior Congress leader of Surat and advocate Darshan Naik Thursday sent a written complaint to National Green Tribunal (NGT) chairperson Prakash Shrivastava against “illegal” shrimp ponds on government land worth Rs 10,000 crore. Seeking action by the Tribunal, Naik claimed that such ponds have affected the environment as well as livelihood of people.
In the complaint letter Naik says, “Representations and complaints in relation to illegal shrimp ponds on government land were made at the highest level for the last 8-10 years. The issue of shrimp ponds has been raised from the Gram Panchayat to the Assembly, despite this, even today the business of shrimp ponds is going on in full swing, yet no action is being taken by the administration. This has affected the environment and livelihood of the entire area.”
The letter further adds, “According to the information sought under RTI from the District Land Registry Department regarding the measurement done, a total of 1343.9 hectares (1,34,39,000 sq.m.) of land in Olpad taluka of Surat district is covered with shrimp ponds. The total number of ponds operating illegally on government land in Majura taluka of Surat city is 5,641 and total area is 4,039 hectares, covering four hectares (1,34,39,000 sq m). This land falls under CRZ (Coastal Regulatory Zone) area, hence prior approval from Gujarat Coastal Zone Management Authority is required, but despite the fact that no approval has been obtained by the encroachers.”
The letter further states, “Electricity and water theft takes place due to shrimp ponds activity. Because even today, the farmers have to face a dire situation due to lack of irrigation water, shrimp farmers are able to get as much water as they need, due to hand in glove with government officials.”
Naik, in his letter, also brought allegations against the Olpad Choryasi Mamlatdar, Deputy Collector, Fisheries Department, DGVCL (Dakshin Gujarat Vij Company Limited), Irrigation Department and others involved in shrimp business. The letter claimed that due to shrimp ponds, farmers and government treasury are suffering losses of lakhs and crores of rupees every year.

Newly elected Chandigarh Mayor Harpreet Babla of the BJP said Thursday that her priority is to address the financial crisis of the municipal corporation as she hit out at the outgoing Mayor Kuldeep Kumar of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP).

According to reports, Wajid’s car was hit by the truck in Plymouth County in northwest Iowa, about 500 km away from Chicago. The reports said he was taken to a hospital where he died. “Wajid’s semi struck the rear of the grain trailer, splitting in two and came to a rest on both sides of the road. headline: On streets of Kalkaji, woman who climbed Mt Everest helps Cong candidate Alka Lamba woo voters
description: For Megha Parmar the difference between BJP and Congress is that the latter gives “clear cut responses” when compared to the other.
content:
These days, a woman can regularly be seen shadowing Congress’s Alka Lamba as she goes around campaigning in her constituency of Kalkaji for the February 5 elections. The 29-year-old, who can be seen interacting with local residents and helping Lamba in her campaign, is no ordinary party worker. She is Megha Parmar – the first woman to climb Mount Everest from Madhya Pradesh.
A member of Congress since 2022, Parmar is pursuing PhD in ‘Importance of Yoga in Adventure Sports’. A trained underwater diver, paraglider and expert mountain climber, she has not only scaled Everest but also five peaks on different continents, including Mount Kilimanjaro.
Hailing from Bhojnagar village in Madhya Pradesh’s Sehore, Parmar comes from a humble background. While her father is a farmer, her mother is a homemaker. She also has a younger brother.
Parmar says that in her village, girls don’t play with others or go outside their homes to play once they attain puberty. Trapped at home, for Parmar, sports was a medium of expression, a place where she felt free and in control.

British-Irish woman’s rape-murder in Goa: Behind the conviction that earned investigators a ‘thank you’
Fitness came naturally to her as she resided on the second floor and had to take the stairs multiple times to fill around 15 pots of water daily from a hand pump. The round trips built her muscle strength.
In 2015, when she was studying in a government college, her teacher asked her to participate in a judo competition. “No woman was participating in my weight category,” she says. This led Parmar to take part in a few other such contests.
Next year, she joined the National Cadet Corps (NCC). “When you can’t afford private colleges or other perks in life, you start looking at what is free and accessible. You make the most of what is available. So, I joined the NCC… I also enrolled for the basic mountain climbing course.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Later, she read about two men climbing Mount Everest in the newspaper. She went on to discover that no woman from MP has till now achieved this feat and decided that she would be the first.
In 2018, when Shivraj Singh Chouhan-led BJP government was in power in the state, she was granted sponsorship from the state and undertook the journey to scale Mount Everest. But as luck would have it, she fell short by 700 m.
“Though I could not complete the expedition, the news spread that I had climbed Mount Everest. When I returned, I informed everyone that it was an unsuccessful attempt. Following this, I received a lot of hate and trolling,” says Parmar.
“I never told anyone that I had completed the expedition. How the news spread and how I was portrayed after that really hit me hard,” she adds.
Soon after, Congress returned to power in the state.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Determined to be the first woman from MP to climb the Mount Everest, Parmar re-started her journey. In 2019, the Congress government sponsored her expedition and on May 22, she made it to the highest mountain peak in the world.
It wasn’t easy, Parmar says. “You see bodies, your friends leave your side… lack of food, oxygen… and the will to be mentally strong, it takes a lot to reach there”.
She was, however, the happiest when she returned home. “My father was tossed like a football on shoulders by relatives and villagers, even strangers. The entire village was proud of me.”
“What really made the difference was when women started saying they would also want their daughters to climb the Everest,” she says, describing it as her biggest achievement.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Soon after, she was made the face of ‘Beti Padhao, Beti Bachao campaign’ in Madhya Pradesh. In 2022, she joined the Congress.
For Parmar, the difference between BJP and Congress is that the latter gives “clear cut responses” when compared to the other.
“Women leaders in politics always impressed me… I thought it could be a bigger platform to help people,” she adds.
On January 15, this year, hardly a month after her wedding, she came to Delhi and started helping Lamba in her campaign. She has been living on rent along with other party workers.

headline: Praise for PM, holy dip at Mahakumbh: BJP’s Sirsa steps up campaign, assures resolution from present woes
description: A large number of people in the area — women, children, and elderly — step out of their homes to meet him and get clicked with him. He is popular because of his "helpful nature", some say.
content:
As Rajouri Garden BJP candidate Manjinder Singh Sirsa passes through the lanes of Mangal Bazaar and Vishnu Garden, during a foot march ahead of the February 5 Assembly elections, he is greeted with the commonly used Punjabi phrase that translates to “high spirits” or “positive energy”.
A large number of people in the area — women, children, and elderly — step out of their homes to meet him and get clicked with him. He is popular because of his “helpful nature”, some say. Sirsa, 52, is accompanied by party workers, supporters, and Sadulshehar BJP MLA Gurveer Singh Brar, among others.
“I have a feeling that he will win… inka zor hai (he holds an influence in the area),” says Krishna Goyal, a resident of the Mangal Bazaar area who rushed from her balcony on the first floor to meet Sirsa. Among the major issues in the area she counts are cleanliness and overflowing sewers during rain.
However, Kulbhushan, a resident of Vishnu Garden, says, “It’s not easy to decide who we will vote for this time. You never know until the final day when you have to vote.. but yes we will vote for change this time”. He complains that he had applied for a ration card three years back; but to date, there has been no progress.

The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has fielded Dhanwati Chandela, its current MLA, against Sirsa. In the 2020 Assembly elections, she defeated the BJP’s Ramesh Khanna. The Congress has fielded Dharam Pal Chandela from the constituency.
Sirsa’s padyatra continues with people joining him or greeting him with folded hands from the terrace of their homes. The drumbeats charge up the atmosphere. A volunteer shows the step count on his mobile phone, which has been in the 17,000-20,000 range every day with the election campaigning reaching fever pitch.
An elderly couple tells Sirsa that they want to cast their vote at the closest booth and they have shifted to a new area recently. Sirsa assures them that he will try to help.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
As the BJP leader moves ahead, he meets another senior citizen — Pritpal Singh, 78. The two share a friendly banter, which begins with Sirsa touching his feet while Singh greets him in Punjabi. Sirsa asks Singh for his blessings and says he won’t budge unless he is promised his vote. Singh laughs along.
The next stop is ‘Purvanchal Sansad’ — a gathering of the community — in the Khayala area where migrant workers from various places like Uttar Pradesh and Bihar have gathered. Sirsa is joined by Gorakhpur BJP MP Ravi Kishan, a well-known face among the Purvanchalis, who constitute a large chunk of Delhi’s electorate.
Praising Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the work done by him for the citizens during the last 10 years, Kishan called him a fakir (holyman). He calls Sirsa his “brother” and asks the crowd— Who wants to take a holy dip at the ‘Maha Kumbh’ in Prayagraj? Many people in the crowd raise their hands. Kishan then asks them to vote for Sirsa and he will ensure all arrangements are made.
In a veiled jibe at the AAP, Sirsa says, “Whether it takes one or two trains or multiple buses, I will take all of you for the holy dip. People doing politics of alcohol and dirty water will go away and new people will come and bring clean water”.

Listing the BJP’s poll promises, he underlines that women will be given Rs 2,500, a cylinder at the price of Rs 500, and Rs 21,000 for pregnant women.
While addressing the public collectively, Kishan and Sirsa both speak about the Ram Mandir, the development of the Mahakal temple, and the Kumbh Mela as things the PM had done for the people. Kishan also added that unlike people from other parties who have built a ‘sheeshmahal’ the PM has stuck to the ground and not used the money of the people for his gains.
The day for Sirsa continues with multiple meetings, padyatra, and then a dinner at a home hosted by a family in Rajouri Garden.
