headline: Developers, construction material firms raise concerns over ban on heavy vehicles in Pune
description: Recently, the traffic administration introduced a new schedule with dedicated routes for heavy vehicle movement in Pune.
content:
Following the traffic police’s decision to ban heavy vehicles in the city’s red zones to ease congestion, developers and construction material associations have raised concerns, calling it a financial burden on both businesses and as well as citizens constructing homes.
Recently, the traffic administration introduced a new schedule with dedicated routes for heavy vehicle movement in the city. After identifying red zones based on black spots, accident-prone areas, public spaces, and school zones, the Traffic DCP, in a recent meeting, declared a complete ban on heavy vehicles within the city limits. However, construction material suppliers, transportation bodies, and real estate associations have called the move unilateral, arguing that they will have to bear the financial brunt of the decision.
Kapil Gandhi, Management Committee Member, CREDAI Pune Metro, acknowledged concerns about citizen safety but questioned whether heavy vehicles alone should be considered a risk. “There are all sorts of vehicles in the city, but the ban is only on construction vehicles, which will impact the timely transportation of materials for homes and other projects. We have deadlines issued by RERA and commitments to our customers. If the supply of materials is halted, ongoing projects will come to a standstill, creating further chaos,” he said.
As per the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA), housing projects must be completed within a specific deadline. If raw materials do not arrive on time, construction delays are inevitable. Additionally, Ready-Mix Concrete (RMC) transportation is highly time-sensitive, and its pricing is determined by strict parameters.
Gandhi also pointed out that allowing heavy vehicle movement only at night presents multiple challenges, including noise pollution for sleeping residents and increased material costs. “If heavy vehicles are restricted, people will have no option but to hire smaller vehicles, which will increase the number of trips and raise loading-unloading charges,” he explained.
CREDAI suggested alternative measures such as driver education programs, road widening, and better traffic management instead of outright bans.
Yogesh Sasane, Secretary of the District Mining and Crusher Entrepreneurs Association, Pune, highlighted concerns over the increased cost of night-time transportation. “Night wages for Mathadi workers are doubled, and this decision will require additional manpower and resources, further increasing costs. We will present these facts during a meeting with the Police Commissioner on Saturday. If a resolution is not reached, all transportation of raw materials required for construction in the city and district will be halted indefinitely from Monday,” he warned.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
DCP (Traffic) Amol Zende defended the decision, emphasising the need to control traffic congestion and prevent accidents. “Our priority is decongesting the city and ensuring public safety. RMC trucks are permitted from 12 AM to 4 AM, while dumpers can operate from 11 AM to 5 PM. During peak hours, no heavy vehicles are allowed. Trucks and similar vehicles are only permitted at night, with trailers being an exception. Many trailers traveling from Chakan to Solapur pass through the city, so we have designated dedicated routes for them,” he stated.

headline: Retired Justice SN Dhingra withdraws PIL in Delhi High Court seeking to end poll freebies, told to approach SC
description: The petition, which also called attention to the collection of voter data, was filed days before Delhi headed to Assembly polls on February 5.
content:
Retired Justice S N Dhingra, in his capacity as president of non-profit Samay Yaan (Sashakt Samaj), Wednesday withdrew a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) from the Delhi High Court seeking that promising freebies be declared a corrupt practice and collection of voter data for distribution or schemes and freebies be stopped.
The petition was dismissed as withdrawn, with the court advising the petitioner to approach the Supreme Court instead.
The plea was filed days before Delhi headed to Assembly polls on February 5 and challenged the poll promises of the BJP, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and the Congress besides calling attention to voter data collection by the AAP on the pretext of extending benefits of the Mukhyamantri Mahila Samman Yojana.
The Election Commission of India (ECI) informed the division bench of Chief Justice D K Upadhyaya and Justice Tushar Rao Gedela that the Supreme Court is already looking into the issues raised in retired Justice Dhingra’s PIL.
While advocate Siddhartha Borgohain, representing Dhingra, contended that his PIL has two-fold issues – declaration of financial schemes promised as part of poll sops as a corrupt practice as well as the issue of data collection – Chief Justice Upadhyaya reiterated that both issues are being dealt with by the apex court.
“Collection of data for the purpose of reaching out to target group will also be covered… Matter pending before SC has taken up both issues… Better seek your impleadment there… Both matters of freebies and whether it is corrupt practice, is being looked into by SC,” Chief Justice Upadhyaya remarked orally.
As a trial court judge, Justice Dhingra had awarded the death sentence to Parliament attack accused Afzal Guru. He had also probed the land deals of Robert Vadra and faced judicial scrutiny in 2017 for possible misuse of his mandate as a court-appointed observer in a family business dispute.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He was appointed as the chairman of the SIT looking into closed cases of the 1984 Sikh riots in 2018. He was elevated as a Delhi High Court judge in 2006 and retired in 2011.

headline: UP cops question Madhya Pradesh man who threatened to ‘kill’ CM Adityanath
description: Sunil Gurjar, who studied till class 8 and was involved in farming, told PTI that he issued the threat as he wanted to become a "don".
content:
The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) has questioned a Madhya Pradesh-based man who allegedly threatened to kill UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, police said on Wednesday.
The man, identified as Sunil Gurjar (20), resident of Hasai Mewda village in MP’s Morena district, had allegedly called authorities at the UP CM’s office over phone and threatened to kill Adityanath, Civil Lines police station in-charge Darshan Shukla told PTI.
A team of the UP STF reached here on Tuesday and questioned Gurjar, but he was not arrested, the official said.
No case has been registered so far, he said.
No criminal background of Gurjar has been found and further investigation is underway, he added.
Gurjar, who studied till class 8 and was involved in farming, told PTI that he issued the threat as he wanted to become a “don”.

headline: ‘I am just not confident of HAL’: IAF chief Amar Preet Singh expresses displeasure over delay in delivery of Tejas aircraft
description: Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) said Tuesday that it would be able to deliver at least 11 Tejas Mk1A aircraft to the Air Force by the end of March.
content:
Delay in the delivery of Light Combat Aircraft Tejas by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) has not gone down well with Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh who was quick to express his displeasure with the defence manufacturing PSU.
In a video recorded on Monday, Air Chief Marshal Singh can be seen saying, “You have to alleviate (IAF worries) and make us more confident. At the moment, I am just not confident of HAL, which is a very wrong thing to happen.” The clip surfaced on Tuesday.
“I can tell you what our requirements and worries are,” he can be heard to the HAL staff while seated in the cockpit of HJT-36 Yashas.
“I was promised that when I come here in February, 11 Tejas Mk1As would be ready. And not a single one is ready. We all have worked there (in HAL). But I find that HAL is just not in mission mode,” he added.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
'Main aisa aadmi nahi hoon': Samay Raina 'breaks the facade' of comedy
In the same video, the Air Chief Marshal can be heard saying, “The aircraft that you flew, calling it Mk1A. It is not Mk1A. It cannot happen just by change of one software or by looks. When the weapons come and the capability comes, then it is Mk1A.”
He was also seen shaking his head and saying, “Mazaa nahi aa raha hai (Not having fun)”. “I will be the happiest person if I’m proved wrong. I feel that only a few are putting in any effort. Or maybe everyone is putting in effort in their own silos without looking at the overall picture. Something has to change… Some drastic change… This needs a magic wand so everything gets aligned. It’s high time,” Singh said.
HAL, which has also faced criticism from previous IAF chiefs, said Tuesday that it was confident of delivering at least 11 Tejas Mk1A aircraft to the Air Force by the end of March. The Public Sector Undertaking (PSU) is currently pursuing two major contracts – 97 Light Combat Aircraft (Tejas) and 156 Light Combat Helicopters (Prachanda).
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
HAL Chairman and Managing Director D K Sunil on Tuesday attributed the delay to sanctions imposed on the country after the 1998 nuclear tests but said they would meet the timelines of the overall project. “It is no secret that this programme started in 1984 and it was delayed. At the same time, I have to put it in context: You know that we (India) had sanctions after our nuclear test in 1998, so we had to build things from the ground up. A lot of work has gone into it. So, the delays cannot be attributed to just, you know, laziness on part of the industry,” he stated.

headline: Maharashtra police files FIR against Ranveer Allahbadia and Samay Raina over ‘India’s Got Latent’ row
description: This is the second FIR against the duo, with the Assam police having registered one on Monday.
content:
The Maharashtra cyber police have booked podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia, comedian Samay Raina and other artists for allegedly making obscene content and broadcasting it on Raina’s India’s Got Latent show after it sparked a huge controversy. This is the second FIR against the duo, with the Assam police having registered one on Monday.
A senior officer confirmed the development to The Indian Express, adding that the police have invoked section 67 (transmission of obscene material in electronic form) of the Information Technology Act, among other sections.
The cyber police have booked 30 people over obscene and foul language allegedly used during the show. “On Monday evening, we registered a case against 30 individuals, including artists, hosts, judges, and participants of all six episodes of India’s Got Latent, and we will be issuing summons to all, asking them to join the police probe,” said a senior police officer from Maharashtra state Cyber police.
ALSO READ | Ranveer Allahbadia episode shows the bar for comedy is as low as ever
Earlier, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma announced on social media that Allahbadia, Raina and others were booked in his state on Monday.
Maharashtra Women’s Commission Chairperson Rupali Chakankar said, “We received a complaint and have instructed the police department to stop the show’s telecast and immediately take necessary action as per Indian laws, and submit a report to the commission.”
The Mumbai police have summoned Allahbadia, Raina and other artists who were present on the show. In response to the summons, lawyers for Ashish Chanchalani and another artist visited the Khar police station on Tuesday evening.

headline: Amid Guillain Barre Syndrome, SPPU canteen worker seen sitting with his feet in water filter
description: Pune has seen an increase in Guillain Barre Syndrome (GBS) cases, with over 190 suspected patients
content:
A controversy has erupted in Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU) after a worker at the Adarsh canteen was seen climbing on to a water filter to fetch water for cleaning the canteen floor. Rushikesh Chavan, a second-year student at the Political Science department who is associated with the National Students Union of India, said that while walking on the campus on Saturday night he noticed a worker sitting on top of the water filter at the Adarsh Canteen.
The Adarsh Canteen is one of the main canteens on the university campus. In the video captured by Chavan, a worker is seen sitting on the top of an open water filter and passing buckets full of water to another worker, who uses it to clean the canteen floor. Chavan alleged that the feet of the worker were inside the water filter.
Pune has seen an increase in Guillain Barre Syndrome (GBS) cases, with over 190 suspected patients. With the National Institute of Virology (NIV) confirming that contaminated water was the main reason behind GBS in parts of the city, such lack of hygiene with the water filter is of concern.
“These repeated incidents prove that the university administration has allowed the dining hall and canteen operators to play with the lives of students. The administration should put a stop to these wrongdoings as soon as possible to prevent such incidents from happening again and take punitive action against those who commit such wrongdoings”, said Chavan.

headline: Investors get red carpet, not red-tapism in India, Rajnath says in Karnataka, stresses ‘cross-political party consensus’
description: At the Invest Karnataka 2025 meet in Bengaluru, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh says there is a consensus in India that sustainable economic development must be driven by a market-led economy, with a leading role for the private sector.
content:
Investors no longer face red tape in India, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said during the inaugural session of Karnataka’s Global Investors Meet in Bengaluru on Tuesday, urging global investors to commit to long-term plans in the country.
“Today, investors do not face red-tapism in India. Instead, we roll out the red carpet for them. This kind of cross-political party consensus on promoting investment plays a crucial role in reducing uncertainty for our investors,” he said.
The defence minister said investors would benefit from India’s formidable strengths, including political stability, vast market potential, and an ecosystem based on the rule of law, free from uncertainty and disorder. He said India’s immense investment potential has witnessed sustained success, lasting impact, and enduring growth.
Calling for investment in Karnataka, Singh said that in the era of cooperative federalism, central and state governments are working closely together to shape the country’s economy. He cited Bengaluru as a pioneering hub for various industries like IT and software, adding that the city is now a rising centre for artificial intelligence. This is the moment and the perfect time to invest in India, he said.
Singh said India’s constitutional values are deeply rooted in its rich history of accepting different ideas, illustrated by the “close coordination” between Union and state governments.
The government has actively worked to address challenges, including red tape, that investors previously faced, the Union minister said, adding that the cumbersome process of obtaining multiple clearances has been replaced by a single-window system. He recalled that entrepreneurs had shared with him concerns about investing in promising sectors, only to face unexpected policy changes later, disrupting their plans and profits. To allay such concerns, he said that across all levels of governance in the country, there is a broad consensus that sustainable economic development must be driven by a market-led economy, with a leading role for the private sector.
Singh elaborated that this shared commitment provides a stable and predictable policy environment, ensuring that businesses can invest with confidence in policy continuity.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Assuring investors of strong market demand to tap into India’s potential, the Union minister said several recent government decisions are expected to further strengthen the demand environment in one of the world’s fastest-growing markets.

headline: After stone-pelting at Mysuru police station, BJP alleges appeasement is emboldening fundamentalists
description: Several people have been arrested over the stone-pelting targeting the Udayagiri police station in Mysuru.
content:
Karnataka’s Opposition BJP has accused the Congress government of emboldening fundamentalists with its “appeasement policies” after a mob attacked a Mysuru police station demanding that a social media user picked up over a provocative post be handed over to it.
“For a post on Rahul Gandhi and Kejriwal, fundamentalist Muslims attacked the police by carrying stones in bags. They have threatened Hindus, and an atmosphere of fear was created in Mysuru,” Leader of the Opposition R Ashoka said at a news conference on Tuesday.
The police have arrested several people involved in the stone-pelting that took place at the Udayagiri police station late on Monday.
Ashoka, who visited Mysuru on Tuesday evening, said the law and order situation had deteriorated in the state. The BJP leader further alleged that Muslim fundamentalists were emboldened by the withdrawal of cases against those involved in the Hubballi riots.
“Police have now realised that it is futile to book cases against Muslims… For a vote bank, the entire system is being compromised,” Ashoka said.
A tense situation had prevailed in Mysuru over a social media post made by a resident of Kalyan Nagar in the city. He had allegedly morphed the faces of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, AAP supremo Arvind Kejriwal and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav onto a picture of three semi-naked men, adding a skull cap. He is also accused of making a derogatory statement against the Muslim community.
BJP state president B Y Vijayendra alleged that fundamentalists were indulging violence in Udayagiri police station limits, where Muslims are a majority. “They have grown strong enough to attack the police. There have been a series of murders of Hindu activists in the region in the past,” he claimed.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Home Minister G Parameshwara said the police used tear gas to disperse the crowd as the situation threatened to spiral out of control.
“Around 200 people came to the police station and demanded that the accused be handed over to them. The police did not oblige. Due to this, stones were pelted at the police station,” he said. “Those who pelted stones are being arrested.”

headline: Prime accused in Naihati TMC worker’s murder arrested from UP: SIT
description: Aide of accused Rajesh Shaw also arrested during raid at Ballia village
content:
More than a week after a TMC worker was shot dead in broad daylight in Naihati in North 24 Parganas district, the SIT of West Bengal Police arrested the prime accused, Rajesh Shaw, and his accomplice, Vishal, from a village in Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh.
The Special Investigation Team (SIT), formed to probe the murder of 40-year-old Santosh Yadav, arrested the two during a raid in a village in the Fefna area of Ballia on Monday night.
Sources in the SIT said they were tipped about the presence of Rajesh and Vishal in Ballia. Rajesh had been absconding since the murder of Yadav on February 1.
Sub-Inspectors Satyanarayan Pandey and Aritra Chandra of the Barrackpore Police, with the assistance of UP Police, raided a cowshed in a remote village within the Fefna Police Station area of Ballia district in Uttar Pradesh on Monday. They caught Rajesh and Vishal while they were sleeping. Both were presented in the Ballia district chief judicial magistrate’s court, which granted a four-day transit remand to West Bengal,” a senior member of the SIT said.
Previously, the SIT had arrested four men, including Rajesh Shaw’s son Akash in connection with the murder.
The SIT had formed four groups of police officers to find the absconding accused in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. Sources said SIT members also visited Begusarai and Sikandarpur to find Rajesh.
Yadav’s murder had led to a slugfest between the ruling TMC and the Opposition BJP. While the TMC alleged that local BJP leader and strongman Arjun Singh was behind the murder, Singh called it a fallout of internal rift in the TMC.

headline: Teenager stabbed to death in Delhi’s Seelampur, 2 minors apprehended
description: The Delhi Police are looking to apprehend another associate of the two minor boys involved in the murder.
content:
The Delhi Police Tuesday apprehended two minor boys for allegedly stabbing to death a teenager in North East Delhi’s Seelampur. The police also recovered the knife used in the crime from their possession.
The Seelampur police said they received information that a boy was lying injured in Gautampuri at 9.45 pm on Sunday. A police team reached the spot and found the body of a boy aged around 17-18 lying in a pool of blood with stab injuries. Forensic teams and crime scene investigators were called to examine the area, while the body was transported to GTB Hospital for an autopsy.
The police team, meanwhile, examined CCTV footage from cameras nearby and gathered information from local sources, enabling them to locate and apprehend two suspects, aged 16 and 15.
“During the interrogation, both the suspects revealed that being from the same locality, the victim was known to them, but he frequently used to bully them and asked to pay money which they were not able to pay. Hence they assaulted him,” said Ashish Mishra, Deputy Commissioner of Police, North East.

headline: Bengaluru-based space tech firm Digantara eyes $30 million revenue with US expansion
description: Digantara plans to invest $10 million to $15 million over the next six to eight months to establish a spacecraft manufacturing and space optics production facility in Colorado, it said.
content:
Indian space tech firm Digantara said on Tuesday it is targeting $25 million to $30 million in revenue over the next two years by expanding into the US, aiming to secure large-scale defense contracts and tap into the $60 billion space surveillance and intelligence market.
The Bengaluru-based startup plans to invest $10 million to $15 million over the next six to eight months to establish a spacecraft manufacturing and space optics production facility in Colorado, it said.
Dignatara also said it has signed contracts with multiple US Department of Defense (DoD) agencies, including the US Air Force and Space Force, but did not disclose further details.
Also Read | No glitch in SpaDeX, says ISRO chairman
The company recently launched its first space-based surveillance satellite aboard SpaceX’s Transporter-12 mission. Equipped with advanced electro-optical sensors, the satellite can track space objects as small as 5 cm in diameter.
Space traffic and debris management is an escalating concern for the global space industry, with low Earth orbit the most congested with human-made objects as it offers a balance between cost and proximity, making it a prime target for the rapidly growing commercial space sector.
Also Read | Bengaluru space startup team upbeat as ‘Digantara’ finds mention in PM Modi’s ‘Mann Ki Baat’
More than 14,000 satellites, including some 3,500 inactive, surround the globe in low Earth orbit, data shows.
“At a time when space safety and security are more critical than ever, our expansion into the US, particularly Colorado, enables us to collaborate closely with key stakeholders and accelerate space surveillance capabilities,” said Anirudh Sharma, co-founder and CEO of Digantara.

headline: Pune police entangled in drama of ‘kidnapping’, Bangkok flight involving ex-minister Sawant’s son
description: Pune City Police on Monday evening said they had launched a probe after a First Information Report was filed with them over allegations that Rushiraj Sawant had been kidnapped from Pune.
content:
The Pune police got entangled in drama on Monday evening over the purported abduction of Rushiraj Sawant — the 32-year-old son of former Maharashtra Minister and Shiv Sena leader Tanaji Sawant — who had in fact boarded a chartered flight “without telling his father”. The curtains fell after the chartered flight, which was supposed to be destined for Bangkok, landed back in Pune on Monday night with Rushiraj and his two friends onboard.
Pune City Police on Monday evening said they had launched a probe after a First Information Report was filed with them over allegations that Rushiraj had been kidnapped from Pune.
A senior officer with Pune City Police said, “On Monday evening we received a complaint from an office bearer of an education institute headed by Mr Tanaji Sawant in Pune. The complainant said Rushiraj had allegedly been kidnapped from Narhe area on Monday afternoon in a Swift car. At the time, he was on his way to the airport, the complainant said. We registered an offence and launched a probe.”
Tanaji Sawant however had told reporters in Pune, “I can’t say whether this is a kidnapping or he is missing. We have come to know that the two people with him are his friends. We became concerned after we came to know he had taken a flight without informing family members. He (Rushiraj) always informs me or my elder son Giriraj where he is going. My son (Rushiraj) and the other two friends went to the airport in a car that is not my son’s. Because of this, we have involved the police and they are probing (the matter). It has come to light that they have taken a chartered flight, but we don’t know their location.”
Another officer from Pune city police said, “As we launched a probe, our preliminary findings suggest Rushiraj boarded a chartered flight from the Pune airport some time after 4 pm. We did not verify it, but got to know the flight was destined for Bangkok.”
Joint Commissioner of Police for Pune, Ranjan Kumar Sharma, on Monday eveing said, “Our teams swung into action after the complaint was received. Initial probe suggests that he is on a flight that took off from Pune. Efforts have been initiated by the police machinery to bring him back. In this regard, an FIR of kidnapping has been registered at Sinhagad Road police station. Case has been handed over to the crime branch.
Later the same night, Sharma told The Indian Express, “The update in the case is that this chartered flight has landed back in Pune around 8.45 pm. The son of Mr Tanaji Sawant and two others were on the flight and are safe. We will be speaking to them to ascertain exactly what has happened.” When asked about the course of investigation for the kidnapping case registered, Sharma said, “We will take a call on that after we complete the probe.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
When asked whether Pune police had contacted civil aviation authorities to divert the plane back to Pune, a senior Pune police officer said, “Those discussions happened at a ministerial level.”

headline: Contempt plea in Elgaar Parishad case: Court summons Taloja jail superintendent to explain why cot is not provided to accused Surendra Gadling
description: The authorities said that getting a cot is difficult in the general barracks due to crowding, but mattress and pillows are purchasable from the jail canteen at one's own expenses. They added that Surendra Gadling can be transferred to a high security prison to avail cots.
content:
A special court designated under NIA Act has asked Taloja Central Prison superintendent to remain present before it to explain why the facility of cot cannot be provided to Elgaar Parishad accused Surendra Gadling, who had sought the same citing his physical condition and ailments.
The jail authorities had told the court that as Gadling is placed in general barracks, it is getting difficult to provide him cot due to crowding and he can purchase cotton mattress and pillow from the jail canteen on his own expenses and use the same. It had added that the facility can be provided to him if he is transferred to high-security prison or any other jail.
On August 14, last year, the special court, considering ‘ill health’ of Gadling had asked jail authority to ‘sympathetically check out’ feasibility of use of western commode available in other barracks and if he can be taken there whenever required. The court had noted, so far as the use of cot or bed stand is concerned, if it was available in the cells of the jail, Gadling may be accommodated there. The court had, meanwhile, permitted him to purchase a mattress from the jail canteen at his own expense and allowed him to use the same.
However, on January 20, the jail authority wrote to the court that it was not possible to provide cot or bed stand to Gadling as there was no space in the barracks in which he was lodged, but the same can be provided if he can be transferred to another cell or prison in Mumbai area.

headline: Eknath Shinde, Sharad Pawar to share dais in Delhi today
description: Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar will share the dais in Delhi where Shinde will be honoured with the Mahadji Shinde Rashtriya Gaurav Award. The event will be attended by Union minister Jyotiraditya Scindia, among others.
content:
Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar will share the dais on Tuesday in Delhi where Shinde will be honoured with the Mahadji Shinde Rashtriya Gaurav Award, presented by the Pune-based Sarhad Institute.
“The award ceremony will be held at New Maharashtra Sadan in New Delhi on Tuesday, where the award will be conferred upon Deputy CM Shinde by Sharad Pawar, the chairman of the 98th All India Marathi Literary Conference,” a Sena functionary said.
The event will be attended by Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia, Union Minister of State for Cooperation and Civil Aviation Murli Dhar Mohol, senior writer Dr Sadanand More, and Padma Bhushan awardee sculptor Ram Sutar as chief guests.
Also Read | Tavleen Singh writes: In Delhi, this was no election, but a referendum on Kejriwal
The Mahadji Shinde Rashtriya Gaurav Award includes a cash prize of Rs 5 lakh, a certificate of honour, a memento, and the traditional Shindeshahi turban.
Mahadji Shinde was a key military commander and strategist of the Maratha Empire. Born in 1730, he was the chief of the Shinde dynasty, which later became known as the Scindia dynasty of Gwalior. After the Battle of Panipat, Mahadji Shinde played a crucial role in restoring Maratha power in North India.

headline: Budget session begins: Despite no Central funds, Bengal govt didn’t back out from ensuring employment and housing to rural poor: Governor
description: Governor’s speech reflects thaw with the TMC govt as last year he had refused to read out ‘government-prepared’ speech
content:
West Bengal Governor CV Ananda Bose on Monday said that “despite financial constraints and non-receipt of Central funds”, the TMC government in the state “has not backed out from its commitment to ensuring employment and housing for our rural brethren”.
In his inaugural address to the West Bengal Legislative Assembly’s Budget Session, the Governor said the TMC government, led by Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, introduced schemes like Karmashree, which guarantees employment, and Banglar Bari (Gramin), a rural housing scheme, which were funded entirely through its own resources in the absence of central funds.
The Mamata Banerjee government has been at loggerheads with the Centre over non-disbursal on funds for several welfare schemes, such as MGNREGA and PM Awas Yojana. While the TMC alleges that the BJP government at the Centre blocked the state’s share of funds for the schemes due to political vendetta, the BJP claims that corruption in the implementation of the scheme in the state has led to the Centre withholding funds to the state.
In his speech, the Governor said the state government’s “efforts towards women’s development and empowerment” was one of its “most important priorities”.
“About one-third of our total expenditure is made on the development and empowerment of women. Under the able guidance of my chief minister, the state government has taken a number of unique initiatives towards women empowerment like Lakshmir Bhandar, Kanyashree, and Rupashree to name a few,” Bose said.
Minister of State for Finance Chandrima Bhattacharya will present the Budget for 2025-26 in the Assembly on Wednesday.
Elaborating on the state’s measures under these schemes, the Governor said: “With effect from April 1, 2024, the monthly benefit under Lakshmir Bhandar has been raised from Rs 1,000 to Rs 1,200 for women under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe categories and from Rs 500 to Rs 1,000 for women from other categories. 2.21 crore women are (benefitting from the scheme)… The state has ensured life-long financial benefits by the automatic inclusion of a Lakshmir Bhandar beneficiary in the old age pension scheme upon attaining the age of 60. The number of beneficiaries under the internationally acclaimed Kanyashree Prakalpa has touched 92 lakh. In the current financial year, 2.08 lakh beneficiaries have been covered under Rupashree Prakalpa.”
Notably, Governor Bose had last year refused to read out the state government’s prepared speech during the inauguration of the Budget Session. However, this year, Bose agreed to read the speech prepared by the state government without any objection.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Governor also called the recently concluded 8th Bengal Global Business Summit (BGBS), organised by the TMC government to woo investors, an “overwhelming success”.
“With the participation of the captains of industries and business delegates from India and abroad, including 20 partner countries, as many as 212 MoUs and LOIs have been signed and investment proposals to the tune of Rs 4,40,595 crore have been received. Upon implementation, this will lead to enhanced economic activity in the state and create more employment opportunities for the youths of Bengal,” the Governor said.
“Under the visionary leadership of my Chief Minister, the state of West Bengal has made significant progress in economic growth and other financial parameters over the past 13 years,” he said.
“The state government has taken numerous initiatives over the past 13 years to benefit the minority population, focusing on education, modernisation of madrasas, employment generation, skill development, and sustainable livelihoods,” he added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Governor, in his speech, also said the state remained peaceful with no law and order situation. “I am very proud that all the major festivals, including Durga Puja, Kali Puja, Diwali… Gangasagar Mela and others, have been celebrated peacefully and gracefully.”
The equation between the Raj Bhawan and the TMC government in the state had gone through several ups and downs. Signs of thaw began to surface in December 2024 when the Governor conducted the swearing-in of six TMC MLAs. The ceremony was held in the Vidhan Sabha and was attended by Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and Speaker Biman Banerjee.
Bose was appointed as the Governor of West Bengal in November 2022. Over the past three years, he has had several confrontations with the state government. The Governor has openly criticised the functioning of the state government under Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, particularly regarding the law and order situation.
The relationship between Governor Bose and the TMC government hit a low in May 2024 when a Raj Bhavan employee accused Bose of sexually assaulting her. Following this, the TMC leadership, including the CM, criticised the Governor. The CM also claimed that women told her that they did not feel safe visiting Raj Bhavan. In response, the Governor filed a defamation case against the chief minister in the High Court.

headline: Amid factional war in Karnataka, BJP leadership serves second show cause notice to Yatnal
description: Yatnal, considered the leader of this faction, is spearheading the campaign against Vijayendra, the son of former chief minister B S Yediyurappa.
content:
The Karnataka BJP camp that is pushing for the removal of MLA B Y Vijayendra as state chief received a major jolt Monday as the party’s Central Disciplinary Committee issued a second show cause notice in three months to MLA Basangouda Patil Yatnal for breach of discipline.
Yatnal, considered the leader of this faction, is spearheading the campaign against Vijayendra, the son of former chief minister B S Yediyurappa.
Yatnal, along with other members of his camp such as MLA and former minister Ramesh Jarkiholi and former minister Kumar Bangarappa, have visited New Delhi multiple times over the past few weeks to ask the top brass to change the state president.
The fresh notice was issued to Yatnal on February 10 by Om Pathak, member secretary of the committee. It said that his statements against Vijayendra contravened the code of discipline in the BJP’s constitution.
“Despite your assurances of good behavior and conduct in response to earlier show cause notices, you continue to violate and flout your own assurances,” the notice read, asking why the party should not initiate disciplinary action against him.
The committee has sought the Yatnal’s within three days.
The previous show cause notice to Yatnal was issued in the first week of December 2024 for his “continuing tirade against the state-level party leadership” and “defiance of party directives”. Responding to the notice, Yatnal had said that he had simply presented the facts about the current state of the BJP in Karnataka.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Even after that notice, the Vijayapura MLA continued to lash out at Vijayendra and his allies in the party, while lobbying hard to ensure his ouster as party chief.
Vijayendra was appointed BJP Karnataka president in November 2023. Soon after Yatnal had accused Yediyurappa of “blackmailing” the BJP high command to secure the berth for his son. A week ago, Yatnal termed Vijayendra as “characterless and corrupt”.
Last week, the group of MLAs and senior BJP leaders backing Yatnal — who were in Delhi to meet the party top brass — had hinted at a possible replacement of Vijayendra, saying that the leadership would “send a good message” soon.

headline: Maharashtra govt to strictly enforce Bombay Nursing Home Act
description: Hospitals, nursing homes can’t detain patients or refuse to handover bodies over pending bills, warns minister.
content:
The Maharashtra health department is set to implement a long-overlooked provision of the Bombay Nursing Homes Registration Act, 1949, ensuring private hospitals and nursing homes can no longer demand full payment of due bill amounts at discharge. The move aims to strengthen patient rights, improve transparency and prevent financial exploitation in healthcare facilities across the state.
Speaking to The Indian Express, state Health Minister Prakash Abitkar underscored the urgent need to enforce the Act, which regulates private hospitals, nursing homes and maternity centres in Maharashtra. The legislation mandates registration, licensing and adherence to minimum healthcare standards, ensuring patient safety, preventing malpractice and promoting accountability in the sector.
“Despite the Act being in place for years, compliance has been weak, with many private hospitals operating without strict adherence to its provisions,” he said.
To address these lapses, the government is prioritising the enforcement of two major rules. Firstly, hospitals will no longer be allowed to detain patients over pending bills at the time of discharge. Secondly, in cases where a patient dies, hospitals will be prohibited from withholding the body over unpaid dues. “Hospitals often refuse to discharge patients due to outstanding payments, violating both patient and human rights. The same applies to deceased patients—we will implement these rules immediately,” he said.
The Act also mandates that all registered private hospitals and nursing homes meet essential infrastructure and staffing standards while maintaining strict hygiene, fire safety, and biomedical waste disposal norms. However, compliance remains inconsistent. “We lack data on the actual implementation of these regulations. Right now, we are compiling this information and will ensure stricter enforcement, particularly in fire safety norms,” he added.
In the past month alone, over 3,000 private hospitals and nursing homes were found violating some provisions of the Act, prompting the government to take corrective measures. Alongside these reforms, all private hospitals will now be required to display the cost of medical procedures prominently within their premises. “Patients have the right to know treatment costs in advance. They should be able to compare prices before deciding on hospital admission,” the minister said.
While the state government is pushing to strengthen the Bombay Nursing Homes Registration Act, many experts argue Maharashtra should also adopt the Centre’s Clinical Establishments (Registration and Regulation) Act, 2010 (CEA), which offers broader regulatory oversight. The CEA establishes uniform standards for medical facilities across India, addressing licensing, pricing, and service quality. In fact, a recent Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) report criticised Maharashtra for failing to implement this legislation, which could help curb unethical practices in private healthcare.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Despite the broader coverage of the CEA, health activists stress the importance of enforcing the Bombay Nursing Homes Registration Act, particularly for smaller nursing homes with only a few beds. These facilities, often criticised for employing unqualified medical personnel and overcharging patients, remain largely unregulated.
Dr Abhay Shukla, co-convenor of Jan Swasthya Abhiyan (JSA), highlighted that despite its limitations, the Bombay Nursing Homes Registration Act offers essential protections for patients. “The Act mandates that hospitals display indicative rates for treatments, ensuring transparency in medical billing. It also requires a toll-free grievance redressal mechanism for patients to report issues. However, these provisions remain largely unenforced, leaving patients vulnerable to overcharging and lack of accountability,” he said.
Under the Act, penalty for non-registration states that any violation of Section 3 shall, upon conviction, be punishable with imprisonment of up to six months, a fine of up to Rs 10,000, or both.

headline: After Baramati, Ajit Pawar’s NCP turns attention to Pune city ahead of Maharashtra civic polls
description: Sunetra Pawar has been discussing the NCP's strategies with senior party leaders ahead of civic polls in Maharashtra.
content:
After two hotly contested elections in the Pawar family bastion Baramati, the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) led by Ajit Pawar is now shifting its focus to Pune city to demonstrate its strength in Maharashtra politics ahead of civic polls expected later this year. Civic elections have been delayed in Maharashtra due to multiple petitions in the Supreme Court challenging the reservation of seats.
Following the split in the NCP, Ajit Pawar’s wife Sunetra Pawar contested the Lok Sabha elections 2024 from Baramati against his uncle Sharad Pawar’s daughter Supriya Sule. But she suffered defeat in the first electoral battle within the Pawar family. However, her husband Ajit Pawar later won the Maharashtra Assembly election from Baramati, defeating his nephew Yugendra Pawar of the NCP (SP).
Sunetra Pawar, a Rajya Sabha MP, recently held a meeting of all former party corporators in Circuit House. “There was a detailed discussion on party strategy for the forthcoming civic elections. It was decided that the party will reach out to every household in the city to convey the party’s development agenda and leadership of Ajit Pawar,” said Sunetra Pawar.
Meanwhile, Sule, the NCP (SP) working president, has also been regularly focusing on Pune city issues and reviewing the civic election preparations of her party’s local unit.
Parth Pawar said Sunetra Pawar conducted the meeting of all former Pune corporators. (Express Photo)
The Ajit-Sunetra couple’s son Parth Pawar, who had contested the 2019 Lok Sabha elections from the Maval seat and lost, was also part of her mother’s meeting with former corporators. Along with former party corporators, sitting legislator Chetan Tupe, former legislator Sunil Tingre, and city NCP chief Deepak Mankar were also present,” said Parth.
Outlining the NCP’s strategy, Tupe said, “In the election review meeting, it was decided to carry out maximum development work in the city under the leadership of Guardian minister Ajit Pawar, increase public relations and reach out to citizens to inform them on the work done so far and strengthen the party base.”
City NCP working president Pradeep Deshmukh said that A delegation led by Sunetra will soon meet the administration of Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) to take up various issues being raised by citizens.

headline: 2 AMU students, provost booked over beef biryani notice
description: After a protest from a section of students, the AMU administration clarified there was a typing error and that chicken biryani would not be discontinued.
content:
The Uttar Pradesh Police Monday booked two students and the provost of the Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) over a recent beef biryani notice.
Those named in the FIR have been identified as Mohammed Faizzullah and Mujjaism Ahmad Bhati, and provost Fasih Raghiv Gauhar.
The notice claimed that beef biryani would be served for lunch at the hostel on Sunday instead of the usual chicken biryani.
After a protest from a section of students, the AMU administration, though, clarified there was a typing error and that chicken biryani would not be discontinued.
“The matter had come to our notice Sunday morning. It contained a typing error. The notice had no official signatures and was immediately withdrawn and a show cause notice was issued to those who were authorised to put up posters at the AMU,” said Wasim Ahmed, Proctor, AMU.
The FIR has been lodged at the Civil Lines police station under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Sections 302 (uttering words with deliberate intent to hurt religious feelings), 270 (public nuisance) and 353 (public mischief).
“The FIR has been lodged and we are investigating the charges in the complaint. A definite legal action will be taken against those found guilty. The notice has hurt the sentiments of a large section of students,” said Dinesh Kumar, Station House Officer (SHO), Civil Lines police station.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Meanwhile, the Karni Sena has also expressed resentment over the biryani controversy and submitted a memorandum on the matter to Abhay Pandey, Deputy Superintendent of Police, Civil Lines.

headline: Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Shinde asks Centre to develop Shivaji Maharaj tourism circuit in Maharashtra
description: Union Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat told Shrikant Shinde that the Centre would give his proposal of a Shivaji Maharaj tourism circuit due consideration.
content:
Shiv Sena Lok Sabha MP Dr Shrikant Shinde Monday urged the Centre to establish a ‘Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Tourism Circuit’ under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme, an initiative seeking to preserve Maharashtra’s historic forts.
On day seven of Parliament’s Budget Session, Dr Shinde raised the demand in the Lok Sabha, emphasising the need to showcase these sites on national and global platforms. Union Tourism Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat assured him that the Centre would give the proposal due consideration.
During the Question Hour, Dr Shinde highlighted that the Union Ministry of Tourism had already supported Maharashtra’s coastal and spiritual circuits under the Swadesh Darshan Scheme. He proposed similar assistance for a dedicated ‘Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Tourism Circuit’, encompassing key forts such as Raigad, Rajgad, Sinhagad, and Shivneri. These historic sites, he noted, hold immense significance and could attract both domestic and international tourists with proper infrastructure development.
“Integrating these forts into a structured tourism circuit will offer visitors an immersive experience into the valorous history of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. It will also help future generations understand his legacy,” Dr Shinde said, expressing gratitude to the Centre for its ongoing support of Maharashtra’s tourism sector.
Responding to Dr Shinde’s appeal, Union Minister Shekhawat reaffirmed the government’s commitment to preserving India’s historical heritage. He cited recent initiatives such as the Shivsrushti Historical Theme Park in Pune, for which the state government allocated Rs 50 crore and the Centre Rs 76 crore.
Additionally, Rs 46 crore has been sanctioned for an underwater museum at Sindhudurg Fort. Minister Shekhawat also mentioned that a consolidated list of forts from Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu has been submitted to the World Heritage Committee, demonstrating the government’s dedication to fort tourism.
Dr Shinde further pressed for the release of pending funds, including Rs 122 crore for Sindhudurg district and Rs 132 crore for developing historical tourist areas in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar into a world-class tourism hub. He also inquired about the approval status of conservation and beautification proposals for the heritage corridor in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar, Koyna Nagar Garden, and Koyna Backwater Development. Minister Shekhawat assured that these proposals would be reviewed and approved soon.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“If implemented, this initiative will not only strengthen Maharashtra’s tourism sector but also elevate global awareness of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s legacy, reinforcing his historical and cultural significance on a broader scale,” a Sena functionary said.

headline: Delhi High Court grants 2-day custody parole to Engineer Rashid to attend Parliament
description: The Delhi High Court also imposed conditions that Abdul Rashid Sheikh, also known as Engineer Rashid, shall not use his phone or address the media.
content:
The Delhi High Court Monday granted Jammu and Kashmir Independent MP Abdul Rashid Sheikh, who is accused in a terror funding case, two-days custody parole to attend the ongoing Parliament session.
Justice Vikas Mahajan granted Rashid, who is also known as Engineer Rashid, permission to attend the Parliament session on February 11 and 13 under custody parole, while imposing conditions that he shall not use his phone or address the media.
A detailed order is yet to be made public.
Rashid is in judicial custody in connection with a terror funding case being investigated by the National Investigation Agency (NIA).
Last Friday, the High Court reserved its order in the plea by the Baramulla Independent MP. Noting that the court has jurisdiction to exercise its discretion in such cases, relying on past judicial precedents, Justice Mahajan orally remarked to the National Investigation Agency (NIA) counsel Akshai Malik and senior advocate Siddharth Luthra that “there has to be material” to indicate that there might be a security concern or risk, to deny him custody parole.
Rashid was arrested in 2019 under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. According to NIA, he allegedly used various public platforms to “propagate the ideology of separatism and secessionism”, was closely associated with various terrorist organisations, and wanted to “legitimise” the United Jihad Council, a platform of anti-India militant groups in Jammu and Kashmir.
The first part of the Budget Session of Parliament ends on February 13.

headline: Body of teen boy with stab marks found in North East Delhi
description: The Delhi Police said the victim was around 17 years old.
content:
The body of an unidentified teenage boy was found with multiple stab wounds on a street in North East Delhi’s Gautampuri Sunday night. According to the Delhi Police, the Seelampur police station received information about the injured boy around 9.45 pm, and dispatched a team to the spot.
When the team arrived at the spot, they found the victim, estimated to be around 17-18 years old, lying in a pool of blood. Crime and forensic teams were called to examine the scene, and the body was sent to GTB Hospital for a postmortem.
A case has been registered under sections 103 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) at the Seelampur Police Station.
“Efforts are underway to identify and apprehend those responsible, with police teams actively investigating the case,” said Ashish Mishra, Deputy Commissioner of Police, North East.

headline: As residents fear serial killer on prowl, Bengaluru police identify man behind slashing spree in Indiranagar
description: The Bengaluru police have launched a search for the man who allegedly attacked four others with a knife in the span of five hours.
content:
Four slashing incidents occurred in the upscale Indiranagar area of Bengaluru on the intervening night of Saturday and Sunday, and these are suspected to involve a single perpetrator for whom a search has been launched, said the police.
“The suspect has been identified as one Kadamba, who is known in police records as a mobile phone thief and drunkard. He committed the attacks in a drunken state. He is a resident of the Byappanahalli slum (near Indiranagar). He was last seen in Hoskote (in rural Bengaluru),” said D Devaraj, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Bengaluru East).
Two of the attacks targeted street snack vendors, one a bike taxi rider, resulting in the theft of the rider’s motorbike and mobile phone, and the fourth involved a security guard who attempted to intervene and stop the attack, according to the police. The Indiranagar police filed four FIRs regarding these attacks between 9.40 pm Saturday and 2.30 am Sunday.
The first attack occurred near the Kund hotel, close to the Indiranagar 100 Feet Road, around 9.40 pm. A snack vendor named Deepak Kumar Verma, 24, was allegedly attacked by an unidentified man estimated to be between 23 and 25 years old. The assailant approached Verma under the pretence of requesting a snack, as per the complaint.

Verma said he told the man that only pani puri was available but he lingered near the store. When all the customers at the store had gone, he allegedly began abusing Verma in Kannada, Tamil and Hindi. He then allegedly pulled out a knife and slashed at the neck of the vendor, causing an injury on the neck. The complainant described the attacker as wheatish in complexion and wearing a red shirt and white trousers.
The second incident occurred around 800 metres away from the first when another snack vendor, Tammaiah M, 44, who sells chaat on the street near a phone store on 100 Feet Road was attacked. According to the police complaint by the vendor, the man approached the store at around 9.50 pm and ordered a pani puri. When Tammaiah prepared a pani puri, the attacker allegedly refused to eat it without making a payment and demanded the scanner to make a UPI payment.
However, when the vendor gave the scanner, the man allegedly claimed that he could not pay Rs 30. He soon started an argument with the vendor and began abusing him before pulling out a knife, slashing at the vendor’s face, and running away, as per the complaint.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The third incident reportedly occurred around 2.30 am near the Lono pub on 80 Feet Road. A bike taxi rider named Adil Aamirsab, 24, was allegedly stopped on the road by a man who requested that he be taken to the Krishnaraja Puram (K R Puram) railway station in East Bengaluru. When the scooter rider refused to comply with the stranger’s request and said he was going to his home near Magadi Road in west Bengaluru, the attacker allegedly pulled out a knife and slashed at the neck and finger of the scooter rider who tried to resist the attack.
The man allegedly stole the scooter along with a mobile phone that was being used for navigation. According to the complaint filed by the scooter rider, a security guard who attempted to stop the attacker was also slashed, the police said.
The news of the slashings spread rapidly on Sunday and Monday among the resident welfare groups in Indiranagar, with some suggesting the presence of a serial killer. “The criminal’s modus operandi seems to be that he stops people randomly and engages them in some conversation, he then slashes/stabs them in the neck when they are in a vulnerable position and runs away afterwards,” said a social media message in one resident welfare group in Indiranagar.

headline: Mumbai woman kills husband, dumps body 500-metre away with help of boyfriend; CCTV footage helps crack case
description: Woman’s purported boyfriend was living with the couple at the time of the murder.
content:
The Malvani police in Mumbai Sunday arrested a woman for allegedly killing her husband and then dumping his body 500 metres from their residence with the help of her purported boyfriend. The woman’s boyfriend has also been arrested on charges of assisting the woman in dumping the body. CCTV footage from the area helped the police to crack the case within four hours of the crime being reported.
The police control room was informed Sunday early morning that a man’s body with its throat slit was lying in the Soham compound.
Thereafter, Anand Bhoite, zonal deputy commissioner of police (DCP), pressed multiple teams to solve the case. A police team while scanning CCTV footage, spotted a woman and a man carrying the body on a two-wheeler. When the police checked footage from other CCTVs, they ascertained that the two suspects had come from the direction of the Gamdevi Temple. The police then started making inquiries and eventually managed to ascertain the identity of the deceased person as one Rajesh Chauhan, 30.
When the police reached his home in Malvani Ali Talai Gate Number 6, they found blood stains in the house. The police then subjected his wife Puja, 30, to sustained interrogation in which she admitted to having killed her husband.
“She claimed that she was fed up with her husband’s drinking habit. He would come home drunk and beat her up. Out of frustration, she slit his throat Sunday when their two kids were sleeping. After killing her husband, she woke up her friend Imran Mohammad Rizwan, who also lives with them and hails from the same village. With the help of Rizwan, she dumped the body. They covered Chauhan’s body with a bedsheet pretending to take him to the hospital,” said a senior police officer.
“Rizwan had been staying at their place for the past two to three months. Puja had told Chauhan that she considered Rizwan to be her brother,” said Inspector Jeevan Bhatkule of Malvani police station.
The police, however, said they were not believing Puja’s claims and trying to find out if she killed her husband owing to her extra-marital affair.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Both the accused have been arrested under relevant sections of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita,” DCP Bhoite said.
The police were trying to trace the weapon used in the crime. They would produce the accused in court on Monday.

headline: ZSI, University of Calcutta, others develop novel technique for fruit fly control
description: "This new method will not only protect crops but also reduce our dependence on chemical pesticides," the Director of ZSI said.
content:
In a collaborative study led by researchers from the Zoological Survey of India (ZSI), the University of Calcutta and other institutions have developed a novel technique for fruit fly control which they say can potentially revolutionise global efforts to combat the pests.
Fruit flies (tephritidae) infestations pose a significant threat to global agriculture, impacting crop yields, food security, and international trade.
The research focused on true fruit flies collected from various districts across West Bengal. The team sequenced mitochondrial COI gene regions from the fruit fly species found on cucurbitaceous crops like pumpkins, cucumbers, and gourds. The analysis revealed 30 uniquely variable sites at nucleotide positions, thereby offering a “crucial target for species-specific interventions.
Highlighting the importance of the study, Dr Dhriti Banerjee, Director of the ZSI, said, “Fruit flies are devastating pests, and in West Bengal, where over 70% of rural households depend on agriculture, our work is critical. This new method will not only protect crops but also reduce our dependence on chemical pesticides. By enabling targeted pest-control measures, we can minimise environmental damage and empower agricultural professionals with precision tools, moving away from broad-spectrum approaches that can harm non-target species.”
The damage is caused either directly by the larvae of the fruit flies or indirectly by harmful microorganisms or decomposers that enter fruits and vegetables through egg-laying holes made by the female fruit flies. This leads to fruit rot, premature dropping, and massive economic losses, amounting to billions of dollars annually.
This novel method enables rapid, accurate, and reliable species identification, facilitating earlier interventions and mitigating crop damage during outbreaks.
Researchers Ankush Mitra, Pubali Mitra, Pradosh Mahadani, and Subrata Trivedi believe their findings will be instrumental in safeguarding agricultural productivity. They envision this method as being implemented across diverse regions and applied to a broader range of pest species, establishing it as a versatile and powerful approach in the pest control sector.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Dr Madhusudan Das, Professor, University of Calcutta, said, “With increasing population, the demand for healthy food continues to grow. So, ensuring sustainable agricultural practices is more important than ever. By identifying specific fruit fly species with precision, more sustainable pest control strategies can be implemented. This would also align with the global push towards reducing chemical pesticides in agriculture, thereby promoting healthier ecosystems and preserving biodiversity”.

headline: ‘What is need for INDIA bloc if we keep fighting with each other’: Uddhav Sena blames Congress, AAP for Delhi election setback
description: Shiv Sena mouthpiece 'Saamana' said it is now time for the INDIA bloc to be seen everywhere, not just inside Parliament, after the BJP dethroned the AAP in Delhi Assembly elections.
content:
Shiv Sena (UBT) Monday said the infighting between the Congress and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) contributed to the BJP’s victory in the Delhi Assembly elections. The Uddhav Thackeray-led party questioned the necessity of the Opposition INDIA bloc if its members continue to be in conflict with each other instead of uniting against the BJP, which won 48 seats in the Delhi elections, while the AAP secured only 22 seats and the Congress none.
“The disunity and discord among opposition parties in Delhi and Maharashtra directly aided the BJP in its victory. In Delhi, both the AAP and the Congress fought to destroy each other, making the victory easier for the BJP. If this continues, why even form alliances? Just fight to your heart’s content… Just keep fighting among yourself,” Sena (UBT) mouthpiece Saamana wrote in its editorial as the BJP is set to return to power in Delhi after 27 years.
“If no lesson is going to be learnt by anyone from these polls and its results, then these people should take credit for aiding the autocratic regime to gain power. There is no need to even take a dip in the Ganga river for doing such noble work,” the editorial added.
It stated that the INDIA bloc is only seen inside Parliament, and now it is time for the alliance to be visible everywhere, even on the streets. It emphasised that the ongoing discord, evident in the recent polls in Maharashtra, only strengthens the BJP’s position under Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
Sena (UBT) accused the Congress of actively contributing to the AAP’s defeat in at least 14 seats in Delhi. It also said a similar scenario unfolded in Haryana during last year’s Assembly elections, which also the BJP won. The editorial questioned whether internal factions within Congress were deliberately undermining Rahul Gandhi’s leadership.
“The losses in the Delhi elections are directly impacting the democratic processes in the country. Even in Maharashtra, local Congress leaders prolonged seat-sharing negotiations for the Assembly polls until the last minute, resulting in a chaotic situation,” the editorial stated.
Congress should take initiative for coordination with allies: Sanjay Raut
Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut said that as the leading party in the INDIA bloc, the Congress is responsible for taking the initiative to facilitate smooth coordination with all alliance partners. Raut emphasised that Congress should act as a convener rather than just raising its arms during the seat-sharing negotiations. Raut, however, said the AAP is just as accountable as the Congress for the Delhi defeat and advised that alliance politics should involve no ego.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“The ‘Batenge toh katenge’ slogan raised by Prime Minister Narendra also applies to the INDIA bloc. If we were to hand over the state to the BJP in this way, how will we fight the future Lok Sabha elections? We fought the Lok Sabha (elections 2024) together. Every party in the alliance worked for each other, and the INDIA bloc did well, said Raut.
He said that before the Lok Sabha elections, the INDIA allies were holding regular meetings and discussions, however, this did not happen during the state polls. Raut said there is uncertainty and confusion among the public regarding whether the Opposition bloc is meant only for contesting elections or if it aims to be a united front at all times.
“The duty of the Opposition party is also to take to the streets, including in the Assembly and Lok Sabha. The India bloc is only visible in Parliament. It is also necessary to come out of Parliament. There are Big leaders in the Opposition bloc like Uddhav Thackeray, Sharad Pawar, Akhilesh Yadav, Tejashwi Yadav, and Farooq Abdullah. The INDIA bloc should remain strong and united. Is the INDIA bloc or Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA) only for contesting elections? This is the question in the minds of the people,” said Raut.
“The Congress is the dominant force in the INDIA bloc, as a national party with 100 (99) MPs. It has the potential to win over 100 seats, but this can happen only if we all unite and fight together. We have seen this success in states like Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra. The Congress needs to take a leadership role in every aspect. Being the ‘big brother’ should not be limited to seat-sharing; it also encompasses the coordination responsibility,” Raut added.

headline: Air pollution kills as many people every year as the world wars did: Sonam Wangchuk
description: The third world war is not in the future but it has begun, not between nations but between man and nature, Sonam Wangchuk added.
content:
Innovator and activist Sonam Wangchuk on Sunday noted that the issue of air pollution claims as many lives as the world wars do, while speaking at the Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics (GIPE).
“Air pollution alone kills 70 lakh people every year. Add to that some other climate related incidents and at least one crore people die every year… I looked up to compare it with other unnatural deaths in history and it took me to the World Wars…they lasted for around 10 years combined and also killed one crore people every year,” Wangchuk said.
Adding to his point Wangchuk said, “Air pollution matches the death rate for the first and second World Wars yet the difference is that we know them as ‘World Wars’ but this (air pollution deaths) we don’t even recognize.” The third world war is not in the future but it has begun, not between nations but between man and nature, he added.
Quoting Mirza Ghalib’s famous couplet “hazaron khwahishen aisi ki har khwahish pe dam nikle, bahut nikle mere armaan lekin phir bhi kam nikle”, Wangchuk explained the harms of consumerism and how it leads to the destruction of the planet. Humorously remarking that people in Delhi use thicker blankets than people in Ladakh due to the air conditioning being on full blast, Wangchuk said that the people of Pune were much better.
Gurudas Nulkar, Professor, Director Centre for Sustainable Development at GIPE, also spoke at the event and said, “People like Sonam and so many other activists who are working there know the pulse of the people. The elected representatives need to be brought along with that on a much larger scale.”
