headline: 31 new MLAs have criminal cases against them, AAP tops list: ADR
description: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) tops the category with 68% (15) of its winning candidates having criminal cases against them, compared to 33% (16) of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s newly-elected legislators
content:
Of the 70 newly elected MLAs, 31 have criminal cases filed against them, as per the latest report by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR).
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) tops the category with 68% (15) of its winning candidates having criminal cases against them, compared to 33% (16) of the Bharatiya Janata Party’s newly-elected legislators.
The BJP on Saturday secured a decisive victory in the Delhi elections by winning 48 of 70 seats, against the AAP’s tally of 22.
The financial disparities among winners are stark, as per the ADR report. BJP MLAs are significantly wealthier, with an average asset value of Rs 28.59 crore —more than three times the average assets of AAP winners at Rs 7.74 crore. Among the wealthiest, three BJP winners are billionaires: Karnail Singh (Rs 259.67 crore), Manjinder Singh Sirsa (Rs 248.85 crore), and Parvesh Sahib Singh (Rs 115.63 crore). By contrast, AAP’s Sanjeev Jha from Burari reported the lowest assets at just Rs 14.47 lakh.
The ADR report on the Delhi Assembly Elections 2025 highlights that 24% of the winning candidates (17) face serious charges — 45% (10) of AAP MLAs and 15% (7) of BJP winners. Serious criminal cases include offences that are non-bailable, carry a maximum punishment of five years or more, or relate to crimes such as murder, kidnapping, and crimes against women and children.
When compared to previous Assembly elections, the proportion of winners with criminal cases has declined — from 61% (43) in 2020 to 44% (31) in 2025. Similarly, the number of winners facing serious charges has dropped from 53% (37) in 2020 to 24% (17) this year.
In terms of education, 64% (45) of winners have qualifications at the graduate level or higher, with 23 candidates holding postgraduate degrees and one possessing a doctorate. However, 33% (23) of candidates declared their educational attainment as between 5th and 12th pass.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Assembly also remains predominantly male, with only 7% (5) of 70 female leaders getting elected — a decline from 2020 when female members accounted for 11% (8) of the total strength of the Assembly.
The age distribution shows that 67% (47) of winners are between 41 and 60, while 20% (14) are aged 61 or older. The youngest winner, BJP’s Umang Bajaj, is 31, while the oldest, Tilak Ram Gupta of BJP, is 73.

headline: ‘AAP govt did nothing in the last 10 years… except switch off our mics’: BJP MLA Vijender Gupta
description: Under the leadership of PM Modi, the new BJP government will present the 14 long-pending CAG (Comptroller and Auditor General) reports in the very first session of the Delhi Assembly, claimed Gupta.
content:
Vijender Gupta, former Leader of the Opposition in the Delhi Assembly and three-time MLA from Rohini, will now find himself across the political aisle. On Saturday, the BJP swept the Assembly election with 48 seats and Gupta himself won by the highest margin — 37,816 votes — among other BJP MLAs. In an interview with Gayathri Mani, he says the first order of business for the new government will be presenting all 14 CAG reports in the first sitting of the Assembly session.
Excerpts:
This is your third consecutive win. How do you feel?
I am very thankful to the public for trusting me… In a way, the people have handed over Delhi to the Prime Minister because the AAP-da had created such a mess that the city is crumbling today. They (the public) wanted change, development and relief from the AAP-da government.
What is BJP’s roadmap for the first year?
Delhi is the national capital and its people are crying for basic facilities like pothole-free roads and clean water. Ensuring this is the government’s responsibility. The previous government did nothing in the last 10 years. We will not wait or take two-three years to achieve our target. We’ll start working to resolve these issues from day one on a war footing. This is our commitment.
Also Read | After Delhi victory, BJP eyes its next goal — winning MCD Mayoral polls
After resigning, former CM Atishi said the AAP would make BJP fulfill the promise of giving Rs 2,500 to women…
First, I think they should apologise to the people for making fake promises. They promised women Rs 1,000 in Delhi and Punjab but did not deliver. The people have punished you for that and instead of apologising, these non-performers are advising us now. If we have promised it, we will do it.
How is the BJP going to implement this scheme?
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
It is on our agenda, and we will deliver it. PM ki guarantee matlab poori hone ki guarantee (If the PM has said it, it will be done). AAP implementing its scheme was a mere gimmick. We will bring our scheme and work in a time-bound manner to deliver it.
As LoP in the previous Assembly, you raised several issues from pending CAG reports to renovation costs of the CM’s official residence. Will this be taken up by the new government?
Under the leadership of PM Modi, the new BJP government will present the 14 long-pending CAG (Comptroller and Auditor General) reports in the very first session of the Delhi Assembly. I met the Lieutenant-Governor sahab in this regard today. He has promised full cooperation. As soon as these reports are made public, the massive corruption of the now-defunct AAP government will be laid bare, revealing how Kejriwal and his party leaders misled the people of Delhi with lies while engaging in corruption worth crores.
Till now, they did not let us raise issues in the Assembly and never let us speak. Be it issues of roads, sewage, cleaning the Yamuna or pollution, as soon as we started raising the issues, they used to switch off our mics… This will now change.
Who is going to be Delhi’s CM?
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
This is a high-command issue. There are 48 MLAs and the party can choose anyone. Whatever decision the party takes, it will be for the benefit of Delhi, the country, the government, and the people… We have full confidence in our leadership that the decision will be taken keeping everything in mind…

headline: BJP’s senior leaders meet newly elected MLAs to analyse poll results
description: Delhi’s seven MPs also held meetings with MLAs in their constituency.
content:
A day after its massive victory in the Delhi Assembly polls, senior leaders of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and MPs held meetings with all 48 MLAs to discuss their performance, and results and to guide the new leaders on how to work to develop the national capital.
National General Secretary (Organisation) BL Santosh, National Vice-President and Delhi BJP Election In-Charge Baijayant Panda, National Secretary and Delhi BJP co-in-charge Dr Alka Gurjar, co in-charge Atul Garg, Delhi State President Virendra Sachdeva and others were part of the meetings.
Besides, Delhi’s seven MPs also held meetings with MLAs in their constituency.
“Senior leaders provided the MLAs with guidance on working within proper organisational and administrative frameworks. They were further advised on how to start working in their constituency on development-related issues… they were also told to maintain complete transparency in their working style,” said a BJP official.
Further, the official said, the senior leaders also drew attention to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s victory message on Saturday evening and said efforts should begin to build a developed Delhi, in line with the PM’s vision, without wasting any time.
Several MLAs on Sunday took out victory marches in their constituency to thank the people.

headline: 3 fake cops steal gold ornaments of 71 yr old woman in Pune
description: The victim woman, who is a resident of Tingre Nagar, lodged a first information report (FIR) in this case at the Vishrantwadi police station.
content:
Three individuals posing as police personnel duped a 71 year old woman by stealing her jewellery worth Rs 2.75 lakhs on the Airport road in Vishrantwadi on Saturday morning.
The victim woman, who is a resident of Tingre Nagar, lodged a first information report (FIR) in this case at the Vishrantwadi police station.
Police said the woman and her husband were passing through the Joshi Wadewale on the Airport road in Vishrantwadi around 10 pm on Saturday. Three persons posing as policemen approached the woman. They asked the women to remove her jewellery as some investigation was going on.
After she removed the jewellery, the trio allegedly played a trickster and made away with the gold ornaments worth Rs 2.75 lakhs. The woman later came to know that her jewellery was missing. She approached the police and filed a complaint against the conmen.
Police sub inspector Anil Padekar, the investigation officer said, “No arrest has been made yet. Investigation is on.” Police have booked the accused persons under sections 318(4),204,3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

headline: Shraddha Walkar’s father dies of heart attack in Vasai
description: Shraddha was allegedly strangled by her boyfriend Aftab Poonawala in May 2022 in Delhi.
content:
Vikas Walkar, father of Shraddha Walkar who was allegedly murdered by her live-in partner in 2022, died at his Vasai residence early Sunday due to a heart attack. He was 62.
According to police, Walker lived in Vasai’s Sanskrit Apartment. His son told police that Walkar was found motionless in the morning and he was rushed to Cardinal Grace hospital, where doctors declared him dead.
“Walkar died of an (heart) attack. Panchnama and post-mortem procedures were duly done. His son has not made any complaint. There was no foul play in his death. Following due procedure we have registered an accidental death report,” said Balkrishna Ghadigaonkar, senior inspector of Vasai police station.
Also Read | Rolling out UCC, Pushkar Singh Dhami says ‘aim to ensure an Aaftab never commits brutality against a Shraddha Walkar’
Shraddha was allegedly strangled by her boyfriend Aftab Poonawala in May 2022 in Delhi.
After killing her, Poonawala allegedly chopped her body into on the night of May 18 inside their house at Chattarpur Pahadi in South Delhi. Poonawalla then allegedly disposed of these pieces across the city.

headline: 8,000 contractual workers of Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation to go on indefinite strike from Monday
description: The workers have been protesting wage disparities for several months, with some participating in a hunger strike outside the municipal headquarters since December 2024.
content:
Around 8,000 contractual workers of the Navi Mumbai Municipal Corporation (NMMC) have declared an indefinite strike from Monday, demanding “equal pay for equal work”.
Essential civic services, including sanitation, water supply, and healthcare, are likely to disrupted due to the strike.
The workers have been protesting wage disparities for several months, with some participating in a hunger strike outside the municipal headquarters since December 2024. They argue that despite repeated appeals, the administration has not taken significant steps to address their concerns.
The strike is led under the banner of Samaj Samata Kamgar Sangh, a union of the municipal workers. Mangesh Lad, secretary of Samaj Samata Kamgar Sangh, said, “We called for the strike just to get the equal work equal pay criteria checked. We all work in different segments like healthcare, sanitation, water supply, cleanliness, crematorium, etc and if we are not heard we would step by step stop working in all the departments.”
NMMC, however, has denied these claims, stating that it has consistently ensured fair wages, bonuses, provident fund contributions, and other statutory benefits as per the Minimum Wages Act.
The civic body also emphasised that it sought guidance from the Maharashtra government regarding wage parity for contractual workers, but no additional funds were allocated for this purpose by the state government.
Following this, the municipal commissioner appointed a special committee, led by an additional commissioner, to examine the legal and financial feasibility of the workers’ demands.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The committee’s report, based on legal provisions and past court rulings, was shared with labour unions, which were then rejected by them.
The NMMC is engaging in discussions with labor representatives to avoid disruption of services.

headline: Ahmedabad: Teen ‘sexually exploited’ for 10 months; brother of HIV-positive accused held
description: The brother of the main accused in the case is suspected to have helped him conceal the whereabouts of the girl, along with their mother.
content:
A 22-year-old man, whose HIV-positive brother allegedly kidnapped and sexually exploited a 16-year-old girl for 10 months, has been arrested in Ahmedabad city. The brother of the main accused in the case is suspected to have helped him conceal the whereabouts of the girl, along with their mother. The police, however, said that the main accused had allegedly lured the minor on the pretext of marriage.
The police on Friday also received a five-day remand of the main accused from a local court, said an inspector connected with the probe.
On March 22 last year, the victim had gone to a locality in Ahmedabad for a social event with her family. Around 8 pm, her father filed a complaint alleging that her daughter had been kidnapped from the venue. An FIR was filed at the police station concerned. A case was filed under Section 363 of the Indian Penal Code.
The minor girl remained missing for three months following the FIR, after which the investigation was handed over to the Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP), F Division, Ahmedabad city police. However, when the divisional ACP also failed to find the girl, the case was handed over to the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of the Crime Branch.
Meanwhile, the minor’s father had also filed a habeas corpus plea in the Gujarat High Court.
The AHTU finally managed to trace the main accused to a town in Madhya Pradesh. He was apprehended and the girl was brought back to Ahmedabad where she reunited with her family. The accused was handed over to police and placed under arrest on February 6.
During questioning, it was revealed that the main accused had been suffering from HIV for the past 10 years, leading investigators to suspect that the survivor could have contracted it. The inspector told The Indian Express that the medical test of the survivor was still pending as she was sick and traumatised by the 10-month ordeal.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Notably, an AHTU statement mentions that the HIV-positive accused may have sexually exploited six other females earlier. The police are investigating into this matter.
An AHTU statement also said that the main accused used to work near the workplace of the minor’s father and had developed an acquaintance with him. He began to frequent their house and attend social functions, thus also developing a bond with the minor.
On March 22, 2024, he called the minor to a village in Ahmedabad and hid her at a rented house. The AHTU alleged that the main accused’s brother and mother had helped him in the act. The AHTU had also alleged that the main accused had then taken the minor to Surat in Gujarat, Aurangabad, Nagpur and Beed in Maharashtra, Hyderabad in Telangana, and Bilaspur in Chhattisgarh to evade the police. Further investigation in the case is underway.

headline: If Uddhav Thackeray had felt assured of Maharashtra CM post in 2019, he should’ve at least discussed it: Fadnavis
description: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis narrates his side of the story of the breakdown of the BJP-Shiv Sena alliance after the 2019 Assembly elections.
content:
Speaking about the breakdown of the long-time alliance between the BJP and the undivided Shiv Sena after the 2019 Assembly elections, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis alleged on Saturday that Uddhav Thackeray had had a tacit understanding with NCP founder Sharad Pawar.
“If you (Uddhav Thackeray) were under the impression that you were told you would be made CM behind closed doors, you could have at least discussed it. You didn’t discuss it because you had decided since the first day… Sharad Pawar ji had a pre-poll tacit understanding with them.”
The senior BJP leader was speaking at an event hosted by The Jaipur Dialogues, a right-wing website, in Pune on Saturday.
Fadnavis said that when Thackeray demanded the chief minister’s post for 2.5 years after the 2019 polls, he discussed it with Amit Shah, who outright refused to entertain the idea.
According to Fadnavis, he then told Thackeray, “We can’t give you the CM post for 2.5 years. We are the largest party and will be the largest party in the future as well, so the CM post will remain with us for 5 years. We did not give you the deputy CM post last time. We can offer that this time.”
Fadnavis said the alliance broke down at that point, but Thackeray reached out for talks after four days.
At this point, Fadnavis said, Thackeray had given up his demand for the CM post and was instead seeking the Palghar Lok Sabha seat. “Amit bhai and others told me that they are our old partners. ‘One seat doesn’t matter; you give it to them’. So we gave them the seat with the candidate,” he added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Thackeray later requested a meeting with Shah before a press conference, where they spoke privately for around 10 minutes.
After this meeting, Fadnavis said, he spoke at press conferences as agreed to by both parties, but Thackeray later claimed at another press conference that “all their options were open”.
“If you (Uddhav Thackeray) were under the impression that you were told you would be made CM behind closed doors, you could have at least discussed it… The day their (Maha Vikas Aghadi) government was formed, I tried getting in touch with Uddhav Thackeray, but he even refused to answer my call,” the BJP leader said.

headline: A brief celebration, then silence: At AAP office, workers stare at party’s rout in Delhi
description: A pavilion draped in AAP’s signature blue and yellow was set up outside the office, with a stage under it, mounted with a podium and rows of empty chairs.
content:
Delhi Assembly Elections: As jubilant supporters danced to the beats of dhol-nagadas outside the Bhartiya Janata Party’s (BJP) Delhi headquarters on Saturday, the mood at the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) office on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Marg was markedly different — a solemn silence enveloped its premises.
Before the counting for the Delhi Assembly polls began, AAP’s Delhi spokesperson, Jasmine Shah, stepped outside to address the press. Exuding confidence, he said, “We believe the AAP is going to form the government with a huge majority. This was not a normal election. On one side, it was AAP, whereas on the other, it was the entire system… This was an election between two models — the AAP model and the BJP model.” However, as the day progressed and the numbers told a different story, the party office’s gates remained shut, with no ministers, senior leaders, MLAs, or even municipal councillors in sight.
Once the BJP’s victory became more certain, at 11.27 am, a few of the party’s Punjab leaders arrived, but they too chose to enter the party office without any comments on the voters’ decision.
Also Read | Why AAP defeat in Delhi polls is a setback to Uddhav Thackeray and Sharad Pawar
A pavilion draped in AAP’s signature blue and yellow was set up outside the office, with a stage under it, mounted with a podium and rows of empty chairs. A massive screen displayed live voting trends, drawing the attention of a handful of party volunteers and media personnel. Some volunteers, clad in party scarves and the signature AAP cap, kept a watchful eye on the fluctuating numbers, hoping for a turnaround.
The battle for the New Delhi constituency, a key contest featuring AAP chief and former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal against BJP’s former MP Parvesh Sahib Singh had momentarily kept spirits alive.
As per the Election Commission data, at 9.50 am, Kejriwal was leading after the second round of counting. A short-lived celebration ensued as party workers erupted in cheers, breaking into a dance to the party’s campaign song, ‘Phir Layenge Kejriwal.’
However, each time the margins narrowed and the BJP regained its lead, a hush fell over the party office.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Once the results were evident, pointing to an AAP rout — and Kejriwal’s defeat — volunteers began trickling out of the premises.
Some party workers attributed the loss to AAP being under continuous scrutiny, echoing Kejriwal’s earlier allegations of BJP candidates in general, and more specifically his competitor Parvesh Singh, using “money power” to influence voter decisions.
Others, like Amarjeet Nanda — who claims to have been associated with the party since its inception during the Anna Hazare-led anti-corruption movement — expressed a need for introspection. “I have been with the party for 12 years. This election loss should prompt us to reconsider our choices. The party needs to reassess its leadership and restructure to regain public trust,” he said.

headline: Twist in Kochi teen’s ‘suicide’? Father seeks probe into what happened at flat where boy lived with mother, stepfather
description: The 15-year-old’s mother had earlier alleged he committed suicide because of bullying he endured at school.
content:
The father of a 15-year-old boy, who allegedly died by suicide after facing assault and harassment from schoolmates in Kochi, has called for a probe into what happened at the apartment where the boy was living with his mother and stepfather.
According to his mother, the teenager jumped from the 26th floor of his apartment building in Kochi on January 15 following ragging and “humiliation” from his schoolmates over his skin colour. The mother had petitioned police regarding his alleged treatment by his schoolmates and raised allegations against the vice-principal of another school where he had studied until October last year.
The boy’s death triggered widespread outrage in Kerala, with several celebrities joining a campaign seeking justice for the boy.
However, his father, who divorced the boy’s mother years earlier, has filed a police complaint asking for a probe into the circumstances surrounding his death.
In his January 21 complaint, days before the mother approached the police, the father said he had constantly been in touch with his son, who never indicated having any issues in school. A day before the boy’s death, he had promised to talk the next day, the father said.
The father said the boy had happily returned from school on the day of his death, and the suggestion that he then jumped to his death without any provocation raised doubts.
“It is difficult to believe that the boy had certain issues with classmates and that prompted him to take the extreme step. What happened at the apartment and who all were present at the flat must be probed into. I want the truth behind my son’s death to be brought out,” the father claimed in the complaint.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The father claimed that his son had been on a phone call with his stepfather before his death and that the boy had hung up, after which the stepfather tried to get in touch with him through the house help’s phone but wasn’t successful. “His life with the family (mother and stepfather) was tense, which was evident from his chats with me. I was not informed when he was moved” from his previous school, the father claimed.
Thrikkakara Assistant Police Commissioner P V Baby said police were looking at all angles. “We are verifying the veracity of the allegations from both sides and scrutinising the evidence,” he said.
A member of the boy’s mother’s family said, “Let the police find out the truth. We have nothing to say regarding the allegations raised by the boy’s father.”
His school has rejected allegations of ragging and said it was open to any investigation.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The boy’s mother had alleged that he was forcibly taken to a washroom, where was made to lick the toilet seat and that his head was pushed into the toilet, which was flushed.
The school said it conducted an investigation into the allegations, collecting statements from teachers and classmates regarding the alleged bullying, but found no evidence or eyewitnesses regarding such an incident.

headline: Why AAP defeat in Delhi polls is a setback to Uddhav Thackeray and Sharad Pawar
description: Sharad Pawar and Uddhav Thackeray often joined hands to help the AAP and vice versa in their political battle against the BJP.
content:
The Aam Aadmi Party’s defeat in the Delhi Assembly elections is a body blow to the Shiv Sena (UBT) and NCP (SP) in Maharashtra which made their fight against the BJP a common cause with AAP National Convenor Arvind Kejriwal.
The outcome in the Delhi Assembly elections has given the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) reasons to celebrate in a big way not just in the Capital but also in Maharashtra.
While the AAP was never a major force to reckon with in terms of electoral base in Maharashtra, the Shiv Sena (UBT) and NCP (SP) held hope in Kejriwal. It had a presence as Shiv Sena (UBT) president Uddhav Thackeray, NCP (SP) chief Sharad Pawar, and the AAP led by Arvind Kejriwal often came together through the INDIA bloc or otherwise to counter the BJP at the Centre and in the state.
Also Read | AAP-Congress alliance would have restricted BJP, says Shiv Sena (UBT); Cong says Kejriwal wasn’t ready to join hands
AAP’s Maharashtra link
In many ways, Kejriwal’s connection with Maharashtra had its origins in the Indian Against Corruption crusade which gained momentum in 2011-12, and was led by social reformer Anna Hazare, a resident of Ralegaon in Pune district.
At the rally held in Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, those who played significant roles in the fight against corruption and pressing for the Lokpal Bill included Arvind Kejriwal, Shanti Bhushan, Prashant Bhushan, Kiran Bedi, Medha Patkar, Swami Agnivesh, Col Devinder Sehrawat, Harsh Mandar et al. It was in April 2011 when Hazare went on a hunger strike demanding the Lokpal Bill.
Anna Hazare and Kejriwal, who shared the platform and a cause 14 years ago, are no longer on the same page. In fact, Hazare had given a clarion call to vote against the AAP in the 2025 Delhi Assembly elections.
As the BJP marched to victory pulling a hat-rick post Haryana, Maharashtra, and now Delhi, Hazare minced no words to attack Kejriwal. Hazare said, “A leader should always be selfless and upright. If you want to elicit people’s support these are necessary qualities.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Lending a helping hand
In Kejriwal, who after graduating from IIT Kharagpur joined the Indian Revenue Services and then took to politics, these regional parties saw a firm and committed leader who dared to speak against the BJP’s central leadership.
Also Read | ‘Congress, AAP did not put their egos aside’: INDIA allies say a united front could have defeated BJP in Delhi election
There are several instances where Sharad Pawar and Uddhav Thackeray have joined hands to help the AAP and vice versa in their political battle against the BJP.
When the BJP through its ‘Operation Lotus’ split the Shiv Sena led by Uddhav Thackeray and Sharad Pawar’s Nationalist Congress Party, AAP leaders both at the Centre and Maharashtra were at the forefront of attacking the saffron party.
When the Centre promulgated an ordinance to create an authority for the transfer and postings of Group A officers through legislation, Kejriwal visited Matoshree to meet Uddhav Thackeray to seek his support, and also met Pawar. He appealed to all non-BJP parties to come forward and protest against the legislation arguing it was undermining the roles of elected state government.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
When Kejriwal was arrested, Shiv Sena (UBT) and NCP (SP) pledged support and participated in the protest rally held in Delhi. During the Lok Sabha and Maharashtra Assembly polls, Kejriwal participated in the INDIA bloc rally held at Shivaji Park and BKC, respectively, last year.
The Delhi Assembly results have upset the Shiv Sena (UBT) and the NCP (SP) which believe Kejriwal had to fight a battle on many fronts against the BJP.
Also Read | After Delhi drubbing, word of advice for AAP from its Goa chief: Alliance with Congress only way forward
Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut said, “The BJP seems to have replicated its Maharashtra pattern in the Delhi Assembly elections. From subjecting AAP leader Kejriwal to harassment through Central agencies, getting all their prominent party leaders arrested and imprisoned to the bogus voter list,” said Raut, adding the saffron party’s formula is to first finish the leader who dares to rise against Modi-Shah.
After the setback in the Maharashtra Assembly polls, regional parties were hoping the AAP would withstand the BJP. Unfortunately, that has not happened as Kejriwal’s party failed to retain power after 12 years of ruling in Delhi.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
With local bodies elections, including those of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation, scheduled to be held this year, Thackeray surely knows it’s not going to be easy. The BMC polls will in every sense be a do-or-die battle for Thackeray who is struggling to reaffirm his political leadership and identity of the party in Mumbai and Maharashtra.
Senior BJP leader Sudhir Mungantiwar said, “The BJP is on a victory spree. After the success in Haryana and Maharashtra, we have made it in Delhi. And this clearly is an indication that people have trust in the party and its leadership in Narendra Modi and Amit Shah. We will win Bihar Assembly polls too.”

headline: Delhi Assembly elections: ‘No files to be taken outside Delhi Secretariat without permission’
description: The General Administration Department ordered that no document can be taken out of the Secretariat premises without permission.
content:
No files, documents or computer hardware can be taken outside the Delhi Secretariat complex without prior permission of the General Administration Department (GAD) “to address security concerns and the safety of records”, an official notification underlined Saturday as the Assembly election results were out and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) lost power in the Capital.
“It is, therefore, directed that necessary directions may be issued to the branch in-charges concerned under the departments or offices situated in Delhi Secretariat to ensure the safety of records, files, documents or electronic files under their section/branches,” read the order issued by the GAD following L-G VK Saxena’s directions.  The order also underlined that the rule is applicable for all the Secretariat officials and the Council of Ministers. Delhi Secretariat is the seat of the city government.
The order comes as the BJP registered a historic victory in the Assembly elections by securing a win in 48 of 70 seats.  The party is set to return to power in the Capital after 27 years.
In its manifesto, the BJP had promised to adopt “zero tolerance” against the alleged widespread misgovernance and corruption of “AAP-DA” (disaster) and constitute a special investigation team to launch a probe into the “scams” related to Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC), Mohalla clinics, excise policy, and the Delhi Jal Board, among others.

headline: Cash-strapped Punjab Govt brings back stamp duty on transfer of property among family
description: The agenda of stamp duty on property transfers will be put up to the Punjab Cabinet in its meeting on February 10.
content:
Over a decade after the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD)-Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government had done away with stamp duty on the transfer of property among blood relatives, the cash-crunched Punjab dispensation has decided to impose 2.5 per cent stamp duty on such transfers.
The agenda would be put up to the Cabinet in its meeting on February 10 by the Department of Revenue and Rehabilitation. If the Cabinet gives its nod to the agenda, it will be notified.
While direct transfer from parents to children (sons and daughters) and grandparents to grandchildren will invite one per cent stamp duty, for all other transfers including between brothers, sisters, husband and wife, it would be 2.5 per cent.
Sources in the Punjab Government said the rise in stamp duty would help add a few crores of rupees to the state exchequer. “We have been observing that the transfer of property among blood relations had many takers as it did not have any duty. We observed that parents were transferring property to their children’s names and the same property was transferred back. This transfer was shown as a sale deed to mortgage it in a bank to raise a loan. At least 25 per cent of sale deeds were between blood relatives. The revenue staff was busy dealing with these transfers. With the government levying stamp duty now, only serious transfers would take place,” said a government official.

According to the notification issued by the then Punjab Government on May 7, 2014, no stamp duty was chargeable on the instruments pertaining to the transfer of immovable property by an owner during his lifetime to any of his blood relations — his children, grandchildren, brothers and sisters. The transfer between spouses was also free of charge.
In February last year, the government made home and vehicular loans dearer by levying a 0.25 per cent registration fee on the loans sanctioned by respective banks.
The government had also notified levying a 2 per cent stamp duty on property transferred through General Power of Attorney (GPA) by notifying The Transfer of Property (Punjab Amendment) Act, 2023.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The government had planned to make Rs 500 crore each from these two levies. It was targeting an additional collection of Rs 1,000 crore annually.
However, sources said that it was not looking at adding Rs 1,000 crore. Against a target of Rs 5,750 crore from stamp duty in the Budget Estimates for the current fiscal, the government has been able to collect Rs 4,172 crore till December.
While notifying duty on GPA, the government had stated that transfer of property to the spouse, legal heir, and blood relations would not attract any stamp duty.
The government stated that it had decided to levy transfer fees on GPAs as several sale deeds were executed in the form of GPAs causing a loss to the state exchequer.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The government said in October 2022 alone, as many as 7,000 GPAs were registered. Out of these, 90 per cent were related to usual sales and 10 per cent were genuine transfer of property. Roughly, this has caused a loss of Rs 850 crore.

headline: Delhi and Noida schools, St Stephen’s College receive bomb threat; police launch search
description: According to police sources, Ahlcon International School in East Delhi’s Pandav Nagar and Shiv Nadar School in Noida received the bomb threat email on Friday.
content:
At least two private schools in Delhi and Noida and Delhi University’s St Stephen’s College in the Capital received bomb threats over emails on Friday, prompting security agencies to conduct checks at the premises.
According to sources in the police, Ahlcon International School in East Delhi’s Pandav Nagar and Shiv Nadar School in Noida received the bomb threat emails. Soon after receiving the information, the bomb detection team, disposal squad, dog squad, fire department officials, and local police reached the spot, a police officer said, adding that nothing suspicious had been found so far.
Ahlcon International School issued a statement to parents over the threat. “Due to an email threat received this morning, we are compelled to close school today keeping the safety of our students in mind. Your patience and cooperation in this regard shall be highly appreciated. The competent authorities are being contacted for further instructions and clearance,” it stated.
The Shiv Nadar School also issued a statement to the parents, saying: “This is to share that we have received a threat to the safety of students on campus. We are therefore closing the campus down for the day, Friday, February 7, in order to complete a sweep to ensure safety for all. Please keep your child at home to support this. Those who have already boarded the bus will be sent back home with immediate effect.”
DCP (Noida) Ram Badan Singh said, “It is suspected that some mischievous element sent the email. Our cyber team is working to arrest the sender.”
This is the latest in a series of bomb threat emails sent to schools in Delhi-NCR over the past few months — all were declared hoaxes and students were apprehended in several cases.

headline: Ladki Bahin scheme: Govt declares 5 lakh beneficiaries ineligible, says won’t take back amount paid earlier
description: Rs 450 crore deposited into their accounts over 6 months
content:
The Maharashtra government on Friday declared five lakh beneficiaries of Chief Minister Ladki Bahin Yojana as ineligible as they receive benefits under other schemes or do not fulfill the eligibility criteria.
However, the money which has already been deposited into the bank accounts of these women over the last six months will not be taken back from them, said Women and Child Development minister Aditi Tatkare.
Sources in the government said that an aggregate of over Rs 450 crore have been deposited into the accounts of these 5 lakh women between July 2024 and December 2024 — eligible women are provided a monthly stipend of Rs 1,500 under the scheme.
“Those who have been declared ineligible will not get the benefits from January. However, taking forward the concept of a welfare state, it will not be proper to seize the money deposited in the accounts earlier. Therefore, money deposited from July 2024 to December 2024 will not be taken back,” Tatkare said.
Among the five lakh women who have been declared ineligible, 2.30 lakh avail benefits under the Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Scheme,  1.10 lakh are above the age of 65 and 1.60 lakh have four-wheeler and are also beneficiaries of schemes such as Namo Shetkari scheme.
Under the Ladki Bahin scheme, the government provides Rs 1,500 per month to women up to the age of 65 with an annual family income of less than Rs 2.5 lakh. To avail benefits under the scheme, the beneficiary should not have a government employee as family member, should not own a four-wheeler or be getting monthly assistance under any other government scheme.
According to the government, a total of 2.46 crore beneficiaries exist under this scheme.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Ladki Bahin scheme was announced by the previous state government led by Chief Minister Eknath Shinde in the Budget presented by the then finance minister Ajit Pawar for the year 2024-25, months ahead of the Assembly elections in Maharashtra.
The goverment’s announcement of a slew populist schemes ahead of the Assembly elections  in November 2024 — the Mahayuti government returned to power with a huge majority in the polls — had met with criticisms after the fiscal deficit of the state rose to Rs 2 lakh crore.
For the Ladki Bahin scheme alone, the government had earmarked 46,000 crore.

headline: RG Kar rape-murder case: Calcutta HC allows CBI plea, dismisses state’s appeal challenging life term to convict Sanjoy Roy
description: The CBI and the West Bengal government had filed appeals in the Calcutta High Court seeking the death penalty for RG Kar rape-murder case convict Sanjoy Roy.
content:
The Calcutta High Court Friday admitted CBI’s appeal challenging the life imprisonment sentence awarded to Sanjoy Roy for the rape and murder of a junior doctor at Kolkata’s R G Kar Medical College and Hospital, and dismissed the West Bengal Government’s plea on the matter.
The CBI and the West Bengal government had filed appeals in the high court seeking the death penalty for Roy.
“…we are of the view that since the investigation of the case was conducted by the Central Bureau of Investigation, a central agency, in pursuance of an order passed by this court, Central Government is the appropriate authority to issue directions for presentation of an appeal against inadequate sentence,” the division bench of Justices Debangsu Basak and Arindam Mukherjee said.
“In view of the words ‘Save as otherwise provided in sub-section (2)’, in the opening paragraph of Section 418 of BNSS, the State Government cannot issue such directions so long as the Central Government or the CBI is willing to do so. For the aforesaid reasons, the appeal filed on behalf of the State of West Bengal…cannot be admitted and entertained. Consequently, the appeal filed on behalf of CBI…is admitted,” the court said.
“The investigation was conducted by the CBI. The CBI appeal admitted and state appeal dismissed,” Justice Debangsu Basak said on Friday.
On January 20, Roy was sentenced to life imprisonment till death by a Sealdah court. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee had expressed her dismay at the verdict, saying the government would seek capital punishment for the convict. A day later, the state government moved the Calcutta High Court.
The CBI moved the high court on January 24. It objected to the West Bengal government’s plea, submitting that only the victim’s family, the investigating agency, or the convict could appeal to a higher court. The state government had argued then that the incident had taken place at a state hospital and law and order was a state subject.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Roy, a 35-year-old civic volunteer, was convicted under sections 64 (punishment for rape), 66 (punishment for causing death or a persistent vegetative state to a woman), and 101 (1) (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita in a ruling that came five months after the August 9 incident sparked outrage and triggered protests across the state.
Earlier, the central agency’s plea seeking the death penalty for Roy was turned down by a trial court, where the judge said that the crime did not fall under the “rarest of the rare” category.

headline: Gujarat: GEER begins data analysis of crocodile census conducted in Vishwamitri river stretch
description: With the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) looking to start the work of dredging and desilting the river as part of a flood mitigation project, the census will help the civic body plan the relocation of the crocodiles if required.
content:
The Gujarat Ecological Education and Research (GEER) has begun analysing the data of the crocodile census conducted in a 25-km urban stretch of the Vishwamitri river passing through Vadodara city.
With the Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) looking to start the work of dredging and desilting the river as part of a flood mitigation project, the census will help the civic body plan the relocation of the crocodiles if required.
It was for the first time that the VMC had requested the GEER to conduct the census, as it is usually done by the Forest department.
For two days on Wednesday and Thursday, 25 teams were deployed across the stretch to conduct the count while drone cameras were deployed in about four inaccessible locations along the river course to help the teams. Each team consisted of a representative of the GEER, members of the Forest department and a crocodile expert consultancy firm from Anand, local volunteers from NGOs, and student volunteers from the zoology department of the MS University.
Dr Ranjitsinh Devkar, Assistant Professor of Zoology at MSU, who prepared the programme for the census, said the data sheets had been submitted to the GEER for the analysis of the estimated population. Devkar said, “We conducted the census in two counts as per protocol, which is sighting during the day and a nocturnal count as crocodiles are predominantly nocturnal. In that too, the code is spotting fire-red eyes (orangish red) as there are other aquatic species, as well as dogs and cats, that can be part of the riverbanks. Crocodiles have distinct fire-red eyes. We scanned the riverbank on the night of Wednesday between 8.30 pm to 11 pm as they are most active at that time.”
Devkar added that winter is the preferred season for conducting a crocodile census as the reptiles are “relatively less aggressive” and moderately active at night. “After February, they get more active as the temperature changes. The aggressive behaviour sets in after March when they indulge in territorial fights, mating, creating dens, and finally nesting. It goes on until September. We first conduct a vantage point scan of an area and then get into the river,” he said.
While physically tagging protected crocodiles requires permission from the Central Wildlife board, the teams conducted a physical count of the crocodiles along with the estimated size and activity.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Some specific marks on the crocodiles are noted. We scan at least a distance of 30 metre and places of thick foliage are avoided. We note a rough estimate of the size (of the crocodile) in feet as well as activity like swimming or basking. We also document nearby vegetation, dens, or landslides. The estimates are close to accurate because crocodiles do not move fast and the census team walks from point A to B, making it virtually impossible for a crocodile found at point A to reach point B before the team,” said Devkar.
Devkar said that the conclusion of the census is only meant to be an estimate. Some parts of the riverbank remained inaccessible or needed a detour. “We deployed drones in areas where the foliage was thick and there were Babul trees. For instance, the riverbank close to Kashiba Children’s Hospital in Vadodara was not trekkable. We lowered the drone in the centre of the river and scanned the under part of the canopy.”
The GEER Foundation has not set a deadline for the census’ conclusion.
Ritesh Gelot, Deputy Director, (Research and Development), GEER, told The Indian Express, “The teams have observed crocodiles basking, swimming, and taking rest. No unusual occurrence has been reported yet. Once the data analysis is done, we will be able to put out the estimates.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Gelot added that drone videography was conducted for the entire census. In the last census of 2020, an estimated 270 crocodiles had been spotted in the Vishwamitri river.

headline: As Trump acts against USAID, LGBTQ organisation in Pune faces funding uncertainties
description: Pune-based MIST LGBTQ Foundation is trying to find alternative funding sources to enable it to carry on its work after the freeze on all ongoing USAID projects.
content:
US President Donald Trump’s decision to put a freeze on all ongoing United States Agency for International Development (USAID) projects has impacted Pune-based MIST LGBTQ Foundation, which is now trying to find alternative funding sources to enable it to carry on its work.
“Our project was for three years and was to be over by the end of 2025. So this sudden cessation has caught us off guard,” Shyam Konnur, the founder-director of MIST, which received USAID funding, said.
As part of the project, MIST worked with the LGBT community on HIV prevention, PrEP (pre-exposure prophylaxis is a medicine that can help prevent people from contracting HIV) distribution, empowerment initiatives etc and collaborated with doctors and mental health professionals. On average, Konnur said, MIST distributed over 200 PrEP kits and conducted 300 HIV tests monthly.
Over the years, MIST has been catering to a section of the LGBTQ community that would otherwise remain unserved, according to Konnur. “A section of the community is not comfortable in approaching NGOs or government-run testing centres. Along with USAID, we have managed to ensure test kits reach the homes of those who want to test at home. Distribution of PrEP and condoms were also part of the initiative,” he said, adding that MIST bore the cost of parcelling and shipping the kits.
Konnur said they have prioritised the HIV prevention project and are working to get funding for the same. “We have approached CSR heads of companies as well as individual donors,” he said, adding that they are hopeful of finding a solution to their funding woes soon.
USAID has emerged as the latest casualty in the Trump administration’s bid to rehaul the federal government and the new administration’s actions are set to reduce the agency’s workforce to fewer than 300 staff globally, from over 10,000, according to multiple reports.

headline: Solving Crime: From falling in love on a train journey to visiting Shirdi temple, how Mumbai couple’s love story ended with cold blooded murder
description: From falling in love on a train journey to visiting Shirdi to repent for their ‘sins’, how Prajakta Shelar and Prafulla Ghadi ended up being arrested for murder.
content:
In 2010, a couple visited the Pimpleshwar temple at Dombivali on the outskirts of Mumbai and left a suitcase with the watchman standing guard outside, asking him to keep an eye on it till they returned. They never did. Hours later, suspecting something amiss, the watchman alerted the Manpada police in Thane. When the police opened the suitcase, they were shocked to find the body of a young man inside. The investigation that followed unravelled a story of love, lust and murder – and two temple visits.
It all began when Ghatkopar resident Prajakta Shelar, 21, and Bandra resident Prafulla Ghadi, 22, met on the Madgaon-Mumbai Express and travelled together from Ratnagiri to Mumbai. The duo talked for hours, got attracted to each other, and fell in love by the end of the train journey. The two shared their contact numbers, started chatting with each other, and began going out to movies together.
According to the police, after two months, the two started staying in a rented house in Diva as live-in partners. After a few weeks, however, Ghadi lost his job. A police officer said that the two were under financial stress and decided to make money the easy way. Nilesh Sonar, 26, the son of a jeweller who owned a store near the couple’s house, was an easy target.
Shelar allegedly knew Sonar was attracted to her so she and Ghadi decided to lure him and rob his gold chain. The police said that Shelar sweet-talked Sonar into dropping in at her place when she was alone.
On October 22, 2010, when Sonar came to her house, Shelar allegedly seduced him and asked him to take off his clothes and chain to take a shower. When Sonar agreed, Shelar allegedly replaced his gold chain with a duplicate one. Sonar, however, realised he had been duped, the police said. He asked Shelar to return his chain and allegedly threatened to call the police.
Shelar signalled Ghadi, who then entered the house, and before Sonar could run away, grabbed him and strangled him, the police said. Sonar lost consciousness. Scared that Sonar would inform the police, Shelar and Ghadi allegedly wrapped cellotape around his mouth and nose. They also tried to burn his private parts, as per the police.
Later, the couple allegedly sold his gold chain and bought a suitcase with the money. They allegedly stuffed Sonar’s body in the suitcase and took an auto-rickshaw to go to a deserted place to dump the body. But as the auto-rickshaw ran out of fuel, they stopped at Pimpleshwar temple, the police said. They entered the temple, leaving the suitcase outside, and escaped from another gate, the police added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Once the police found the body, it did not take time to ascertain Sonar’s identity as his family had already filed a missing person’s complaint after he failed to return home.
When the police visited Sonar’s father’s jewellery store in Diva, they came across a local who told him that he had last seen Sonar moving towards Shelar’s house. When the police visited Shelar’s house, it was closed. The police enquired with the neighbours and got the address of Shelar’s Ghatkopar residence. However, when the police arrived there, she was not home.
The police told her family that they just wanted to enquire about her concerning a small matter. A couple of days later, her family informed the police that Shelar had called them, saying she had gone to the Shirdi Sai Baba temple and was returning to Diva.
When Shelar arrived at her Diva house, the police were waiting. After her arrest, Ghadi was also arrested. When police asked them why they went to Shirdi Sai temple, they claimed that they had gone there to repent for their sins, officials said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Two years later, Shelar and Ghadi were convicted of murder in December 2012 by the Thane sessions court. They appealed the decision before the Bombay High Court but the higher court upheld the life imprisonment sentence given to them.

headline: Big court verdict day on Feb 7 for Karnataka – CM Siddaramaiah in Muda case, former CM Yediyurappa in Pocso case
description: The same single-judge Karnataka High Court bench is set to pronounce verdicts in the two high-profile cases.
content:
A single-judge bench of the Karnataka High Court is set to pronounce verdicts in two politically significant cases on Friday with respect to Karnataka’s Congress Chief Minister Siddaramaiah and former BJP chief minister B S Yediyurappa.
The bench of Justice M Nagaprasanna is scheduled to pronounce its order on Friday in a plea by an RTI activist for a CBI probe against Siddaramaiah and his family for alleged corruption in land allotments made by the Mysore Urban Development Authority (Muda) in 2021 – where the Karnataka Lokayukta police have conducted an investigation.
The same bench is also scheduled to announce its verdict on Friday in a plea filed by former BJP CM B S Yediyurappa for the quashing of a case filed against him under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act in March 2024 – where a chargesheet has been filed by the Criminal Investigation Department of the Karnataka Police.
Explained | What Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has been accused of in the alleged MUDA scam
Siddaramaiah’s Muda case

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’

The high court reserved its judgment on January 27 in a plea filed by RTI activist Snehamayi Krishna for a CBI probe into land grants made by Muda to the current Karnataka Congress CM Siddaramaiah’s family in 2021 when the BJP was in power in the state.
The RTI activist who obtained a sanction from Karnataka Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot to prosecute the Karnataka CM was granted clearance by the high court on September 24, 2024, to seek an investigation into Muda land allotments to Siddaramaiah’s family.
Also Read | Why Karnataka HC allowed investigation against CM Siddaramaiah in alleged MUDA scam case
A special court ordered an investigation by the Karnataka Lokayukta police on September 25, 2024, after the RTI activist sought a probe by the Lokayukta, the CBI or any other agency. The RTI activist however approached the high court again on September 28 – a couple of hours before the Lokayukta police registered an FIR – to seek a CBI probe in the matter.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Lokayukta police were originally due to submit their investigation report on December 28, 2024, to the special court – which ordered the probe – and submitted a report on its investigations to the HC on January 27.
Justice Nagaprasanna reserved his order on the plea for a CBI probe after taking on record the sealed cover containing the investigation report of the Lokayukta police.
While taking the probe report on record and reserving the judgment, the high court also extended the time for the trial court to receive the Lokayukta police report until the date of the judgment.
During the arguments, on January 27, the high court indicated that it would peruse the report of the Lokayukta police and decide on the plea for a CBI probe. The advocates for Siddaramaiah argued that a decision on the report is the prerogative of the trial court and not the Karnataka HC.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Also Read | MUDA case a ‘sham’, says Siddaramaiah after HC setback; BJP asks CM to resign
The high court was informed by the advocates for Siddaramaiah that the RTI activist himself had sought a probe by the Lokayukta police or the CBI or any other agency in the first instance and a probe by the Lokayukta police was ordered by the special court.
It was argued on behalf of the chief minister that the HC bench cannot suo motu decide on the demand for a CBI probe after perusing the probe report since the matter falls in the jurisdiction of the special court which ordered the Lokayukta police investigation.
The RTI activist who filed the plea for a CBI probe in the Muda case of land allotment to Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah’s wife B M Parvathi argued that the Lokayukta police were not investigating the case effectively. The complainant has sought a CBI probe in the matter on the grounds that the Lokayukta police function under the purview of the state government.
The case is centred around 14 sites worth Rs 56 crore that were allotted to CM Siddaramaiah’s wife as compensation by Muda in the year 2021 when the BJP was in power – after around 3.16 acres of land which were gifted to the CM’s wife by her brother in 2010 had been “wrongfully” acquired by Muda in 2014.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Also Read | Karnataka HC reserves order on B S Yediyurappa’s plea to quash Pocso case against him
Karnataka CM Siddaramaiah has argued in public that there was no wrongdoing or corruption on his part in the allotment of 14 housing sites by Muda to his wife during the BJP’s tenure.
The wife of the chief minister has meanwhile returned the 14 compensation sites allotted to her by Muda under a controversial 50:50 scheme.
In his September 24, 2024, order facilitating a probe against the Karnataka CM and his kin, Justice Nagaprasanna had raised questions with regard to the value of the original land vis-a-vis the value of the land allotted in compensation.
Siddaramaiah has filed an appeal in the HC against the single-judge order of September 24, 2024, which facilitated the investigation into the alleged illegalities in the allotment of the Muda housing sites to his wife. A division bench is due to hear the appeal on March 22.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Also Read | Karnataka govt moves high court over halt in proceedings against former BJP CM Yediyurappa in POCSO case
Yediyurappa’s Pocso case
Former Karnataka CM B S Yediyurappa, 81, who was accused in March 2024 by the mother of a teenager of sexually inappropriate behaviour has sought the quashing of an FIR registered against him under the Pocso Act.
The CID unit of the Karnataka Police filed a charge sheet against the former BJP CM and three others on June 27 in the Pocso case.
The CID filed the chargesheet under Section 8 (sexual assault) of the Pocso Act, and Sections 354 A (sexual harassment), 204 (destruction of evidence), and 214 (offering gifts to silence the victim) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A special court for Pocso cases took cognizance of the charge sheet on July 6 last year and issued a summons for the former CM and others.
The Karnataka HC ruled on June 14, 2024, that Yediyurappa should not be arrested in the Pocso case and later, on July 12 of the same year, allowed the exemption of Yediyurappa and three others from appearing in court on the basis of the July 6 summons.
Although no stay was issued by the high court against the proceedings in the special court, the Pocso court proceedings were stalled on account of Yediyurappa seeking the quashing of the chargesheet in the high court.
In November 2024, the Karnataka government moved an application in the high court for withdrawal of the exemption granted to Yediyurappa from appearing in the trial court and sought a clearance from the HC for proceedings to continue in the trial court.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The high court’s attention was drawn by the special public prosecutor to Section 35 of the Pocso Act which specifies that the evidence of the child victim of sexual offences must be recorded within 30 days of the trial court taking cognizance of a case filed under the Pocso Act.
The Karnataka HC in a 2021 judgment by Justice B V Nagaratna and Justice M G Uma had directed judges of special courts for Pocso cases to comply with Section 35 of the Pocso Act in the matter of recording of evidence of the victim child and the conclusion of the trial within the stipulated time (one month after taking cognizance and one year, respectively).
Justice Nagaprasanna observed in September 2024 that long delays in the trial process of cases of sexual offences against children, despite the Pocso Act mandating completion of trial in a year, put the entire judicial system to shame. The observation was made in a Pocso case where the victim was killed and the matter remained pending for over seven years.
According to the police complaint filed by the minor victim’s mother on March 14, 2024, she visited the home of Yediyurappa on February 2, 2024, with her daughter to seek justice in an earlier case of sexual assault by a relative on her daughter when the former CM allegedly touched her daughter inappropriately.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Three associates of the former CM – Arun Y M, Rudresh M, and Y Mariswamy – are also accused in the case under Sections 204 and 214 of the IPC for allegedly destroying evidence by deleting a video recording of the victim’s mother’s confrontation with Yediyurappa over the incident.
The advocates for the former CM have questioned the validity of the FIR which was registered over a month after the alleged incident and the credibility of the victim’s mother – who passed away a few months after filing the case.
The defence advocates have argued that the victim and her mother also met Yediyurappa after the alleged incident and before the filing of the FIR.

headline: RG Kar Corruption case: HC gives 1 week time to Ghosh, framing of charges put on hold
description: Says ‘no heaven will fall in postponement, accused needs to get reasonable time’, cites 25,000 pages of CBI papers
content:
A Division Bench of the Calcutta High Court on Thursday gave seven days to Sandip Ghosh, the former principal of RG Kar Medical College and Hospital, to read the documents submitted by the CBI as part of the chargesheet in a case of financial irregularities during his tenure, saying “no heaven will fall in a days’ postponement”.   The special CBI court in Alipore is awaiting the framing of the charges against Ghosh and four others named in the CBI chargesheet.
The Division Bench of Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice Subhendu Samanta of the Calcutta High Court, while hearing a plea of Ghosh and others seeking postponement of framing of charges in the case, said that reasonable time needs to be given to the accused.
On Wednesday, a day after the single judge bench of the High Court rejected Ghosh’s plea, his counsel moved the Division Bench seeking postponement of the framing of the charges and cited that the CBI had recently handed over them documents running in “thousands of pages”.
Also Read | RG Kar case | As Mamata calls for death penalty, victim’s father reacts: ‘She should not do anything more... her police tampered with evidence’
The counsels of Ghosh and another accused Suman Hazra told the Division Bench that the CBI gave them documents, running into thousands of pages on February 1, while the date for framing of charges was fixed before the special court on February 4, giving them “hardly four days to go through the voluminous documents related to the case”.
“Give me reasonable time to paginate the documents,” senior counsel Sabyasachi Banerjee, who was representing Hazra, told the Bench.
After hearing him, Justice Bagchi observed: “No heaven will fall in a days’ postponement. Every accused has the right to due process. Also, one has to examine the requirement of the accused to prepare his defence. Twenty-five thousand papers have to be examined.”
Justice Bagchi, however, also told the counsel of the accused that he does not have the privilege of dilating the proceedings before the trial court.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Also Read | Verdict in Kolkata rape-murder: ‘Many questions still unanswered, motive not clear’, say Jr doctors, to continue their fight
The Division Bench proposed that the accused may get a week’s time to go through the documents for filing a discharge petition, if he so wishes.  “Seven days’ time to look into the papers, and file your discharge petitions. The discharge petitions are heard within seven days from the date on which the discharge petitions are given. We would like all the counsels appearing for the accused to sit together with the deputy solicitor general to work out a reasonable time frame,” Justice Bagchi said.
Of the five accused in the case, three have filed discharge petitions. Ghosh is not one of them.

content:
A 24-hour operation conducted by the Surat Fire Department and the NDRF to rescue a two-year-old boy, who accidentally fell into an open manhole in Surat’s Variyav on Wednesday, ended with a tragedy as the child was found dead on Thursday afternoon.
As per fire officials, Vaishali Vegas, accompanied by her son Kedar, residents of Suman Sadhna Awas on Variyav Amreli road, had gone to a ‘Budhwar Market’ at Varyav on Wednesday afternoon. Vaishali was also accompanied by other women from her neighbourhood.

headline: KSRTC to take Rs 623-crore loan to clear PF, fuel dues

content:
The Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) recently invited expressions of interest from financial institutions and commercial banks for a term loan of Rs 623.8 crore to settle pending arrears, including statutory payments such as provident fund (PF) contributions and fuel expenses.
The loan will be disbursed in a single instalment and repaid over a seven-year period, with the state government acting as the guarantor and providing primary and collateral security, according to official documents.
V Anbukumar, Managing Director, KSRTC, stated that the decision to take the loan was made following government directives. “All four state transport corporations will avail a combined loan of Rs 2,000 crore to clear pending dues related to provident fund and diesel,” he added.

headline: Equal Opportunity, ST/SC cells at many Pune colleges receive nil complaint on discrimination
description: Among the data collected by the The Indian Express, the lone higher education institute that reportedly received complaints was Pune’s Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU).
content:
Several colleges and other higher education institutes in Pune city have not received any complaints pertaining to caste and gender-based discrimination at their Equal Opportunity Cells and SC/ST cells, according to data collected by The Indian Express.
The cells have been set up as per a 2012 norm of the University Grants Commission (UGC) to ensure effective and transparent redressal of grievances of the disadvantaged groups. The UGC, through a notice issued on January 10 this year, requested all higher education institutes in the country to set up Equal Opportunity Cells and SC/ST Cells.
Savitribai Phule Pune University, affiliated colleges
Among the data collected by the The Indian Express, the lone higher education institute that reportedly received complaints was Pune’s Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU). It had established a committee to look into caste-based discrimination complaints by students and staff in 2021. According to Dr Parag Kalkar, Pro-Vice Chancellor of SPPU and current chairman of the committee, the committee had received three to four complaints from teaching and non-teaching staff in the last two years, all of which had been resolved. However, it received no complaints from students, Kalkar said.
SPPU-affiliated Modern College of Arts, Commerce, and Science where an Equal Opportunity Cell has been functioning since 2018-19 has so far recorded no formal complaint, said Dr Sanjay Kharat, cell chairman.
Same is the case with SPPU-affiliated Fergusson College, where the Equal Opportunity Cell was established five years ago. Prof Prakash Pawar, head of the cell at the college, said it conducts various activities to promote equality. The college also has a separate student grievance redressal committee, he said.
Bharati Vidyapeeth’s College of Engineering affiliated to the SPPU, is also yet to record any complaint in the last two years, said Dr R N Patil, head of the ST/SC Cell.
Other universities
Data also shows that College of Engineering Pune (COEP) Technological University, Maharashtra Institute of Technology World Peace University’s Kothrud campus, and Ajeenkya DY Patil University are yet to receive any complaints on discrimination despite having grievance redressal cells.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
However, authorities at Vishwakarma University, Symbiosis International University and Flame University failed to share details when contacted by The Indian Express.
What are Equal Opportunity Cells and SC/ST Cells?
Equal Opportunity Cells were introduced in the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Educational Institutions) Regulations, 2012 as a way to fight caste discrimination on university and college campuses.
In January this year, while hearing a Public Interest Litigation filed by mothers of Rohit Vemula and Payal Tadvi, the Supreme Court asked the UGC to submit data regarding the setting up of Equal Opportunity Cells in universities and on the number of complaints received.
As a result, the UGC issued a notice on January 10 that said “all HEIs are requested to establish an Equal Opportunity Cell and SC/ST Cell to ensure the effective and transparent redressal of grievances of the disadvantaged groups.” The notice also requested higher education institutes to provide information about the cells and the complaints received to the UGC by January 20.
Experts raise concern over lack of complaints
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On the lack of complaints received by the cell, former UGC chairman Dr Sukhdeo Thorat said that the question arises whether the the universities and students are aware about the 2012 regulations and also on the need for implementing the regulations. “Since they are not even aware of the regulation, the students don’t know whether to complain or not. The universities and the students both are unaware, they only know the Atrocities Act,” Thorat pointed out.
Rahul Sasane, president of the University Student Struggle Action Committee at SPPU, has called for more awareness on the mechanism. “The SPPU SC/ST Committee is visible on the website, but there needs to be more awareness about it. Only students, professors, and non-teaching staff are aware of this committee. Can they complain against injustice done to them. Secondly, most of the members of the committee displayed on the website are upper caste. How can all these people provide justice in a proper manner?” he pointed out.
Dr Sanjay Dabhade, member of the Tribal Doctors Forum, said that zero complaints mean that the existence of these cells is not known to students or teachers. “It is also important to see the composition of the committees — if the members are from upper caste or from the Schedules Castes and Scheduled Tribes. The structure and functioning of the higher education institutes is also important; if it is not democratic and if the management forces their decisions, then no one will dare to complain,” Dabhade said.

headline: American dreams shattered for Punjab youths and their families: ‘Rs 42 lakh has gone down the drain, don’t know what to do next’
description: Many families of the deportees hailing from Punjab prefer to stay anonymous, still grappling with the loss—both financial and reputational.
content:
Pradeep Singh, 21, from the Jaraut village of Mohali, left Punjab for the United States six months ago with high hopes of securing his debt-ridden family’s future in the “land of dreams”. After enduring an uncertain journey, the details of which are still not known, he finally reached the US a few days ago.
However, his stay was short-lived—just 10 days later, he was deported back to India. Pradeep is among the 104 Indian deportees who landed in Amritsar Wednesday in a US Air Force aircraft.
As The Indian Express caught up with his mother, she hid her face in her shawl, refusing to reveal her identity, and said, “We spent around Rs 41-42 lakh in the hope of paying off our debts. We had 5 acres of land, but half of it was sold. We don’t know how to recover from this loss. He has completed his Class 12 education. Now, we appeal to the Punjab government for help during this difficult time. Please assist us in repaying our debt, and if there are job opportunities in Punjab, we kindly request that they provide one for my son based on his qualifications.”
Pradeep’s father, Kuldeep Singh Kala, said his son is in shock, and the family members have yet to sit and discuss what to do next. “I am an illiterate farmer. Now only 2.5 acres of land is left with me. He had gone after consulting his mother and around Rs 42 lakh has gone down the drain,” said Kala.
Kala said his son decided to go to the US because he could not find a better future in Punjab. “We now think the money invested here could also have brought some earnings. But we did not have any guidance. So, the Punjab government should guide such youngsters and their families. We hope the government will come out with jobs as per his qualifications,” said Kala, adding that his son used to help him in farming before going abroad.
This is the story of most of the deportees who hail from Punjab. Parents risking everything—money, safety, and even their dignity—in hopes of securing a better future for their children abroad. The harsh reality, however, is that many who take the illegal route end up facing deportation, financial ruin, and social stigma upon their return. According to official sources, among the deportees from Punjab, six are from Kapurthala, five from Amritsar, and four each from Patiala and Jalandhar, two each from Hoshiarpur, Ludhiana, and SBS Nagar, and one each from Gurdaspur, Tarn Taran, Sangrur, SAS Nagar, and Fatehgarh Sahib.
As The Indian Express attempted to contact some of these families, almost everyone preferred to remain anonymous. But they all said they spent between Rs 40 to 50 lakh to send their children to the US but for stays lasting as short as 15-20 days.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A 30-year-old man from the Kahanpur village in Punjab’s Fatehgarh Sahib with only Class 10 education embarked on one such journey to the US in October and finally reached there on January 15. However, his stay was also short-lived, lasting only for 20 days before the deportation. According to information from his family, they spent nearly Rs 50 lakh in his desperate attempt to settle in the US.
His father, who owns just 1.5 acres of land, is completely shocked. After investing a significant amount of money, the family’s dreams of seeing him build a prosperous life in the US have been completely shattered. The family has chosen not to speak openly about the matter, and even the village residents seemed hesitant to discuss the issue.
An eighteen-year-old from the Ahru Khurd village in Patiala embarked on his journey seven to eight months ago, hoping to build a better future. However, his American dream came crashing down with the deportation. His father owns approximately five acres of land, and his elder sister has settled in Canada.
Since the news of his deportation broke, his family has remained quiet. Even the village residents, who are usually outspoken about youth migration, seemed reluctant to discuss his journey and the circumstances leading to his deportation. Despite having a relatively stable background, he chose to take the illegal route to the US, raising questions about what motivated him to make such a risky decision.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
‘Success stories of settled Punjabis in foreign countries tempt youths’
Sukhwinder Kaur, general secretary of Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) Krantikari, reasoned that dollar-to-rupee conversion is the major factor attracting people to such risks.
“Lack of jobs in our own country and success stories of other settled Punjabis in foreign countries lure them to take such risks. Being in a farmer union, I come across these people daily. When farming is not profitable, such risks are taken at times,” said Kaur.
Lakhwinder Singh, the sarpanch of the Chamaru village in Patiala, confirmed that one village resident was among the Indians deported. However, the family has chosen not to disclose their identity.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In response to the deportation, Harjeet Singh Grewal, a national executive member of the BJP, said, “It is now the responsibility of the respective state to rehabilitate the deported individuals. Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann should make arrangements for their resettlement. These individuals took out loans or sold their land, but their dreams have been shattered. Strict actions need to be taken against the travel agents who charged them large sums of money and sent them through illegal means.”

headline: Man shoots friend mistaking him for wild boar on a hunting trip, the group leaves his body hidden in forest: Police
description: The Palghar police say they have arrested eight of a group of 12 hunters after the victim’s wife lodged a missing-person complaint.
content:
A hunting trip to a forest in Maharashtra’s Palghar district last week turned tragic after one of a group of 12 people ended up shooting dead a friend of theirs, mistaking him for a wild boar, police said.
The incident remained under wraps for a few days until the victim’s wife lodged a missing-person complaint with the police on Monday, leading to the arrest of eight people. An officer said the police were searching for the others, who are on the run.
Balasaheb Patil, Superintendent of Police, Palghar, said that the group, consisting of members from an adivasi community in Borsheti village of Shahapur taluka, went to the nearby forest to hunt for wild boars on the evening of January 28. They also invited their friend Ramesh Vartha, who agreed to join them the next morning.
“The next day, as Vartha was walking towards the spot where they were staying, his friends, while searching for wild boars, saw some plants moving. Suspecting it to be an animal, they shot in that direction, inadvertently killing Vartha,” Patil told The Indian Express.

Realising what had happened, the group panicked, hid the body behind a tree and left the forest, deciding not to inform anyone about the incident.
For the first two-three days, Vartha’s family suspected he was still in the forest, as the group typically stayed there for several days. However, when he did not return after a few more days, Vartha’s wife Amitha approached the local Manor police station. She informed the police that her husband had gone hunting with his friends but had not come back.
The police then summoned Vartha’s friends for questioning. Initially, they claimed that Vartha had returned with them the next day.
