headline: Gujarat: ‘Caught accepting Rs 12,000 as bribe’ from contractor, official held in Tapi
description: A few days ago, when the contractor contacted Dolvan TDO Virendrasinh Dodhiya and requested him to clear his dues, the latter allegedly demanded Rs 12,000 for the same.
content:
The Anti Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested the Dovlan Taluka Development Officer (TDO) for accepting a bribe of Rs 12,000 from a contractor to clear his dues of Rs 6 lakh.
The contractor had in 2023-24 carried out development works for laying of a water pipeline network and construction of toilet blocks in different villages in Dolvan taluka of Tapi district. The contractor had received a certain amount of money for his work, while Rs 6 lakh stood pending. He had also submitted the bills to the office concerned.
A few days ago, when the contractor contacted Dolvan TDO Virendrasinh Dodhiya and requested him to clear his dues, the latter allegedly demanded Rs 12,000 for the same.
The contractor contacted the Surat ACB office and lodged a complaint against the TDO. The ACB officials laid a trap at the Dolvan TDO office and caught Dodhiya red-handed, accepting the bribe. He was brought to the Tapi district’s Vyara ACB office for further procedures. Dodhiya was arrested under different sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act.
Surat ACB Assistant Director R R Chaudhary said, “We have caught the TDO and are carrying out further procedures. He was deputed as the TDO at Dolvan in 2023.”

headline: Exorcism, kidnapping and ritualistic sacrifice — Bihar woman among 4 arrested for ‘killing toddler to help daughter conceive’
description: According to the police, the exorcist, who is absconding, had assured the woman that her daughter will be able to conceive if a male child was sacrificed.
content:
The Bihar Police on Saturday arrested a woman and four others for allegedly abducting and killing a two-year-old boy on the advice of an “exorcist”.
According to the police, the exorcist, who is absconding, had assured the woman that her daughter will be able to conceive if a male child was sacrificed.
The matter came to light in the course of an investigation into the disappearance of the child, who was last seen on January 22 playing outside his relatives’ house in Lalapur village in Kaimur district. The boy, from Gazipur district of Uttar Pradesh, had travelled to Lalapur with his mother to attend a family function. A week later, the two-year-old’s body was found in a pit near Kudra railway station in the district.
Kaimur Superintendent of Police Hari Mohan Shukla said, “We have arrested one Munni Devi and four others. She admitted that she got the two-year-old kidnapped on the advice of an exorcist who said that sacrificing a male child would result in her daughter conceiving one.”
According to the SP, Devi said that her daughter had been under tremendous pressure from her in-laws to give birth to a child. When medical treatments did not help her daughter conceive, the woman decided to approach the exorcist.
The Kaimur SP said the exorcist had been identified and will be arrested soon.

headline: Upcoming museum in Devbhoomi Dwarka to give a ‘Talk to Krishna’ experience
description: The Directorate of Archaeology and Museums is also planning to integrate sculptures found around Dwarka with the theme and story line of the museum.
content:
By Janmashtami this year, a museum coming up in Devbhoomi Dwarka will show a “Vishwaroop darshan” (supreme form of Lord Vishnu) and give the visitor a “Talk to Krishna” experience, using Artificial Intelligence.
Director of Archeology and Museums, Gujarat Pankaj Sharma told The Indian Express that the immersive museum located some 1.2 kms from the famous Dwarkadheesh temple would be completed by June, ahead of the festival celebrating Krishna’s birth in August.
“Initially, the limit per visitor has been fixed at five questions. The software for the same is under process. Also, care is being taken on the privacy and data sharing issue. “There will be five to seven kiosks with headphones which visitors can use to speak with Krishna taking care of their privacy. Further, visitors will be informed that no recording or data will be stored in this section,” Sharma added.
The museum will give a 5D and 7D experience to the visitor through Lord Krishna’s life in Dwarka, Mathura and Vrindavan.
Built on a total area of 13000 square metre at a cost of Rs 82 crore, the work on the museum began in November 2023.
Built on a total area of 13000 square metre at a cost of Rs 82 crore, the work on the museum began in November 2023.
Dwarka is one of the temple towns with the highest footfalls in the state, recording 13 lakh visitors in 2023.
“ The Museum is based on the life of Krishna and aims to disseminate his teaching and philosophy to the world with use of modern technologies like AI and interacting and immersive engagements to convey the life and teachings of Krishna,” says Sharma.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Museum will also have a dedicated section on teachings and significance of Bhagavad Gita in the present context. It will have nine galleries spread from ground floor to second floor to convey the life and teachings of Krishna.
Artist impressions of the crossing of the river Yamuna experience.
Sharing details on the galleries, Sharma says, “The Bhagavad Gita section is dedicated with the purpose of making people understand the importance of Gita. Very few are aware about Gita and how it is important, the life management sutras will be presented in an easier way and how the gyan, bhakti and karma yog-the three principles of Bhagavad Gita are even relevant today. Everybody is stressed these days and their social life is disturbed. So, in the ‘Speak to Krishna’ section they can share their problems to which using AI they will get positive responses.”
One floor will be entirely dedicated to Krishna as a King of Dwarka and his teachings of Bhagavad Gita.
“The focus will be more on the authentic information of Bhagavad Gita along with its philosophy and not just imagination but with proof from scriptures. Also, focus will be on meaning, relevance and importance of different names of Krishna and Arjun in Gita like Keshav, Dhananjay, Bharat, Parth. Gyan, karma and bhakti shlokas with their Hindi, Gujarati and English translations along with detailed information on translations of Gita in different languages will be provided,” Prof Ravindra Kumar Khandwala, Head of Department of Sanskrit Prakrit at H K Arts College Ahmedabad who is one of the committee members for the section on Bhagavad Gita told this paper.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Artist impressions of the birth of Krishna.
Prof Khandwala is also advisor for the AI content development for ‘Speak to Krishna’ section.
The Directorate of Archaeology and Museums is also planning to integrate sculptures found around Dwarka with the theme and story line of the museum. Further, videos and visuals of excavations shot under water will be a part of it.
The Museum will also have outdoor attractions such as special landscape showcasing multi-facets of Krishna (Dashavatar Exhibit), Lotus Pond, Light and Sound Projection, Amphitheatre and other visitor amenities. Deliberations on the final name for the museum is also underway.

headline: Delhi Election Results 2025: AAP ousted, Congress stuck at zero, voters hand over Delhi keys to BJP after 27 years
description: 5-fold jump in BJP seats: PM promises to build modern city
content:
Ending its 27-year exile from power in the national Capital and handing the ruling AAP a stunning defeat, the BJP swept the Delhi Assembly elections Saturday, bagging 48 of the 70 seats in the House.
The remaining 22 seats went to AAP while the Congress drew a blank for the third time in a row. AAP leader and former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, former Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia were among the prominent leaders who lost. Of the AAP tally of 22 – down from 67 and 62 seats in 2015 and 2020 – most came from the reserved constituencies (8 out of 12) and Muslim-majority seats (6 out of 7).
Read | BJP’s Delhi journey: From Metropolitan Council in ’60s to staying out of power for 27 yrs
Thanking the people of Delhi for reposing faith in the BJP, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while addressing a gathering at the party headquarters hours after the verdict, said, “Delhi has liberated itself from a decade of AAPda (calamity)… Delhi’s voters have shown the truth to those who, in their arrogance, believed that they owned Delhi. The verdict proves that there is no place in politics for shortcuts, lies and deceit. The people have short-circuited the politics of shortcuts… Even after getting 100% success in three Lok Sabha elections, our workers had the pain of not being able to serve Delhi fully. This desire, too, Delhi has fulfilled this time.”
Listing what he called the failures of the AAP government in improving the delivery of basic services, Modi said, “Wherever NDA has got the mandate, we have brought new heights of development to that state. People are choosing our governments two-three times… Broken roads, garbage dumps and polluted air – these are the problems that people of Delhi have faced. We will build Delhi as a modern city. For the first time ever, the BJP will have a government in every state within NCR.”
Promising that the pending CAG reports will be tabled and action will be taken against the corrupt, Modi said, “A party that was formed to ‘rid’ the country of corruption became completely corrupt. They deceived the people of Delhi. When the world was grappling with Covid, these people were building a Sheesh Mahal. I guarantee that the CAG report on Delhi will be placed. Each charge of corruption will be probed and those who have looted will have to return the loot. This is Modi’s guarantee.”
Earlier in the day, accepting defeat, Kejriwal in a video address, said, “We humbly accept whatever decision the people have made. The people’s verdict is paramount. I wholeheartedly congratulate the BJP on this victory. I hope they fulfill all the expectations and aspirations with which people have given them this mandate.”
Also read | What AAP’s Delhi win map tells us about where the party is left standing
“Over the past 10 years, we have made sincere efforts to improve the lives of Delhi residents. We have undertaken initiatives in the fields of education, healthcare, water supply, electricity, and various other areas to provide relief to the people. We also worked to improve Delhi’s infrastructure. Now that the people have given their verdict, we will not only play the role of a constructive Opposition but also continue serving society… We did not enter politics for power… We will continue this work,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
BJP leaders celebrate the party’s win at the headquarters on Saturday. (Express photo by Praveen Khanna)
Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, in a post on X, said, “We humbly accept the mandate of Delhi. Heartfelt thanks to all the Congress workers of the state for their dedication and all the voters for their support. This fight for the progress of Delhi and the rights of Delhiites – against pollution, inflation and corruption – will continue.”
The BJP vote share went up from 38.5% in 2020 to 45.6% this time, gaining 40 seats in the process. The AAP, meanwhile, went down to 43.5% from 53.5% in 2020. The Congress vote share went up by nearly two percentage points.
Don't miss | Politics of hope and handouts: Why BJP’s Delhi win will have a national echo
The “double engine government” was one of BJP’s primary campaign pitches which, it promised, would work better in Delhi than in any other part of the country, with land, law and order, police and services under the Centre through the Lt Governor.
Over its decade-long tenure in the Delhi government, the AAP has been locked in a constant battle with the office of the Lt Governor. This intensified under the tenure of the present Lt Governor V K Saxena with enquiries being ordered into the Delhi excise policy scheme, the reconstruction of the official residence of Kejriwal when he was Chief Minister.

headline: India’s first kidney transplant for a patient with rare ‘Bombay’ blood group successfully performed in Mumbai hospital
description: The recipient, a 30-year-old woman from Shirdi, had been suffering from end-stage kidney disease due to diabetes and had been on dialysis since 2022.
content:
In a rare and complex medical procedure, a 30-year-old woman with the extremely rare ‘Bombay’ (hh) blood group underwent a successful kidney transplant in India. The procedure, conducted at a city hospital, marks the first such recorded transplant in the country. The procedure, which required overcoming significant immunological and logistical challenges, is among the few reported cases worldwide.
First identified in India, the ‘Bombay’ blood group is exceptionally rare, occurring in approximately one in 10,000 Indians and only one in a million people globally. Unlike common blood groups, people with this type lack the H antigen, making them incompatible with all standard blood types, including O-negative, complicating both transfusions and organ transplants.
The recipient, a 30-year-old woman from Shirdi, had been suffering from end-stage kidney disease due to diabetes and had been on dialysis since 2022. Initially misdiagnosed as having ‘O’ blood group, her actual blood type was only identified when she was being evaluated for a transplant at Jaslok Hospital. A misdiagnosis in such cases can lead to catastrophic outcomes, including graft rejection or fatal transfusion reactions.

Since individuals with this rare blood type can only receive organs from donors with the same blood group, finding a suitable match was nearly impossible. With no compatible deceased donors available and multiple hospitals declining the case due to its complexity, her mother, a B-positive donor, stepped forward. However, the mismatch introduced significant risks, requiring doctors to modify the recipient’s immune response before transplantation.

Dr Rishi Deshpande, director of nephrology (academics) at Jaslok Hospital, highlighted the unprecedented nature of the transplant. “To the best of our knowledge, there are no documented cases of a kidney transplant for a patient with the ‘Bombay’ blood group worldwide. The key to success was the accurate identification of the patient’s blood type—had this been overlooked, the consequences could have been catastrophic,” he said. “This case underscores the importance of precise blood typing in transplantation and demonstrates how meticulous planning and advanced immunological protocols can overcome even the most challenging medical barriers.”
To lower the risk of rejection, doctors employed a specialised desensitisation protocol, including plasma exchange therapy and immunosuppressive treatment. These measures helped reduce antibody levels, increasing the chances of a successful graft acceptance.
Another major hurdle was securing compatible blood products. Since ‘Bombay’ blood group patients cannot receive blood from standard donors, Jaslok Hospital had to coordinate with rare blood donor registries across the state to source blood before and after surgery. Unlike other transplants where emergency blood transfusions are readily available, this case required extensive pre-planning explained doctors.

The transplant was carried out by a multidisciplinary team of nephrologists, urologists, anesthesiologists, and transfusion specialists, who worked together to mitigate risks. Dr Ashwin Patil, a consulting nephrologist, emphasised the importance of accurate blood typing in such cases. “A misdiagnosis could have led to severe complications or even graft failure. This case highlights the importance of precise immunological assessment before transplantation.”
Following the procedure, the patient was closely monitored for early signs of rejection. “We have successfully crossed the critical post-transplant phase, but long-term success depends on continued immunosuppressive therapy and careful monitoring,” said Dr J G Lalmalani, a senior urologist.
Expressing gratitude, the patient said, “When multiple hospitals turned me away, I lost hope. But this transplant has given me a second chance at life.”

headline: 500-cr dues of private hospitals not cleared, AAP misusing Ayushman funds: Partap Singh Bajwa
description: It has been more than four months since the Punjab and Haryana High Court had asked the AAP government to furnish details of the expenses incurred on advertising and purchase of new vehicles.
content:

It has been more than four months since the Punjab and Haryana High Court had asked the AAP government to furnish details of the expenses incurred on advertising and purchase of new vehicles. headline: Air quality remains ‘moderate’ in Mumbai, temperature touches 33.9°C
description: The IMD bulletin stated that the maximum temperatures in Mumbai are expected to oscillate between 34 and 35 degrees Celsius until February 14 at least.
content:
Mumbai’s air quality remained in the ‘moderate’ category Saturday, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) at 162. However, at least four stations experienced ‘very poor’ air, with the AQI exceeding 200.
Data from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) indicated that the worst air quality was recorded in Malad West with an AQI of 274, followed by Deonar at 259, Shivaji Nagar at 217, and Mazgaon at 201. This situation followed a day when the city experienced an AQI of 166. Among the city’s 25 monitoring stations, only two areas, Borivali and Colaba, recorded AQIs below 100, indicating better air quality. AQI readings between 0-50 are regarded as ‘good’, 51-100 ‘satisfactory’, 101-200 ‘moderate’, 201-300 ‘poor’, 301-400 ‘very poor’ and above 400 are considered ‘severe’.
According to the CPCB dashboard, O3 and PM2.5 were among the most prominent pollutants in the city over the past two days. Experts have attributed the current dip in Mumbai’s air quality to a combination of human-made, natural, and meteorological factors.
In no respite for citizens, the daytime temperatures also soared above normal, with the maximum temperatures touching 33.9 degrees Celsius, three degrees above normal.
Indicating that the hot spell is here to stay, the India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its forecast bulletin, stated that the maximum temperatures are expected to oscillate between 34 and 35 degrees Celsius until February 14 at least.

headline: Not over yet: In more than a dozen seats, the AAP-BJP contest is still too close to call
description: Most of the AAP candidates that are locked in close battles, including Kejriwal, are three-time MLAs.
content:
Of the 70 seats where the Election Commission of India trends have started coming in, the margins are under 2,000 votes in 18 seats. The BJP is ahead in 40 seats and the AAP in 30.
These include New Delhi, where AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal is ahead of BJP’s Parvesh Sahib Singh by just over 220 votes after four rounds. AAP’s Rakhi Birla is leading by under 100 votes in Madipur.
Seats where the margins are low also include Rohini, where BJP’s Vijender Gupta is leading; Jangpura, where BJP’s Tarvinder Singh Marwah is ahead of AAP’s Manish Sisodia; and Malviya Nagar, where BJP’s Satish Upadhyay is ahead of AAP’s Somnath Bharti.
The Congress is yet to gain a lead in any seat so far, as per early trends.
As per ECI data, the BJP’s vote share at the moment is around 48%, while AAP’s is 43%. The Congress has a nearly 8% vote share.
In 2020, the AAP vote share was 54%, the’s BJP 38%, and the Congress’s around 4.5%.
If the trends hold, the BJP and Congress appear to have eaten into the Aam Aadmi Party’s vote share.

The battle for Delhi is a matter of prestige for the Bharatiya Janata Party, as it was neither in power in the state (since 1998) nor in the municipal corporation (since 2022). The AAP, on the other hand, is facing turbulent times with its entire leadership having gone in and out of jail in the Delhi Excise Policy case, its MLAs and leaders quitting and joining other parties, and several of its prominent leaders likely to lose their seats.
Most of the AAP candidates that are locked in close battles, including Kejriwal, are three-time MLAs. The others are Manish Sisodia, who changed his seat from Patparganj to Jangpura, Saurabh Bharadwaj from Greater Kailash and Sahi Ram Pehelwan from Tughlakabad.
AAP Delhi Convenor and former environment minister Gopal Rai, with around 23,000 votes, is more comfortably placed. He was ahead of his BJP rival Anil Kumar Vashisht, with a margin of over 9,000 votes after the fifth round of voting in Babarpur.

headline: Ajit Pawar proposes Rs 500 crore water supply project for GBS affected area
description: The NIV had recently communicated to PMC that the spurt in GBS cases was due to contaminated water and gave instructions for safety measures.
content:
In a move to provide a permanent supply of treated water to the area of Pune hit by guillain-barre syndrome cases, State Finance minister Ajit Pawar on Friday said the state government and Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) will jointly take up a Rs 500 crore water supply project.
“It is the responsibility of PMC and state government to provide clean and safe drink water to its citizens. A water supply project of Rs 500 crore has been decided upon for the affected area of Sinhagad Road in which the state will fund Rs 250 crore and PMC will spend Rs 250 crore,” said Pawar.
The NIV had recently communicated to PMC that the spurt in GBS cases was due to contaminated water and gave instructions for safety measures.
The PMC has started to provide treated water through tankers in the area as well as chemicals in every household to disinfect water.
Till now, the civic body had been supplying only chlorinated water to citizens without treatment. The water from Khadakwasla dam was being poured in a well and from there it was supplied to the area which was merged under the civic body’s limits in 2021.

headline: Karnataka HC refuses to quash Pocso case against Yediyurappa
description: In March last year, a woman had accused former Karnataka CM B S Yediyurappa of touching her daughter inappropriately when they visited his house in February to seek help regarding an earlier case of sexual assault.
content:
The Karnataka High Court on Friday quashed a special court’s order taking cognizance of the case registered against former Karnataka chief minister and BJP leader B S Yediyurappa, 81, under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act, 2012, but allowed the criminal proceedings against him to continue.
In his plea, Yediyurappa, who was accused of sexually inappropriate behaviour by the mother of a teenager in March last year, had sought the quashing of the case as well the cognizance taken of the case by the special court on July 6 last year. Yediyurappa had been summoned to appear in the special court before the framing of charges.
“The Writ Petition is allowed in part. The order of taking cognizance by the concerned court dated July 6, 2024 qua accused number one stands obliterated. The crime, the investigation and the final report all remain intact. The matter is remitted back to the concerned court to pass appropriate orders on the final report so placed before it by the CID bearing in mind the observations made in the course of the order,” Justice M Nagaprasanna of the Karnataka High Court ruled on Friday morning.
“It is made clear that this court has not answered any of the contentions advanced by both the senior counsels for the petitioner and respondent except with respect to taking cognizance. All other contentions would remain open. The petitioner is at liberty to avail of remedy as is available under law at the appropriate stage before the appropriate forums,” the high court stated in the summary of the order pronounced in the open court.
The development means that the special court will have to reconsider the chargesheet before deciding to summon Yediyurappa to start the trial process in the Pocso case.
The case against Yediyurappa
A woman lodged a police complaint on March 14 last year saying that she visited Yediyurappa’s house on February 2, 2024, with her minor daughter to seek justice in an earlier case of sexual assault by a relative on her daughter when the former chief minister allegedly touched her daughter inappropriately.
Yediyurappa’s three associates, Arun Y M, Rudresh M, and Y Mariswamy, were also named accused in the case for destroying evidence by deleting a video recording of the woman’s alleged confrontation with Yediyurappa over the incident.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On June 27 last year, the CID unit of the Karnataka Police filed a chargesheet against Yediyurappa and the three others in the Pocso case filed by the woman. The chargesheet was filed under Section 8 (sexual assault) of the Pocso Act and sections 354 A, 204 and 214 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) on charges of sexual harassment and for destroying evidence and offering gifts to silence the victim. A special court for Pocso cases took cognizance of the chargesheet on July 6 last year and issued summons to Yediyurappa and others.
Hearing an anticipatory bail plea by Yediyurappa, the Karnataka High Court ruled on June 14, 2024, that he should not be arrested in the Pocso case. Later, on July 12, the high court allowed the exemption of Yediyurappa and three others from appearing in court on the basis of the July 6 summons.

headline: Dispute over dog feeding: HC issues show-cause notice to Navi Mumbai society member for ‘derogatory’ circular against judiciary
description: The society was accused of not allowing one of its members to feed stray dogs and not permitting the member's maid to enter the society.
content:
The Bombay High Court on Friday issued show-cause notice as to why contempt action cannot be taken against a member of the managing committee of Navi Mumbai society over ‘objectionable’ communication/circular disobeying court’s order related to dispute between the society and its member over feeding of stray dogs.
The society was accused of not allowing one of its members to feed stray dogs and not permitting the member’s maid to enter the society.
It also said it would consider if contempt proceedings can be initiated against other members of society’s managing committee.
The communication in question was authored by one Vineeta Srinandan, Cultural Director of Seawoods Estates Limited (SEL) that manages a residential complex consisting of 1500 plus flats and her authorised representative Alok Agarwal.

Last week, a bench of Justices Girish S Kulkarni and Advait M Sethna had said that the contempt proceedings were required to be initiated for ‘brazen and derogatory’ comments against the judicial system in the said communication.
On January 21, while hearing Verma’s interim application, the bench had directed the housing society not to prevent domestic help from visiting her, only because she was feeding dogs in the society’s premises. It had said that by doing so, the society was breaching her fundamental rights.
The society subsequently issued a circular/communication using ‘derogatory’ language against the judicial system.

The Court had asked the managing committee of the society/Board of Directors (BoD) of the firm managing the society to pass a resolution expressing regret and remorse for action by Srinandan along with ‘impunity and tenor’ in her writings. It was unable to initiate contempt proceedings last week as Srinandan was abroad.
It had also observed that the communication was issued with ‘tacit knowledge and understanding’ of the BoD.
On Friday, Agarwal filed an affidavit on behalf of Society tendering an unconditional apology to the court, which the court termed as ‘casual’. Her lawyer sought time to file another appropriate affidavit.
“The question is whether we should continue to give laxity to the petitioner to go on filing affidavits as he had presented before the court. It appears quite clear to us that communications issued which we found objectionable amounting to criminal contempt are issued with the full knowledge of members of BoD. There is nothing to show they have distanced themselves from such communication,” the bench noted and said that the same cannot be ‘overlooked.’
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The bench then sought to know the names and contact details of the members of BoD to consider whether action of criminal contempt can be initiated against them along with Srinandan.
“With whatever post you (Srinandan) are holding (in housing society), there comes with onerous responsibility and public duty, which this woman has totally forgotten what is her legal duty. We had not come across such audacity at least in our decades of journey in law that an educated person has written something like this about the judiciary. Irrespective of whether educated or not, people have the highest respect (for the judiciary). But this is a new breed. People with so much knowledge go and tarnish the image and prestige of the court, rule of law in our country. We do not want this to happen again and cannot tolerate any reckless citizen sitting in housing complexes doing this,” Justice Kulkarni for the bench orally remarked.
“We have not the slightest of doubts that looking at the nature of the communications and the more particularly language used in communication which lowers the dignity of the court as also interferes in administration of justice, contempt proceedings are required to be issued against its author Srinandan,” the bench noted in the order and issued show-cause notice to her and posted hearing after two weeks on February 21.

headline: Niki Prasad embarks on WPL venture with Delhi Capitals after U19 World Cup triumph
description: Earlier this week, Prasad led the India U19 team to a victory in Kuala Lumpur, defeating South Africa in the finals to secure the Championship trophy. The 19-year-old batting all-rounder believes that her World Cup experience has prepared her for the challenges ahead in the WPL.
content:
By Aryesh Chakraborty
Fresh off a historic ICC U19 Women’s T20 World Cup victory, young Indian cricket team captain Niki Prasad has embarked on a new chapter in her career, joining Delhi Capitals for the Women’s Premier League (WPL) 2025. The JSW-GMR co-owned franchise gave the newly crowned World Cup winning captain an unexpected reception as she arrived in Pune for the pre-season camp.
Prasad, who has been playing cricket since the age of six, reflected on her journey into professional cricket. “I remember playing with young boys for four to five years before joining an academy. Seeing more than 90 girls playing cricket at the academy for the first time made me nervous. But today, seeing young players come up and do well for their state is very special.”
Earlier this week, Prasad led the India U19 team to a victory in Kuala Lumpur, defeating South Africa in the finals to secure the Championship trophy. The 19-year-old batting all-rounder believes that her World Cup experience has prepared her for the challenges ahead in the WPL.
“The important thing was that we were calm and composed during the finals. We just went out there and expressed ourselves. That’s why we looked like the more dominating side,” Prasad said. “Winning the World Cup for the second time feels special. I am proud of my team and the way we performed. We have shown the world what we are capable of, and we will continue to ensure that India stays on top”, she noted.
As she transitions to the WPL, Prasad is eager to capture the opportunity with Delhi Capitals. “Being part of a WPL team is a great opportunity for youngsters to learn from experienced players. I am very grateful to DC for showing faith in me. Coming into this franchise, I know I will learn a lot, and more importantly, I will try to contribute as much as I can to help win the title for the team and contribute as much as possible,” Prasad said.
Prasad also acknowledged the invaluable support from senior Indian cricketer Jemimah Rodrigues. “She reached out to congratulate me and gave me advice ahead of this journey. Jemimah is a down-to-earth person, and she made me feel comfortable when I first joined the team. With such a team and support staff, you never feel nervous,” she added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Ahead to her WPL debut, Prasad is determined to make the most of this platform, she said, “A tournament like WPL, one of the biggest leagues in the world, is definitely a place to express oneself. It gives young players the opportunity to showcase their talent. For me, it’s a chance to prove myself.”
Beyond the WPL, Prasad has shared her insights that are set in her cricketing career. “Winning the U19 World Cup was one of my dreams, but the bigger goal is to win the World Cup for the senior team. This is just one step toward my greater goal, and I know there are a lot of expectations from me. I am working hard to achieve my dreams.”
Delhi Capitals will begin their WPL campaign against Mumbai Indians on February 15 in Vadodara.

headline: Agra man dies in police custody, 3 SIs suspended as family alleges torture
description: Protesting locals lay siege to police outpost, block Yamuna Expressway for two hours; police deployed in the village in large numbers
content:
A 52-year-old man died in police custody after alleged torture in Uttar Pradesh’s Agra district on Thursday afternoon, prompting a protest by locals who laid siege to a police outpost and blocked the Yamuna Expressway for nearly two hours.
The deceased, Kedar Singh, 52, who ran a small flour mill from his house at Garhi Hisia village, 22 km from Agra city, was summoned to the Kabis police outpost in connection with a forgery case in which he was a witness, the police said.
Singh’s wife Chandrakanta, in her complaint to the police, alleged that her husband was assaulted at the police station that led to his death. A large number of police and Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) personnel were deployed at Garhi Hisia when Singh’s body was handed over to his family on Friday afternoon after post-mortem.
Following the incident, the government on Friday suspended three sub-inspectors (SIs) deployed at the police outpost and initiated departmental inquiry against them, while the Dauki police station officer in-charge, Tarun Dhiman, was sent to Police Lines for negligence in duty.
The suspended officials, all of SI rank, are Kabis police outpost incharge Sidharth Chaudhary, Shivmanagal Singh, the investigating officer (IO) in the forgery case and Ram Sevak.
The victim’s wife Chandrakanta said, “Around 2.45 pm on Thursday, four policemen from the Kabis police outpost came to our house and forcibly took my husband along. He went to the outpost on his motorbike with a police constable riding pillion. They started beating him up on the way to the outpost.”
“Once at the outpost, they stuffed his mouth with clothes and thrashed him again. Our grandson, Aakash, 16, who was present at the Aadhaar centre opposite the outpost saw four policemen rushing him in an unconscious state to the hospital in a hired vehicle. He informed us about the incident and we rushed to the S N Medical College where doctors pronounced my husband dead,” Chandrakanta stated in the complaint to Agra Police Commissioner J Ravindra Gaud, demanding a murder case be registered against the guilty policemen.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The police, however, are yet to file a first information report (FIR) in the matter.
Agra Deputy Commissioner of Police (East Zone) Atul Sharma said the allegations of death due to police torture would be investigated and promised strict action against the police officials if found guilty.
“A departmental inquiry has been ordered against the officials. They will face a strict legal action if found guilty. The autopsy of Kedar Singh was conducted by a panel of doctors and the process was videographed today (Friday) to rule out any possibility of foul play on part of the police,” the DCP said.
“Kedar Singh and two others were called to the police outpost for inquiry into a pending case of forgery and fraud. His condition deteriorated at the outpost, after which he was rushed to the medical college where he was declared dead. Doctors said he died of heart attack,” Sharma added.

headline: 2.03 lakh at cancer risk, 1.93 lakh dialysis patients — how Kerala is battling surge in lifestyle diseases
description: State health department had launched a lifestyle disease screening programme, under the ‘Aardram’ health mission, in two phases.
content:
Indicating the high prevalence of morbidity in Kerala, a health survey held among one crore people in the state found that around 45 per cent of the screened population is vulnerable to lifestyle diseases.
State health department had launched a lifestyle disease screening programme, under the ‘Aardram’ health mission, in two phases.
Kerala Health Minister Veena George Thursday said in the first phase, 1.54 crore people above the age of 30 had been screened and another one crore people had been screened in the second phase.
“When one crore people were screened in the second phase, 44.85 per cent of them were found susceptible to lifestyle diseases. Of them, 13.35 per cent have hypertension, 8.82 per cent have diabetes and another six per cent have both. The screening brought out that 2.03 lakh people are at risk of cancer and they were referred for further screening. Among those found susceptible for cancer, 1.25 lakh have been asked to undergo further screening for breast cancer,” said the minister.
The minister also said the state wanted to bring down the morbidity by conducting annual health surveys. “In the first and second phase screenings, 11 lakh people were found vulnerable to various types of cancers. However only 1.90 lakh people have come forward for further screening. Hence the state earlier this week launched a special campaign for enlightening people for cancer prevention and treatment,” said the minister.
Kerala’s health sector has been internationally acclaimed for various indicators including infant mortality rate and maternal mortality rate etc. However, the state is facing the burden of lifestyle diseases.
As per the figures submitted in the Assembly by the Health Minister with regard to kidney patients in the state, there had been only 43,740 patients undergoing dialysis in 2020. The figure more than doubled in 2021 with 91,759 patients, further growing to 1,30,633 in 2022 and eventually went up to 1,93,281 in 2023. The data shows an alarming growth, of dialysis patients, of 341 per cent in three years.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A major factor behind this escalation is the high prevalence of diabetes in Kerala. As per the Indian Council of Medical Research-India Diabetes-17 (ICMR-INDIAB-17) study, the prevalence of diabetes is 11.4 per cent in India and 23.6 per cent in the state.

headline: Right to know medical status of human beings can also be considered as a Fundamental Right: Punjab and Haryana HC
description: Seeks assistance of Punjab, Haryana and Chandigarh on measures taken about illegible writing by doctors.
content:
Finding it “surprising and shocking” that notes prescriptions by government doctors are written by hand which cannot be read by anybody, except perhaps by some doctors and chemists, the Punjab and Haryana High Court says it will not be out of place to note the right to know medical status of a human being can also be considered as a Fundamental Right under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
Perusing the Medico-Legal Report (MLR) of a rape victim filed by the State of Haryana while hearing an anticipatory bail plea of the accused, the single bench of Justice Jasgurpreet Singh Puri said, “The handwriting in the aforesaid MLR is absolutely illegible and cannot be understood at all. It is very surprising and shocking to note that in this era of computers, the notes on medical history and prescriptions by Government Doctors are written by hand which cannot be read by anybody except perhaps some Doctors. This Court has also seen in a number of cases where even the medical prescription is written in such handwriting which nobody can read except perhaps some Chemists. The same is the position in the State of Punjab and probably in the UT, Chandigarh also.”
Also Read | Punjab and Haryana HC slams police inaction in Jalandhar POCSO case, orders affidavit from Commissioner
Justice Puri said that “to have the knowledge about the medical prescription by the Doctor and the notes on the medical history is prima facie a right which is vested in the patient or the attendants to peruse the same and apply the mind, especially in today’s technological world.”
“It will not be out of place to even note that the right to know the medical status of a human being can also be considered a Fundamental Right under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. Health and the treatment given to a human being is a part of life and therefore, it may be considered as part of the Right to Life”, Justice Puri noted.
Taking serious note of the issue, the bench asked the Advocate Generals of Haryana and Punjab and the Senior Standing Counsel of Chandigarh, to assist “as to what remedial and corrective measures can be taken about the illegible writing on the medical notes and also on the prescriptions not only by the Government Doctors but also by the Private Doctors in both the States and the UT, Chandigarh”.
Also Read | 27% of food samples fail tests in Haryana: RTI
“It deems it fit and proper to request the Advocate General, Haryana to assist this Court on this issue. Since this problem is rampant in the State of Punjab and probably in UT, Chandigarh as well, this Court is also of the view that the State of Punjab as well as UT, Chandigarh should also assist this Court in this regard,” the bench said.
Noting that the assistance of the National Medical Commission (NMC) is also required in the present case, the HC asked advocate Ravi Sharma, on the NMC panel, to assist the Court on the issue.

Meanwhile, the HC appointed Advocate Tanu Bedi, as Amicus Curiae in the case to assist the Court.
The matter was adjourned for a hearing on February 13.

headline: Inside US deportation of 104 Indians: ‘Handcuffed, legs chained, struggled to use washroom for 40 hours’
description: The US military aircraft — a C-17 Globemaster — that the Donald Trump administration deployed made four pit stops for fuel refilling before landing at Amritsar Wednesday.
content:
“For 40 hours, we were handcuffed, our feet tied with chains and were not allowed to move an inch from our seats. After repeated requests, we were allowed to drag ourselves to the washroom. The crew would open the door of the lavatory and shove us in,” said Harwinder Singh.
The 40-year-old from Tahli village in Punjab’s Hoshiarpur is among the 104 ‘illegal’ immigrants whom the US deported in the first batch to India.
Recounting the travel as a “worse than hell,” experience, Harwinder said that they couldn’t even eat properly for 40 hours. “They would force us to eat with handcuffs on. Our requests to the security personnel to remove the cuffs for a few minutes fell on deaf ears. The journey was not only physically painful, but also mentally exhausting…,” he said, adding that a “kind” crew member offered them fruits.
Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal, Punjab Cabinet Minister addresses the media after U.S. military plane deporting Indian immigrants lands in Amritsar (Reuters)
The US military aircraft — a C-17 Globemaster — that the Donald Trump administration deployed made four pit stops for fuel refilling before landing at Amritsar Wednesday. Harwinder said he could not sleep as he kept thinking about the promise of a better life that he made to his wife before his “dunki” travel eight months ago.
Also Read | As US sends military plane to India, what to know of Trump's mass deportation efforts
In June 2024, Harwinder and his wife Kuljinder Kaur, took a decision. With two children — 12-year-old son and 11-year-old daughter — the couple, married for 13 years, was struggling to make ends meet by selling cattle milk. Out of nowhere, a distant relative offered to take Harwinder to the US in 15 days legally, not via a dunki route, in exchange of Rs 42 lakh. To gather the amount, the family mortgaged their only acre of land and borrowed from private lenders at steep interest rates.
People look at the U.S. military plane deporting Indian immigrants as it lands in Amritsar (REUTERS)
Life had not prepared Kuljinder for the adversities to come. “But for 8- months, my husband was shuffled between countries,” Kuljinder said. “He was passed from one place to another like a pawn in a game. He never made it to the US.”
Also Read | Indian migrants sent back from US: Why Trump is using expensive military planes for deportation
Harwinder endured life-threatening conditions but despite the hardships, he documented his ordeal and sent videos to Kuljinder. She last spoke to him on January 15.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Harwinder remained in contact with his family until mid-January. The news of his deportation came as a shock to Kuljinder, who learned of it only when villagers informed her that he was among the 104 deportees sent back from the US on Wednesday.
Kuljinder said they had already filed a complaint against the travel agent with the village panchayat after losing contact with Harwinder last month.
She is demanding strict action against the agent and a refund of the Rs 42 lakh spent on the failed journey. “We have lost everything,” she said. “We only wanted a better future for our children and now we are left with debt and heartbreak.”
Kuljinder revealed that the agent extorted money at every step of Harwinder’s journey, including a final payment of Rs 10 lakh when he was in Guatemala just two and a half months ago.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Before Harwinder’s departure, the family managed a modest living by farming leased land and rearing cattle.
His younger brother also farms rented land, but their income was not enough to secure a better future. Harwinder’s elderly parents—his 85-year-old father and 70-year-old mother—still work in the fields.

content:

headline: CSMIA recorded over 64,000 lost items in 2024
description: Wallets, passports, mobile phones, and wristwatches rank among the most frequently lost valuables. Airport officials say they follow a structured tagging and storage system to ensure misplaced items are secured and accounted for.
content:
Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport (CSMIA) recorded over 64,000 lost items in 2024, highlighting the scale of misplaced belongings at one of India’s busiest airports. The airport’s Lost & Found Department, responsible for managing these items, has facilitated the return of 9,588 belongings to their rightful owners this year.
Every month, around 5,000 items are left behind by passengers, high-traffic areas like security checkpoints, boarding gates, lounges, and food courts being the most common locations where items are misplaced. Wallets, passports, mobile phones, and wristwatches rank among the most frequently lost valuables. Airport officials say they follow a structured tagging and storage system to ensure misplaced items are secured and accounted for.
Unclaimed items such as spectacles, belts, and earphones are stored for a stipulated period before being donated to NGOs, while valuables like jewellery and electronics are handed over to Customs after 90 days. Officials estimate that 30% of all misplaced belongings in 2024 were classified as valuables, of which 80% were successfully reunited with their owners.
Lost items undergo a verification and documentation process before being returned, with most recoveries completed within a day. The airport’s Lost & Found team operates round the clock, handling more than 5,000 queries every month.
“At CSMIA, every lost item holds value and sentiment for our passengers. Our dedicated Lost & Found team works 24/7 with unwavering dedication, ensuring cherished items are reunited with their rightful owners. With efficiency, trust, and care, we strive to make every journey seamless and stress-free for our passengers,” said CSMIA spokesperson.
According to the officials, some notable recoveries last year included a passport returned to its owner a month before an international trip, a handbag containing an engagement ring and heirloom ornaments located and handed over the same day, and a bride’s wedding lehenga, which was retrieved from a security checkpoint and delivered to a relative before her scheduled wedding.

headline: Dahisar check naka: Sarnaik directs contractors to reserve lanes for heavy vehicles to ease traffic jams
description: Additionally, height restrictions have been placed on two lanes at each side to accommodate only cars. Asked why the toll booths were not removed entirely, the MSRDC official explained that dismantling them would require a two-day traffic block, which could lead to severe disruptions.
content:
Amidst complaints of frequent traffic jams at the Dahisar check naka, Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik has instructed toll contractors to reserve specific lanes for heavy vehicles at the check naka to ease traffic congestion in the area. Three lanes will be designated for vehicles heading to Mumbai, while two lanes will be set aside for those travelling out of the city. These lanes will be dedicated to toll collection, while the remaining lanes will be cleared for light vehicles, aiming to streamline traffic flow.
The current system on NH-48 (Mumbai-Ahmedabad) consists of 12 lanes (6+6). A representative from the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC), which manages toll collection at Mumbai’s entry points, said that in the southbound direction during peak hours, seven lanes are allocated for traffic, with three reserved for light motor vehicles. Similarly, seven lanes are designated for northbound traffic in the evening. One additional lane from the opposite side is also utilised for the reverse flow.
Additionally, height restrictions have been placed on two lanes at each side to accommodate only cars. Asked why the toll booths were not removed entirely, the MSRDC official explained that dismantling them would require a two-day traffic block, which could lead to severe disruptions.
On Thursday, Sarnaik conducted an on-site inspection of the Dahisar check naka, accompanied by Mira-Bhayander Municipal Commissioner Sanjay Katkar, local traffic police officers, and toll contractors. Last year, the government, led by then CM and current Deputy CM Eknath Shinde, exempted light four-wheelers from toll charges. However, traffic jams continue to be a persistent issue during peak hours. The current toll lane configuration has contributed to slow vehicle movement, causing significant delays.

headline: Digital arrest: Cyber fraudster arrested for duping IIT student of Rs 4.3 lakh
description: The accused was earlier arrested by the Rajasthan Police in a NDPS case, said police.
content:
A 29-year-old man has been arrested for allegedly duping a fourth-year student of IIT Delhi of Rs 4.33 lakh by placing him under digital arrest.
The police identified the accused as Madan Lal (29), a resident of Lohawat in Rajasthan, who was arrested from Chennai last month. A Class 10 dropout, the police said Lal used to purchase bank accounts details of victims and withdraw money through their debit cards. He then bought USDTs – a cryptocurrency – and sold the same at higher prices.
“The accused used to purchase USDTs and was in touch with a Chinese national to whom he sold the same at a higher price,” Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Surendra Choudhary said.
He added that on November 16, 2024, the IIT student received a call from someone claiming to be from a courier service. The caller allegedly falsely informed him that a suspicious parcel in his name was being shipped from Mumbai to Beijing. When the student denied any knowledge of the parcel, the caller advised him to report the issue to the police and transferred the call to an alleged officer at Gamdevi police station in Mumbai, he added.
The caller, impersonating impersonating police and Enforcement Directorate officials, allegedly falsely accused the victim of being linked to illegal cases and stated that an arrest warrant had been issued in his name.
On November 18, the alleged frauds called again and claimed that another illegal parcel has arrived in his name. They managed to coerce the victim into transferring Rs 4.33 lakh to prove his innocence through online transactions, police said.
When the victim realised that he had been deceived, he filed a police complaint and an FIR was registered, said the DCP.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
During the probe, the police discovered that a foreign number from Hong Kong had been used to contact the complainant and that a portion of the defrauded money was transferred to a bank account linked to one Tejpal Sharma from Rai Singh Nagar in Rajasthan.
The DCP said that when questioned, Sharma claimed that he gave his ATM card to his friend, Gagandeep Singh, who had then changed the account’s registered mobile number. When tracked down, Gagandeep told the police that he had provided the account to his associate Bajrang.
Following this, surveillance revealed that withdrawals were made from an ATM in Lohawat. “Based on technical surveillance, Madan Lal was traced to Chennai,” said the DCP.
During interrogation, Lal admitted to receiving the bank account details from Bajrang for Rs 20,000, withdrawing fraudulent funds, and exchanging the money for cryptocurrency through a contact named Ravi Chaudhary, said police. “Madan later sold USDTs to a Chinese woman via WhatsApp, receiving payment in rupees,” said an officer.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The accused was earlier arrested by the Rajasthan Police in a NDPS case, said police.

headline: Karnataka to sign MoUs with leading universities for KWIN City at GIM 2025
description: St John’s University (New York) and the England-based University of York are expected to participate in the Global Investors Meet.
content:
Karnataka Industries Minister M B Patil recently said the state was expecting to ink a series of Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with top Indian and foreign universities for the development of KWIN City.
Patil said: “The agreements will be formalised during the Global Investors Meet (GIM) 2025, marking a significant step in strengthening Karnataka’s position as a leader in the knowledge economy.”
The minister also informed that a high-level roundtable hosted by Higher Education Minister Dr M C Sudhakar, and Medical Education and Skill Development Minister S Prakash Patil will be held during the GIM, laying the groundwork for “transformative academic partnerships”.
Top institutions expected to join
Several prominent Indian universities, including Azim Premji University, PES University, MS Ramaiah University, Manipal Academy, and Christ University, have been invited to collaborate on this ambitious project. In addition, leading research institutions such as the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research (JNCASR), National Institute of Mental Health and Neurosciences (NIMHANS), and National Law School of India University (NLSIU) are also expected to be part of the discussions.
Scheduled for February 13, the session is expected to witness the signing of MoUs with five to six foreign universities and six to eight Indian universities. Discussions are currently ongoing, and final decisions will be taken in the coming days, Patil said. Highlighting the significance of this initiative, Patil noted that under UGC norms, the world’s top 500 universities are permitted to establish campuses in India, and Karnataka will actively leverage this opportunity.
“The upcoming Global Investors Meet will not focus solely on industrial investments but will also prioritise research, skill development, and ancillary sectors aimed at creating a highly skilled workforce. KWIN-City represents a futuristic urban development model aligned with global standards in entrepreneurship, skills, and innovation,” Patil said.
International universities, including St John’s University (New York) and the University of York (England), along with experts from VIT Vellore, Christian Medical College (CMC), Birla Institute of Technology and Science (BITS) Pilani, Sastra University, and Lovely Professional University (LPU), are also anticipated to participate.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Prominent Indian corporate leaders and foundations, such as Azim Premji Foundation, Infosys, Reliance, Adani, Bharti, Wipro, Biocon, Kotak Education Foundation, Shiv Nadar Foundation, Bajaj and Mahindra Foundations, Tata Trusts, and HDFC, will also be part of the discussions. Representatives from HDFC Bank Parivartan, Aditya Birla Group CSR, and Asian Paints CSR will present their ideas on collaboration and investment in research and education.
The KWIN-City project will be developed on approximately 5,000 acres between Doddaballapur and Dabaspet. It aims to establish a hub for education, healthcare, research, and innovation, bringing together world-class institutions and industries to drive Karnataka’s growth in these sectors.

headline: No one in voting lines remembers the 26,000 Delhi residents who died in the Covid waves — except those who lost their loved ones
description: As Delhi residents lined up outside various centres to cast their vote on Wednesday, the Covid pandemic — which killed 26,000 people in Delhi alone, according to official figures — was a distant memory.
content:
“Last time, he was there…” Waiting for her turn to vote at an MCD primary school in Delhi, Krishna Mandal, 40, chokes up as she remembers her younger brother, Prasanjit, whom she lost to Covid four years ago. He was 22.
As Delhi residents lined up outside various centres to cast their vote on Wednesday, the Covid pandemic — which killed 26,000 people in Delhi alone, according to official figures — was a distant memory. No one seemed to remember the time when virtually no hospital beds were available for patients, how people were scrambling to get oxygen cylinders and oximeters. No one, except those who lost their loved ones.
“In five days, everything was over,” said Krishna, who works as a house help in Mehrauli. It was on May 16, 2021, that she learnt that her brother had contracted Covid.
“We took him to Madan Mohan Malviya Hospital and the doctors kept telling us to get the receipt. We are poor people; we did not know what to do. Doctor told us that he would need an oxygen cylinder and for that we had no money,” she told The Indian Express.
Also Read | BJP questions Kejriwal income: Rise in Covid yr, fall thereafter
“My brother worked as a cleaner at a private company. His manager arranged an oxygen cylinder illegally for Rs 3,000,” she added. “But, there was no mask to supply the oxygen from the cylinder. We were running mad on the roads, calling everyone that we knew. In all this, we lost five days and on May 22, he died,” said Krishna.
“No one came to see us; no BJP, no AAP and no Congress,” she said, her eyes welling up. Having grown indifferent to politicians, she had a practical reason for casting her vote this election. “I was told that if I do not vote, they will remove my name from the voter list. So, I came,” said Krishna, who hails from West Bengal’s 24 Parganas district and has been living in Mehrauli for the last 25 years. At the same voting centre, mother-son duo, Praveen and Kanchan Bali, are seated on the stairs.
“I lost my father, Prakash Bali,” said Praveen, 34, a mass-media graduate who now runs his own business. “My father was a liver patient. His health started deteriorating in July 2021, during the second wave. We took him to a hospital but the administration refused to take him in, asking us to get a Covid test done,” said Praveen.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Also Read | While people were dying of Covid, Kejriwal was building Sheesh Mahal: Parvesh Verma kickstarts campaign
“The entire thing (tests, admission, oxygen mask) would have cost us Rs 1 lakh. We did not have the money and so, they didn’t admit him. The hospital asked him to be put under observation for three days but he needed immediate help… We kept running around… and finally, we were able to get him a hospital bed on October 1. Two days later, he was no more…,” said Praveen. “Had the healthcare facilities been good, my husband could have been saved,” said Kanchan.
“I blame the system,” said Santosh Kumar Chaubey, 40, a resident of Chhattarpur, whose 50-year-old uncle succumbed to the infection in 2021. “We stay in a joint family. I was already infected. So, once he started showing the symptoms, we thought that it was viral fever,” he added.
“It was a tough time… There was no space in any of the Covid centers in Delhi,” said Chaubey, standing outside the Rajkiya-sah Shiksha Varishtha Madhyamik Vidyalaya in Sanjay colony, Bhati Mines. His uncle died within two days of being admitted to a private hospital in Noida.
Chaubey, who hails from UP’s Mirzapur, said, “In all these years, we could not get the number of hospitals we needed. Even on regular days, people fail to find a bed in the hospitals…No government can build a hospital overnight but they failed to do so in even 10 years!”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Standing in front of the polling booth at the MCD school at Mehrauli dargah was Yogesh Kaushik, a teacher at an NGO. Though he did not lose a family member, he still remembers the pain and sense of loss a number of his students went through. “I saw many lose their parents… It was intense. I had students call me for help,” said Kaushik. “Sadly, people don’t remember these things anymore. Many are voting just for the sake of it.”

headline: ‘Handcuffed deportees’: Haryana Congress MPs slam BJP-led Centre, call episode ‘insult’ to India
description: Rohtak Lok Sabha MP Deepender Hooda was part of the INDIA bloc group that protested in the Parliament House complex.
content:
Haryana Congress Members of Parliament (MPs) Thursday termed the handcuffing of Indian nationals deported in a US Air Force aircraft an insult to the entire country. Among 104 Indians recently deported for illegally entering the US, 33 are from Haryana.
Rohtak Lok Sabha MP Deepender Hooda was part of the INDIA bloc group that protested in the Parliament House complex. Congress Rajya Sabha MP Randeep Surjewala, too, questioned the government in the House.
“Sending back Indian citizens in handcuffs, shackled in military planes is an insult to every Indian and India. The US government is humiliatingly deporting Indian citizens on the basis of illegal documents, handcuffing them, and shackling them in military planes. These youths went there by selling their land and property in search of employment, putting their lives at risk. But now they are facing economic ruin and social displacement. The BJP government has been repeatedly claiming that the President of America is a friend of PM Narendra Modi, but as soon as he became the President of America, the PM’s same friend forcibly deported a large number of Indians in such a humiliating manner,” Hooda said.
Hooda demanded that “the prime minister should immediately talk to the US government so that Indians living in America for years are not expelled in a humiliating manner. Apart from this, the central government should hold diplomatic talks with the US to provide legal aid for Indians facing deportation… A legal aid cell should be set up to help the affected families.”
The Congress MP said he had raised the issue of youths going abroad without a visa in the Budget session of Parliament last year, but Kirti Vardhan Singh, Minister of State, External Affairs, had shrugged off the responsibility and said the government was not responsible if people going abroad adopted other means. “If the government had taken my words seriously that day, then we would not have to see this day today,” Hooda added.
He also blamed the lack of jobs in Haryana for forcing the youths to adopt unfair means to move abroad.
“According to the data of US Customs and Border Patrol, between October 2022 and September 2023, over 90,000 Indians were arrested while crossing illegally into the US from Mexico after trekking through the jungles of Panama… Wrong policies of the government are completely responsible for the highest unemployment rate in Haryana, migration due to it, and now forced deportation,” Hooda remarked.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Seeking clarifications from the government in the House, Surjewala said, “Why is the government silent? Indian citizens were chained for over 40 hours and had only one toilet at their disposal during this arduous journey. Are Indian citizens terrorists? Why is the government silent? Thousands of our Indian brothers and sisters are imprisoned in US detention centres. How will they be brought back? Has the government raised this issue with the US to provide counsellor access to Indian nationals detained there?”
Sirsa MP Kumari Selja said if the youths were provided employment opportunities in India, the current situation would not have arisen.
“There is an immediate need to eliminate the human trafficking network, provide financial and social reintegration assistance to the deported individuals, and establish a transparent migration framework to prevent such difficulties for Indians in the future,” Selja added.

headline: Who is on the flight carrying 104 individuals deported from the US?
description: The flight is set to land at Amritsar at 1 pm, Punjab government says they will be received in a ‘friendly manner’
content:
A United States military C-17 aircraft carrying 104 deported Indian nationals from Haryana, Gujarat, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Chandigarh is set to land at Amritsar airport around 1 pm today. The flight, which departed from San Antonio, Texas, on Tuesday afternoon, has 11 crew members and 45 US officials on board.
According to sources, the highest number of deportees – 33 each – are from Gujarat and Haryana, followed by 30 from Punjab. Two passengers each are from Uttar Pradesh and Chandigarh, while three are from Maharashtra.
The deportees include 25 women and 12 minors, with the youngest passenger being just four years old. Forty-eight individuals are below the age of 25.
A senior Punjab Police official said that most of the 30 deportees from Punjab hail from the Majha belt, including Gurdaspur, Amritsar, and Tarn Taran, while others are from Jalandhar, Nawanshahr, Patiala, Mohali, and Sangrur.
The repatriation comes amid increasing US immigration enforcement measures, particularly targeting individuals who entered the country illegally or overstayed their visas.
Punjab police have made strict arrangements at the airport. Speaking to media persons on Tuesday, Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav said, “We discussed it in the meeting chaired by the Chief Minister today. He has asked us that the Punjab government receive them in a friendly manner. We shall set up our counters there (at the airport). We are in touch with the central government. Whenever we shall receive any more information, we will share it. We still have unconfirmed reports that a large number of people are likely to be deported.”
Earlier, Punjab NRI Affairs Minister Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal said it was better to “send illegal residents back home rather than putting them in jail in the US.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann said they will provide all possible help to the individuals.
A senior Punjab police officer said they will also scan the past criminal record, if any, of the deportees at the airport itself.

headline: I-T Department conducts raid on Punjab Congress MLA Rana Gurjeet’s houses
description: The I-T raids were on in Kapurthala, Chandigarh, and Jalandhar establishments of Congress MLA Rana Gurjeet Singh.
content:
Several teams of the Income Tax Department Thursday morning conducted raids on the premises of Punjab Congress MLA Rana Gurjeet Singh in Kapurthala, Chandigarh, and Jalandhar.
Officials said the I-T Department teams arrived at the Sector 4 residence of the Congress leader in Chandigarh at around 6.30 am, and started conducting their search. No one was allowed to leave the premises, and Singh was reportedly present at the house when the raid took place.
Simultaneous raids also took place at the MLA Hostel official residence of Rana Gurjeet Singh in Chandigarh, as well as his establishments in Jalandhar and Kapurthala.
Rana Gurjeet Singh represented the Jalandhar Lok Sabha constituency from 2004 to 2009. He had been a Cabinet minister in the Punjab Government, and handled portfolios like power and irrigation.
His political career reflects the complex interplay of power, business interests, and public service in Indian politics, marked by achievements and controversies.
He faced allegations of impropriety related to sand mining contracts in Punjab, leading to his resignation from the Cabinet in January 2018. There have been instances of legal proceedings and public scrutiny regarding his business dealings, particularly in relation to how contracts were awarded and managed.
In the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections, Rana Gurjeet Singh won his seat in Kapurthala, defeating his nearest Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) rival. His son, Rana Inder Pratap Singh, also won from Sultanpur Lodhi, contesting as an Independent, which highlights the family’s political influence in the region.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
However, his ambitions for central politics were reportedly thwarted when he did not secure a ticket for himself or his son for the Lok Sabha elections from Anandpur Sahib or Khadoor Sahib in 2024.
Born in Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand, Rana Gurjeet is known for his involvement in agriculture and business. His educational qualification is listed as having cleared Class 10, and he is noted for his assets, making him one of the richest MLAs in the Punjab Assembly.

headline: Bengal witnessing economic renaissance, best time to invest: Ambani lauds Mamata at 8th Bengal Global Business Summit
description: Says Reliance created over 1 lakh direct jobs, announces retail sector expansion
content:
Lauding Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee for being a “tireless leader and one of the most-ablest administrators in the country”, Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani on Wednesday said that West Bengal was experiencing a “renaissance in economy and business” and added that it was the best time to invest in the state. He also promised to double the investment in the state to Rs 1 lakh crore by the end of the decade.
Reliance Industries has interests in petrochemicals, oil and gas, telecom, retail, media and financial services.
Addressing the inaugural session of the eighth edition of the Bengal Global Business Summit (BGBS) in Kolkata, Ambani said: “I come from the western part of India. It is generally believed that the western states are leaders in economy and business. But this situation is changing rapidly. Bengal has always been a land of renaissance. Now, Bengal is witnessing a renaissance in economy and business… Today, Bengal means soaring vision. Today, Bengal means mighty ambition. Today, Bengal means efficient implementation.”
“In today’s fast-changing world, India has become a beacon of growth and hope. Within this fast-changing India, Bengal has become a source of growth and hope. Therefore, it is the best time for investing in Bengal as we are marching towards leadership based on technology and the power of our youth,” he added.
Praising Mamata Banerjee’s leadership, Ambani said, “What the chief minister promises, her team delivers.”
Addressing the CM, the billionaire industrialist, said: “Each time I come here – and I have come here for every Summit from 2016 – I think it cannot be better. But you have proved me wrong every single time. This summit is consistently becoming bigger and more prestigious. And today we have 20 global partner countries with us.”
“She (Mamata Banerjee) has been in office for nearly 14 years means that Bengal has immensely benefited from policy continuity and her leadership. Her name, ‘Mamata’, stands for empathy or compassion. But Didi in your name stands for a tireless leader. You are empathy and energy personified.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Empathy for the common people is the guiding principle of all your policies and welfare schemes. This is most strikingly seen in your initiatives for the education of the girl child, women’s empowerment and poverty alleviation. All of India needs this kind of inclusive and sustainable model of development, so that no Indian is left behind and no region in India is left behind. Thank you for your leadership, Mamata Didi,” he added.
Urging other industrialists to invest in the state, Ambani said: “Our investment in Bengal is not only financial. More importantly, it is an emotional investment. Most of it is because of our respect for Didi. As one of the leading private sector employers in Bengal, today I have both a recommendation and an appeal to make to potential investors – to those who are present here today and those who are not. Reliance has had a wonderful experience of doing business in this state. Mamata Didi is one of the most ablest administrators in India. With Didi at the helm, the business community receives a red carpet treatment in Bengal. Bountiful Bengal beckons you. So, friends, come to Bengal, and script new and beautiful chapters in Bengal’s growth story.”
Claiming that Reliance Jio’s 5G network covers the entire West Bengal, Ambani, who is among the top 10 richest industrialists in the world, said: “CM (Mamata Banerjee) proved lucky for us. By the end of 2023, Jio covered 100 per cent of Bengal’s population. Bengal continues to maintain record of being the highest user across India. Jio has transformed rural Bengal.”
Promising to double the investment in West Bengal by 2030, Ambani said that a new AI-ready data centre in Kolkata will be operational in nine months and a new cable landing station in Digha will boost the state’s digital leadership. “Bengal’s strategic location and fast-improving physical infrastructure gives the state an enviable edge. But the biggest asset of Bengal is its people — over 100 million hard-working, extremely talented and highly cultured people. In the emerging era of Knowledge Economy, your state has a special advantage because Bengal has always been a land of super-intelligent people. When natural intelligence is enhanced by the capabilities of Artificial Intelligence, there is no way that Bengal can fail. And no power on earth can stop Bengal’s resurgence,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“In 2016, when I first attended this summit, Reliance’s investments stood below Rs 2,000 crore. Today, in less than a decade, our investments in Bengal have increased 20 times, and we have invested over Rs 50,000 crore. We shall double this investment by the end of this decade. More importantly, our investments have created over one lakh direct jobs and spurred significant economic growth in West Bengal,” Ambani claimed. He also announced that Reliance will expand its retail network in the state to 1,700 stores with 2.2 million square feet of warehousing.
He also said that Reliance is looking forward to investing in solar energy projects in the state: “Our motto is: “Solar Bangla for Sonar Bangla”, he added.

headline: As Milkipur betters 2022 turnout figure, Akhilesh says presiding officers fulfilling fake voting target
description: The Milkipur bypoll has turned into a prestige battle between the SP and the BJP as the seat is part of the politically significant Ayodhya district.
content:
MORE THAN 65% of total 3.70 lakh voters exercised their franchise till 11 pm in Milkipur Assembly bypoll Wednesday, surpassing the turnout in 2022 at 60.23%.
SP chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged “fake voting” and rigging by officials, a charge rejected by the police. According to the EC turnout app, the polling percentage was 65.35%.
The Milkipur bypoll has turned into a prestige battle between the SP and the BJP as the seat is part of the politically significant Ayodhya district.
SP chief Yadav alleged that presiding officers are “fulfilling the target of fake voting”.
Yadav posted on X an audio clip from a purported sting and said, “This is a sting operation of the truth of presiding officers who are fulfilling the target of fake voting for the ruling party.” He alleged that police are checking identity cards of voters to “create fear”.
In another post on X, Yadav said, “The Election Commission should immediately take cognisance of pictures related to the news that Ayodhya Police are checking the ID cards of voters in Milkipur…” he said, attaching a picture with the post.
Ayodhya Senior SP Raj Karan Nayyar denied the allegations. He said the photo in question depicted police personnel verifying the identification credentials of a polling agent, and emphasised that law enforcement officers are not conducting any verification of voters’ identification documents.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
SP leader and Faizabad MP Awadhesh Prasad alleged the BJP was “creating pressure on officers.”
The main contest is between SP’s Ajit Prasad and the BJP’s Chandrabhanu Paswan. Stakes in Milkipur were raised by Ajit’s father Awadhesh Prasad’s win from Faizabad in LS polls. With SP looking to retain the seat, BJP sees the bypolls as a chance to avenge its Faizabad loss. — WITH PTI

I don’t think any other state offers the kind of facilities at business summits that I see in Bengal… Bengal is turning into a gateway of commerce to India.
