headline: ‘Where is Maharashtra politics headed?’: Why Sharad Pawar’s felicitation of Eknath Shinde has sparked unease
description: The Shiv Sena (UBT) has hit out at Sharad Pawar for honouring Eknath Shinde with the Mahadji Shinde Rashtriya Gaurav Award.
content:
NCP (SP) president Sharad Pawar’s decision to felicitate Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde at an event in Delhi this week has created ripples in state politics, sparking unease in the ruling Mahayuti alliance and the Opposition Maha Vikas Aghadi (MVA).
At a time when allies, the BJP and the NCP, are asserting their political camaraderie, Shinde seems to be mending fences on the outside. And with local body elections slated later this year, parties are keeping a close watch on the movements of their rivals – and their allies.
The Shiv Sena (UBT), for one, has hit out at Sharad Pawar for attending the Maharashtra Sahitya Sammelan and honouring Shinde with the Mahadji Shinde Rashtriya Gaurav Award.
“Where is Maharashtra politics headed? Pawar should have avoided sharing the same platform with Shinde. What is more appalling is he went on to award Shinde and honour him, which is very insulting to us. It has hurt the sentiments of Marathi people in Maharashtra,” Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut said.
At the event, in a subtle message to the BJP, Pawar generously praised Shinde’s leadership in Maharashtra from 2022 to 2024, saying, “Shinde has a good understanding of urban issues and has done good work in Mumbai, Navi Mumbai and Thane.”
On the other hand, Shinde underlined, “Pawar’s googlies are famous. But he has never bowled a googly at me, and I hope he never will.”
The bonhomie has not gone down well with the Shiv Sena (UBT). Unlike Pawar Senior, who is known for his inherent ability to reach out to his rivals with ease, the Shiv Sena (UBT) is reluctant to shed its rigidity when it comes to Shinde. The Uddhav Thackeray-led party has often publicly admonished Shinde as a “gaddar (betrayer)” for engineering the split in the party and dislodging the MVA government in the state.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
After its dismal performance in the Assembly elections last year, the cracks within the MVA were evident as both the Shiv Sena (UBT) and the Congress held each other responsible for the alliance’s poor show. In such a scenario, the Shiv Sena (UBT) and Thackeray have looked at Sharad Pawar to keep the Opposition bloc united and strong.
Therefore, Pawar’s display of proximity to Shinde has come as a rude shock to the Shiv Sena (UBT), especially at a time when Thackeray is confronting the biggest political challenge for his party — the upcoming local body elections, especially the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation polls. The undivided Shiv Sena has ruled the BMC for three decades, and Thackeray knows his party will have to hold its grounds to retain its identity on its home turf, Mumbai.
Ironically, the development, which has raised many eyebrows, saw Shinde, who had been sulking for a while, emerge happier for the first time since the BJP picked Devendra Fadnavis as the chief minister after the Mahayuti swept the Assembly elections last year.
For the last couple of weeks, Shinde has skipped cabinet meetings to express his displeasure over his party leaders not getting the Nashik and Raigad guardian minister’s posts. The government’s decision to appoint an IAS officer as the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation chairman by bypassing Shiv Sena minister Pratap Sarnaik has also upset the Shiv Sena, sparking murmurs of discontent at being sidelined. In another development, Shinde was not named as part of the State Disaster Management Authority even though his counterpart, Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar, was. Days later, the government tweaked the rules and included Shinde in the list.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
However, a senior BJP functionary, requesting anonymity, dismissed the clamour over the event. “In politics, there are no permanent friends or enemies. Why make a hue and cry over Pawar and Shinde coming together at a cultural event? While nobody underestimates Pawar’s googlies in politics, today, the fact is that the Mahayuti has a majority. Besides, leaders from rival parties can come together at events,” the BJP leader said.
The political landscape of Maharashtra has seen numerous such instances. In the past, the late Congress leader Vilasrao Deshmukh and the late BJP leader Gopinath Munde were known to be political rivals and friends.
In recent times, despite their sarcastic jibes at each other, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Sharad Pawar have shown how ideological differences do not come in the way of personal relations. Weeks after the split in his party, Pawar shared the dais with Modi at the Lokmanya Tilak National Award ceremony held in Pune in 2023. “It was just a cultural event. Why link it to politics?” NCP (SP) MP Amol Kolhe had quipped then.
Another NCP official said, “Politics is about perception and timing. Everything is not for polls and the vote bank. If Shinde finds solace in Pawar, why shouldn’t he reciprocate?”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
State BJP chief Chandrashekhar Bawankule said the BJP has nothing to fear. “If Pawar was praising Shinde’s leadership, it is welcome. It is likely Pawar was drawing a parallel between Shinde and Uddhav Thackeray’s leadership,” Bawankule said. Earlier, Pawar, in his biography, had expressed disappointment with Thackeray’s tenure as the chief minister, pointing out that he had only visited Mantralaya, the state headquarters, twice.

headline: CBI books 7 Chandigarh cops for abducting a dentist
description: The Supreme Court had directed the CBI to conduct a preliminary probe into the alleged abduction of Dr Mohit Dhawan by Chandigarh Police personnel to prevent him from appearing in court.
content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered an FIR against seven Chandigarh policemen for allegedly abducting a city-based dentist in 2022.
The FIR names then-Inspector Crime Branch Harinder Sekhon, Sub-Inspector Suresh Kumar, Assistant Sub-Inspector Ajmer Singh, Head Constable Anil Kumar, Constable Vikas Hooda, Constable Subhash, and Constable Neeraj Kumar.
They have been booked under Section 365 (kidnapping or abducting someone with intent to wrongfully and secretly confine them) read with Section 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Indian Penal Code. The FIR was registered nearly six months after the Supreme Court directed the CBI to conduct a preliminary probe into the alleged abduction of Dr Mohit Dhawan by Chandigarh Police personnel to prevent him from appearing in court.
According to the FIR, the CBI’s Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB) in Chandigarh registered a Preliminary Enquiry (PE) on August 29, 2024, against unknown Chandigarh Police officials and others, in compliance with a Supreme Court order dated August 6, 2024.

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'

The enquiry revealed that Dr Mohit Dhawan, a dentist, runs a clinic at his residence in Sector 21, Chandigarh, along with his wife, Dr Rosy Dhawan.
The investigation further found that Chandigarh Police had earlier registered FIR No. 76 in March 2018, FIR No. 75 in September 2020, and FIR No. 56 in October 2021 against Dr Dhawan at Sector 19 police station. In FIR No. 56, he was granted interim anticipatory bail on October 22, 2022, by an Additional Sessions Judge in Chandigarh. However, his anticipatory bail plea was rejected on November 16, 2021, in the same case. Subsequently, two arrest warrants were issued against him in December 2021 by the District Court in Sector 43, Chandigarh.
Dr Dhawan later moved the Punjab and Haryana High Court, seeking anticipatory bail in FIR No. 75 of 2020. On January 5, 2022, the High Court directed him to appear before the Magistrate at the District Court in Sector 43 on January 7, 2022, at 11 AM. However, according to a handwritten complaint filed by Dr Dhawan while in judicial custody, he was allegedly abducted near the District Court Complex entry gate by four Chandigarh Police officials—ASI Ajmer Singh, Head Constable Anil Kumar, Constable Vikas Hooda, and Constable Subhash—while he was on his way to appear before the Magistrate in compliance with the High Court order.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The CBI enquiry found that between 10:20 and 10:50 AM on January 7, 2022, these Crime Branch officials forcibly picked up Dr Dhawan near the District Court Complex entry gate in an i20 car registered in the name of Constable Vikas Hooda’s cousin.
On that day, Dr Dhawan was accompanied by Mithilesh Jha alias Modi, a domestic help at the residence of retired Punjab Jail Superintendent Paramjit Singh Sandhu, a friend of Dr Dhawan. Maluk Chand, a notary advocate, who had notarized documents submitted by Dr Dhawan in the Sector 43 court complex, was also examined during the enquiry.
According to the CBI, Paramjit Singh Sandhu and others confirmed that Dr Dhawan had indeed visited the court complex after 10 AM. After notarizing affidavits, he proceeded towards the court entry gate, where he was forcibly made to sit in the i20 car by the four accused policemen.
The CBI investigation also referenced a DDR (Daily Diary Report) No. 28, dated January 7, 2022, from the Sector 45 police post, which stated that Inspector Harinder Sekhon and his team apprehended Dr Dhawan at 6:32 PM from behind ISBT Sector 43 and took him to the Crime Branch office in Sector 11. The arrest memo was signed by Inspector Sekhon in the presence of SI Suresh Kumar and Constable Neeraj Kumar as witnesses.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On January 8, 2022, Dr Dhawan was remanded to seven days of police custody by a Judicial Magistrate in Chandigarh. After completing police custody on January 15, he was sent to Model Jail, Burail, Chandigarh, until February 4. He was released from judicial custody on February 5, 2022.
The CBI also found that call data record (CDR) analysis of Dr Dhawan’s mobile number confirmed his location at the Sector 43 court complex between 10:24 and 10:27 AM on January 7, 2022. He was later traced to Sector 44C between 12:50 PM and 5:24 PM. However, no calls were made from his phone between 10:30 AM (the alleged time of abduction) and 6:32 PM (the time of his reported apprehension).
Additionally, CDR analysis of the suspected Chandigarh Police officials’ mobile phones placed them in and around the Sector 43 District Court Complex during the relevant period on January 7, 2022, the CBI enquiry found.

headline: Capital-isation: The importance of Kapurthala House in Delhi
description: Recently, the ECI raided the Kapurthala House premises where Punjab CM Bhagwant Singh Mann was staying during the run up to the Delhi Assembly elections.
content:
The Kapurthala House, the official residence of the Punjab chief minister in New Delhi, has been in the news lately, following the Election Commission of India (ECI) raids and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor’s address to the Punjab party leaders there. Here’s a look at the House:
The property story
The Kapurthala House — house number 3 on Mansingh Road near Connaught Place in New Delhi — has been in the state government’s possession since 1950. It is allocated to the Punjab CM, for his visits to the Capital. It was the erstwhile residence of the Kapurthala maharaja in Delhi.
Why in the headlines
Recently, the ECI raided the Kapurthala House premises where Punjab CM Bhagwant Singh Mann was staying during the run up to the Delhi Assembly elections. The ECI’s flying surveillance team (FST) arrived at the Kapurthala House on January 31 for a raid, following a complaint of “money distribution” filed on poll body’s cVIGIL portal. On Tuesday, AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal held a meeting of the Punjab party leadership at the Kapurthala House. Prior to this, it came into the limelight in May 2023, when AAP Rajya Sabha member Raghav Chadha’s engagement ceremony with actor Parineeti Chopra was held there.
How Punjab govt took its possession
Kapurthala was a sovereign state until it merged with the Patiala and East Punjab States Union (PEPSU) and subsequently into the Dominion of India. The royal property was requisitioned through an order passed on June 17, 1950, under Section 3 of the Delhi Premises (Requisition and Acquisition) Act, 1947. On December 4, 1950, the Indian government took possession of the property from late Radheshyam Makhanilal Seksaria, who had purchased it from erstwhile Maharaja Paramjit Singh Bahadur, former Kapurthala ruler, by a registered sale deed dated January 10, 1950, for a consideration of Rs 1.5 lakh.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
Delhi gets its fourth woman CM: All about Rekha Gupta
State’s long overdrawn battle to retain possession
It was a 59-year-long legal battle for the state government to retain the property’s possession.
Seksaria filed a suit in 1960 for the declaration of his title to the property in a Delhi district court. Subsequently, it was transferred to the high court in 1967. During the suit’s pendency, Seskaria died and his four children were substituted as plaintiffs in their capacity as his legal representatives. In 1989, a single-judge of the HC decided in favour of the plaintiffs on the grounds that it had been derequisitioned by the Indian government in 1987 — on the expiry of 17 years, as mandated by the 1952 Act. The Punjab government had submitted an appeal later, and a division HC bench held that the plaintiffs had no right in the property.
What happened thereafter
Several appeals and applications followed through the years in the HC and the Supreme Court, with the now repealed RTI also being used by the petitioners to fight their case, which finally returned before a Delhi HC division bench. The bench, in 2019, dismissed the petitioner’s right to the property on the ground that the erstwhile Kapurthala ruler had no title to the property after its requisition. Hence, he could not have conferred valid title on the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioners.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
About the Capital residence
The construction of Kapurthala House began in 1603 and completed in 1611. The residence has 66 rooms and a floor area of 11,000 sq ft. It was built by the erstwhile maharajas of Kapurthala as their capital residence — inspired by the French Renaissance style of architecture.
The state of Kapurthala
The history of Kapurthala is linked to the Ahluwalia Dynasty — founded by Baba Jassa Singh Ahluwalia in 1718. The Kapurthala state extended from Jagraon to the Beas. The fortunes of the Kapurthala state fluctuated during the Anglo-Sikh Wars. Raja Randhir Singh restored much of the state’s fortune during the Great Mutiny of 1857.

headline: Massive raids on illegal immigration firms in Chandigarh, seven arrested
description: A raiding party seized 60 passports from a single agency.
content:
In a major crackdown on illegally operating immigration consultancies, the Chandigarh Police raided several firms accused of deceiving citizens with false promises of visas and overseas jobs and arrested seven persons, including two women. Two of those arrested were later bailed out.
The Chandigarh police released the following details of the agencies raided and the people arrested.
Police Station, Sector 3
• Milestone Immigration : FIR No. 11 under Section 24 of the Immigration Act and Section 223 BNS was registered against owner Anu Thakur for advertising work permits and construction visas for Dubai on Instagram without authorization. She was arrested, and her mobile phone was seized.
• Greenland Overseas Consultancy: FIR No. 12 under Section 223 BNS was registered against owner Alka Thakur for employing staff without mandatory police verification. She was arrested.
Police Station-17
• Abroad Plus Consultant: FIR No. 22 was registered against Raj Kumar alias Rajbir of Mohali under Section 24 of the Emigration Act.
• Immigration Consultancy Agency: FIR No. 23 was registered against Sagar Singh of Ferozepur under Section 24 of the Emigration Act.
• G.S. Visa Point Pvt. Ltd.: FIR No. 24 was registered against Gagandeep Singh of Sector 22, Chandigarh, under Section 24 of the Emigration Act.
Police Station-19
• Calgiri Overseas : FIR No. 12/25 under Sections 223 BNS and 24 of the Emigration Act was registered. Accused Harshdeep Singh of Ropar was arrested, and a laptop and entry register were seized.
Police Station-31
• FIR No. 38 under Sections 223 BNS and 24 of the Emigration Act was registered against Rupinder Singh of Rupnagar and Mohd Arif of Chandigarh. Both were arrested and later released on bail. Stamps of the company, a PAN card, and Aadhaar copies were seized.
Police Station-34
• Dream Future Consultant: FIR No. 21 was registered against owner Vikas Malhotra under Sections 223 BNS and 10, 24 of the Emigration Act. He was arrested.

• Veracity Overseas: FIR No. 23 was registered against owner Vinay Choudhary and others under similar sections.
Police Station-Maloya

• Satyam Immigration Services: FIR No. 21 under Section 24 of the Emigration Act and Section 223 BNS was registered against Rajveer Singh and Satyam Bhatnagar of Patiala. A raid led to the seizure of 60 passports, a CPU, and ₹2.6 lakh in cash. Rajveer Singh was apprehended.

headline: We deliver, you promise: Bengal CM contrasts state, Union budget
description: Mamata hits out at Sitharaman for her remarks on Bengal: ‘Biased, far from truth’
content:
Contrasting TMC government’s social welfare schemes with that of the BJP-led government at the Centre, West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Wednesday said while we deliver, the Union Budget only makes promises.
Addressing a press conference after the presentation of the Budget in Kolkata, the chief minister said: “On one hand, there is the Central budget. They promise only ahead of elections. Their budgets are based on elections. We don’t do that in our budget. Ours is based on what we say.”
Hitting out at the Centre for failing to release West Bengal’s share of funds for implementing welfare schemes, the CM said: “The Centre has failed to release Bengal’s legitimate dues. We have been struggling to receive our rightful funds… The Centre has stopped funding programmes such as MGNREGA and the Awas Yojna (housing scheme). There is no 100 days’ work (MGNREGA); rural road work has been stopped. Despite this, we have been given grants for building houses to 28 lakh families. We have already paid half the amount, and the rest will be paid in June.”
“The Central Budget contains only promises… We allocate funds from our own revenue, and what we say in our budget, we deliver,” she asserted.
“Our vision is very clear; it is to create more and more development,” she added.
Responding to Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman’s recent comments on Bengal, the TMC chief called them “biased” and “not based on facts.”
Sitharaman on Tuesday accused the TMC government of corruption and undermining institutions. “They should first fix their own corruption. They control the media and set the narrative. None of them speak the truth. Nirmala Ji, what happened to Ujjwala Yojna? You do nothing but give speeches. The BJP has bulldozed the federal structure.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Reflecting on the state’s achievements in her 14-year-long reign, she said, “I made the barren land fertile. 75% of the demand for onions is being produced locally. I have set up a research centre on hilsa fish, and now you see so much hilsa from the Ganga is available.”

headline: Booked in ‘fake & baseless FIR’: AAP MLA Amanatullah Khan writes to police chief
description: The alleged incident took place on Monday evening when a Crime Branch team was in Jamia Nagar to arrest one Shavez Khan in connection with an assault case.
content:
Booked for allegedly obstructing police officers from arresting an alleged proclaimed offender, AAP MLA-elect Amanatullah Khan on Wednesday wrote to Delhi Police Commissioner Sanjay Arora, claiming that a “fake and baseless FIR” has been lodged against him and sought a probe into the matter. This comes a day after police sources alleged that Amanatullah  was “unreachable”.
In a four-page letter, which was reportedly sent through email, the Okhla MLA-elect said he has been booked “without reasonable grounds or allegations”.
The alleged incident took place on Monday evening when a Crime Branch team was in Jamia Nagar to arrest one Shavez Khan in connection with an assault case.
The FIR, lodged on the basis of a complaint flied by the Crime Branch, stated when the policemen were questioning Shavez, Amanatullah Khan arrived with 20-25 people. “Amantullah said, ‘you don’t know who I am, I will get your uniform removed and it doesn’t matter to me if one more case is filed against me. I will finish you off and no one will find a witness to this and even if one finds one, I will take care of it myself’. Amanatullah and his companions pushed and grappled with us and got Shavez released and took him away,” it added.
In his letter to Arora, Amanatullah wrote, “On February 10… I was told that some people dressed in plain clothes, claiming to be police officers, were causing undue harassment and threats to Savez Khan. I was asked to save Shavez, who I was told was a resident of our area.”
Khan said he has no close connection with Shavez. “…I was informed… that Shavez being pressurised… He was granted anticipatory bail by Saket court (in the assault case) on July 30, 2018. In spite of (getting) anticipatory bail, the men in civilian clothes… were threatening him that they will arrest him and it will not be good if anybody interferes.”
“Being a respected member of the Legislative Assembly, it was my duty to ensure that nothing illegal should happen and hence, I sent a message to ensure that any action taken should be as per law. I was told that the people claiming to be police officers refused to identify themselves and threatened to implicate all of us in a false case,” he added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The MLA-elect wrote that after Shavez produced the court order that granted him anticipatory bail, the said police officers left. He claimed that while he wanted to get an FIR lodged against them, he was instead booked so that he could be stopped from reporting the “illegality”.
Meanwhile, Shavez on Wednesday released a purported video on his social media account stating that he had “already recorded his statement before the court” and had been granted “bail”.
The police, however, maintained that he had not been granted bail in the case. When contacted, a senior police officer said multiple teams were looking for Shavez. The teams were also in the process to reach out to Amanatullah, the officer added.

headline: AAP’s Kuldeep Dhalor questions ‘absence’ of civic funds for Chandigarh; Mayor Babla assures smooth functioning
description: During official meetings, committees have different financial powers to clear an amount for agendas. However, the CMC must be finding it difficult to clear and implement development agendas at a time when it fails to give salary to its employees, he stated.
content:
Raising concerns about the recent formation of 12 sub-committees of the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation (CMC) — after a gap of three years — AAP councillor and former mayor Kuldeep Dhalor said that the civic body is likely to face difficulties in functioning smoothly in the “absence” of funds.
“Amid shortage of funds, how will the committees function and consent agendas?” he asked.
During official meetings, committees have different financial powers to clear an amount for agendas. However, the CMC must be finding it difficult to clear and implement development agendas at a time when it fails to give salary to its employees, he stated.
The CMC is under a severe financial crisis — with the last grant in aid instalment of Rs 33 crore, which would partially meet its liabilities for February.
“When I was the mayor, I saw shortage of funds, and had raised the issue too. Though funds were not released during my tenure, it should be released now for the development of the city, and to tackle other financial issues,” Dhalor said.
Reacting to this, current Mayor Harpreet Kaur Babla, however, said he was “hopeful of receiving a grant” from the Chandigarh administrator. “We have a good budget — more than the last year’s. We are trying our best to discuss things with UT administrator Gulab Chand Kataria.”
Babla further said that the 12 sub-committees have been formed with an aim to manage small agendas of Rs 4-6 lakh. “Panel meetings will be held once a month. I will let everyone be in the panels — have given chairmanship to Congress and AAP members — so that a balance could be maintained. These chairpersons will be called for the meetings soon, to address the issues and development of the city,” Babla said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The 12 sub-committees comprise three statutory panels — roads, water supply and sewerage disposal, and house tax assessment. The remaining nine are that of sanitation, electricity, women empowerment, enforcement, environment & city beautification, fire & emergency services, apni mandi & day market, slum colonies & village development, and art, culture & sports. The statutory panels have a financial power of Rs 25-lakh each, while the remaining nine will be authorised to handle work of Rs 15-lakh each.
The Finance and Contract Committee (F&CC), with an authority of Rs 50 lakh, plays a pivotal role in the decision-making.
Meanwhile, praising Babla for setting up these committees within the first month of her being the Mayor, Congress councillor Gurpreet Singh Gabi said: “I congratulate the Mayor (Harpreet Kaur Babla) for forming these committees. At least, the committees are formed. About the financial crunch, Chandigarh MP Manish Tewari is also trying to get Rs 200-crore funds for the municipal corporation.”

headline: 15 years on: Strength, scars and survival after the German Bakery blast
description: Time may not have erased the scars but it has helped the survivors become stronger, tackle adverse situations with resilience and deepen their gratitude.
content:
Fifteen years have passed since the devastating German bakery blast that changed several lives in an instant. Time may not have erased the scars but it has helped the survivors become stronger, tackle adverse situations with resilience and deepen their gratitude.
For Sumeet Singh (40), who is a General Counsel and on the Board of Directors of fintech company BharatPe, it is about taking a pause and being grateful. He credits the mental strength that he developed from surviving a blast to overcoming challenges at the workplace. “The experience has made me mentally tough and in turn, helped me develop resilience in the face of adversity,” Singh recalled.
On the day of the blast (Feb 13), Singh was meeting four of his friends at the bakery for a quick snack before heading for the Symbiosis College festival at Koregaon Park. They were about to leave when the blast took place and the next two months, Singh was in trauma care undergoing treatment for high-degree burns and splinter injuries on his hands and legs. The ringing sound in his left ear has also been a constant but Singh prefers not to dwell on it any more. “Our bodies are so strong and adaptable,” says Singh.
A month ago, when he stopped his car briefly outside the German bakery while on a short trip to Pune, Singh admits that he did not feel like going inside. This February, Singh and his wife Yamini Chawla decided to celebrate their sevebth wedding anniversary by offering prayers at Ujjain’s Mahakal temple. “I was fortunate to be given a second chance at life and I am deeply grateful,” Singh added.

‘Still avoid taking North Main Road as far as possible’
Shrikrishna Thapa (47), another survivor who is a captain at Malaka Spice, one of the popular fine-dine restaurants in the city, admits that till date, he avoids taking the North Main Road at Koregaon Park where the bakery is located.
“It is 15 years since the incident but that memory is still fresh. I was working as a cashier and would also make sandwiches at the German bakery where I worked from 1997-2010. It was a fun place to be at where work never felt like work. During Christmas and New Year celebrations, the place would be packed with people singing and playing their guitars, creating a lively and joyful atmosphere. It always felt more like a place of enjoyment than a job,” recalls Thapa until February 13, when the blast killed 17 people and left 56 others injured.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Sumeet Singh and wife Yamini Chawla. On the day of the blast (Feb 13), Singh was meeting four of his friends at the bakery for a quick snack before heading for the Symbiosis College festival at Koregaon Park.
“I had just completed my work and was leaving the place when the blast occurred. I was flung to one side and was unconscious. Later all I could see was smoke, bodies with no legs, hands. It was horrible. I had 30 per cent burns and still remember telling the ambulance driver to first assist those who were severely injured. Later, with a few people I walked towards Inlaks and Budhrani hospital for treatment,” said Thapa who now lives with his family at Yerawada and works in Kharadi.
‘My heart skips a beat when I hear the name Pune’
Rajeev Agarwala tragically did not survive. His sister Radhika, who is based in Kolkata, admits that even hearing Pune’s name makes her heart skip a beat. Rajeev Agarwala was among the top five bright students at Symbiosis Law College and was in his final year when he went to the German Bakery with his friends and died in the blast.
Shrikrishna Thapa (47), another survivor who is a captain at Malaka Spice, one of the popular fine-dine restaurants in the city.
Radhika, who works as a company secretary at a public limited firm in Kolkata, remembered how a month before the incident, he had spoken at length with her and said that he would always be there for her. “That year, I had to take the CS examination and I remember Rajeev telling my mother not to get so worked up as I would clear the examination. He had amazing confidence in me and I cleared the exam. 15 years on, my brother continues to be with us. My elder brother Ravi and I have set up a Rajeev Agarwal memorial trust and have planned some activities in his memory,” Radhika said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
She however added that while she has not been to Pune in a while, her heart skipped a beat when her husband mentioned that he had to travel to the city.
After a hectic day, while heading back from Inlaks and Budhrani hospital, noted plastic and cosmetic surgeon Dr Sumit Saxena got an emergency call and amid the mayhem was provided a green corridor. (Express Photo)
‘Patients come and go but these left memories’
After a hectic day, while heading back from Inlaks and Budhrani hospital, noted plastic and cosmetic surgeon Dr Sumit Saxena got an emergency call and amid the mayhem was provided a green corridor. “We had the maximum number of patients due to the proximity of the hospital to the German bakery,” Dr Saxena recalled.
Patients were being wheeled into the emergency room, limbs had to be amputated to save lives, bleeding had to be stopped, injuries had to be catered to. The blood bank was getting exhausted and for Dr Saxena, months of work had just begun.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Patients come and go but these left memories, a myriad of them. Among these was the only daughter of my senior from Ludhiana. She was very critical. Despite the best of our efforts, we were not able to save her. It struck me hard and it still hurts. Then there was the chef of the bakery. He had burnt his whole face. With proper handling of skin and care for a few months, the skin was to have whitening and anti-aging effects. True to my conviction, he looked much more youthful and fairer than he was,” said the surgeon.
“Another woman underwent multiple reconstructive surgeries and later cosmetic procedures, including laser, peels and dimple creation. She ended up becoming a motivational speaker, acted in some movies and got involved in social welfare activities,” Dr Saxena said, adding that like every year, he still gets a call to attend the lamp lighting ceremony near German Bakery. “I attended a few and missed many but the light always remained ignited. The patient’s scars might have healed. As for mine, I am not sure though,” added Dr Saxena.

headline: Minor among 16 illegal immigrants deported to Bangladesh: Police
description: The remaining 48 illegal immigrants included 31 men, 13 women and four children. They were detained at Gujarat's second Joint Interrogation Centre (JIC) in Ahmedabad.
content:
A TOTAL of 16 illegal immigrants, including a minor, who were residing in Chandola lake area of Ahmedabad, were deported to their home country Bangladesh, said the Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) of Ahmedabad City Police on Wednesday.
Notably, the deported immigrants were among 53 Bangladeshi nationals who were detained by the Crime Branch on October 25 last year for living illegally in Ahmedabad. Of them, five were also involved in two cases — one related to forgery and the second pertaining to trafficking of women from India’s eastern border.
The remaining 48 illegal immigrants included 31 men, 13 women and four children. They were detained at Gujarat’s second Joint Interrogation Centre (JIC) in Ahmedabad.
Harsh Sanghavi, Gujarat’s MoS for Home, in a post on X, said: “Ahmedabad Crime Branch Cracks Down on Anti-National Activities! Successfully deported 15 immigrants to Bangladesh. Identified and arrested persons involved in trafficking minor girls for prostitution. Busted a racket producing fake Indian documents for illegal immigrants. Detained 50 illegal immigrants during combing operation. Successfully deported 15 immigrants and 1 minor child. Ongoing legal process for deportation of remaining immigrants.”
An official of the Crime Branch said: “The Crime Branch identified and arrested people involved in trafficking of minor girls for prostitution. On further investigation, a racket, which used to produce fake Indian documents to illegal immigrants, was also busted. Subsequently, during the combing operation, 50 illegal immigrants were detained. Of those, 16 immigrants, including a child, have been successfully deported. As for deportation of others, a legal process is under way.”

headline: Maharashtra invites developers to build on MSRTC land, plans to upgrade ST depots to airport level
description: The state will soon issue nearly 150 tenders for these projects, Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik announced at the NAREDCO NextGen Conclave 2025 in Mumbai on Wednesday.
content:
The Maharashtra government has invited real estate developers to participate in projects on 3,360 acres of land owned by the Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC). These land parcels will be developed under public-private partnership (PPP) models on a build-operate-transfer basis.
The state will soon issue nearly 150 tenders for these projects, Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik announced at the NAREDCO NextGen Conclave 2025 in Mumbai on Wednesday.
MSRTC owns 26 acres in prime locations across the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR), including Mumbai Central, Kurla, Vidyavihar and Chinchbunder. Additionally, it has nearly 24 acres in Pune, with key plots in Swargate and Sangvi. Beyond these urban centres, MSRTC holds 885 acres in district areas, 1,535 acres in talukas, and 945 acres in villages.
The projects will be awarded based on the premium offered by developers, with the floor space index (FSI) allotted according to the Unified Development Control and Promotion Regulations (UDCPR). Developers will be responsible for leasing out the commercial portions of these projects.
The plan includes developing commercial properties such as offices, hotels, shopping centres, and retail spaces. Additionally, 100-bed hospitals will be constructed at district-level sites, along with facilities for MSRTC operations.
Sarnaik spoke at the annual conclave as the keynote speaker addressing all the young entrepreneurs in the real estate sector. “We have plans to improve facilities for passengers and employees, right from clean toilets for everyone, sanitation for women and amenities for night-shift staff. As the planning authority, it will monitor approvals under one roof. With help of architect Hafeez Contractor, the goal is to upgrade ST depots to airport standards,” said Sarnaik.
Architect Hafeez Contractor has been appointed by the government to prepare a presentation outlining the development framework for the bus depots.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
To streamline the process, MSRTC will sanction development plans centrally, reducing the need for multiple approvals from various government agencies. The corporation is also enhancing the capacity of its technical teams to oversee the projects effectively.

headline: Bengaluru Metro fare hike: Tejasvi Surya calls for new fixation committee, urges govt to write to Centre
description: BJP MP Tejasvi Surya criticises the fare fixation committee, appointed by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, for failing to understand ‘the socio-economic status of people who use’ Bengaluru Metro.
content:
A day after Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah blamed a centrally appointed fare fixation committee’s recommendations for Bengaluru Metro’s fare hike, BJP MP Tejasvi Surya has urged the Congress government to write to the Centre seeking a new panel to review the “unscientific” fare revision.
“I have met the Union urban affairs minister on the metro fare hike and explained that the current ticket prices of Bengaluru Metro are the most expensive in the country, making them unsustainable for the middle and low income groups. The ridership of the metro has come down following the price hike, increasing the ridership of BMTC buses and bringing out more private vehicles on the road,” the Bangalore South MP told reporters on Wednesday.
He said the metro must be encouraged as an affordable public transport model to resolve the city’s traffic chaos, adding that the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs had assured its support for a revision of the fares. “I urge the Karnataka government to seek a review of the fare structure and reduce this burden on the middle class and the poor of Bengaluru,” he said.
Surya further said, “The fare fixation committee that came up with this unscientific proposal to raise metro prices reportedly went on a study tour to Singapore and Hong Kong at taxpayers’ expense. They would have served Bengaluru better had they gone to Singasandra or Hongasandra instead and understood the socio-economic status of people who use the metro in Bengaluru.”
Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) revised fares on February 9, pushing the ticket prices by more than 50 per cent, following the recommendations made by the fare fixation committee. With a maximum fare of Rs 90, Bengaluru now has the costliest metro in India.
The fare hike—amounting to 89-100 per cent in some cases—has attracted significant public backlash and the metro has recorded a dip of 4 per cent, or 30,000 rides.
Maheshwara Rao, Managing Director, BMRCL, said the corporation would review the fare hike. “We are aware of the public feedback on the revised metro fares. We are taking in the criticisms constructively. Since certain fare slabs have seen a significant increase, we will review them and plug the anomalies, if any,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Meanwhile, Siddaramaiah accused the Opposition BJP of misleading the public. “The @BJP4Karnataka leaders, who are now opposing the fare hike, are once again spreading false and misleading information to blame the Karnataka Government and mislead the public. People have the right to question and oppose any government policy—this is their constitutional right, and I respect that,” he wrote on social media.
He added, “However, the state BJP, which the people have placed in the opposition, is deliberately spreading falsehoods for political gain and fueling public outrage with misinformation. The same BJP leaders who take credit for Bengaluru Metro’s expansion as the Centre’s achievement are now shifting the blame onto the Karnataka Government when there is public anger over the fare hike. This is nothing but self-deception and hypocrisy.”
Defending the fare hike, BMRCL has said the hike was necessary to cover significant financial obligations, particularly loan repayments, which amount to Rs 500-800 crore annually. These payments include interest on borrowed funds and investments made to expand and upgrade the metro network. The revised project costs and ongoing infrastructure developments, such as additional trains and station improvements, further contribute to these financial commitments.
BMRCL had not revised fares since June 2017, when phase 1 (42.3 km) was completed. However, phase 2 is partially complete and the metro network has expanded beyond 42.3 km. By December 2026, metro lines 2, 2A and 2B (96.6 km) are expected to be completed, expanding the network to 175.55 km, necessitating more financial support.

headline: Country’s first vertical lift span Pamban bridge likely to open in March
description: R Srinivasan, deputy general manager, RVNL, said the construction of the new bridge began in February 2019. “The old bridge was closed in December 2022 due to its deteriorating condition.
content:
The newly built Pamban sea bridge, connecting Rameswaram on Pamban Island with Tamil Nadu’s Mandapam town in mainland India, is ready and is expected to be inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in March. The new bridge has been built parallel to the old Pamban Bridge, India’s first sea bridge which was opened in 1914. The new bridge will replace the old structure.
The Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd (RVNL) has built the 2.10-km-long bridge. The new sea bridge is the country’s first ‘vertical lift span’ bridge, featuring a ‘vertical lift span’ of 72.5 metres in the middle, which can lift upwards upwards 17 metres in 5 minutes, 30 seconds to allow ships to pass under it.
The old bridge, on the other hand, was a cantilever bridge. It was opened manually, requiring 14 people for its operation. In contrast, the new bridge is fully automatic.
R Srinivasan, deputy general manager, RVNL, said the construction of the new bridge began in February 2019. “The old bridge was closed in December 2022 due to its deteriorating condition. The new bridge was originally planned for completion in three years, but work was delayed due to Covid-19. The bridge was completed in November 2024, and train trials have successfully been conducted. After successful trials, the Commissioner of Railway Safety granted approval to run trains. Now, the only thing left is the inauguration of this bridge.”
The design of the new bridge was prepared by a Spain-based company. It is a single-track bridge. The old bridge allowed diesel trains to travel at 10 kmph. The new bridge, however, is fully electrified, which will allow trains to operate on 25,000 volt through overhead wires (OHE). The speed limit on the new bridge is 75 kmph, although trains will slow down to 50 kmph at navigational span stretch.

headline: Seven months later, still no sanitary pads vending machine at new airport terminal
description: The Emergency Medical Room (EMR), which was inaugurated in August last year to enhance passenger safety and is operated 24/7 by Ruby Hall Clinic, was expected to provide essential medical assistance.
content:
It’s been more than seven months since the Pune International Airport’s (PIA) New Terminal Integrated Building became operational, yet there are still no sanitary napkin vending machines or incinerators available for women passengers. This has led to disappointment among women passengers, who feel their basic hygiene needs are being neglected.
In 2018, the Airports Authority of India (AAI) announced plans to install vending machines at 125 airports across the country. Some airports have even been providing sanitary napkins free of charge, in collaboration with NGOs. It was also decided that a woman attendant would be stationed near the vending machines to provide guidelines.
However, an official from Pune Airport said that the old terminal, which currently handles only 20 percent of the airport’s operations, has nearly 18 to 20 sanitary napkins vending and dispensing machines. The new terminal, on the other hand, is expected to have these facilities available in the coming days.
The Airports Authority of India (AAI) issued an Expression of Interest (EOI) on May 6, 2024, inviting service providers for the operation and maintenance of sanitary pad vending machines and an incinerator at Pune Airport. The initiative aims to install 22 vending machines (19 operational, 3 in reserve) and ensure free sanitary pad availability for passengers. However, as of now, passengers continue to face issues due to the lack of functional machines, highlighting a gap between policy and on-ground implementation.
Women passengers and cleaning staff have expressed disappointment over the lack of hygiene facilities, health provisions, and the unavailability of basic needs for women at the airport’s new terminal.
A cleaning staff member at Pune airport, when asked about the availability of sanitary pads in the new terminal, said there are currently no pads available inside the terminal. “There were machines installed at the old terminal, but women often complain about the non-functioning vending machines there as well,” she said.
Raveena Katkar, who landed at Pune airport at 4.30 am, needed a sanitary napkin unexpectedly. She told The Indian Express that she searched for pads in bathrooms on the ground floor and even enquired to the cleaning staff there but didn’t find any. “Since I am not from Pune, I had to travel by cab for over four to five hours to reach home, and no pharmacy was open that early in the morning,” she said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Swananda Dhananjay Tatke, a 62-year-old woman travelling from Pune to Chennai on January 30 said that while she may not need sanitary pads at this age, the absence of the vending machines is noticed by all women.
The Emergency Medical Room (EMR), which was inaugurated in August last year to enhance passenger safety and is operated 24/7 by Ruby Hall Clinic, was expected to provide essential medical assistance. However, women passengers reported that when they approached the EMR, they were informed that sanitary napkins were unavailable.
Alice Barwa said that while she was travelling from Pune to Raipur a few times back, she realised that she got her periods and when checked the washroom near Zone 1 bathroom, there was no Sanitary Pad Dispenser. She said that since she found no pharmacy in the airport, she could not buy a packet either.
“I asked about it from the workers, who said that currently there is no dispenser unlike the washrooms in the old terminal. She said that if I urgently need one, they can send someone outside to get a pad. I asked if they had one in their staff room but they didn’t. I asked staff near the boarding check-in if pads are available in the Emergency Medical room (EMR) but they said no. Only a doctor would be available if I need it in case of an emergency such as pain,” Barwa added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Pune Airport director Santosh Dhoke said that the old terminal already has this service, and the process for the new terminal is underway. “Soon, every ladies toilet will have a vending machine. Nearly 20 vending and dispensing machines will be available in the coming days.”
When asked about the medical shop at the airport in relation to the napkins, he explained that if there are no customers, there’s no reason to open the pharmacy. Operating it requires both financial resources and staff. “The bare minimum needed for passengers is already available at the airport,” he said.

headline: AI dangerous tool, be it in Chinese or American hands: Delhi HC on plea to ban DeepSeek
description: The court's observation came while it was hearing a petition seeking a direction to the Centre to block access to DeepSeek, an AI chatbot developed by Chinese entities, in all forms in India.
content:
The Delhi High Court observed on Wednesday that artificial intelligence is a “dangerous tool” in anybody’s hand, whether Chinese or American.
The court’s observation came while it was hearing a petition seeking a direction to the Centre to block access to DeepSeek, an AI chatbot developed by Chinese entities, in all forms in India.
“AI is a dangerous tool in anybody’s hand, whether it is Chinese or American, it does not make any difference. It is not that the government is unaware of these things. They are very well aware…,” a bench of Chief Justice D K Upadhyaya and Justice Tushar Rao Gedela said.
The Centre’s counsel submitted that the issue requires consideration and urged the court to grant some time to get instructions in the matter.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
The court listed the matter for February 20 to enable the Centre’s counsel to get complete instructions.
The petitioner’s counsel urged the court to issue notices to authorities in the matter and said it pertains to a direct infringement of the right to privacy.
Also Read | DeepSeek’s AI model is the ‘best work to come out of China’: Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis
To this, Justice Gedela said, “You are in the dark web 97 per cent. What are you saying? You are next generation youngsters. You know about it more than us. You think this data, any data is safe? Are you aware of the dark web? Are you aware that 97 per cent of the iceberg is tilted around? Are you aware of that? So therefore, they are saying consideration. We are giving them an opportunity, please wait.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Petitioner Bhavna Sharma, a lawyer, said the plea seeks to protect the personal data of citizens as well as the data in government systems and devices from cyber attacks and data breaches, and uphold the confidentiality of government data and documents.
The plea said within a month of the DeepSeek application’s launch on play stores, various vulnerabilities were discovered in it, causing a large-scale leak of sensitive personal data online, including chat history, back-end data and log streams.

headline: The sound of ‘Ubuntu’: African rhythms and Indian traditions unite at Ruhaniyat festival in Pune
description: If you are in Pune, don't miss the performance by Dumza Maswana and Volley Nchabeleng at the Ruhaniyat festival on February 15.
content:
It was from Archbishop Desmond Tutu, the anti-apartheid activist and Nobel Laureate from South Africa, that most people in other countries first heard the term Ubuntu, signifying an African philosophy that is difficult to translate into a Western language.
Ubuntu refers to an intricate interrelationship of a person with others. One of the highlights of the Ruhaniyat festival in Pune’s Empress Garden on February 15 is ‘Ubuntu: The Spirit of Togetherness’ by musicians Dumza Maswana and Volley Nchabeleng.
Maswana says that Ubuntu is at the heart of African culture. “Despite our diverse backgrounds and traditions, Ubuntu unites us. For Volley and me, who come from different places and ethnic groups, music and Ubuntu have become the threads that weave us together. That’s one common value we also noted in India,” he says.
Nchabeleng adds that theirs is a collaborative performance that merges the sounds from the Northern province of South Africa and the Western Cape province. “Dumza is known as an Afro Jazz artist, and I am a percussionist and specialist in African indigenous instruments. Together, we encourage unity and peace,” says Nchabeleng.
Ruhaniyat, organised by Banyan Tree Events of Mumbai, is a music festival that draws from the treasure trove of works of saints, mystics and spiritual traditions worldwide. Most of these count as “intangible cultural heritage” that have been passed orally through generations and over millenniums. The line-up at this year’s Ruhaniyat in Pune includes Sivasri Skandaprasad, a versatile personality whose achievements include proficiency in Carnatic music and Bharatanatyam.
In January 2024, Prime Minister Narendra Modi posted on X that a rendition by Sivasri “beautifully highlights the spirit of devotion to Prabhu Shri Ram. Such efforts go a long way in preserving our rich cultural heritage”.
Another renowned artist at Ruhaniyat is Mir Mukhtiyar Ali, a folk and Sufi vocalist from the semi-nomadic Mirasi community of Rajasthan. Singer Nandesh Umap invokes the feminine force through his performance, while the Nizami brothers bring their quintessential qawwali to Pune.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The African troupe has been listening to some of this music on their travels in the country. Maswana and Nchabeleng have been visiting India for the past few years.
“The experience is always the same – warm, welcoming and friendly. It will be my first performance in Pune, though,” he says.
Musician Volley Nchabeleng.
Nchabeleng grew up in a musical family so it is not easy to tell when he started playing. In 2000, he decided to become a professional musician. “The colonialism and oppression that South Africa experienced, has affected the value of our indigenous musical instruments and music in general. I try my best to be an ambassador of African instruments,” he says.
Maswana, too, started performing at a very young age, at his grandmother’s hut. “She taught me to sing, dance and tell stories, and the importance of it all. I never studied music formally, but learning from elders and artists who loved and respected the craft is a blessing,” he says.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“I’m thrilled to be performing in India, as it presents a fantastic opportunity to collaborate with local artists. This aligns perfectly with the spirit of the Ruhaniyat festival, which celebrates creative exchange and collaboration. For every show, we share ideas and create something special and memorable for the audience,” says Maswana.

headline: One more traffic arm of coastal road opens: Vehicles towards Marine Drive from Haji Ali can now enter coastal road directly
description: Prior to this, south-bound vehicles would enter the coastal road either from the Worli interchange or the Amarson’s interchange apart from the direct connectivity that is provided via the Bandra Worli Sea Link (BWSL).
content:
One more traffic arm of Mumbai Coastal Road at the Haji Ali traffic interchange was opened on Wednesday morning. This traffic arm will allow vehicles travelling towards Marine Drive to directly enter the coastal road and ply on the southbound carriageway of the high-speed connector.
Prior to this, south-bound vehicles would enter the coastal road either from the Worli interchange or the Amarson’s interchange apart from the direct connectivity that is provided via the Bandra Worli Sea Link (BWSL). The Haji Ali interchange comprises eight vehicular arms, which is followed by the Amarson’s and Worli interchange comprising four five and four arms each. After this, only one arm awaits opening at the Worli interchange that would provide direct connectivity towards the BWSL to northbound vehicles coming from Worli.
“The arms of the interchanges were being opened in a phased manner since the balance works like evening the road surfaces were underway. Now only one arm remains, which will be opened by us in the next one month,” said a civic official.
“We also had to construct vehicular parking spaces for the traffic arms, as a result of which the opening of these arms took some time,” the official added. Prior to this, vehicular arms at the Haji Ali interchange were opened in December 2024.
Meanwhile, in January 2025, the BMC opened the linking bow-string arch bridge that connects the BWSL with the coastal road. Built at a cost of Rs 13,000 crore, the 10.58 km high-speed corridor has brought down travel time to less than 10 minutes, earlier when it used to take nearly an hour.

headline: Bombay HC allows Adani plea for felling of mangroves for electricity transmission near Vasai creek
description: In October, last year, the Divisional Forest Officer, Mangroves Division, North Konkan issued a demand notice to the petitioner to deposit Rs. 6.77 lakh as cost of plantation of mangroves (compensatory afforestation) in 1:5 ratio, which the firm deposited.
content:
Maintaining that the electricity transmission line near Vasai creek “shall benefit electricity consumers in Mumbai and its suburbs leading to the potential growth of the city,” the Bombay High Court last week allowed Adani Electricity Mumbai Infra Ltd to fell 209 mangroves for the project.
A bench of Chief Justice Alok Aradhe and Justice Bharati H Dangre passed an order on February 6, copy of which was made available on Monday night.
The Adani electricity appointed as Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) to implement the project had approached the HC seeking direction to authorities to permit it to execute the project involving 80-kilometres stretch consisting of 50 kilometres of High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) line and 50 kilometre of HVDC underground cable in the mangrove area.
Senior advocate Vikram Nankani for the petitioner submitted that of the 80-km line only 1 kilometre passes through areas having mangrove presence and 2.22 km of the transmission line falls in the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ). The line is  proposed to be laid at the depth of 20 metres below the ground using horizontal directional drilling (HDD) and duct bank trenches method across the Vasai Creek.
As per the inspection, the project involved felling of 209 mangroves including 144 located in Mumbai Mangroves Conservation Unit (MMCU) and 64 mangroves are located in Sanjay Gandhi National Park (SGNP) forest division. The petitioner firm obtained an Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) and Environment Management Plan (EMP) for the HDVC project.
Subsequent clearances and recommendations were given by the Maharashtra Coastal Zone Management Authority (MCZMA) and  Ministry of Environment, Forests and Climate Change (MoEFCC).
In October, last year, the Divisional Forest Officer, Mangroves Division, North Konkan issued a demand notice to the petitioner to deposit Rs. 6.77 lakh as cost of plantation of mangroves (compensatory afforestation) in 1:5 ratio, which the firm deposited.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Thereafter, required approvals were obtained from authorities including Eco Sensitive Zone Monitoring Committee of SGNP, Mangrove conservation cell and National Board for Wildlife (NBWL) and the plea was moved in HC seeking its nod for felling of 209 mangroves.
Nankani argued that the project was critical for Mumbai as existing capacity of the transmission corridor is not sufficient to carry further power into the city and the petitioner has availed all statutory permissions and is required to commence the project by March 21, 2025.
NGO Bombay Environmental Action Group (BEAG) opposed the plea stating that there was inconsistency in mangroves to be cut. It said while MCZMA meeting had indicated 79 mangroves to be cut, the petitioner sought felling of 209 of them.
The bench considered ‘public importance at large’ of the proposed project and necessary approvals availed by the petitioner firm from authorities and found it “appropriate to confer the desired permission.

headline: Summoned by Mumbai police over the Ranveer Allahbadia row, who are Ashish Chanchlani and Apoorva Mukhija?
description: The two were among the five artists summoned by Mumbai Police in the wake of podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia’s controversial question on the show ‘India’s Got Latent’.
content:
After YouTuber Ashish Chanchlani recorded his statement with Mumbai Police Tuesday in connection with the inquiry into podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia’s controversial question on the show ‘India’s Got Latent’, content creator Apoorva Mukhija also reached Khar police station on Wednesday to record her statement.
The three were among the five artists summoned by Mumbai Police on Tuesday over the incident. The others are Samay Raina, who organised and hosted the show, and content creator Jaspreet Singh.
All five were on the panel of the reality show ‘India’s Got Latent’, which saw Allahbadia asking a contestant a controversial question, leading to an uproar on social media followed by two FIRs – first by Assam Police and then by Maharashtra Cyber Police.
Who is Ashish Chanchlani?
Hailing from Ulhasnagar, located 26 km from Thane City, Ashish Chanchlani is a civil engineer by education and a YouTuber and actor by profession. He started uploading short comic videos in December 2014. In his career spanning 10 years, he has reviewed movies and shows, and created short format comedy videos on various subjects, before moving to a longer, story-based video format.

Apoorva Mukhija is a Mumbai-based social media influencer and content creator popularly known by her username ‘The Rebel Kid’ or her description ‘Kaleshi Aurat’. A computer science engineer by education, the 23-year-old is known for her mini vlogs, rant videos and skits.

She gained recognition during the Covid-19 pandemic when she started sharing her unfiltered commentary on everyday life on Instagram. Today, she has over 2.7 million followers on Instagram and half a million on YouTube. In 2023, she made her acting debut with the web series ‘Who’s Your Gynac’ and more recently, she was seen in the Terribly Tiny Tales series, ‘Baat Pakki’.

headline: How Noida family fell prey to 5-day digital arrest and lost Rs 1 crore
description: The accused “informed” Paliwal that a bank account had been opened in his name to launder money
content:
As always, it started with a phone call.
On February 1, a man called 73-year-old Chander Bhan Paliwal, a resident of Noida, saying that he was calling from the Colaba police station in Mumbai. “Contact TRAI (the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India) urgently or your phone will be switched off permanently within the next two hours,” he threatened Paliwal, who did as instructed.
Over the next five days, Paliwal, his wife and their daughter, who live in a three-storey house they own in Sector 19, were placed under “cyber arrest” and forced to transfer over Rs 1 crore to different bank accounts. On February 6, the septuagenarian approached the Noida Cyber Police for help.

Noida Deputy Commissioner of Police (Cyber Crime) Preeti Yadav said Paliwal, a retired insurance official, arrived at the police station around 3 pm to get an FIR registered. “He told us that a group of unknown fraudsters had forced him to transfer Rs 1.1 crore from his account to theirs,’’ she said.
The police went on to register a case of extortion and cheating under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act.
In his complaint, Paliwal said that nearly 10 minutes after he received the first call around 2.50 pm on February 1, a “senior police officer” called him. “He said he was an IPS officer with the Greater Mumbai Police. He claimed that there were 24 cases against me, including a case of money laundering. He claimed to be the investigating officer in the case,” he added.
Also Read | Of 30 Punjabis deported from US, 14 reveal names of their agents; only two deportees are graduates: Prelim data
The accused “informed” Paliwal that a bank account had been opened in his name to launder money. “He said a few complainants had received a call from a number issued against my Aadhaar Card and that they had been tricked into depositing money into the account. He said a warrant had been issued in my name, and that I would be arrested and presented before the Mumbai Cyber Crime cell,” Paliwal told the police.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Next, the police said, Paliwal was asked to show his Aadhaar Card “for verification” over a WhatsApp video call. “I was trembling as I sent them a photo of my Aadhaar Card. They also asked me for details of my personal bank accounts, which I supplied,” the complaint said.
Also Read | ‘If your Budget is so good, why are Indians leaving country?’: Opposition lashes out at Govt in Parliament over US deportation
“They said that an initial investigation report had been sent to the CBI and that senior CBI officers would now investigate the case. Another imposter joined the ongoing video call to say that it would be impossible for a man my age to stay in jail… One of the imposters then confirmed that (Paliwal’s) Aadhaar Card had been used to launder money and that the case would now go to the CBI court,” it added.
A series of video calls from various numbers continued over the next few days, police said, quoting Paliwal. “Next, the imposters posed as CBI officers and told me that my case would be heard in a CBI court on February 3. They asked me for my wife and daughter’s contact details. They also warned me against answering any other call and sharing information about their calls with others since my case was linked to Naresh Goyal’s case,” Paliwal said in his complaint.
The Enforcement Directorate had arrested Jet Airways founder Naresh Goyal on September 1, 2023, on charges of money laundering.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Also Read | In proposed immigration law: Tougher rules & specific roles
On February 2, 2024, the police said, the fraudsters warned Paliwal that his family would be arrested and put in different jails in Mumbai. “…They (wife and daughter) too were threatened in a similar way. Some other accused posed as Noida Police officer and said that they were under surveillance,” Paliwal told the police.
In the video call received by Paliwal, his wife and daughter on February 3, the accused used the backdrop of “a court”. “A man posing as a CBI judge asked me to turn the phone camera toward me. He told me that I was Goyal’s associate and that my bail plea had been rejected. The accused even sent me my bail rejection orders,” said Paliwal in the complaint.
Next, the victims were asked to visit their bank and withdraw all the money from their accounts to “avoid arrest”. “On February 4, my wife and I transferred the money to the imposters via RTGS from the bank. They were on a video call with us the whole time. The next day, they asked for more money. That is when the branch manager told us to seek help,” the complaint said.
Inspector Vinod Yadav, who is investigating the case, said, “They have not been socialising with neighbours. They hardly left the house since the incident. The couple has only one daughter who lives with them.’’

“It is a tragic incident… The fraudsters seem to have done proper research before targeting this family, as they typically chose elderly people with limited social contact,” he added.

headline: ISRO and IIT Madras jointly develop indigenous semiconductor chip for space-based applications
description: IRIS has been built on the SHAKTI processor baseline. This allows a wide deployment onto diverse domains from Internet of Things (IoT) to compute systems that are inbuilt in various strategic areas.
content:
In a strategic move to strengthen indigenous semiconductors development for the country’s various space-based applications, ISRO and IIT Madras scientists have jointly developed the Indigenous RISCV Controller for Space Applications (IRIS).
IRIS has been built on the SHAKTI processor baseline. This allows a wide deployment onto diverse domains from Internet of Things (IoT) to compute systems that are inbuilt in various strategic areas.
SHAKTI belongs to a class of systems on RISC-IV, which is an open-source Instruction Set Architecture used for designing custom processors. SHAKTI, supported by the Electronics and IT, is a flagship initiative to promote indigenous development of microprocessor-based products offering high-end security for users.
Indian Space Research Organisation’s (ISRO) Inertial Systems Unit, Thiruvananthapuram, had conceived the design of a 64-bit RSIC-V-based controller and the chip configurations and computing requirements were finalised based on the existing sensor systems used by the space agency. The IIT Madras team, led by V Kamakoti at the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, developed it under the chip under the SHAKTI microprocessor project.
The internal memory being fault-tolerant, the system offers higher reliability ; integration of peripheral interface modules and advanced serial buses were performed and the overall system underwent both software and hardware testing, following which
results hold promise for expanding it to future space missions, the team said.
ISRO Chairman, V Narayanan, lauded the indigenous development of the IRIS Controller.
He said, ” I am sure that this high-performance controller will contribute significantly to the future embedded controllers for space mission-related applications. Its performance will be confirmed during the planned product-based flight test to be done shortly.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
” The chip design, fabrication, packaging, motherboard design and fabrication, assembly, software boot were all done in India, validating the existence of the complete semiconductor ecosystem and expertise within the country,” said Kamakoti.

headline: Delhi sees above-normal temperatures, Tuesday marked its warmest day this season
description: Similar to 2022 and 2016, this year too saw no cold-wave days in January. Feeble western disturbances have also meant no cold wave days in February so far. Feeble western disturbances have also meant that there have been no cold wave days in February so far.
content:
As mid-February approaches, Delhi has been recording significantly above-normal temperatures for this time of the year. With the mercury constantly on the rise and touching the 30 degree Celsius mark on Tuesday, which is six degrees above normal, the National Capital experienced its warmest day this season.
This follows an exceptionally warm January when Delhi logged the hottest month since 2019 with the monthly average climbing to 21.1 degree Celsius this January. The average was 21.2 degree Celsius in January 2019.
While the maximum temperature in Delhi remains above normal over most places by 4 to 6 degree Celsius, the minimum temperature has also been on the rise over the past four days and was logged at 11.6 degree Celsius on Wednesday, which is a notch above normal.
Clear sky conditions with winds reaching 20-30 kmph from the northwest direction have mainly been forecast for the day. The IMD has forecast strong surface winds during the daytime till Friday, after which mist conditions are likely. The minimum is forecast to rise to 13 degree Celsius, by February 17. During the same time, the maximum is forecast to remain above normal between 27 and 29 degree Celsius.
Similar to 2022 and 2016, this year too saw no cold-wave days in January. Feeble western disturbances have also meant no cold wave days in February so far. Feeble western disturbances have also meant that there have been no cold wave days in February so far.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD), in its monthly forecast for February, had warned of above-normal temperatures with below-normal rainfall over most parts of the country. It also forecast fewer cold-wave days over the northwest plains. The lack of substantial western disturbances brought a deficit in rainfall and snowfall, leading to higher-than-usual temperatures and impacting air quality. The Air Quality Index (AQI) has remained moderate to poor this month so far because of warmer temperatures and strong surface winds.
Impact on agriculture in Northwest plains
According to the IMD, the below-normal rainfall, coupled with higher temperatures over the plains of Northwest India in February, is expected to have significant adverse effects on standing crops such as wheat, particularly during the flowering and grain-filling stages.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Crops like mustard and chickpea may also experience early maturity. Horticultural crops like apples and other temperate stone fruits may face premature bud break and early flowering due to the warmer temperatures, resulting in poor fruit setting and quality, which could ultimately affect yield.
To mitigate these adverse impacts and sustain crop growth, intermittent light irrigation will be necessary, the Met Office stated. It also said that the expected normal to below-normal maximum temperatures in Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh will likely limit the adverse effects of cold waves on field crops.

headline: Pune Inc: Enjoy a Roman holiday at Donna Cucina in the city, one pasta platter at a time
description: It was the taste of fresh pasta that changed the course of Arshita Singhvi’s life. The Chartered Accountant now runs an Italian restaurant in Pune's Kalyani Nagar.
content:
Love, in true Italian style, is best expressed through food. So, Arshita Singhvi has been perfecting dual-tone ravioli and a walnut, green chilli and garlic sauce dressing in her kitchen at Donna Cucina, the new Italian restaurant in Kalyani Nagar, for Valentine’s Day guests.
The menu, at any time, boasts Cappelletti Al Fungi (small, hat-shaped pasta filled with garlic mushroom and served with mushroom thyme butter), an array of Gnocchi, risotto, lasagna and Napolitana pizza, among others. “The dual-tone ravioli is very pretty to look at, with pink and yellow colours,” says Singhvi.
Italian food lovers would be familiar with Singhvi as the home cook who became popular on Instagram by rustling up delectable artisanal pasta during the Covid-19 pandemic. Orders came in such large numbers that she grew her business into a cloud kitchen in Koregaon Park. In late October, she shifted to an 80-plus seater, Donna Cucina, in a vintage villa where guests are served freshly handcrafted pasta and other dishes just the way it is done in Italy. The restaurant makes its own fresh ricotta – or Italian whey cheese – every day.
The Italian food market has been steadily growing in India, with surveys indicating that it is second only to Chinese in the foreign cuisine segment. In Pune, it is indicative of the trend that Singhvi was receiving orders from across the city but mostly from Koregaon Park. Donna Cucina is building a niche among the upper crust by building a clientele among people who are well-travelled and enjoy authentic Italian food.
“We have kept it simple when it comes to the business model. We are going to keep doing what we are good at and that means even when we serve coffee, it is Illy, which is a premium, family-owned Italian brand founded in 1933. We are keeping to our niche so as not to confuse our brand. Donna Cucina is not for the mass public, because they might not get the flavours and might feel that there’s not enough chilli and so on,” Singhvi adds.
A Chartered Accountant who has been cooking since she was a child, Singhvi draws her culinary philosophy from the simplest form of pasta that is made with just sage, butter or parmesan. “Just a few ingredients and it was one of my best and most comforting meals. It is so simple and quick but you have to get the ingredients right. Whatever you are using must be fresh,” she says. Significantly, her pasta does not use egg as “the magic of flour and water is amazing”.
Donna Cucina’s major investment has been in the kitchen, which boasts two imported machines from Italy for pasta making, among others. While Singhvi broke even at the Koregaon Park outlet in six months, it took three months to achieve an operational break even at the new space. A number of diners invariably still pick up fresh pasta to take home. “Once you eat fresh pasta, it is very difficult to go back to the packet variety. We also have a live kitchen and a live pasta room, where you can see your pasta being made from scratch,” says Singhvi.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
She had tasted fresh pasta for the first time while travelling in Manali years ago, and “I was hooked”. “I came back and, immediately, bought a pasta machine for myself. I was just making pasta just for me to eat. It is rare to find fresh pasta,” she says. It also changed the course of her life – she is the first in her family to enter the hospitality business.
With Donna Cucina, Singhvi will in all likelihood make others too fall in love with fresh pasta.
