headline: CIDCO signs four major MoUs at Davos WEF
description: While launching the International Educity project, CIDCO announced it would bring together 8-10 foreign universities to create a global education hub.
content:
The City and Industrial Development Corporation (CIDCO) has signed four major Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) at the World Economic Forum in Davos, aiming to bring significant economic and infrastructural development to Navi Mumbai.
Among the key agreements, CIDCO has partnered with Eruditus and BookMyShow for large-scale projects in Navi Mumbai. The MoU with Eruditus involves an investment of Rs 20,000- Rs 25,000 crore over the next decade to develop an International Educity, creating 20,000 direct employment opportunities. The collaboration with BookMyShow will establish an outdoor entertainment arena in Maharashtra with an investment of ₹1,700 crore, generating around 500 jobs.
While launching the International Educity project, CIDCO announced it would bring together 8-10 foreign universities to create a global education hub. “The project aims to attract students and faculty from around the world, fostering academic collaboration and cross-cultural exchange,” said a CIDCO official. Located within a 5 km radius of the upcoming Navi Mumbai International Airport, the Educity will offer world-class education infrastructure and research facilities, he added.
“The project also aligns with broader development plans, being strategically positioned near key infrastructure such as Aerocity, Sports City, Medicity, and major transport corridors,” said the official.
For the entertainment industry, CIDCO has partnered with BookMyShow to develop a state-of-the-art outdoor entertainment arena modeled after international venues like Madison Square Garden in New York and The O2 Arena in London. The arena will have a seating capacity of 20,000 or standing space for 25,000, making it the largest of its kind in the country.
“This multi-purpose venue will host concerts, award shows, sports tournaments, and cultural events throughout the year, catering to a diverse audience,” said the official.
CIDCO has also signed two more MoUs to enhance Maharashtra’s digital and logistics infrastructure. An MoU with Panchshil Realty will bring an investment of Rs 25,000 crore for a state-of-the-art data center, supporting the growth of businesses and technology firms. Another agreement with Welspun World involves a Rs 1,500 crore investment in a logistics park, creating 2,000 direct employment opportunities.

headline: At Kumbh, a family’s search for missing member hits a wall
description: The Kumbh officials did not respond to calls seeking their response on the posters.
content:
Ram Ishwar Chauhan, 24, came to Prayagraj all the way from Deoria district in Uttar Pradesh looking for his grandmother who has been missing from the Maha Kumbh area for more than a week.
His grandmother Phoolpati Devi, 70, had come to the Kumbh with her son Lalu Chauhan, 47, a farmer, and daughter-in-law Ganeti Devi but went missing amid a chaos that broke out soon after the January 29 stampede near the Sangam that left 30 dead and 60 injured.
Devi’s is among the posters of several other missing people which were pasted on the walls of the mortuary at the Motilal Nehru National Medical College and elsewhere in the city.
Also Read | ‘My mother died in Kumbh stampede… now I’m running from one office to another for death certificate’
“My grandmother was returning from the Sangam ghat with my parents to catch a train for Deoria. In the crowd, she got separated from them in Sector 21 of the mela area. My parents searched for her, but to no avail. They informed the Prayagraj police and the Kumbh administration before returning home after four days,” Ram Ishwar says.
“This was the first time our family came to Prayagraj for Kumbh,” he says.
A missing police complaint has also been filed in Prayagraj, he says. The Kumbh police are examining CCTV footage from Sector 21, which is about 2 km from the stampede site. On the inner and outer walls of the hospital mortuary, posters of several missing persons have been pasted, since the January 29 stampede.
Their families are afraid they could be among the stampede victims. Besides her physical appearance, clothes and jewellery worn at the time she went missing, Phoolpati Devi’s family has also announced a monetary reward for anyone providing information about her. The poster also has the contact number of the station house officer of the local police station in Deoria.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Also Read | Maha Kumbh stampede a conspiracy, culprits will face sternest action: Adityanath
The Indian Express contacted some families who had pasted posters of their missing members to find that many reached their homes. The family of a couple from Nepal who also went missing from the Kumbh could not be contacted.
The Kumbh officials did not respond to calls seeking their response on the posters.

headline: In Delhi Assembly polls, AAP’s Aaley Iqbal records highest margin — from Matia Mahal seat
description: Aaley's candidature was not guaranteed initially. The AAP had named Shoaib, his father and the sitting MLA from the seat, as its candidate from the constituency.
content:
In a high-stakes election that saw the AAP suffer major setbacks, one candidate stood out. Aaley Mohammad Iqbal (34) won from Matia Mahal constituency by a margin of 42,724 votes — the highest margin of victory in the entire election — securing 58,120 votes and defeating BJP’s Deepti Indora.
With Aaley’s landslide victory, his family’s deep-rooted hold over Matia Mahal remains unshaken. His father Shoaib Iqbal, the outgoing MLA from the seat, has won from the constituency six times, beginning in 1993. Shoaib had previously been part of the JD, JD(S), LJP, JD(U) and Congress, ensuring electoral win for every party he contested from.
In 2015, he was defeated by AAP’s former minister Asim Ahmed Khan, who contested the 2025 election on a Congress ticket from the same seat. In 2020, shortly after joining the AAP, Shoaib reclaimed the seat from Khan by winning with a margin of over 50,000 votes.
Political Pulse | Muslim-dominated seats in Delhi set to go with AAP, no love for Congress
Aaley’s candidature was not guaranteed initially. The AAP had named Shoaib, his father and the sitting MLA from the seat, as its candidate from the constituency.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
As Rekha Gupta is appointed Delhi CM, the 4 big challenges she will face
After Delhi election, lesson for all parties: Listen to the ground
However, Aaley had earlier told The Indian Express that an internal survey and discussions with party chief Arvind Kejriwal led to his candidature.
This had come amid Shoaib’s intention to leave state politics and to carve an identity at the national level. Reflecting on this decision, Aaley had said, “In the election survey, we both received favourable public reviews. My father has served as an MLA from this seat six times and now wants to step into national politics.”
Although this was his first Assembly election, Aaley is no stranger to electoral battles.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
His political journey began at 21, when he became the youngest councillor in Delhi after winning the 2012 Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) elections from Turkman Gate as a candidate from the Rashtriya Lok Dal.
Also Read | In 2020 riot-hit NE Delhi, BJP bags 3 seats, AAP 1; Kapil Mishra among winners
After being re-elected in 2017 and then again in 2022 — both times with record-breaking margins — he was until recently serving as the Deputy Mayor. While winning the seat, he had managed to reach another historic milestone — becoming the first Muslim Deputy Mayor of Delhi since 1977.
His accessibility and hands-on approach to governance are behind his popularity among the masses, said party insiders. As a Deputy Mayor, he was known for personally addressing grievances — his office was a revolving door for residents seeking immediate resolutions to their problems. From morning till late afternoon, his office was known to be open to all. People visited him with their issues, and he had earned a reputation of being responsive to their problems.
Stepping into the role of the Matia Mahal MLA, Aaley said he will remain committed to his grassroots ethos.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“I thank the people of Matia Mahal for considering me worthy of this remarkable victory. My purpose now is to ensure that all incomplete tasks are finished on priority. As a councillor, I have stood up to people’s expectations, and will continue to do so, just like my father,” he added.

headline: 38th National Games: Five Himachal pugilists bag as many medals — none are training in state
description: A total of 10 boxers, including six women, from the state have participated in the Games that began on January 28 in Uttarakhand.
content:
Five pugilists, including three women, from Himachal Pradesh participating in the 38th National Games-2025 in Uttarakhand clinched as many medals, including a silver and four bronze, but none have trained in the hill state due to a lack of infrastructure.
A total of 10 boxers, including six women, from the state have participated in the Games that began on January 28.
Vinakshi Dhota won silver in the 57kg weight category and Meenakshi Devi and Ekta Thakur won bronze in the 60kg and 75kg weight categories, respectively. In men’s category, Ashish Chaudhary and Chetan Chauhan won bronze in the 57kg and 92kg weight category, respectively.
Vinakshi and Ashish were selected under the National Centres of Excellence (NCOE) programme of the Sports Authority of India (SAI) and trained in Haryana’s Rohtak, while Menka and Ekta of Kullu and Chetan of Mandi are getting training on their expenses in Haryana, sources said. Vinakshi and Ashish represent India at the international level too.
Vinakshi, who lost the final bout to Sakshi of Services, was offered a Group D post and the post of a constable with the Himachal Pradesh Police in recognition of her performance at the national and international level, but she declined, they said.
Speaking with The Indian Express, Vinakshi, a resident of Ghumna village near Rohru in Shimla, said, “I started training at the age of 14 at a government sports centre at Sangla in Kinnaur and then moved to other centres. I give the credit of my success to my coaches in Himachal Pradesh, who taught me to compete on the national and international levels. Himachal has yet to get infrastructure meeting the requirements of its sportspersons. We have a tough topography and the best climate for training.”
Himachal Pradesh Olympic Association Secretary Rajesh Bhandari said, “We need to do a lot to enhance our sports infrastructure. The medal-winning pugilists have been practising in Haryana but are sportspersons of Himachal Pradesh. Recently, we got a new SAI centre in Bilaspur. We also have an NSOE centre in Hamirpur, especially for boxing. Besides, we are also in touch with multinational conglomerate JSW, which opened a few sports facilities and is willing to provide more sports facilities.”
Coach Tek Chand, who accompanied the boxing team, said, “We have the best talent in our state but need infrastructure. There are certain reasons why states like Haryana dominate the field of boxing. The prime reason is nurseries, sports complexes and stadiums, besides private coaching institutes where many pugilists from Himachal Pradesh and other states are getting training.”

headline: Beyond dollars: Farmer couple’s reverse migration push, son to quit Canada job to work in family’s fruit orchard
description: Their orchards bear fruits the year round except during June-July months, ensuring a steady income for the couple.
content:
At a time when most young people in Punjab are trying all means to reach foreign shores, Rajinder Kaur Virk and her husband Gurnam Singh Virk of Moranwali village in Faridkot are elated as their son will return from Canada in April this year and join them in farming.
The couple, in their mid 50s, have transformed their 18 acres of farmland into a thriving orchard in just six years and now hope to venture into the food processing area with the expertise of their son, who has a Masters is agriculture from Ludhiana’s Punjab Agriculture University.
To ensure that their orchards thrive, the couple uses grafting techniques which gives them fruits in the second or third year.
While Rajinder Kaur worked as an instructor in district welfare department and took premature retirement, her husband Gurnam is still serving as the PA to the Faridkot deputy commissioner.
“We had earlier leased out our land and farmers grew wheat and paddy. When our son and daughter left for Canada, we wanted to start a sustainable business model and pursue our children to return to their homeland. Now when our children see what we have achieved, they have realised that they can earn more here. We are looking forward to having our son join us in April, especially since there is great potential for fruit processing, which would require more hands on the deck,” says Rajinder, adding that they started with kinnow, malta, lemon, and mosambi on around 8 acres.
The Virks’ shifted to orchard farming in 2019. Gurnam adds that when they started they were often met with ridicule. “People laughed and thought that we would fail. They couldn’t understand how we will manage with our respective jobs. But our focus was clear. I once asked my son if he wants to earn less working under someone else or come here and take over the family tradition and earn way more. From our 18 acres, we now earn around Rs 50 lakh annually. Now that my son is convinced, I am half relieved. Once he is back, our daughter will also understand,” he says, adding that his son first went to Canada to study and now he will return despite having a post-study work permit.
Explaining how it all started, the Virks say, “When our children were leaving for Canada for higher studies, we were busy with our respective careers. Over time, we realized that they might never return. We then gradually started withdrawing our land from lease agreements and started planting fruit trees. We took guidance from Rajinder’s brother, Jaswinder Brar, who is a horticultural scientist at PAU and with his expertise, we first planted kinnow, malta, lemon, and mosambi on approximately 8 acres. Over time we expanded to guava on 8 acres and apple in one acre. We also grew papayas, ber (Indian Jujube), pear, persimmon, dragon fruit, pomegranate, karonda and jamun.”
Their orchards bear fruits the year round except during June-July months, ensuring a steady income for the couple.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
To ensure that their orchards thrive, the couple uses grafting techniques which gives them fruits in the second or third year.
“To conserve water and optimize crop yield, we have installed a drip irrigation system throughout our farm. We also use plant residues and fallen fruit to create a natural ecosystem that protects crops from pests and increases productivity. Apples are typically not for hot weather, but several varieties have now been developed that suit Punjab’s climate. We have dedicated one acre to apple and the trees have started to bear fruit,” says Rajinder, who retired in 2022.
Apart from the fruits, the couple also grows wheat on 12 acres during winter through intercropping and plant maize, moongi (green gram) and sugarcane in summer. “We handle marketing and sales ourselves and sell our produce directly to buyers. We transport the fruits to local mandis in Faridkot, Bathinda, Zira, and Kotkapura early morning or late evening, where we have our purchasers. We grade and pack our fruits carefully and our 15-20 labourers help with the work during the season while 5-6 people are employed around-the-year.”

headline: Can protein powder have side effects? Here’s what you need to know
description: Experts tell you who needs it, when and how to have it
content:
Many of us think that we can meet our protein requirements by simply using supplements but that’s not what we need to do. Unless you are an older adult with a limited appetite, have a restricted diet, a medical condition that warrants use or are into endurance sports, you can get your protein from normal food. For a person with a normal activity level, who is not engaging in heavy strength training or endurance sport, the recommended protein intake is about 0.8-1.0 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight per day. This can easily be met through a well-balanced diet rich in natural high-quality protein and other essential nutrients like vitamins, minerals, fibre and healthy fats that protein powders may lack, say experts.
Protein powders lack essential nutrients
A well-balanced diet rich in whole foods that include lean meats, fish, eggs, dairy, legumes, nuts, seeds, and whole grains should suffice, says Dr Aastha Khungar, Head, Nutrition and Dietetics, Max Hospital, Mohali. “Foods like chicken, turkey, tofu, Greek yoghurt, lentils, chickpeas, quinoa, and cottage cheese provide high-quality protein and deliver other essential nutrients that protein powders may lack, like vitamins, minerals, fibre and healthy fats,” she says.
Some powders can have side effects
Consuming too much concentrated protein in the form of powders can strain the kidneys which have to work harder to excrete excess nitrogen in the form of urea. “This increases the risk of kidney stones, allergic reactions and acne, especially in those consuming concentrated whey protein. These also change gut microbes, upping the risk of irritable bowel disease and colon cancer,” says Dr Amit Sharma, nephrologist, Fortis, Mohali.
Khungar points out some protein powders may contain added sugars, artificial sweeteners, preservatives or low-quality protein isolates, which may not be ideal for long-term health. “Users complain of bloating, gas or diarrhoea when consuming certain protein powders, particularly those containing whey (for lactose-intolerant individuals and artificial sweeteners,” she says.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
An average person, adds Dr Rakesh Kochhar, former head, gastroenterology, PGI, Chandigarh, needs 45-55 grams of protein per day which is easy to manage from both plant and animal sources with a component allocated for each meal. “Soy-based concentrated protein products can alter hormonal levels. A recent study has shown that some supplements contain heavy metals like lead, arsenic, cadmium, mercury, and Bisphenol-A (BPA), a carcinogen. These toxins could come from manufacturing processes, packaging or groundwater. In India, the problem is likely to be worse as regulations for drug manufacturing do not govern supplements,” says Kochhar.
Watch out for quality, digestibility and allergens
Normal, healthy people with routine physical activity do not need protein powder supplementation, as excessive protein intake in the long-term adversely affects kidney and liver functions, says professor Rajesh Vijayvergiya from Department of Cardiology, PGIMER. “High amounts of sugar and calories also increase the weight of regular consumers. There is concern about toxicity due to contamination with heavy metals (lead, arsenic, cadmium, and mercury), bisphenol-A (BPA, which is used to make plastic), pesticides and artificial sweeteners. The safety and labelling of various protein powder contents are not as tightly regulated and supervised as in the pharmaceutical industry. For healthy adults, it is preferable to meet protein requirements by consuming nuts, low-fat dairy products, legumes, fish, poultry, eggs, and lean meat,” adds Vijayvergiya.
Protein powder is a concentrated source of dietary protein derived from sources like whey, casein, soy, pea, or hemp, explains Dr Amit Garg, senior consultant, Bariatric and Metabolic Surgery, Livasa Hospital, Mohali. “When selecting a protein powder, consider factors like its quality, digestibility and potential allergens. Read labels, ingredient lists and third-party testing and certifications,” he says.

headline: Humanity is supreme, not religion: Rajmohan Gandhi
description: Addressing students from African countries and staff at SIU, Gandhi said that India is for everyone — for Hindus, Muslims, Jews, Christians — and equality of rights is very crucial.
content:
“Today’s world is in a turbulent state. Supremacy is considered as a respected thing and not equality, loyalty and democracy, this is a disturbing trend worldwide. Equality, humanity, loyalty and democracy — these values should be honored and not disgraced”, said Rajmohan Gandhi, grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, during his visit to Symbiosis International University, Lavale, Pune.
Addressing students from African countries and staff at SIU, Gandhi said that India is for everyone — for Hindus, Muslims, Jews, Christians — and equality of rights is very crucial. He said race and religion are not supreme but humanity was.
“The world has an immense shortage of hospitals and medical facilities. Taking this as an opportunity India can produce more doctors, nurses and allied staff to cater to the needs of the world. Millions of Indians are also suffering from physical and mental health. These medical personnel will be of great help to our country people as well,” Gandhi added.
Speaking at the occasion, founder and president of SIU S B Mujumdar said, “Being a biologist, I can see chromosomes from Mahatma Gandhi and C Rajagopalachari in Rajmohan Gandhi. Today, I can see Mahatma Gandhi present at Symbiosis International University in the form of his grandson and this is indeed a moment of pride for all of us.”

headline: Ex-Karnataka CM Yediyurappa gets protection from arrest; Pocso case reset to cognisance stage
description: The Karnataka High Court grants anticipatory bail to B S Yediyurappa under special considerations such as his age and eminence as a former chief minister, even as it refuses to quash the Pocso case.
content:
Anticipatory bail granted by the Karnataka High Court on Friday to former chief minister B S Yediyurappa in a case filed under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act is set to protect the veteran BJP leader from arrest as the case returns to a special court for Pocso cases.
With the HC also refusing to quash the Pocso case against the 81-year-old Yediyurappa—while striking down the July 4, 2024, decision of the special court to take cognisance of the chargesheet filed by the Criminal Investigation Department of the police—the case has been reset to the cognisance stage again.
The HC ruled that the special court judge had erred in the application of mind while taking cognisance of the chargesheet against the former CM since no reasons were stated by the court for the decision to take cognisance after studying the chargesheet.
“The Writ Petition is allowed in part. The order of taking cognizance by the concerned court dated July 4, 2024 qua accused number one stands obliterated,” Justice M Nagaprasanna said in his order.
“The crime, the investigation and the final report all remain intact. The matter is remitted back to the concerned court to pass appropriate orders on the final report so placed before it by the CID bearing in mind the observations made in the course of the order,” the HC ruled.
The HC has stated that the special court must make a reasoned order for taking cognisance of the chargesheet filed by the CID.
“The court is expected to record reasons for taking cognizance. Though the reasons need not be so elaborate when it records framing of charges or conviction, nonetheless, it must bear application of mind to set further proceedings in motion, as taking of cognizance or issuance of process has some judicial sanctity,” the HC said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Case reset to cognisance stage
The HC’s order implies that the special court for Pocso cases, to which the matter will return soon, will now have to provide valid reasons for taking cognisance of the chargesheet in order to facilitate the trial of the case, legal sources said.
Incidentally, the CID police, which investigated the Pocso case against Yediyurappa, has filed an additional chargesheet in the case and this would also need reasoned cognisance by the special court when the case resumes.
The special court noted on July 31, 2024, that “the Special Public Prosecutor for the state filed a memo along with an additional chargesheet”.
The Pocso case has been in limbo since Yediyurappa approached the HC to quash the case.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The next date for the Pocso case is February 28, but the special public prosecutor is likely to seek an advancement of the hearing in the wake of the HC order cancelling the earlier cognisance taken by the court while keeping the case intact, sources said.
The Supreme Court and the HC have mandated adherence to section 35 of the Pocso Act—which specifies that the evidence of the child victim of sexual offences must be recorded within 30 days of the trial court taking cognisance of a case and that the trial must be completed within one year. In a 2021 judgment by Justice B V Nagarathna and Justice M G Uma, the HC directed judges of special courts for Pocso cases to comply with section 35 of the Act.
FIR and chargesheet
An FIR was registered on March 14, 2024, against Yediyurappa by the Bengaluru police on the basis of a complaint by the mother of a teenager stating that her daughter had been subjected to sexually inappropriate behaviour by the former CM during a visit to his house on February 2 that year.
The CID filed a chargesheet against the BJP veteran and three others on June 27, 2024, under section 8 (sexual assault) of the Pocso Act 2012 as well as Indian Penal Code section 354 A (sexual harassment), sections 204 (destroying evidence) and 214 (offering gifts to silence the victim).
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A special Pocso court took cognisance of the chargesheet on July 4, 2024, and issued a summons for the former CM and others to appear in court to face trial.
Yediyurappa approached the HC for the quashing of the case and the court ruled on June 14, 2024, that the former CM should not be arrested. Later, on July 12, it allowed the exemption of Yediyurappa and three others from appearing in the special court based on the July 4 summons.
Although no stay was issued by the high court against the proceedings in the special court, the Pocso court proceedings were stalled since July 4, 2024, on account of Yediyurappa seeking the quashing of the chargesheet in the high court.
Anticipatory bail under special considerations
The former CM has been provided protection against arrest by the HC while also allowing the case proceedings to resume in the special court from the stage of taking cognisance—through separate orders passed on Friday.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Yediyurappa was granted anticipatory bail by the HC under special considerations such as his eminence as a former chief minister and his age. “In the light of the filing of the final report by the CID, the petitioner would undoubtedly not be required for any custodial interrogation, as no investigation is pending against the petitioner,” the HC said.
“The petitioner, as observed hereinabove, is an octogenarian and has held the position of the Chief Minister of the State of Karnataka, and there can be no apprehension that he would not cooperate with the trial on its ensuing. Therefore, notwithstanding the vehement opposition of the learned Special Public Prosecutor to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner, I find it appropriate to entertain the petition, filed before this Court in the peculiar circumstance and grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner on certain conditions,” the HC added.
In the event of arrest as the case returns to the special court, Yediyurappa should be released under a personal bond for Rs 5 lakh but should “not indulge in tampering with the prosecution witnesses or hamper the investigation, either directly or indirectly”, the HC stated.

headline: West Bengal Fire Brigade contradicts civic body, claims blast-ripped Kalyani firecracker unit was illegal

The factory was located in a congested residential area in the Rathtala neighbourhood of Kalyani. The state government has announced a compensation of Rs 2 lakh each for the kin of the deceased. Among the four dead, three were women. Another woman who suffered injuries in the explosion is currently under treatment.
The police arrested factory owner Khokan Biswas on Friday night and produced him in court on Saturday after a medical check-up. Biswas has been remanded in police custody for four days.
The investigators were trying to find out why a large amount of firecrackers was stored at the factory. The site has been cordoned off and a large number of policemen has been deployed in the area.

headline: Man arrested for assaulting ticket checker at Virar railway station
description: Aditya Pawar allegedly attacked ticket checker Birju Singh Tanwar after he was caught travelling without a valid ticket.
content:
A 23-year-old man was arrested in Mumbai earlier this week for allegedly assaulting a ticket checker at Virar railway station on February 1, the Western Railway said in a statement.
Ticket checker Birju Singh Tanwar was allegedly attacked by a person who was caught travelling without a valid ticket. Subsequently, the Government Railway Police (GRP) on February 3 lodged a case against an unknown person under sections 121(2) (intentionally causing grievous hurt to a public servant) and 132 (use of criminal force or assault against a public servant while they are performing their duties) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
An RPF Crime Prevention and Detection Squad comprising Head Constable Kailash Jadhav and Constable Rakesh Tanwar was tasked with tracking the accused. Aditya Pawar, a resident of Virar East, was identified as the accused through CCTV analysis and facial recognition software.
Pawar was arrested at the Borivali railway premises on Tuesday, the Western Railway said. While being questioned by Senior Inspector Devendra Kumar, he allegedly admitted to assaulting Tanwar and was then handed over to the GRP for further action.

content:

headline: It’s a cover-up, Yogi govt hiding actual stampede toll: Congress
description: Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai claimed that hundreds of people died in the stampede in Kumbh due to mismanagement on the intervening night of January 28 and 29. Thousands of people were injured while thousands went missing.
content:
Claiming that hundreds of people died in the January 29 stampede at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai on Friday alleged that the state government is hiding the actual death toll to cover up its failure.
According to the state government, the death toll in the stampede was 30 while 60 were injured.
Speaking to media persons in Lucknow, Rai said, “Hundreds of people died in the stampede in Kumbh due to mismanagement on the intervening night of January 28 and 29. Thousands of people were injured while thousands went missing. The UP government is so insensitive that it has not yet released a correct list of the missing and the dead. People are running from door to door in search of their loved ones. The Yogi (Adityanath) government is hiding the correct figures to cover up its failure.”
The last rites of many of the victims were not performed as per their religious beliefs, he added. “Some bodies were thrown into the Ganga, some were picked up by bulldozers, some were cremated anonymously in electric crematoriums while some bodies are still lying in garbage heaps. headline: State govt computes compensation of Rs 31.75L each for 12 student victims
description: The order of the Deputy Collector states that the victims’ kin had demanded a compensation of Rs 5 crore per family as well as a “handsome compensation” of Rs 50 lakh for the two injured persons.
content:
The state government Friday informed the Gujarat High Court that it has computed the compensation to be awarded to the  kin of the victims of Harni Boat tragedy — which claimed 14 lives, including 12 children and 2 teachers on January 18, 2024 after their boat capsized in Vadodara — “keeping in mind the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988”.
The state government submitted the notice following multiple hearings held by the Deputy Collector as per the November 29, 2024, direction of the High Court division bench hearing the suo motu PIL in the case.
In an affidavit submitted by Advocate General Kamal Trivedi to the court on Friday, the state government informed the high court that it has calculated a compensation of Rs 31.75 lakh each for the 12 deceased children while the two deceased teachers — Chhaya Surti and Falguni Patel — have been awarded a compensation of Rs 11.21 lakh and Rs 16.68 lakh, respectively. The two injured school helpers have been awarded a compensation of Rs 50,000.
The affidavit of the state, submitted by Sub Divisional Magistrate and Deputy Collector, Vadodara, VK Sambad — who was appointed by District Collector of Vadodara to compute a compensation — states, “… issued notices to the families of victims as well as the contractor i.e. Kotia Projects and due opportunity of hearing was also provided on various occasions… after considering all the documents and evidence produced by either parties, while keeping in mind the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, as well as the principles laid down by the Honorable Supreme Court [in two cases pertaining to compensation].. has arrived at the probable computation of compensation for the 14 deceased persons and two injured persons.”
The annexed February 6 order of the Deputy Collector in computing of compensation states that since the deceased children were minors, they had “no independent income”, the amount has, therefore, been arrived at as per the guidelines laid down by the SC in the 2013 landmark judgment to compute the annual income of children or deceased without income in accidents.
The order of the Deputy Collector states that the victims’ kin had demanded a compensation of Rs 5 crore per family as well as a “handsome compensation” of Rs 50 lakh for the two injured persons.
The order states that the notional computed annual income of the 12 children was estimated to be Rs 1.54 lakh while the income of the teachers had been proven to be Rs 12,500 for Chhaya Surti and Rs 15,624 for Falguni Patel.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The final computation of the compensation of Rs 31.75 lakh per family of the 12 children was done taking into account notional “increments, expenditures, loss of and dependency”.
The order of the Deputy Collector also states, “The decided compensation is to be paid along with 9 per cent annual interest from the date of filing of the PIL till the date of the payment of the compensation.”
Advocate for the victims’ families in the High Court, Utkarsh Dave, told The Indian Express: “The order of the Deputy Collector has specifically awarded the compensation of Rs 31.75 lakh to the 12 deceased minors and Rs 11.21 lakh and Rs 16.68 lakh to the two teachers… We will also raise a strong case in the matter that the Vadodara Municipal Corporation as well as the New Sunrise school may also be compelled to pay compensation as it has been established on record that the lapses on part of the VMC and the fault of the school in seeking no permission and conducting no inspection of the place and also failing to keep the children safe, led to the tragic incident”.
The High Court will next hear the case on February 17.

headline: Over 300 residents of three high-rises fall ill after drinking contaminated water in Greater Noida West
description: “Around 6,500 families living in 56 towers of Eco Village 1 were examined on February 4 after they complained of suffering from loose motion,” Chief Medical Officer Dr Lalit Kumar told The Indian Express.
content:
As many as 334 people have fallen ill after allegedly consuming contaminated water in three Greater Noida West high-rises, health officials said on Friday.
Medical Superintendent Sachindra Mishra from Bisrakh in Greater Noida West said, “On February 3, the (Gautam Buddh Nagar) district health department received information that around 40 people living in Supertech Eco Village 1 fell ill after drinking contaminated water.”
He added that the residents complained of symptoms like loose motion, vomiting and abdominal pain. “Similar complaints were received from Arihant Arden and Panchsheel Hynish societies, following which we set up health camps,” he added.
“Around 6,500 families living in 56 towers of Eco Village 1 were examined on February 4 after they complained of suffering from loose motion,” Chief Medical Officer Dr Lalit Kumar told The Indian Express.
“Following this, around 21,600 residents from all three societies were examined by Friday. Among them, 334 were found suffering from loose motion, fever, cold and abdominal pain. They also include 37 children,” read a statement issued by the district health
department.
A resident of Eco Village 1, Ranjan Suri Bhardwaj, said, “We get the water tanks cleaned but the pipes through which water is supplied by the GNIDA (Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority) is damaged at many places.”
A senior GNIDA official, on condition of anonymity, said that initial tests have shown that the water used for drinking purposes in the three societies is contaminated.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Maintaining that penalty has been imposed on one builder, the official added, “A team of officials who went to inspect the water problem found issues with the builder and the facilities provided to the residents.”
“We have confirmed that the water was contaminated,” the official further said.
Deputy Chief Medical Officer of Noida, Tikam Singh, said prima facie the water was contaminated by E.coli bacteria.
Singh, however, said they are still awaiting test reports. “We have collected water samples and sent them for tests… We are waiting for reports, but prima facie it looks like the water was contaminated due to the presence of E.coli bacteria,” he added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
When contacted, Gautam Buddh Nagar Additional District Magistrate Atul Kumar also said that samples of stool and water from the three societies have been sent for testing.
“We have also sent a district malaria officer and the sub-divisional magistrate to these societies. Further, we have asked the Greater Noida authority to collect water samples and submit a report… the reports should arrive in 48 hours,” he added.
Singh, meanwhile, said that as incidents of consumption of contaminated water in Gautam Buddh Nagar have been on rise in the recent times, the health department will soon initiate an exercise to examine water samples at societies. “We are planning to hold a routine examination every three months,” he added.

headline: The wait ends, Delhi Assembly poll verdict today
description: Former Deputy Chief Minister and AAP leader Manish Sisodia also accused the BJP of having relied on “money and intimidation” rather than a democratic mandate.
content:
A third consecutive term in power for the AAP, a possible return to the helm of the Capital’s governance after 26 years for the BJP and a chance at resurrecting itself after 11 years in the political wilderness for the Congress — only one of these will materialise when votes for the Delhi Assembly polls are counted on Saturday.
Amid allegations of poaching, exit polls predominantly projecting a majority AAP or BJP  government as well as the Congress’s re-entry into Delhi’s legislature — which it held sway over for three back-to-back terms — the counting of votes will determine which party will script the next chapter of the city’s political history.
AAP Delhi Convenor Gopal Rai sought to assert that the party was poised to return to power with more than 50 seats based on ground-level feedback received from party candidates on the eve of the results. “All candidates presented their ground reports in a meeting, which indicated that AAP is set to win over 50 seats decisively with a close contest in seven to eight seats,” Rai told mediapersons.
He added that the Opposition was, through exit polls, seeking to spread a “narrative that they are forming the government” which, however, only reflected their “frustration over an imminent defeat”.
“They are trying to exert psychological pressure using exit polls and are attempting to execute ‘Operation Lotus’. But let me make it clear… BJP’s ‘Operation Lotus’ will not succeed at any cost,” he said.
Former Deputy Chief Minister and AAP leader Manish Sisodia also accused the BJP of having relied on “money and intimidation” rather than a democratic mandate.
While the Congress’s Delhi leadership said that it was certain about the people of the Capital having voted for change, Delhi BJP president Virendra Sachdeva, following a review meeting, declared that the results would be “unprecedented” and hand a decisive mandate of 50 seats to the BJP.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“The people of Delhi are fed up with the corruption-ridden, anarchic, and incompetent rule of the Arvind Kejriwal government… people from all sections of society cast a decisive vote against Kejriwal yesterday,” Sachdeva said.
“Election results will be unprecedented, and BJP will win more than 50 seats to form the government,” he added.
The AAP, which took centrestage in the Capital’s politics after toppling the Congress’s three-term rule in 2013 and then in 2015 when it won 67 of its 70 Assembly seats, remained at the helm of the Delhi government with 62 seats in 2020.
After extending outside support to the AAP, enabling it to form a 49-day government in 2013, the Congress drew a blank in both the 2015 and 2020 polls while the BJP, which had 32 seats in 2013, slipped to four seats in 2015 and could only manage eight seats in 2020.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The counting process will begin at 8 am with early trends likely to start coming in soon after. According to the Election Commission, 60.54% of votes were polled on Wednesday. Delhi Chief Electoral Officer R Alice Vaz said 5,000 personnel will be deployed for the counting of votes.

headline: Delhi results today, ACB notice to Kejriwal over horse-trading claim
description: On Thursday, Kejriwal and AAP Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh alleged that the BJP had embarked on ‘Operation Lotus’ in Delhi, and was seeking to bribe as many as 16 leaders of their party, offering each Rs 15 crore, to jump ship.
content:
As candidates, parties and the city braced for the counting of votes Saturday to decide a new government and Assembly in Delhi, the Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB) showed up at the door of the ruling AAP Friday to serve notices to its leaders over claims that the rival BJP had offered bribes to AAP MLAs and others to jump ship.
The ACB issued notice to AAP convener and former Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal, in addition to other senior party leaders, to join an inquiry regarding allegations that the BJP was seeking to poach sitting and potential AAP legislators to form the next government in Delhi.
On Thursday, Kejriwal and AAP Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh alleged that the BJP had embarked on ‘Operation Lotus’ in Delhi, and was seeking to bribe as many as 16 leaders of their party, offering each Rs 15 crore, to jump ship.
Responding to the allegation, Delhi BJP president Virendra Sachdeva called it a result of panic arising out of “frustration” and the AAP’s acknowledgment of its “seemingly inevitable defeat”.
On Friday, the Delhi BJP wrote to Lieutenant Governor V K Saxena seeking registration of a case against AAP leaders, including Kejriwal, over the party’s allegation of the BJP approaching AAP MLAs with bribes.
Sanjay Singh told reporters: “They have tried to break our candidates, we are going to complain, we have already released a phone number from which one candidate got a call. The ACB should act, not create drama. I dare the ACB to take action against these BJP leaders.”
An ACB team reached Kejriwal’s residence on Ferozeshah Road but was not allowed inside since it “did not have any official warrant” or documentation related to the proposed enquiry, according to the AAP.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Following this, the anti-graft body issued a notice to Kejriwal as well as AAP minister Mukesh Ahlawat, who had made a similar allegation, asking them to make themselves available to provide information regarding the allegations.
“Whether the tweet posted at the following URL of X (formerly Twitter), has been posted by you or otherwise?… Details of the 16 candidates for MLA of AAP who received phone calls regarding the offer of a bribe,” the ACB stated in its notice.
It also sought details of the phone numbers or people who approached these AAP legislators with the alleged offer of bribes, evidence and proof to support the claim or allegations of the offer of bribe and to explain why “appropriate legal action should not be taken against the persons spreading such information on media/social media platforms which is tantamount to create panic and unrest situation amongst the people of Delhi”.

headline: Man returning from funeral killed in hit-and-run accident in Mumbai’s Goregaon
description: The man and his nephew were returning from Kandivali when the accident took place, said the Mumbai police.
content:
A 36-year-old man returning from a relative’s funeral was killed and his nephew was injured in a hit-and-run accident in Goregaon (East) in Mumbai early Thursday.
According to the Mumbai police, Ramesh Jhore and his nephew Naresh, 18, were returning home on Jhore’s scooter from Kandivali. When they reached the Dindoshi flyover on Western Express Highway, a speeding four-wheeler rammed into their vehicle from behind. As they fell off the scooter, the speeding vehicle fled the scene.
Naresh lost consciousness and Jhore suffered serious injuries, and were rushed to a hospital. A police officer said Naresh was informed at the hospital that his uncle had died.
After Naresh told the officers about the accident, the Dindoshi police registered a case under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Motors Vehicle Act for causing death by negligence and not providing medical assistance to the injured.

headline: Fatehgarh police bust inter-state drug supply network, arrest 6
description: The drug supply network spanned Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana and Punjab.
content:
The Fatehgarh Sahib district police in Punjab Friday informed they have arrested six drug traffickers and seized 2,56,846 drug tablets/capsules, 21,364 injections, and 738 vials (Avil) from their possession. The police also seized three vehicles used by the criminals.
Those arrested have been identified as Parvinder Singh, Sahil, Pankaj Chaudhary, Shubham, Shahid and Wasim.
Parvinder Singh was already booked in an attempted murder case in Mohali’s Kharar (Sadar) police station, while another accused Sahil was earlier booked in a drug smuggling case. Meanwhile, Wasim was wanted in an attempted robbery case in Uttar Pradesh.
Dr Ravjot Grewal, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP), Fatehgarh Sahib, said, “A case under the sections… of the NDPS (Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances) Act was registered at Badali Aala Singh police station.”

“Using technical and digital assistance, one drug trafficker after another was traced and arrested, leading to a significant drug bust that dismantled an interstate drug supply network operating from Uttar Pradesh to Punjab via Haryana,” she added.
Giving details of the case, the SSP revealed that the Crime Investigation Agency (CIA) Sirhind team arrested accused Parvinder Singh from Cholta Khurd village in Mohali district on January 27, and seized a large quantity of drug injections/vials and tablets. During the investigation, it was found that Parvinder Singh was both a drug addict and a supplier. He used to procure drugs from an individual named Sahil in Yamunanagar (Haryana) and supply them in Fatehgarh Sahib and Mohali.
On January 29, during further investigation, Sahil was arrested from Yamunanagar, along with a large quantity of drug tablets/capsules. Sahil owned a gym supplement store in Yamunanagar, which he used as a front to distribute illegal medical drugs in Haryana and Punjab. During interrogation, Sahil revealed that he sourced these drugs from Pankaj Chaudhary alias Virat, a resident of Saharanpur, Uttar Pradesh.

On January 30, the CIA team arrested Virat and his partner Shubham in Saharanpur. Shubham had illegally rented a warehouse in Saharanpur, where commercial quantities of drug injections, vials, and tablets/capsules were seized. During questioning, Virat confessed that he procured these drugs from Abdul alias Wajid, a resident of Meerut in Uttar Pradesh.
On February 4, the CIA team raided Meerut and arrested Abdul’s two partners, Shahid and Wasim. Following their statement, the police raided Abdul’s illegal warehouse, where commercial quantities of drug injections, vials, and tablets/capsules were seized. A manhunt is currently on to nab Abdul.
The investigation revealed that this drug supply network spanned from Meerut (UP), Delhi, Saharanpur (UP), and Yamunanagar (Haryana) to Punjab.
The CIA team not only arrested six drug traffickers but also busted three illegal drug warehouses.

“This operation has significantly disrupted the interstate drug supply chain running from Uttar Pradesh to Punjab via Haryana. Further investigation is ongoing,” SSP Grewal added.

headline: Pune civic body not to hike property tax for next financial year
description: The PMC has also launched a drive to recover dues of property tax defaulters by sealing properties and discontinuing water supply.
content:
With civic elections likely in the forthcoming financial year and citing the absence of an elected civic body, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) has decided not to hike property tax rates for 2025-26.
“The civic administration proposal was not to hike the property tax rates for 2025-26, which has been approved in the civic standing committee,” said Rajendra Bhosale, Municipal Commissioner and Administrator, PMC.
PMC hiked the property tax rate last time in 2015-16 by 10 per cent. The civic body will continue the discount of 5 or 10 per cent in tax for the properties implementing vermicomposting, and rainwater harvesting, among other environment-friendly measures.
It will also continue the discount scheme for one property of the wife or mother of a soldier who has died while serving the country, ex-servicemen of Defence forces or his wife or mother, and President’s award winners.
The civic body has made no changes in the entertainment tax levied on films, plays, circuses, music concerts, and wrestling events held within its jurisdiction.
The PMC has also launched a drive to recover dues of property tax defaulters by sealing properties and discontinuing water supply to them.

headline: ‘Rahul Gandhi is doing cover firing to hide Congress’s failure’: Fadnavis dismisses voting irregularity charges
description: Rahul Gandhi had alleged that voter turnout in Maharashtra was above the total adult enrolment in the state. He also questioned the rise in voter numbers between two elections.
content:

Therefore, such an approach will lead to further setbacks and completely wipe out Congress,” Fadnavis added.

headline: BEST driver booked for negligence, 3 months after death of elderly passenger

content:
Three months after a 65-year-old man from Mumbai died following a fall from the state-run BEST bus at Mulund, the police on Thursday booked the bus driver who allegedly started the vehicle without ensuring that all commuters had got in.
According to the police, Laxman Mohane, a Bhandup resident, died on November 8, two days after the incident at Gyan Sarita bus stop.
The police said that due to driver’s negligence Laxman lost balance and fell, sustaining injuries to his head.
The Mulund police have registered a case against Suresh Gursale, 55, for causing death due to negligence based on the complaint of Lata, wife of the deceased, who approached the police earlier this week, and after recording eye-witness accounts.
The police said that they would soon issue a notice to the driver and record his statement.
Soon after the accident, though the local police had approached the family of the deceased, Lata, who works at a catering and event management firm in Mulund, had told the police that she was then not in the right frame of mind to examine deep into the reasons behind the death, the police said.
Recently, Lata and her son-in-law visited the accident spot and got to know from people from nearby shops that the incident occurred as the bus driver allegedly sped off without ensuring that the back door was closed and whether all passengers had entered the vehicle, the police said.

headline: Vehicle’s brakes were rusty and slow, no safety belt in bogies: Chandigarh toy train accident inspection report
description: Chandigarh's Engineering Department has found that the working of the brakes of the toy train were “rusty and slow”, and there was no provision of safety belts in any of its bogies.
content:
More than seven months after an 11-year-old boy died of head injuries after a toy train overturned at Elante Mall in Chandigarh, an engineer of the UT Engineering Department has found that the working of the brakes of the train were “rusty and slow”, and there was no provision of safety belts in any of its bogies.
The inspection of the toy train was conducted by engineer Navraj Singh, a Sub-Divisional Engineer, Mechanical Sub-Division, Chandigarh, who inspected the train on September 13, 2024.
The inspection report has been attached in the chargesheet filed by the police before a court. The police had registered a case of causing death by negligence under Section 304-A (causing death by negligence) of the IPC at the police station in Industrial Area, Chandigarh against the operator of the toy train, identified as Saurav, who was arrested and later bailed out. The police, along with Saurav, have also chargesheeted Puneet Kumar Ahuja and Sunil Kumar Goel, under the same section.
According to the case, the victim, identified as Shahbaj Singh, 11, from Bhel Adampur in Jalandhar, Punjab had died in the incident. Sazmaan Singh, 5, fortunately received just minor injuries, while a train compartment fell on the head of Shahbaj.
Meanwhile, in the inspection report, it has been stated that the working of the toy train had been checked by operating and running it. The UT engineer mentioned that the vehicle is in functional condition and its mechanical parts are in working order. However, there were some shortcomings in the train.
“The work of the brakes is rusty and slow. The safety grills in the windows are not provided in the bogies of the toy train. There is also no provision of safety belts in any of the bogie,” the report mentioned.

description: The agency’s exit poll also predicted that the Congres is likely to bag zero to one seat(s), with a vote share of 7% and the same number for ‘others’ but with a lower vote share of 3%.
content:
Two more exit polls projected an edge for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in the Delhi Assembly elections on Thursday, predicting a sweep that was likely to end the party’s 27-year power drought in the capital.
According to the Axis My India exit poll, the BJP was likely to bag between 45 to 55 of the 70 seats in the Delhi Legislative Assembly, obtaining a vote share of 48%, while the AAP was projected to get 15 to 25 in addition to a vote share of 42%.
The agency’s exit poll also predicted that the Congres is likely to bag zero to one seat(s), with a vote share of 7% and the same number for ‘others’ but with a lower vote share of 3%.
Today’s Chanakya projections put the BJP’s possible seat tally at 51, plus or minus six seats, the AAP’s at 19 with a similar, six-seat margin of error, and zero to three seats for ‘Others’.
Exit polls are projections made by election survey agencies based on interviews of voters as they come out after casting their votes. These may vary widely from the actual results.
In the 2020 Delhi polls, most exit polls got their predictions wrong.

Exit polls had gone wrong in the Lok Sabha elections and, more recently, in the Haryana Assembly polls as well. The exit polls on Wednesday – which also predicted a sweep for the BJP – were not linked to television channels.

If his party is getting more than 55 seats, then what is the need for him to call our candidates?… But you abusive people, not even one of our men will break down.”

content:
A state government employee posted at the Karigori Bhawan in Kolkata on Thursday allegedly stabbed his four colleagues with a knife in a fit of rage, the police said.  The man, identified as Amit Sarkar was arrested by Bidhannagar police.
According to sources in the police station all four persons were admitted to a nearby private hospital, where two of them are in critical condition.
Sarkar allegedly stabbed his colleagues because they “made jokes about his father,” said police, adding that the incident took place around 12.30 pm and an FIR has been filed against Sarkar at the station.  “Sarkar, a resident of Ghola in Sodepur, North 24 Parganas district, works in the technical education department,” a police officer said.
It was only after a traffic policeman “repeatedly requested” him to throw the knife, did Sarkar let go of the sharp weapon, police said.  “After the arrest, Sarkar said his four colleagues joked about his father and so he attacked them. We are verifying the cause of the incident,” he added.
The police said, “After a preliminary inquiry, we came to know Sarkar was angry as he had not gotten any leave for several days. Even when his mother was unwell, he had appealed for leave, but that request was declined. We will question his higher officials.”
The injured have been identified as Joydev Chakraborty, Sheikh Shatabul, Shantanu Saha and Sartha Let.   —WITH PTI

content:
Pune city police have arrested a married man from Jammu and Kashmir for allegedly cheating a Pune woman of Rs 45 lakh after developing contacts with her through a matrimonial website.

headline: Badlapur custodial death: Parents say don’t want to pursue case further, HC asks state why no FIR yet
description: The court said it will hear the matter next on Friday, February 7, remarking that it cannot close the plea like this as a lot had happened in the case and questioned why FIR was not yet registered.
content:
The parents of deceased accused in Badlapur sexual assault case on Thursday told the Bombay High Court that they do not want to pursue further their plea seeking SIT inquiry into his son’s custodial death.
The parents also told the court that they were not under any pressure to withdraw the case and that they did not want to run around for the case any longer due to personal difficulty and sought to “stop the case”.
The court said it will hear the matter next on Friday, February 7, remarking that it cannot close the plea like this as a lot had happened in the case and questioned why FIR was not yet registered. The state government informed the court that it will continue independent investigation into the custodial death in accordance with law.
The 23-year-old janitor arrested in August last year for the alleged sexual assault of two minor girls at a school in Badlapur in Thane district was shot dead while he was being transported in a police vehicle on September 23 last year. The police had claimed he was killed in retaliation after he snatched an officer’s service weapon and fired three rounds, injuring an officer.
A bench of Justices Revati Mohite-Dere and Neela K Gokhale on February 3 had sought to know what the government intended to do with respect to a magistrate inquiry report which found that five police officers, including a police driver, were responsible for the custodial death of the accused.
In a report submitted before the HC last month, the magistrate, based on Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) reports, held that “false encounter” allegations made by parents of the deceased “found substance”.
Also Read | Badlapur sexual assault: Probe finds 5 cops responsible for custodial death of accused, HC directs govt to file FIR
On Thursday, the bench questioned the state government as to why no FIR had been filed against the officers indicted in the magistrate’s report.
Senior advocate Amit Desai, representing the state as its special public prosecutor, argued that an independent probe by state CID was still in progress. He said that the scope of the magistrate’s probe was limited to ascertaining cause of custodial death and not of assigning responsibility.
“Scope of magisterial inquiry under sections 196 and 193 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) is only limited to ascertaining cause of death. The magistrate enquiry should not have gone into who is responsible (for death). It has gone into the job in terms of commission of inquiry. One requires powers of probe to look into every aspect of matter, which the magistrate does not possess,” Desai argued.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He added, “As an agency we cannot take this (magistrate’s report) as binding on us and have an independent duty on us to see if offences made out and chargesheet is filed. If the agency is attempting to do it, it should be given time. I am conscious these are matters to be dealt with. However, the Supreme Court in past judgment had said that the agency should have unimpeachable evidence.”
Desai also sought that the additional material collected by the magistrate during the probe, which was not with the police, which can be further sent to the judicial commission set up in October, last year along with the magistrate’s report.
Also Read | Why Maharashtra has a notorious record when it comes to custodial deaths
The state government had formed a judicial commission headed by former Chief Justice of Allahabad High Court Dilip Bhosale, to look into the custodial death and “false encounter” charges and if any person was responsible for the same.
The bench then questioned the state that once the Accidental Death Report (ADR) had been filed, was the same not required to be taken to “logical end” and an FIR was needed to be registered.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Commission of inquiry is a parallel aspect, but as far as ADR is concerned, it has to be taken to a logical end. Further, the court report (magistrate’s) can’t be on paper without action. It’s a full-fledged report with statements… Is the state not duty-bound to register an FIR?” the bench orally questioned.
Desai responded that proper independent investigation was required to be carried out before acting on the ADR. The HC also allowed applications filed by the police officers concerned seeking access to the copy of the magistrate report and directed state lawyers to furnish copies of the report to applicants within a week.

headline: Delhi High Court asks NIA: ‘Can Baramulla MP Engineer Rashid attend Parliament sessions on custody parole?’
description: Abdul Rashid Sheikh alias Engineer Rashid, who is currently in Tihar jail in a 2017 terror funding case, submitted that without his presence in Parliament, his constituency would remain unrepresented.
content:
The Delhi High Court Thursday sought a response from the National Investigation Agency (NIA) on whether Lok Sabha MP from Jammu and Kashmir’s Baramulla, Abdul Rashid Sheikh alias Engineer Rashid, can be permitted to attend Parliament sessions, scheduled until February 13, on custody parole.
The Delhi HC was hearing a plea by Rashid, who is seeking custody parole as an immediate interim relief for attending the ongoing Parliament session. The MP, who is currently in Tihar jail in a 2017 terror funding case, submitted that without his presence in Parliament, his constituency would remain unrepresented.
Justice Vikas Mahajan directed the NIA counsel on Thursday to come up with instructions on the specific aspect on whether Rashid can be considered for custody parole release on Friday for attending Parliament sessions.
NIA orally opposed Rashid’s demand, and informed the court that “the NIA officers say there is a security issue too, he can’t be taken inside Parliament”.

headline: Delhi to Mexico in 4 months: Surviving on mother’s panjiri, man’s harrowing journey via Darien Gap ends in deportation
description: Harjinder Singh, 35, still gets nightmares of what had happened five years ago. Belonging to Jalandhar’s Mundi Chohlian, he lived the foreign dream till June 26, 2019 when he boarded a flight to Dubai on the promise of a safe entry to the USA and a job.
content:
“It’s dark, the stretch is swampy and half eaten bodies are lying on the mud. Their shoes torn but the faces of 20 year olds still have the innocence left. With prayers on their lips and hissing of snakes hitting their eardrums, a group of 20 keeps walking on a 106-km stretch of Panama jungle. A few minutes away my feet gets stuck in the swamp and I wake up sweating…..”
Harjinder Singh, 35, still gets nightmares of what had happened five years ago. Belonging to Jalandhar’s Mundi Chohlian, he lived the foreign dream till June 26, 2019 when he boarded a flight to Dubai on the promise of a safe entry to the USA and a job. He paid Rs 17 lakh ($20,000) to a travel agent.
With three boxes of panjiri (sweet dish) made by his mother, packed in his bag Harjinder, then 30, set out for the new journey. Reality hit hard when a middle man asked him for $2000 to take him through a donkey trail.
Read | US crackdown fails to deter illegal migration from Punjab, Haryana
“The next day a new agent asked for more money for Mexico…we had no legal entry,” he said. “We were then plonked on horses for crossing a mountain and a stream.” The group later received a temporary document that allowed them to stay in the country for up to a month. “From Colombia, we reached Cali after an 8-hour bus ride…we went towards the coastal town of Turbo before taking a boat into the heart of the Panama jungle, where we were joined by a group of 15 African immigrants,” he said.
Crossing Darien Gap
Harjinder and the group spent over 10 days to cross the 105 km stretch of the Panama jungle. “We crossed at least 40 bodies, some half eaten and some skeletons… It’s been five years but I still get nightmares of crossing that stretch. After days…we saw soldiers. It was relief and fear. They shoved us in a camp where I slept after days,” he said.
Read | As US sends military plane to India, what to know of Trump’s mass deportation efforts
Bus, trucks to Mexico
“At one camp, we were made to wait for 13 days until we were allowed to travel to…Costa Rica. After…we were allowed to board a bus to Nicaragua…We moved from Nicaragua to Guatemala and to Tapachula in Mexico in trucks,” he said.
Deportation
In Tapachula, the group stayed for 20 days and waited for their papers to get processed. “We were then taken to a camp in Veracruz… we were made to talk to US border officials through video conferencing… We thought we will go to the USA but we were…deported to India,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Reality check
“For months I had locked myself in my room out of fear. With the passing years, I have gained back a little confidence…grow garlic, wheat and paddy in 14 acres, including 10 acres on lease. I earn around `9 lakh per annum but the loanis still going on,” he said.

headline: 100-metre-long steel bridge launched over four rail tracks
description: An 84-metre-long launching nose weighing about 525 metric tonnes was used for the launch of the 100-metre-long steel bridge (weighing 1,432 metric tonnes) over Western Railway and Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) tracks.
content:
The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) on Wednesday said it has launched a crucial steel bridge over four railway tracks between Kim and Sayan in Surat for the ongoing Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail Corridor Bullet Train project stretching across 508 km.
The steel bridge is the sixth of the 17 bridges planned in Gujarat, launched over two lines of Western Railway and two Dedicated Freight Corridor tracks.
An 84-metre-long launching nose weighing about 525 metric tonnes was used for the launch of the 100-metre-long steel bridge (weighing 1,432 metric tonnes) over Western Railway and Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) tracks.
The NHSRCL said on Wednesday, “The bridge comprises two spans of 100 metres and 60 metres, and will facilitate double-line standard gauge rail track. This crucial infrastructure development involved the crossing of four major tracks — two Western Railway and two DFC tracks and an irrigation canal. The 100-metre span was launched over the Western Railway and DFC tracks from January 28, 2025 to February 5, 2025, while the 60-metre span will be erected over the irrigation canal located adjacent to the tracks at the construction site.”

content:

headline: After successful space docking, Isro’s SpaDex satellites face delay in undocking exercise
description: The SpaDex experiment made India the fourth country in the world -- after the US, Russia and China -- to successfully demonstrate the capability of docking spacecraft.
content:
In a sign that its SpaDex experiment involving space docking is experiencing technical issues, the Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) has delayed an undocking manoeuvre that was scheduled soon after the successful docking on January 16.
Space docking refers to the joining of two fast-moving satellites in space.
On January 29, Isro chairman V Narayanan indicated that the space agency is still conducting a review of the undocking process and that the move could take a while. He was speaking after the launch of the NVS-02 satellite by the GSLV-F15 rocket.
 Isro sources have indicated that “there are some issues with the docking experiments” and that the “undocking has not been possible yet”.
Isro had on January 16 announced the successful docking in space of two satellites it had launched on December 30 which were moving at a speed of over 28,000 kmph. The SpaDex experiment made India the fourth country in the world — after the US, Russia and China — to successfully demonstrate the capability of docking spacecraft.
“SpaDeX Docking Update: Post docking, control of two satellites as a single object is successful. Undocking and power transfer checks to follow in coming days,” ISRO had reported on its official social media handle on January 16.
Also Read | ISRO Docks SpaDeX Satellites in Space: What was done and how – and why does it matter?
Ahead of the mission’s launch, the agency had said, “After successful docking and rigidization, electrical power transfer between the two satellites will be demonstrated before undocking and separation of the two satellites to start the operation of their respective payloads for the expected mission life of up to two years.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On February 2, Switzerland-based s2a systems which develops and operates “systems for Space Situational Awareness” posted images on social media indicating that the SpaDex satellites are still in a docking position.
“SpaDeX A & B during today’s pass over South America, 2025-02-02, 01:19:06 UTC,” s2a systems reported on social media with visuals of the docked SpaDex satellites in space.
Replying to a query on SpaDex on January 29, Narayanan said in Sriharikota that they have to think of the money involved in such projects and utilise it to the maximum. “Now we are in the process of reviewing when to do the undocking, the power connections and when to totally separate them again and dock again. All these processes are going on. We do not want to undock and leave it,” the Isro chairman said.
“We have loaded five kg of propellant on both the satellites. The propellant is needed for docking and undocking exercises. Currently we have 60 to 70 per cent of the propellant (as of January 29) remaining in the spacecraft. There are going to be a lot of experiments in the docking, undocking, power connection exercises and it is not a one time exercise,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Both the satellites are currently moving as one entity and we want to study if things are going correctly and whether they can be controlled together.  After complete review and freezing of the experiments that we have planned we may discuss after a month or two,” he added.
Explained | India to launch its first mission to Venus in 2028: Everything you need to know
Isro sources said the agency has “not been able to undock” the satellites yet.
Space docking is considered essential technology for India’s future space ambitions such as bringing back a sample from the Moon, the plan to build its own space station, the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS), and a possible human landing on the Moon.

headline: Dunki route ruined us’: Wife of deported man demands action against agent
description: Says husband endured 10-month ordeal, left family with Rs 42 lakh debt
content:
Kuljinder Kaur, wife of 40-year-old Harwinder Singh from Thalia village in Punjab’s Hoshiarpur district, has spoken out against the deceitful travel agent who lured her husband with false promises of a safe and quick journey to the United States. Instead, Harwinder was forced into the treacherous ‘Dunki route,’ enduring a harrowing 10-month journey that left the family drowning in a Rs 42 lakh debt.
Kuljinder said poverty had driven her husband to seek a better future abroad, but he never intended to take an illegal route. The agent had assured them that Harwinder would reach the US in just 15 days, demanding an exorbitant Rs 42 lakh for the process. To gather the sum, the family mortgaged their only acre of land and borrowed heavily from private lenders at steep interest rates.
“For 10 months, my husband was shuffled between countries,” Kuljinder said, her voice trembling. “He was taken to Brazil for about a month and a half, then moved through several other countries, including China. He was passed from one place to another like a pawn in a game. He never made it to the US.”
Also Read | As ‘illegal’ immigrants from US land in India today, Punjab consultants call for action against travel agents behind ‘dunki’ routes
Harwinder endured life-threatening conditions, crossing dense jungles, treacherous rivers, and dangerous seas. Despite the hardships, he documented his ordeal, sending videos to Kuljinder whenever possible. She last spoke to him on January 15, the day he was preparing to cross into the US from Mexico.
Harwinder had left home in April last year and remained in contact with his family until mid-January. The news of his deportation came as a shock to Kuljinder, who learned of it only when villagers informed her that he was among the 104 deportees sent back from the US on Wednesday.
The travel agent responsible for their ordeal is from their own village and a distant relative. Kuljinder said they had already filed a complaint against him with the village panchayat after losing contact with Harwinder last month. She is now demanding strict action against the agent and a refund of the Rs 42 lakh spent on the failed journey.
“We have lost everything,” she said. “We only wanted a better future for our children—our 12-year-old son and 11-year-old daughter. Instead, we are left with nothing but debt and heartbreak.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Kuljinder revealed that the agent extorted money at every step of Harwinder’s journey, including a final payment of Rs 10 lakh when he was in Guatemala just two and a half months ago.
Before Harwinder’s departure, the family managed a modest living by farming leased land and rearing cattle. His younger brother also farms rented land, but their income was not enough to secure a better future. Harwinder’s elderly parents—his 85-year-old father and 70-year-old mother—still work in the fields.
Now, Kuljinder is urging the authorities to intervene and help them recover their money. “The government must act against such agents who exploit people’s desperation,” she said. “I am speaking out so that no other family suffers like ours.”

headline: ‘Ensure no outsider or ex-student enters campus’: Calcutta HC after Saraswati Puja college row
description: This comes days after two colleges on the Jogesh Chandra Chaudhuri College campus fell out over a pandal, and law college students alleged that an ‘outsider group’ was harassing them.
content:
The Calcutta High Court on Wednesday observed that authorities of the Jogesh Chandra Chaudhuri College should formulate policies to prevent the entry of outsiders and former students of the college.
A single bench of Justice Jay Sengupta observed that the alleged threat culture on campus cannot continue and that the entry of ex-students without any valid reason cannot be accepted.
Justice Sengupta said, “I do not want any untoward incident to occur in an educational institution.” The court further observed that those students who have alleged that they have been threatened can file a complaint at the local police station at Chari Market. “The police should take immediate action, and if not, then the court will intervene.”
Traditionally, the Jogesh Chandra Chaudhuri Day College and Law College, which share a campus, celebrate Saraswati Puja separately within it. However, this year, allegations surfaced that the Day College students forcibly erected a pandal in front of the Law College’s pandal, effectively blocking the latter’s puja celebrations.
In response, Day College representatives denied any involvement, claiming that outsiders were responsible for setting up the pandal. Following a row between two groups of students, a student had moved a petition before the Calcutta High Court seeking its intervention in the matter.
On January 30, the court asked police to remove the makeshift pandal outside the main building of the campus to allow the Law College students to perform Saraswati Puja on the campus on February 2.
The single-judge bench of Justice Jay Sengupta had asked the police commissioner to depute a joint commissioner and deploy armed police personnel to ensure students of both the day and the law colleges could hold their pujas on the campus, and no outsiders were let in.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Meanwhile, students of the Law College alleged that a group led by outsider Mohammed Shabbir Ali and his group have regularly been coming to the college and threatening and harassing the students there.
The State government had filed a report on Wednesday stating that the makeshift pandal had been removed. The HC had ordered the removal of both pandals, to be carried out by police on Saturday, with the entire process being videographed. Following this, the two colleges will hold separate Saraswati Puja celebrations each year.
