headline: Know Your City: How Portuguese saved Daman from the Mughals
description: Strategic manoeuvres and naval battles thwarted Mughal ambitions in coastal India.
content:
With the conquest of Gujarat by Akbar in 1573 and the establishment of the formidable power of the Mughals, the small Portuguese settlement of Daman on the west coast of India faced multiple serious crises that threatened its very existence. In 1580, Akbar appointed Qutubuddin Mohammed Khan, who had his jagirs at Bharuch, to capture the Portuguese port of Daman. The sultan of Ahmednagar, whose territories bordered Daman’s jurisdiction, was asked to support the imperial forces. However, the Portuguese governor, Martin Afonso de Mello, proved too clever for the Mughals. He received information from his spies about the advance of the Mughal army and ordered the garrison to gather at the church for mass and confession to receive absolution.
At midnight, the south gate of the fort was opened, and the drawbridge was let down in great silence. Three hundred Portuguese soldiers crossed the moat with secret instructions to throw hand grenades and pans of powder among the elephants and other camp animals of the enemy. The Mughal troops were awoken by the noise of explosions and found their animals frightened and burnt by the gunpowder. The animals broke their chains and went mad, smashing everything in their terror. Unable to ascertain the cause of the confusion and unable to distinguish friend from foe in the darkness, the Mughals thought a large Portuguese army was upon them, leading to infighting or panic. It was only in the morning that the Mughal general realised that the Portuguese had, through a clever ruse, ruined a significant part of his army. He deemed it expedient to abandon the siege.
Interestingly, the Jesuit fathers at Agra brought this aggression to the emperor’s notice and protested against the unprovoked attack on the Christian rulers of Daman. Akbar could not deny the charge but shifted the responsibility onto his generals. At the Jesuit fathers’ request, he sent orders to Qutub-ud-din Khan to withdraw his forces, which he promptly obeyed. The Portuguese further strengthened their defences, building a land gate on the south side, with a large inscription slab commemorating the valour of the Portuguese under the stewardship of their commandant, Martin de Mello.
However, hostilities did not end there. In the eighth year of Jahangir’s reign, tensions flared again between the Mughals and the Portuguese. During the autumn of 1613, the latter incurred the wrath of the Mughal emperor by plundering a large Mughal pilgrim ship, the Rahimi, which had a capacity of 1,500 tonnes and was carrying a rich cargo. This act of defiance, aimed at expressing displeasure over the favourable reception given to the English at Surat, provoked extreme resentment among the Mughal court, particularly as some of the most important nobles, including the emperor’s mother, had vested interests in the cargo valued at Rs 10 lakh. The emperor resolved to inflict a severe punishment on the Portuguese.

Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Jahangir patched a truce with his enemy, the sultan of Ahmednagar, so that imperial and Deccani troops could carry out a joint attack on the Portuguese forts in western India. Muquarrab Khan, the governor who seems to have been on a visit to the court, was instructed to proceed to the coast and seize the goods and persons of all Portuguese in the empire. In Agra and Lahore, all their church doors were sealed and the exercise of their religion was forbidden. Father Jerome Xavier, who had been in high favour at the court, was sent down to the governor of Surat in disgrace and placed under detention by the Mughal officers, though he was shortly released to discuss terms of peace with the Portuguese viceroy.
Viceroy Dom Jerónimo de Azevedo, who played a significant role in the Portuguese expansion in the Indian Ocean.
Since the Mughal naval power was insignificant, active steps were taken to lay siege by land to the Portuguese at Daman, Bassein and Chaul. Simultaneously, Muquarrab Khan appealed to the Dutch at Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam today), who had a factory at Surat, for help, promising them Daman when it was taken by the besieging Mughal forces. Faced with this grave threat, the Portuguese sought reconciliation, offering to restore the ship and the goods, but their offer was rejected.
In revenge, the Portuguese sent frigates to Ghogha, burning 120 vessels, of which 10 were of large size, as well as a significant portion of the city. They also conducted raids along the coast, pouncing upon Broach (Bharuch) and setting fire to many houses in the suburbs. Meanwhile, the combined Ahmednagar and Imperial forces dispatched by the Mughal emperor appeared before Daman after laying waste to the surrounding country and burning some villages. Around this time, Luiz de Britto, who had captured the Mughal ship, arrived with his squadron of 14 vessels and 350 Portuguese soldiers. This force, combined with the garrison at Daman, attacked the besieging Mughal army, which, despite being greatly superior in numbers, was forced to retreat. Britto then sailed for the Bharuch port, burning part of the town and all the vessels lying in the river. He subsequently attacked and burned Bhadbhut, which was held by the Rajputs, resulting in the deaths of 450 of them.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
These incidents illustrate that although nearly 70 years had passed since the time of D Jao Castro, the Portuguese in India had not modified their old policy of terrorising the coastal towns of Gujarat to maintain their claims. At the same time, the smaller kings and the great Mughals had not learned any lessons and not taken effective steps to strengthen their navy. The Portuguese exploited this inability of the Mughals to their full advantage. Their viceroy, Jeronimo Azavedo, at Goa, collected a great armada and personally sailed to Surat in December 1614 to deliver a decisive blow against the great city, completing the series of reprisals made by his captains against the Gujarat ports.
The Portuguese and English clash at sea
A few weeks before, Captain Nicholas Downtown reached Surat on October 15 with a fleet of four ships and 400 men sent out by the East India Company. Muquarrab Khan was pleased to learn of this but was disappointed when Downtown flatly refused his request for support on the grounds that there was peace between the English and the Spaniards. The Portuguese, however, made a tactical mistake. Taking the English neutrality to be a weakness, the Portuguese viceroy decided to use this opportunity to crush the English attempt to intrude upon the Portuguese monopoly of trade on the west coast of India. Another major assumption was that success in the struggle with the Mughal power depended on visibility and the ability to destroy Downtown’s small fleet, which stood between him and the attack on Surat.
In the decisive battle that took place on January 20, 1615, the English, despite their smaller numbers, carried the day due to the sheer valour of their crew. The English flagship, Hope, was anchored some distance ahead of the others. The Portuguese viceroy sent three of his great ships, along with some frigates, to grapple with her and to pour swarms of Portuguese soldiers on board the Hope. After boarding, they soon engaged in hand-to-hand combat with the English crew. Other English ships quickly came to the rescue, directing a steady stream of fire into the enemy’s men of war. At the end of a desperate struggle, the Portuguese soldiers were driven back from the Hope, suffering heavy casualties. Many were killed or threw themselves overboard, leaving the shore littered the next day with the bodies of those who drowned.
The failure of the Portuguese armada was also due to their galleons being cumbersome and sailing slowly, while their guns, though more numerous, were operated with much less skill than those of the English. When Jahangir heard the news of the Portuguese naval disaster, he was obviously delighted by this serendipitous turn of events and recorded it in his autobiography. Within six months of the defeat, a treaty of peace was signed between the Portuguese viceroy and the Mughal governor on 7th June 1615. One result was the withdrawal of forces besieging Daman, which thus once again escaped conquest and absorption into the Mughal empire.

(Dr Amarjit Singh is a retired IAS officer from the Gujarat cadre who has held posts in the central and state governments.)

headline: CBI arrests mastermind of CAPF recruitment scam in West Bengal
description: The arrest comes after a Calcutta High Court order on August 2, 2023, prompted the CBI to launch an investigation into the allegations of undeserving candidates receiving CAPF appointments using forged domicile certificates.
content:
In a significant breakthrough in the alleged Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) recruitment scam in West Bengal, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested the alleged mastermind behind the fraudulent scheme.
The arrest comes after a Calcutta High Court order on August 2, 2023, prompted the CBI to launch an investigation into the allegations of undeserving candidates receiving CAPF appointments using forged domicile certificates.
The arrested individual, identified as Mahesh Kumar Choudhary, a Sepoy at the Engineering Store Depot (ESD) in Kanikinara, North 24 Parganas, is accused of orchestrating a racket that provided fake West Bengal domicile certificates, including those claiming residency in border or Naxal-affected districts.
Choudhary’s name was already listed in the initial FIR, which also named Raju Gupta and other unknown individuals.
CBI investigations revealed Choudhary’s central role in the scam, showing he collected substantial sums of money from candidates, directly and through intermediaries.
Following searches at multiple locations, Choudhary was apprehended on January 31, 2024. He was presented before the CBI Court No 1 in Alipore and has been remanded to five days of police custody. The CBIs investigation is underway.

headline: How a 35-yr-old farmer has mushroomed a success story in this Sangrur village
description: Growing seasonal and off-season mushrooms on a 3-acre farm, generating sales worth around Rs. 1 crore, while earning 10 times more than the combined income from wheat and paddy.
content:
Baljit Singh Gill, a 35-year-old progressive farmer from Kakra village in Bhawani Garh tehsil of Sangrur district, has transformed the traditional mushroom farming model in Punjab.
What began as a modest venture 15 years ago has now grown into a thriving business with innovative practices that caters to the round-the-year demand for mushrooms.
While mushrooms are typically grown in Punjab during the Rabi season (October to March), Gill produces the crop throughout the year. He has set up four air-conditioned sheds to that maintain the ideal temperature for mushroom cultivation.
Over a decade and a half back, he started with just one small open shed of 225 square feet. He gradually expanded his operation to cover 3 acres of his 6-acre farm.

He now operates 26 makeshift sheds, each measuring 60×30 feet and spread across two acres, to grow seasonal mushroom. The sheds, which are designed to hold over 2,000 bags each, have compost to grow the crop. He also has four air-conditioned rooms, each measuring 40×17 feet with a height of 17 feet, featuring six shelves in each room with a capacity to hold 1,500 bags, and four compost making units spread across the remaining one acre.
These rooms help maintain a consistent temperature of 18°C, making year-round cultivation possible. With his innovative approach, Gill is not only meeting the needs of his regular customers but is also tapping into a lucrative market. He sells mushroom worth Rs. One crore including over Rs 20 lakh annually grown in four AC rooms. This season, he produced 1.20 lakh kg (1200 quintals) button mushroom from 60,000 bags, with each bag yielding about 2 kg of mushrooms. The harvest typically begins in late November and continues till March.
“I earn between Rs 70,000 to Rs 80,000 per shed after meeting my expenses and earn a net profit of around Rs 23 lakh from 3-acre in just six months which around 10 times more than traditional crops. With traditional crops such as wheat and paddy earnings are around Rs 2.25 to Rs 2.50 lakh from three acres annually,” he says, adding that the investment in cash crops is high, but the results are very promising.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
While for mushrooms the efforts are way more that the traditional crops, he said that the returns are also much higher.
While mushrooms are typically grown in Punjab during the Rabi season (October to March), Gill produces the crop throughout the year. (Express Photo)
“I wanted to meet the year-round demand from my customers, so I decided to grow mushrooms in air-conditioned sheds. Bag filling, spawning for the summer season mushroom has already taken place in my AC rooms and from February 15, we start maintaining the temperature of 18 degrees Celsius,” he says.
Mushroom cultivation requires careful management of several factors, including compost preparation, which is made from dry wheat fodder. He also benefits from a 40% subsidy on compost-making units provided by the government.
Not only has Gill seen remarkable financial success, but he has also earned recognition for his efforts. He was twice awarded by the Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) Sangrur for his progressive farming methods. KVK Sangrur associate director Mandeep Singh said, “Gill has proven that with determination and right technology, nothing is impossible. By using air-conditioning to grow the crop even during the summer months, he has set a new standard in the agricultural community. Gill’s story highlights how modern technology, combined with hard work and creative thinking, can turn traditional farming practices into a profitable and sustainable business,” Singh says.

headline: Dhankhar at Kumbh: ‘Accident happened… but just imagine the speed with which the situation was handled’
description: Speaking to reporters, he said the world would be astonished to know that the number of people who have arrived at the Maha Kumbh is almost equal to the population of the United States of America.
content:
Vice-President Jagdeep Dhankhar on Saturday took a dip in the Sangam and showered praises on Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for the “excellent” arrangements at the Maha Kumbh.
Speaking to reporters, he said the world would be astonished to know that the number of people who have arrived at the Maha Kumbh is almost equal to the population of the United States of America.
“This is historic… to date, so many people have never come together anywhere on the Earth. The arrangements and the work done by the administration are excellent… I am overwhelmed. I had never imagined that such an event would be organised in India,” he said.
Referring to the January 29 stampede at Maha Kumbh in which at least 30 people were killed, Dhankhar said: “Haadsa hua par andaza lagaiye ki kitna tuarit gati se maamle ko handle kiya gaya (The accident happened… But just imagine the speed with which the situation was handled).”
Dhankhar said Adityanath must be praised for organising a historic event and highlighted that more than one lakh toilets have been built for the Maha Kumbh and the visitors were getting top quality food. “When I took the dip, it was the happiest moment of my life. I’ve realised that there is no country like India in the world. Yogi ji has shown that if you have dedication, ability, knowledge of culture and a feeling of service towards the nation, then miraculous work can be done,” he said.
He also offered prayers at the Maha Kumbh and described the event as a blessing, the Uttar Pradesh government said in a statement. Dhankhar, along with his wife and family members, reached Prayagraj in a helicopter and was welcomed by Chief Minster Adityanath.

headline: Delhi Police gets Rs 12,000 crore in Budget, 7% surge compared to last time
description: The Budget has been allocated for routine expenses as well as infrastructure and IT projects, including developing a modern traffic system and communication networks.
content:
The Delhi Police has been allocated Rs 12,259.16 crore in the Union Budget 2025-26 — an increase of Rs 858.35 crore or about 7.4% compared to the last fiscal.
The Budget has been allocated for routine expenses as well as infrastructure and IT projects, including developing a modern traffic system and communication networks.
The increase in allocation this year will help in boosting several flagship schemes, including the Safe City project which the Delhi Police is working on, an official said.
Under the category of revenue allocation, the force has received Rs 11,315.63 crore — the funds are expected to be used in developing traffic and communication networks in NCR, upgradation or expansion of communication infrastructure, upgradation of training, induction of latest technology and installation of traffic signals, another official said.
Under the Capital allocation, the force has received Rs 943.53 crore.
The funds given under this category will be used for the construction of new buildings, and the purchase of vehicles and weapons. This will also help in setting up various units of Delhi Police, the official added.
In the Budget presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in Parliament on Saturday, emphasis has been laid on making the police technically strong, he added.

content:

headline: Mangaluru police shoot at second key bank robbery suspect after alleged escape bid
description: Key accused Murugandi Thevar allegedly attacked accompanying policemen when he was taken to Ajji Nadaka in Mangaluru to find a gun hidden by an accomplice.
content:
The Mangaluru police investigating a Rs 15 crore robbery – wherein 18.3 kg of gold was stolen from a cooperative bank in the city on January 17 – shot a key accused in the case below his knee on Saturday after the accused allegedly attacked policemen and tried to flee during the process of finding a gun hidden by an accomplice ahead of the robbery.
The Mangaluru police said Murugandi Thevar, 36, who was arrested three days after the robbery from Tirunelveli in Tamil Nadu, volunteered to reveal the location of a gun hidden by an associate, identified as Shashi Thevar, at a location in Mangaluru. But he allegedly attacked the accompanying policemen when he was taken to the Ajji Nadaka neighbourhood.
“In response, the Ullal Inspector first fired a warning shot into the air. However, as Murugandi Thevar continued to flee despite the warning, a second round was fired below his knee,” the Mangaluru police said.
Following the incident, constable Manjunath and Murugandi Thevar were admitted to a private hospital for medical treatment.
Earlier on January 21, shortly after three of the eight persons involved in the January 17 bank robbery were arrested in Tamil Nadu, the Mangaluru city police fired gunshots at one of the arrested accused.
The suspect, Kannan Mani, 36, who was also arrested in Tirunelveli on January 20, was shot after he was taken for a spot inspection at the crime scene at the bank in Kotekar. He was shot in the leg after he reportedly tried to attack escorting officers.
The gang involved in the Kotekar cooperative bank robbery in Mangaluru is allegedly linked to several crimes that have occurred in Mumbai.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Murugandi Thevar, who reportedly drove the Fiat car used for the January 17 robbery at the Kotekar cooperative bank, is also accused of involvement in a 2016 armed robbery at the Popular Finance Company in Seawoods in Navi Mumbai, where gold and cash to the tune of Rs 6 crore were looted by a five-member gang. Murugandi Thevar was also the alleged driver of the getaway car in the 2016 Navi Mumbai robbery and was out on bail in that case.
The two others who have been arrested by the Mangaluru police for the January 17 armed bank robbery have been identified as Yosuva Rajendran alias Joshua alias Prakash, 35, from Dombivli West and Kannan Mani alias Manivannan, 36, from Chembur in Mumbai.
The police have recovered the entire 18.3 kg of gold looted from the Kotekar bank from the home of Murugandi Thevar in Tirunelveli.

headline: Worker killed in ammonia leak at pharma company lab in Vadodara; 4 hospitalised
description: The incident occurred in the lab of Apothecon Pharmaceuticals located on Padra-Jambusar highway; condition of 4 employees stable.
content:
An ammonia gas leak at a pharmaceutical company in Padra taluka of Vadodara district late on Friday evening killed one person and left four others unconscious, police said Saturday.
The incident occurred in the lab of the R&D department of Apothecon Pharmaceutical Private Limited — a company involved in the manufacture of “highly potent, niche generic APIs from the oncology segment”, located on Padra-Jambusar highway.
Police said that a worker, Dharmendra Solanki, 22, collapsed on the premises of the company and was rushed to a private hospital nearby, where he was declared dead on arrival. Four others who were also affected by exposure to the gas were rushed to a hospital.
The four hospitalised employees have been identified as Ruval Rathod, Pradeepsinh Sindha, Ilesh Govil and Arjun Padhiyar.
Speaking to The Indian Express, Vadodara district Superintendent of Police Rohan Anand said, “We have lodged a case of accidental death at Padra police station and begun a probe into the incident. If any negligence is found on the part of the company during the course of the probe, an FIR will be lodged.”
Anand added that the four hospitalised employees were said to be “stable”.

headline: Booster packages, easing of income tax slabs – what Industries want from Budget 2025
description: The MSME sector, as per surveys of the Mahratta Chamber of Commerce Industries and Agriculture (MCCIA), is optimistic about growth with most units talking about a double-digit growth.
content:
Ahead of the 2024-25 Union budget, Pune has hopes that Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman will address long-standing issues regarding income tax and availability of industrial land. Micro and small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in particular hope that the budget would announce a special package for them to help them keep their growth momentum.
Sandeep Belsare, president of the Pimpri Chinchwad Small Scale Industries Association, said they wanted income-tax slabs to be raised to ensure more savings in the hands of the people. For the MSME sector, Belsare said the budget should announce a special booster package for the MSME sector. ‘The sector is now going through a plateau and this package would help kickstart the sector,” he said.
The MSME sector, as per surveys of the Mahratta Chamber of Commerce Industries and Agriculture (MCCIA), is optimistic about growth with most units talking about a double-digit growth. Credit outlay for the sector has also seen good growth as business has picked up. But many in the sector have complained of bottlenecks, which they hope the union minister would iron out.
Another concern the sector wants to be addressed is the lack of land for startups especially in manufacturing. Abhay Bhor, president of the Federation of Small Scale Industries Association, talked of schemes that would allow them to get land at economical rates. “Since the last five years, a large number of micro units have closed down. The finance minister should make efforts to ensure they restart, as such units are employment generators,” he said.
Luxury car manufacturer Mercedes Benz hopes the budget would push for infrastructure development and R&D incentives. Managing Director and CEO Santosh Iyer also pointed out that reduction of trade barriers and simplifying regulatory frameworks would help the country break further into the global network.
Warren Harris, CEO and MD of Tata Technologies, said that the budget should prioritise innovation-driven policies and invest in emerging technologies. “Key growth drivers such as smart manufacturing, AI, digital transformation, and software-defined vehicles (SDVs) require strong government backing through incentives for R&D, skill development, and infrastructure enhancement. We recommend increased allocation toward upskilling initiatives aligned with Industry 4.0, creating a future-ready workforce capable of excelling in advanced technologies like AI, IoT, and cybersecurity,” he said.

headline: Budget expectations: Salaried class people want lower taxes, promoting job creation
description: With Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman set to present the 2025 Union Budget on February 1, both corporate employees and ordinary citizens have various expectations from this budget.
content:
By Sonali Priya and Riddhi Wadhwani,
With Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman set to present the 2025 Union Budget on February 1, both corporate employees and ordinary citizens have various expectations from this budget.
Lower taxes on housing, rentals
Alkesh Santosh Lajurkar, a 23-year-old employee at Asset Analytix in Pune, hopes the government will prioritise healthcare and education. Lajurkar said, “Taxes on housing and rent should be lowered, as food, clothing and shelter are basic necessities for the middle class. Inflation and GST on essential items like groceries and medicines have reduced my purchasing power.” He added that saving money has become more difficult, as a large part of his income is spent on taxes. Due to inflation, their salary is not incremented yet. Lajurkar also suggested that the government should prioritise policies that encourage startups and job creation.
No tax upto Rs 10 lakh income
Shilpa Sanap, a 25-year-old employee at MKCL in Pune, said, “My salary is 34,000, but I only received 28,000 after 7,000 was deducted in taxes. I would suggest there be no tax up to Rs 10 lakh as it would allow me to meet my basic needs while also saving or investing some money.” She aded that since she travels by scooter, it sometimes becomes difficult to afford petrol. Currently, petrol is taxed through VAT, but she believes that applying GST on petrol would improve the situation.
Lower interest rates for startups
Prathmesh Gurjar, a 25-year-old political science teacher at Modern College, Ganeshkhind shared his views on the 2025 Budget. “This year, there should be a higher allocation in the education sector, especially for research and development, as human development is crucial and will benefit the future,” Prathmesh said. He also felt the interest rates on loans for startups should be as low as possible, as this would encourage young people to develop and implement more ideas, ultimately leading to the creation of more job opportunities. Also, there must be low disinvestment.
Lower food, entertainment taxes
Priyanka Dhoot, a 25 year old content manager at AOS Brand Consultants in Pune, said, “From this year, I’ll be in the tax bracket, that of 5 per cent, but I don’t think it will have much impact.” Dhoot added that infrastructure was still lacking and there were a lot of areas that required attention. Expressing her concerns over high taxes on dining and entertainment, she said, “Restaurant taxes are so steep that 30-40 per cent of what I spend goes to taxes.”
Income tax professional and chartered accountant Ravi Patil hoped the government would ensure better and easier tax rates for industries. “A lot of this comes on the final consumer indirectly,” he said.

headline: Missing for 12 days, Shinde Sena’s leader’s body found in car dumped in stone quarry in Gujarat
description: Four arrested, three including the deceased's brother, on the run.
content:
Ashok Dhodi, a senior activist of Shiv Sena (Eknath Shinde), was on Friday found dead in his car, which was found 45 feet deep in a defunct stone quarry in Bhilad, Gujarat, 12 days after he was reported missing. The Palghar police have already arrested four persons for the murder, and the accused on Friday took police to the spot where they dumped Dhodi’s body.
Dhodi’s younger brother is allegedly behind the murder and is on the run along with two other associates. A decade-old fight between families of two brothers over control over local mafia is prima facia seen as the motive behind the killing, the police said.
Dhodi was missing since January 20. His family told police that while returning home from Mumbai, he had called his wife informing her that he was coming home, but he did not reach home and his mobile was also found switched off.
“After eight days of investigation, we nabbed four accused who were involved in the crime. On the basis of information revealed during their interrogation, our team on Friday reached a defunct stone quarry in Bhilad and we managed to lift Dhodi’s car from 45-feet down the quarry,” said Balasaheb Patil, Superintendent of Police, Palghar.

Car’s glass shreds and Dhodi’s spectacles found on the turn of a road with marks of car’s tyres on the road at a stretch became the first clue in our case. We worked on the clue and nabbed the four involved in the crime,” the SP added.

headline: Pune on my plate: ‘Lose customers or lose profits’, inflation leaves street food vendors in the lurch
description: As vendors face the heat of inflation, many have resorted to ‘shrinkflation’ to survive, which means providing a product at the same price but reducing its size or quantity.
content:
BY SONALI PIRYA, ABHIJIT SHEREKAR, ARYESH CHAKRABORTY
Your favourite cup of tea or that piping hot Vada Pav you would enjoy on your way home from school or work isn’t the same anymore. Inflation has steadily crept up, with popular go-to street snacks seeing the most prominent price increases. Roadside vendors who claim to work on paper-thin margins said they are forced to increase prices as they do not “have the capacity to digest the losses.” They are, however, stuck between a rock and a hard place. Increase prices and lose customers or lose profits without raising prices.
Shubham Gupta, who runs a chat and vada pav stall on FC Road for the last 4 years said he was forced to increase the price of his tea from Rs 8/- to Rs 10/cup. He had hiked the price of vada pav from Rs 12 to the present going cost of Rs 20 last year. But Gupta admits, even this hike is not enough to make his ends meet. “It’s a choice between the devil and the deep sea for us, if we increase prices we lose customers and if we don’t we incur losses,” he said.
Poha, a staple breakfast option across Pune has also seen its price increasing. Most vendors in Kothrud now price it about Rs 20. “But from February, I’ll have to increase it to Rs 30 to sustain my business and to make profit,”said a vendor from Kothrud requesting anonymity.
As vendors face the heat of inflation, many have resorted to ‘shrinkflation’ to survive, which means providing a product at the same price but reducing its size or quantity.
Misal, a signature dish for Pune, has perhaps seen the highest price rise. It now hovers around Rs 60-100 depending upon the popularity of the location and taste. ‘We are crushed from both sides, on one side there is a consistent increase in prices of cylinder, potato, tomato and other materials but on the other hand when we increase the prices of products, customers complain or tend to shift to other shop or decrease their consumption, says Raju Tare owner of Pratiksha Bhel and Pav Bhaji corner at Sanghvi. Most vendors here have raised the price of misal to Rs 80-120m, with more price rises on the anvil.
Sanjay Kadukar who owns Tanishk Snacks center near Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) said that he was forced to raise the price of vadapav to Rs 15 from Rs 12  last year.  Some of the roadside vendors have taken to working by themselves and laid off staff to make ends meet.  Most street vendors echoed the sentiment that the cost of ingredients such as potatoes, chickpea flour, onions, and milk has surged significantly, forcing them to increase the prices of their dishes.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Not just local vendors, but famous establishments in Pune, such as Joshi Vada Wala and Santosh Bakery, have also raised their prices. An employee at Santosh Bakery said, “In 2023, our most popular item, patties, was priced at ₹18. Now, it costs ₹20. We increase the price by ₹1 each year.”
Starting this January, Joshi Vada Wala also raised the price of vada pav from ₹20 to ₹25.

headline: Total suspected GBS deaths in Pune rises to four
description: Total suspected GBS cases now at 140.
content:
Two people who were diagnosed with guillain barre syndrome (GBS) in Pune have died, state health authorities said on Friday. One of the victims, a 60-year-old man from Dhayari, Sinhagad Road, died after suffering a cardiac arrest at Poona Hospital on Friday morning. The other man, a 36-year-old cab driver from Pimple Gurav, died of severe acute respiratory distress syndrome at YCM Hospital Pimpri on Thursday, January 30.
The count of suspected GBS deaths has now gone up to four and the total number of cases is at 140.
The 60-year-old man who originally hails from Buldhana and in Pune stayed at Dhayari, was diagnosed with both GBS and a rare condition called bickerstaff brainstem encephalitis (BBE), which according to Dr Sudhir Kothari, consulting neurologist at Poona Hospital and Research Centre, was a rare and unusual case.
“The patient had reported symptoms like loose motion and lower limb weakness. He was also drowsy and unable to pass urine. BBE is a rare disorder where the brainstem becomes inflamed,” Dr Kothari said.
He was admitted to Poona hospital on January 27, was intubated and put on ventilator support.
The condition was confirmed after an MRI and stool PCR tests also identified the patient had Campylobacter jejuni. “This bacterium can trigger GBS by confusing the immune system into attacking the body’s nerves. He had beenwas responding to treatment over the last couple of days but died of cardiac arrest today,” Dr Kothari said.
In the case of the cab driver, the primary cause of death was pneumonia, Shekhar Singh, Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Commissioner who visited the hospital on Friday, told The Indian Express.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The cab driver who was admitted to YCM hospital on January 21 with GBS-like symptoms, underwent a nerve conduction test on January 22. The death audit committee experts confirmed that the patient had GBS.
Dr Laxman Gophane, medical officer of health, Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation, said the immediate cause of his death was acute respiratory distress syndrome.
The YCM hospital presently has nine patients with GBS, of which five are in the intensive care unit and one is on ventilator support.
“Precautionary measures have been taken. Ventilator management protocols are in place and our doctors and physicians have gone through ARDS management,” Singh said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
GBS is a rare neurological disorder and respiratory muscles in some patients also get impacted. PCMC authorities have appealed citizens not to panic and has also set up a helpline number (7758933017) to respond to queries from citizens.
Earlier, a 56-year-old woman from Kirkatwadi, Sinhagad Road, who was suffering from oral cancer, and a 40- year-old man from Solapur were suspected to have died due to GBS related complications.

description: Rajya Sabha MP Medha Kulkarni had visited the Ram-Mula confluence last Thursday at the behest of environmentalists and citizens' groups and spent two-and-a-half hours there.
content:
On Thursday, Rajya Sabha MP Medha Kulkarni updated the Guardian Minister Ajit Pawar on concerns about the threat to trees and the river because of the Riverfront Development Project (RFD). The commissioners of PMC and PCMC and Collector were present at the meeting. “We presented our queries about the project to the Guardian Minister and he said that he would think over this,” said Kulkarni.
The MP had visited the Ram-Mula confluence last Thursday at the behest of environmentalists and citizens’ groups and spent two-and-a-half hours there.
Kulkarni, who belongs to the BJP, has insisted that the RFD should be carried out without harming nature. Across the city, many groups are opposing the methods in which the RFD is being implemented. While Kulkarni takes the struggle to the top, there is on-ground mobilisation to send a strong message against the RFD in Pune. On February 9, citizens and organisations under the umbrella of Pune River Revival organised a Chipko March under the tagline “Save Trees, Save Rivers”. It will start at the Kalmadi High School and culminate at the Ram Mula Confluence in Baner.
“The reason for the march is that the RFD work from Wakad to Sangvi has started. Currently, the work is going on on the PCMC side. On the PMC side, thousands of trees, like the Indian willow, have been tagged. We will walk to the Ram-Mula confluence and hug the trees that have been tagged. content:

This plan covers an area of 20,550 square meters and envisions a 276 km metro network along with six new Bus Rapid Transit System (BRT) corridors over the next three decades.
The plan will be implemented in three phases at an estimated cost of Rs 1,26,489 crore. Various government agencies will be involved in its execution.
Proposals for Vanaz to Chandni Chowk and Ramwadi to Wagholi metro routes have been sent to the central government for approval. Besides this, a 128 km metro corridor has been planned, covering routes like District Court to Alandi, Wakad Chowk to Shewalewadi. headline: Criminal misconduct probe sought against suspended IPS officer Qaiser Khalid in Ghatkopar hoarding collapse
description: The crime branch has recommended that the case be transferred to the state’s Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), as they handle cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
content:
The Mumbai Police crime branch, investigating the May 2024 Ghatkopar hoarding collapse that claimed 17 lives, submitted a report to the Maharashtra home department last week, revealing potential criminal misconduct by suspended IPS officer Qaiser Khalid. The report alleges that Khalid’s actions led to losses to the state exchequer and may constitute offenses under the Prevention of Corruption Act (PCA).
The crime branch has recommended that the case be transferred to the state’s Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), as they handle cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act. So far, the crime branch has arrested five persons and filed charges against four in connection with the collapse.
A government official said the investigation uncovered that although the land on which the hoarding was erected belonged to the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), Khalid, who was the Government Railway Police (GRP) Commissioner at the time, allegedly instructed a law officer to alter his report to state that the land belonged to the Railways. This action is said to have caused financial losses to the state. Additionally, the Crime Branch found that the tendering process for the hoarding violated government regulations.
The report specifically references Section 13 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, which deals with criminal misconduct by public servants. This section states that a public servant can be charged if they dishonestly or fraudulently misappropriate property entrusted to them or intentionally enrich themselves illicitly while in office.
While the Crime Branch has not yet directly linked Khalid to a financial trail, the chargesheet notes that Arshad Khan, an accused in the case, took Rs 84 lakh from Bhavesh Bhinde, the owner of the illegal hoarding that collapsed. Khan was also a partner in a company where Khalid’s wife was a partner. Khan told police that he provided services to Bhinde and was paid for them.
According to the Crime Branch, Khan had received cheques from Bhinde, which were then deposited into various bank accounts before being converted into cash.
So far, the crime branch has officially not clarified what happened to the cash handed over to Arshad.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Sources said a decision on the report sent by them would either be taken by CM Devendra Fadnavis who is also the home minister or the additional chief secretary (home). An official said that under Section 17(A), an approval from the state government would be needed to carry out a probe against a government servant under the PC Act.
“Once the government approves the same, it can hand it over to the ACB which may either begin an enquiry on the facts mentioned in the report or register an offence against Khalid,” the source said.
Soon after the case came to light, the Maharashtra government suspended IPS officer Khalid who has not yet been reinstated. The government also formed a judicial commission to probe the rules flouted in the collapse.
Incidentally, Khalid had been summoned by the ACB on Wednesday in connection with a complaint given against him by a person who claimed to have sponsored the officer’s hotel stay in the US to get a hoarding contract at Dadar.  The agency had begun the probe against the officer in July last year. Khalid did not appear before the agency and sought more time.

description: The court further observed that the CBI informed the Calcutta High Court about the sanction bypassing the lower court.
content:
Pulling up the CBI for not informing the trial court about the West Bengal government giving sanction to prosecute Dr Sandip Ghosh, the former principal of RG Kar Medical College and Hospital, and another doctor in a corruption case, special court judge Sujit Kumar Jha on Thursday ordered the central agency to submit in writing the reason why it failed to do so.
Issuing the show-cause notice to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), which is probing the financial irregularities in the state-run hospital in the wake of the rape and murder of a junior doctor, the judge expressed dissatisfaction, saying three days had passed since the state government’s nod but the CBI did not inform the court. CBI Investigating Officer Manish Upadhyay told the court that the agency had received the required sanction from the state government on January 27, “but they were busy with the investigation and therefore were unable to inform the court”.
The court further observed that the CBI informed the Calcutta High Court about the sanction bypassing the lower court.

With the CBI submitting the chargesheet against Ghosh and others in the case, the court directed the probe agency to produce all documents related to the case on the next hearing date. The judge ordered the CBI to bring all evidence, including electronic evidence, to the court and hand over copies of the documents to all the accused so that the charges could be framed and the trial could begin soon.
The court’s direction came after the lawyers of the accused alleged that they had not received all the documents from the CBI.
On November 29 last year, the CBI had submitted a 100-page chargesheet against Ghosh, and approval was required under section 218 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for the trial to start. The CBI has arrested former principal Sandip Ghosh, doctor and TMC youth leader Ashish Pandey and three others — Biplab Singh, Afsar Ali, and Suman Hazra – in connection with the alleged financial irregularities at the Kolkata hospital.

headline: AAP collects water samples from Yamuna, challenges BJP and Congress leaders to drink it
description: AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh, during a press conference, said the Nayab Singh Saini-led Haryana government had ignored appeals from the Delhi government to rectify the problem of ammonia entering the riverstream from the neighbouring state.
content:
With four bottles of water that had “7 ppm of ammonia and chlorine”, each labelled with the names of Home Minister Amit Shah, Delhi BJP chief Virendra Sachdeva, Haryana CM Nayab Singh Saini and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi, the AAP challenged the leaders to take a sip at a press conference or issue a public apology.
AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh, during a press conference, said the Nayab Singh Saini-led Haryana government had ignored appeals from the Delhi government to rectify the problem of ammonia entering the riverstream from the neighbouring state.
Kejriwal said, “Today, we have kept bottles of 7 ppm ammonia water mixed with chlorine. The BJP and Congress have joined forces — both are playing with the health and lives of the people of Delhi. We are sending these bottles to: Amit Shah, Virendra Sachdeva, Nayab Singh Saini and Rahul Gandhi. Let these four leaders drink this ammonia-mixed water in a press conference. If they do, we will accept that we were wrong,” he said.
The EC has sent notices to Kejriwal for calling the water “poisonous”.
During the press conference, Kejriwal said, “Toxic water means that the level of ammonia in it has risen significantly — up to 7 ppm. Ammonia at this level is extremely dangerous to health; it can cause irreversible damage to multiple organs and pose a severe health hazard. It can even be fatal — exposure to such high levels of ammonia in water can lead to death.”
He said his party raised this issue a few days ago because it was left with no choice. “… Atishi ji called Nayab Singh Saini ji — once, twice, three times, four times — requesting him to take action, as the rising ammonia levels posed a threat to lives.”
Hitting back at Kejriwal, Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Thursday released a video flagging the issue of pollutants in Yamuna and challenged Kejriwal to take a dip in it.

headline: Sukanta Majumdar meets RG Kar rape-murder victim’s family, says will raise their issues with CBI probe
description: The parents handed him a letter, detailing their grievances about the CBI’s investigation into the case.
content:
West Bengal BJP president and Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar on Thursday visited the parents of the R G Kar hospital rape and murder victim and assured them that he would forward their grievances against the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to “appropriate authorities”.
The parents handed him a letter, detailing their grievances about the CBI’s investigation into the case.
While speaking with the mediapersons Majumdar pointed out that the parents are “unsatisfied” with the probe.
“I have told them to keep the fight on. They are not satisfied with the investigation of the state police and the CBI. Previously the parents alleged that they were under pressure to not meet us. We assured them that we are with them,” he said, adding, “They have particularly raised concerns about one CBI officer, alleging inadequate efforts in the probe.”
Read | CBI moves HC against life sentence to convict after objecting to state govt’s similar plea
“The parents are under constant attack from TMC leaders who made demeaning statements as they raised questions against the state administration and continued their fight for justice,” Majumdar said.
Meanwhile, the victim doctor’s father said the family discussed with Majumdar on how to take forward their fight for justice. “Sukanta Majumdar gave us guidelines of how to go forward. I have given him a letter, which is addressed to the Director of CBI, where I have expressed my dissatisfaction with the CBI team’s investigation. He has assured me that the letter will reach the proper hands,” he said.
Later in the evening, the victim doctor’s family met with Governor C V Ananda Bose. After an hour long meeting the father told mediapersons, “I asked for justice for my daughter and also that the CBI should do their investigation properly. I have even informed the Governor that I would like to meet the President of India, Prime Minister and Home Minister in this regard. He has said we have his complete support.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The post-graduate trainee doctor was raped and murdered at the RG Kar Medical College and Hospital on August 9, 2024, triggering nationwide outrage. The investigation into the case was handed to the CBI by the Calcutta High Court. A civic volunteer, named Sanjay Roy, was convicted by a court in the rape and murder case, and sentenced to life imprisonment till death.
However, the parents of the doctor claimed that the investigation was done half-heartedly and several other culprits involved in the crime were shielded.
They had also demanded the resignation of Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee, stating that being the CM, she cannot disown the responsibility for the “attempts of the police and hospital authorities to destroy evidence of the rape and murder of our daughter”. — WITH PTI

headline: Election Commission says Arvind Kejriwal’s ‘Haryana poisoning Yamuna’ claim promotes disharmony, enmity
description: The Election Commission wrote to AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal asking for evidence of the poisoning of Yamuna by 11 am on Friday.
content:
The Election Commission of India (ECI) on Thursday wrote to Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convener Arvind Kejriwal, saying that his allegation that the BJP-ruled Haryana government had poisoned Delhi’s water supply from the Yamuna river was prima facie “promoting disharmony and enmity between different groups”. The EC asked him to submit evidence to support his allegation by 11 am on Friday.
Acting on complaints by the BJP and the Congress, the EC wrote to Kejriwal on Tuesday asking him to provide the “factual and legal matrix” for his allegation made during the ongoing Assembly elections campaign. The EC had said that the complaint from Delhi Chief Minister Atishi and Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on the high levels of ammonia in the water supply to the Capital from Haryana was being dealt with separately from Kejriwal’s allegation of “poisoning”.
Kejriwal responded on Wednesday, saying that Delhi had recently received water from Haryana that was “highly contaminated and extremely poisonous for human health”.
In reply to Kejriwal’s response, the EC wrote on Thursday that his response was “entirely silent on your public and widely circulated” statement regarding the poisoning of the water supply. The EC noted that all governments concerned should engage in securing sufficient and clean water for residents and that it would leave the matter to the “competence and good discretion of the governments and agencies”.
“Coming back to your response on your statement under reference, Commission has prima facie found your allegations about poisoning of river Yamuna as promoting disharmony and enmity between different groups, and overall public disorder and unrest even by the most sober interpretation…as a prominent public figure and a former Chief Minister, the Commission need not remind you of the dire consequences that such utterances and actions of yours can have and leave permanent scars between well identifiable groups of residents of two States and/or living together in State of Haryana and NCT of Delhi,” the EC wrote.
The EC asked Kejriwal what kind of poison was mixed by Haryana, what was the supporting evidence about the quantity, nature and manner of detecting poison and the location where and the method of detection of the poison.

headline: Dalit man’s ‘honour killing’: wife’s grandmother, father and brothers among 6 arrested in Telangana
description: Telangana police said they have arrested under charges of murder and conspiracy, and those under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
content:
Days after a 32-year-old Dalit man was found murdered and his body dumped near a canal in Telangana’s Suryapet district, the police said Wednesday they have arrested six people, including his wife’s grandmother, father, and two brothers in connection with the case.
The Suryapet police said they have arrested Bhargavi’s Kotla grandmother Buchamma, 65, father Kotla Saidulu, 43, and brothers Kotla Naveen, 24, and Kotla Vamshi, 22, for the murder of Vadlakonda Krishna. The police also arrested their friends Bairu Mahesh, 30, and Nuvvula Sai Charan, 23, in the case.
Sunpreet Singh, Superintendent of Police, Suryapet, said they have been arrested under charges of murder and conspiracy, and those under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989. “Saidulu and his sons planned and executed the murder to punish Krishna for marrying Bhargavi against their will,” said Singh.
The police said Naveen and Vamshi killed Krishna and then took the body to show it to Buchamma, before dumping it near the River Musi canal.
Singh said Krishna and Naveen were acquaintances, and Krishna frequently visited his house. During this time, Bhargavi fell in love with Krishna, but her family did not approve of their relationship. While Krishna belonged to the Scheduled Caste (SC) Mala community, Bhargavi is from the Backward Classes (BC) Goud community. The police said Krishna and Bhargavi got married on August 7, 2024, without the knowledge of her family, enraging them.
“Naveen, Vamshi, and Mahesh made three unsuccessful attempts to kill Krishna, but due to various reasons such as the presence of the public, etc they could not execute their plan. Krishna was unaware and had no such doubts about their intention to kill him,” said Singh.
The police said Krishna left home after a call from Mahesh Sunday evening, and that Naveen and Vamshi had asked him to call the deceased to an isolated location. Both of them then met and consumed liquor. On Mahesh’s tip-off, the two brothers ambushed Krishna by strangling him and smashing his head. They then stuffed his body into a car and drove it to Buchamma and Saidulu. Afterwards, they dumped the body near the canal.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Krishna’s father David complained to police that Bhargavi’s family was behind the murder, and told them that marrying against her family’s wishes cost his son’s life.

headline: With Dhruv helicopters grounded, Sarang team’s participation in Aero India 2025 doubtful
description: Known for its breathtaking manoeuvres, the Indian Air Force’s Sarang is one of the prime attractions at the biennial Aero India show in Bengaluru.
content:
In this year’s Aero India show, the participation of the Indian Air Force’s premier display team Sarang is uncertain, as all 330 Dhruv advanced light helicopters, or the ALH Dhruv, have been grounded following a crash reported in January.
The Sarang display team, known for its breathtaking manoeuvres, is one of the prime attractions at Aero India, a biennial air show held in Bengaluru. However, the team may miss this edition due to the grounding of its helicopters. Sarang and another IAF team, Suryakiran, have participated in every edition of the show along with international teams.
Following the recent crashes that forced Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) to ground all Dhruv helicopters, Sarang has not confirmed its participation. The team did not participate in an air show held on January 21 and 22 in Vadodara, Gujarat, as it failed to get clearance. Suryakiran performed at the event.
Speaking to indianexpress.com, a source in the IAF said there had been no communication regarding Sarang’s participation in Aero India 2025. “We are waiting for the communication and the team is ready. However, considering the gravity of the past incidents, it may take time for a comprehensive evaluation,” the source added.
Three deaths in Gujarat
The last performance of Sarang was at the Beypore International Water Fest in Kozhikode on January 4. The following day, an Indian Coast Guard ALH Dhruv MK III crashed at Gujarat’s Porbandar Airport, resulting in the deaths of three crew members. In response, HAL directed the temporary grounding of all 330 Dhruv helicopters and is conducting a detailed investigation, including a technical review of the helicopters. A committee has been formed under Air Marshal Vibhas Pande, a former chief of the Indian Air Force Maintenance Command, to provide inputs on the maintenance of Coast Guard helicopters.
An IAF officer said, “Until the investigations are completed and a report with recommendations is submitted, the ALH cannot be flown. We are waiting for the intimation. But even if the Sarang display team receives a positive word at the last minute, they are confident about participating in Aero India 2025.”
The advanced light helicopter variant flown by Sarang is the ALH Dhruv MK I. Safety concerns regarding these helicopters have been raised for some time, with a series of incidents reported. In October last year, an ALH had to make a forced landing due to engine failure during Bihar flood relief operations. In September, an ALH Dhruv MK III of the Coast Guard crashed into the Arabian Sea during a medical evacuation, resulting in the deaths of two personnel onboard.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Sarang was formed in 2003 and its first international public performance took place in 2004 at the Asian Aerospace Show in Singapore. The team, which began with a three-helicopter formation, has since expanded to five helicopters and performed over 1,200 displays at over 385 venues in India and abroad.
The Dhruv helicopter, designed and conceived by HAL, is an all-weather, multi-mission capable helicopter. It features rigid, hingeless rotors, making it highly manoeuvrable and suitable for military roles.

headline: Rajasthan High Court paves way for registration of live-in relationships in state
description: The High Court directed that a copy of the order be sent to the Rajasthan Chief Secretary as well as the Secretary, Department of Justice and Social Welfare, New Delhi, among others, for compliance and that they send a compliance report and steps being taken by March 1.
content:
The Rajasthan High Court on Wednesday directed the state to establish an authority or tribunal to register live-in relationships until a law is enacted for the same.
Hearing a number of petitions, a Bench of Justice Anoop Kumar Dhand said, “The live-in relationship agreement is liable to be registered by the competent authority/tribunal, which is required to be established by the government. Till enactment of the appropriate legislation by the government, let competent authority be established in each district of the state to look into the matter of registration of such live-in relationships.”
The court said the authority would “address and redress the grievances of such partners/couples who have entered in such relationships and the children being born out therefrom. Let a website or web portal be launched in this regard for redressal of the issue arising out of such relationships.”
The court also said that until a law is enacted by the state as well as the Centre, “a scheme of statutory nature is required to be formulated in legal format”, which should fix the liability of the partners regarding responsibility for the upbringing, education and health of children born of such relationships. It should also “fix liability of the male partner for maintenance of the non-earning female partner residing in such relation and children born out of such relationship”.
The Bench put emphasis on the need to ensure the well-being of children born of live-in relationships. “Minor children born out of such relations are expected to be maintained by their parents, and specially by the father, because women from such relations may often be found to be sufferers as well,” it said.
The High Court directed that a copy of the order be sent to the Rajasthan Chief Secretary as well as the Secretary, Department of Justice and Social Welfare, New Delhi, among others, for compliance and that they send a compliance report and steps being taken by March 1.
The court said that several live-in couples, facing “danger from their families and society”, are approaching constitutional courts for the protection of their life and liberty. The court noted that it appears “police agencies are overburdened with investigations and the responsibility of maintaining law and order”, so they don’t get time to address the grievances of such people. “…but certainly, this cannot be a ground for denial” of protection, the court said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“The need of the hour is to take a step to bring out a law or enact new legislation which would look into the matter of live-in relationships and would grant rights and impose obligations on the part of the couples in such relationships. A separate legislation should be competent enough to grant assistance to the children and female partners” who suffer in such relationships, the court said.
The court referred to a larger Bench the matter of whether married persons in live-in relationships with others are entitled to protection.

headline: Irked by Army’s attitude, Punjab and Haryana HC grants additional compensation to Vir Chakra awardee
description: The war-injured officer sustained 80 per cent disability and lost an eye in the war but was not granted enhanced disability benefits under the ‘broad-banding’ policy introduced by the central government in 1996.
content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has directed the Army and the Central government to pay an additional 15 per cent interest on the arrears of war injury pension to an Army Captain who was awarded the Vir Chakra in the 1965 Indo-Pak War.
The court imposed the additional interest for unnecessarily challenging an Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) order in favour of Captain Reet MP Singh of 8 Cavalry, who was decorated with the Vir Chakra for his role in the 1965 war in the Khemkaran sector. He lost an eye in a tank skirmish near Village Machhike in Khemkaran.
The war-injured officer sustained 80 per cent disability and lost an eye in the war but was not granted enhanced disability benefits under the ‘broad-banding’ policy introduced by the central government in 1996.
These enhanced benefits were initially extended by the Ministry of Defence (MoD) only to post-1996 “invalidation” cases, excluding pre-1996 cases and those who were released with disability or war injury pension upon completing their terms, voluntary retirement, or superannuation.
The Supreme Court, however, struck down the cut-off date, quashing the distinction based on the mode of exit from service. It directed that benefits be paid with arrears from 1996, along with 8 per cent interest, to all affected disabled retirees.
Despite these rulings, several AFTs and High Courts had to repeatedly direct authorities to release the benefits. The financial wing of the MoD, however, instructed the Army to challenge such orders, leading to a series of strictures and strong observations, including from the Supreme Court, which criticised the Army’s practice of contesting disability pension cases.
A bench comprising Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma and Justice Meenakshi I Mehta expressed shock that the war hero was dragged into litigation despite the Supreme Court having already settled the issue. The court noted that the AFT had ruled in his favour in 2018, yet the Army was still contesting the decision. It then imposed an additional 15 per cent interest on the amount due to him, to be recovered from the officers responsible for withholding the payment.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Earlier this month, the Supreme Court expressed its displeasure over the Army challenging disability benefits for a veteran who developed diabetes during service. In December 2024, it imposed costs of Rs 50,000 on the Army and the MoD for contesting a military widow’s pension.
In March 2024, the Supreme Court granted disability pension and compensation of Rs 50 lakh to a soldier who had contracted HIV in service and had been denied pension by both the Army and the AFT.
Advocates handling military cases say courts across the country are being flooded with petitions and appeals from military authorities against their own disabled soldiers, widows, and pensioners— a stark contrast to the approach of other ministries and departments.

headline: 5 Mehsana residents held in Mumbai as fake call centre busted
description: An FIR had been filed based on the complaint of one Ashok Kanti Patel from Surendranagar. He had received a call from a person who allegedly identified himself as a broker of a firm named Share Analyst.
content:
The Gujarat Cybercrime Cell Wednesday said it has arrested five members of a gang, which was running a fake call centre in Mumbai. The arrest was made based on a complaint received on the National Cybercrime Reporting Portal (NCRP), it said.
An FIR had been filed based on the complaint of one Ashok Kanti Patel from Surendranagar. He had received a call from a person who allegedly identified himself as a broker of a firm named Share Analyst.
The caller allegedly enticed the complainant with profits and convinced him to invest in certain companies listed on the stock market.
The caller initially asked him to invest small amounts and then gave him a “return” by depositing `35,000 in his bank account. Having developed the victim’s trust, the accused convinced him to invest in “offline trading” for “higher returns”. The victim ended up transferring a total of `9.5 lakh. However, after he stopped receiving further “returns”, the complaint realised that it was a trap and filed the complaint on NCRP.
The Cybercrime Cell tracked the phone numbers of the accused and traced them to D-Wing of JP North Aviva on Mira Road in Mumbai’s Thane.
A police team from Gandhinagar reached the premises, raided it, and arrested the accused, identified as Shaikh Mohammad Jahid Allahrakha, Shakilkhan Yakubkhan Chauhan, Faizan Mohammad Khalid Mohammad Chauhan, Mohammad Junaid Allaudin Shaikh and Ramiz Nasir Sipai. All five are residents of Mehsana.
The police also seized 13 mobile phones, 4 debit cards and recovered a list of potential victims.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In a statement Wednesday, the Cybercrime Cell said that investigation revealed that the accused hid their identities and obtain SIM cards on false names. They would call people and dupe them by convincing them to invest in the stock market.
The accused were booked for cheating and fraud under relevant sections of the IPC and the IT Act.
Detective PI PD Makwana said that the accused are part of an inter-state gang, which would make sure their victims do not approach the police.
The officer said, “After duping their victims, the accused would begin threatening them claiming that all their trades were illegal. Fearing arrest, the victims would not approach the police.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“We believe these accused have entrapped several people from several states, but the victims are not coming forward due to the empty threats. But we urge people to come forward and file complaints,” Makwana also said.

headline: Bombay High Court raises concerns over pendency of 45,000 cases with FSLs in Mumbai, Thane for 5 yrs
description: It said the information provided by the state government showed a  “shocking state of affairs”, resulting in stalling of criminal trials as FSL reports are submitted with inordinate delays.
content:
The Bombay High Court on Wednesday expressed serious concerns over “huge pendency” of over 45,000 cases with the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) units in Mumbai and Thane for the last five years.
It said the information provided by the state government showed a  “shocking state of affairs”, resulting in stalling of criminal trials as FSL reports are submitted with inordinate delays.
The HC asked the government to take urgent measures to reduce existing pendency and recruit staff with special expertise at FSLs for the same.
It noted that “considering the huge number of pendency, trials cannot proceed without chemical analyser (CA) reports being placed before the trial courts”.
A bench of Justices Revati Mohite-Dere and Neela K Gokhale was hearing a plea by EduEdge Pro Pvt Ltd, represented by its Director Dr Amarjeet Singh. The petitioner global EdTech institute had complained that its former senior executive had allegedly stolen sensitive company data and used it to create a competing skill-development firm, and she defrauded the petitioner, who is her previous employer.
Advocate Himanshu Kode for the petitioner sought the transfer of an FIR registered with the Bandra Police Station to an independent probing agency including Cyber Cell or the Crime Branch of the Mumbai police.
On December 18, the bench had raised concerns over pendency and asked the Maharashtra government to inform how many cases were pending with the FSL units in Mumbai and Thane for the last five years. It had also raised concerns over delay in receiving FSL reports in cybercrime probes and other cases.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On Wednesday, Additional Public Prosecutor (APP) V B Konde-Deshmukh informed the bench that 34, 158 cases were pending before Mumbai FSL and 11,390 before Thane FSL unit.  “This is a very shocking state of affairs,” the bench orally remarked.
It asked APP Konde-Deshmukh to take instructions from officers concerned as to how many qualified persons were recruited at FSL units in Mumbai, Thane and other places as special expertise is required in the different fields of ballistic, DNA analysis, Cybercrime among others.
The court asked the government lawyer to bring the pendency issue to the notice of authorities concerned including the Home secretary so that appropriate steps are taken to resolve the same “as preparation and submission of FSL report is crucial in any trial to commence and conclude.”
The court also expressed displeasure over non implementation of “semi-automatic” project for the removal of the pendency at the Cyber Division of FSL.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
It questioned the delay despite the approvals for purchase of tools, materials and equipment were received and work order for the same was issued in October, last year.
“What is the use if equipment is received but is not in use and not made operational? Such people (responsible for delay) be removed. How do we expect the trials to commence and conclude if such is a state of affairs (at FSL),” the bench orally questioned.
The court directed the APP to inform Director General (Legal and Technical) of Directorate of Forensic Science Laboratories to remain present during the next hearing on February 5.

headline: Pay 5 lakh for motor vehicle number 0001: Punjab hikes reserve price for fancy vehicle registration numbers
description: Previously, the reserve price for 0001 was Rs 2.5 lakh, which has now been doubled to Rs 5 lakh
content:
Buyers of fancy vehicle registration number 0001 will now have to shell out Rs 5 lakh as the reserve price to bid for the number, which will be put up for e-auction by Punjab’s Transport Department. The reserve price for 0001 has been doubled after a government notification issued on Wednesday, while the prices of other fancy numbers have increased manifold, in some cases up to eight times.
The revised reserve prices are as follows:
• 0001 – Rs 5 lakh
• 0002 to 0009, and 0786 – Rs 2 lakh
• 0010 to 0099 – Rs 1 lakh
• 0100, 0200, 0300, 0400, 0500, 0600, 0700, 0800, 0900, 1000, 0101, 0111, 0777, 0888, 0999, 1111, 7777, 1008, 0295, and 1313 – Rs 1 lakh
• 2000, 3000, 4000, and similar series – Rs 50,000
• 0123 and several other fancy numbers – Rs 20,000
• Other fancy numbers – Rs 10,000
Additionally, the fee for obtaining a registration number of choice (out of turn), other than the prescribed fancy numbers, has been increased to Rs 10,000 within the district and Rs 20,000 for outside the district.
Previously, the reserve price for 0001 was Rs 2.5 lakh, which has now been doubled to Rs 5 lakh. The price for 0002 to 0009 was Rs 25,000 last year and has now surged to Rs 2 lakh, marking an eightfold increase. The price for 0010 to 0099 has increased from Rs 12,500 to Rs 1 lakh. Other fancy numbers, which were previously priced at Rs 5,000, now have a reserve price of Rs 10,000 to Rs 20,000.
The number of fancy registration numbers available for auction has also increased from 272 to 450 this year.
By raising the reserve prices, the cash-strapped Punjab government expects to generate Rs 100 crore from this auction, compared to Rs 60 crore last year. The move is part of the government’s efforts to boost revenue.
The e-auction charges will range between Rs 1,000 and Rs 2,000, and bidders must deposit 20% of the reserve price as earnest money along with non-refundable registration charges as notified earlier.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In a bid to improve finances, the Punjab government had withdrawn the Rs 1,500 crore subsidy introduced by former Chief Minister Charanjit Singh Channi. It also increased VAT on petrol and diesel, raised bus fares, and imposed a green tax on vehicles that have outlived their operational life.
