According to residents, the smoke emitted by the plant after the waste is processed in the incinerator is one of the primary contributors to the pollution in the area.
In October 2022, residents of Deonar moved a petition in the Bombay High Court, seeking immediate closure of the facility. The plea also sought a penalty against the private contractor and the shifting of at least half of the biomedical waste that, at present, is being received by the Govandi plant to some other plant outside the city limits.
In its reply, SMS Envoclean informed the High Court that it would relocate the plant to a new site after obtaining the necessary permission within 13 months.
Civic body officials said they have written to the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) urging them to push for immediate handover of the land. “The plant needs to be relocated outside the geographical boundary of Mumbai and since BMC doesn’t own big land parcels outside the city we are awaiting allotment from the MIDC or the state government,” a BMC officer told The Indian Express.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Last year, Deonar residents submitted before the National Green Tribunal (NGT) that medical records of people infected with tuberculosis, respiratory diseases, and lung cancer in the M (East) Ward showed a disturbing trend. They said at least 4,500-5,000 people in the ward have been diagnosed with TB every year till May 2022, and the number of deaths caused by the infection was 1,877 from 2013.

headline: 14 Kenyan nationals among 18 intercepted by customs at Mumbai airport while smuggling gold, diamonds worth Rs 9 crore
description: The Customs officials said the passengers were intercepted on Tuesday and Wednesday at the Mumbai airport.
content:
The Customs Department said Thursday it intercepted at least 18 passengers at Mumbai’s Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport while they were allegedly trying to smuggle gold and diamonds worth crores of rupees into the country by concealing them.
The Customs officials said the passengers were intercepted on Tuesday and Wednesday, and 5.92 kg of gold and diamonds worth Rs 9.12 crore were seized from them.
According to the officials, during a routine frisking and scanning procedure Tuesday, Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) officers found suspicious objects inside the laptop of a passenger flying to Bangkok from Mumbai. The passenger was then handed over to the Air Intelligence Unit (AIU) at the airport. After they examined the contest, Customs officials recovered 2147.20 carats of diamonds valued at Rs 4.93 crore. The passenger was arrested under the Customs Act for smuggling, the Customs officials added.
On Wednesday, three passengers who arrived from Dubai were intercepted, and 24-carat crude gold rhodium-plated rings and buttons — weighing 775 gram and valued at Rs 61.45 lakh — were recovered from them. The gold was concealed in belt buckles and trolley bags carried by the passengers, according to the Customs officials.

headline: Changing City: Navi Mumbai’s busy Kalamboli Junction to get signal-free interchange for smooth traffic flow
description: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari, Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, and PWD Minister Shivendra Raje Bhosle have instructed officials to treat the Kalamboli Junction Development Project in Navi Mumbai as a top priority.
content:
The Kalamboli Junction, which experiences persistent traffic congestion due to the convergence of vehicles from Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Goa, and Uran, is set to undergo a major transformation to streamline the movement of vehicles. The critical intersection in Navi Mumbai, connecting the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, NH-48/NH-548, and the Sion-Panvel Highway will be reconstructed in such a way that there would be no traffic signals.
About the Project:
The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MORTH) have jointly undertaken the Kalamboli Junction Development Project to enhance connectivity between Mumbai, Pune, JNPT, and the Navi Mumbai International Airport and ensure seamless traffic flow. The project is being executed by the Maharashtra State Infrastructure Development Corporation (MSIDC).
Why is it needed?
The chaotic traffic at Kalamboli Circle gets worsened by the heavy container trucks travelling to and from JNPA, leading to time, fuel, and financial losses, along with severe pollution concerns. As a key link to the upcoming Navi Mumbai International Airport, the junction connects vital routes, including the Sion-Panvel Highway, Mumbai-Pune Expressway, Kalamboli Steel Market, Shilphata, and national highways leading to JNPA and the Konkan region.
Currently, the five-arm signalised rotary junction has a 90-meter diameter roundabout and a six-lane flyover catering to traffic from JNPT and the surrounding road network. Due to heavy vehicular movement, congestion and delays are frequent. With the upcoming airport and increasing traffic volumes, a two-level interchange is necessary to ensure signal-free movement and reduce queuing delays at the junction.
Features:

Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
A two-level interchange with a directional/stack system is being implemented to eliminate at-grade cross-conflict points. The project involves constructing eight arms, a vehicular underpass, and multiple roads at two levels:
Total length of arms: 15.53 km
Underpass Subway: 817 m
Grade road length: 8.565 km
First-level length: 3.50 km
Second-level length: 3.46 km
Cost and Timeline
The project is estimated to cost Rs 482 crore and is scheduled to be completed within 18 months. It received government approval in October 2024, marking the official sanctioning of the plan. The construction work formally commenced in February 2025, with a structured implementation plan laid out by the Maharashtra State Infrastructure Development Corporation (MSIDC).
According to MSIDC officials, if the work progresses as planned, the project is expected to be completed by June 2026. Authorities have prioritised its execution to minimise disruptions and ensure smooth traffic flow at the earliest.
Administration speaks
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Given the high traffic volume, executing this project poses challenges related to traffic diversions, utility shifting, and design implementation. However, MSIDC is fully prepared to address these challenges and complete the project swiftly for the benefit of commuters,” said Brijesh Dixit, Managing Director, MSIDC.
Nitin Gadkari, Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways, along with Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and PWD Minister Shivendra Raje Bhosle, are closely monitoring the project and have instructed that it be treated as a top priority.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who inaugurated the Indian consulate in Marseille, highlighted the strategic partnership between India and France.

headline: Chandigarh: To bolster testing, health ATMs soon in wellness centres
description: . So far, these machines have been installed in Dadu Majra, Maloya, Dhanas, Mauli Jagran, Raipur Kalan, Makhan Majra, Sector 35, 38 and 39 health centres, though they are not operational yet.
content:
To facilitate better diagnostic facilities and increase testing in various Health and Wellness Centres (HWCs) of Chandigarh, there is a plan to install new machines, ‘Health ATMs’, in all 60 HWCs. So far, these machines have been installed in Dadu Majra, Maloya, Dhanas, Mauli Jagran, Raipur Kalan, Makhan Majra, Sector 35, 38 and 39 health centres, though they are not operational yet. The effort is to reduce the waiting time of patients, ensure that most tests are done at the HWCs, and also strengthen the existing hub and spoke model, where samples from HWCs and dispensaries are sent to the Civil Hospitals of Sector 22, 45 and Mani Majra and GMSH-16 for testing, and some samples also to PGI.
The ‘Health ATMS’ are a result of a CSR initiative by a computer company. The fully automated machine will facilitate various basic tests, with a biochemistry analyser enabling reliable testing and accurate sample analysis. All consumables required for tests for a year, says Dr Suman Singh, Director, Health Services, Chandigarh, will be given by the company and the plan is to also work out a system where the final test results can be given to patients on their phones. In case the doctor at the HWC needs the opinion of a specialist, the report would be sent to GMSH-16. Several health facilities are being provided to the patients at the HWCs by the Health Department, which include facilities for mother and child, newborns, children, and adolescents, treatment for communicable diseases under the National Health Mission, and treatment of minor diseases, Now, five more facilities, basic oral health care, common eye and ENT services, elderly and palliative health services, emergency medical services, screenings, and basic management for mental health have been added here.

headline: Amid calls for change, Punjab CM Mann says anyone can take top post chair
description: Sources said that after discussions on the agenda placed in the Cabinet meeting, the officers were asked to leave while Mann asked ministers to stay back.
content:
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann Thursday said he will step down from the post if any party leader wants to take charge. Mann’s remarks came in a Cabinet meeting hours after Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) MLA from Amritsar North, Kunwar Vijay Partap Singh, said that he believed it was time to replace him as the chief minister.
Sources said that after discussions on the agenda placed in the Cabinet meeting, the officers were asked to leave while Mann asked ministers to stay back. While talking to them about upcoming Zila Parishad and Panchayat Samiti elections, and discussing strategy, Mann took to another tangent.
“He started telling us that he is fine if anybody wants to become the chief minister. He said whosoever wants to become the CM can take his chair. But there is no point giving statements in the media. He can step down. He has no qualms about it. He said he does not want to stick to the post. He was referring to statements of party leaders in newspapers,” said a source privy to the developments in the meeting.
He added, “It appeared that the CM was saying all this in jest, because he usually jokes a lot. But he was serious”.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Delhi gets its fourth woman CM: All about Rekha Gupta
As Rekha Gupta is appointed Delhi CM, the 4 big challenges she will face
The source said that AAP state president Aman Arora, who is also a Cabinet minister, was present in the meeting. Arora had, a few days ago, given a statement that CM of Punjab should be picked on merit and it does not matter if the person is a Sikh or a Hindu.
His statement had invited strong reactions from the Opposition, with claims that after AAP’s debacle in Delhi, Arvind Kejriwal would try to become the CM of Punjab — remarks that were strongly denied by the ruling party.
Kunwar Vijay Partap, who had skipped a meeting called by of Kejriwal with leaders from Punjab, said, “I did not go to the party MLAs’ meeting in Delhi. That meeting was not held to raise any demands…it was more like a one-way communication from the higher-ups. I marked my attendance over the phone and conveyed my concerns,”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Kejriwal told the AAP leaders in Punjab at the meeting that winning the 2027 elections in the state was of utmost importance.
“I have been demanding to change the Punjab CM. I have given the reasons to party. We want to call a meeting of party MLAs so that they can elect a new leader. We are MLAs, and it is our right to elect the leader of the House,” Kunwar Vijay Pratap said.
“In my view, the reason behind the Delhi debacle is the bad governance in Punjab. One more reason is the Congress in Punjab is taking it for granted that they will form the next government in the state. Even the BJP has been gaining confidence that it will be able to win Punjab in 2027. So we must set our house in order. I can only tell you this. I have given the rest of the feedback to the party,” Kunwar Vijay Pratap said.
A 1998-batch IPS officer who was once the inspector-general of Punjab Police, Kunwar Vijay Pratap, the Amritsar North MLA, was among the high-profile AAP faces before its victory in the 2022 Assembly elections.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Dissatisfied with the then Captain Amarinder Singh-led Congress government’s stand in court over the 2015 sacrilege cases, Singh had opted for premature retirement from service soon after the Punjab and Haryana High Court on April 9, 2021 quashed the probe report filed by the Special Investigation Team he had led into the Kotkapura firing case. His resignation sparked events that led to the ouster of Captain Amarinder Singh as the chief minister a few months later. Later, Singh joined AAP, and Arvind Kejriwal pushed his image to promise justice in the sacrilege cases.
After AAP’s defeat in Delhi, Singh posted on Facebook, “It is time for introspection. I was deeply saddened by AAP’s defeat in Delhi, especially the personal defeat of senior leaders, which is extremely painful. Particularly when Congress leaders are rubbing salt into the wounds. This is a clear reflection of poor governance in Punjab.”
“In cases like sacrilege and the Kotkapura-Behbal Kalan firing, the government system deliberately protected the guilty, even after the main culprit confessed his crime at Sri Akal Takht Sahib—an outcome of my investigation that proved true,” he wrote.
“There is apathy and insensitivity in government institutions towards public work, along with open corruption and exploitation of the public in districts and municipal offices,” he said, alleging that gangsters have been joining AAP and mocking honest police officers.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“These are just some examples of poor governance in Punjab that I have already highlighted, especially during my meeting with Madam Sunita Kejriwal in August. Due to my domestic circumstances—especially the sudden and untimely death of my wife—I have not been very active in politics. Yet, seeing all of this is painful. Although time has passed, introspection must be done soon. I am fully committed to strengthening the party and upholding the principles of Swaraj,” he added.

headline: BJP’s pick for Delhi CM will be from MLAs, not MPs: Rekha Gupta, Ashish Sood among frontrunners
description: BJP national president J P Nadda says decision in ‘15 mins’; women MLAs also in the race
content:
The next Delhi Chief Minister will, in all likelihood, be chosen from among BJP’s elected MLAs and not MPs, with names like Rekha Gupta, Ashish Sood, Satish Upadhyay and Shikha Roy being discussed as potential candidates, The Indian Express has learnt.
Since Saturday, several meetings have taken place between the RSS and BJP top brass, attended by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, National General Secretary (organisation) B L Santhosh to discuss frontrunners for induction into the Cabinet.
According to sources, the new Cabinet’s composition is expected to reflect Delhi’s diverse social fabric, drawing representatives from various communities, including Punjabi, Baniya and Purvanchali, as well as ensuring representation for women, SC, OBC, and Brahmin communities.
Among the criteria being discussed to shortlist names are a “clean public image”, not being more than 60 years of age and “preference” for leaders whose rise and fall has been tied to BJP-RSS organisation in the Capital since they entered active politics.

A BJP leader confirmed that the Chief Minister’s post will go to a serving MLA rather than an MP. “The party leadership, however, hasn’t completely closed the door on including recent defectors like Arvinder Singh Lovely in the Cabinet,” a senior leader said.
Speaking to mediapersons on the sidelines of an event on Thursday, BJP national president J P Nadda said, “Selecting the Delhi CM will not be a tough call at all. It will be decided within 15 minutes when the party leadership meets.”
The selection process is expected to pick up pace after Prime Minister Narendra Modi returns from his foreign visit over the weekend, said sources.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Ashish Sood is among the top contenders for the CM’s post, sources said. A long-standing organisational man, he had served as councillor as well as Leader of the House in the erstwhile South MCD and was also the party Goa in-charge and J&K co-incharge.
Considered close to Nadda and Union Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, Sood won from Janakpuri by a margin of almost 19,000 votes this election. In 2020, he had lost the seat.
He was general secretary of the BJP youth wing, Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM), before being elevated as its national vice president. In 2008, he was appointed secretary of Delhi BJP and later general secretary, before being elected as a councillor in the then-SDMC.
According to sources in the BJP, what works in Sood’s favour is that he is one of Delhi BJP’s prominent Punjabi-speaking leaders and enjoys backing from the RSS. He is also perceived to be close to the BJP’s top leadership. His political journey began with ABVP before he joined the party ranks.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Another party leader said the CM post may also go to a woman. “The CM is most likely to be chosen from among women as well as Punjabi and Jat leaders. Right now, the party seems to be leaning towards making a Punjabi leader the CM.”
“Senior leaders with decades of legislative experience such as Vijender Gupta and Mohan Singh Bisht will be given significant responsibilities, most likely in the Delhi Assembly,” a source added.
Another senior leader considered to be in the running for the CM post is Rekha Gupta, an old RSS hand who joined the Sangh’s students wing, Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad, paving the way for her to be elected as DUSU president in the late 1990s.
In addition to being the secretary of BJYM’s Delhi unit, which she also served as the national secretary, Gupta has been elected as a councillor, general secretary of Delhi BJP’s Mahila Morcha and a member of the BJP’s National Executive.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Shikha Roy, a two-time BJP councillor from Greater Kailash, who hit headlines after she unfurled the Tricolour at Lal Chowk in Srinagar during a curfew in 2011, is also being considered as a significant frontrunner. She had unsuccessfully contested from Kasturba Nagar constituency in 2015 and Greater Kailash in the 2020 polls. In addition to serving as the Leader of the House, she was chairperson of the then SDMC Standing Committee and held organisational posts such as secretary, general secretary and vice-president of the Delhi BJP.
Satish Upadhyay, former Delhi BJP president and vice-chairperson of the New Delhi Municipal Council, is also being considered a frontrunner. He has served in organisational posts such as Delhi BJP vice-president and chairperson of the SDMC Standing Committee, among others.

headline: ‘Strong criticism’ may have ‘devastating impact on officials’: Delhi HC expunges remarks against Crime Branch
description: Justice Amit Mahajan, in a February 7 order, recorded that “strong criticism, vituperative remarks, may have a devastating impact on the reputation and career of officials involved in the case”.
content:
Accepting that the “anguish” of trial court orders is “not without reason”, the Delhi High Court has, however, ruled in favour of Delhi Police while directing the expunging of critical remarks made by the trial court against the Crime Branch and its officers in three cases.
Justice Amit Mahajan, in a February 7 order, recorded that “strong criticism, vituperative remarks, may have a devastating impact on the reputation and career of officials involved in the case”.
The Crime Branch, in a bunch of petitions filed in 2022 and 2023, had sought that the remarks, observations and strictures made by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate of Northeast district’s Karkardooma court, in nine orders in 2022 — ranging from July until October — in relation to three FIRs, be expunged
These include one from 2007 (for offences of forgery under IPC) and two others from 2020 — one for offences under the Emblems and Name (Prevention of Improper Use) Act, 1950) and another for offences under the Arms Act. In these orders, the trial court had rued the non-compliance of directions issued by the court to Crime Branch officers.

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’

Justice Mahajan recorded that while it was apparent the trial court’s remarks were “made in regard to the failure on the part of the investigating agency to carry out the investigation in a proper manner,” he said, “the anguish of the learned trial court is not without reason, yet the use of disparaging remarks that tend to lower the credibility of the investigating authority ought to be avoided”.
“If the learned trial court was concerned with the manner of the conduction of investigation, the court could simply have recorded the fact. However, use of castigating remarks, showcause notices to the Commissioner of Police seeking action taken against the officers, manner of enquiry, etcetera, in the opinion of this court, cannot be sustained… It is not in doubt that the orders of the court must be obeyed and complied with. Further, no individual shall be allowed to diminish the authority and majesty of the court. However, scathing remarks tend to have lasting consequences. It cannot be overlooked that every word that forms part of the record/judicial order gains permanence,” Justice Mahajan recorded.

headline: Police: 11 held for opening bank accounts using fake Aadhaar cards to commit cyber crimes
description: Based on the information received by Inspector NB Nakum, a police team raided the premises and arrested nine of the total 11 accused.
content:
Eleven members of a gang were arrested in Ahmedabad for allegedly forging Aadhaar cards to open “benami” accounts in multiple banks to commit cyber crimes, said the police, adding that gang kingpin is absconding.
The Cyber Crime Police station received a tip-off about the gang operating from Ahmedabad’s Chandkheda area.
Based on the information received by Inspector NB Nakum, a police team raided the premises and arrested nine of the total 11 accused.
During investigation, the police found out that one of the accused, Suresh Jagdish Bishnoi, was leading this operation.
All the accused belong to Rajasthan’s Jodhpur.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

A statement from the Cyber   Crime Police Thursday stated that the “employees” allegedly revealed that they would go to different branches of multiple banks, open up accounts and hand over their account details to Bishnoi and another person named Sunil Dhirani, who was based in Jodhpur.
The accused used to submit fake Aadhaar cards while opening up their bank accounts, said the statement.
During the probe it was found that several Aadhaar cards had the same phone number but different addresses. The accused had, using the phone number, allegedly received OTP from UIDAI and changed the original address of Rajasthan to those in Chandkheda (Ahmedabad), Morbi and Rajkot on the said Aadhaar cards, according to the statement.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
During the raid, the police seized 12 mobile phones, 21 identity documents (Aadhaar cards, PAN cards and cheque book), 10 bank passbooks, 43 ATM debit cards and 15 SIM cards, said DCP (Cyber Crime) Lavina Sinha.
Further interrogation revealed that 109 complaints were filed on the National Cyber Reporting Platform (NCRP) against the accounts opened by them in 21 states, out of which four complaints were registered from Gujarat. The accused had opened bank accounts across 26 branches, said the police.
The nine accused arrested during the raid include Suresh Jagdish Bishnoi (19), Anil Ugrasen Bishnoi (20), Kailash Khamoram Bishnoi (43), Hukamram Bhagwanram Bishnoi (19), Manish Hajariram Bishnoi (20), Vikas Punaram Bishnoi (18), Rakesh Sukhram Bishnoi (22), Rakesh Sahiram Bishnoi (22) and Mankul Sahiram Bishnoi (25).
Notably, when accused Rakesh Sahiram Bishnoi was searched, the police found a pistol with seven live cartridges from his person.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Based on the inputs given by the nine accused, two more accused, Lalit Shankarlal Bishnoi and Kuldeep Hanumanram Kichar, were arrested from Rajasthan. The alleged leader of the gang, Sunil Dhirani, remains absconding, said the police.
A case has been registered against all the accused in the cybercrime police station under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Sections 318(4) (cheating), 316(2) (criminal breach of trust), 61(2)(a) (criminal conspiracy), 54 (abettor present) and Sections 66(c), 66(d) of the IT Act.

headline: Karnataka brings into force law to prevent coercive loan recoveries in microfinance sector
description: Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah says the government will ensure the law won’t be misused against moneylenders, as apprehended by Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot.
content:
The Karnataka government has issued a notification to bring into force a law to regulate the microfinance sector in the state, with penal provisions such as imprisonment for up to 10 years and a fine of Rs 5 lakh for violations.
The notification, bringing into force the Karnataka Micro Loan and Small Loan (Prevention of Coercive Actions) Ordinance 2025, was issued on Wednesday by the Department of Parliamentary Affairs and Legislation after Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot cleared the ordinance by accepting clarifications given by the government on his concerns.
“The Karnataka Microfinance and Small Loans (Prevention of Coercive Measures) Ordinance 2025, which we have framed with the aim of controlling and imposing restrictions on inhumane, illegal practices such as harassment, mental torture and abuse by microfinance companies or other private financial institutions/individuals under the pretext of debt recovery, has come into force as a law from this moment,” Chief Minister Siddaramaiah said on Wednesday.
“Those who have been harassed after taking out loans through microfinance can file a complaint with the police, and they will receive greater protection under the new law. I am confident that through our efforts, the harassment and abuse of microfinance, finance, and moneylenders in the state will end,” he said.

Express View on Himanta Sarma's allegations against Gaurav Gogoi: Self-defeating strategy
The chief minister said the government would ensure that the new law would not be misused, as apprehended by the governor.
The ordinance proposed by the Congress government was initially rejected by the governor, who sought clarifications while returning the ordinance on February 7. The government sent the ordinance back to the governor on February 10 with clarifications but with no changes to the legal provisions.
The ordinance has proposed stringent punishment for the use of coercive tactics by moneylenders of all forms to collect dues from borrowers. The ordinance was proposed in the wake of several suicides in the state linked to coercive tactics—including the use of criminal intimidation—by moneylenders.

“The clarifications sought by the Governor to the microfinance ordinance have been sent back to the Governor with full details,” Siddaramaiah’s office said on February 10.
The governor earlier objected to the ordinance on the grounds that the punishment of 10 years and a fine of Rs 5 lakh proposed under the law is excessive and that existing laws can be used by the police department to control the situation.
The governor said the law should be reconsidered since it can have a negative impact on microfinance and stifle the sources of credit available to the poor in the state.
The governor had said the state should use the forthcoming budget session next month to enact a proper law “instead of bringing an ordinance in a hurry”. “I advise the state to deliberate this issue in detail and bring an effective enactment in the interest of the affected people and to protect their rights,” the governor said in his reply on February 7.

One of the key proposals in the ordinance is to ban microfinance institutions from outsourcing loan recovery to anti-social elements who tend to harass borrowers with extreme measures.

headline: Yes Bank-DHFL money laundering case: Bombay HC grants bail to Wadhawan brothers, cites long incarceration
description: The special PMLA court had rejected the default bail pleas of the two Wadhawan brothers.
content:
The Bombay High Court Wednesday granted bail to former DHFL promoters, Kapil and Dheeraj Wadhawan, accused in the multi-crore Yes Bank money laundering case, citing their long incarceration and no possibility of trial commencing soon. The applicants were arrested by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) on May 14, 2020.
“Applicants in the present case have been in custody since 4 years and 9 months. There is no possibility of the trial commencing in the near future. Detaining an under-trial prisoner for such an extended period further violates his fundamental right to speedy trial flowing from Article 21 of the Constitution,” a single-judge bench of Justice Milind N Jadhav noted in the February 12 order, copy of which was made available on Thursday.
On March 7, 2020, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) registered a corruption case against Kapil and Dheeraj Wadhawan, and Rana Kapoor, the then managing director and chief executive officer of Yes Bank. After the CBI FIR, on the same date, ED had registered an Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) and launched a separate money laundering probe in the case.
Senior advocate Amit Desai for the applicants argued that the maximum punishment that can be imposed on them upon conviction is seven years, however, they had already undergone pretrial incarceration of almost four years and nine months. He added that all accused except the Wadhawans were on bail in the case and submitted that ED’s probe in the case is pending till date and there was no statement or intimidation made by ED that the investigation is completed.

However, advocate Hiten Venegavnkar for ED opposed the plea and stated that the delay could be attributed to applicants’ conduct as they strategically kept their bail pleas before a special court designated under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) pending for over a year.
“In the facts of this case in my opinion due to the observations made herein above, further incarceration of Applicants is not required and they are entitled to bail under Section 436-A… without entering into the merits of the case at this stage,” the bench noted.
Justice Jadhav examined records before a special PMLA court and noted that the “delay in trial cannot be solely attributed to Wadhawans when admittedly ED has filed draft charges before the PMLA Court only on May 10, 2023, despite which charges have not been framed till date.” It noted that there are 36 accused involved in the matter and a total of 51 witnesses to be examined.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD

The judge said considering “no possibility of trial being concluded in the foreseeable future,” applicants having served over one-half of the maximum period of imprisonment which can be imposed after conviction, were entitled to bail.
The special court designated under PMLA had rejected the default bail pleas of the two in July 2020, which were challenged in the high court. The high court had granted default bail to them in August 2020, noting that the ED could not file a prosecution complaint or charge sheet within the stipulated 60 days of their arrest. However, the Supreme Court subsequently set aside the high court order.

headline: Karnataka woman found dead in Bengaluru lake, boyfriend alleges honour killing
description: According to Bengaluru police, the victim, a resident of Harohalli, and her father fell into Huskur Lake at Hebbagodi, after their motorcycle allegedly went out of control.
content:
A 21-year-old woman from a village in Karnataka was found dead in a lake on the outskirts of Bengaluru under mysterious circumstances on Monday. The police on Wednesday arrested the woman’s father based on the complaint of her boyfriend who alleged that it was a case of honour killing as the couple belonged to different communities.
According to the police, the victim, identified as R Sahana, a resident of Harohalli near Hosur, and her father, Ramamurthy, fell into Huskur Lake at Hebbagodi, after their motorcycle allegedly went out of control at the lake bund.
Sahana, who was riding pillion, reportedly drowned between 12.30 pm and 1 pm, the police said. Ramamurthy swam to safety, later went to the police station, and filed a complaint, they added.
Sahana’s boyfriend Nithin claimed that Ramamurthy must have deliberately pushed her into the lake as Sahana’s parents opposed their relationship. Ramamurthy was later released on station bail.

“I belong to the Naidu caste and Sahana is a Kuruba community member. After learning about our relationship, her father had arranged her marriage to their relative. But she insisted on marrying me,” he added.
Nithin alleged that Ramamurthy had called him to his friend’s house in Hebbagodi on Sunday night and assaulted Sahana in his presence. “Despite this, Sahana stood firm on marrying me. Ramamurthy declared that he would never allow the marriage. Even my mother tried to intervene, urging Ramamurthy to accept our relationship,” Nithin told the police.
A police officer said on interrogation, Ramamurthy said that he was sleepless after learning about his daughter’s relationship. “He lost control while riding the bike. He knew swimming but claimed he could not save his daughter’s life,” the officer said.

headline: ‘We don’t have hope left anymore’: In Jai Bhim Nagar demolition row, residents clueless whether filing of FIR would assuage their crisis
description: BMC demolished nearly 500 unauthorised structures at Jai Bhim Nagar in Central Mumbai on June 6, 2024, rendering its residents homeless; over 55 people were injured in the clashes between residents and municipal personnel.
content:
Nearly eight months since the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) razed over 500 shanties at Powai’s Jai Bhim Nagar, the Mumbai police on Tuesday booked senior civic and police personnel for carrying out the drive during monsoon without prerequisite clearances from State Human Rights Commission (SHRC). But for the residents of the slum, many of whom continue to dot the streets, the “delayed action” from the police hardly made a difference to their state of affairs with many of them even struggling to get water for daily needs. The slum dwellers say they are clueless about what the filing of First Information Report means to them.
On Wednesday, Shreemati Chauhan, 45, was seen busy reconstructing her make-shift house along Powai’s 90-feet-road, trying to make it snake-proof and withstand the summer heat. “Our problems are increasing by the day but we are yet to hear from the authorities. We had been living at Jai Bhim Nagar since 2004 but lost everything all of a sudden, last year. Despite the FIR, we have received no aid and are even struggling to get adequate water,” said Chauhan.
BMC demolished nearly 500 unauthorised structures at Jai Bhim Nagar in Central Mumbai on June 6, 2024, rendering its residents homeless. The drive took a violent turn following clashes between residents and municipal personnel that left over 55 people injured. Even as the civic body claimed that the action was based on directives from the SHRC, the drive drew flak from activists who pointed to a government resolution that prohibits demolitions during the monsoon (June 1-September 30).
Also Read | Mumbai police files FIR against BMC officials and police personnel for carrying out demolition at Powai’s Jai Bhim Nagar last year
“While my son who was at the police station told us that an FIR had finally been filed, we have received no news from the authorities and nobody has approached us guaranteeing any kind of relief,” said Chauhan.

While several affected families have relocated to nearby ‘chawls’ in the months following the demolition, nearly 40-50 families, including the Chauhans, continue to live on the streets.
“Since we have no proper house, there is high chance for our wares to get stolen. Therefore, it is impossible to leave the house unattended. I used to work as a domestic help but now due to this situation I am forced me to leave my work. How can we afford to pay Rs 15,000 to rent a space when we are struggling to earn even thousands? There is no surety of water supply from the BMC, with the tankers either delayed for days or coming at odd hours. That makes it even harder to leave the house,” said Chouhan, who was the sole breadwinner of her family of three.
Her son, Sagar Chauhan, had taken up the job of a delivery boy to support his family. “But I had to quit my job owing to a muscle problem which bars me from walking long distances. Even the doctors are unable to help me and we can’t afford any further treatments,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The eviction drive had sparked criticism, prompting the residents to file a petition in the Bombay High Court. After the Special Investigation Team (SIT), set up on the directive of the HC, found that the drive had been conducted without the SHRC orders, it informed the court in September 2024 that they would initiate action against the officials concerned.
A report published by Collective Mumbai showed that the residents are plagued by increasing cases of heatstroke, diarrhoea, jaundice, and allergic infections. The report, which was recorded during two medical camps by Sabki Library, also showed that cases of malaria, dengue, and typhoid were also registered after the eviction.
“We don’t even have any hope left anymore. With the lack of clean water and unsanitary conditions, my health is only deteriorating further,” another slum dweller, Jaidevi Mirge, who has been diagnosed with asthma and infections told The Indian Express.
According to Huma Namal, a member of Collective Mumbai, the issues of residents are bound to aggravate further with the summer season fast approaching. “While the delay in filing the FIR which the HC had directed months ago itself is very disturbing, the next hearing has now been scheduled for March. This consistent delay has resulted in increased problems for the residents of the area, for whom judicial justice is the only hope. Furthermore, the BMC has been denying adequate water and sanitation in an indirect attempt to drive the people away from the streets,” said Namal.

headline: Karnataka HC rules in favour of 2 Kerala nurses, says no law that people can only work in state where they got education
description: Two women who studied BSc Nursing at a Mangalaru institute had approached the Kerala Nurses and Midwives Council to get registered in the state.
content:
The Karnataka High Court has directed the Kerala Nurses and Midwives Council (KNMC) to register two nurses who had secured their BSc Nursing degrees from an institute in Mangaluru, saying that “no law can…mandate that a person can only work in the state where he or she has obtained his or her education”. The high court also said that the council cannot insist on recognition from the Indian Nursing Council.
The observations were made in an order passed on February 7 by a single-judge bench of Justice Suraj Govindaraj.
As per the case, two women from Kerala secured BSc Nursing degrees from an institute in Mangaluru in 2023. They submitted an application to the KNMC, which insisted on an Indian Nursing Council registration of the institute they had graduated from. The nurses then approached the Karnataka High Court.
The counsel for the petitioner nurses argued that the KNMC could not reject them as their college was recognised by the Karnataka State Nursing Council. This being the case, there could not be any insistence on registration by the Indian Nursing Council, especially since the Supreme Court had ruled that only the state councils and not the Indian Nursing Council could grant recognition, the counsel submitted. It was further argued that any degree affiliated with respective state councils should be recognised by all other states.

Perusing the Indian Nursing Council Act, 1947, the high court stated, “….a State Nursing Council cannot insist on the need to furnish a certificate of registration/recognition from the Indian Nursing Council for the purposes of enrolment/registration to practice the profession of nursing in that state.”
The court added, “…. what is to be seen is whether the State can restrict registration to students educated within its own territorial limits insofar as registration of nurses are concerned….No law can bind a person to a particular State, or mandate that a person can only work in the State where he or she has obtained his or her education. Narrow parochial views like these must be avoided…”.
The judge also pointed out that considering that the nurses were Kerala residents returning to the state after getting an education in Karnataka, a “disservice” had been done by the Kerala council. The KNMC was then directed to register the petitioner nurses and any others with a nursing degree.

headline: 38th National Games in Dehradun: Chandigarh girl becomes champion in -78kg category in women’s judo: ‘My extra fingers (are) my strength ‘
description: Ishroop had become the Punjab champion in 44 kg in Punjab Judo Championships in 2017 before she won the 44kg state champion in 2018 and 55kg state champion in 2019.
content:
Back in 2017, when the then 12-year-old Ludhiana native Ishroop Narang enrolled for judo at the Guru Nanak International School under coach Kishore Kumar, the youngster started the sport to lose weight. The MCM DAV College Chandigarh student, who was born with Polydactyly having five fingers and a thumb in each of her hands and feet, became the -78kg champion in women’s judo with a win over Aswathy of Kerala by Ippon on golden score in the 38th National Games in Dehradun on Wednesday. The Chandigarh player called her parents Tajinder Pal Singh Narang and Jaspreet Kaur Narang to share the joy.
“My parents Tajinder Pal Singh Narang and Jaspreet Kaur Narang have always taught me to see my extra fingers as my strength and not something to be stressed or see as a bad omen. I see them as my strength and the extra finger in my feet also helps me in maintaining extra balance on the mat in judo. To win my first senior national title is a special feeling and I dedicate this medal to my parents as well as brother,” said Ishroop while talking with The Indian Express from Dehradun.
Ishroop had become the Punjab champion in 44 kg in Punjab Judo Championships in 2017 before she won the 44kg state champion in 2018 and 55kg state champion in 2019. In 2019, the youngster won the bronze medal in the +70 kg pre-cadet category in the Commonwealth Judo Championships held at Walsall, Great Britain. After winning multiple medals in cadet and junior nationals in 2022 and 2023, Ishroop won her first National Games medal in the form of a bronze medal in the National Games in Goa in 2023. The same year saw her winning a silver in senior nationals in Jaipur before she won the bronze medal in Junior Asian Championship in Korea last year.
“Winning the bronze medal in pre pre-cadet category in the Commonwealth Judo Championship in 2019 made me believe that I can achieve international success too. Competing in junior as well as senior events from my junior days has taught me how to face much stronger and experienced judokas. While I also trained under Dronacharya awardee national coach Jiwan Kumar Sharma, I shifted to Chandigarh in 2023 to train under Vivek Thakur sir. The junior Asian medal last year was one of the high points of my junior career apart from competing in junior world championships in Tajikistan last year,” said the youngster.

She has almost mastered the move Ura Nage and has been using this technique with finesse. She will only improve in coming years,” said coach Vivek Thakur.

headline: Gujarat Confidential: Being Prepared
description: The Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has finalised the appointment of Manoj Patil as the Chief Fire Officer.
content:
The Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) has finalised the appointment of Manoj Patil as the Chief Fire Officer. Even as the Opposition had raised questions over the appointment of “an outsider” – Patil is from Maharashtra – in a General Board held earlier this year, the VMC has finalised him to lead the Vadodara Fire and Emergency Services (VFES) owing to his prior postings in “critical” installations. Given the topography of Vadodara city, which is surrounded by an industrial belt comprising chemical companies and is also home to Gujarat Refinery, Patil’s experience working in a power plant in Maharashtra was seen as “impressive”, besides his postings in Mumbai and Bengaluru, which have a number of multistoreyed apartments, officials said. VMC officials, though, stated that an officer of the VFES has moved the High Court challenging the appointment. An official confirmed that the legal team of the civic body has begun preparing affidavits of authorities concerned that will need to be filed before the HC when the notice is issued.
Warm Welcome
Radhikaraje Gaekwad of the royal family of Vadodara, who has been an advocate of women’s empowerment, extended her support to the Gujarat Giants Women’s Cricket Team, ahead of their much-anticipated home debut in the Women’s Premier League (WPL) to be held in Vadodara Thursday. Radhikaraje invited the Gujarat Giants captain Ashleigh Gardner, along with teammates Kashvee Gautam, Phoebe Litchfield, and Deandra Dottin, at the iconic Lukshmi Vilas Palace and also took the players and their coaches and administrative staff to the Gazra Cafe, which is the royal family’s initiative for the LGBTQ+ community.

headline: Deportees from US included former Haryana cop’s son who entered America in third attempt
description: A travel agent from Ambala was arrested after Jitesh Walia’s father filed a police complaint for cheating.
content:
Among the 104 deportees who arrived in Amritsar on a US military plane last week was the son of a former Haryana Police officer who had finally reached the United States after two failed attempts, only to be sent back within 18 days.
Jitesh Walia, 31, set out from Ambala on May 16, 2024, and just about managed to enter the US on January 18 this year. As soon as he crossed the border, he was arrested.
His father Sushil Kumar Walia, a retired sub-inspector, lodged a police complaint on Sunday against five travel agents for cheating him of Rs 40 lakh on the pretext of sending his son abroad. headline: Former Delhi top cop Ajay Raj Sharma dies at 81
description: After serving three years in the Delhi Police, from 1999 to 2002, he was appointed the Director General of the BSF, a post from which he retired in 2004
content:
Former Delhi Police Commissioner Ajay Raj Sharma died at a hospital in Noida on Monday night after prolonged illness. He was 81.
A person close to his family said Sharma, who had been suffering from lung infection, was admitted to Kailash Hospital two weeks ago. He is survived by his wife and two sons.
A 1966-batch Indian Police Service (IPS) officer, Sharma was the first Delhi Police commissioner to be appointed from outside the AGMUT (Arunachal Pradesh-Goa-Mizoram and Union Territory) cadre. After serving three years in the Delhi Police, from 1999 to 2002, he was appointed the Director General of the BSF, a post from which he retired in 2004.
Sharma completed his primary education in Dehradun before moving to Allahabad, now known as Prayagraj. He graduated from the Allahabad University in 1965.

He was selected for the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in his first attempt and chose IPS. He was allotted the Uttar Pradesh cadre and received his first posting in Agra, where he took part in the encounter of several gangsters operating in the forests along the borders of Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.
During Sharma’s tenure with the Uttar Pradesh Police, a Special Task Force (STF) was formed to counter organised crime in the state. The STF, led by his team, gunned down gangster Shri Prakash Shukla in September 1998.
His performance led to his induction into the AGMUT cadre by then Deputy Prime Minister L K Advani. He was appointed the commissioner of police in Delhi in June 1999.

Remembering Sharma, Vijay Malik, retired deputy commissioner of Delhi Police, told The Indian Express, “He was a great character… always supportive of his staff. He would always back them during any challenge or critical situation.”
“During his tenure, the Delhi Police faced an attack on Parliament. However, under his leadership, the force successfully cracked the case and apprehended the culprits,” Malik added. “We will always miss him,” Malik said, adding Sharma’s funeral will take place at Lodhi Cremation Ground at 11 am on Wednesday.
Paying tribute to Sharma, BSF posted on X, “DG BSF & All Ranks pay heartfelt tributes to Shri Ajai Raj Sharma, IPS, former DG BSF (2002-2004) on his demise. His visionary leadership and legacy continue to inspire us. Prahari Parivar stands in solidarity with his family.”

headline: Former Deputy Mayor awarded six-month jail for slapping then ward officer in 2014
description: Patel was accused of causing voluntary hurt, misbehaviour along with obstructing a ward officer from duty during an anti-encroachment drive in the city’s Karelibaug area.
content:
A local court in Vadodara  sentenced former BJP  Deputy Mayor of Vadodara Municipal Corporation, Yogesh Patel (Mukti), to six months imprisonment in connection with a 2014 case of slapping the then Ward Officer during an anti-encroachment drive in city’s Karelibaug area.
Patel was accused of causing voluntary hurt, misbehaviour along with obstructing a ward officer from duty during an anti-encroachment drive in the city’s Karelibaug area.
The court of Chief Judicial Magistrate AS Shaikh examined 16 witnesses in the case and also considered 22 documentary and oral evidences during the proceedings. The court also slapped a fine of Rs 1,000 on Patel.
While the prosecution emphasised that Patel being an elected representative had a “responsibility of setting a fine example” and had “failed to do so”, the defence argued that the complainant, Jagmal Nandaniya, was not present at the spot when the incident occurred. The FIR in the case, lodged at Karelibaug police station, by former Ward Officer Jagmal Nandaniya  had stated that Patel had slapped him after he refused to give in to Patel’s demand of releasing the  street carts that had been removed as part of the drive.

headline: CBI court convicts former Chief Manager of Bank of India in bank fraud case of Rs 80 lakh
description: Jeevangine Srinivasa Rao was sentenced to 3 years of imprisonment and a fine of Rs 1.5 lakh
content:
The Special Judge for CBI cases in Ahmedabad sentenced Jeevangine Srinivasa Rao, ex-Chief Manager of the Bank of India, SM Road branch, to 3 years of imprisonment and imposed a fine of Rs 1.5 lakh in a bank fraud case involving a loss of Rs 80 lakh to the bank.
A statement from the CBI on Tuesday said that it had registered a case on October 30, 2003, against Rao and others on allegations that the accused had committed the offences of cheating, used forged documents as genuine for availing credit facility/loans, forgery of valuable security and others, under the Prevention of Corruption Act.
It was alleged that the accused had declared fake collateral security, opened an account in the name of a supplier of machinery, and deposited the cheque issued by the bank for the purchase of machinery in the said account. Rao allegedly destroyed the documents related to the fake collateral security while sanctioning it.
The statement further said, “During the investigation, it was also revealed that accused public servant Rao sanctioned loans by conspiracy to private accused persons in the forms of working capital of Rs 30 lakh, LC of Rs 25 lakh, and term loan of Rs 25 lakh, based on forged and bogus collateral security and thereby caused wrongful loss to the bank… to the tune of Rs 80 lakh.”

headline: 276 acres reclaimed in anti-encroachment drive, 1,500 illegal structures razed
description: Monday’s action was coordinated by the PCMC’s building permission and unauthorized construction control department, along with zonal rapid response teams.
content:
The Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation has (PCMC) intensified its ongoing crackdown on illegal encroachments in the Chikhali–Kudalwadi area in last three days. Under the continued operation, 682 unauthorised structures were cleared on Monday, covering approximately 33.58 lakh square feet of construction. In the past few days, as many as 1,511 illegal structures have been demolished, officials said.
This large-scale initiative targeted unauthorised sheds, factories, warehouses, scrap shops, and illegal buildings erected on land reserved for future city development and public amenities. Municipal Commissioner Shekhar Singh and Police Commissioner Vinaykumar Chaube are jointly overseeing the drive, the civic administration said.
Monday’s action was coordinated by the PCMC’s building permission and unauthorized construction control department, along with zonal rapid response teams. Additional Municipal Commissioner Pradeep Jambhale Patil, Deputy Commissioner Manoj Lonkar, special officer Kiran Gaikwad, Zonal Officers Rajesh Agale, Sucheta Pansare, Amit Pandit, Kishor Nanavare, Umesh Dhakane, Ajinkya Yele, and Shital Wakade took part in the operation, supported by executive engineers, deputy engineers, junior engineers, and other personnel.
Under the supervision of senior police officers—including Additional Police Commissioner Vasant Pardeshi and Deputy Commissioners of Police Swpana Gore, Dr. Shivaji Pawar, Sandeep Doiphode, and Vivek Patil—security was strengthened in the area. Around 600 police officers, 180 personnel from the Maharashtra Security Force, and additional labor staff joined forces with PCMC teams. Heavy machinery, including 16 excavators, 8 JCBs, 1 crane, and 4 cutters, was deployed for demolition. Standby firefighting vehicles and ambulances were also stationed on-site.

description: On Monday, Justice Marne, while dismissing the plea said that he had taken a view in November last year and he could not correct it himself, therefore, Thorat was entitled to file an appeal.
content:
The Bombay High Court on Monday rejected a review petition against an order of dismissal of a plea challenging election of Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Sanjay Dina Patil from North-East Mumbai Lok Sabha constituency last year.
Petitioner Shahaji Nanai Thorat had filed a review petition after the single-judge bench of Justice Sandeep V Marne on November 26, 2024 had rejected his election petition against Patil.

content:
The Russian Su-57 and the American F-35 Lightning II — two of the world’s most advanced fifth-generation fighter aircraft — took to the skies of Bengaluru on the first day of Aero India on Monday, offering defence enthusiasts a glimpse of their manoeuvres at the same event for the very first time.
Their performances were clear showstoppers, overshadowing even the traditionally acrobatic display by the Surya Kiran team.
It was the Su-57’s debut at Aero India. The F-35, manufactured by Lockheed Martin, had participated in the previous edition of the premier defence exposition.
Akshara Patel, an aircraft enthusiast, said the display by both fifth-generation aircraft surprised her. “I was not expecting that both would hit the skies. It was spectacular to see both of them performing,” she said.

headline: Haryana family spent Rs 1.2 crore to reach US, deported back in 12 days
description: In the FIR, Paramjit alleged that in Mexico, they were lodged in a room and were tortured
content:
A Haryana family deported from the US recently has told the police that they reached the USA by spending Rs 1.2 crore on January 22 this year but was deported back within 12 days. The four members were among the 104 people deported by the US on February 3 this year for entering the country illegally. They landed at the Amritsar airport on February 5.
Now the Haryana Police has launched an investigation against the three travel agents who had allegedly promised the family of four to send them to the US by charging Rs 30 lakh per member.
A resident of Haibatpur village of Kurukshetra district, Paramjeet Singh, 45, has lodged a complaint against three travel agents: Salinder Bhura, a resident of Kirmach village; Jinda, a resident of Kaithal; and Rinku, a resident of Thanesar (Thanesar) and their unknown accomplices. The police have lodged an FIR against them under the charges of criminal breach of trust, cheating, human trafficking and under provisions of the Immigration Act.
Paramjit Singh had settled at Kurukshetra to ensure better study of his children. After some time, in May 2024, he met the travel agents. According to Paramjit, the travel agents offered to send the family to the US by promising a job to him and better education to his children. On May 21, 2024, the passports of Paramjit, his wife Omi Devi, daughter Kajal Kainwal, son Jatin Kainwal and Rs 1.5 lakh were handed over to the travel agents.

To arrange more money, Paramjit sold his house for Rs 74 lakh in June 2024. In August 2024, he gave Rs 8 lakh to the travel agents while a payment of Rs 40 lakh was made on December 18, 2024. The agents said that the remaining Rs 70 lakh will be charged once they reach America.
On December 21, 2024, they took a flight from Delhi airport to Rome from where they went to Paris and landed in Costa Rica on December 27, 2024. After 15 days, they reached Mexico by road.

In the FIR, Paramjit alleged that in Mexico, they were lodged in a room and were tortured. He said the associates of the travel agents asked him to make a call to their relatives in Haryana to make the payment of the remaining money (Rs 70 lakh). “Our phones and passports were snatched and we were beaten up badly. We were kept hungry. On January 15, I called my cousin to make a payment of Rs 70 lakh to the travel agents and the same was made to them the next day,” said Paramjit in the police complaint.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
According to Paramjit, on January 22, 2025, they were taken to the US border. “As soon as we crossed the US border, the American police took us into custody and we were lodged in the jail. We were tortured in America too. We were sent back to India on February 5,” Paramjit said.
Paramjit told the police that he made a phone call to travel agent Salinder Bhura after landing in India but he did not pick up the phone.
The investigation officer (IO), Sub-Inspector Rampal, told The Indian Express that the police were investigating the matter but no arrest has been made so far. Till now, the Haryana Police has lodged at least five FIRs against the travel agents.

headline: 26 students who withdrew their admissions at K J Somaiya college to appear as private candidates for HSC exam
description: According to the board, these students lost their admissions at their college after it was found that they too secured seats via unfair means in last academic year.
content:
Months after the cash-for-admission racket was unearthed at junior colleges run by the Somaiya Trust, 26 students from K J Somaiya College of Arts and Commerce approached the Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary (MSBSHSE) to appear for Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examination as private candidates.
According to the board, these students lost their admissions at their college after it was found that they too secured seats via unfair means in last academic year. The college administration, however, denied it stating that they withdrew admissions on their own but refused to provide any reasons for so many students withdrawing admissions months before HSC exam.
In December 2024, admissions of 50 students from First Year Junior College (FYJC) were cancelled by the Somaiya College after it was found out that they had secured admissions through fraudulent means. The issue was revealed during a scrutiny of admission documents by the college following which FIR was also filed with Mumbai Police against the staff members from the college involved in helping these students secure admissions on fake documents.
Chairman of Mumbai Division of Maharashtra State Board, Rajendra Ahire, said, “Students from Somaiya college approached Maharashtra State Board to appear for HSC exam as private candidates after their admissions were termed irregular following a further scrutiny by the college of admission documents from the previous academic year (2023-24). Their college had asked them to approach the board to obtain permission to appear for HSC as private candidates. As all of them have passed SSC which is the eligibility to appear for HSC, they all can definitely appear for HSC as private candidates.”

headline: Punjab woman deported from US urges govt to help her return to UK: ‘Never told we were being taken to India’
description: The family of the woman from Jagraon in Ludhiana had taken Rs 15 lakh loan to send her to London for higher studies.
content:
A day after she was deported from the US in a military plane, a 21-year-old woman from Punjab’s Ludhiana district said Thursday all she wanted was to fly back to the UK so that she could return to her college in London.
Muskan, who was among the 104 people deported by the US, said she was a student of a three-year business management course at CU College, London. She went to the UK on a study visa in January last year. She said she, along with a group of friends, was taken to the detention centre in the United States after being caught in Tijuana, the Mexican city at the US border.
Speaking to The Indian Express, the Jagraon resident said, “We never intended to enter the US illegally. We had legally travelled to Mexico and did not attempt to cross the border by jumping across the wall or any other illegal way. We were at the Tijuana border when the police stopped us and said that soon the US authorities would take us away. I still have a valid study visa for the UK so why have I been deported to India?”
“A bus came and we were taken to the detention centre where we spent 10 days. They did not ask us anything and only checked our passports. We were a group of at least 40. We had only gone to Mexico.”

When asked why she went to Mexico, Muskan said: “I along with my friends had gone for a holiday trip to the Tijuana border.”
Amid sobs, Muskan said they were never told that they were being deported to India. “We did not face any misbehaviour by the US authorities in any manner. Par unhone humein nahi bataya tha ki India leke jaa rahe hain (They did not tell us that we were being taken to India). It was only after the plane landed in Amritsar that we got to know that we had landed in India. That is when I called my parents to inform them that I have reached Amritsar,” she said.
Huge debts
Like other people who have been deported by the US, Muskan said her family also borrowed money from others to send her abroad. “My family had taken a loan of Rs 15 lakh along with some small loans from relatives and friends to send me to the UK for studies. I hope the government will understand our family’s financial condition and allow me to return to the UK to complete my studies,” said Muskan whose father runs a small eatery in Jagraon.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Now, I am being told that I won’t be allowed to fly to the UK or anywhere else. My two-year course is still pending. I want to return and complete my studies. I humbly appeal to the government to please help me. If I don’t return to the UK, my entire career will be spoiled,” she said.
While expressing shock at her deportation, her father said, “We weren’t aware of this at all. I only got to know at 5 pm yesterday when she called us from Amritsar airport. We are relieved that she is back home safe.”
Jagraon MLA Sarvjit Kaur Manuke has appealed to the government to help the woman travel back to the UK to complete her studies in London. “The family is in debt. It is really important for her to complete her studies so that she can settle in life and help her family,” said Manuke.
However, the woman in her statement to the officials recorded at Amritsar airport revealed that she had gone to UK on study visa through an agent and later reached Mexico via Bahamas to cross the US border.

description: A representative of Vaishali Transcarrier Private Limited, the subcontractor, visited the protest site and assured workers that their demands would be met.
content:
Hundreds of third party vendor employees working at the warehouse of e-commerce giant Amazon at Katraj staged a one-day protest at site on Monday to protest against the company and the vendor for allegedly failing to comply with an agreement of a 30 per cent wage hike and not paying workers for the last three months.
In October last year, Amazon had signed a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) for the first time in India with the warehouse workers, in the presence of the Mathadi Board—a government body established to ensure socio-economic justice exclusively for head loaders in Maharashtra. The board is chaired by the Assistant Labour Commissioner of Maharashtra. The agitating employees are employed by Vaishali Transcarrier Private Limited, who in turn is a sub contractor for Amazon.
Baba Adhav, president of the Hamal Panchayat, a union advocating for the rights of headloaders, laborers, and gig workers in the state, visited the protest and called the situation an exploitation of workers.
He said that their union workers are registered and working under the company, yet the way they are treated should be criticized.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
“This is not a new demand; it is simply what is outlined in the agreement. How are our people supposed to survive? Even the Mathadi Board has remained silent on this issue. Even at my age, I have the strength to stop traffic and fight for our rights,” he said.
CBA is a legal process under labour laws that allows employers and employees—meaning the industry and the workers—to jointly discuss and resolve workplace issues.
Chandan Kumar, an policy & legal advisor to the Hamal Panchayat, stated that companies generally hesitate to sign agreements because they do not want to take responsibility for workers.
“After three years of consistent efforts, the company came to the table, and we managed to get them to sign the agreement in the presence of the government,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Kumar added that before the agreement, the salary was around Rs 18,000, which was raised to Rs 26,000 for the period between April 2024 and March 2025. He further noted that the amount is set to increase to Rs 26,500 from April 2025 to March 2026.
General Secretary Gorakh Mengde said that most of these workers have been working for the past 9 to 10 years and are members of the Hamal Panchayat and Mathadi Board, yet their wages have been pending for the last three to four months.
“Once an agreement is signed, the company is bound to pay the workers. Most of them come from distant places and have significant daily expenses. How will they survive if they are not paid on time? If the company does not comply with the agreement, the families of these workers will be forced onto the streets,” he said.
Nikhil Walke, Chairperson of the Mathadi Board Workers and Assistant Commissioner, Labour Commissioner’s Office, told The Indian Express that a meeting was conducted regarding the issue, but no party was present.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“We will hold another meeting within a couple of days,” he said.
Speaking about the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), Walke stated that both the company and the workers are parties to the agreement, and the company is obligated to fulfill the demands outlined in the official agreement.
According to official agreement documents and worker allegations, since 2021, nine meetings have taken place between workers’ unions and Amazon. As a result, Amazon eventually agreed to a 30 per cent wage hike, which was made effective retroactively from April 2024.
A representative of Vaishali Transcarrier Private Limited, the subcontractor, visited the protest site and assured workers that their demands would be met.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Amazon, the principal employer, has released the statement that states, “Our Supply Chain Standards require all suppliers and third-party service providers to pay their workers, including contract workers, in a timely manner and provide compensation that meets or exceeds applicable laws. While Amazon is not directly responsible for the compensation of our partners’ employees, we take these matters seriously as they impact people working in our facilities. We are actively investigating the situation and are in contact with the concerned service provider to resolve this issue at the earliest.”
