headline: Lawyers in Delhi’s district courts abstain from work today over proposed Advocates (Amendment) Bill
description: Besides prohibiting advocates from boycotting court work, the draft Advocates (Amendment) Bill also allows the Centre to nominate up to three members to the Bar Council of India.
content:
The coordination committee of all District Court Bar Associations across Delhi’s lower courts decided to abstain from work on Monday against the recent draft of the Advocates (Amendment) Bill proposed by the Union Law Ministry which would, in effect, prohibit advocates from boycotting and abstaining from courts’ work.
The circular drafted by the committee on Sunday said it unanimously took the decision against the “proposed unjust, unfair and biased” Bill proposed by the government of India. “The Bill is totally against the unity, integrity and dignity of Advocates but also draconian in nature. It will directly affect the autonomy of all Bar Associations and Bar Council of all states,” it read.
Section 4 of the proposed amendment to the Advocates Act, 1961 also allows the Centre to nominate up to three members to the Bar Council of India in addition to the existing membership of the Attorney General of India, and the Solicitor General.
One of the most contentious provisions in the draft amendment, as per Delhi’s lawyers, is section 35 A which reads that “No association of advocates or any member of the association or any advocate, either individually or collectively, shall give a call for boycott or abstinence from courts’ work or boycott or abstain from courts’ work or cause obstruction in any form in courts’ functioning or in court premises.”
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
There is however, an exception: “…advocates may participate in a strike only when it does not impede the administration of justice such as strikes intended to bring attention to legitimate concerns about professional conduct, working conditions, or administrative matters and may include symbolic or one-day token strikes, as long as they are conducted in a way that does not disrupt court proceedings or violate clients’ rights.”
Any violation of this provision would invite disciplinary action.
A new clause in the draft amendment also says that the State Bar Council may not enrol any person who has been convicted of an offence punishable with imprisonment of three years or more.
The definition of a law graduate has also been expanded from someone who obtains a Bachelor’s law degree from any university established by law in India to someone who has obtained a Bachelor’s degree in law of three or five years from any centre of legal education or university established by law or a college affiliated to any university and recognised by the Bar Council of India.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Published by the Law Ministry on Thursday, the draft Advocates (Amendment) Bill, 2025 is open to comments till February 28.
The coordination committee consists of advocate Jagdeep Vats (chairman), advocate Atul Kumar Sharma (secretary general), advocate Rahul Singh (vice-chairman), advocate N C Sharma (spokesperson), and advocate Nitin Ahlawat (coordinator) among others.

headline: Deportees from US without turbans: ‘We raised the issue but no change in protocol,’ claims Punjab minister
description: Deportees say made to wait on floor at airport as relatives scrambled for clarity outside.
content:
A Punjab cabinet minister and some deportees who landed from the United States in Amritsar on Saturday night have claimed that some of the young men on board the flight didn’t have their turbans, and the Punjab administration had to make last-minute arrangements at the airport.
The second batch of 116 devotees arrived at the Sri Ramdas International Airport a little before midnight yesterday.
Yashpal Singh from Patti, who claimed to have spent Rs 44 lakh to take the “dunkey route” to the US, said, “We were not wearing turbans when we landed at the airport. They had removed our turbans (before the flight). SGPC (Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee) provided us with a siropa, but those were not long enough as these are used to honour someone and not to tie on the head. So I borrowed a cap to cover my head.”
Also See | Why US deportation flights to Amritsar have touched off a firestorm in Punjab
Cabinet Minister Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal, who remained at the airport until early Sunday morning, said, “Some youth on the first flight didn’t have their turbans either. We raised this issue after the first flight, and we will again. But it is sad that despite so much hue and cry, nothing has changed. The third flight will likely be the same – with the youth in shackles and without turbans.”
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
An SGPC official said, “We have a small camp office at the airport where we keep siropas in stock to welcome dignitaries. We provided 15 siropas from our stock to the deportees.”
Officials said that most of the deportees on this flight were men, and they were all handcuffed and shackled.
Deportees also said that they were made to sit on a cold floor at the airport while waiting for immigration clearance.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Unlike the first flight, when only a few people had come to receive the deportees, several parents and relatives turned up outside the airport this time. Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann also visited the airport on Saturday evening, saying he had come to receive the deportees. But he left around 5:30 pm, hours before the aircraft landed at 11:30 pm.
Punjab Cabinet Minister Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal also left after taking a photo with a group of deportees at the aviation club around 3 am on Sunday.
Parents and relatives said there was no system to inform them of when the deportees would be released, so they shuffled between the airport’s arrival and cargo gates for about 12 hours.
Some relief came from the SGPC, which provided food and tea to relatives waiting outside the airport through the night.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Relatives became even more frustrated early Sunday morning when they realised that the deportees would not be handed over to them and the police would drop them off at their respective homes.

headline: Amid the lure of the foreign land, it is ‘ghar vapsi’ for many in Punjab
description: While some left for foreign lands years ago in search of a better future, others migrated only recently. All of them came back for the “cosiness of our friends and family”.
content:
Even as hundreds of Indians are being deported from the US, several NRIs from Punjabi have come back to India on their own to start their lives anew in their homeland. Some of them said they left their villages long ago to settle down abroad — they became Permanent Residents, and some became citizens of those countries with well-placed jobs and businesses to live a “better life”.
While several went to Canada, the United States, and New Zealand to study or in search of jobs, some were born in those countries. Many of them have now come back in what many call a reverse migration.
Here are a few Punjabis who talked to The Indian Express about their lives on foreign shores, their journey back, and what they think of Indians being deported from the US.
Detwal brothers
Residents of Ludhiana’s Detwal village, Dharamvir Singh Detwal, and his cousin Arshvir Singh Detwal went to Canada in 2015 after completing their Class 12. They did a diploma in mechanical engineering and got Canadian PR in 2020.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
The Detwal brothers said they worked as truck drivers in Canada and lived in the same house. “When I used to come back from work, Dharamvir used to be asleep and vice-versa. Our off days too used to be different. We used to sit together and have a nice chat with each other after days together… Sometimes our parents used to come and visit us for a few months,” said 27-year-old Arshvir.
“However, we realised that our lives had become too mechanical and we were working to pay off few instalments and taxes, eat meals, and we hardly had any social life. At a time when many in Canada were struggling to get work permits extended or get a PR, we decided to pack our bags and come back to India with no return ticket,” said Arshvir.
Dharamvir, 28, said they came back in January this year. “We have no plans to move back as of now”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Arshvir said, “India is growing fast, and above all the cosiness of our friends and family is what we had been missing in Canada in the past 10 years”.
Lakhvir Singh Detwal, Dharamvir’s father, said Arshvir is his younger brother’s son and they live in a joint family. “We have about 70 acres of land and we do farming. In 2015, when we had sent them together on a student visa, it was a time when everyone was sending their children abroad. But we self-introspected and asked our sons. They agreed to come back and help us in farming. Life is sorted now,” said Lakhvir.
Green Card holders
Harpal Singh Uppal, 64, got his Green Card in 2017, and shifted to California from the Kothe Puna village in Jagraon with his wife and son in the same year. “I got a Green Card because of blood relation as my wife’s family lives in the US. Initially, we went for two months and came back as my mother was alone here,” said Uppal.
Uppal’s son was pursuing a course in civil engineering in Punjab at that time. “In 2018, my son moved permanently, and me and my wife used to stay for six months each on rotation in India and the US as we had to take care of my mother. I used to drive a truck in California, and was happy that work was available whenever I used to be in California,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“However last year, I returned to India and now we are planning to surrender my Green Card and get a visitor visa. We married off my son Arshdeep Singh two years ago, and his wife who has a Canadian PR has also preferred to stay back in India with us in the village. My daughter is married in Canada,” he said.
Uppal said he travelled through the US and Canada to explore the area. “What I have gathered is that these countries are for skilled people who want to earn money in dollars and save in rupees. The system is organised but there is no social life and a large part of life is spent in paying off loan instalments.
But I feel that if we have two square meals to eat at our native place, there is no need to go to a foreign land,” he said.
Harpal said it is disheartening to see so many Indians being deported from the US. “People should always follow legal ways to go to a foreign land because the life of an illegal immigrant in the US is also of a second-class citizen till the time their court case is not decided … However, youngsters with skills who are not able to earn much in India must try to live their dreams in a foreign land.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Uppal, who has 45 acres of farm and also takes 40 acres on contract, and his son are now busy growing potato, paddy, and maize in their village.
‘Sanjha Ghar’
Charanjeet Singh, 52, came back to his village, Dhande in the Ludhiana district, in October 2023 after celebrating his 50th birthday in Canada. “We were very clear that after I would turn 50, I and my wife will move to our village,” he said.
Charanjeet went to Canada in 1998 after getting married to Harminder Kaur Mangat who had a Canadian PR. “In the initial years, I did whatever work I could do to earn money and gradually in 2005, I started my trucking company which had 25 trucks. In 2016, I opened a grocery store. My wife was working as a director of nursing”.
He said they gradually started winding up in 2020. They started the construction of Sanjha Ghar in 2020 on 1.5 acres of land on the Neelon-Ropar highway, and sold off the trucking company and grocery store by 2021. “So by the time, we came back permanently in October 2023, Sanjha Ghar was ready. After having a contended life in Canada, now we are living our second phase of life in India,” said Charanjeet.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Harminder Kaur Mangat (left) and Charanjeet Singh (right) at Sanjha Ghar project. (Express Photo)
“We also built our accommodation within the premises of this Sanjha Ghar where we grow organic vegetables and cook them in our restaurant to provide fresh Punjabi meals to customers. We also have two rooms where people spend weekends… Around 20 people have got employment in our Sanjha Ghar,” he said.
He said he has a 19-year-old daughter, and a son who is 25. “My daughter is a student in Canada, and my son has his own IT business … They chose to stay in Canada… We have told our kids to come to India to meet us whenever they want,” he said.
“At the same time, parents are also advised not to get too interfering in the lives of their children that they feel suffocated.. make them independent and self-reliant and also capable of taking their own decisions,” he said. “I don’t stop youngsters from going abroad, but there is so much to do here as well.”
A daughter’s return
Born in New Zealand, Avantika Panjtoori came back to her village Fatehgarh Panjtoor in Moga last year inspired by her father’s journey. Accepting a call from the Punjab Government for Non-Resident Punjabis (NRPs) to contribute to their homeland, Avantika said she has no plans to go back as of now.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
She is now empowering the local youth, especially girls, by equipping them with skills for self-reliance.
A government school science teacher, Jatinder said he went to New Zealand but maintained strong ties with his native village. “Though I had gone to New Zealand in 1999 after quitting my government job, I kept coming back to help my father in the school which he had established. I settled in the village in 2007, and used to go to New Zealand only during vacations. I am glad that now my daughter has also joined me,” said Jatinder, 54, who returned in 2007 following his heart.
Avantika at Auckland Institute of Skill Development, Fatehgarh Panjtoor village, Moga. (Express Photo)
Jatinder said his wife, eldest daughter, and son are in New Zealand. While his eldest daughter is married in New Zealand, his son who is 17, is in school.
Apart from her grandfather’s initiative SRM Senior Secondary School in the village, Avantika also takes care of Auckland Institute of Skill Development — another venture of the Panjtoori family. She said, “The institute provides free skill courses in computer literacy. We train students in logistics management and BPO for employment with the support of SS Group of Company (Mohali) and SBPS Group (US). So far, education in various vocational courses to more than 500 girls has been provided, helping them secure employment.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Understanding the transportation challenges faced by rural girls, Avantika said she has arranged free bus services from nearby towns like Makhu, Zira, and Dharamkot to her training centre for women.
Vishesh Sarangal, Deputy Commissioner, Moga, praised Avantika’s efforts in empowering women and urged NRPs from Moga district to step forward and give back to their homeland.

headline: In two-hour period before Delhi stampede, a telltale sign: 2,600 extra general tickets sold
description: The Indian Express has learnt that, on an average, 7,000 tickets are booked at the New Delhi Railway Station between 6 pm and 8 pm every day. On the day of the incident, however, more than 9,600 general class tickets were booked in the same duration.
content:
The Unreserved Ticketing System (UTS) used to book general class tickets shows that 2,600 more tickets than usual were booked on Saturday between 6 pm and 8 pm.
The stampede broke out at the station between 9 pm and 9.20 pm, killing 18 people and injuring several others.
The Indian Express has learnt that, on an average, 7,000 tickets are booked at the New Delhi Railway Station between 6 pm and 8 pm every day. On the day of the incident, however, more than 9,600 general class tickets were booked in the same duration.
In total, more than 54,000 general class tickets were booked through UTS on Saturday. “While there is no doubt that there were a huge number of people on the platform on February 15, it is still less than the total UTS tickets booked on 8 February and 29 January. On both of these days, 54,660 and 58,000 general class tickets were booked respectively. The crowd could have been managed,” said a senior official of the Ministry of Railways.

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
British-Irish woman’s rape-murder in Goa: Behind the conviction that earned investigators a ‘thank you’
Another official said that because of the rush to take dip in the Triveni sangam during Maha Kumbh, the total tickets booked can not give a clear picture of the actual crowd. “Because of the Maha Kumbh, currently, Indian Railways is not checking for the tickets on many key lines. There is already a huge rush; people are fighting to even stand inside the train. In such a situation, it is impossible to check if people in general class have booked a ticket or not. This figure of UTS ticket is reflective, but the actual crowd could have been much more,” said another Railways official.
The official said the incident could have been averted if the railway administration would have prepared itself taking a clue from more tickets being booked through UTS between these two crucial hours.
“The station master takes a call on rerouting trains. In yesterday’s incident, the announcement of the special train for the Prayagraj was crucial. Initially, the Kumbh passengers tried to board the Shiv Ganga Express, which was scheduled to leave platform no. 12 at 8.05 pm. But many could not get in and they kept waiting at the same platform. On the other side, at platform no. 14, the general class passengers were boarding the Magadh Express, which was scheduled to leave at 9.05 pm. But here, too, all the passengers could not get in,” said a senior official of the Ministry.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He said that a special train was announced at 8.50 pm for platform no. 12, while keeping in mind that the Prayagraj passengers of the Shiv Ganga Express were waiting there.
“There is no clear answer on how the incident could have been averted. However, if a special train could have been called on platform 14 or 15 after the trains there departed, this would perhaps not have happened as the remaining passengers, who intended to board Magadh Express, could have boarded the special train on the same platform,” said the official.
The officials also said that an appropriate number of personnel at the platform and a clear announcement for the passengers could have averted such a large-scale tragedy. There were around 60 personnel of Railway Protection Force (RPF) and 20 Delhi Police personnel deployed at 16 platforms of the New Delhi Railway station at the time of the stampede.
“These officers were on their regular duties on Saturday,” a Delhi police officer said. The officer said the Railways shared no alert with them about the swelling crowd.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In the past, stampedes in 2004 and 2010 occurred during festive seasons due to crowding at the station.
After these incidents, the government began deploying extra personnel during Holi, Diwali and Chhath Puja.
On Sunday, after the latest stampede, eight companies of paramilitary forces, including the Rapid Action Force, were deployed along with additional security personnel from the RPF and Delhi Police to manage the crowd until the conclusion of the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj.
They were primarily deployed at platforms 12, 13, 14, 15 and 16 — which trains heading to Prayagraj usually originate from.
“The deployment of RPF & GRP forces in New Delhi Railway Station has been increased. It has been decided that all special trains in the direction of Prayagraj will be run from platform number 16. Therefore all the passengers wanting to go to Prayagraj shall come and go from Ajmeri Gate side of the station. Indian Railways received more than 130 calls relating to yesterday’s unfortunate incident on Railways Helpline no 139 by 5 PM today,” said an official spokesperson of Ministry of Railways.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Delhi Police have also called six inspectors who were earlier posted at the New Delhi Railway Station to manage the crowds going forward.

headline: Live cartridges, firearms used in shootouts seized, 5 men arrested: Bengal police STF
description: A detailed probe revealed that cartridges were manufactured at an ordnance factory and were supplied from there, a police officer said
content:
The Special Task Force (STF) of the West Bengal Police on Sunday said that it has arrested five persons from the Jibantala area of South 24 Parganas district and recovered a huge cache of live cartridges and firearms.
A series of raids were conducted in Jibantala and Minakha areas of South and North 24 Parganas and 190 live cartridges of 7.65mm calibre, one double-barreled 12-bore IOF gun, and nine live 12-bore cartridges were recovered, the STF said.
A detailed probe revealed that cartridges were manufactured at an ordnance factory and were supplied from there, a police officer said. “We suspect these cartridges were supplied to the criminals. Officers are trying to trace them,” he added.
According to a source in the STF the cartridges were used in various shootouts across the state.

headline: Nothing wrong in interfaith marriages but action needed against fraudulent alliances: CM
description: Speaking in Nagpur, Fadnavis said that the Supreme Court and the Kerala High Court have made observations about the reality of “love jihad”.
content:
Two days after the Maharashtra government issued a Government Resolution (GR) on the formation of a committee headed by the state director general of police (DGP) to suggest steps to tackle the complaints of “love jihad” and forced conversions, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis Sunday said there was nothing wrong with interfaith marriages, but steps are needed against matrimonial alliances formed fraudulently or through false identity.
Speaking in Nagpur, Fadnavis said that the Supreme Court and the Kerala High Court have made observations about the reality of “love jihad”.
“It is a reality, and in Maharashtra, incidents of being duped into marriage and then abandoned once children are born are on the rise,” he said.
Adding that there was nothing wrong with interfaith marriages, the CM said instances of using fake identities and fraud are serious and need to be curbed.

headline: Need to seriously introspect whether death penalty required after 75 years of Constitution: SC judge Abhay Oka
description: Justice Abhay S Oka's observation comes in the backdrop of a recent report of Project 39A, a criminal justice programme at the National Law University, Delhi, which stated that the SC did not confirm a single death sentence in 2024 and 2023, while trial courts awarded 139 such verdicts.
content:
The legislature and judiciary should “seriously introspect” whether there should be capital punishment in our criminal justice system after 75 years of the Constitution and if it proved deterrent, said Supreme Court judge, Justice Abhay S Oka, here on Saturday.
His observation comes in the backdrop of a recent report of Project 39A, a criminal justice programme at the National Law University, Delhi which stated that the SC did not confirm a single death sentence in 2024 and 2023, while trial courts awarded 139 such verdicts.
Justice Oka also said there is a need to analyse how far our courts have protected the fundamental rights of fair trial and safeguards against arrest under the Constitution.
Justice Oka was delivering the third Ashok H Desai Memorial annual lecture on the topic “What ails our criminal justice system: Some thoughts”, organised by the Bombay Bar Association at Y B Chavan Auditorium. Desai was former Attorney General and Solicitor General of India.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Justice Oka, who became a Bombay HC judge in 2003 and is presently a member of the SC Collegium, said that “easy” measure of increasing strength of judges across courts was not being undertaken in a proper manner, but that alone would not solve the problem. Corresponding infrastructure for courts was also essential, he said.
Unlike Karnataka where he served as Chief Justice, he said the judiciary in Maharashtra struggles to get sufficient infrastructure for district and other trial courts, and several constructions for district courts took place only after orders of the Bombay High Court.
“Of course, to some extent I see there is a change for the good… It is a very sad story that we lack basic infrastructure. In Karnataka, the situation is exactly the reverse. Whatever the court wants, the government gives and, therefore, if you go to some of the courts in Karnataka, you will find far better judicial infrastructure,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Justice Oka emphasised that the well-settled principle of “bail is the rule and jail is an exception” should be “strictly implemented”, even for cases under special laws such as PMLA and UAPA with some modification. He raised concerns over the pendency of over 5,000 bail applications in the Bombay HC, inadequate public prosecutors and 80 per cent of prisoners in jail across Maharashtra being undertrials.
He said that in many cases, trial courts impose death penalty and High Courts or the SC have to let off the accused not only on benefit of doubt but also due to lack of legal evidence.
“Even today, when a ‘rarest of rare case’ comes before me, it will be my duty to impose capital punishment. Not as a judge, but as a student of law, I feel that we (judiciary) and the legislature must seriously introspect on one thing, whether in our system, there should be capital punishment. The reason is that our justice system is not foolproof. There is always a margin for error,” the judge said.
“We must also examine whether capital punishments have proved to be a deterrent. And third and most important thing, after 75 years of existence of the Constitution, it is an issue for debate, whether the state can take away somebody’s life,” Justice Oka said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Moreover, he said that as per criminal procedures, it was not mandatory for police to arrest each and every accused even when punishment is of more than seven years’ jail term, and accused can be summoned whenever required. However, he added that the situation is “different at grassroot level due to lot of pressure on police machinery, by citizens, NGOs and media” and politicians making statements such as accused will not get bail.
“It is a sad reflection of retributive tendencies which are still present in our society. Common people presume that once a person is named as an accused, he or she has definitely committed the offence,” Justice Oka said.
He said every citizen has the right to criticise judgment in a constructive manner. “However, even some educated people in the media and on social media platforms lack elementary knowledge of criminal jurisprudence and do not understand the difference between grant of bail and acquittal. The judges cannot go by perceptions.”
Justice Oka said that as per his personal experience, he cannot deny that there is an “element of truth in a criticism that people are not getting bail in deserving cases”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The SC judge suggested that instead of approaching courts, there should be a grievance redressal framework for victims if he or she has any issue with the manner in which the probe is being carried out and criminal justice suffering from ‘ailments’ can be strengthened with the help of all stakeholders.

headline: ‘Stop whitewashing these serious incidents’: AAP’s Sanjay Singh blames Railways for New Delhi stampede
description: AAP MP Sanjay Singh calls for accountability and compensation for families of the victims of Saturday's stampede at the New Delhi railway station.
content:
A day after a stampede claimed at least 15 lives at the New Delhi railway station, senior AAP leader and Rajya MP Sanjay Singh said that negligence and poor crowd management led to the tragedy, further alleging that the Railways never learnt lessons from its past mistakes.
“It is very painful to see a lot of people and devotees lost their lives in the stampede… but the Railways is still trying to whitewash the incident… While the exact number of deaths is unclear, reports vary, with some claiming 15 fatalities and others suggesting 20. Eyewitnesses at the scene have indicated that the death toll might be even higher, but official confirmation is still pending. The incident has raised serious concerns about the safety and management of the station,” he said on Sunday.
Singh added, “Wherever such incidents occur due to the mismanagement of the Railways, it tries to maintain that no such incident happened. They try to hide the entire matter by saying there was no such stampede. But when the matter gets out, they try to cover up by saying we have ordered a high-level inquiry… When is the Railways going to take responsibility and give answers to the people? Many rail accidents have taken place earlier and people have lost lives.”
Also Read | Delhi railway station stampede: Behind 10-minute chaos, delay of two trains, and an announcement
Discussing the scenes at the New Delhi railway station, Singh said, “Yesterday’s video of people standing on platforms at the station was so shocking. But the railway team was nowhere to be seen. Why was a proper announcement and security not deployed in advance to manage the crowd? Even after the news of the stampede, the Railway minister refuses to acknowledge that such an incident took place. The Delhi L-G posts a tweet and then edits it after 29 minutes. What is happening? Are you here for this?”

What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
Singh said that similar accidents had occurred in Uttar Pradesh after platform numbers were changed, but the Railways administration repeated the mistake in Delhi. “Kya hum logon ki marne ki niyati ban chuki hai? Why are you deploying security now at the hospital? To guard the dead? Where were you when they were alive, struggling at the railway station? Why are you trying to hide the total number of deaths? Because you don’t want to learn from your mistakes. Par aapko lage hue ghaav par namak chidakna hai…,” he said.
Further, taking a dig at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Singh said, “God has been elected in 2014, so God cannot be criticised… But the BJP government should stop whitewashing these serious incidents and the railway minister should give answers to the people now.”
The AAP leader also demanded compensation for families of the victims of the stampede.

headline: After GBS outbreak, Pune civic body may face water shortage as Maharashtra govt seeks dues
description: The water resources department will reduce the water supply to the PMC from February 25 onwards if the dues are not paid.
content:
The Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), already facing criticism for the Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS) outbreak due to the supply of contaminated raw water to residents in some parts of the city, is now likely to encounter a water shortage. This potential shortage arises from a warning issued by the state water resource department, which has stated that it will reduce the water supply from the Khadakwasla dam if the PMC does not pay its outstanding dues of Rs 726.12 crore by February 25.
In a notice served to the PMC, executive engineer of Khadakwasla Water Works S Y Kurhade said, “The water charges have been recovered as per the rates approved by the Maharashtra Water Resources Regulatory Authority (MWRRA) in 2022. The PMC has dues of Rs 726.12 crore on water charges till February 2025. This should be paid immediately to the water resource department.”
“If the dues are not cleared, then the water supply to the PMC will be reduced in phases from February 25 onwards. Thus, it is requested to take note of it and pay the dues as early as possible,” he said.
The PMC has been allocated 11.5 thousand million cubic feet (TMC) of water annually since 2005. However, the state water resource department claims that the civic body extracts more water than what is designated.

“The PMC has requested the state government to allocate 34.71 TMC of water for the city. Additionally, an appeal has been filed with the Maharashtra Water Resources Regulatory Authority (MWRRA) regarding the high rates imposed by the state water resource department for water charges,” said a civic officer.
The state irrigation department issued a notice after the PMC released a list of organisations, including the water resource department, with property tax dues and urged them to pay the amount as soon as possible.

headline: Gautam Buddh Nagar police urge YEIDA to widen roads around upcoming Noida airport
description: Widening the roads around the Noida International Airport is crucial for smooth traffic flow, benefiting both local residents and visitors, as per the letter from the police to the YEIDA.
content:
The Gautam Buddh Nagar police have written to the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) requesting the widening of all link roads and routes around the upcoming Noida International Airport to ensure smooth traffic, said officials Saturday.
“The construction work of Noida International Airport at western Uttar Pradesh’s Jewar is going on at a rapid pace. The operation of the airport is proposed to be done in the near future. Once the operation at the airport begins, various passenger terminals and cargo terminals will operate at Noida International Airport, leading to the movement of additional numbers of people from the country and abroad,” read the letter by Commissioner Laxmi Singh as per the official statement of the Noida police.
“The pressure of vehicles is increasing on all the roads connecting Noida International Airport. It is very important to widen the roads connecting Noida International Airport to make traffic smooth and accessible for local residents as well as outsiders,” it added.

headline: In ‘like & share’ cyber fraud, Delhi man arrested from Haryana’s Sirsa
description: The complainant was offered a part-time job involving liking and sharing online channels, with promises of commission and high returns, said police
content:
A cyber fraudster from Dwarka has been arrested from Sirsa in Haryana for allegedly duping people via an online “like and share” scheme.
The police identified the accused as Raj Kumar, who was arrested on February 6. The matter came to light when a complaint was registered at Dwarka’s Cyber Crime police station on December 9, 2023, detailing how the victim was lured into a fraudulent scheme through the Telegram app.
The complainant was offered a part-time job involving liking and sharing online channels, with promises of commission and high returns, said police.
DCP (Dwarka) Ankit Singh said, “After gaining the complainant’s trust, the fraudsters asked him to invest in packages… and assured him that they would provide high returns… The complainant invested Rs 3.3 lakh…”

“Following this, the cheaters switched off their cellphones, deleted the investment groups from Telegram and did not return the money or the promised high returns to the complainant,” he added.

headline: AIIMS doctor who accused colleague of rape says threatened to drop case, police registers 3rd FIR
description: The woman had in July 2023 filed a case against the doctor accusing him of rape, causing miscarriage and criminal intimidation.
content:
Almost two years after a doctor from All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) was booked on charges of rape of another doctor, the 39-year-old victim on Friday approached the police alleging that she was being threatened to drop the case.
Following this, Hauz Khas police on Friday lodged an FIR under sections 232(1) and 351(4), pertaining to threatening and intimidating a person, of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
This is the third case lodged in relation to the matter. While the rape case was lodged in July 2023, on December 2, 2024, too, a case was lodged after the woman alleged that she was being threatened by the accused doctor and his associates. All three cases have been lodged by the Hauz Khas police.
According to the FIR, the woman was on her way to the hospital on Friday when she received two phone calls from an unknown number. “The caller threatened me and asked me to take back the rape case… He said he will shoot me dead and also said he knew about my whereabouts and timings. I was shocked, scared and immediately dialled 112 (police helpline number) and informed the police,” the FIR quoted her as saying. She alleged that the caller also abused her.

headline: Ex-Goa MLA dies shortly after physical altercation with auto driver in Belagavi
description: Former Goa MLA Lavoo Suryaji Mamledar represented the Ponda constituency from 2012 to 2017. Police say his car brushed past the accused’s auto
content:
Former Goa MLA Lavoo Suryaji Mamledar, who represented the Ponda constituency from 2012 to 2017, died shortly after a physical altercation with an autorickshaw driver in Karnataka’s Belagavi on Saturday afternoon.
According to police, the 69-year-old was travelling to Belagavi and had booked a suite in a hotel in Khade Bazar. As his car navigated a narrow curve, it allegedly brushed against an autorickshaw, leading to an argument between Mamledar and the auto driver.
The driver allegedly demanded compensation for damage, which Mamledar refused before proceeding towards his hotel, police said.
However, the autorickshaw driver followed him to the hotel and according to eyewitnesses, the auto driver allegedly slapped Mamledar in the hotel’s parking area. As Mamledar attempted to climb the stairs to reach his suite, he collapsed in front of the reception counter. He was rushed to the emergency of the government civil hospital, where doctors declared him dead.

headline: Punjab and Haryana HC rules in favour of Army widow’s right to adopt, grants benefits to children
description: She had adopted two children 13 years after her husband, a sepoy in the Jat regiment was killed in action
content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has ruled that the legally adopted children of a war widow are entitled to the same benefits as biological children of deceased soldiers, setting aside an earlier decision that denied them educational benefits. The division bench, comprising Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma and Justice Meenakshi I. Mehta, held that the widow’s right to adopt is protected under the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956, and that such an adoption must be recognised for all consequential benefits.
The case involved Nirdesh Devi, widow of late Sepoy Ramesh Kumar of the Jat Regiment, who “suffered battle casualty” on 25 February 2000. She had married Ramesh Kumar on 5 February 1999, but they remained childless at the time of his death. Facing societal pressures, she adopted two children, Nikhil and Nancy, from her husband’s elder brother in 2013 through a registered adoption deed. Seeking to secure educational benefits for them under a government scheme for children of personnel below officer rank (PBOR) killed or permanently disabled in action, she submitted a request to the army authorities.
However, her application was rejected based on a Ministry of Defence (MoD) letter dated 28 August 2002, which stipulated that only serving personnel or living ex-servicemen could adopt children for the purposes of government benefits. Further, the army declined to issue a Part-II order—the official military record of adoption—for the children, stating that adoption after the death of a soldier was not recognised for welfare benefits.
Devi challenged this decision in the Punjab and Haryana High Court, but her writ petition was dismissed by a single judge. She then filed an appeal before the division bench, arguing that under Section 8(c) of the Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, a widow has the right to adopt, and such adoption carries full legal validity. Her counsel further contended that the MoD letter did not explicitly bar the recognition of adopted children in cases where the soldier had died in action.

During the appeal, it was revealed that in December 2016, while the case was pending, the army had briefly recognised the adoption by issuing a Part-II order and granting the children Education Scholarship Entitlement Cards. However, in 2017, the army withdrew this recognition, citing a clerical error. The High Court took serious note of this reversal, calling it arbitrary and against public policy.
The division bench ruled that once an adoption is legally valid under Hindu law, the rights of the adopted children must be treated as equivalent to those of biological children. The court observed that the army’s interpretation of the MoD policy was incorrect, as it did not explicitly bar adoption by widows. It further noted that denying benefits to legally adopted children of deceased personnel violated the principles of fairness and equality.
Setting aside the single judge’s order, the bench quashed the army’s rejection order dated 6 February 2014 and directed that the benefits be restored to Devi’s adopted children. The court also held that the MoD letter of 2002 must be interpreted in a manner that includes children adopted by war widows, ensuring that they are not unfairly excluded from entitlements granted to soldiers’ families.

headline: Kesari Tours founder Kesaribhau Patil dies at 90
description: Teacher-turned-businessman, Patil set up ‘Kesari Tours’ in 1984 to fulfill his dream of making travel affordable for middle-class families.
content:
Kesaribhau Patil, the founder of leading travel company Kesari Tours, passed away in Mumbai on Saturday. He was 90 years old.
Kesari Bhau Patil was born in 1935 in Mathane village, in the Safale area of Palghar district, Maharashtra, to a middle-class family. In the early years of his life, he worked as a teacher. Later, to fulfill his dream of making travel affordable for middle-class families, he established ‘Kesari Tours’ in 1984 when he was 50 and settled in Mumbai with his family.
He started the first office of Kesari Tours in the Dadar-Mahim area. The company today has expanded across the globe, organising domestic and international tours. He was honoured with several national and international awards for his contributions to the tourism industry.

headline: ‘Maratha community has been let down’: Quota activist Jarange-Patil reacts to BJP MLA Dhas’s meetings with NCP minister Dhananjay Munde

content:

Jarange-Patil said Dhas has let down the Maratha community which had admired him for raising his voice against the killers of Beed sarpanch Santosh Deshmukh.
“Dhas has been vocal against those behind the murder of Santosh Deshmukh. He vowed to destroy the political careers of those people. Now he has gone and seen the faces of those people. How can he meet a cruel man? How can he meet a man whose associates are responsible for the murder of Santosh Deshmukh? Now, whom should the Maratha community seek justice from?” Jarange-Patil told media persons at Antarwali-Saraati in the Jalna district.
“He tried getting compliments from the Maratha community and at the same, he is playing politics… If he wanted honour from the Maratha community, then he should have fought for the community till the end,” the quota activist added.
On Friday, it emerged that Dhas, a vocal critic of Dhananjay Munde, had met the minister twice. Once, he had met Munde a fortnight ago at the residence of BJP state president Chandrashekhar Bawankule in Mumbai. The second meeting happened at Munde’s residence in Mumbai on Wednesday.

headline: Bhupesh Baghel appointed Punjab in-charge, Congress gears up for ‘Mission 2027’ in state
description: Insiders say Bhupesh Baghel’s appointment reflects the Congress leadership’s serious intent to unify the party ranks in Punjab and wrest power from the AAP in the next Assembly polls.
content:
The Congress has appointed former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel as the AICC general secretary in charge of Punjab in what appears to be the launch of a firm bid by the party for the 2027 Assembly polls in the state. The appointment was announced on Friday night.
Baghel replaces Devendra Anand who took over the charge in December 2023. The appointment comes in the wake of a reshuffle by the All India Congress Committee (AICC) that saw the in-charges of several states being changed.
Leader of Opposition Partap Singh Bajwa has welcomed Baghel’s appointment and said he looked forward to working as a team for Mission 2027.
There had been considerable discussion in Punjab Congress circles regarding the impending changes involving the appointment of the new general secretary in charge as well as the new Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) president. Former state in-charge Harish Chaudhary was reportedly very keen to get his old job back.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
A revamp of the state Congress structure is also on the cards with new appointees being considered for all levels of PCC. There are speculations on whether former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi, the Lok Sabha MP from Jalandhar, will return to state politics as the PCC chief, being the party’s Dalit face. Congress sources said he was slated to be appointed as an AICC general secretary in charge of a major state but requested a major role in Punjab.
Congress insiders say Baghel’s appointment as Punjab in-charge reflects the Congress leadership’s serious intent to unify the party ranks in the state and wrest power from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) in the 2027 Assembly polls. It is believed that the AAP rose to power in Punjab mainly because the Congress ranks were fractured in 2021-22 which led to the removal of Captain Amarinder Singh as the chief minister.
Bhupesh Baghel served as the chief minister of Chhattisgarh from 2018 to 2023. Born on August 23, 1960, in Durg district, he has had a long-standing association with the Congress. He is often referred to by the nickname “Kaka” which translates to uncle, reflecting his approachable public image.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Baghel’s political journey began in the 1980s with the Indian Youth Congress. He represented Patan constituency in the Chhattisgarh Assembly, winning elections multiple times since 1993, with a brief hiatus after losing in 2008.
Before Chhattisgarh was carved out of Madhya Pradesh in 2000, Baghel was the Cabinet minister for transport under Digvijaya Singh’s government. After the state’s formation, he served as the minister for revenue, public health engineering and relief works in the first Chhattisgarh government led by Ajit Jogi.
In 2018, Baghel became the chief minister after leading the Congress to a significant victory in the state elections, ending the BJP’s 15-year rule. His tenure focused on social welfare, agriculture support and tribal rights, among other initiatives.
Baghel introduced schemes like the Rajiv Gandhi Kisan Nyay Yojana to provide financial assistance to farmers. He launched the Swami Atmanand English Medium School Scheme to improve educational infrastructure and accessibility.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Known for his efforts to foster social equality, Baghel has also initiated low-cost marriage campaigns to make weddings less extravagant.
His term was not without controversies, including allegations of involvement in a liquor scam and scrutiny over the Mahadev betting app case, where he was named in the Enforcement Directorate’s chargesheet. However, he has denied these allegations, framing them as political vendetta.
After losing the 2023 Chhattisgarh Assembly elections, Baghel has continued his political activities, focusing on national Congress strategies and state politics.

headline: ‘Artha Chakra’ event at GIPE: OLA CEO calls Western AI firms ‘East India Company Part 2’
description: Bhavish Aggarwal also criticised the American AI model, citing its control over the algorithms and training data.
content:
While India generates 20 percent of all the world’s data, only 3-5 percent of it is used in AI training, as most Indian data is exported and then imported back as AI-driven services sold in dollars by the west. Bhavish Aggarwal, CEO of Ola Cabs likens this situation to a modern-day “East India Company,” where India supplies the raw material (data) but pays a premium for the finished product.
He said this on the first day of Gokhale Institute of Politics and Economics (GIPE)’s ‘Artha Chakra’ event which is being held between 14-16 February. Agrawal in his address emphasised that India must develop its own AI ecosystem, given that the country has the largest number of developers and vast amounts of data.
“This is the East India Company Part 2. This time they (West) are not selling us clothes with cotton but they are selling AI with our data..We need to build our own foundational large language model (LLMs) but they need to be built from an ‘Indic lens’ with Indic data, Indic context, Indic knowledge system,” he said while responding to Sanjeev Sanyal, GIPE Chancellor in an interactive session on ‘AI to Mobility’.
Ethics, Open-Source AI, and India’s Approach
Aggarwal also criticised the American AI model, citing its control over the algorithms and training data. “…there’s a big global debate on ethics in AI and the American paradigm here I actually believe is not the right one. The American paradigm is a closed source one where large corporations like Open AI or Google control their algorithms and the training data,” he said. Instead, he advocates for an open-source, community-driven approach, similar to India’s success with UPI and ONDC.

I think America has 20 gigawatts already and will be adding 20 gigawatts in the next 2 years,” he said.
“India must invest in data storage and computing power. Krutrim aims to build a hyperscale cloud infrastructure comparable to Amazon Web Services (AWS)…Krutrim’s cloud services are already revenue-generating, with 100,000 developers currently using the Krutrim cloud,” added founder of Ola Electric and founder of Ola Krutrim.

headline: Telangana businessman’s murder: Karnataka court rejects bail plea of Haryana man accused of conspiring with victim’s estranged wife
description: A Kodagu district court rejected the bail plea of Ankur Rana, who has been accused of murdering businessman Ramesh Kumar, noting he had escaped from police custody once.
content:
A district court in Karnataka has rejected the bail plea of a Haryana man accused of murdering a Telangana businessman near Hyderabad and dumping the body in a coffee estate in Kodagu in October last year after allegedly conspiring with the businessman’s estranged wife and her boyfriend.
On Wednesday, a Kodagu court rejected the bail plea of Ankur Rana, 32, a driver from Haryana, noting that he had already escaped from police custody once when he was taken to Telangana during the investigation. The police filed a chargesheet in the case on January 20.
The district court noted that “the offences are severe in nature and allegations are grave in nature and participation of Petitioner is clear along with accused No.1 and he has scant respect for the law, therefore, the court is of the opinion that, this is not a fit case to exercise the discretion u/Sec. 483 of BNS, 2023 to enlarge him on regular bail”.
The semi-burnt body of a 54-year-old businessman, Ramesh Kumar, from Telangana, was found in a private coffee estate in Suntikoppa in Kodagu on October 8, 2024. The probe led to the arrest of Rana, Panthalu Niharika alias Nikita alias Sailatha alias Akula Sailatha, 29, Kumar’s Bengaluru-based estranged wife, and her boyfriend Mai Reddy Nikhil, 28.

The police probe revealed that Niharika was lodged in a prison in Haryana’s Karnal from February 2021 to December 2021 in a cheating case filed by her second husband, Kamaldeep Saini, where she met Rana, who used to visit the same prison to meet his mother who had been arrested in an atrocity case.
Niharika allegedly hatched the murder plot to lay her hands on documents to a property worth Rs 8 crore in Telangana, which Kumar, her third husband, had not shared with her.
According to the Kodagu police, Niharika bought a flight ticket for Rana to travel to Hyderabad on October 3 last year, and the duo executed Kumar’s murder on October 4 after Niharika lured him to a meeting. According to the police, Rana strangulated the businessman to death in a Maruti car after getting Kumar to stop by the side of the road.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Kumar’s body was allegedly transported over a distance of 850 km from Hyderabad to Suntikoppa in the hill district of Kodagu by Niharika, Rana and Nikhil in a Mercedes Benz GLA 2022 car loaned to the businessman by a friend in Hyderabad, as per the police.

The Kodagu police cracked the case of the unidentified body after nearly 12 days of investigations through the analysis of CCTV footage from over 500 cameras, which led to the identification of the Mercedes Benz in which the body had been transported to Kodagu.
Technical analysis of Kumar’s phone records led the police to Niharika and Nikhil and later to Rana in Haridwar, Uttarakhand, where he was working as a driver after the murder. During the probe, Rana escaped from the Kodagu police custody in Hyderabad on October 31 last year before he was tracked down again to Jaipur in Rajasthan on November 5 through the combined efforts of police from multiple states.
The investigation into Kumar’s murder unravelled the criminal history of Niharika, allegedly a thrice-married woman involved with honey-trapping software engineers in Bengaluru by posing as a software engineer on dating sites.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Niharika allegedly had a registered marriage with Kumar in 2018. She allegedly met him on a train in Hyderabad and claimed to be an information technology sector employee.
She was named an accused in a 2017 case in Bengaluru where she was arrested for allegedly luring a software engineer with sexual favours before attempting to extort funds from the techie. She was allegedly part of a gang involved in honey-trapping software engineers for extortion, the police had alleged at the time. She was acquitted in the case in 2019.

headline: West Bengal: Youth held for ‘sexually assaulting’ teen
description: According to police sources, the accused had been harassing the girl in public places and stalking her
content:

headline: Commuters cry foul despite recalibration of fares, say BMRCL committing ‘daylight robbery’
description: BMRCL accepted that errors were identified in fare calculations across 450 different station-to-station combinations.
content:
Even after the Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) recalibrated its fare structure following severe public backlash, several commuters Friday complained that the revised fares, too, were exorbitantly high.
Many passengers took to social media, accusing BMRCL of failing to adhere to its commitment of capping abnormal fare hikes at 70 per cent.
Kumar, a regular metro commuter, criticised the steep fare increase. “The earlier fare from RV Road to Trinity was ₹33.25, then it was increased to ₹57, and now it has been further raised to ₹60. This is ridiculous!” he wrote on X, calling the hike unjustified.
Similarly, Sreejith Pai pointed out inconsistencies in the new fare structure, alleging that BMRCL was overcharging commuters beyond the limits recommended by the Fare Fixation Committee (FFC).
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
“Earlier, the fare was ₹33.25, then it increased to ₹60. Even after yesterday’s commitment of a maximum 71% hike, it’s still the same at 81%. The FFC recommended a 45% increase, yet BMRCL is charging almost double,” he wrote.
Several other passengers also voiced their frustration, with many calling the fare hike “daylight robbery” and questioning the rationale behind the calculations. Some demanded greater transparency from BMRCL in explaining how the new fares were determined.
Speaking to The Indian Express, a BMRCL spokesperson said, “We reviewed some of these complaints and found out that some commuters are comparing the fare structures of smart cards (which have discounts) to that of QR tickets where discounts have been revoked. The 5 per cent discount on QR tickets was removed and such tickets are costing 5 per cent more. Meanwhile, after recalibration of fare structure, the maximum hike has been slashed by 30 per cent and we have restricted it to 70 per cent as per the FFC.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
According to BMRCL, errors were identified in fare calculations across 450 different station-to-station combinations. These discrepancies led to abnormal fare hikes in certain routes, prompting a review and recalibration of the fare structure.
As per BMRCL estimates, around three lakh passengers (46 per cent) are expected to benefit after the rationalisation of the fare structure. However, the maximum fare remains at Rs 90, making Bengaluru metro the costliest in India.
Bengaluru metro, which usually records a daily ridership of over eight lakh, has seen a dip of nearly 1 lakh passengers since the fare hike kicked in on February 9. In the last four days, the ridership has dipped by 11 per cent, indicating a significant drop due to the fare hike.

headline: Amid Ranveer Allahbadia row, Marathi YouTube channel BhaDiPa cancels episode after MNS objection
description: The team behind BhaDiPa announced that they are cancelling the episode as they don’t wish to “harm people’s sentiments nor risk the safety of our audience and talent."
content:
The Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) has issued a warning to Marathi YouTube channel Bharatiya Digital Party (BhaDiPa) and asked it to discontinue airing its show ‘Atishay Nirlaj Kande Pohe’ alleging that its content is obscene.
The issue comes amid the controversy surrounding standup comedian Samay Raina’s YouTube show ‘India’s Got Latent’ on which podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia made remarks that have since drawn widespread condemnation.
Chetan Dhotre, city unit president of the MNS Film Wing, said his party has warned the makers of BhaDiPa against recording and airing content on February 14 as its previous episode allegedly had “vulgar content”.
“No one ever expected that Ranveer Allahbadia would make a vulgar statement on the show ‘India’s Got Latent’. It was shameful. Similar work is being done by Marathi content providers through its show ‘Atishay Nirlaj Kande Pohe’ on YouTube. This is disrespectful to Marathi-speaking people,” he said.

Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Dhotre alleged that BhaDiPa has been producing content that goes against cultural values for the sole purpose of increasing ratings. “This trend…is on the rise. We will not allow it to happen in Pune. They should be involved in clean entertainment which will be supported by MNS but the vulgar statements in the show will not be tolerated now. We are condemning the channel and its producer for hosting a show with vulgar content,” he said.
“The MNS will stop these shows on its own. Marathi people attending or viewing the show should think about these things, considering Marathi culture,” Dhotre stated.
The BhaDiPa team informed The Indian Express that they cancelled the upcoming episode and announced the decision over social media on Tuesday. The team’s statement read, “We cancelled the show because we wanted to be responsible given the current climate, we don’t want to harm people’s sentiments nor risk the safety of our audience and talent.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The show was planned on February 14 for a live audience ahead of being uploaded on the YouTube channel.
The statement added, “We are assessing the situation and will re-evaluate our programming once things normalise because we have a large family audience and want to keep their best interests in mind. We have been in touch with MNS to resolve the issue.”

headline: Punjab pilgrims on way to Ayodhya from Mahakumbh meet with accident, father of 2 young children among dead
description: The Mahakumbh pilgrims were from the Fazilka and Muktsar districts in Punjab.
content:
Two people died and nine got injured when a tempo traveller carrying devotees from Punjab collided with a truck on the way to Ayodhya late Thursday night.
The pilgrims were from the Fazilka and Muktsar districts in Punjab and visited the ongoing Mahakumbh Mela in Prayagraj. They had also planned to visit the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya.
The deceased include the driver, Tarksheel, 35, a resident of Sureshwala village in Fazilka district, and pilgrim Hardyal Chand, a resident of Fazilka city.
Tarksheel was a tempo driver and the pilgrims had hired his services. The group started off from Fazilka on February 9 and was supposed to be back by the coming Sunday.

Harpal Singh, father of Tarksheel, said, “Tarksheel made a video call on Thursday morning and showed us the Sangam at the Mahakumbh. He even sent me videos of the Mahakumbh. He told me that he was going to Ayodhya from Prayagraj along with the pilgrims and afterward would be back in Punjab. We never knew that it would be his last call.
“The pilgrims accompanying him called us on the intervening night of Thursday and Friday to inform us that Tarksheel had met with an accident. I got another call on Friday morning at around 8 am, informing us that Tarksheel was no more.”
Tarksheel is survived by his parents, wife, and two young children – a son, 5, and a daughter, 3. He was the only child of his parents.

headline: Day after Maghi Purnima Snan at Maha Kumbh: Main rituals over, crowds start thinning
description: After akharas, 10 lakh kalpvasis begin to leave Mela area for their homes
content:
With the main rituals at Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj being wrapped up a day after the Maghi Purnima Snan got over on Wednesday, more than 10 lakh kalpvasis camping at the mela site since Makar Sankranti on January 14 have started leaving for home.
Most of the akharas have already moved out after the Basant Panchmi Snan on February 3.
While 10 akharas had left by February 7, the rest of three were leaving by Thursday evening, said Mahant Dharmendra Das of Udaseen Akhara (Bandhua).
The Bada and Chhota Udaseen Akhara have left but the Udaseen Bandhua would stay at the mela until Shivratri which happens to be the final day of the Maha Kumbh, Das added.

Delhi gets its fourth woman CM: All about Rekha Gupta
Priyanka Chopra helps needy man on Mumbai streets, ends her India trip with daughter Malti Marie. Watch videos
Sectors 18 and 19, occupied by kalpvasis, would be vacated in the next three days. All the akharas were camping at Sector 20.
While camps of various religious organisations would continue until the end of Maha Kumbh, the events being organised so far would start wrapping up today onwards, informed and office-bearer of one such outfit.
DGP Prashant Kumar told The Indian Express, “After Magh Purnima Snan, it seems the withdrawal would begin. Nearly 5 lakh kalpvasis have already left by morning. Remaining are leaving. All the arrangements including security, traffic, observation, administration would be in place as usual and would continue till the completion of Mahakumbh on February 26.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He said while the pilgrims are coming to Prayagraj, the number is expected to reduce comparatively. The pressure on road traffic would also be eased, he added.
According to the Mela administration, traffic is moving smoothly on all major routes, including Malak Harhar (Lucknow), Mirzapur Road, Rewa Road, Sahson (Jaunpur), Phaphamau (Lucknow), Andawa (Varanasi route), and Kaushambi.
The Traffic Department has urged devotees to adhere to the instructions issued by the administration and avoid unnecessary halts on any route.
Meanwhile, a Climate Conference is scheduled to be held at Kumbh on February 16.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The UP Department of Environment, Forest, and Climate Change is organising the Climate Conference on ‘’Kumbh ki Aastha aur Jalvayu Parivartan’ (Faith and Climate Change). CM Yogi Adityanath will attend the conference, along with spiritual leaders, environmentalists, social organisations, and business leaders to discuss ways to protect and improve the environment.
The same day, a three-day bird festival will also begin. The International Bird Festival will feature around 200 bird species, including rare Indian skimmers, flamingos, and Siberian cranes. The visitors will also get a glimpse of migratory birds from Siberia, Mongolia, Afghanistan, and more than a dozen other countries.

headline: AAP MLA Amanatullah Khan gets interim protection from arrest
description: Asked if Delhi Police have any CCTV video to show that AAP MLA Amanatullah Khan tried to prevent a proclaimed offender’s arrest, the additional public prosecutor informs the court, ‘Light udd gayi thi.’
content:
A Delhi court Thursday granted AAP Okhla MLA Amanatullah Khan interim protection from arrest in connection with an FIR registered against him on Monday for allegedly obstructing police from arresting a proclaimed offender.
Special Judge Jitendra Singh of the Rouse Avenue Court questioned Delhi Police why they had gone to arrest Shavez Khan, the proclaimed offender in question, when he was on anticipatory bail. “If Shavez Khan was on anticipatory bail, was the police right in going to arrest the accused… was this in discharge of their duty?” the judge asked.
“The allegation of the police team that the applicant was instrumental in facilitating the escape of accused Shavez Khan does not seem to carry weight as he (Shavez Khan) was already on anticipatory bail in the case in which allegedly police had gone to arrest him,” he said in the order.
Police alleged that the MLA “pushed and manhandled” officers threatening that action would be taken against them.

What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
Judge Singh asked the police if they had any CCTV footage of the MLA’s alleged intervention in preventing the arrest of Shavez Khan. “Is there any footage? Let the court know what happened,” the judge said.
“Light udd gayi thi (there was no electricity),” came the response from Additional Public Prosecutor (APP) Atul Kumar Srivastava.
“We have phones these days… police record every little thing on their devices these days,” the judge responded. “This is going heavily against you. Please take time and get me the complete facts of this case,” he added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
APP Srivastava said it was not the first time Amanatullah had misbehaved with police. “I can show the court what Amanatullah Khan is… he’s habitual in mistreating police officers,” he said.
While granting the MLA interim protection from arrest until the next date of hearing — February 24 — the judge directed him to join the investigation. The judge also directed that the police questioning of him be recorded on a CCTV camera.
Police questioned the MLA at the Jamia Nagar police station on Thursday evening.
The MLA and his supporters have been booked under sections 221 (obstruction of public servants while they are performing their duties), 132 (criminal force or assault against a public servant while they are performing their duties), 121 (voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt to deter public servant from his duty), 191 (rioting), 190 (unlawful assembly), 263 (resistance or obstruction to lawful apprehension of another person), 351 (criminal intimidation), and 111 (organised crime) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The FIR against him stated: “… the local MLA, Amanatullah Khan, came there with 20-25 people and said, ‘how dare you come here…’ (He) and his companions pushed and manhandled us and… threatened us… said ‘no one will know where you people have gone and your police and court papers will remain here’.”
In 2018, Shavez Khan and his associates allegedly attacked a group of men near Batla House. As per the FIR in the case, Shavez and a person named Shabbu approached the victims at an empty plot along with four other men. Shavez allegedly fired at the men, who were also attacked with rods.
Police sources said Shavez was arrested but granted conditional bail by a court in 2018, following which he stopped responding to court summonses, prompting the court to declare him a proclaimed offender.

headline: 21-year-old man critically hurt after ticket checker ‘pushes’ him off train; case lodged
description: The Vapi GRP Police has registered a case against the accused, Ashok Kumbhare, and started a probe. According to police sources, victim Sandeep Arya, and Ajay Kumar, who work at a factory in Vapi, had gone to Bhilad to buy some parts required for repairing a boiler.
content:
A 21-year-old man sustained serious injuries after he was allegedly pushed out of a running train when the ticket checker found that he was travelling — on a local passenger train going from Bhilad to Vapi in Valsad — without a ticket, said police on Thursday.
The Vapi GRP Police has registered a case against the accused, Ashok Kumbhare, and started a probe. According to police sources, victim Sandeep Arya, and Ajay Kumar, who work at a factory in Vapi, had gone to Bhilad to buy some parts required for repairing a boiler.
On Tuesday night, when the duo reached Bhilad railway station, they found that the Mumbai-Valsad local train was about to leave and boarded the train without buying a ticket, said police sources.
On the way, the ticket checker caught them travelling without a ticket following which he asked them to pay Rs 1,000 each as penalty, to which they refused, leading to heated arguments between them. The duo also made Kumbhare talk to their firm owner, Sarfaraz Malavikya, but the former was not convinced, said police. Later, Kumbhare allegedly took away Arya’s mobile phone as he was trying to reach out to other people. When the train arrived at Vapi station, both attempted to get down but were stopped by Kumbhare, who told them to accompany him to Valsad railway station to be handed over to the Railway Protection Force.

content:

headline: The flight to Bangkok: How a ‘business trip’ by former Maharashtra minister’s son sent state machinery into a whirl
description: Less than an hour after the kidnapping case was registered, Sawant held a press conference to announce that his son had been “traced”.
content:
Former minister Tanaji Sawant’s son Rushiraj Sawant was gone for only four hours. But by the time his flight landed back at the Pune airport at 8.45 pm Monday, he had been reported missing, the Pune Police were scrambling to investigate his possible “kidnapping”, and his father had moved the state machinery, including Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis — all in an attempt to get him back.
At 4.30 pm Monday, Rushiraj Sawant, 32, the younger of the two sons of former Maharashtra minister and now Shiv Sena MLC Tanaji Sawant, took off with his two friends on a chartered flight to Bangkok. Minutes later, the Pune City Police registered an FIR under kidnapping charges based on a complaint from a staffer at the JSPM Narhe Technical Campus, an institute that’s part of the Sawant family-run Jayawant Shikshan Prasarak Mandal (JSPM) Trust.
In his complaint at the city’s Sinhagad Road police station, the staffer claimed that Rushiraj, the director of the institute, had allegedly been kidnapped in a Swift car. The case was soon handed over to the Crime Branch.
Around the same time, Sawant and his family allegedly contacted the state machinery – including the chief minister of Maharashtra and other senior leaders in Mumbai – as well as the Union Ministry for Civil Aviation.

Read | Chartered Bangkok flight was for business trip: Ex-minister Tanaji Sawant’s son
Police say that as their investigation progressed, it became clear that Rushiraj and his two friends had, in fact, boarded a chartered flight to Bangkok. The probe also revealed that Rushiraj had booked the flight the day before for Rs 78 lakh from a Noida-headquartered chartered flight operator.
Less than an hour after the kidnapping case was registered, Sawant held a press conference to announce that his son had been “traced”.
“It never happens in our home. Even if he (Rushiraj) is going to Wakad in the suburban Pimpri-Chinchwad, he informs me,” Sawant, flanked by senior police officers, told the media. “But when we got to know that he had gone with two friends without taking his car and had taken a private chartered flight, we became concerned… And because of this, I called CP saheb (the Police commissioner of Pune), other senior officers and Fadnavis saheb (CM Devendra Fadnavis). Police are also trying their level best and we are also trying our level best to bring him back”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Read | ‘Power misuse’: MVA demands ex-minister’s arrest, MoS exit
Officials say that a flurry of messages between the state government and the Ministry of Civil Aviation led to the flight being turned around when it was somewhere between Chennai and the Andaman Islands. The drama, which involved the police, central government entities and the media, finally concluded when the flight landed back in Pune at 8.45 pm – all without the knowledge of its three passengers, including Rushiraj.
Back in Pune, Rushiraj told the police that he had booked the flight for a “business trip”. He also said that he had gone to Dubai the week before, and, fearing that his family would not approve of “consecutive foreign trips”, had chosen not to inform them about this one.
A police source said, “One of Rushiraj’s travelling companions is associated with JSPM (the Trust) and the other is a private businessman.”
Rushiraj and his older brother Giriraj are office bearers at JSPM and hold positions in several family run companies in agriculture and real estate sector, public records show. Meanwhile, their father Tanaji Sawant, a current Shiv Sena MLC, was a minister in the Eknath Shinde government but was reportedly kept out of the Devendra Fadnavis Cabinet formed in December.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Both of Tanaji’s sons are married into the family of Shankar Jagtap, a BJP MLA from Pimpri-Chinchwad.
Sources in the Pune Police have conceded that Minister of State for Civil Aviation Murlidhar Mohol, a BJP leader from Maharashtra, had helped them get in touch with the civil aviation department, which had “contacted” the Thai authorities.
Pune Police Commissioner Amitesh Kumar too admits that authorities had sought help from the ministry and the Director General of Civil Aviation.
“After the FIR was registered, we had made a request to the DDCA that if the aircraft was in Indian territory, it should be told to land in Indian airspace anywhere on India soil… The case could have had widespread implications. From the police point of view, we acted very swiftly and took the case to its logical conclusion in the shortest possible time,” he says.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The police now say they will file a closure report in the case.
But the episode has sparked opposition allegations of a “family feud” and “misuse of state machinery”, with many leaders demanding a case against Sawant. There are also calls from some quarters for Mohol to resign for “enabling” the drama.
“The entire system seems to have been misused just because the son of a politician angrily left for Bangkok. This is nothing but blatant misuse of power,” says Sanjay Raut, spokesperson of Shiv Sena (UBT), the rival Sena faction. “Both Sawant and Mohol should face action in the matter”.
Opposition leaders alleged that the entire system bent over backwards to accommodate one leader.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“One of the accused in the Beed sarpanch murder case has still not been found after two months. And here the entire system was moved to get back the son of a former minister…What kind of system has been put in place by the Mahayuti government,” says Baramati MP Supriya Sule, a leader from the Nationalist Congress Party-Sharadchandra Pawar.
However, the Sawants deny any misuse of power, also claiming there was “no family feud”. “We have never had any feuds in the family. I approached the police because he had left without informing anyone in the family,” Sawant claims.
His older son Giriraj too claims his father acted “as any parent would”.
“No, there was no misuse of power. You should look from the point of view of parents. Their son left without informing anyone… That’s why we approached the police… We want to thank Chief Minister Fadnavis, Deputy chief ministers Shinde and Ajit Pawar, and Mohol for their intervention in bringing Rushiraj back,” he says.
