headline: Chandigarh MP Manish Tewari questions shifting deadlines to clean Dadumajra dump: ‘most unfortunate’
description: The Centre cited Swachh Bharat Mission funding and ongoing bio-remediation while extending the timeline for clearing the Dadumajra dump to July.
content:
Chandigarh MP Manish Tewari Thursday criticised the shifting of deadlines yet again for clearing the massive garbage dump at Dadumajra, alleging that the government has been evasive about the expenditure incurred on the project.
Tewari said he had asked in Parliament about the amount of money spent since April 2019 on clearing and managing the site. “The government ducked the question because the expenditure runs into a huge sum, running into high numbers in crores,” he said.
The Congress leader pointed out that the Chandigarh Administration and the Municipal Corporation had assured the National Green Tribunal (NGT) that the site would be cleared by December 25, 2024. This commitment was made in the Administrator’s Advisory Committee meeting in August 2024, he added.
Also Read | Union minister denies taking loan for Chandigarh’s 24×7 water project, MP Tewari calls it a ‘wrong’ answer
However, Tewari said, when the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Housing and Urban Affairs visited Chandigarh, the Municipal Corporation said the dump, including both legacy and concurrent waste, would be cleared by June 2025. He said in its latest response in Parliament, the government said it has extended the deadline to July 31, 2025, with a caveat that it is subject to weather conditions. “It is most unfortunate that timelines are arbitrarily shifted every couple of weeks,” Tewari said.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
In its reply, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs stated that under Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, Rs 28.50 crore had been approved as Central assistance for the remediation of the legacy waste dumpsite in Chandigarh. However, no separate allocation of funds had been made specifically for the Dadumajra dump, as funds for such projects are released under the mission’s Solid Waste Management (SWM) component.
The ministry informed Parliament that two of the three legacy waste dumps at Dadumajra had already been cleared. Bio-remediation of the third dump, which contained approximately 2.40 lakh metric tonnes (LMT) of waste as of January 2025, had now begun. The government reiterated that the entire dump site would be cleared by July 31, 2025, subject to weather conditions.
While hearing a PIL on the Dadumajra dump last month, the Punjab and Haryana High Court orally warned Chandigarh authorities that if they don’t clear the Dadumajra garbage dump by May this year, contempt proceedings would be initiated against them.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Addressing concerns about waste management, the ministry said sanitation is a state subject under the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution, making it the responsibility of the state and urban local bodies (ULBs) to plan, design, execute, and operate sanitation projects. It added that the central government provides policy directions, financial assistance, and technical support to states and ULBs.
To prevent the recurrence of such garbage dumps, the government said it had issued various advisories and guidelines on solid waste management, landfill reclamation, and disposal of legacy waste. It also provided model procurement documents to states to help expedite the bidding process for waste management projects.

headline: Guru Dutt found it easy to pen his love for Geeta Dutt, Einstein was raunchy; A V-Day play in Mumbai that seeks to explore love letters of iconic figures
description: Letters exchanged between legends like Guru Dutt and Geeta, Charlie Chaplin and his wife Paulette, poet-artist Khalil Gibran and educator Mary Haskell come to live with ‘Letters of Love’
content:
Did you know that Guru Dutt, regarded as one of the greatest filmmakers of Indian cinema and lauded for his depiction of melancholy, struggled to express his feelings to his wife, Geeta Dutt—one of Hindi cinema’s most celebrated playback singers? Instead, he resorted to writing letters, finding them a better medium of communication than speaking to her.
In contrast, comic actor and filmmaker Charlie Chaplin’s letters to his third wife, Paulette Goddard, made love look easy and playful—he compared her to coffee, something he cherished. Meanwhile, Russian poet Vladimir Mayakovsky, a prominent figure of the Russian Futurist movement, exchanged letters with author Lilya Brik, a married woman who neither wanted to leave her husband nor deny Mayakovsky’s love.
Letters exchanged between lovers are deeply personal—they can be intertwined with their work or exist separately, revealing complexities one might never imagine. After all, we often view these historical figures through a lens that makes them larger than life due to their contributions to politics, art, science, and other fields.
But their personal facets come alive on stage as Letters of Love — an initiative by Readings In The Shed, a one of a kind theatre centric initiative by Nikhil Katara and Himali Kothari that focuses on performative readings — returns for its seventh edition.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'

Scheduled for Valentine’s Day at NCPA’s Sunken Garden, the evening will present letters from six couples—poet-artist Khalil Gibran and educator Mary Haskell, naturalist Gerald Durrell and zoologist Lee McGeorge, poet-novelist Rainer Maria Rilke and expressionist painter Paula Modersohn-Becker, along with Chaplin and Goddard, Mayakovsky and Brik, and the Dutts.
Tying these love letters together is Cupid himself. But this time, he is no longer content being the matchmaker—he has fallen in love and is struggling with writer’s block as he attempts to pen his own love letter. A postman comes to his rescue, handing him copies of letters exchanged by great minds across different eras, hoping to inspire him. Playing Cupid is the director of the show, Nikhil Katara, who puts together this performance alongside writer-scriptwriter Himali Kothari, actors Kyla D’Souza and Ajinkya Ovhal, and students of Wilson College, where Katara teaches Theatre and Stagecraft.
“We have performed over 35 letters in the last seven years,” says Katara, who has always been drawn to spoken performances. In 2018, when he approached Kothari, they co-conceptualised Readings in the Shed. “Over time, we conducted extensive research and stumbled upon so many letters. At the Asiatic Library, there’s an entire section dedicated to letters—they reveal so much about a person beyond their public persona,” he adds.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
When asked about the most surprising discoveries over the years, Nikhil Katara and Himali Kothari picks the letters exchanged between Albert Einstein and his wife, Mileva Marić, which was performed in a previous edition. (Express Photo)
Kothari agrees, comparing letter writing to “digging your nose in the bathroom.” “You are certain of its secrecy. But globally, after years of their passing, family members or trusts entrusted with their belongings often decide to publish these letters, seeing them as part of their legacy. That’s how we got access to these intimate correspondences,” she explains. While they condense the letters to keep the performance engaging, she emphasises that the words are always read verbatim.
For the first time, they are performing a Hindi letter. “The letter was originally written in English, but since it was Guru Dutt’s, we decided to translate it, blending it with Geeta Dutt’s Waqt Ne Kiya Kya Haseen Sitam. The words and emotions, however, remain entirely his,” shares Katara.
When asked about the most surprising discoveries over the years, the duo picks the letters exchanged between Albert Einstein and his wife, Mileva Marić, which was performed in a previous edition. “They were raunchy—anyone reading them would turn red,” Katara shares with amusement, adding that such revelations offer a glimpse of Einstein beyond his towering reputation as a scientist known for the theory of relativity. “Warren Hastings and his wife even had pet names for each other’s genitalia,” he adds.
“When Marie Curie won her second Nobel Prize, one might expect a grand celebration. Instead, she was writing a letter asking someone to leave their marriage and children to be with her,” Katara notes, highlighting how deeply personal and unexpected these correspondences can be. At the same time, many letters reflect the public vision of their writers. “For instance, when we presented B.R. Ambedkar’s letters to his wife last year—our first Marathi letter—they carried both his personal affection and his unwavering vision for India. Similarly, Rabindranath Tagore’s letters to writer Victoria Ocampo, are filled with reflections on nationhood, and Jyotirao Phule’s letters to Savitribai reveal a blend of political and personal devotion.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“The biggest discovery was perhaps knowing how love can be intense and complex, but also sweet and playful. For me, Chaplin’s letters were a refreshing breath of fresh air, of being told that love can also be light,” adds D’souza, who brings all these letters to life with Ovhal.
Through Letters of Love, these intimate exchanges take on new life—giving not only performers but also the audience a rare chance to see the human side of the icons they revere.

headline: MSRTC bus driver fired for drink driving, crashing vehicle on Pune-Solapur Highway
description: After the accident, MSRTC authorities said no injuries were reported after the crash on the Pune-Solapur Highway.
content:
The Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) Wednesday terminated the services of a driver found intoxicated while driving a bus that met with an accident on the Pune-Solapur Highway.
The driver was driving a Lal Pari bus carrying 44 passengers when it crashed near Kalbhor Lawns in Kadam Wak Wasti on the Pune-Solapur Highway at around 12.30 am. Authorities said no injuries were reported after the crash.
Pramod Nehul, Puje Divisional Controller, MSRTC, said the driver and bus belong to the Dharavi Division and police are looking into the case. “We investigated and found no injuries except the minor damage worth Rs 5,000 to the bus bumper. The driver was drunk… We have suspended and terminated him,” he said.
Nehul said alcohol checks are conducted on drivers as a precautionary measure. “It might have happened between the routes. We are not aware of it. However, the investigation is launched and police are also overseeing the case,” he said.

In recent months, multiple accidents involving MSRTC buses have been reported. On January 27, an MSRTC bus travelling from Dahiwadi to Jyotiba fell off a bridge on the Pune-Bengaluru National Highway in the Sangli district, injuring 35 passengers and the driver.

headline: Traffic chaos on first day of expansion work on Navi Mumbai’s Kalamboli Circle
description: The restrictions were put in place due to the ongoing construction of a flyover and an underpass at Kalamboli Circle in Navi Mumbai.
content:
Severe traffic jams were reported at Kalamboli Circle in Navi Mumbai in the first two hours of the closure of the exit from the Pune-Mumbai Expressway, forcing authorities to reopen it temporarily.
The Navi Mumbai traffic police had announced the closure of the expressway exit through a notification, enforcing it Tuesday. The restrictions were put in place due to the ongoing construction of a flyover and an underpass at Kalamboli Circle by the Maharashtra State Infrastructure Development Corporation (MSIDC). Vehicles heading towards Panvel and JNPT were rerouted via the Sion-Panvel Highway and Taloja Link Road to reach Kalamboli Circle.
The exit, which was initially closed for six months from Tuesday, February 11, had to be reopened within two hours due to severe traffic congestion. However, the exit was shut again by Tuesday evening, leading to further confusion. The decision was also made considering the ongoing Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examination.
The police later stated that the exit would remain open for the next two to three days as the contractor had not yet deployed the required wardens for traffic management. However, the exit was shut again on Wednesday, raising concerns about the planning and execution of traffic arrangements.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
“The road was temporarily reopened for a few hours in the late morning due to heavy congestion at the junction. However, after reviewing the situation and implementing revised traffic measures, authorities decided to proceed with the original plan and keep the exit road closed,” said a senior Navi Mumbai police officer.
The repeated opening and closing of the exit highlighted inconsistencies in the implementation of traffic regulations, creating confusion among the commuters.
Kalamboli Circle connects multiple major roads and has witnessed increasing traffic. With the upcoming Navi Mumbai International Airport, the need for expansion was seen to handle future traffic volumes.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
However, delays due to uncoordinated planning by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI), CIDCO, and the Public Works Department have pushed the project timeline further. With only a few weeks left for the airport’s operations to begin, the expansion work is now being initiated, which could lead to traffic congestion for commuters.

headline: Mumbai man gets life term for killing wife over suspected affair
description: The court found Dinesh Parshuram More, who was aged 38 at the time of incident in February, 2020, guilty under section 302 (punishment for murder) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) on the basis of “direct and circumstantial evidence”.
content:
The sessions court in Mumbai sentenced to life imprisonment a man arrested in 2020 for killing his wife over a suspected extramarital affair at Kurar area in suburban Malad (West).
The court found Dinesh Parshuram More, who was aged 38 at the time of incident in February, 2020, guilty under section 302 (punishment for murder) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) on the basis of “direct and circumstantial evidence”.
Additional Sessions Judge Datta G Dhoble, in the February 10 verdict, which was made available on Wednesday, said that the case did not fall under “rarest of rare” category, therefore there was no need to award death penalty to the accused.
As per prosecution, More used to work in a security agency and his wife was employed as housemaid and the marital relationship between the two was allegedly strained due to frequent quarrels, as the accused husband suspected that she had an extramarital affair.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

British-Irish woman’s rape-murder in Goa: Behind the conviction that earned investigators a ‘thank you’
Man convicted of raping 7-month-old toddler in Kolkata gets death sentence
Five days prior to the incident, the deceased woman had lodged a domestic violence complaint at Kurar Police station against the accused, which further increased the tensions in the house.
As per FIR, during early hours of February 27, 2020, More killed his wife with a sharp weapon.
After perusing material on record, the judge held that the prosecution had “proved that the accused had committed murder of his wife in their house”, therefore he was guilty of the offence of murder.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
However, the judge noted the prosecution failed to prove that the weapon Koyta used in the crime was a prohibited weapon and therefore he was required to be acquitted under provisions of Arms Act.
The court said that the “offence, though heinous, does not indicate premeditated plan which shocks the collective conscience of the society,” and took place due to family discord.
The court added that the accused being sole earning member of the family, having minor unmarried daughters, be awarded with life imprisonment instead of death penalty.

headline: Chief Secy directs Health dept to keep Cabinet note on Ayushman Bharat ready
description: Sources also said that the Woman and Child Welfare Department has been directed to start working on implementing BJP's poll promise of giving Rs 2,500 per month to women from poor families.
content:
The Delhi Chief Secretary has directed the Health department to prepare a Cabinet note on the implementation of the Union government’s Ayushman Bharat Yojana in the Capital. The health insurance scheme has been implemented in all states except West Bengal and Delhi.
“The Health Department should prepare Cabinet note to implement Ayushman Bharat Yojana, which provides free treatment of a person up to Rs 5 lakh with an additional Rs 5 lakh cover from the state government,” reads the minutes of the meeting Chief Secretary Dharmendra held with all department heads on Monday.
The outgoing AAP government, which was in power in Delhi for 10 years, did not implement the scheme, maintaining that under its Delhi Arogya Kosh, free treatment is already being provided to the people of Delhi. The BJP, meanwhile, had highlighted that under Ayushman Bharat Yojana, those aged 70 or more — irrespective of their income — will be entitled to a cover of Rs 5 lakh annually to be shared within the family.
“All those schemes/programmes of the Central governments, which have not yet been implemented in Delhi, may be taken up for implementation. The departments may take urgent action on these schemes/programmes for taking requisite approval of the competent authority,” reads the minutes of the meeting.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
Delhi gets its fourth woman CM: All about Rekha Gupta
“The department had prepared documents and the file (on implementation of Ayushman Bharat Yojana) was sent to the previous CM and Health minister for approval but they never replied to it,” a source said, adding that work on preparing the Cabinet note has started and as soon as the government is sworn in, it will be sent to the minister concerned for approval.
Sources also said that the Woman and Child Welfare Department has been directed to start working on implementing BJP’s poll promise of giving Rs 2,500 per month to women from poor families.
The Chief Secretary, meanwhile, also instructed all departments to prepare a 100-day action plan to implement ‘Viksit Delhi’ and submit the same by Thursday.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“The action plan should focus on targets to be completed within 15 days, monthwise and 100 days. The departments should submit the action plan to the General Administration Department (GAD) by Thursday positively. If any project/scheme needs to be placed before the Council of Ministers, the department should start preparing the draft Cabinet note,” reads the minutes of the meeting. The GAD will compile the action plan for 100 days and keep it ready for presentation before the new BJP government, officials said.
Moreover, to tackle waterlogging in the monsoon season, all concerned departments were directed to take steps for desilting and cleaning of drains. The DJB was asked to take measures to prevent overflow of sewage.

headline: Tata Power ranked among top 10 in Smart Grid Index 2024
description: “In the evaluation process, Tata Power-DDL achieved an impressive score of 83.9%...Tata Power through is discoms in Delhi, Odisha, Ajmer and Mumbai is serving 12.5 million consumers (over 5 crore),” it added.
content:
Tata Power Delhi Distribution Limited (Tata Power-DDL), which supplies electricity to the north and northwest parts of the Capital, has been ranked among the top 10 power utilities globally in the Smart Grid Index 2024.
“The 2024 Smart Grid exercise evaluated 92 utilities across 36 countries or markets recognising global best practices in Smart Grid Deployment. The recognition reflects the company’s commitment to driving the future of India’s power distribution sector,” read an official statement issued by the power company.
“In the evaluation process, Tata Power-DDL achieved an impressive score of 83.9%…Tata Power through is discoms in Delhi, Odisha, Ajmer and Mumbai is serving 12.5 million consumers (over 5 crore),” it added.
The Smart Grid Index (SGI), developed by Singapore Power Group (SP Group), defines itself as a “simple and quantifiable framework that evaluates
the smartness” of power grids globally.

headline: Nearly 2 crore take holy dip on Maha Kumbh Maghi Purnima
description: CM monitors arrangements; real-time data on vehicles collected from toll plazas
content:
THE FOURTH significant ritual bath, ‘Magh Purnima Snan’, during the Maha Kumbh Mela in Prayagraj on Wednesday also witnessed a massive gathering of devotees for holy dip. According to the state government, the footfall on Wednesday stood at 1.95 crore until 8 pm and the total till date as more than 48.29 crore.
As the devotees had started reaching the Maha Kumbh area late Tuesday evening, the Mela administration reinforced the ghats and managed water levels in the rivers to facilitate hassle-free bathing.
Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was also seen in pictures shared by the government,  personally monitoring the Maha Kumbh Mela from his residence at 4 am, along with Director General of Police Prashant Kumar and Principal Secretary (Home) Sanjay Prasad.
Additional Fair Officer, Vivek Chaturvedi, informed that the turnout for the sacred bath was “unexpectedly high”, with devotees continuously arriving for the ritual. Given the massive crowd, riverbanks had been strengthened and water level management had been ensured. The police had also set up barricades and watchtowers and changing rooms had been reinforced, added officials.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
In anticipation of the massive influx, Variable Messaging Displays (VMDs) were activated across the fairgrounds, providing real-time guidance and instructions to pilgrims.
The auspicious period for Magh Purnima began at 6:55 pm on Tuesday and continued till 7:22 pm on Wednesday.
Officials said real time data is being collected from toll plazas and officials of neighbouring districts so that the number of vehicles coming and the routes can be monitored and regulated.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
DGP Prashant Kumar pointed out that Wednesday saw the fifth snan of the Maha Kumbh Mela, with the coming Maha Shivratri snan being the final one.
Taking lessons from the stampede on January 29 (Mauni Amavasya), the approach of ‘Build Back Better’ was adopted to ensure even more efficient management, officials said. Community feedback from officials and devotees present at the site was incorporated to enhance arrangements, leading to the safe and smooth participation of approximately 46 to 47 crore pilgrims in the Maha Kumbh so far. By 2 pm on Wednesday, around 1.83 crore devotees had taken a dip at Sangam, he said.
Kumar added that apart from Prayagraj, special attention is also being given to Chitrakoot, Mirzapur Vindhyachal Temple, Varanasi Kashi Vishwanath and Ayodhya Ram Mandir, as a number of pilgrims visiting Maha Kumbh extend their journey to these sites. The Maha Kumbh Mela area is being continuously monitored live from Lucknow and necessary instructions are being given via IIIC (Integrated Intelligence & Information Centre).
Lakhs of people are arriving from across the country and abroad. Initially, most pilgrims travelled by trains and buses, but since February 3, there has been a sharp rise in visitors using private vehicles, Kumar said. On major snan days, around 5 lakh people travelled by train, for which over 400 trains were arranged, while on regular days, approximately 3.5 lakh people commute daily, serviced by 350 trains, the DGP added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Additionally, thousands of four-wheelers enter the city daily, making their smooth entry and exit a major challenge in crowd management. To handle this efficiently, contingency planning was also implemented.
Even on Mauni Amavasya, immediate action was taken in response to the stampede. Instances where officers carried elderly and differently abled women on their shoulders to ensure their safety have been widely covered in the media, Kumar said.
To counter misleading information on social media, a fact-checking account has been actively debunking false claims and urging people not to spread misinformation. Some individuals have been attempting to tarnish the image of Maha Kumbh by sharing unrelated incidents from other states and even foreign countries as if they occurred here. Legal action is being taken against such social media accounts, and those operating them are being identified for strict action. — with ptI inputs

headline: Former President Pranab Mukherjee’s son back in Congress: ‘Soon after joined TMC, I realised I did wrong’
description: Abhijit Mukherjee had left the Congress for the TMC in 2021.
content:
Former President Pranab Mukherjee’s son Abhijit Mukherjee rejoined the Congress on Wednesday after a four-year-long placid stint in the Trinamool Congress.
The former Lok Sabha MP was given the Congress membership at the party’s state headquarters here in the presence of AICC general secretary and West Bengal in-charge Ghulam Ahmed Mir.
Regretting his decision to have joined the TMC in 2021, Mukherjee said, “I apologise for this; it was not right for me to leave the Congress.”
“The nephew of Mamata Banerjee (Abhishek Banerjee) called me and I joined TMC. But soon after I joined, I realised I did wrong… This is my second birthday in the Congress and politics,” Mukherjee told reporters after being handed over the party flag by the national and state leadership.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Claiming that there is no alternative to the grand old party in the country’s politics, he said, “Only the Congress takes along all people irrespective of their caste, creed and religion.” Mukherjee said that he had expressed his desire to rejoin the Congress in June last year, but owing to different state elections, it could take place now.
He returned to the Congress four years after switching over to the Trinamool Congress in July 2021.
Mukherjee had not been seen in a much active role during his stint in the TMC.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Maintaining that Mukherjee has come back to the “right party,” Mir said that his joining will help the Congress in its efforts to strengthen the party’s base in West Bengal.
“There are two types of ideologies working in the political arena at present in the country – on one side are the divisive forces and on the other the secular forces who take everyone together,” said Mir, an MLA of Jammu and Kashmir.
He claimed that the Congress was working together with all sections of the society.
“While one force is trying to change the Constitution, the Congress is working for the welfare of all within the scope of the Constitution,” Mir said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Stating that several political parties in different parts of the country want to tread the path of secularism, “but some are indirectly playing into the hands of others.”
Mukherjee had won a bye-election to the Jangipur Lok Sabha constituency in 2012 on a Congress ticket after his illustrious father, who had helmed several key positions in the Union government as a Congress leader, was elected the President of India.
Mukherjee had also won the 2014 parliamentary elections from the same constituency as a Congress candidate.
He had lost in the 2019 Lok Sabha polls from Jangipur securing the third position after the candidates of the TMC and the BJP.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He joined the Congress party as a political novice in 2011 and won the 2011 assembly polls as its candidate from the Nalhati segment. Prior to joining politics in 2011, Mukherjee worked as a corporate executive both in the private and public sectors.

headline: Jamia Millia Islamia student stabbed during argument, 1 held
description: The Delhi Police said the victim is out of danger, and teams have been formed to nab the absconding accused.
content:
A 24-year-old student from Jamia Millia Islamia was stabbed on Monday following a fight with two youths at New Friends Colony in South East Delhi, police said on Wednesday.
The police identified the injured as Zeshan, who hails from Jammu and Kashmir (J&K). Both the alleged attackers — Tajamul Islam (22) and his friend Lukman (23) — also hail from J&K and study at a private university in Noida, said police.
They live in rented accommodation in East of Kailash.
While Tajamul, a native of Srinagar, was arrested on Monday, Lukman escaped, police said, adding that a knife used in the crime has been recovered.
Zeshan and his friend Safdar Rashid Rathar, also a student of Jamia Millia Islamia, were standing at a parking lot when Lukman and Tajamul allegedly passed remarks about them.

headline: JSW, Baldota, Tata, Mahindra among top investors at Invest Karnataka 2025
description: While JSW Neo Energy pledged Rs 56,000 crore for solar and wind energy projects as well as other initiatives, Baldota Steel & Power followed with an announcement of Rs 54,000 crore at Invest Karnataka 2025.
content:
Leading global and domestic firms committed to large-scale projects at the Global Investors’ Meet: Invest Karnataka 2025 with a significant influx of investments across renewable energy, manufacturing, semiconductors, R&D, and infrastructure that promised to transform the state’s industrial landscape.
The top 20 investments came from JSW Neo Energy, Baldota Steel and Power Limited, Tata Power Renewable Energy, Mahindra Susten, and Epsilon Group among others.
Among the biggest announcements, JSW Neo Energy Ltd pledged Rs 56,000 crore for solar and wind energy projects, battery storage, blade manufacturing, and a wind turbine generator plant, making it the highest investment among the top 20. Steel magnate Sajjan Jindal announced that the Jindal Group will invest over Rs 1 lakh crore in Karnataka in the coming years. Of this, Rs 45,000 crore will go into steel production, while Rs 56,000 crore will be channelled into hospitality, solar energy, green hydrogen and other eco-friendly ventures, he said.
Baldota Steel & Power Ltd followed with an investment of Rs 54,000 crore for an integrated steel plant, while Tata Power Renewable Energy Ltd and ReNew Pvt Ltd committed Rs 50,000 crore each for renewable energy projects. Other major investments in the sector included Rs 43,975 crore from Serentica Renewables India Pvt Ltd and Rs 35,000 crore from Mahindra Susten Pvt Ltd.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Also Read | Karnataka’s new industrial policy eyes investments of Rs 7.5 lakh crore and 20 lakh jobs in 5 years
Anand Mahindra, chairman of the Mahindra Group said the investment “will be allocated to renewable energy, with plans to develop over 5 gigawatts of solar and hybrid projects. This initiative is expected to generate 6,000 to 8,000 new jobs, making Karnataka a key hub for clean energy solutions.”
The company also plans to expand its Mahindra Holidays segment, with additional investments of Rs 1,000 crore in new resorts across locations like Gokarna and Hampi. The group is currently in talks with the state government regarding land aggregation and has requested industry status for tourism and single-window clearance to facilitate faster approvals.
Mahindra Defence Services and Mahindra Aerospace are exploring strategic expansion opportunities in Karnataka, with several hundred crores earmarked for investment.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Other investments in tech, infra, mobility
Hero Future Energies announced Rs 22,200 crore for renewable energy and green hydrogen projects, while Suzlon Energy Ltd committed Rs 21,950 crore for wind power initiatives.
Semiconductor manufacturing saw a boost with Lam Research signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Board (KIADB) for an investment of Rs 10,000 crore. TVS Motor Company pledged Rs 2,000 crore for a cutting-edge R&D facility, aiming to develop smarter and greener vehicles, while Honda committed Rs 600 crore for electric vehicle manufacturing, bolstering Karnataka’s vision of becoming a centre for sustainable mobility solutions.
Beyond renewable energy and industrial manufacturing, several global corporations announced significant R&D and infrastructure investments. Schneider Electric will invest Rs 2,247 crore in manufacturing and related R&D activities, Hitachi Energy has committed Rs 1,000 crore, and Bosch has pledged Rs 450 crore. Havells is expanding its manufacturing footprint in Tumkur with a Rs 710 crore investment, while UltraTech Cement and Dalmia Cement have announced Rs 4,500 crore and Rs 3,000 crore investments, respectively, in cement production.
The summit also strongly emphasised Karnataka’s knowledge economy, with the KWIN City initiative drawing interest from nine universities, including St John’s University of New York, which plans to establish a campus in the state. ESR Advisers is set to develop industrial parks and data centres with a Rs 2,500 crore investment, while Sotefin Bharat will introduce fully automated robotic multilevel car and bus parking systems with an investment of Rs 8,500 crore.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
CM launches Single Window System
Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on Tuesday launched Karnataka’s revamped Single Window System to improve ease of doing business in the state. He said the new system will simplify approvals, reduce compliance burdens, and fast-track industrial investments while ensuring transparency and efficiency. The system integrates over 150 business services across 30 state departments.
It will provide real-time status updates, allowing investors to track approvals, amendments, and renewals without delays. “The initiative is particularly beneficial for the manufacturing sector as it introduces an Affidavit-Based Clearance (ABC) mechanism through Karnataka Udyog Mitra. This will enable investors to begin construction and preparatory activities without waiting for multiple approvals,” Siddaramaiah added.
“The revamped Single Window System is integrated with the National Single Window System, allowing investors to access central-level services seamlessly. It also incorporates several KIADB services, such as land search, selection, allotment, and building plan approvals. These services are now available through a single portal,” the chief minister stated, adding that with this “Karnataka aims to further strengthen its position as one of India’s top investment destinations.”

A GIS-based Industrial Information System has also been introduced. It will help investors check compliance with site-related regulations before proceeding with their projects. A wizard-based discovery tool will assist investors in identifying the required state and central approvals, no-objection certificates (NOCs), and clearances at different stages of the project. Further, an Incentive Wizard & Calculator allows investors to check their eligibility for various incentives, concessions, and rebates.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
An AI-powered multi-lingual chatbot will provide instant responses to investor queries on policies, incentives, approvals, and compliance requirements. Chief minister said this move is aimed at enhancing investor convenience. The system also focuses on improving the overall investor experience. It simplifies forms, eliminates duplicate information, and integrates with over 40 other systems. It also provides real-time status visibility with event-based alerts and triggers.
To ensure ease in incentive claims and disbursement, the system enables investors to apply for and track their claims online. This will reduce paperwork and improve transparency. A dashboard-based system allows government stakeholders to monitor application status and implement threshold-based escalations for timely service delivery, Siddaramaiah explained.
The system is available in multiple languages and is designed to be mobile-friendly. It also includes an online grievance redressal mechanism for quick resolutions.

headline: Gujarat HC calls CRPF denying promotion to HIV+ staffer a ‘clear case of discrimination’
description: A division bench of Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal and Justice Pranav Trivedi made the observation while hearing a plea filed by the woman staffer of the CRPF who said she was being denied promotion despite meeting other eligibility criteria because she was suffering from HIV-AIDS.
content:
The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) denying a female staffer promotion to a higher post because she was infected with HIV-AIDS was a clear instance of discrimination, the Gujarat High Court noted on Wednesday.
A division bench of Chief Justice Sunita Agarwal and Justice Pranav Trivedi made the observation while hearing a plea filed by the woman staffer of the CRPF who said she was being denied promotion despite meeting other eligibility criteria because she was suffering from HIV-AIDS.
The court directed that the matter be brought to the notice of in-charge Additional Solicitor General of India and sought the law officer’s appearance before it on the next date of hearing on March 6. The counsel appearing for the respondents — the Union of India, CRPF and Commandant, CRPF — contended that a standing order was passed pursuant to the rule which stipulates that a candidate has to be in “shape one” for the purpose of promotion.
“This case highlights clear instances of discrimination in the Central Reserve Police Force for the incumbents who are suffering from the disease known as HIV-AIDS,” the HC said in its order.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
The counsel for the petitioner contended the woman has been denied promotion consistently despite being fit for elevation on all other aspects of eligibility except the fact that she is suffering from the infectious disease which is progressing. The petitioner challenged the validity of the Standing Order Number 4/2008 as well as Rule 5 of the CRPF Assistant Commandant (Ministerial), Recruitment Rules 2011, on the ground the same is contradictory to the provisions of HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017 and the National HIV Counselling and Testing Guidelines 2024.
They were also violative of Articles 14, 16 and 21 of the Constitution as the petitioner was being denied promotion to a higher ministerial post only on the basis of a decision of the medical board dated February 3, 2024, reporting the petitioner was suffering from higher grade of the disease, the court noted in its order.

headline: First GBS death in Mumbai: 53-year-old man succumbs to symptoms; BMC yet to confirm link to Pune cases
description: Speaking to The Indian Express, a senior BMC official said cases of GBS are recorded throughout the year and that, unless a direct link to the Pune outbreak is established, there is no cause for alarm.
content:
A 53-year-old man from Mumbai has succumbed to Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS), marking the city’s first fatality from the rare neurological disorder.
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) was yet to confirm whether this case is linked to the ongoing GBS outbreak in Pune.
BMC commissioner Bhushan Gagrani confirmed to PTI that it is the first death in the metropolis due to the GBS.
The patient, an employee of BMC’s V N Desai Hospital, had been on ventilator support at the civic-run Nair Hospital before succumbing to complications from the illness.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

British-Irish woman’s rape-murder in Goa: Behind the conviction that earned investigators a ‘thank you’
Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
According to the man’s family, he had travelled to Pune for a day last month before falling ill.
He was admitted to the hospital on January 23 after experiencing fever.
Following extensive medical tests, including cerebrospinal fluid analysis, doctors diagnosed him with GBS. Due to the severity of his condition, he was placed in the hospital’s intensive care unit (ICU) but succumbed to the illness on February 10 night, according to municipal authorities.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“We are investigating the matter to determine if there is any connection between this case and the outbreak in Pune,” said a senior BMC official.
In addition to this case, a 16-year-old girl diagnosed with GBS has been admitted to Nair Hospital. Her condition is stable, and she continues to receive treatment. The girl, a Class 10 student from Palghar district, was brought to Mumbai for medical care. Meanwhile, a 64-year-old woman from Andheri (West), was also diagnosed with GBS and admitted to the BMC-run Seven Hills Hospital on February 5.
GBS is a rare but serious autoimmune condition in which the body’s immune system mistakenly attacks the peripheral nerves, leading to muscle weakness, paralysis and, in severe cases, respiratory failure.
While its exact cause is unknown, it is often triggered by infections such as influenza, gastrointestinal bacteria like Campylobacter jejuni, or, in some cases, vaccinations. The disease can progress rapidly, requiring intensive medical intervention, including mechanical ventilation if respiratory muscles are affected.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Speaking to The Indian Express, a senior BMC official emphasised that cases of GBS are recorded throughout the year and there is no immediate cause for alarm.
“GBS occurs sporadically, and unless we identify a clear connection between this case and Pune, it does not hold epidemiological significance,” the official said.
8th death in Pune
A 59-year-old man from Khadakwasla succumbed to Guillain Barre Syndrome. This is the eighth death reported by Pune health authorities with the case count now crossing the 200 mark.
On Wednesday, a total of 203 suspected GBS cases were reported in Pune. Of these patients 109 have been discharged till now, 52 are in ICU and 20 are on ventilator support.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In the latest suspected death due to GBS, the man was admitted to Kashibai  Navale Medical College and general hospital late on February 10 after he showed symptoms like weakness.
According to Pune district health authorities a nerve conduction velocity indicated acute motor axonal neuropathy, which signifies damage to nerves related to motor function. Plasmapheresis was initiated as part of the treatment for GBS. However, early on February 11 he suffered a sudden cardiac arrest and succumbed to complications.
With inputs from ENS, Pune

headline: Taiwanese giant Foxconn bags Investment Titan Award at Karnataka Global Investors Meet
description: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal presented the award at Invest Karnataka 2025, the Global Investors Meet, in Bengaluru.
content:
Taiwanese electronics manufacturer Foxconn won the Investment Titan Award for the highest one-time investment in the last 10 years at Invest Karnataka 2025, the Global Investors Meet, on Wednesday. In August 2024, Foxconn infused around Rs 1,200 crore into its Karnataka unit and announced an investment of Rs 25,000 crore to establish the company’s second-largest plant in the world.
This and a few other awards were presented by Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal.
The Investor of the Decade Award went to JSW Group for being the largest investment generator in the last 10 years. The Industrial Legacy Award was given posthumously to Vikram Kirloskar. The award, according to the industries department, honoured “an individual creating a legacy and is a champion of industrial excellence and innovation in Karnataka”. The Samsung Research and Development Institute in Bengaluru bagged the Innovation Excellence Award for the highest number of India patents filed from Karnataka.
The Diversity Leadership Excellence Award for the highest number of women in the workforce went to Shahi Exports Private Ltd, the Ecosystem Enabler Award for the largest number of manufacturing clusters in tier-2/3 regions went to the firm Aequs and the Pioneer in Karnataka’s R&D Ecosystem Award for setting up the first global research and development centre in Karnataka went to Texas Instruments.

The Sunrise Sector Pioneer Awards in the auto and electronic vehicle, biotech and life sciences, aerospace and defence, and aerospace and defence-public sectors were bagged by Toyota Kirloskar, Biocon, RTX and Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd, respectively.

Investments

Delivering a talk on Make in India for the World, Chaitanya Sarawate, President & CEO, GE Healthcare South Asia and MD, Wipro GE Healthcare, said this investment continues the Rs 32,000 crore invested in the state over the last two decades. The company has four manufacturing plants.
Among other investment announcements made was a 3,000-MW wind energy project in Vijayapura district, the home district of Industries Minister M B Patil. headline: ‘Need time to go through voluminous documents’: Ex-R G Kar principal Sandip Ghosh’s counsel tells court in CBI graft case

content:

headline: From F-16 to Airbus: the foreign fighter jets and other aircraft participating in Aero India 2025
description: Aircraft from Sweden, Germany and Brazil, besides those from the US and Russia, are participating in the Aero India 2025 show in Bengaluru.
content:
Aero India 2025 in Bengaluru has witnessed several firsts. While US and Russian aircraft are displaying their skills on the same platform for the first time, there are many other fighter jets that are drawing the attention of aviation enthusiasts. Aircraft from Sweden, Germany, and Brazil, besides those from the US and Russia, are being displayed at the biennial show.
Here is a list of aircraft from abroad participating in Aero India 2025.
F-16
The F-16 Fighting Falcon is a multi-role fighter developed by Lockheed Martin for the US air force. It is known for its agility, speed, and advanced avionics.
This is one of the most widely exported fighter jet with more than 25 countries. It has the abilities to carry air-to-air and air-to-ground missiles, bombs, and a 20mm cannon. It was part of several operations including the Gulf War and Afghanistan invasion. The US also supplied F -16s to Ukraine to strengthen its air defence.
F-35

‘Great friend of India’: PM Modi meets former UK PM Rishi Sunak
This fifth-generation fighter is considered to be the backbone of the US air force. Developed by Lockheed Martin, it is known for its air superiority, ground attack, intelligence, and electronic warfare. It is one of the most advanced fighter jets in the world.
Artificial intelligence-assisted targeting and network centric warfare capabilities have made the F-35 stand out from other aircraft. The software and hardware upgrades of this aircraft including AI-powered combat systems have been a game changer.
For the first time in Aero India 2025, the F-35 hit the skies displaying its manoeuvring skills.
Sukhoi 57E
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Sukhoi 57E is a fifth-generation stealth fighter developed by Russian Sukhoi. It is considered to be the rival of the F-22 Raptor and the F-35 Lightning II of the US.
Known for its speed and range, the Su 57E has a range over 3,500 km. With AI-assisted combat systems, sensor fusion, and electronic warfare capabilities, Russia is aiming to produce more such aircraft. It has also shown interest in exporting these products to India and China.
The Su 57E stands out as a statement of Russian modernisation of defence products. (Express Photo)
The Su 57E stands out as a statement of Russian modernisation of defence products. The Su 57E has also played limited roles in the recent Russia-Ukraine wars. The Su 57E may see unmanned versions in the days to come.
For the first time, the Su 57E participated in Aero India displaying its capabilities. The aircraft is codenamed “Felon” by Nato.
Embraer C-390 Millennium
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Embraer C-390 Millennium is a modern, multi-mission military transport aircraft developed by Embraer Defense & Security in Brazil. Designed to replace older turboprop transporters like the C-130 Hercules, it offers higher speed, greater payload capacity, and advanced avionics.
The Embraer C-390 Millennium is often compared with theC-130J Super Hercules of Lockheed Martin. (Express Photo)
The Embraer C-390 Millennium is often compared with theC-130J Super Hercules of Lockheed Martin. It has a range of Rs 8,500 km and is used for troop and cargo transport, air-to-air refuelling, medical evacuation, and humanitarian missions.
It is operated by the Brazilian air force and has orders from Portugal, Hungary and Netherlands.
JAS 39 Gripen
Handsome when stationed but devastating in its action, the Saab JAS 39 Gripen is a fourth-generation multi-role fighter developed by Sweden’s Saab Group.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
With a speed of 2,400 km per hour and range of 3,200 km, it has the ability to take off and land on short runways and highways. It is considered to be the competitor of the Rafale, F-16 and Eurofighter Typhoon in global defence markets. Designed for air superiority, ground attack, and reconnaissance, it is known for its agility, advanced avionics, and cost-effectiveness.
Gripen has been displayed at Aero India 2025, where the public can taste the experience of its cockpit but only on invitation. (Express Photo)
It is presently used by the Swedish air force and exported to countries like Brazil, Hungary, Czech Republic, Thailand, and South Africa.
Gripen has been displayed at Aero India 2025, where the public can taste the experience of its cockpit but only on invitation.
Airbus A330 MRTT
Known as “critical force multiplier”, the Airbus A330 MRTT (multi-role tanker transport) is a strategic air-to-air refuelling and transport aircraft developed by Airbus Defence and Space.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Based on the Airbus A330 commercial aircraft, it provides extended-range refuelling capabilities and strategic airlift for military operations. (Express Photo)
The fuel capacity of this aircraft is a whopping 1.1 lakh kg and can carry troops, tankers, and massive materials. It is also used by over 15 air forces, including those of the UK, Australia, Germany and France. It can act as a supporter for fighter jets and bombers due to its vast operational ability. Based on the Airbus A330 commercial aircraft, it provides extended-range refuelling capabilities and strategic airlift for military operations. It can also be used in humanitarian aid and medical evacuations.
Airbus A 440 M
The largest aircraft stationed at Aero India 2025 is Airbus A400M Atlas, a tactical and strategic military transport aircraft operated by the German air force (Luftwaffe). With a payload capacity of 37 tonnes, the A 400 M is faster than the traditional transport aircraft. It is used for troop deployment, equipment transport, and disaster relief. It has been used for Afghanistan, Mali and Ukraine operations. It can carry even helicopters and armoured vehicles including tankers and even land and take off from unprepared runways.

headline: At Khanauri, farmer leader Jagjit Singh Dallewal raises US deportations: ‘Agriculture not profitable…youth have no choice’
description: The deportation of Indians from the US was a sign of the growing unemployment in the country, Punjab farmer leader Jagjit Singh Dallewal said at the Khanauri Kisan Mahapanchayat.
content:
The deportation of 104 Indians from the United States was the main topic of discussion at the Kisan Mahapanchayat held at the Khanauri border on Wednesday to mark one year of the farmers’ protests, with Punjab farmer leader Jagjit Singh Dallewal saying that it was a sign of the growing unemployment in the country.
“In the last week, America deported 104 Indians and the flight landed at Amritsar. Out of these, 30 were from Punjab and 33 from Haryana. Now, America is ready to deport more Indians. People are criticising the people who went to the US in this way (through the ‘dunki’ route). But the big question is, why did they have to go like this?” Dallewal asked, addressing farmers, lying on his trolley.
Dallewal has been on a fast-unto-death on the Khanauri border since November last year over several long-pending demands by farmers, including a legal guarantee for minimum support price (MSP).
“Employment opportunities are not enough in our country and hence youngsters have to go outside…the agriculture sector is not strengthened…agriculture is not a profitable venture anymore. So youngsters have no choice but to go abroad. Hence, it is high time that the state and Centre wake up to this reality,” Dallewal said.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
“If the country’s agriculture sector is strengthened, the country will progress. That is why we are struggling to seek MSP as a legal guarantee and want the Swaminathan Commission report to be implemented to determine the rate of crops. Farmers, labourers and even people from other sectors must understand that this fight is not just to get MSP legal guarantee law implemented but it is also indirectly linked to solving the unemployment rate of the country,” he added.
Farmer union leaders Abhimanyu Kohar, Kaka Singh Kotra, Sukhjit Singh Hardojhande, Surjit Singh Phul and many others addressed the gathering at Khanauri.
On Thursday, another Mahapanchayat will be held at the Shambhu border. On Friday, farmers from Kisan Mazdoor Morcha (KMM) and Samyukta Kisan Morcha (SKM, non-political) will be going to Chandigarh for talks with a delegation of Union ministers.
Farmer union leader suffers heart attack
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Farmer union leader Baldev Singh Sirsa, the president of Lok Bhalai Insaf Welfare Society, suffered a heart attack at the Khanauri border amid the Kisan Mahapanchayat proceedings. He was rushed to Rajindra Medical College and Hospital, Patiala, where he is now receiving treatment.
“He was feeling uneasy due to which he was rushed to hospital,” Surjeet Singh Phul, a member of Bharatiya Kisan Union Krantikari, said.
The National Investigation Agency (NIA) had summoned Sirsa in January 2021 in connection with a case lodged against Sikh separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun.
Farmer dies in an accident
Farmer Charanjit Singh Kala Badwala, a resident of Barwala village in Punjab’s Fatehgarh Sahib district, died on Tuesday following an accident. Badwala, who was in his late 40s, was associated with the Bharatiya Kisan Union Ekta Sidhupur, the union said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
On Monday, Badwala was on his way back from PGI Chandigarh, where he had gone to collect medicine for his kidney infection when he met with an accident. He was rushed to the Government Hospital in Chandigarh’s Sector 16 and later referred to PGI Chandigarh. He passed away at the hospital, the union said.

headline: ‘Are you sure plastic flowers are biodegradable or can be recycled?’: Bombay HC asks Centre
description: The Bombay High Court also pointed to existing rules which provide for banning the production and sale of single-use plastic items less than 100 microns in thickness.
content:
The Bombay High Court Wednesday questioned the Centre’s decision to exclude plastic flowers from the list of banned single-use plastic items while hearing a writ plea seeking a ban on the use of artificial flowers used for decoration or gifts.
The plea by the Growers Flowers Council of India (GFCI) raised concerns over the use of plastic flowers with a thickness of less than 100 microns. GFCI referred to a report of the International Association of Packaging Research Institutes (IAPRI) which stated that the maximum thickness of plastic flowers is usually 30 microns and the minimum and average thickness is 29 microns, which is less than 100 microns. The Council claimed in its plea that the Maharashtra Government banned several single-use plastic items through a March 2022 notification.
The bench of Chief Justice Alok Aradhe and Justice Bharati H Dangre orally questioned the Centre’s lawyer, “Are you sure that plastic flowers, which are so flimsy, are biodegradable or can be recycled?”
The bench also questioned that while the existing rules provide for banning the production and sale of single-use plastic items less than 100 microns in thickness, plastic flowers, which are used for decoration and are 30-micron, are not yet included in the list of prohibited items.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
The lawyer representing the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB), however, submitted that it has recovered Rs. 17 lakh fine for the use of such plastic flowers.
The court directed the petitioner to file a rejoinder affidavit to the Centre’s stand that the usage of plastic flowers was not prohibited by the next hearing after two weeks.
In July last year, the High Court noted that “there does not appear to be any impediment in prohibiting use and sale of plastic flowers of thickness less than 100 microns” and sought responses from the Centre and state government on the plea. The court asked authorities to take up the matter with “serious earnestness” in regard to the “impact of the use of plastic flowers of less than 100 microns thickness on the ecosystem and environment”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In response, the Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) filed an affidavit, stating plastic flowers are not included in the banned single-use plastic items’ list as they did not come under criteria of “high littering potential and low utility”. The Union ministry stated that the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) had forwarded the issue for its consideration but there was no supporting analysis for the same.
The Centre stated that an expert committee constituted by the Department of Chemicals and Petrochemicals (DCPC) had identified 40 single-use plastic items for detailed analysis. Plastic flowers were not part of the same. It also added that the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016, did not mention a requirement of a minimum thickness of 100 microns for plastic flowers.

headline: Bandra man kills senior citizen, visits crime scene to stay off police’s radar, but CCTV derails his plans
description: Residents of her building in Bandra Reclamation alerted authorities after noticing a persistent foul odor.
content:
A 64-year-old woman was found murdered in her Bandra flat on Tuesday. Within two hours of registering a case, police arrested a man from her neighborhood, identifying robbery as the likely motive, as valuables were reported missing.
The deceased, Rekha Ashok Khonde, lived alone, while her daughter, Shrishti, resided in Malad. Residents of her building in Bandra Reclamation alerted authorities after noticing a persistent foul odor. Initially mistaking it for a dead cat, they soon realised the smell was strongest near Khonde’s flat. Concerned, they contacted her daughter, who arrived and discovered her mother’s decomposing body on the bed.
Khonde’s hands were tied with a dupatta, and had severe wounds on her head and throat. Police believe the killer used both a blunt metal object and a sharp weapon in the attack. A post-mortem at Bhabha Hospital confirmed she had been murdered on February 5.
Following the crime’s discovery, Zonal DCP Dikshit Gedam formed multiple teams to investigate. Bandra police, led by Senior Inspector Sanjay Marathe, analysed CCTV footage and technical evidence, leading to the arrest of Sharif Ali Shaikh, a neighbor known to the victim.

Preliminary inquiries revealed that Khonde’s late husband, a Maharashtra State Electricity Board employee, had passed away in 2017. She was receiving family pension and trusted Shaikh, who worked for a private company, with assisting her in her errands, medical visits, and banking tasks.
“Khonde wanted her daughter Shrishti, 25 to marry Shaikh, but she was unwilling. Because of this, the mother-son were not talking to each other for a long time and Shaikh was playing mediator between the two,” said a police officer.
However, tensions arose between Khonde and her daughter due to Shaikh’s involvement in their lives.
Police sources indicate that Shaikh had secretly withdrawn Rs 23 lakh from Khonde’s bank account, which she had recently discovered. Fearing she would inform her daughter, Shaikh allegedly killed her.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The daughter of the deceased has said that jewelry worth around Rs 15 lakh had gone missing, prompting police to suspect that the killer came to rob ornaments from the house.
In a bid to mislead investigators, Shaikh remained in the area, pretending to be shocked by Khonde’s death as well. He even called her phone multiple times after the murder and later informed Shrishti that her mother was not answering calls.
However, police grew suspicious since he was among the few people who regularly visited her house. A crucial breakthrough came when CCTV footage captured him entering and exiting Khonde’s building on February 5. Upon interrogation, he confessed to the crime.
Shaikh was produced before the Bandra court and remanded to police custody until February 17.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“The accused was produced in Bandra court and was remanded to police custody up to February 17. We are further investigating the case and collecting strong evidence,” said senior inspector Sanjay Marathe of Bandra police station.

headline: Maha kumbh 2025: IndiGo to launch direct flight from Pune to Prayagraj from Feb 16
description: According to sources, these flights will commence operations from February 16 and may continue until the Mahakumbh concludes. While IndiGo has not officially disclosed the fares, online ticket booking platforms indicate prices starting at over Rs 20,000.
content:
With the Maha Kumbh Mela drawing pilgrims from Pune and increasing travel demand, IndiGo has announced a direct flight from Pune to Prayagraj, starting February 16.
The flight will operate six days a week—Monday to Friday and Sunday—while remaining non-operational on Saturdays. Flight 6E 2062 will depart from Prayagraj at 11:10 AM and arrive in Pune at 1:10 PM. In the return direction, Flight 6E 2065 will take off from Pune at 2:00 PM and land in Prayagraj at 4:10 PM.
According to sources, these flights will commence operations from February 16 and may continue until the Mahakumbh concludes. While IndiGo has not officially disclosed the fares, online ticket booking platforms indicate prices starting at over Rs 20,000.
First direct flight from Pune to Prayagraj
Before this launch, no direct flight service existed between Pune and Prayagraj for the Maha Kumbh Mela. With this new route, IndiGo becomes the fourth airline to operate flights on this sector, following Akasa Air, SpiceJet, and Air India—all of which operate with layovers.

headline: Legal (Registered) travel agents of Punjab: They play by the rules, not with lives
description: This extensive network of more than 7,500 registered agents operates alongside 217 registered recruitment agencies across Punjab, all regulated by the MEA.
content:
The ongoing US deportation controversy involving illegal travel agents operating in Punjab has eclipsed the bright spot of the state: a wide network of legal travel agents. They have been there for donkey’s years, feeding and fuelling Punjabis’ foreign dreams without showing them the ‘dunki’ route. 
According to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA), Punjab is home to 217 registered recruitment agents/ agencies. However, the Punjab NRI’s Affairs Department says the state has more than 7,500 registered travel agents, including immigration agents, travel agencies, ticketing agents, IELTS centres, and consultancies. All of them operate within strict legal frameworks designed to ensure safe and lawful immigration.
The Doaba region, comprising the districts of Jalandhar, Kapurthala, Nawanshahr and Hoshiarpur, has the highest concentration of registered agents. Jalandhar, with over 1,200 agents, leads not only in Doaba but across the state. The other three districts in the region — Kapurthala (334), Hoshiarpur (262) and Nawanshahr (227) — bring the total number of registered agents in the Doaba region to over 2,000, reflecting a network of professionals committed to guiding individuals on legal immigration routes.
The other major cities with high numbers of registered agents are Amritsar (860), Ludhiana (789), Moga (683), and Mohali (385). These licensed agents/professionals fulfil all the conditions to get licence and are bound to adhere to immigration laws, focusing on legal avenues such as study permits, work visas and visitor visas.

This extensive network of more than 7,500 registered agents operates alongside 217 registered recruitment agencies across Punjab, all regulated by the MEA.
“The presence of 7,500 registered agents across Punjab reflects the state’s well-established legal framework for immigration. While illegal agents continue to exploit the system, it is important to highlight that there are alternative, lawful routes available for those wishing to migrate. The real challenge now is to ensure that the people of Punjab choose to rely on the registered, licensed agents who adhere to the law, rather than falling prey to dangerous and illegal routes that jeopardise their safety and future,” said one of the Deputy Commissioners from the Doaba region, who wished to remain anonymous.
Even the police department acknowledges their contribution. “While illegal agents exploit individuals and put their lives at risk, there are thousands of legitimate agents working within the law to provide safe and legal immigration options,” said a senior officer from the Punjab Police.

However, the growing threat posed by illegal agents remains a cause for concern. The MEA has blacklisted 170 banned agents, many of whom continue to operate under different names or at new addresses.
Tirath Singh of Pinnacle Immigration in Jalandhar feels that unscrupulous agents are tarnishing the reputation of both the state and legitimate consultants and travel agencies. “After such incidents, people start viewing everyone with suspicion. They are looting the gullible youth of the state to the tune of lakhs and crores, and pushing them under huge financial debts and playing with their lives,” he added.
Another registered consultant, Sukhchain Singh, emphasised that although the majority of registered agents follow all immigration rules, there is still a large network of illegal agents in the state. These agents primarily target individuals who are less educated and lack the financial proof required to travel legally.

“One of the primary challenges law-enforcement agencies face is the high demand for migration, particularly in rural areas, where families often fall victim to the false promises of illegal agents. Despite widespread awareness campaigns and government crackdowns, the desperation to leave and start a new life abroad remains powerful,” said registered educational consultant Gurpreet Singh of i-Can consultancy from Kapurthala.

Rajya Sabha member Vikramjit Singh Sahney said after conducting an investigation through his teams, he had found that several unscrupulous travel agents banned by the MEA in Punjab were still operating.
“As authorities continue to tackle the issue of illegal immigration head-on, a shift in public perception is also needed. The message must be clear: while illegal agents exploit desperation, a legal, safer pathway exists, facilitated by the state’s large network of registered professionals. With education and awareness, there is a hope that Punjab’s reputation for immigration can be restored to one based on legality and integrity, rather than the dangers of human trafficking,” he said.

headline: Kashmiri shawl seller beaten, robbed in Kapurthala, third incident in 45 days
description: Nasir Khuehami, national convenor of J&K Students Association posted on social media handle that this was a repeat incident and that Kashmiri shawl sellers, who have significantly contributed to the local economy and become part of the social fabric, now live in constant fear.
content:
In the third incident of its kind in past month and a half, a Kashmiri shawl seller was targetted by unknown individuals in Kapurthala district and robbed of his belongings after being beaten up badly.
Fareed Ahmad Bajad, a Kashmiri shawl seller from Karlpora, Kupwara, was mercilessly attacked by miscreants in Kapurthala, Punjab. According to fellow Kashmiris he was brutally thrashed leaving him with multiple bruises all over his body. His belongings, which included shawls and cash, were also looted in this attack.
Nasir Khuehami, national convenor of J&K Students Association posted on social media handle that this was a repeat incident and that Kashmiri shawl sellers, who have significantly contributed to the local economy and become part of the social fabric, now live in constant fear.
“The alarming trend of targeting Kashmiri traders continues unabated, creating an atmosphere of hatred and intimidation that threatens their businesses and livelihoods,” he wrote.
