British-Irish woman’s rape-murder in Goa: Behind the conviction that earned investigators a ‘thank you’
Man held for raping 12-year-old girl on way to school in UP’s Bulandshahr, search on for his mother
Speaking to The Indian Express, SSP Kapurthala, Gaurav Toora, said that drug addicts and petty criminals were involved in the two incidents in the past and that the present one also appeared to be on the same lines.
“We have arrested four people in the past attacks and recovered all the belongings which were stolen from the victims. This is not a hate crime. There is no other angle to these incidents apart from the intent to rob,” he said. He added that an FIR has been registered in the case at City Police Station, Kapurthala even though the incident took place on the border jurisdiction of adjoining district. “The DGP has given strict instructions on immediate registration of FIRs and we will resolve the jurisdiction matter later,” he said.
The SSP said the shawl sellers often visit the villages alone which makes them a lucrative target for petty criminals. “We have asked them in the past to move in groups of 6-7 people. The shawls that they carry are very expensive in some cases,” he said. He added that the attackers in the present instance will also be arrested soon.

headline: Opposition finds fresh ammo in Kejriwal-Punjab MLAs’ meet: ‘split, mid-term poll imminent’
description: Congress MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa said while the meeting is an internal matter of the AAP, it reflects the confusion within the party after the Delhi Assembly elections were declared on February 8.
content:
The assertions of Arvind Kejriwal that the Aam Aadmi Party is united in Punjab and that there is no plan to replace Bhagwant Mann as chief minister, the opposition parties Tuesday continued to claim that the ruling party in border state is set for a split and a mid-term election is imminent. The Opposition parties also questioned the AAP’s move to use Kapurthala House — the official residence of Punjab CM in New Delhi — for the meeting.
Shiromani Akali Dal spokesperson Arshdeep Kler said it was surprising that the meeting took place at Kapurthala House. “So now the party meetings of AAP will also happen at the cost of Punjab government? This indicates that Delhi leadership of AAP is still having control over Punjab government. It is high time that Mann should start taking decisions at his own level in Punjab as only two years of his government are left. People of Punjab are watching everything, the way Delhi has shown the door to AAP, they will do the same to them in Punjab as well”.
Congress MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa said while the meeting is an internal matter of the AAP, it reflects the confusion within the party after the Delhi Assembly elections were declared on February 8.
“The party will break soon. There will be mid-term polls in Punjab. When a party loses, there is a discussion within the state, and MLAs of other states are not called. They are worried that what happened in Delhi may be repeated in Punjab,” he said. “Many are in touch with Congress over the past several days,” he added.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Randhawa said the meeting should have taken place in Punjab. “Only one person (Kejriwal) would have needed to come here. The chopper and the chartered plane of Punjab would have been used to get him here. The people of Punjab would also have been able to see him,” he added.
Also Read | As Kejriwal meets party’s Punjab MLAs in Delhi, Congress leaders predict defections and a mid-term poll
Randhawa said he raised the issue of terrorism and repeated grenade attacks in Punjab in Parliament, and pointed out what he called the apathy of the state government — including CM Mann. “The CM did not show courage against the terror acts of Khalistanis. Pakistan is sending in drones with grenades and drugs deep inside Punjab. Why is the BSF, which has a mandate to act up to 50 km from the international border, not doing anything? I have twice written to the Home Minister for an NIA investigation into the grenade blasts on police establishments close to the Indo-Pak border but nothing has been done,“ he said.
Partap Singh Bajwa, the Leader of Opposition in Punjab Vidhan Sabha, also claimed that over 30 AAP MLAs are in touch with his party, predicting potential defections and a possible mid-term poll in Punjab. Bajwa again claimed said Kejriwal might contest from Ludhiana to replace Mann as CM.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Meanwhile, AAP’s Rajya Sabha MP Swati Maliwal too took a dig at Kejriwal. “Some people have started treating Punjab as their personal ATM. Today, massive corruption is rampant in Punjab.” “There is blatant sand mining at different places, corruption is there in transfer postings. People of Punjab and several MLAs are angry on this.
Arvind Kejriwal has appointed his goon Bibhav Kumar as the chief advisor of Punjab CM,” she said, adding ever since Kejriwal faced defeat in Delhi, he is planning to go to Punjab to “keep his politics alive”.
BJP leader and newly elected MLA from West Delhi’s Rajouri Garden Manjinder Singh Sirsa took a jibe at Kejriwal for holding a meeting with Punjab MLAs despite party’s defeat in Delhi.
Also Read | Kejriwal puts chatter to rest: Mann to remain Punjab CM
“He is dreaming of becoming Punjab chief minister. Just like a fish out of water, Kejriwal can not live without power or luxury. The people of Punjab are self-respecting and have mellowed the arrogance of many, so, Kejriwal should stop dreaming about becoming Punjab’s CM,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Congress MP Gurjit Singh Aujla said, “If Kejriwal is holding a meeting immediately after the defeat then it has a different meaning. He has lost Delhi, so he should call Delhi leaders and brainstorm, but Punjab MLAs have been called. Both his models, Punjab and Delhi, have failed”.
Aujla said Kejriwal wants to bring about some changes in the leadership of his party’s Punjab unit. “The people of Punjab are fed up with him, no matter how many meetings he holds, it will not make any difference,” he said, adding that 24-30 AAP MLAs were in contact with the Congress.
Punjab BJP chief Sunil Jakhar took a swipe at Mann. In a post on X, Jakhar said, “While all sorts of political kite-flying about the fate of Punjab CM is going on, at least one thing can be said with certainty that whatever transpired in Kapurthala House today, it did nothing to soothe the frayed nerves of CM Mann. While interacting with the media afterwards, he seemed so distraught that ‘chutkule sunana to dur, aaj bolte hue unke apne sur, taal mel nahin kha rahe they’ (Forget about cracking jokes, today his tone and rhythm were not matching while speaking).”
Also Read | ‘Let Congress say what it wants to’: After meeting Kejriwal, Mann trashes speculation of rift in AAP
BJP’s Punjab spokesperson Pritpal Singh Baliawal, said “the one who lost the polls is giving lectures” to the elected ones. “For a 30-minute meeting, crores of Punjab’s money was wasted —MLAs, ministers, and over 1000 security personnel were rushed to  Delhi. The crux is that Punjab will still be ruled from Delhi only”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Speaking to media persons in New Delhi, Congress MP from Chandigarh Manish Tewari said it’s a “tragedy” that “Delhi will never understand Punjab because the state has a different ethos, a culture, a syncretism, and it ticks to a different beat”.
He pointed out that Punjab, as a border state, needs to be handled very carefully and the Centre needs to have a ‘border policy’ for such states. “Any political instability in Punjab will have very severe national repercussions.
Punjab is a border state. Our western neighbour is always hyperactive in trying to subvert and destroy the peace of Punjab. Therefore, there are certain border states which need to be handled very carefully. The situation in the Northeast, Manipur, is far from stabilising and so the Government of India should really concentrate on having a border policy for the border states,” Tewari said.

headline: Maha Kumbh: Millions gather for Maghi Purnima ‘snan’ amid elaborate arrangements
description: CM Adityanath is taking regular updates on the 'Snan' at Sangam, from the war room set up at his official residence in Lucknow.
content:
The sacred bath on Maghi Purnima began early Wednesday as millions of devotees gathered in the Maha Kumbh Mela area here amid elaborate arrangements, with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath monitoring the event from Lucknow.
With the Maghi Purnima bath, the month-long Kalpavas will also end and the around 10 lakh kalpvasis will start leaving the Maha Kumbh. The administration has requested all Kalpvasis to follow traffic rules and use only authorised parking spaces.
Lakhs of devotees have already taken the holy dip at the Triveni Sangam and other ghats since the bathing started early morning. Millions of devotees are headed to the Sangam Nose to take a dip.
CM Adityanath is taking regular updates on the ‘Snan’ at Sangam, from the war room set up at his official residence in Lucknow.

Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
Kumbh SSP Rajesh Dwivedi said, “The movement of devotees is going on smoothly and we are taking care of all (crowd) pressure points.” “We have made elaborate arrangements during the previous ‘snan’ on Basant Panchami too. Our arrangements have been further augmented this time. More deployment has been done at all the pressure points. Along with that, we are briefing people to ensure a smooth movement,” he said.
Chief Minister Adityanath greeted devotees and the residents of the state on the holy bathing festival.

“Heartiest greetings to all the revered saints, religious leaders, Kalpvasis and devotees who have come for the holy bath at the sacred Triveni in Maha Kumbh-2025, Prayagraj. May everyone’s life be filled with happiness, prosperity and good fortune by the grace of Lord Shri Hari. May Maa Ganga, Maa Yamuna and Maa Saraswati fulfill everyone’s wishes,” he posted on X.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Officials said they have made elaborate arrangements for the occasion to ensure the devotees take the sacred bath without any hassle.
The fair area has been declared a ‘no vehicle zone’ from 4 am on Tuesday, while the entire city will become a no-vehicle zone from 5 pm onwards, with an exemption for emergency and essential services. To avoid traffic chaos, designated parking lots have been marked for public and private vehicles.
Prayagraj ADG Bhanu Bhaskar said special police forces have been deployed at all places where crowd management becomes challenging.
The special traffic plan will remain in force till the completion of the bathing ritual to ensure safe evacuation of devotees from the fair area in case of any emergency.

Bhaskar said that real time data is being collected from toll plazas and officials of neighboring districts so that the number of vehicles coming and the routes can be monitored and regulated.

Srinivas, who has come from Andhra Pradesh to take a holy dip, said, “It feels good. The UP government has made good arrangements. The UP government has created a good atmosphere here. Actually being a Hindu, this is the first time I have really felt like an Indian. People have shown their religiousness and unity has been promoted.” Officials said the state transport department has arranged 1,200 additional shuttle buses, which will be available every 10 minutes, for the return of the devotees, The Uttar Pradesh government said on Tuesday that only 14 days are left for the Maha Kumbh to end. More than 45 crore people have taken a dip in the Sangam so far since the grand religious event started on January 13.
The Maha Kumbh will conclude on February 26 with the final Amrit Snan on the occasion of Mahashivratri.
A stampede during the Manui Amaswya ‘Amirt Snan’ on January 29 had left, according to the Uttar Pradesh government, 30 dead and 60 injured.

headline: Ahmedabad court orders FIR against man who posed as judge, set up ‘fake tribunal’ to obtain civic body land
description: The court ordered the registrar to file an FIR against Christian and his associates under relevant sections of the law.
content:
The City Civil Court in Ahmedabad recently ordered its registrar to file an FIR against a man who allegedly posed as an arbitrator-judge and set up a false tribunal to obtain a land owned by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC).
The order was passed on February 6 by judge J L Chovatiya. It said that the man, identified as Morris Samuel Christian, allegedly entered into a criminal conspiracy to obtain land owned by the AMC at revenue survey number 117 at Shahwadi in the Daskroi taluka.
Christian’s tribunal was reportedly replete with “staff and lawyers”.
“They had a claim statement application drawn up, had it presented before himself, and passed a fraud award-order in the name of the petitioner in spite of the fact that this land has been owned by the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation for several years. This same award-order was presented as genuine in this court,” stated the order.

It further stated, “Morris Samuel Christian then made arguments in continuity of his fraudulent activity, and carried out an organised crime with his associates.”

headline: Narmada: DM order bans unauthorised people from climbing towers for protests
description: The development comes over a month after the Narmada district police stationed round-the-clock guards and increased police patrolling across all the accessible transmission tower installations to deter people indulging in frequent Sholay-like protests for “fulfillment of demands”.
content:
The Additional District Magistrate of Narmada District recently issued a notification making it mandatory for the utilities and telecom companies to ensure fencing and deployment of guards to prevent unauthorised persons from climbing up the transmission towers.
The development comes over a month after the Narmada district police stationed round-the-clock guards and increased police patrolling across all the accessible transmission tower installations to deter people indulging in frequent Sholay-like protests for “fulfillment of demands”.
In a notification issued Monday, Additional District Magistrate CK Ungad stated that the notification will extend to the entire district of Narmada although the request was made by the Narmada District police to notify mandatory provisions in the area around the Statue of Unity in Ekta Nagar.
The notification states, “As per the request application of the Narmada District Superintendent of Police… several tourist spots, including Statue of Unity (SoU) and Sardar Sarovar Narmada Dam are located in Ekta Nagar in Garudeshwar taluka… On several instances, in order to pressurise the administration to give in to their demands, locals climb up telecom towers”. “Therefore, in order that such incidents are not repeated, the (police) request has been received to issue a notification making it mandatory to have fencing and other arrangements in place for towers of various companies… so prohibit unauthorised persons from entering and climbing the towers. Therefore, it appears to be necessary to issue this notification,” said the order.

Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?

The notification makes it mandatory for utilities and companies setting up towers to “ensure fencing and deploy security guards while also installing a lock system to ensure that unauthorised persons do not climb up the towers” and also need to put up boards on the towers stating that “prohibitory orders are in place against unauthorised persons intending to climb the towers.” The notification states that those violating the orders will be punished under Section 223 (disobeying orders in place) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Earlier instances
In December, The Indian Express had reported that at least 35 transmission towers in the periphery of SoU had been put under “round-the-clock security” while patrolling, especially in the wee hours, has been increased to prevent instances of people protesting against the administration and creating a ruckus.
The decision had come a few days after a man and a woman from the Narmada project-affected villages climbed up a telecom tower in Kevadia colony on December 6, seeking that their demands from the 2016 protests be met, leaving the district administration on toes.

Both had agreed to descend from the telecom tower after almost five hours when the Sardar Sarovar Punarvasahat Agency (SSPA) officials assured them that their demands would be forwarded to the government, sending out an urgent letter.
In a separate case, another local resident had climbed up a tower in protest against his dismissal from a government posting. A similar instance was reported when a local resident with a private grouse against someone had climbed up a tower.

headline: 42 ‘copy’ cases reported on Day 1 of HSC exam in Maharashtra
description: Out of the total 42 copy cases, the maximum (26) are from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar division of Maharashtra state board
content:
Despite statewide campaign for “copy-free-exams” by the Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (MSBSHSE), a total of 42 copy cases were recorded from 19 exam centres across Maharashtra on the first day of the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examination which commenced on Tuesday.
Out of the total 42 copy cases, the maximum (26) are from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar division of Maharashtra state board. Out of the nine divisions of the state board, only three – Mumbai, Kolhapur and Konkan—recorded no copy cases on the first day of the exam.
Chairperson of Maharashtra State Board Sharad Gosavi, said, “We did not expect that there will be no copying at all. Compared to last year’s 58 copy-cases on day one of the HSC exam, the number of copy cases reported this year are lesser. The awareness under the copy-free-exam campaign seems to have made an impact.”
All the 42 copy cases will be scrutinised further to decide if any action needs to be taken. The scrutiny will include knowing the nature of these copy cases and whether these cases are reported by the respective exam centres or the ones spotted by state-board appointed vigilance squads.

“Knowing the nature of the copy-case is important as it determines the severity of the case. Furthermore, if the cases are reported by respective exam-centre heads, it indicates that our awareness regarding “copy-free-exams” has shown results and exam centres are being more vigilant. Action will be taken against the centres if they are found aiding the copying even if it is by not reporting it. If the copy-case is reported by our flying-squads visiting exam-centres, it indicates that the exam centre has failed in its duty,” explained Gosavi.
Responding to a significant number of copy-cases reported from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar division, Gosavi said, “We have already deployed additional vigilant squads in Marathwada region. Furthermore, we are again instructing exam centres to become vigilant in identifying copy-cases during exam.”
Meanwhile, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Wednesday ordered that any exam center found facilitating mass copying during state board exams would have its approval permanently revoked. He also directed the dismissal of any teachers or staff members who assist in such malpractice.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The decision was made during a state cabinet meeting led by Fadnavis, where he held discussions with district collectors and police officers across the state about the preparations and measures to be taken for the upcoming exams.
The HSC exam, which started on Tuesday, will continue till March 18 at 5130 exam-centres. The Secondary School Certificate (SSC) exams will be held at 5,130 centers from February 21 to March 17.

headline: ‘New govt will implement AB-PMJAY in first Cabinet meeting’: BJP MPs withdraw plea from HC
description: Earlier, then AAP government had categorically told the HC that it “does not want to implement the AB-PMJAY scheme as it will amount to downgrading the schemes already in place in Delhi”.
content:
Seven Delhi BJP MPs, who had moved a public interest litigation (PIL) in the Delhi High Court challenging the “arbitrary decision” of the then AAP government to not implement Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana) in the Capital, withdrew the petition on Tuesday. They informed the HC that the new BJP government will issue instructions on implementing the scheme in its first Cabinet meeting.
The PIL was moved last November by BJP MPs Bansuri Swaraj, Praveen Khandelwal, Ramvir Bidhuri, Kamaljeet Sehrawat, Harsh Malhotra, Manoj Kumar Tiwari and Yogender Chandolia, challenging the “arbitrary decision” of the government to not implement PMJAY in Delhi. In January, then AAP-led government had opposed the PIL, saying that it has its own Delhi Arogya Kosh (DAK) scheme, which is a “much more robust scheme in comparison to AB-PMJAY”.
Advocate Tejasvi Gupta, representing the petitioners, informed the division bench of Justices Prathiba Singh and Manmeet Pritam Singh Arora that the “the present dispensation has assured that the scheme will be implemented in the first Cabinet meeting”. The bench permitted the request.
Earlier, then AAP government had categorically told the HC that it “does not want to implement the AB-PMJAY scheme as it will amount to downgrading the schemes already in place in Delhi”. The BJP MPs, on the other hand, had highlighted that under the health insurance scheme, those aged 70 or more, irrespective of their income, will be entitled to a cover of Rs 5 lakh annually to be shared within the family.
The AAP government had pointed out that AB-PMJAY scheme will only benefit 12-15% of the city’s population, impressing that “the healthcare model of the state provides for high quality specialised care for all, whether local or not”.

headline: Over, 7,000 birds culled, 2,230 eggs destroyed as bird flu strikes Maharashtra
description: Animal Husbandry officials have distributed Rs 2,91,963 as compensation to poultry farmers after their birds, eggs and feed were destroyed.
content:
Since January 1, 7,200 poultry birds have been culled and 2,230 eggs destroyed in the 7 epicentres of areas affected by bird flu (Avian Influenza). Most of the outbreaks have been reported in unorganied and backyard poultry farms with the organised sector being spared of the outbreak.
The latest outbreak was reported from the village of Mangli in Brahmapuri taluka of Chandrapur district. As per officials of the state Animal Husbandry Department, 2,065 birds were killed in villages under a 5 km distance from the area where the first incident was reported. As per operational protocol, all birds, eggs, and animal feed has to be destroyed within 5 km radius of the area where the first incident has been reported. In the Chandrapur case, 1,165 eggs and 50 kg of feed was destroyed.
Animal Husbandry officials have distributed Rs 2,91,963 as compensation to poultry farmers after their birds, eggs and feed were destroyed.
Till February 6, Maharashtra reported seven epicentres of bird flu incidents from the districts of Latur, Nanded, Nagpur,Thane, Raigad and Chandrapur. Other than poultry, bird flu has been reported in tigers, leopards, vultures and crows. Mortality reported due to the flu till date is 693 which includes three tigers and one leopard. The big cats were housed in the Gorewada Rescue Center in Nagpur. Three white backed vultures have died of bird flu at the centre.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Gold medallist female power-lifter dies after 270-kg barbell falls on neck during practice in Bikaner
British-Irish woman’s rape-murder in Goa: Behind the conviction that earned investigators a ‘thank you’
In Udgir taluka of Latur district, 71 crows died that had later tested positive for the disease. Caused by the influenza A virus, bird flu is a highly contagious disease, reported mostly in birds. In all the seven epicentres the H1N5 strain of the virus was said to be the cause of the mortality in the animals and birds. Being zoonotic in nature, strict vigilance is kept when such cases are reported. The outbreak in Indian animals and birds is caused when they come in contact with migratory birds. Most cases have been reported from areas near water bodies which were frequented by migratory birds.
Animal husbandry officials said not a single case has been reported from organised poultry firms. Poultry farms have undertaken bio security measures and ensured their birds do not come in contact with any migratory birds so as to prevent any outbreak.

headline: Karnataka govt sends microfinance ordinance to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot again, with clarifications
description: While acknowledging the ordinance’s objective to ‘address the issue of harassment’ of borrowers, Karnataka Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot had underscored lenders’ ‘lawful and genuine rights’ .
content:
The Congress government in Karnataka has sent back an ordinance to regulate the microfinance sector in the state to Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot with clarifications after he returned it last week expressing concerns.
The Karnataka Micro Loan and Small Loan (Prevention of Coercive Actions) Ordinance 2025 has proposed stringent punishment for the use of coercive tactics of all forms by money lenders to collect dues from borrowers in the state. The ordinance was proposed by the government in the wake of several suicides in the state linked to coercive tactics—including the use of criminal intimidation—by money lenders.
Gehlot returned the proposed ordinance on February 7 with a direction to reconsider the proposed law. However, the government has sent the ordinance back without changes. “The clarifications sought by the Governor to the microfinance ordinance have been sent back to the Governor with full details,” Chief Minister Siddaramaiah’s office said on Monday.
The governor objected to the ordinance on the grounds that the proposed punishment of 10 years and a fine of Rs 5 lakh is excessive and that police can use existing laws to control the situation.

The governor returned the file on the ordinance to the state government “with a direction to re-submit along with clarifications”.

One of the key proposals in the ordinance is to ban microfinance institutions from outsourcing loan recovery to anti-social elements, who tend to harass borrowers with extreme measures.
“It is acknowledged that the Ordinance is trying to address the issue of harassment and to prevent unlawful and forceful actions of a few anti-social elements of society,” the governor said but added that “it is also necessary to protect the lawful and genuine rights of the persons who have lent to the needy” using existing laws as checks and balances.
“If all the pending loans with interest as on date are discharged, the lawful and genuine lenders may face trouble; further, they have no remedy to recover their pending amounts, which may lead to legal battles,” the governor said in response to a proposal in the ordinance for abatement of all pending repayments of loans and interest to microfinance firms.
“It is also seen that provision has been made for imposing a penalty for contravention of section 8 of the ordinance for punishment for a term which may extend to ten years and with a fine extending up to Rs 5 lakh, and offences under this ordinance are non-bailable. headline: Delhi court sentences ex-superintendent of children’s shelter to life for sexually assaulting minors in 2016
description: The court ruled that the former superintendent of a government-run children’s shelter in Delhi ‘misused his authoritative position’ to sexually assault the minors.
content:
A Delhi court last week sentenced the former superintendent of a government-run children’s shelter in Lajpat Nagar to life imprisonment for the rape of several minor inmates who were aged under 10 years.
“On the basis of overall facts and circumstances, the convict…is sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life, which shall mean imprisonment for the reminder of natural life of the convict for the offence punishable under Section 6 (punishment for aggravated penetrative sexual assault) of the POCSO (Protection of Children against Sexual Offences) Act and a fine of Rs 20,000,” Additional Sessions Judge Anu Aggarwal of Saket Court said in her order dated February 7.
The convict was also sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for seven years for the offence punishable under Section 10 (punishment for aggravated sexual assault) of the Pocso Act.
“The convict was supposed to take care of these children. He was assigned the duty to look after the upbringing of these children and therefore, his role can be equated with the role of a father in a family. However, convict misused his authoritative position and taking advantage of his position and vulnerable age of the children, sexually assaulted them,” the court noted while sentencing the accused.

headline: Woman kills daughters aged 3, 7 before attempting suicide in UP’s Amroha: police
description: The Amroha police said Sonia Singh, 29, had strained relations with her husband over the family’s financial situation.
content:
A woman allegedly strangled her two minor daughters before attempting to die by suicide following a fight with her husband in Uttar Pradesh’s Amroha on Monday.
The police said Sonia Singh, 29, has been admitted to a hospital where her condition is said to be critical.
According to officers, Sonia is believed to have strangled her daughters Anushka, 7, and Kitto, 3, after a dispute with her husband Kopin Singh late on Sunday night. Kopin, who works at an industrial unit in Gurgaon, had come to their village in Bahadurpur Khurd on Saturday.
Kopin’s elder brother, his wife and their children also live in the same house.

headline: Lay green pavers in kutcha parking, plant sufficient trees to provide parking space for 4-wheelers in Chandigarh: HC
description: The Punjab and Haryana HC also pointed out that the suggestion made by it on earlier occasion for restoration of green cover and simultaneously laying green pavers for parking was not only reasonable but a step towards sustainable development.
content:
Noting that there is an extreme shortage in the open areas behind the heritage building, a division bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court has asked the Chandigarh Administration to lay green pavers in the kutcha parking and plant sufficient numbers of trees to provide space for parking for four-wheelers.
The directions have been issued by the division bench of Chief Justice Sheel Nagu and Justice Sumeet Goel, which is hearing a petition filed by Vinod Dhatterwal, secretary, Punjab and Haryana High Court Employees Association, on the implementation of the high court’s holistic development plan, which envisaged setting up of multi-storey buildings to cater to the requirement of additional space.
During the resumed hearing of the matter, the building committee was unsuccessful in convincing the Chandigarh Administration to allow green pavers to be laid in the area of kutcha parking with an adequate number of trees to be planted so that the green cover can be restored and the vacant space can be used for parking purposes.
The bench, after hearing this, pointed out that the suggestion made by it on earlier occasion for restoration of green cover and simultaneously laying green pavers for parking was not only reasonable but a step towards sustainable development. The high court noted that there is an extreme shortage of parking space in the open areas provided for parking behind the heritage building of the court and on any given hour during a working session, about 3,000-4,000 four-wheelers visit the court, of which at least 2,000 vehicles are permanently parked.

The bench asserted that the existing underground multi-level parking, which has three tiers, can accommodate only 600 four wheelers while the remaining vehicles are parked in the open parking areas which also fall short and therefore, there is need to use the kutcha parking area.
Asserting that the green pavers are meant to allow water to percolate down to replenish ground level water and therefore, are much beneficial and eco-friendly as compared to pavements or roads, the bench said that the objection of Chandigarh Administration that the said area of kutcha parking is “earmarked within the capital complex as a green belt/forest, will also be taken care of and the dire need for parking space can be satisfied”.
“Moreover, the planting of at least 200 or more trees in the said kutcha parking is possible to increase the green cover and will facilitate the four wheelers parking,” noted the high court
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The bench said that despite the UT administration having made available the additional parking space of about 200 four-wheelers near the junction of Janmarg and Uttar Marg, the problem of acute shortage of space for parking within the high court premises remains.
The high court thus ordered the Chandigarh Administration to lay green pavers in the kutcha parking and plant sufficient numbers of trees at reasonable intervals with tree guards providing space for parking of four-wheelers. The bench also noted that the management and regulation of traffic, especially between 9 am to 12 noon and during post-lunch session from 2 pm to 4.30 pm, there is extreme congestion due to various bottlenecks in and around the campus of the court, which gets aggravated by the fact of the high court and its surrounding areas having been declared as Unesco World Heritage Site.
Thus, as a temporary measure, the bench further directed the Chandigarh Administration to depute adequate number of traffic policemen to regulate and manage the flow of traffic and also to ensure the vehicles to be parked at the right place in an ordinarily manner so that the limited space for parking available can be utilised to its optimum.
“The UT administration is directed to ensure this by deputing adequate numbers of traffic policemen between 9 am to 5 pm every day,” the bench ordered.

headline: Pune reports 7th GBS fatality, 3 more cases take suspected case count to 192
description: Of the 4,769 water samples collected from different parts of the city that have been sent for chemical and biological analysis to the Public Health Laboratory, samples from 65 water sources were found contaminated.
content:
A 37-year-old man from Upper Indiranagar, Bibvewadi, died of of Guillain Barre Syndrome (GBS), making it the seventh fatality from the autoimmune neurological disease, while three new suspected cases were reported on Tuesday, taking the case count to 192.
Of the 192 suspected patients detected till date, 167 patients tested positive for GBS.
In the latest case, Dr Nina Borade, chief medical officer (health) of the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) told The Indian Express that the man had travelled to Sangli and was admitted to Bharati hospital there. He had weakness in the limbs on January 31 and had difficulty in breathing.
The man was administered intravenous immunoglobulin injection but relatives later took a discharge against medical advice and admitted him to Kamala Nehru Hospital on February 5. He suffered a cardiac arrest and succumbed to septic shock with acute coronary syndrome, according to Pune district health officials.

Of the total patients, 39 are from Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC), 91 from villages newly added in PMC’s jurisdiction, 29 from Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation area, 25 from Pune rural and eight from other districts. 65 water sources found to be contaminated

headline: Delhi election 2025: BJP grabs 2 constituencies for first time since formation of Legislative Assembly in 1993
description: The Congress and the AAP had won both Mangolpuri and Jangpurafour times and three times, respectively, before the BJP won these seats in Delhi Assembly election 2025.
content:
As the BJP regains power in Delhi after 27 years, it has won the Mangolpuri and Jangpura Assembly seats that it had never secured previously since the establishment of the Legislative Assembly in 1993. Before the formation of the Delhi Assembly, the capital had a Metropolitan Council from 1966 onwards, which had the authority to make recommendations but not to legislate.
The BJP won the Mangolpuri by a margin of 6,255 votes and Jangpura by a thin margin of 675 votes. In Jangpura, considered a safe seat for the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), BJP’s Tarvinder Singh Marwah beat former deputy chief minister Manish Sisodia. The Congress had secured the Jangpura seat four times and the AAP thrice before the BJP grabbed it. In Mangolpuri, which had also been won four times by the Congress and three times by the AAP, the BJP’s Raj Kumar Chauhan beat the AAP’s Rakesh Jatav this time.
Another constituency the BJP has won for the first time is Vikaspuri. But it came into existence only in 2008, when the Congress won it, followed by the AAP thrice.
New Delhi, previously known as Gole Market, was won by the BJP for the first time in 1993. The victory in 2025 marks its second time securing the seat. Both the Congress and the AAP have held the seat thrice each.

In Delhi elections, the BJP emerged victorious by winning 48 seats with a voting percentage of 45.61 per cent. In contrast, the AAP secured only 22 seats despite receiving a vote share of 43.55 per cent. The BJP’s success marked a significant increase from just eight seats in 2020 to 48 seats in 2025, representing a fourfold increase. Its vote share also grew by 7.1 percentage points compared to the 2020 elections.
On the other hand, the AAP experienced a setback, with its vote share dropping by 10.02 percentage points from the 53.57 per cent it achieved in 2020. Consequently, the AAP’s seat count fell sharply from 62 to 22.

headline: ‘Farmers tied to pole’: Son of ginning mill owner arrested in Gujarat
description: In the FIR, Baria has stated that the altercation began when the two farmers decided to take back their cotton crop after being dissatisfied with the per quintal price offered by the mill owner
content:
A day after the videos of two farmers from Bhojpura village in Tilakwada taluka of Narmada district, allegedly tied to a pole in a ginning mill in Chhota Udepur district, went viral, police arrested the son of the owner of the mill on Saturday.
Based on the complaint of farmer Dinesh Baria, who, along with his son Kaushik, was allegedly assaulted at the mill, where they had gone to sell off their cotton yield on Friday, the Sankheda police station lodged an FIR under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against the “son of the mill owner, Hiteshbhai”. In the FIR, Baria has stated that the altercation began when the two farmers decided to take back their cotton crop after being dissatisfied with the per quintal price offered by the mill owner.
Chhota Udepur Additional Superintendent of Police Gaurav Agarwal, said, “We have registered the FIR and also arrested the son of the mill owner. The complainant has not been able to identify other accused or provide names but we are scanning the CCTV footage to identify more people involved in the incident. We have also brought in some of the mill workers and the owner for questioning as they were part of the group that had restrained the complainant and his son.”
Agarwal added that the CCTV footage “did not show” any sequence of an assault but confirmed the wrongful restraint. Agarwal said, “The CCTV footage shows that the two were tied with ropes but there has been no assault as per the video. The probe is on… We have primarily understood that the heated altercation took place when the ginning mill owner asked the farmers to wait for the queue to end, in order to have the workers re-fill their truck to take back their cotton yield that they had withdrawn from sale.”

headline: Despite unimpressive record, why BMC is opting for mechanised robotic parking in Mumbai
description: A robotic parking facility is a parking lot equipped with robotic arms and platforms that act as parking pitches for the vehicles.
content:
Despite the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) facing some serious roadblocks concerning construction and maintenance of multiple of its electromechanical robotic parking facilities, the civic body in its budget this year has allocated a substantial corpus of Rs 200 crore to set up two new robo-parking facilities at south Mumbai’s Flora Fountain (Hutatama Chowk) and Worli.
Even though this project was announced officially in 2023, it didn’t see any mention in last year’s civic budget. A robotic parking facility is a parking lot equipped with robotic arms and platforms that act as parking pitches for the vehicles. These parking spaces are multilevel, with vehicles vertically organised.
Why are the civic authorities opting for robotic parking facilities?
The BMC in its budget has proposed that the Flora Fountain facility will be able to house 194 vehicles at a time, while the one in Worli will be able to accommodate 640 four wheelers and 112 two-wheelers in a given time. Speaking to the Indian Express, civic officials said that in a space-starved city like Mumbai it’s much more convenient to have these kinds of facilities due to their vertical shape.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
After Vivek Joshi’s appointment as EC, Haryana gets new Chief Secretary
Karnataka to stop cash transfer under Anna Bhagya; beneficiaries to get 10 kg rice from February
“Setting up a horizontal conventional parking lot would require larger parcels of land. These kinds of vertical facilities could be set up on much smaller land parcels. These facilities are pretty common in the western countries and we have all the necessary facilities to operate and maintain them,” a civic official told the Indian Express.
In Mumbai, land parcels for parking units are usually reserved in the BMC’s development plan 2034 roadmap. However, with the increase in vehicular ownership in Mumbai, reservation of plots for gardens and open spaces are being made to make space for parking facilities. In 2023, the civic authorities mooted a proposal of setting up a parking facility in Bandra’s Patwardhan Park, however, this project was rolled back after protest from local citizens.
“At present, there is a dearth of open spaces in Mumbai, therefore, changing the reservation of the existing gardens and parks for making them into parking lots would be unfair. At the same time, vehicular density is increasing and if we don’t find a parking solution then the roads will get occupied with illegal parking, therefore, setting up these kinds of facilities is the only way forward,” the official added.
Features of the upcoming projects
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
At present, the BMC has issued work orders for the Flora Fountain facility, while the tenders for the Worli facility are to be floated this year. The facility at Flora Fountain will be divided into four floors with facilities to charge electric vehicles too. The entry and exit points will be strategically placed to ensure that retrieval time for a car will not exceed three minutes.
Civic officials said that the idea behind this project is to decongest the roads in the periphery of Hutatma Chowk as many of them are occupied with cars parked by people coming to the High Court as well as the commercial neighbourhood nearby.
Meanwhile, the Worli facility will be larger in size and is going to be set up in a land parcel that is primarily owned by the BMC.
An unimpressive track record
Over the past six months, two of BMC’s robotic parking projects have been stalled in the ideation and construction stage, while one operational lot is lying defunct after the contractor’s agreement was revoked.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In 2023, the BMC had initiated a Rs 122 crore 17 storey-parking lot project in Mumbadevi, and a Rs 127 crore 26 storey facility in Matunga. The civic authorities had issued a stop-work notice for the Mumbadevi project last year, while tenders for the Matunga project were scrapped in the last week of January.
Besides this, another under construction parking facility at Mumbadevi was stopped last year, after the state government directed the civic authorities to issue a stop work notice to the contractor. This facility was supposed to accommodate 600 vehicles at a time.
Prior to this, in November 2024 another robotic parking facility in south Mumbai’s Bhulabhai Desai road had to stall its operations after the BMC revoked the agreement with the contractor that was responsible for maintaining the parking lot. The 21 storey facility was operational in 2021 was Mumbai’s first ever robotic parking facility equipped to accommodate 240 vehicles at a time.

headline: Toto driver arrested for New Town girl’s rape and murder in ‘den of anti-socials’
description: Locals say the area where the minor girl’s body was found, near a plot owned by the West Bengal Infrastructure Development Finance Corporation, witnesses anti-social activities as there is no lighting.
content:
A minor girl from Gouranganagar, New Town, near Kolkata, was found murdered early on Friday, around 6 km from her home, which she left after an argument with her mother and sister late on Thursday. Her body was discovered in a bush next to a canal, close to a premium housing complex.
On Saturday, police arrested Soumitra Roy, a 22-year-old Toto driver, in a Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act case registered over the incident.
According to police, they learnt after reviewing CCTV footage from several cameras that around 11.30 pm, the girl approached the three-wheeler driver, who agreed to drop her off after other passengers. The driver then drove around with the girl before taking her to an isolated location, where he allegedly assaulted her sexually around 12.30 am. When she attempted to scream, he allegedly strangled her and fled the scene.
CCTV footage captured the girl walking nearly 2 km from her home before she was seen speaking to a biker who slowed down upon noticing her, the police said, adding that only the arrested accused was involved in the crime.
Around 6.30 am on Friday, morning walkers discovered the girl’s body with multiple bruises and scratch marks on a 1.7-acre plot owned by the West Bengal Infrastructure Development Finance Corporation. Although the area is secured by steel mesh, the police discovered a section that had been cut. Locals say the lack of lighting in the area contributes to numerous anti-social activities after dark.
Because the accused was not using a mobile phone, tracking him was challenging for the police. Eventually, they located his wife, who revealed that he was at the Kolkata Book Fair, leading to his arrest from there.
It was only when it began to get late that the girl’s mother raised an alarm and began searching for her daughter with neighbours.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A missing-person report was filed at the New Town police station at 5.30 am on Friday. Within an hour, the police received a call about the body next to the canal.
According to the police, the accused has confessed to the crime. They plan to request his custody for further investigation when he is presented in court.

headline: Priyank Kharge says social media platforms restricting content critical of PM Modi, Amit Shah, BJP: ‘Suppression undermines democratic discourse’
description: Priyank Kharge said restricting critical content not only stifles free expression but also distorts the democratic process by preventing citizens from accessing a diverse range of perspectives.
content:
Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge Sunday accused social media platforms of restricting content critical of the Central government, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah. The platforms he named are X, Meta, YouTube and Facebook.
In a post on X, Kharge said he was “increasingly convinced” that social media platforms were deliberately limiting or restricting the visibility and reach of posts critical of PM Modi, Shah and the BJP regime. “This suppression not only undermines democratic discourse but also skews public perception by silencing dissenting voices,” he said.
The Congress leader added, “This pattern of restricting critical content not only stifles free expression but also distorts the democratic process by preventing citizens from accessing a diverse range of perspectives. Such actions erode public trust in the social media platforms, highlighting the need for greater transparency and accountability in content moderation practices.”
Almost all of the social media users in the country have accounts in either one of the platforms Kharge tagged in the post.

headline: LIGO-India event held to educate Hingoli residents on proposed gravitational wave detector
description: Telescopes distributed among local schools
content:
The LIGO-India Education and Public Outreach (LIEPO) team organised Star Fest at Hingoli in Maharashtra, the site of the proposed Laser Interferometer Gravitational wave Observatory (LIGO), on February 5, to reach out to locals and increase awareness about the scientific project.
LIGO is a giant gravitational wave observatory that comprises two 4-km-long vacuum chambers, built perpendicular to each other.
Five Newtonian 5 inch telescopes donated by the Newton-Bhabha scheme, along with two refractor 2.5 inch telescopes, were distributed by the Collector and District Magistrate Abhinav Goel and Zila Parishad CEO Neha Bhosale to representatives from selected schools in each of the five talukas around the LIGO-India site. For each cluster, a “Khagol Manch” astronomers’ group has been identified, to ensure regular and proper usage of the telescopes.
The programme also included lectures on basics in Astronomy by Prasad Adekar, scientific assistant at IUCAA Scipop team; gravitational wave astronomy by Sudhir Gholap, PhD scholar at IUCAA PhD; interaction sessions with gravitational wave scientists and a demonstration session with interactive models by Kshitij Pareshetti, research student at Fergusson College, and Aarya Thuse, physics student at Savitribai Phule Pune University, LIGO Livingston virtual tour and workshop on optics and telescope usage by Tushar Purohit, Outreach Associate at IUCAA Scipop team, followed by a session on telescope assembly and skywatching by the teams from the five talukas.

Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
The sessions were attended by more than 150 school teachers from the region. Resource materials including a LIGO-India Science guidebook (in Marathi) were also distributed among them. The event was followed by a visit to a primary school in Ambala village, where the school children had a chance to interact with gravitational wave scientists and the EPO team to find out about the importance and future opportunities of the LIGO-India project.
Debarati Chatterjee, associate professor at IUCAA and chair of LIEPO, said, “The LIGO-India Star Fests at Hingoli have played an important role towards disseminating correct information about gravitational wave science and the project, highlighting its significance and opportunities to the local inhabitants. The Hon’ble Collector and District Magistrate Abhinav Goel also spoke about the synergy between LIGO-India outreach activities with the goals of the local administration in promoting astronomy to popularise science among the young generation and encouraged the participants to harness the opportunities presented by the LIGO-India mega-science project.”
The Nobel-prize winning discovery of gravitational waves in 2015 by the LIGO and Virgo detectors was a milestone in physics. The LIGO-India detector, a proposed gravitational wave detector on Indian soil, will enhance the current network of global gravitational wave detectors through its geographic location and enhanced sensitivity.

headline: Know Your City: How Atal Bridge celebrates Ahmedabad’s vibrant culture, promotes pedestrian-friendly public spaces
description: Since its inauguration by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in August 2022, Atal Bridge in Ahmedabad has attracted approximately 66.6 lakh visitors.
content:
Written by Keshav Varma
Atal Bridge is a 300-metre-long pedestrian bridge that spans the Sabarmati River, connecting Ahmedabad’s east and west sides. It is an iconic landmark for the city, designed to connect public spaces developed under the Sabarmati Riverfront Development Project. The bridge’s architecture, conceived through a design competition, draws inspiration from the vibrancy of kites and the celebrations of Uttarayan, an integral festival to the city’s culture.
The curvature of this iconic bridge is achieved through a space frame truss, which uses mild steel pipes with diameters ranging from 700 to 1200 mm and a thickness of 16 to 32 mm. The construction involved 2500 metric tonnes of steel. The structure rests on both ends and in between two supports; its three spans rest on a bundle of 1,200 mm diameter and 8-10 piles up to 36 metres deep. Spherical bearings accommodate vibration and peak thermal expansion of about 200 mm.
The curvature of this iconic bridge is achieved through a space frame truss, which uses mild steel pipes with diameters ranging from 700 to 1200 mm and a thickness of 16 to 32 mm. (Express Photo/Nirmal Harindran)
The tubular bridge structure was precisely fabricated using CNC cutting machines and detailed with Tekla BIM software. The pedestrian pathway is partially shaded by a coloured Ferrari fabric tensile structure and finished with granite and wooden flooring. The Ferrari fabric was imported from Germany, Japan, and Switzerland.

The bridge’s architecture, conceived through a design competition, draws inspiration from the vibrancy of kites and the celebrations of Uttarayan, an integral festival to the city’s culture. (Express Photo/Nirmal Harindran)
Challenges in the construction of Atal Bridge
The construction of the bridge faced several challenges. Unlike other bridges on the Sabarmati River, which have bulky pile caps, temporary cofferdams had to be created to build the piles. Another challenge was the erection of the hundred-meter spans, which rested on specially designed foundations equipped with bearings to manage thermal expansion during peak summer. The cutting, bending, and welding were all performed at the contractor’s fabrication yard in Punjab before being transported to Gujarat. High standards of finishing components were used to ensure resilience in an open environment.
The pedestrian pathway is partially shaded by a coloured Ferrari fabric tensile structure and finished with granite and wood flooring. (Express Photo/Nirmal Harindran)
The floor space of the bridge has been further enhanced for public use, incorporating food kiosks, seating areas, and sprinklers to create a meaningful and lively destination. Throughout the construction, methodologies for fabrication, erection, and finishing were continuously updated.

Since its inauguration by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in August 2022, the bridge has attracted approximately 66.6 lakh visitors, both tourists and residents, making it one of the most visited pedestrian bridges in the world.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Atal Bridge has transformed how people and the city interact with urban assets. (Express Photo/Nirmal Harindran)
Atal Bridge has transformed how people and the city interact with urban assets. Whether the mesmerising sight of birds murmuring against a sunset backdrop or the tranquil connection with the river evoking peace and serenity, the bridge fosters a profound relationship between individuals, their surroundings, and the city.
The bridge fosters a profound relationship between individuals, their surroundings, and the city. (Express Photo/Nirmal Harindran)
As a catalyst for the Sabarmati Riverfront, Atal Bridge enhances the city’s livability by providing spaces for relaxation, walking, and socialising. This experience is enriched by nearby flower gardens, plazas, and seasonal flower shows. In the future, the bridge will become an even more vibrant and dynamic place as it connects Imagicaa, a planned theme park on the riverfront, to the cultural centre on the western side. The bridge’s popularity also drives significant economic activity, establishing it as a self-sustaining model.
As a catalyst for the Sabarmati Riverfront, Atal Bridge enhances the city’s livability by providing spaces for relaxation, walking, and socialising. (Express Photo/Nirmal Harindran)
The intangible contributions of Atal Bridge to Ahmedabad are immense. It has significantly changed how citizens perceive and utilise public spaces, showcasing the potential for projects that bring visible change. The success of pedestrian bridges worldwide, such as Atal Bridge in Ahmedabad, Zero Bridge in Srinagar, and the Millennium Bridge in London, underscores the importance of prioritising the development of pedestrian-friendly public spaces along water bodies. These projects create environments that seamlessly blend utility with community and natural harmony.
-Keshav Varma is a retired Gujarat cadre IAS officer and Chairman of the High Level Committee on Urban Planning under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

headline: Region around Shiv Shakti point, where India’s Chandrayaan-3 landed, is 3.7 billion years old: study
description: Earth may be 4.5 billion years old but microbial life emerged some 3.7 billion years ago.
content:
A study by scientists of the Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) has estimated the age of the region where the Chandrayaan-3 landing site on the moon is located to be 3.7 billion years — an age that coincides with the period when primitive microbial life first emerged on Earth.
A team of scientists from Isro’s Physical Research Laboratory (PRL), Ahmedabad, has performed morphological and topographic analysis within the Chandrayaan-3 landing site, now known as the Shiv Shakti point. On August 23, 2023, India became the first country to successfully achieve a soft landing on the moon’s south pole. With the help of data generated by the Pragyan rover housed inside the Vikram lander onboard Chandrayaan-3, Indian scientists have been uncovering new interpretations and insights into the moon’s evolution.
PRL scientists deployed high-end imaging techniques, such as the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter wide-angle camera and terrain camera, to gather crater and rock distribution data from the lunar surface near Shiv Shakti. They noted that the Pragyan rover encountered several rock fragments (over 1 cm in size) at the landing site. The chains of secondary craters and crater ejecta rays were used to infer the potential source of materials within the landing area. Numerous craters with three distinct terrain types were studied: high-relief rugged terrain, high-relief smooth plains, and low-relief smooth plains.
“For the low-relief smooth plains, the area that hosts the landing site, the best-fit age is about 3.7 Ga (billion years), done using 25 craters (diameter 500-1,150 metres),” the researchers said in the study. Further age estimates from another 23 craters (measuring 500-1,250 metres in diameter) with rugged terrains and an additional five craters (measuring 600-1,150 metres in diameter) with high relief and smooth plains established the age of the region to be 3.7 billion years.

Gold medallist female power-lifter dies after 270-kg barbell falls on neck during practice in Bikaner

The lunar surface often suffers from the combined influence of micro-meteorite bombardments and extreme thermal excursions. As a result, the exposed rock fragments in this geologically old terrain would have fragmented into regolith over the past several hundred million years, the PRL team explained.
Based on morphological interpretations, the Isro scientists concluded that the local area around the landing site was mainly formed by the ejecta of secondary craters, Manzinus and Boguslawsky.

Landing site enclosed between multiple large-impact craters
The latest study, published in the Advances in Space Research, described the regional geography around the Shiv Shakti point. The Chandrayaan-3 landing site is enclosed between multiple large-impact craters: Manzinus (diameter about 96 km, age about 3.9 billion years) to the north, Boguslawsky (diameter about 95 km, age about 4 billion years) to the southeast, and Schomberger (diameter about 86 km, age about 3.7 billion years) to the south.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The landing site is surrounded by craters Manzinus to the north, Boguslawsky to the southeast and Schomberger to the south. (Credit: PRL)
Over the years, images have helped lunar scientists globally to rebuild the history of Manzinus and Boguslawsky, with both craters appearing to have flat crater floors and subdued crater wall structures. Each of these craters is categorised as shallow, with Boguslawsky being hollower than Manzinus and Schomberger. What distinguishes the Schomberger crater is its depth and well-preserved structures — including the central peak, wall terrains, raised crater rim, and steep crater walls — along with an ejecta blanket.
Further interpretations by the PRL scientists now suggest that these large impact craters would have spewed massive ejecta in the area surrounding the landing site. Previous geological mapping had revealed significant influence of Schomberger crater secondary cratering on the terrain, about 35 km south of the landing site.
Don't miss | What the first findings from ISRO’s Chandrayaan 3 mission tell us about the Moon
In addition, the PRL team analysed the distribution of rocks within the landing area and in the local area navigated by the Pragyan rover to identify the potential source craters for the emplacement of rocks.
Craters with three types of terrains were studied. (Credit: PRL)
“A higher rock population was concentrated near and around a morphologically fresh crater — denoted by continuous ejecta and a sharp crater rim. This fresh crater is about 14 km south of the landing site. Diagnostics of the fresh crater material revealed that it was less affected by space weathering in comparison to the surrounding area near the landing site,” the study noted.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Interestingly, about 9.1 per cent or 525 rock samples (of the total 5,764 rocks) measured more than 5 metres in length, whereas 428 rocks were situated around this fresh crater. Researchers found the two largest rock samples (measuring over 17 metres in length) in the entire landing area to be located near this fresh crater and another one close to its rim, the crater (1.8 km in diameter) located 8 km west of the landing site.

headline: Godawari: A step towards India’s Atmanirbharta in tur
description: Developed by the Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth in Parbhani, the tur variety of Godawari gives an astounding amount of yield and has several other benefits too.
content:
A year ago, if anyone asked Vijay Avtade if Indian farmers would ever become self-reliant through tur farming, he would have responded in the negative. The farmer from Phisare village in Solapur’s Karmala taluka has been growing tur on a portion of his 10-acre holding for years now. “Average yields are usually low and ranges between 4-5 quintals an acre. We take tur only when water is less,” he said.
But all that has changed now since Avtade, who also grows pulses like moong and urad over four-five acres and maintains a two-acre mango orchard, was introduced to the newly released variety of tur called Godawari. “During initial talks with the scientists from the Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth, we were asked what would be the expected yield from this new variety. My honest answer was seven quintals per acre as against the normal four to five quintals,” he said.
However, when Avtade began harvesting the crop in January, he was simply astounded. “As the crop progressed, I had an inkling that the harvest would be good. All the plants were thick with pods and when the final harvest figures came in, my yield from the 1.5 acres stood at 15.66 quintals – an astounding 10.44 quintals per acre. Such yields are unheard of,” said the farmer who had sowed the crop along with 11 others from his village.
“Hanumant Rokade, one of our villagers, reported a yield of 19.88 quintals from his one-acre tur crop. Now we are thinking of ditching crops like sugarcane and increasing tur cultivation,” he said. Avtade and his fellow farmers said this variety can really help India achieve atmanirbharta (self-reliance) in tur farming, which Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had mentioned in her recent Budget speech.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
Behind the success of farmers like Avtade is the new variety of tur Godawari or BDN 2019-41 developed by the Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth (VNMKV) in Parbhani. Godawari is distinguished by its milky white flowers that also act as a marker for the variety.
Pulse breeder Deepak Patil, who is in charge of the Agriculture Research Station at Badnapur in Jalna district, said the new variety was developed from established varieties of BDN 2 and ICP 7035. BDN 2, Patil said, is a well-established variety released in 1976 and is the dominant one grown in Maharashtra and Gujarat. “However, this variety is susceptible to wilt and sterility mosaic disease (SMD). The male genotype of Godawari was derived from ICP 7035, thus it has inbuilt resistance to diseases,” he said.
Indra Mani Mishra, Vice-Chancellor of VNMKV, said the Godawari variety released in 2021 ticks several boxes in terms of demands from farmers. Thus, this variety is resistant to both SMD and wilt and can grow in rainfed areas, he said, adding that it is also more tolerant to biotic stress (damage from living organisms), which is particularly important since the crop is grown in rainfed areas.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In her Union Budget speech, Sitharaman mentioned that the government intended to increase the production of three pulses, which included tur.
For the 2024-25 Kharif season, the Pani Foundation tied up with the VNMKV university to popularise the variety in Karmala taluka. “In our university we developed the whole standard operating procedure (SOP) to ensure the best yield. From seed treatment to post-harvest care, every aspect in the 165-170 day lifespan of the crop was taken into account,” Patil said.
Along with the foundation, which has been working in the area for the last few years, the university also carried out an awareness drive. Ashish Lad, a trainer from the foundation, said they worked with 40 groups of farmers with 11 members each. “Given the promise shown by this new variety, almost 80 per cent of the taluka has now come under it. Our farmers are really excited about this variety,” he said.
The SOP includes seed treatment and using raised beds to sow the crop. According to Sunil Dounde, another farmer from the village, this was the first time they actually paid attention to tur as a crop. “Having raised beds for tur was unheard of, so was the installation of bird perches or pheromone traps to control pests. Our usual practice with tur is to sow it on flat ground and harvest once the crop is ready,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Weeding became difficult as on flat ground we could not enter the field but with raised beds, both manual and mechanical weeding using the small cycle mounted weeders became easy,” he said. Dounde’s 1.5-acre tur crop has yielded 18.60 quintals. He also grows crops like urad and moong on four acres of his seven-acre holding.
Most farmers in Phisare village grew tur as a standalone crop and thus the distance between beds was 90 cm and the distance between two plants was kept at 20 cm. The university has also recommended this variety for intercropping in which case the distance between rows would be 180 cm. Farmers had used biological plant growth promoters like Dashaparni Ark (a mixture of leaves of 10 medicinal plants) besides relying on manure during soil preparation. The crop’s stubble, Avtade said, was stored to be used as fertilizer for the next season. Given its nitrogen fixation capacity, the farmers have reported a rise in soil fertility as well. On average, they reported that the cost of production was between Rs 25,000-30,000 per acre.
What tilted the scales in favour of Godawari is the economy of scale. “With market prices being unpredictable, the only way we can make money is to have more to sell. This variety does exactly this and we see this being favoured by farmers in the coming seasons. Perhaps we will soon change the name of Karmala taluka to Turmala considering the crop’s predominance here,” quipped Avtade.

headline: West Bengal Board of Secondary Education bans invigilators from carrying mobiles, smartphones inside exam halls
description: This year, 9,84,753 students will be appearing in the Madhyamik examination, among whom 5,55,950 are girls.
content:
The West Bengal Board of Secondary Education (WBBSE) has banned teachers from carrying any electronic gadgets during invigilation duty in the upcoming Madhyamik (Class 10 board) examination.
The WBBSE recently released guidelines stating that invigilators must submit their mobile phones and other electronic gadgets to “their respective Centre Secretary/Venue Supervisor immediately on reporting to duty on examination days.”
The restriction will be applicable on examination days from 9 am to 4 pm. A daily register will be made to keep a record of the gadgets submitted.
If any teaching or non-teaching staff does not carry any device then they would have to give a declaration stating the same.

Teachers and other staff not directly involved in the examination process would also be required to submit their mobiles if they are present at the centre during the examination.
According to sources, centre secretaries and venue supervisors have been instructed to report any instances of non-compliance immediately via the ELIXAM App. The ad-hoc committee of the WBBSE will swiftly address any violation of the directive and the teacher or staff member concerned will be held liable for non-compliance, said a source.
In another development, the WBBSE has decided to not depute any civic volunteers inside examination centres. Para teachers and contractual teachers will also not be given invigilation duty or any duty which will involve handling confidential examination materials.

The Board has also asked guardians of examinees to not enter examination halls. In case of any emergency if a guardian is required to enter the hall, then s/he will be frisked by the police on duty.
“This is being done as previously it has been seen that people have misused the access given to them and helped students to cheat,” said a source.
Invigilators, on the other hand, will not be frisked by the police but by the school staff themselves before entering examination halls.
This year, 9,84,753 students will be appearing in the Madhyamik examination, among whom 5,55,950 are girls. The examination will be held from February 10 to February 22.

headline: Impasse ends in Bengali film and TV industry; directors’ body agrees to resume shooting from Monday
description: Earlier in the month, director Srijit Roy had taken to Facebook Live to allege that certain individuals were intentionally hindering his production.
content:
The prevailing impasse in the Bengali film and television industry that started following the ‘disruption’ of director Srijit Roy’s shooting earlier this month ended Saturday. The Directors Association of Eastern India (DAEI), which had called for an indefinite strike since Thursday, decided to resume shooting following a meeting with two state ministers — Aroop Biswas and Indranil Sen — on Saturday.
Biswas and Sen stressed that the film industry is a big family and that problems can be solved through talks and negotiations.
Earlier in the month, Srijit Roy had taken to Facebook Live to allege that certain individuals were intentionally hindering his production. Previously, directors Kaushik Ganguly and Joydip Mukherjee’s productions also faced difficulties owing to a ‘shortage’ of available technicians.
Some DAEI members alleged that they were being targeted for criticising certain directives of the Federation of Cine Technicians and Workers of Eastern India. They complained that technicians were being asked to ‘boycott’ their shootings, resulting in significant financial damage.

headline: Fire breaks out at under-construction Sabarmati bullet train station in Ahmedabad; no casualties reported
description: The fire at the under-construction Sabarmati bullet train station in Ahmedabad was reportedly caused by welding sparks that fell on wooden planks being used for construction, as per officials.
content:
A fire broke out at the under-construction Sabarmati bullet train station in Gujarat’s Ahmedabad early on Saturday morning during welding work at the site. Workers at the location were immediately evacuated and no injuries or casualties were reported, officials said.
The incident occurred at around 6.30 am when welding work for roof shuttering a part of the station was going on. The Ahmedabad Fire and Emergency Services (AFES) rushed 14 fire tenders to the spot and brought the fire under control.
The fire broke out on the terrace of the third floor of the station, at a height of approximately 15 metres, officials said. The workers were building the terrace using metal rods (girders), setting up a grid of wooden planks and filling it with construction material mix when the incident occurred.
Officials said primarily, the blaze seems to have been caused when sparks from the welding iron flew into the wooden planks due to strong winds early in the morning.

Fire tenders were initially rushed to the spot from the Sabarmati and Chandkheda fire stations. Later, more fire tenders were brought in from Sahpur, Navrangpura, Maninagar and Jamalpur, AFES officials added.
It took AFES about four hours to control the blaze as it had spread across the top of the under-construction ceiling. “We first stopped the propagation of the fire by conducting external firefighting. We then created two teams and breached the structure to carry out internal firefighting to tackle the main blaze. Fortunately, nobody was injured in the incident,” said Inayat Shaikh, Divisional Officer.
The National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) issued a statement, saying “normalcy has been restored” at the site. “Early this morning around 6.30 am, a fire was reported at the roof shuttering of one part of the construction site of the Sabarmati Bullet Train station. No injuries or casualties have been reported. The cause of the fire is yet to be determined, but prima facie, it appears that welding sparks from temporary shuttering work may have triggered it…NHSRCL officials are on-site, monitoring the situation,” the statement said.

NHSRCL workers attempted to douse the flames using fire extinguishers on site but the blaze was too strong to be controlled, which led them to contact the AFES.

headline: Major renovation underway at Pune’s British-era Central Building, work to get over in a year
description: The Public Works Department has sanctioned Rs 30 crore to repair the broken tiles, outdated sewage system, and leaking roofs and toilets at Pune Central Building.
content:
Pune’s Central Building, the iconic colonial-era structure that has witnessed the city’s transformation for over a century, is going through a major restoration work to wipe out the wear and tear and re-enhance its British neo-classical architecture architectural glory.
Constructed in 1915, the Central Building that now houses 40 Maharashtra government offices has shown signs of wear and tear over the years with broken tiles, outdated sewage system, and leaking roofs and toilets apart from overgrown wild shrubs, causing cracks in the black-stone structure.
The Public Works Department has sanctioned Rs 30 crore for renovating the historical black stone structure that stands on 10-acre land. It expects the refurbishing work to be completed within a year. As part of modernisation activities, more parking lots would be housed within the compound and old windows would be either replaced or repaired adhering to the heritage design, it said.
The areas damaged by plant growth are being repaired using traditional lime mortar, said architects assigned for the project.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
