Karnataka to stop cash transfer under Anna Bhagya; beneficiaries to get 10 kg rice from February
“The electrical conduits, water and sewage channels will be worked upon. The Jack arch floors will undergo non-destructive stability tests before restoration, and modern waterproofing techniques will be employed while maintaining the building’s original character,” said architect Kiran Kalamdani who has been assigned the restoration project along with Anjali through a tender process.
“The renovation was fixed after a consultation meeting with the heritage department. The building’s growing footfall has also highlighted infrastructure inadequacies, particularly in parking facilities that will be added within the project as the building houses around 40 government offices,” said Surendrakumar Katkar, executive engineer, PWD Pune.
The government offices that function inside the building are the departments of Education, Agriculture, Town Planning, and PWD, Office of Additional Director General of Police (ADG), and Inspector General of Prisons among others.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Legacy in Stone
According to Pune Gazetteer, the Central Building was constructed around 1915. It was designed by Scottish architects George Wittet and John Begg. Wittet was also behind constructing Mumbai’s Gateway of India. The structure incorporates British neo-classical architecture, a style of building that combines elements of Greek and Roman architecture and was also a part of Britain’s art and craft movement which began post-1850s.
The Central Building was thoughtfully designed in a ‘I-shaped layout’ that incorporates traditional black stone on the outside and bricks from within, providing a strong foundation and stability. A well-illuminated central passage runs through the structure, while semi-circular entrances on both the north and south sides welcome visitors through raised porches and elegant arches.
Its load-bearing walls, over two feet thick, support a wooden roof system known as ‘queen-post type scissors’. The floors feature a ‘jack arch floor’, a type of floor construction that uses lime concrete arches and steel I-beams to support the floor and reduce the building’s weight.
The facade is crowned with umbrella-shaped domes, known as cupolas, perched atop robust stone pillars. The architects created visual poetry in stone, weaving together delicate lattice work with sturdy cast iron railings. While the cornerstones are deliberately oversized, anchoring the building firmly to its foundations.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Within this iconic architecture, countless files have been signed, decisions made and destinies shaped.
Architectural splendor
As one steps inside the premises, this building exudes grandeur with soaring ceilings and wide hallways, creating an awe-inspiring sense of space.
Natural light floods the central corridor through around 500 windows – with different designs, adding characters to the walls.
Massive teak doors with intricate craftsmanship are still impressive. The building breathes through its thoughtful design, aided by the surrounding trees that help maintain a pleasant temperature both inside and out.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The structure’s imposing presence is enhanced by its strategic location and distinctive design elements. Originally made for the British bureaucracy, the complex expanded over time with the addition of the Executive Building in 1943 and a second administrative building in 1964. The structure’s rainwater pipes are ingeniously tucked within the stone walls, preserving the aesthetic appearance, though this has posed maintenance challenges over the years.
Elaborate details, like arched doorways inspired by Roman architecture, the leafy patterns carved into pillars, and the delicate stonework framing each floor of the three-storey building, add a touch of elegance and sophistication.

headline: Punjab Governor Kataria overturns predecessor’s orders, allows govt to directly send files
description: Sources in the government said Kataria has allowed such files to be sent to him directly without awaiting Cabinet nod, pointing to a “softening of relations between the Raj Bhavan and the state government”. During Purohit’s tenure, the Punjab government often locked horns with the Governor’s office over various issues.
content:
Over two years after former governor Banwarilal Purohit directed the Punjab Government to route files pertaining to remission of convicts’ sentences through the Cabinet, his successor Gulab Chand Kataria has done away with the practice.
Sources in the government said Kataria has allowed such files to be sent to him directly without awaiting Cabinet nod, pointing to a “softening of relations between the Raj Bhavan and the state government”. During Purohit’s tenure, the Punjab government often locked horns with the Governor’s office over various issues.
Punjab currently has 200 pending cases in which convicts have sought remission of their sentences. “We are now sending the files to the Governor gradually. We do not need to take the files to the Cabinet now,” said an official.
Soon after the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) came to power in the state in 2022, Purohit had laid down the condition that he would sign files on remission of convicts’ sentences only on the Cabinet’s advice.
He had also asked the government to ensure that a separate file was prepared for each convict deemed eligible for remission. The files were separately cleared by the Cabinet.

A government official said earlier the government used to send the names directly to the Governor. “The Governor used to sign on the file of premature release. The decision on premature release was taken by the governments and the Governor would only sign on it. However, Purohit made it clear that all convicts’ cases would be discussed and recorded in the minutes of the meeting,” the official said.
“Later, he would take a call on the advice of the Cabinet. This had made the work of the Department of Jails and the Cabinet a little time-consuming. They had to wait for the Cabinet meeting. Purohit had written to us, citing the Constitution, that the Governor was bound to accept the advice of the Cabinet,” the official added.
After Kataria took over, the state government took up the issue with him. “We wrote to the incumbent Governor that the cases will be put to him through the Jails Minister and the Chief Minister. We also told him that the Cabinet authorises the Chief Minister and the government to send the cases of remission directly,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
When the government pointed out to Kataria that convicts eligible for remission had to wait for the Cabinet meeting, he immediately agreed to sign the files directly, the official said, adding, “We put it up to him and he has agreed. Now, the files will go straight to the Governor.”
Unlike the current situation, earlier the Punjab government had frequent tussles with the former Governor. The state government had even moved the Supreme Court against Purohit when he did not allow the government to hold the Vidhan Sabha session.

headline: Delhi polls: In a first, turnout of women voters higher than that of men
description: Of the total registered women voters in the city (72.37 lakh), 60.92% voted, as compared to 60.21% of men.
content:
For the first time in Delhi, the turnout of women surpassed that of men in the Assembly elections.
Delhi voted on February 5 and the results will be declared today, February 8.
Of the total registered women voters in the city (72.37 lakh), 60.92% voted, as compared to 60.21% of men.
The percentage of women who came out to vote as compared to their share in the electorate has been on the rise over the years, and in the 2020 polls, it nearly matched that of men.

Delhi has 70 Assembly constituencies. Only 25 of the 210 candidates fielded by the AAP, BJP and Congress were women. More than 46% of Delhi’s electorate comprises women.
As per data released by the Election Commission of India on Friday, the percentage turnout of women was higher than that of men in 40 constituencies.
This includes several constituencies in South, Southeast, Central, Northwest and Southwest Delhi.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The biggest difference, of over 5 percentage points, was seen in Okhla, where 58.2% of the registered women voters turned up against 52.5% of male voters.
The women electors in Badarpur, Tughlakabad, Kalkaji and Sangam Vihar constituencies, all held by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) at present, who came out on February 5, were proportionally higher than men by at least three percentage points.
In two constituencies — Greater Kailash and Vishwas Nagar — the turnout of men and women was the same.
Delhi has had three women chief ministers since the reinstatement of a Vidhan Sabha in 1993 — BJP’s Sushma Swaraj (1998), Congress’ Sheila Dikshit (1998-2013) and AAP’s Atishi (September 2024 — till date).
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Aam Aadmi Party’s election campaign, much like that in the states of Maharashtra, Jharkhand and Madhya Pradesh, commenced with an announcement that non-tax-paying women would be given Rs 2,100 per month if AAP came back to power. Free bus rides for women, one of the party’s most popular schemes, was part of its poll campaign as well.
The BJP and Congress followed suit, each announcing that they would give women
Rs 2,500 per month if voted to power.

headline: Bengal Global Business Summit yields Rs 4.4-lakh crore bids, Mamata says Bengal a growth powerhouse
description: In the seven previous summits held between 2015 and 2023 — there was no BGBS in 2024 — West Bengal received investment proposals worth a total of Rs 19.54 lakh crore.
content:
West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Friday described the state as having “emerged as a powerhouse of growth and opportunity” and said this year’s Bengal Global Business Summit (BGBS) yielded “212 MoUs and Letters of Intent, with investment proposals totalling Rs 4,40,595 crore”.
In the seven previous summits held between 2015 and 2023 — there was no BGBS in 2024 — West Bengal received investment proposals worth a total of Rs 19.54 lakh crore.
In this year’s summit, held on Wednesday and Thursday in Kolkata, the investment proposals received amounted to Rs 4.4 lakh crore. In the BGBS 2023, the amount was Rs 3.76 lakh crore, and in the year before that, it was Rs 3.42 lakh crore. No BGBS was held in 2020 or 2021 due to the pandemic. In the five summits held before that, the total investment proposals each year ranged from Rs 2.43 lakh crore in 2015 to Rs 2.84 lakh crore in 2019.
“The dream of ‘Biswa Bangla’, a Bengal that leads by example, a Bengal that is future-ready, a Bengal that speaks to the world, is a reality, unfolding before our eyes. The vision I set in motion has borne fruit, and Bengal is on the map, as a leader, as an innovator, as a partner for the world,” the Chief Minister said in a post on X a day after the summit’s conclusion.

At BGBS 2025, Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani said that the group had invested over Rs 50,000 crore in West Bengal since 2016 and that it would double that investment by 2030.
Other major investment proposals came from JSW Group chairman Sajjan Jindal, who announced the setting up of two thermal power plants of 800 MW each at Salbani in West Medinipur district with a proposed investment of Rs 16,000 crore; Harshvardhan Neotia, chairman of Ambuja Neotia Group, who announced an investment of more than Rs 15,000 crore in the next five years; and RP-Sanjiv Goenka Group chairman Sanjiv Goenka, who announced investment of Rs 10,000 crore.
Mamata Banerjee, who assumed office as West Bengal Chief Minister in 2011, organised the first BGBS in 2015.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“During the seven editions of the BGBS, we had received investment proposals of over Rs 19 lakh crore. Of these, projects worth Rs 13 lakh crore have already been completed and projects worth Rs 6 lakh crore are in process,” Banerjee said.
The CM has looked to use this year’s summit to highlight the state as a business-friendly one and has announced the formation of a new state-level synergy committee to facilitate ease of doing business in the state.
“(The committee) will be chaired by the Chief Secretary. It will be a one-stop destination for all forms of clearance for doing business in Bengal,” Banerjee said.
Officials said that the BGBS 2025 focused on sectors like micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME), textiles, engineering, energy, transport and urban infrastructure, real estate, agriculture, tourism and international trade and logistics.

Opposition parties, however, have raised questions about the summit, with Leader of Opposition Suvendu Adhikari saying that while investment proposals have been talked about for decades, very little has been seen on the ground.
“In reality, BGBS is a glossy facade. The real meaning of BGBS isn’t Bengal Global Business Summit, it is Businesses’ Graveyard in a Bankrupt State,” Adhikari said in a post on X.

headline: Ladki Bahin scheme: Maharashtra govt clears way for ineligible beneficiaries to return money, new head in accounts opened
description: In its order dated January 29, the Women and Child Development department has informed all district officials about the opening of a new head under which the money returned by ineligible women will be deposited.
content:
The Maharashtra government has opened a new head in its finance accounts as ineligible women who benefited under the CM Majhi Ladki Bahin scheme have started repaying the money they received.
According to an estimate from the state Women and Child Development department, around one lakh women across the state have come forward to return the money they received despite not fulfilling the eligibility criteria of the scheme.
In its order dated January 29, the Women and Child Development department has informed all district officials about the opening of a new head under which the money returned by ineligible women will be deposited. “As women started coming forward to various zilla parishad and local administration offices, officials conveyed to us that there is no head in financial accounts under which the money can be deposited,” said an official from the department.
Last month, Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister Ajit Pawar had said the government was planning to weed out beneficiaries availing the benefits of the scheme even though they don’t meet the eligibility criteria.

As per the government process, a head under finance accounts has to be opened in case money is to be spent or deposited for a particular reason. That money cannot be spent on any other purpose. Similarly, money coming to the government should also be deposited under a designated head. The government accounts till now had no mention of a designated head in accounts to deposit the money returned by the women.
“There are some women who received the money despite not meeting the criteria. Now those women are voluntarily coming forward to return the money. The money we are receiving will now be deposited under this head,” the official said.
Sources said that with reports of the government scrutinising the existing list and possibility of action, a large number of women are coming forward to deposit the money. As per a primary estimate, around one lakh women across the state have come forward to return the money.

headline: At World Book Fair, a clash of ideologies and a celebration of the republic
description: In the regional languages section of the fair, large spreads of Hindi literature occupy the most space. The various renditions of Ramayanas and Mahabharats and Vedas — for the millennial, for the beginner, for the coffee table — jump out.
content:
Kids hanging off their parents’ backs, university students with excited squeals that pierce through the crowd, lovers, hand-in-hand, and an ocean of books: At Bharat Mandapam (nee Pragati Maidan), connections, interpersonal and with the written word, are apparent. The World Book Fair, 2025, held between February 1 and 9, is on day five – and in full swing.
“I relate to Jo [from Little Women] so much! I am just like her, I don’t want to get married, I don’t want to have kids, I want to write and settle somewhere outside where no one can bother me,” Shivangi Kumari, 22, a final-year computer science student from Ghaziabad says. This is her first time at the Book Fair; she calls it “a dream come to life”. Dressed in all black, with a striking pair of thin, rectangular, white sunglasses holding her hair up, she gushes about the many Dan Browns and (one) Jane Austen she has read. She adds, “I have already told my parents, I’m never ‘settling down’.” Her and two of her friends, both of whom she met in college, arrived at the fair less than an hour ago — they have bought four books they plan on taking turns reading, already. “Self-help books are stupid!” Prerna Kumari, 20, notes, while others nod aggressively, in agreement. “Go to therapy and actually help yourself… for reading, fiction is best”, Shivangi says: “It makes for an escape, and it helps me grow.”
Them and those they deride are both in luck here, though: Self-help books on “mind, body and spirit” can be found at almost every alternate shelf: Sadhguru and Jordan Peterson sitting side-by-side. But publishers, big and small, also have a wide range for Shivangi and her friends — from Jane Austen to Sally Rooney. At Penguin, the stall that has seen the most footfall by a mile (or feet), there is no room to walk; hardly any to browse. “Thank god, my teachers forced me to go to read growing up… yaar, I want to get back into it,” one in a sea of faces shares with another.
The footfall so far, Amit Kumar Singh of the National Book Trust says, has been at par with the year before. “Over the weekend, there was no room to move, we surpassed capacity.” In the “Kidzkingdom”, the massive IAS and CUET/JEE/NET prep publishing houses and shops almost dwarf the comics and biographies-carrying stalls. Yet, hoards move, almost in tandem, towards those very corners of the kingdom; the prep centres host few customers, far in between. “We are waiting so impatiently for the second volume of Divine 5,” Neeru Bangwal, 42, mother of two, says. “It has Indian characters and stories that the kids can relate to. My younger one devoured the first book quicker than I thought possible,” she adds.

Meanwhile, [publishers like] Gita Press and its ilk were selling Bhagavad Gita and Ramayana in the same space.” But all is not lost, he seems to think. “Because of the aggressive propagation of right-wing ideology, today we see, unlike before, class X and XII students are coming to us, wanting to read and explore alternatives. Speakers on the stage discuss, one after the other, the richness of the Indian republic and the many ways it has kept itself alive — and the Constitution, the book that ties it all together. headline: Rajasthan High Court dismisses plea challenging Padmesh Mishra’s appointment as AAG
description: Samdaria had prayed that Mishra be stopped from functioning as the AAG and that the order effecting change in the Policy too should be stayed.
content:
Stating that the State Litigation Policy does not have a statutory force, the Rajasthan High Court has dismissed a petition which challenged Padmesh Mishra’s appointment as the Additional Advocate General for Rajasthan government in the Supreme Court.
In his petition, Jaipur based advocate Sunil Samdaria, 50, had said that Mishra was appointed as an AAG even though he did not have the requisite 10 years’ experience to be eligible as an AAG as per the Policy; that his appointment was not made with effective consultation of the Advocate General and was thus in violation of rules; and that to circumvent the rules, the Law department had added another clause to the State Litigation Policy enabling it to appoint anyone on any post on the basis of their expertise.
Samdaria had prayed that Mishra be stopped from functioning as the AAG and that the order effecting change in the Policy too should be stayed.
In its order dated February 4, a bench of Justice Sudesh Bansal said that although the state government is expected to follow the guidelines prescribed in the Litigation Policy, “it is also equally true that such policy is in the nature of executive instructions for guidance, which cannot be claimed to have a statutory force like a legislation/ legal statute before the court of law.”

Rejecting the challenge to the addition of a new clause in the policy, the HC said that “the Supreme Court has held that the Courts ought not to venture into the question as to whether a particular public policy is wise and the Court should be loathe in interference with policy decisions.”
Regarding the objection over lack of 10 years’ experience, the court said that this requirement “has not been held as an essential and mandatory pre-requisite for appointment of Additional Advocate Generals.”
Initially, Mishra was appointed as a Panel Lawyer in the SC on August 20, 2024. Three days later, this was withdrawn to appoint him as the AAG. The order withdrawing Padmesh’s appointment as the Panel Lawyer, the notification on change in Policy, and Padmesh’s appointment as the AAG are all dated August 23.

However, the Court said that “The sequence of events may be a coincidence, but cannot be made a basis to draw an assumption of arbitrariness, biasness or colourable exercise of powers by the Cabinet,” and that the Cabinet did its “due diligence.”

headline: Gurpreet’s ‘donkey’ journey: Mortgaging his house to pay Rs 45 lakh to an agent, crossing a serpentine river 500 times through Panama’s jungles
description: Previously owning two trucks and running a transport business, Singh faced massive financial losses during the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to the shutdown of his business.
content:
Gurpreet Singh, 39, from Tarf Behbal Bahadur village in Kapurthala district, Punjab, mortgaged his house and took out a loan to arrange Rs 45 lakh to pay an agent for what he believed would be a legal route to the United States. Instead, he embarked on a perilous journey that tested his physical and mental limits.
Previously owning two trucks and running a transport business, Singh faced massive financial losses during the Covid-19 pandemic, leading to the shutdown of his business. With no land to rely on and limited options, he resorted to daily wage labor. Ultimately, he decided to leave everything behind in pursuit of a better future for his family in the US. Unbeknownst to him, this journey would lead him through treacherous jungles, where survival became a battle against nature itself.
One of the most gruelling parts of Singh’s journey occurred in the jungles of Panama, specifically the infamous Darién Gap—a dense, impassable stretch of jungle. Singh was forced to cross a serpentine river more than 500 times, contending with treacherous conditions at every turn.

“At every few meters, we had to wade through the water,” Singh recalled, his voice still shaken by the memories. “It was as if the river twisted and turned in every direction, like a serpent. For days, I crossed it more than 500 times. The water was cold, the current strong, and there was no way to predict where it would take us next.”

After five months, Singh finally made it to the United States on January 14. However, he was detained and, after spending time in a detention center, was deported on Wednesday. Now, he is burdened with a huge debt, having mortgaged his house to finance the journey.

headline: Punjab expands scope of doorstep delivery of citizen-centric services

content:

headline: Ahmedabad: Thematic roads, new fire stations in outgoing civic body chief’s draft budget
description: Besides, four flyovers and an underpass have been planned at a cost of Rs 890 crore. Feasibility studies will also be conducted for three railway overbridges and one underbridge.
content:
Outgoing Municipal Commissioner of Ahmedabad, M Thennarasan, on Thursday presented a Rs 14,001 crore draft budget of the civic body for 2025-26.  New Town Planning roads and redevelopment of existing roads of a total length of 550 km have been planned.
Also, 36 thematic roads with a total length of 72.55 km have been planned around healthcare, education, sports, business and heritage, for a cost of Rs 331 crore.
Other proposals includes the development of an integrated commercial street; a road on the extended section of the west side of the Sabarmati Riverfront, downstream from the Vasana barrage; a 14-km-long iconic road joining the east and south zones between Narol circle and Naroda Patiya; 10 mechanical parking structures; and the development of a city square on the east side of the Sabarmati river. Notably, Rs 1,000 crore has been allocated for the Phase-III of the Sabarmati Riverfront project.
Besides, four flyovers and an underpass have been planned at a cost of Rs 890 crore. Feasibility studies will also be conducted for three railway overbridges and one underbridge.

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Development of sports activity centres in the undercarriages of various flyovers, reconstruction of the Shahibaug underpass, as well as the beautification, lighting and vertical gardening initiatives on Parimal, Usmanpura and Income Tax underpasses have also been planned.
The AMC will set up two municipal markets — one each in the East and West parts of the city — seven urban plazas (1 in each zone), a Craft and City museum, seven open sports complexes, including athletic tracks, and a Science and Future Museum. Amusement parks will be set up in Motera Lake, Lambha lake, Bopal Lake, ICB Flora and Vastral Lake.  An allocation of Rs 2,300 crore has also been made for 15,000 affordable housing units.
As many as 100 additional traffic junctions will be set up across the city at a cost of Rs 25 crore. Ten thematic sculptures, an adaptive traffic control system at a cost of Rs 25 crore, and 37 overhead gantry direction signboards on entryways of the city will also be set up.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
As many as 120 buses will be added to the AMTS fleet, a Multi-Modal Transport Hub will be set up at RTO circle, 120 AC electric buses will be added to the fleet, 800 smart shelters, which will display estimated time of arrival (ETA), and an integrated model terminus at Ghuma are also part of the draft budget. The AMC is also planning to switch to digital daily bus pass through a mobile application.
In addition, the AMC will conduct a feasibility study to set up a Light Railway Transport (LRT) system like trams. Also, 100 mini electric buses for last-mile connectivity, including to metro stations, have been planned at the cost of Rs 15 crore. An additional 200 e-buses will be set up at the cost of Rs 20 crore. A Multi-Modal Transport Hub at Naroda, and new depots and Intelligent Transit Management System (ITMS) will be brought in for BRTS control.
Rs 20 crore has been allocated for the redevelopment of 28 existing gardens and to set up 22 new ones in the city. A 100-acre biodiversity park will come up in Gyaspur at a cost of Rs 10 crore.
Three new fire stations in Lambha, Ramol-Hathijan and Shahibaug at a cost of Rs 54 crore, one fire chowki in Vatva GIDC are also part of the draft budget.

Five new Urban Health Centres (UHCs) will take the total to 100. Of the existing 95, eight UHCs will be renovated. One CHC and 10 health and wellness centres will be set up. Urban heat island zones will be identified under the Heat Action Plan (HAP), the draft says.
Municipal hospitals, Shardaben and Thaltej CHC will get MRI facilities, while PMJAY counters will be set up at LG Hospital, Shardaben and Nagari Eye Hospital. A Sports Science Centre will be set up at SVP Hospital at a cost of Rs 9 crore in association with Sports Authority of Gujarat. Foetal Medicine services will be set up in gynaecology departments of LG, Shardaben and SVP hospitals. The Bhadra Plaza will be redeveloped at a cost of Rs 24 crore. In the old city, the area of Gaekwad Haveli will be developed. Heritage schools will be restored among other projects.
A 2,200 sqm tropical forest will be grown on the West Bank of the Sabarmati Riverfront, a medication centre will be set up in the biodiversity park, an exhibition-performance-convention centre will be set up behind the Event Centre, and a riverside dining area will be built between Nehru bridge and Ellisbridge. headline: Haryana Police book Delhi woman who accused BJP leader Badoli, singer Rocky Mittal of gang rape
description: In a video released in January this year, the Delhi-based woman expressed fear for her life and claimed to have sufficient evidence to prove her allegations.
content:
The Haryana Police have booked a Delhi woman, who had levelled allegations of gang rape against state BJP president Mohan Lal Badoli and Haryanvi singer-composer Jai Bhagwan, for alleged extortion.
The police lodged the First Information Report (FIR) under sections 308 (2) (extortion), 308 (5) (extortion by putting a person in fear of death or grievous hurt), 351 (2) (criminal intimidation), and 61 (criminal conspiracy) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
The FIR was filed at the Sector 5 Police Station in Panchkula on Tuesday based on the complaint filed by Bhagwan, popularly known as Rocky Mittal. Two Panchkula residents, Amit Bindal and a woman, and an unknown person have also been booked in the matter.
According to Rocky Mittal’s police complaint, the woman called him on his WhatsApp number on January 21 and January 22. “When I made a call to the woman, she asked for Rs 50 lakh for a compromise in the gangrape case. When I refused the money, she threatened [me with] dire consequences,” alleged Mittal.

headline: Families of two Punjab deportees say no idea how and when they reached US
description: Hotel management graduate who shifted to Italy on work permit last year; woman who moved to UK on study visa
content:
As a US military aircraft carrying 104 illegal immigrants from India landed in Amritsar Wednesday, at least two families in Punjab expressed shock and confusion on finding names of their kin in the list of the deportees.
While the family of Sukhpal Singh, a 35-year-old man from Darapur in Punjab’s Hoshiarpur district was under the impression that he was in Italy, where he had been sent on a work permit, that of 21-year-old Muskan, a resident of Jagraon town in Ludhiana, believed that she was in the UK, where she had moved to a year ago to pursue higher studies.
The deportees sent to Amritsar in the C-17 Globemaster aircraft of the US Air Force included 33 each from Haryana and Gujarat, 30 from Punjab, three each from Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, and two from Chandigarh.
Among the illegal immigrants hailing from Punjab, six are from Kapurthala, five from Amritsar, four each from Patiala and Jalandhar, two each from Hoshiarpur, Ludhiana, SBS Nagar and one each from Gurdaspur, Tarn Taran, Sangrur, SAS Nagar and Fatehgarh Sahib, as per official sources.

In Hoshiarpur, Sukhpal’s family got a rude shock when they found his name and passport number listed among those of the deportees. A hotel management graduate, Sukhpal had moved to Italy last year, his father Prempal Singh, a retired education department official, said.
“We sent him to Italy in October 2024 and he was supposed to work there. The last time I spoke to him was on January 15. At that time, he was still in Italy. After that, we lost contact. We have no idea how he ended up in the US. We were not even aware of him having made any such plans,” said Prempal Singh.
The family, he said, does not own any land and have limited financial resources. “Sukhpal had been working in a restaurant in India, earning around Rs 25,000 a month. We were struggling. When our relatives in Italy sponsored his work permit, we sent him abroad, hoping that it would lead to a stable future for him and us,” said the father. “But now, we don’t understand why he left Italy or how he reached the US border. It makes no sense. He could have settled in Italy. Why did he risk his life and everything and get deported like this? I am really shocked”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
At the time of going to press, the family was yet to to talk to Sukhpal about the money he may have spent on journey. Sukhpal, who is married with two children — an 11-year-old daughter and an 8-year-old son — was late in the evening sent home in a Punjab Police vehicle.
A nearly similar story played out in Jagraon when Muskan’s family was informed that she too has been deported from the US. Her father Jagdish Kumar, who runs a dhaba, said, “I got to know only today at around 5 pm that she has landed at Amritsar airport”.
Jagdish said Muskan had moved to the UK around a year ago on a study visa. Muskan’s phone had been coming switched off for almost 10 days, he said, adding, “We have no idea why she tried to move to the US. I am also not aware if she paid any money to any agent for moving to the US”.
He said all the details will be clear once Muskan returns home. “For now, we are relieved that she is safe and returning home,” said the father.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
After landing at Amritsar at 1.55 pm, the deportees were questioned inside the airport terminal building by different government agencies. After completing the formalities, the deportees from Punjab were sent to their respective hometowns in Punjab Police vehicles.
Punjab NRI Affairs minister Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal, who met some of the deportees at the airport, said, “Paperwork of deportees hailing from Punjab was done in the first batch. Thereafter, the immigration process of those from Haryana, Gujarat and other states was carried out”.

headline: Auto-rickshaw driver, 2 cops help reunite mentally unstable 12-year-old boy with family
description: The Dariya Police Post (PP) incharge in Chandigarh has recommended a commendation certificate for the auto driver, Ajay Kumar, and two policemen -- Senior Constable Nikesh and ?Constable Ajay -- for timely action in this regard.
content:
An auto-rickshaw driver and two policemen have helped reunite a mentally unstable 12-year-old missing boy with his family.
The Dariya Police Post (PP) incharge in Chandigarh has recommended a commendation certificate for the auto driver, Ajay Kumar, and two policemen — Senior Constable Nikesh and Constable Ajay — for timely action in this regard.
As per the police post incharge, on February 3, 2025, a police naka was set up at Garcha Light Point, where an auto-rickshaw bearing registration number CH01TA0743 was stopped by the naka party. Upon being stopped, the auto driver informed the police that the boy sitting in his vehicle was crying at the Railway Light Point and had requested to be dropped at the railway station. However, when the driver enquired further about the child’s destination, the boy was unable to provide a clear or satisfactory response, raising concerns about his well-being. Understanding the gravity of the situation, the naka party promptly took the child to a safe public space to make him comfortable.
Noticing that the child appeared scared and confused, the police officials spoke to him amicably and with great patience, ensuring that he felt safe and comfortable. It was only after this empathetic and well-natured approach that the boy revealed his arm, where a mobile number (6283623442) was permanently engraved. The police immediately contacted the number, which was answered by Amar Verma, the boy’s father, who informed them that his son had been missing since morning and was mentally ill.

headline: Trafficked and tortured in Myanmar, Hyderabad man now languishes in Thailand jail; family seeks MEA intervention
description: Shaik Ashraf’s family said his wife borrowed Rs 3.5 lakh to pay off a Myanmar company involved in an internet scam operation to secure his release.
content:
A woman from Hyderabad has appealed to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) to help bring back her husband languishing in a Thailand jail. The Thailand Police arrested Shaik Ashraf, 36, upon his entry from Myanmar, where he was allegedly trafficked for internet scam operations by a company.
According to his family, Ashraf, a resident of the Afsar Khan colony near Hyderabad’s Golconda, went to Dubai in search of a job in August 2023. Over there, he was allegedly lured by a Chinese travel agency who promised a job in an IT company in Thailand. In August 2024, he flew from Dubai to Bangkok, where he was allegedly received by another agent, who took him to Mae Sot, another city in Thailand. Ashraf’s family said he was taken in a boat to an undisclosed location and asked to engage in internet scams as a job.
“After six months he was trapped and after three months of my complaint we received an email from Ministry of External Affairs, Govt of India that Shaik Ashraf is in custody of Thailand Police and no assurance has bee given to rescue him. Kindly ask the Indian Embassy in Thailand to rescue him and bring back home as soon as possible,” said social worker Amjed Ullah Khan said in a letter to External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar Thursday. The MEA is yet to respond to the letter from Khan.
.@DrSJaishankar Sir, One Shaik Ashraf resident of H No: 9-3-58/B/124/AK/99, Afsar Khan Colony, Langar House, Golconda, Hyderabad, Telangana State holder of Passport No: R2088006 who went to Dubai, UAE during Aug 2023 but could not find any job there. He was lured by a Chinese… pic.twitter.com/KTA0bGaC7v
— Amjed Ullah Khan MBT (@amjedmbt) February 4, 2025
The family said whenever Ashraf refused to do the scam job, he was tortured physically in Myanmar. Social worker Amjed Ullah Khan said the company demanded $5,000 to release him. In November 2024, Khan wrote to the Indian embassies in Thailand, Myanmar, and Cambodia to rescue Ashraf.
The family said with no support from the Union government, Ashraf’s wife Jabeen Sultana borrowed Rs 3.5 lakh and paid off the company to release her husband. However, the Thailand Police arrested him as soon as he entered the country from Myanmar and sent him to jail.

headline: How a municipality in Panchmahal recycled 6,000-kg seized plastic into garden tiles
description: The stash was part of the 850 tonne of single use plastic (SUP) seized from two trucks from the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) area under the jurisdiction of Halol Municipality.
content:
As part of a pilot project showing alternatives to dispose of plastic waste, the Panchmahal district’s Halol Municipality has recycled 6,000-kg plastic into 3,295 sq feet of garden tiles with zero carbon footprint.
The stash was part of the 850 tonne of single use plastic (SUP) seized from two trucks from the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) area under the jurisdiction of Halol Municipality.
The SUP was seized on January 21 during a drive initiated on the directions of Gujarat Pollution Control Board (GPCB), dated January 16, under Section 5 of Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, for enforcement of ban on SUP. Accordingly, the officials of GPCB, revenue department along with police raided the plastic production units in Halol.
Halol Municipality Chief Officer Hiral Thakar told The Indian Express, “We confiscated 850 tonnes of SUP, under 20 microns thickness, from about 24 production units. The panchnama in the case was conducted by the officials of the revenue department as GIDC is a special revenue area”.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
“After following the due process of confiscating illegal goods, the Municipality took custody of the stash. Since it is an illegal product, as per law, it has to be destroyed. The SUPs were 20 microns, way under the stipulated thickness of 120 microns and also had no information of production unit, GST details and so on that are now mandatory as per law. The disposal of SUP always raises environmental concerns, so we decided to recycle some of the plastic into garden tiles,” said Thakar.
The Halol Municipality has recycled 6,000 kilos of SUP to make 3,295 pieces of garden tiles, of one foot each, and weighing 3.5 kg each.
The Municipality has partnered with Gandhinagar-based Saltech Design Labs, a start-up for waste recycling and reuse, to make a composite material using SUP and industrial dust (flyash).
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Pilot project
Thakar said, “We gave them 6,343 kg of SUP as a pilot, which was mixed with 5,190 kg of ash filler in a 55:45 ratio to create the tiles. Not only are these tiles sturdy, they are also cost-effective as they turn out to be cheaper by Rs 18 compared to cement blocks of the same size. Moreover, it also helps in reusing flyash, which poses the same question of disposal in industries. Thus, the total carbon reduction amounts to a significant 17,414 kilos.”
The start-up is among those recommended under the Swachh Bharat Mission for use of the technology that has been patented in seven countries, he said. “The start-up has also fitted about 17,000 square feet of similar tiles in the Pandit Deendayal Energy University (previously, Pandit Deendayal Petroleum University), which is the alma mater of the start-up founder Aditya Shukla,” Thakar said, adding, “We now have a pilot ready as an example to show how SUP and industrial dust can be reused to reduce carbon emission.”Thakar estimates that reusing the entire 850 ton of confiscated SUP would create tiles to cover a space of 4.21 lakh square feet and cut down carbon dioxide emission by 2,172 tonnes.
The Halol Municipality, on January 30, had also received the approval of the Mission Director of the Gujarat Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) for a “Waste to Value project”.
Under the project, the Municipality proposes to reuse plastic and rubber waste, generated in its area, which is dominated by industrial units by turning it into “reusable items”.   Thakar added, “Since the last two years, we have been attempting to cut down on single- use plastic in the jurisdiction. Every time we raid vendors, they ask us why don’t we stop production.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“The other way of disposing of the SUPs is to send them to the cement factory furnace for burning but we have been working on the project for the last few months to put them to use by blending them with some agent and generating value out of waste… We have considered making blocks, drainage covers, benches, and also a monolith,” she said.
Monolith at Jyoti Circle
A monolith, currently commissioned to the same start-up, will soon be put up at Jyoti Circle in Halol town, giving out the message of reusing waste as part of the project of the Municipality. Thakar said, “It will have a message, ‘I am not part of plastic waste and I am honored to welcome you’ and help us push the campaign.”
“So far, the manufacturers of SUP have been taking advantage of the fact that no one would take responsibility for the muddamal (seized criminal material) and, thus, it would be returned to them. But now that we have a pilot (project) and we can show that this can be done with confiscated waste, it will become an example. The confiscated illegal material is worth Rs 15.5 crore if they are sold to vendors at a cost of Rs 180 per kg,” she said.
Thakar added that they are exploring legal action against the production units under the Environment (Protection) Act, once the ongoing Municipality polls are completed.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
She said, “This is, perhaps, the first time in the state that we have confiscated illegal SUP from production units. Usually, drives are conducted to confiscate the SUPs from vendors but this case will be an example to stop the production. We have sought opinion from GPCB and the Urban Development Department to proceed with this model of recycling…”
“We will also lodge FIRs after seeking the opinion of the state legal department. The local police have already lodged an FIR against 35 people for trying to obstruct the work, we had undertaken during the drive, by cornering the officers,” she added.

headline: Sold to buyer of another faith despite objections, Surat woman’s property sealed under Disturbed Areas Act
description: Residents of the seller’s society complained about the sale to district Collectorate officials, say sources
content:
A woman in the walled city area of Surat, who had sold off her property to another woman of a different faith, found her property sealed by the authorities earlier this week for allegedly failing to comply with the provisions of the Disturbed Areas Act.
According to sources, the action took place after the residents of the seller’s housing society objected to the sale and complained about it to Surat district Collectorate officials.
According to details received from sources at the District Collectorate’s revenue department, a few weeks ago, a woman staying in a residential society in Salabatpura had sold her property to another woman. The buyer, who is also a resident of Salabatpura, had even received the token amount from the seller.
However, when the residents of the society where the property is situated learnt about the deal, they raised an objection on the grounds of the buyer’s religion, said sources. The property owner, though, stuck to her decision and accepted the final property sale deal amount. She then began the process of getting land sale deed documents made.

As the area falls under the Disturbed Areas Act, the woman filed an application with the authorities for approval.
Under the Disturbed Areas Act, statements from local residents are taken by officials and police who make on-the-spot visits. During one such visit, the local residents objected to the sale before the Mamlatdar and the police. Following this, the City Prant official, Neha Savani, rejected the woman’s application for approval.
However, despite this, the owner handed over the possession of the property to the buyer. Following this, the society residents submitted an application to the Surat city Prant office, expressing their objection to the deal. They stated that the seller’s actions violated the norms of the Disturbed Areas Act’s sections 5a and b.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
City Prant officer Savani then directed Katargam Mamlatdar to seal the property. Earlier this week, the Mamlatdar and his team, accompanied by Salabatpura police, reached the property and sealed it off.
Talking to The Indian Express, Prant officer Sawani said, “The Mamlatdar had sealed off the property as the seller had violated the sections of Disturbed Areas Act, and handed the property to the buyer. We have checked and found out that no sale deed documents were prepared by the owner.”
The owner and the buyer could not be contacted for comment.
The 1991 Gujarat Prohibition of Transfer of Immovable Property and Provision for Protection of Tenants from Premises in Disturbed Areas Act empowers the administration to declare parts of the territorial jurisdiction as “disturbed” in the context of communal clashes, prohibiting the direct sale of property between people of different faiths unless it is cleared by the Collector’s office, who has to certify that the transaction involves free consent.

As part of the process, the administration interacts with neighbours to make sure that there is no coercion or threat involved in the sale.

headline: AI-based attack responsible for Kaveri portal crash, suspects Karnataka Stamps and Registration Department
description: The Stamps and Registration Department will file a cyber crime complaint after receiving the relevant details about the suspected Artificial Intelligence-based Distributed Denial of Service attack from the Department of E-governance.
content:
Karnataka government officials Wednesday blamed a suspected Artificial Intelligence-based Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attack for the recent crash of the Kaveri portal.
The Stamps and Registration (SR) Department, which handles the Kaveri portal, has sought assistance from the Department of E-governance to track those responsible for the disruption in the software. The SR Department will file a cyber crime complaint after receiving the relevant details about the suspected DDoS attack.
Dayananda K A, Inspector General of Registration and Commissioner of Stamps, told The Indian Express that the portal was hit after it was flooded with a series of search requests for documents such as Encumbrance Certificate (EC).
“The Kaveri portal has a provision to search for property registration documents, meant to assist the public. Though the search strength of the portal is around 2.5 lakh queries per day, by making use of AI some elements have piled the portal with around 20 lakh searches,” he said.

After Vivek Joshi’s appointment as EC, Haryana gets new Chief Secretary
This caused pressure on the software causing technical issues for the public accessing the portal and also at sub-registrar offices during property registration, according to Dayanand.
On Wednesday evening, the SR Department issued a release noting that the “Kaveri 2.0 application which was affected by a DDoS attack from last one week has now been fully restored and is operating normally.” The worst-hit day during the period when the portal was down was on February 1 when the number of property registrations dropped to 556. This was in contrast to the 8,500-9,000 registrations done daily using the portal.
After the Department initiated interim measures, property registration numbers improved to 5,243 on February 3, said the Department. A day later, on Tuesday (February 4), the application crashed again and fresh steps were taken to restore the application. The portal was restored by Wednesday evening with total registrations reaching 7,225 with a revenue of around Rs 62.59 crore.

“For context, the average figures for December 2024 was 7,721 registrations and revenue collection of Rs 62.93 cr. These numbers clearly indicate that registration activity has returned to normal levels,” the Department added in the statement.
Department data shows that the portal fared the worst due to the DDoS attack during the first three working days of February. Revenue generated by property registration on February 1 was Rs 15.18 crore, Rs 52.24 crore on February 3, and Rs 17.13 crore on February 4.

headline: Mumbai police book UP resident for giving triple talaq to wife over phone
description: The complainant said she approached the Ghatkopar police in Mumbai after learning that the accused had remarried.
content:
Mumbai police Tuesday booked an Uttar Pradesh resident for allegedly giving ‘triple talaq’ to his wife over the phone, a practice made punishable by a 2019 law. The man’s brother and sister-in-law were named as co-accused in the First Information Report (FIR).
The complainant said her husband called her in June last year and pronounced talaq thrice, saying, “Ho gaya game khatam (The game is over)”, before hanging up.
Investigators said the prime accused, Shehbaz Ahmed, remarried later following which his first wife approached the Ghatkopar police and registered the FIR under section 4 (pronouncing talaq in spoken, written or electronic form) of the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights of Marriage) Act 2019 in addition to relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

headline: Parents of victim in R G Kar rape-murder seek time as Calcutta High Court weighs reinvestigation
description: The state government, meanwhile, submitted a report asserting that it had “no role” in the investigation.
content:
The parents of the victim in the R G Kar Medical College rape-murder case have sought additional time from the Calcutta High Court regarding its decision to order a reinvestigation.
Their counsel, Gargi Goswami, informed the court: “We had appealed to the Supreme Court asking whether the single bench of Calcutta High Court has the liberty to hear the matter. The matter will be heard this week in Supreme Court; thus, we are praying for time.”
The state government, meanwhile, submitted a report asserting that it had “no role” in the investigation.
The parents of the deceased doctor initially approached the High Court in December 2024, expressing distrust in the Central Bureau of Investigation’s (CBI) probe. Their counsel argued that key evidence had been lost and urged for a fresh investigation. However, Justice Tirthankar Ghosh, presiding over the single bench, deferred action, seeking clarification from the Supreme Court, given that an earlier division bench had assigned the case to the CBI and mandated progress reports.

headline: ‘A moment of divine connection’: PM Modi visits Maha Kumbh, takes a dip at Triveni Sangam
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi was among the nearly 55 lakh people who took a dip at the Maha Kumbh Mela at Uttar Pradesh’s Prayagraj by Wednesday noon.
content:
Maha Kumbh Mela Updates: Wearing a saffron-coloured jacket, blue track pants and a ‘rudraksha’ chain around his neck, Prime Minister Narendra Modi took a holy dip at the Triveni Sangam on Wednesday and offered prayers to Goddess Ganga. PM Modi was among the nearly 55 lakh people who took a dip at the Maha Kumbh Mela at Uttar Pradesh’s Prayagraj by noon.
After arriving at the Prayagraj airport at around 10 am, PM Modi reached Arail Ghat and went to the Sangam Nose – the strip of land at the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and the mythical Saraswati – in a boat along with UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Later, PM Modi ventured into the water alone, took a dip at the Sangam and recited mantras.
“Blessed to be at the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj. The Snana at the Sangam is a moment of divine connection, and like the crores of others, who have taken part in it, I was also filled with a spirit of devotion. May Maa Ganga bless all with peace, wisdom, good health and harmony,” PM Modi said in a post on X, soon after taking the dip.
Officials said that during his visit, PM Modi offered “Arghya” to the sun god and offered prayers to the Ganga, Yamuna and Saraswati rivers. After the dip in the Sangam, PM Modi performed a puja wearing a black kurta, a saffron stole and a Himachali cap.

headline: Ensure infra, reserve beds for GBS patients, hospitals told
description: Reporting all GBS cases immediately to Swasthya Bhawan among guidelines
content:
Following three fatalities in the state due to Guillain-Barre Syndrome (GBS), the state Health department on Tuesday issued a directive to all government hospitals and medical colleges to establish necessary infrastructure to effectively manage and treat GBS cases.
Guidelines have been issued on how to handle GBS cases and immediately report to the Swasthya Bhawan in case any GBS patient comes to their hospital, said sources.
According to sources in the health department a virtual meeting was held on Sunday by the Health Secretary Narayan Swaroop Nigam enquiring about how well the hospitals are prepared in case there is a rise in the number of GBS cases and the health officials also enquired the number of patients currently affected with GBS.
Sources said that all hospitals and medical colleges have been asked to ensure that all necessary medical assistance such as plasma therapy, ventilation support systems and intravenous immunoglobulin injections is available.

Additionally, child specialist doctors have been briefed on the symptoms of GBS in children, enabling timely identification and treatment.
Meanwhile, the experts have informed the state health department that the situation currently is under control and there is no reason to panic.

headline: As technicians ‘stay away’ from his set, TV serial director finds support from colleagues
description: Roy's latest film project has been stalled as a result of the alleged boycott.  Roy denied the allegations against him in a Facebook Live session on Tuesday, expressing concern over the “unfair treatment” some filmmakers face in Bengal.
content:
SEVERAL FILMMAKERS on Tuesday assembled at a studio in Kolkata to express solidarity with an industry colleague at whose set work has been affected since February 3 as all technicians associated with the project are allegedly staying away.
Although the views of the technicians on this alleged boycott were not available, the director concerned, Srijit Roy, claimed that it could probably be certain remarks attributed to him that were purportedly against the technicians’ federation chief, Swarup Biswas.
Roy, however, claimed he did not make any unsavoury remark against Biswas, who is the brother of West Bengal minister and senior Trinamool Congress leader Arup Biswas.
Roy’s latest film project has been stalled as a result of the alleged boycott.  Roy denied the allegations against him in a Facebook Live session on Tuesday, expressing concern over the “unfair treatment” some filmmakers face in Bengal.

Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
This is the second time that Tollygunge’s entertainment industry is facing yet another production crisis, just six months after a similar conflict. The situation has sparked a war of words between industry figures and political leaders.
The set construction work for Roy’s serial began on January 27, but underlying tensions reportedly existed earlier as well. On Monday night, portions of the set were allegedly destroyed and technicians have since refused to work.
“I  am still trying to understand…The Chief Minister [Mamata Banerjee] has repeatedly said that there cannot be stoppage of work at any cost, but why is this [situation] being repeated,”  said director Raj Chakraborty, who is also a TMC MLA.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Chakraborty emphasised Roy’s long-standing contributions to the industry, which provides livelihoods for hundreds of technicians. He called for “dialogue and internal resolution” rather than involving the CM in every issue
“He (Roy) has been working in this industry for 15-20 years. Nearly 400 technicians also earn their livelihood through it. However, we should not rush to the CM for every single thing. Resolve issues through dialogue,” he said.
“We don’t know on whose instructions the technicians are stopping work, despite the CM’s directive. Roy is a big name. For the past two days, technicians have not been coming to his set. During the previous such conflict, in July last year, the CM said a committee would be formed but this is yet to be done,” said actor Parambrata Chatterjee.
Roy claimed that the technicians are demanding an apology from him before they resume work, but questioned what he had done wrong. “We don’t know on whose instruction technicians are stopping work. Someone must be instructing them,” claimed Roy.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Roy denied allegations of misbehaviour, saying, “False allegations are being made against me. Why is it being said that I have misbehaved? If the set-making work stops, they (technicians) are the ones who will be in trouble. So if they suddenly stop working, it will affect their lives.”
Meanwhile, BJP leader Samik Bhattacharya criticised the TMC, claiming they “harmed lesser-known directors too and created an environment of uncertainty by demanding filmmakers’ subservience.”
“The TMC has spoiled the career of small-time directors who make low budget projects. When TMC demands that filmmakers should bow down before them, it will lead to such uncertainty.”
TMC leader Kunal Ghosh said that such issues within the industry should be “resolved internally through discussion. “There is no need to politicise such matters,” said TMC leader Kunal Ghosh
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
According to sources, members of the Directors Association are visiting the studio to take stock of the situation. There is concern that the stand-off could escalate, potentially leading to a complete shutdown of serial production from Wednesday if the technicians’ demands are not met. Such a widespread stoppage would severely impact Tollygunge’s entertainment industry.
DAEI ( Director’s Association of Eastern India) secretary Sudeshna Roy said, “This is repeatedly happening, who is stopping them to work and why they are doing so. In the past 15 days, three people’s work have been stopped in between. It is unfortunate and  difficult to work like this. When a similar situation cropped up a few months ago, three part of our industry – Dev, Prosenjit Chatterjee and Goutam Ghosh – met the CM. The CM had clearly said she doesnt support strike or cease work. We appeal to those who had met the CM last time… We were asked to wait for sometime for a permanent solution,” she said.  – WITH PTI INPUTS

headline: 26% roads concretised: BMC allocates Rs 3,111 crore to complete project by next fiscal
description: In February 2023, the BMC had issued work orders for concretisation of 324km of road length/ 698 roads in Mumbai at a cost of Rs 6,000 crore.
content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has allocated Rs 3,111 crore for concretising roads in Mumbai in its budget for the 2025-26 financial year.
Two years after work orders were issued for concretising roads, data furnished from the civic budget revealed that the civic authorities have been able to achieve only 26 per cent of the total work till date.
In February 2023, the BMC had issued work orders for concretisation of 324km of road length/ 698 roads in Mumbai at a cost of Rs 6,000 crore. This project was the brainchild of former Chief Minister Eknath Shinde who had proposed completion of this project in two years and making Mumbai ‘pothole-free’.
Meanwhile, the civic body said so far, only 187 roads or 26 per cent of the proposed road length have been concretised so far.

“Even though the work orders were issued in February 2023, the actual work on ground could only begin by October of that year which went on till monsoon arrived in the first half of June. Since civil works couldn’t be taken up during monsoon, the rest of work could only begin after October. As a result, the progress has been slow,” Abhijit Bangar, additional municipal commissioner (Projects) told The Indian Express on Tuesday.
“The contractors who were awarded the work were new in Mumbai and they took time in acquiring permission. These factors also affected the progress of work. However, things have been streamlined now and work is going on at full pace,” Bangar added.
In his budget speech, municipal commissioner and state-appointed administrator Bhushan Gagrani said the civic body aims to achieve 75 per cent of this project by the next financial year.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Meanwhile, in a separate work order issued in December 2024, the BMC initiated concretisation of 377km of road length or 720 different roads in Mumbai. In his budget speech, Gagrani said that in the next financial year, the BMC is set to achieve 50 per cent of this work as well.
“The concretisation work is going on full swing and we have instructed all the contractors to mobilise all their resources to ensure the project deadline is met. We also have received guidance from IIT-Bombay experts to ensure quality and proper standard of work is being maintained,” said Gagrani.
“We have been hearing from sources that some people are facing inconvenience, owing to road concretisation works, even though we haven’t received any formal complaint yet. However, we will consider to mitigate any inconvenience faced by citizens if they are raised formally,” said Gagrani.
In total, for the roads and traffic department, BMC has allocated Rs 5,100 crore for multiple infrastructure projects, an increase of Rs 989 crore from last year. Under this, the civic body has proposed a Mumbai walkability project in which it aims to improve footpaths in the city to increase accessibility. The BMC has also earmarked Rs 200 crore for constructing two multi-level robotic car parking facilities that will come up at Flora Fountain and Worli.

headline: Haryana’s anti-drug campaign goes viral, draws over 2.5 million views
description: #NashaMuktJeevanBucketChallenge sees unprecedented digital engagement, sparking global comparisons
content:
The #NashaMuktJeevanBucketChallenge, a brainchild of DGP OP Singh, who helms the  Haryana State Narcotics Control Bureau (HSNCB), has emerged as one of India’s most widely engaged anti-drug awareness campaigns, gaining significant traction across Haryana’s digital space. In just one week, the campaign has recorded:
A reach of over 2.5 million
More than five lakh impressions
Over four lakh likes, shares, and comments
Fifty-plus user-generated challenge videos
Over one million influencer-driven views
A senior officer of Haryana State Narcotics Control Bureau (HSNCB). The  level of engagement is unprecedented for a state-led digital campaign and indicates strong public support for the fight against drug abuse. With Anti-Drug Day on July 26 set as the campaign’s culmination, it is on track to match some of the most successful global social media-driven anti-drug efforts.
How it compares globally
The campaign’s rapid rise places it alongside international anti-drug initiatives. The US-based “Truth Initiative,” which has reached over 800 million people, and the UK’s “Talk to Frank” programme, which receives over 1.2 million website visitors annually, are among the most successful campaigns. However, unlike these long-running efforts, #NashaMuktJeevanBucketChallenge has gained substantial engagement in just a week.
What sets it apart
The campaign’s growth has been notably swift compared to global counterparts, which took months to reach peak engagement. With 90 per cent of participation from Haryana, Delhi, and Punjab, the initiative maintains a targeted approach, ensuring the message reaches high-risk areas.

headline: In the biggest contest of its political life, how AAP framed the fight for Delhi
description: If, in 2015, AAP volunteers stood apart for their signature white caps, now they sported yellow and blue scarves.
content:
AS THE campaign for the Delhi Assembly elections drew to a close Monday, it also brought the curtains down on a poll that will reverberate far beyond the 70 seats at stake. A return to power will mean a giant victory for the AAP, after surviving the jailing of its entire top brass, and against a party like the BJP that few have been able to so successfully withstand for so long.
Another BJP win, on the other hand, will put the AAP’s ability to bounce back under severe stress.
But, whatever happens come February 8, the AAP cannot be accused of not trying. Long before other parties turned their attention to Delhi, AAP workers hit the ground, trying to repair the cracks in its support base.
Said a senior party leader: “We started campaigning in September itself. In a way, this has perhaps been our longest and most intense election campaign, and most similar to the one we executed in 2015.”
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Read | BJP’s capital hope: AAP vehicle for change stuck – at the bottom
The leader added that a considered decision was taken to not hold big rallies but go door-to-door, like the then fledgling party did 10 years ago. “Kejriwal ji addressed at least three jansabhas a day, alongside campaigning in his own constituency, New Delhi. Big rallies distract MLAs and suck up resources. Our focus was on reaching the voter on the ground.”
AAP leader Arvind Kejriwal takes part in a roadshow in Kalkaji. (Express photo by Tashi Tobgyal)
Alongside Kejriwal was Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and AAP Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh.
This was in contrast to Prime Minister Modi’s four large rallies and the BJP’s mega electoral machine which saw BJP president J P Nadda, Home Minister Amit Shah, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, and all BJP state chief ministers, including Yogi Adityanath, Himanta Biswa Sarma and Pushkar Dhami, campaigning for several days.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Read | Delhi Assembly elections: At bottom of income ladder, AAP secure, wobbles as voters climb up
On how 2015 was similar, a senior AAP leader said: “People’s hearts had to be won all over again then. We had to make them believe we were not a one-time wonder… This time too, we were cornered… which is why we went back to the basics.”
If, in 2015, AAP volunteers stood apart for their signature white caps, now they sported yellow and blue scarves. Also, the ragtag volunteer group of that time acquired a more defined shape in the form of 250 “winners” – comprising AAP councillors, MLAs, including from Punjab, and campaign managers with a track record of winning seats.
Read | EC tells agencies to keep close eye on distribution of cash and inducements among Delhi voters
“The 250 people were in charge of polling booths. They did not report to AAP candidates but to the leadership on a daily basis. Strategy was changed after their inputs,” a party leader said.
From the start of December till the first week of January, AAP leaders staged Ramlilas, where its prominent MLAs such as Saurabh Bharadwaj, Somnath Bharti, Sanjeev Jha and others held regular meetings with people. The Ramlilas also tied in with the urban Hindu image that the AAP has been trying to court, especially since 2019, to fight the BJP.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Read | Posters to pep talks: Targeted messaging at heart of BJP’s grassroots campaign for Delhi polls
Further, the AAP ensured that it did not disintegrate, as the BJP had counted on, after high-profile arrests, including Kejriwal and his deputy CM Manish Sisodia, among others. Instead, Kejriwal held the moral high ground by choosing to serve out his time in jail as CM, and then quitting unexpectedly after he was released. Come elections, he was back as the party’s CM face.
Kejriwal also went big on the AAP’s popular welfare schemes, not shying away from the “revdi” charge made by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The AAP promised not just to fulfill its government’s budget promise of Rs 1,000 for women under the age of 60 who do not pay taxes, but also announced that if returned to power, it would increase this to Rs 2,100.
To preempt a possible BJP offensive on not fulfilling its initial promise, the AAP went to work in October. “We formed 5,000 teams of women who went neighbourhood to neighbourhood, talking to groups of 15-20 women about the benefits they would get from a Kejriwal government,” an AAP leader said. The teams also informed the women how the BJP government at the Centre via the Lieutenant Governor had stalled its functioning.
It had several examples to make this charge stick. Like the ordinance by the Centre nullifying a May 2023 Supreme Court order said that the Services Department, which governs the bureaucracy, should come under the control of the elected Delhi government and not the Lt Governor.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Closer to the elections, after AAP volunteers hit the ground as part of a “registration” drive for the Rs 2,100 dole for women, senior officers in the Delhi government released public notices and disowned the process. A party leader said they banked on the public to see through such BJP measures.
If “freebies” was one aspect of this, the other was the push for the middle class, after the AAP sensed that this group was turning away from it. So, midway through its campaign, it changed tack. In addition to talking about its social welfare schemes and promises, the AAP called for revision of income tax brackets, including zero tax for those earning less than Rs 10 lakh a year – timing it to the run-up to the Union Budget.
So, when the Budget actually made landmark changes, including no tax for those earning up to Rs 12 lakh per annum, the AAP claimed it as its “victory”.
Irrespective of the result, Kejriwal would also have shown the strength of his image surviving at least two high-profile campaigns against him – over the alleged excise policy scam and the so-called ‘Sheesh Mahal’ built under him. Several high-profile associates who left Kejriwal over the past few years, the biggest being former transport minister Kailash Gahlot, also added to this clamour against the AAP chief.

headline: In BMC Budget 2025 of Rs 74,427 crore, key focus on infrastructure growth
description: The largest allocation of Rs 5,545 crore was assigned for the construction of seven Sewage Treatment Plants in the BMC Budget 2025.
content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) Tuesday announced a budget of Rs 74,427 crore for the financial year 2025-26 — exceeding last fiscal’s revised estimate of Rs 65,180 crore by 14.19 per cent.
This year’s budget was presented by Bhushan Gagrani, BMC Commissioner and state-appointed administrator, who took charge in March 2024. This was also the third consecutive year when the civic body’s budget was presented by the administrator, after the general body of elected representatives was dissolved in March 2022.
Of the total budget size, Rs 43,162 crore have been earmarked for capital expenditure, and Rs 31,204 crore have been set aside as revenue expenditure. For FY 2025-26, a lion’s share of funding has been allocated to enhance some of the key infrastructure projects meant to strengthen the city’s outlook.
The highest allocation of Rs 5,545 crore was made for the Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project (MSDP), which is executing the project of constructing seven Sewage Treatment Plants (STP) in Mumbai. These plants will become operational between 2026 and 2028 in a phased manner.

headline: Karnataka implements special learning measures to boost SSLC pass rate, no grace marks this year
description: Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa has said his department is implementing innovative study models and technology-driven invigilation to ensure better results.
content:
With Karnataka’s SSLC examinations for Class 10 students scheduled to be held from March 21 to April 4, the state government has rolled out a series of structured learning initiatives aimed at improving student performance and increasing the overall success rate. This comes following a disappointing pass percentage of SSLC students last year.
Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa on Monday announced the department is implementing innovative study models, additional coaching, and technology-driven invigilation to ensure better results while maintaining exam integrity.
“I am optimistic about SSLC results in view of the innovative and strategic academic measures introduced this year. Some districts are performing exceptionally well, while others need improvement, but I am confident we will see an overall increase in success rates,” Bangarappa told reporters here.
In order to help students prepare effectively, several districts have adopted unique strategies tailored to improve learning outcomes. It includes the ‘One Day, One Mark’ programme encouraging students to study one question every day, ensuring systematic preparation over time. “This approach has been implemented in districts like Yadgir and we expect the other districts to emulate the same,” Bangarappa said.

The government has also introduced a ‘buddy learning system’ where students are paired with peers, allowing underperformers to study with high scorers, promoting collaborative learning. Additionally, as a wake-up call, teachers will personally call students early in the morning, encouraging them to begin their studies on time. “Additional remedial sessions are also being conducted for students who struggle with key subjects,” said Bangarappa.
In a rare move, Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) in some districts have taken on teaching responsibilities to motivate students and teachers alike, Bangarappa said. Many districts have also conducted trial exams, allowing students to experience real exam conditions while ensuring strict monitoring via webcasting.
No grace marks this year, strict monitoring to continue
Despite efforts to support students academically, Bangarappa confirmed that no grace marks would be awarded this year. Last year, the state had granted 10 per cent grace marks after a drastic drop in pass percentage due to stricter invigilation measures. However, Chief Minister Siddaramaiah has now directed that no such provision will be made this year.

Regarding the existing system of awarding minimal grace marks to students who narrowly miss passing, Bangarappa stated that the decision would be taken after discussions with department officials. “This is a sensitive issue, and we will assess whether modifications are necessary,” he added.
Webcasting to ensure exam integrity
The minister also defended the webcasting system introduced last year, which will remain in place for monitoring all SSLC exam centres. “Webcasting helps maintain fairness while also allowing us to evaluate students’ learning levels. It will be mandatory at every centre,” Bangarappa said.
Uncertainty over hijab at exam halls
When asked whether students would be allowed to wear the hijab during exams, Bangarappa said the matter is still in court, and a decision will be taken after consulting the Home Minister.
Study guide and timetable for students
The minister said that to further assist students, the education department has released a comprehensive study guide that includes marking schemes and probable question areas for each subject; memory techniques and study strategies to help students retain information effectively; a recommended 24-hour study timetable, advising students on a structured daily routine from 5 am to 11 pm and health and wellness tips, including suggestions for a balanced diet and proper sleep schedules.
