Police said Sandeep and Pardeep could not be traced later and were declared “proclaimed offenders”.
Family members of the cousins, meanwhile, claimed the two were “falsely implicated” in the case. “The boys were arrested by police before they could reach home from the airport,” said Satnam Singh, a relative. He also claimed that they had spent “approximately Rs 1.2 crore on arrangements” to send them abroad. “An agent had promised secure passage but instead routed the two through a jungle path,” he said.
Punjab Police DIG Mandeep Singh Sidhu (Patiala range) was not available for comment. Rajpura City police station SHO Balwinder Singh confirmed that Sandeep and Pardeep were produced in court and taken in remand. He said the two were among five men named as accused in connection with the incident of 2023 on charges including murder, attempt to murder and rioting.

“Both Pardeep Singh and Sandeep Sunny are cousins and they fled the country after they were booked for murder… The agent sent both through the Dunki (illegal) route and they were arrested by the US authorities and deported,” a police officer said.

headline: ‘It was for everyone’s safety’: US deportees speak about handcuffing, chains and emotional struggles
description: Many of the illegal immigrants who landed in Amritsar on a US military aircraft are struggling with depression, feelings of hopelessness and a deep sense of loss.
content:
After their arrival late on Saturday, some of the illegal immigrants deported from the US shared their experience of being handcuffed and chained during their 66-hour journey. Of the 117 deportees, the majority were men, all of whom were handcuffed and shackled, according to an official who received the deportees at Amritsar airport.
Some of the deportees said the restraints were meant to ensure the safety of the illegal immigrants who were in a state of desperation over shattered US dreams and that any untoward incident on the flight could potentially have dangerous consequences.
Mandeep Singh, 25, from Surkha village in the Bholath area of Kapurthala district, told The Indian Express, “Yes, we were handcuffed and chained just like the youth who were deported on February 5. It was like hell for around 66 hours. But it was for the safety of everyone deported because one cannot judge the state of mind of others, and anything may happen in desperation.”
“The US is simply following its laws. The officials are just doing their job, as they have to abide by their rules. I did not feel good when they handcuffed me and chained my legs, but they explained it was for everyone’s safety,” Mandeep said. “We are not in a good state mentally after being deported. Several of us are depressed. In such a condition, anything could happen. We were in a ‘do or die’ mode, and that kind of desperation could pose a danger not only to ourselves but to everyone on the plane. So, to avoid any potential chaos or harm, the officials had no choice but to chain us.”
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
“I was very happy that I entered the US but never imagined that I would be deported back like a criminal soon,” added Mandeep, who entered the US on January 27, adding that such deportations rarely happened in the past.
Mandeep had set out for the US six months ago and entered the country with high hopes, after paying an agent Rs 45 lakh and working on a “donkey route” for five and a half months. However, his dreams were shattered when he was taken to a detention centre by immigration officials. Mandeep now faces the challenge of dealing with the financial strain as well. His family and maternal uncle had borrowed a large sum to pay an agent to help him secure a passage to the US. He is now in the process of confronting the agent, demanding that either he pay the money back or face legal action.
Many of the deportees had expressed resentment toward the restraints.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The senior official said, “Only five deportees were women, who, along with children, were not shackled this time.”
According to the official, minimal food was given to the deportees and they had not bathed or brushed in fifteen days. “They were quite broken in spirit when they came back,” the official added.
Mantaj Singh, in his mid-20s from Bodal Chauni village in Dasuya, Hoshiarpur, said his paternal aunt, who is settled in the US, had paid a Dubai-based agent Rs 35 lakh to facilitate his journey. Mantaj, who spent three and a half months in a detention camp, recounted his experience of being shackled during his deportation. Like Mandeep, he initially resented the handcuffs and chains.
“It is not a pleasant experience, but when they (officials) explained that the handcuffs and chains were for our own safety during the flight, I understood. Anything could happen when so many people are in such a fragile emotional state, and the officials have to ensure everyone’s safety,” said Mantaj.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Many of them are struggling with depression, feelings of hopelessness and a deep sense of loss. They cried and behaved erratically at the airport. As all of us had only one dream, which was a better future in the US, we are now facing an uncertain future back home. Being caught in a foreign country, detained and then forcibly sent back to India is taking a significant toll on our mental well-being,” said Mandeep.
Nishan Singh, 19, of village Chakoki in Dhilwan (Kapurthala), is in deep depression after going through the “donkey route” six months ago. He said he did not want to talk to the media, which he said was interested only in their stories but no one understood their pain.
Political Pulse | Why US deportation flights to Amritsar have touched off a firestorm in Punjab
While Ankush Kailey of Phagwara refused to talk, Jashanpreet, 20, of Pandori Rajputan in Bholath, said, “Do not rub salt into our wounds now.”
Political uproar
After the first batch of illegal immigrants landed in Amritsar earlier this month, the Opposition raised an uproar in both Houses of Parliament over the manner in which the 104 Indians were deported, with some leaders wearing handcuffs to register their protest.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar then made a statement in both Houses on the matter, saying that deportations were not new. “We are, of course, engaging with the US government to ensure that the returning deportees are not mistreated in any manner during the flight.”
The standard operating procedure for deportations by aircraft used by the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement has been effective since 2012 and provides for “the use of restraints”, Jaishankar added.
While Jaishankar then said that as per US authorities, “women were not restrained”, the first batch of women deportees rejected this claim, saying that they too were handcuffed and shackled at the feet, just like their male counterparts. Only children were not physically restrained then.

headline: Know Your City: Gujarati tycoon who financed East India Company, gifted Arab horses to Shah Jahan
description: Virji Vora dealt with various goods, including opium, bullion, coral, cotton, pepper, ivory, and lead, and held a monopoly over many of these products.
content:
During the Mughal era, India was home to some of the wealthiest people from around the world who established their influence as business magnates and built companies that amassed great fortunes. One notable businessman from this period was Virji Vora, a Gujarati tycoon from Surat. Active from 1619 to the 1670s, he played a significant role in trade and social life within his community.
The East India Company (EIC) factory records describe Virji Vora as the richest merchant in the world during his time, referring to him as the “merchant prince.” According to EIC, his wealth was estimated at Rs 80 lakh, a staggering amount for that period.
Although little is known about his family background, scholars and historians have noted that he belonged to the Srimali Oswal Porwal caste. Due to his substantial involvement in religious matters, he was conferred with the title of Samajapati/Sanghavi, which is awarded to a lay leader who makes significant contributions, such as building a temple or organising a large-scale pilgrimage.
As a trader, he dealt with a wide range of goods, including opium, bullion, coral, cotton, pepper, ivory, and lead, and he held a monopoly on many of these products. Virji employed agents in most of India’s significant commercial hubs to manage his vast commercial empire and diverse business interests. His agents were located in Bharuch, Baroda (now Vadodara), Ahmedabad, Burhanpur, Golkonda, the Malabar region on the east coast, and Agra. Additionally, he had agents in the ports of the Persian Gulf, Red Sea and Southeast Asia.

Through these agents, Virji Vora’s hundis (promissory notes) were recognised as legal tender in various towns in India and abroad. The Dutch East India Company (DEIC) consistently used Virji Vora’s agents to remit money from Surat to Agra. Additionally, his agents largely managed letters of exchange between Surat and Ahmedabad. A significant portion of the funds transferred via hundis also went through Virji Vora’s agents. The principal money changer in Agra was one of his agents, and most of the borrowings by the DEIC were sourced from his network as well.
He was a significant credit provider to EIC and DEIC and their staff in their individual capacity. A shrewd banker, he was known to charge a high interest rate(1-1.5 per cent) per month, which the English often complained about. “The town [Surat] is very empty of money, Virji Vora is the only master of it” and “none but Virji Vora has money to lend or will to lend” are stated in various English records of the time. Most of the capital held by EIC came from Virji Vora.
A contemporary Dutch report indicates that the English in Surat were in debt for an amount equivalent to 7 tonnes of gold, negatively impacting their credit. This significant indebtedness gave Vora a commanding position in their dealings. The English factors often remarked that as long as Vora remained their creditor, they could make little to no profit on the goods they brought to Surat. Despite this, their need for funds was so urgent that they resorted to borrowing various sums of money from him on several occasions. Notably, in 1669, the East India Company borrowed Rs 4,00,000 from Virji, his family, and other sarrafs (brokers) in Surat.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Despite his unreasonable terms, they had no choice but to borrow from him, as he was the only one capable of lending such large sums. The English factors were eager to repay this costly creditor as soon as funds became available. He was always the first to be considered for repayment, as doing so reduced their interest expenses and enhanced their reputation for future borrowing.
According to studies conducted by historians and scholars, even the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb once dispatched an agent to Virji Vora in search of funding during his financially challenging campaign to conquer the Deccan region of India.
Despite being a competitor to the East India Company (EIC), Virji managed to maintain cordial relationships with key EIC officials by sending them valuable gifts at regular intervals. At the same time, he also fostered friendly relations with the Mughal governors of the era. Although he was briefly imprisoned by Hakim Sadra, the governor of Surat, in 1635, he was cleared of all charges by Shah Jahan when he was presented before the emperor. He had previously gifted four Arabian horses to Shah Jahan as part of his generosity.
Business strategy revolved around pepper stock
Virji’s key business strategy was to purchase all the pepper stock procured by the Dutch. He also bought all other pepper stocks arriving in the country from various merchants, which made him the sole owner of all the pepper in the country. After acquiring the entire stock, he would compel the English to purchase pepper from him at a price significantly higher than what they originally intended to pay. As a result of this practice, he was often referred to as a “sole monopolist.” He would buy the entire stock of a product, which could be worth between 5 to 10 lakh, and then sell it at a substantial profit.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Virji often sent his agents to Calicut (Now Kozhikode in Kerala) with cotton and opium, selling these goods at double the price he had paid for them. With the profits, he would purchase pepper from the Calicut merchants and then sell this pepper to the English for a substantial profit. Such was his reputation that no one dared to trade in the commodities he dealt with. Even brokers who worked with EIC would not risk accompanying such a prominent merchant to an EIC trading house.
Quite often, Virji would obstruct the sale of English goods or anything brought for sale by the English merchants. They noted, “The potency of Virji Vora is observed to bear such a sway among the inferior merchants of this town that when they would often times buy and give greater prices, they were still restrained, not daring to betray their intents to Virji’s knowledge, in so much that the time and price of the traded goods depended on his sweet will and pleasure.”
The English came to view him as the most damaging figure to their trade within the Mughal territories. If an ordinary merchant dared to visit the English trading house to enquire about coral or any other goods, Virji, leveraging his influence and connections with the government, would ensure the downfall of such merchants. As a result, no merchant in the town would risk offending him by approaching the English trading house, except when their agents deliberately sent them to bid for items that would either fetch little value or discourage other merchants from pursuing those commodities.
As a banker, Virji invested funds in credit or merchandise purchases solely with a profit motive. He gained an advantage by pressuring his debtors to sell to him at a discount and used the extension of credit to invest the funds obtained from the sale of commodities at specific locations. Additionally, he could transfer funds via hundis more easily than ordinary merchants. However, his only weakness was that he did not own any ships. In this business area, Mulla Ghafur, the renowned ship-owner from Surat in the late 17th century, outperformed him.
Challenges faced during Shivaji raids
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
By the mid-1660s, Virji had become old. He faced major setbacks when Maratha chief Shivaji raided his stores twice: first in 1664 and again in 1670. During the initial raid in 1664, Virji lost six barrels of gold, money, pearls, gems, and other precious goods. However, due to his financial influence and business acumen, he quickly recovered from these losses and regained his financial strength.
The latest records indicate that Virji Vora retired from business in the latter part of the 17th century, with his grandson taking over the operations. He passed away around 1675. His extensive commercial activities and nearly 50 years of dominance in the trade at Surat place him on par with EIC regarding capital resources and turnover.
– Dr Amarjit Singh is a retired IAS officer from the Gujarat cadre who has held posts in the central and state governments

headline: West Bengal Madhyamik exams: Girls outnumber boys in continuation of trend
description: Sources in the West Bengal education department said this was because of several initiatives the state government took to prevent child marriages and promote girls' education.
content:
The West Bengal Board of Secondary Education’s Madhyamik Class 10 exams began on February 10. This year, 9,84,910 students are participating in the exams. Approximately 5,55,000 are girls, and 4,28,000 are boys. This means that girl candidates outnumbered boy candidates by around 1,27,000.
According to sources in the education department, this trend has been consistent for nearly 14 years. Sources in the education department said this was because of several initiatives the state government took to prevent child marriages and promote girls’ education.
According to statistics from the state education department, in 2011, the number of girls who took the Madhyamik exams outnumbered boys by approximately 25,000. In 2016, the percentage of girl students appearing for the exams was nine per cent higher than that of boys, and in 2018, it increased to 12 per cent higher than the boys’ percentage. Sources indicated that during the Covid pandemic in 2021 and 2022, 11 per cent more girl students participated in exams than boys. This increase in the number of girls exceeding boys is attributed to various state government schemes encouraging girls to pursue education.
Over the years, the state government has introduced several schemes, such as Kanyashree (financial aid for girl child education) and Sabooj Sathi (free cycles for students). According to officials, the state government has implemented several schemes to empower women, such as Laxmi Bhandar, Rupashri Prakalpo, and Sastho Sathi (which provides health care in the name of the woman of the household).

Officials report that numerous schemes are available to encourage girls to continue their education. In contrast, boys often leave school as they migrate to other states in search of work to help support their families.

headline: ‘CCTV footage secured, witnesses called’: Railways high-level committee begins probe into stampede at New Delhi Railway Station
description: The inspection was carried out on platform 14 of the railway station in the national capital which is where the Prayagraj Express was stationed leading to a surge of passengers.
content:
A day after the stampede that claimed at least 18 lives and left several others injured, a two-member committee formed by the Railways ministry Sunday inspected the incident site at the New Delhi Railway Station and secured the CCTV footage  for investigation.
The inspection was carried out on platform 14 of the railway station which is where the Prayagraj Express was stationed leading to a surge of passengers. People waiting to board the delayed Swatantrata Senani Express and Bhubaneshwar Rajdhani were also present on this platform as well as on platforms 12 and 13.
“All the CCTV footage of the New Delhi Railway station has been secured. We have inspected the site and collected relevant evidence. The investigation has begun today,” said Narsingh Deo, Principal Chief Commercial Manager (PCCM) of the Northern Railway.
The PCCM also said that all the witnesses of the stampede have been called. “Only after the investigation, we would be able to comment on anything… Action will be taken accordingly,” Deo added.

The high-level committee also includes Pankaj Gangwar, the Principal Chief Security Commissioner of the Northern Railway. The railways announced the names of the two high administrative group officials to probe the stampede on Saturday.
On Saturday, the fire department received distress calls about a stampede on platforms 14 and 15 around 9.55 pm. The injured were rushed to Lok Nayak Hospital.

headline: PGI introduces ‘Digi Seva’ for online patient registration, priority based consultations
description: Director: By ensuring patients with urgent medical needs are examined first, the service promises to improve efficiency
content:
Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh, has launched ‘Digi Seva PGI’ to simplify hospital registration and introduce priority-based doctor consultations.
By ensuring patients with urgent medical needs or prior appointments are seen first, Digi Seva is expected to reduce waiting time and improve healthcare efficiency.
Launched on a pilot basis for the Liver Clinic run by the Department of Hepatology in January, PGI Director Prof Vivek Lal launched the full-fledged Digi Seva service at the institute on Saturday.
Key benefits of Digi Seva include seamless online registration, real-time appointment booking, priority-based consultations, automated notifications, and optimised hospital workflow, minimising administrative burdens and enhancing transparency, allowing medical professionals to dedicate more time to patient care.

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
“Digi Seva marks a major step forward in patient-centred healthcare. The priority-based consultations will ensure those in need receive timely medical attention, making hospital visits smoother and more efficient,” Dr Lal said.
Deputy Director of the PGI Administration Pankaj Rai highlighted that patients could access Digi Seva through http://www.pgimer.edu.in to register, book appointments, and receive confirmation. “Designed to be secure, user-friendly, and available in multiple languages, this initiative aligns with national digital health goals and sets a new standard for smart healthcare services,” Rai said.
According to PGI officials, on average, more than 10,000 OPD registrations are done daily at the PGI, with patients from other states standing in queues for hours before the registration counters open at 8 am to get their registration cards made for treatment. The high volume of patients puts pressure on the infrastructure of the Institute, burdens the doctors and healthcare staff, and affects patient care as well, they said, adding that Digi Seva is expected to address these issues.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
During its initial launch in January, n one month, approximately 450 patients registered for the Liver Clinic through this system in one month, demonstrating its success and patient acceptance.
Officials said the PGI had been working to introduce patient-friendly initiatives to reduce waiting time, have more seamless systems of delivery and use digital services to ease procedures.
In August last year, the Advanced Eye Centre, PGI, introduced a system wherein patients registering online for OPDs in advance would be given priority.
Dr SS Pandav, head of the department, said, “The new facility to book online appointments helps in queue management, decongesting the OPD in morning hours and streamlining the process of registration. While more than 80 per cent of follow-up patients use the online system, this facility encourages new patients to use the website for registration, with 200 slots for online registration.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“With the number of patients increasing in OPDs, the effort is being made to think of ways to save time for patients, and with an appointment system, processes will be more streamlined, including decongestion of traffic and also reduce the rush in the hospital,” Rai added.
Mobile app to come up soon
Talking about future initiatives, Rai said that he was working to start a pilot project that would use an App to schedule online registration, with the online appointment system already in place. “The App which can be downloaded on a phone,” Rai said, “will help patients register from wherever they are. After paying Rs 10, a card number will be generated, and the printout will be the proof of registration. This will save patients from standing in queue at counters.”
“To widen the impact, our goal is to link this service with Common Service Centres (CSCs), like E Sampark, Lok Mitra Kendras, etc., in adjoining states to assist non-tech-savvy patients. We want to make this facility accessible to everyone, irrespective of their technological proficiency,” he said.
Project Sarathi launched in May last year — involving National Service Scheme (NSS) volunteers in managing patient influx at the PGI — was conceived by Rai. It significantly improved the patient management process at the hospital. Under Project Sarathi, volunteers assist patients in registration, guide them to various departments, and provide essential information, ensuring a smoother and more organised experience for everyone involved.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
PGI’s School of Public Health recently surveyed Project Sarathi to analyse the benefits patients are getting. The study revealed a new patient, seeking treatment, usually takes about four hours from getting the registration card made to going to the OPD and receiving treatment. With the help of Sarathi, new patients take only two hours and a few minutes for the entire process, saving about one hour and fifty minutes.
24×7 diagnostic services in the offing
Another facility in the pipeline is the provision of 24×7 Diagnostic Services. The PGI Standing Committee has, in principle, approved the proposal for round-the-clock diagnostic services here. The 24×7 Diagnostic Services will alleviate the burden on patients, enabling them to receive care at their convenience rather than being restricted to standard operational hours of 1 pm.
“We have already identified a space for this facility, and we will work towards this, in association with a public sector undertaking, which will provide all tests at the PGI rates. With this facility, patients don’t have to return the next day for a test, saving their time,” Rai added.

headline: Fake insurance policy racket busted in UP’s Sambhal, 6 held
description: Police said the accused fraudulently exploited the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Yojana (PMJJY), a government life insurance scheme that provides coverage of Rs two lakh at a low premium
content:
The Sambhal police on Saturday said it busted an inter-state racket allegedly involved in issuing fake insurance policies and arrested six of its members.
Police said the accused fraudulently exploited the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Yojana (PMJJY), a government life insurance scheme that provides coverage of Rs two lakh at a low premium. The scheme is open to all savings bank account holders aged 18 to 50, with the premium amount automatically deducted from their accounts on a fixed date, police added.
Police identified the arrested persons as Sharukh Khan, Hirendra Kumar, Sanju alias Roop Kishore, Prem Pal, Prem Singh Yadav and Neelam — all local residents. Prem Pal and Prem Singh, who work for a mobile company, supplied SIM cards issued in others’ names to racket members. Meanwhile, Neelam, an ASHA worker, provided information of persons suffering from cancer and other serious illnesses.
Superintendent of Police, Sambhal, Krishna Kumar, pointed out that the racket operates across 12 states, and they would share details of the UP module’s arrests with authorities in other states.
Describing the modus operandi, police said the accused used various tactics to fraudulently claim benefits under the scheme. They targeted families where a member was suffering from a terminal illness. A detailed probe is on, police said.

headline: CM Fadnavis launches Cop24 initiative for Pune city police
description: Cop24 is expected to reduce the response time of the police in providing assistance to citizens
content:
Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday launched the Cop24 initiative of Pune city police, which aims to prevent serious crimes by conducting patrolling 24 hours a day.
The Cop24 initiative was launched by Fadnavis at Tarang, a musical programme organised for police personnel and their family members at Shivajinagar police headquarters ground.
For the effective execution of Cop24, 39 four wheelers and 123 four-wheelers equipped with GPS tracking systems were provided to Pune city police in the presence of Fadnavis, Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar, Minister of State for Civil Aviation Murlidhar Mohol, minister of state for social justice Madhuri Misal, Commissioner of Pune City Police Amitesh Kumar, businessman Punit Balan and several senior police officers.
Cop24 is expected to reduce the response time of the police in providing assistance to citizens. Women beat marshals will also conduct patrolling to handle cases related to women’s safety.

The government is providing facilities to the police to maintain law and order in the city. A fleet of vehicles has now been provided to the police for round the clock patrolling to prevent serious crimes under the Cop24 initiative,” he said.

headline: Punjab and Haryana HC grants anticipatory bail to author of Sidhu Moosewala book in defamation case
description: The prosecution argued that author Manjinder Singh had allegedly stolen an album of personal photographs from Sidhu Moosewala’s residence and used them in his book.
content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court has granted anticipatory bail to Manjinder Singh, also known as Manjinder Makha, who was accused of defamation and other charges related to his book on the late singer Sidhu Moosewala. The ruling was delivered by Justice Sandeep Moudgil.
Singh had been booked under sections 451, 406, and 380 of the Indian Penal Code, along with Section 356(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), following a complaint by Balkaur Singh, Moosewala’s father. The complainant alleged that Singh’s book, The Real Reason Why Legend Died, published in September 2024, contained defamatory material about his son and the family. He also cited social media posts, including videos and podcasts, which he claimed tarnished Moosewala’s image and violated the family’s privacy.
The prosecution argued that Singh had allegedly stolen an album of personal photographs from the complainant’s residence and used them in his book. Additionally, it was alleged that the book made unverified claims linking Moosewala to gangsters and criminal activities.

Singh’s counsel contended that he wrote the book as an academic exercise and that its content was based on publicly available information. The defence maintained that the publication was not intended to harm anyone’s reputation and did not contain any offensive or defamatory statements.

In his ruling, Justice Moudgil stated that there was no compelling reason to deny Singh anticipatory bail. The court observed that the book appeared to be a legitimate personal account rather than an act of intellectual property theft. It also noted that Singh had shown a willingness to cooperate with the investigation.
Granting him anticipatory bail, the court directed Singh to join the investigation within a week and furnish personal and surety bonds. Conditions were also imposed, including restrictions on leaving the country without permission and avoiding any inducements or threats to witnesses.
The court clarified that failure to comply with these conditions would result in the automatic cancellation of the bail order.

headline: From better prediction to understanding climate change effect, India and Italy plan to work together at Pune workshop
description: The two-day programme saw scientists from the Pune-based Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology and the Euro-Mediterranean Centre on Climate Change discuss the use of AI and ML in climate prediction.
content:
What is common about Pune and Rome’s experience of climate change? Do heat islands and urban flooding in Rome hold lessons for Pune? These are some of the questions that scientists from the Pune-based Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) and the Euro-Mediterranean Centre on Climate Change (CMCC) would try to unravel through the first-of-its-kind collaboration. The first workshop in this regard, which saw the participation of scientists from Italy and India, took off in Pune on February 11.
According to Paola Mercogliano, head of the Italian delegation, no country or city is immune to the global phenomenon called climate change. Mecogliano said the institute had worked with the city of Rome to understand the effect of climate change, especially in the form of urban heat islands and urban flooding.
“This involves downsizing data to a very localised level and to study the effect of climate change. We hope to simulate the same for the city of Pune and collaborate with the scientific community in Pune,” she said. Urban heat islands and urban flooding are recent phenomena wherein parts of the cities receive torrential rainfall or report higher temperatures than the other parts.
For Pune, areas of Koregaon Park, and Magarpattta are places where the recorded temperature is higher than the rest of the city. Increased precipitation has seen flash floods in Pune which has led to the loss of life and property in the past. Both these are linked to climate change with urban planners finding it difficult to find solutions.

Mercogliano the crisis can be mitigated with the involvement of city planners and other stakeholders.
The two-day programme saw scientists discuss the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) in climate prediction.
R Krishnan, IITM director, spoke about the institute’s plan to use AI and ML applications in weather, climate, and ocean sciences.

“I am looking forward to a productive research partnership with our Italian colleagues in the coming years,” he said.
Principal scientist Giovanni Coppini who is the director of Global Coasts explained how Italy is collaborating with Indian institutions in terms of ocean studies and this collaboration would help in deepening their ties further.
“Given the fact that we are from public institutions the work we do and results would be available freely,” he said.
Antonio Navarra, CMCC director, said AI and ML can help increase the accuracy of the traditional forecast. New technology can also reduce the cost of prediction as it eliminates the repetitive, mechanical work, Navarra said.

headline: Amid US deportations, Partap Singh Bajwa hits out at Bhagwant Mann: ‘How many travel agents booked for human trafficking in 3 years?’
description: With the US deporting hundreds of illegal immigrants from India, Congress leader Partap Singh Bajwa accused Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann of failing to curb the human trafficking of Punjabis.
content:
With a second US plane with 119 Indian deportees scheduled to land in Amritsar on Saturday, Leader of the Opposition in the Punjab Assembly, Partap Singh Bajwa, lashed out at Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann and his Aam Aadmi Party (AAP)-led government for its failure to curb the human trafficking of Punjabis in the last three years.
The senior Congress leader said that the Punjab Prevention of Human Smuggling Act, 2012, regulates the profession of travel agents to check and curb illegal and fraudulent activities of people engaging in organised human smuggling in Punjab. “Can CM Bhagwant Mann, who also holds the Home portfolio, let Punjabis know how many travel agents have been booked under the same law in the last three years?” Bajwa asked.
Bajwa said that Mann has said that illegal immigration is not only a problem in Punjab but a national problem. “True, but is his government not responsible for acting if any illegality happens in the state? He seems to have been running away from his responsibilities. However, it was one of AAP’s main election planks to stop the brain drain by motivating youngsters to explore careers in the home state,” Bajwa pointed out.
Bajwa said that it had been 10 days since the first flight carrying 104 deportees, including 30 Punjabis, arrived in Amritsar, and the Mann government failed miserably to provide a helping hand and announce any rehabilitation programme for them.

“He has not announced compensation for them. The AAP government has not assured them that the government would help them get their money refunded by the illegal travel agents. Mann says he is going to receive the 119 deportees arriving today in Amritsar. In the absence of a rehabilitation programme and compensation, this is nothing more than a publicity stunt. He always has a lust for publicity,” Bajwa said.
Hitting out at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Bajwa said that inhuman treatment was meted out to Indian deportees in the previous flight. “They were handcuffed and shackled in the plane, and they were not even allowed to use the washroom. However, during his recent US visit, PM Modi did not bother to raise the issue with US President Donald Trump. Is this how PM Modi would maintain the dignity of the sons and daughters of India?” he asked.

headline: Health ministry’s Rs 531 crore tech push: AI in healthcare, cancer research on cards
description: Dr Bahl said ICMR will support the development of newer therapies such as gene therapy and help take them to the market.
content:
The Union Health Ministry’s Department of Health Research has been allocated an enhancement fund of `531 crore in the Union Budget which it will invest over the next five years in areas such as artificial intelligence in healthcare and development of newer therapies.
“There has been an 18% increase in the budget for the Department of Health Research this year. And, over the last decade, the budget has grown nearly four-fold. Importantly, in this budget, we have received a `531-crore special enhancement for the next five years,” said Dr Rajiv Bahl, Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR).
Some other key areas where the money will go are: tackling persistent health problems such as anaemia and cancers, research implementation, pandemic preparedness and ensuring that Indian institutes rank high in medical research.
When it comes to digital health and AI, Dr Bahl said the department will support the development of new tools and databases on which these tools would be developed and trained.

Dr Bahl said ICMR will support the development of newer therapies such as gene therapy and help take them to the market.
The ICMR, along with NITI Aayog and the apex drug regulator CDSCO, also plans to help startups making medical devices during multiple phases of development: pre-clinical and clinical trials, regulatory approvals, prototype development and scaling up
In the case of pandemic preparedness, the government will work towards setting up the National Institute of One Health, improve facilities for surveillance such as setting up of biosafety level 3 and 4 laboratories, and creating a network between already existing laboratories under various government institutions. The department of health research will also work towards developing medical countermeasures against pathogens that may lead to outbreaks and pandemics. The department plans to create libraries of these countermeasures.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“We are working on developing a vaccine against Kyasanur Forest Disease and a monoclonal antibody for Nipah. We have already developed and made available in the market diagnostic tests for Mpox,” said Dr Bahl.
Kyasanur Forest Disease is a tick-borne infection that causes fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, and in some cases neurological and bleeding symptoms. It kills 3% to 5% people it infects. And, Nipah is a viral infection usually transmitted by infected bats. It may lead to fatal brain swelling, with the disease killing 40% to 75% of those who test positive.

headline: Two held for gang rape, robbery in Surat
description: Police sources said that the accused are friends and were doing petty jobs to earn money
content:
Surat police have arrested two men after they allegedly gang-raped a woman and robbed her and her husband on Thursday, from different areas in Bhavnagar on Friday.
The arrested accused have been identified as Dinesh alias Chhoturam Yadav (24) and Nikunj Bhigradiya (25). Dinesh is a resident of Surat’s Punagam and hail from Uttar Pradesh’s Jaunpur, while Nikunj is a resident of Surat’s Kapodara and hail from Bhavnagar.
Surat Deputy Commissioner of Police, Zone 1, Alok Kumar Sharma, told The Indian Express, “We scanned the CCTV footage from the spot (victims’ apartment). We traced their movement and finally, through sources, we came to know that the accused had gone to Bhavnagar. We sent our teams to Bhavnagar and the accused were arrested from different locations.”
He further said, “The accused had left Surat and reached Bhavnagar separately. We have recovered the silver bracelet, which the accused had robbed the woman of. They had also robbed the couple of cash worth Rs 30,000, and Rs 5,000 has been recovered. They had used some money to buy clothes and used some to cover their travel expenses. Officials, along with the accused, are on their way to Surat.”

content:
A man was arrested after a speeding pick-up vehicle allegedly tried to run over a traffic police warden on duty in Pune’s Bhosari area Thursday evening. The injured traffic warden was taken to a hospital for treatment and his condition is said to be stable.
The police identified the arrested driver as Ayan Patel, 21, a resident of Dhawade Wasti in Bhosari.

headline: Bengaluru temperatures go above normal for February as summer conditions make early appearance
description: Maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be around 34 degree Celsius and 16 degree Celsius, respectively, in the IT capital during the weekend.
content:
Ahead of the formal onset of the summer season in Bengaluru, the maximum temperature in the city has steadily risen over the past few days. But the minimum temperature still reflects the winter weather in the city.
On Thursday, the city recorded a maximum temperature of 33.3 degree Celsius, which was 2.7 degree Celsius above normal for this time of the year. The minimum temperature, however, was 17.1 degree Celsius, which is 0.1 degree Celsius below the normal.
The maximum temperatures were “above normal over Bengaluru, Chitradurga, Chintamani and Mysuru of South Interior Karnataka,” the India Meteorological Department (IMD) reported on Thursday.
“Maximum and minimum temperatures are very likely to be around 34°C and 16°C respectively,” the IMD said in its forecast for the weekend in Bengaluru.

In the 30-year period between 1990 and 2020, the average maximum temperature for February in Bengaluru has been 30.9 degree Celsius and the minimum 17.6 degree Celsius.
The last 10 years have, however, seen warmer February weather with maximum temperatures in the range of 33 degree Celsius to 35.5 degree Celsius. The minimum in the last 10 years has ranged from 13 degree Celsius to 16.5 degree Celsius.
The warmest February day recorded in Bengaluru was on February 17, 2005, when a maximum temperature of 35.9 degree Celsius was recorded. The coldest February day recorded was February 6, 1884, when a temperature of 9.6 degree Celsius was recorded.

In the normal course, the summer season in Bengaluru is generally considered to begin around Maha Shivaratri – which falls on February 26 this year. In February, Bengaluru rarely receives rainfall and it is the driest month after January.

headline: In sea of Kumbh visitors, police have tall order: Identify woman’s body unclaimed since Jan 29 stampede
description: Officials are looking at CCTVs, putting up posters and liaisoning with neighbouring states for any clues on her identity
content:
A middle-aged woman dressed in a saree. No name, no ID.
More than two weeks after at least 30 people were killed in the January 29 Kumbh stampede, a woman’s body that was brought to a hospital in the rush of victims remains unidentified, leaving police with the task of figuring out who she was among the sea of visitors at the mega event.
According to officials, some people searching for their missing loved ones have viewed the body, but no one has recognised or claimed it so far.
In the absence of a comprehensive list of stampede victims, officials did not confirm whether the woman died in the same incident or an unrelated one.

Rahul insulted Shivaji Maharaj with post offering ‘sraddhanjali’: Shinde

Officials did acknowledge that the body, currently at the mortuary of Motilal Nehru National Medical College in Prayagraj, was brought from the Kumbh Mela around the time of the stampede.
A senior doctor said the woman did not appear to have any serious visible injuries. Hospital authorities have made arrangements to keep the body in the mortuary, but police will decide the duration of storage, he said.
All other bodies brought for postmortem at the time have been sent to their respective homes after their identities were confirmed, officials said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
According to officials, police are reviewing CCTVs from the Kumbh area to identify the woman in any of the footage and trace her movements before the stampede.
Also Read | Amid videos of unruly passengers pelting stones and breaking windows of Kumbh trains, Railway Protection Force jumps into action, 4 FIRs filed
“We are making every effort to establish the identity,” said DIG, Prayagraj, Vaibhav Krishna.
Posters have been put up in key locations, including railway stations and bus stops, urging the public to provide any information that could help identify the body.
Details have also been shared with police stations across Uttar Pradesh and neighbouring states, but in vain.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The DIG said the body would be kept for a few days, and if it remains unclaimed, a decision would be made on its disposal.
Asked about when the list of stampede victims would be released, DIG Krishna said it would be issued soon but did not specify a timeline.
Political parties have been demanding that the state government disclose the victims’ names. The government has announced a compensation of Rs 25 lakh for each victim’s family.
The stampede occurred at around 1:30 am as crowds moved toward the Sangam Nose – a strip of land at the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna, and the mythical Saraswati – for a ritual bath on Mauni Amavasya, considered an auspicious day.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The victims were rushed to medical facilities within the Maha Kumbh grounds and hospitals in the city. They were later referred to larger hospitals, from where those who died were sent to the post-mortem house.
Chief Minister Yogi Aditynath has ordered a judicial probe and said a separate inquiry would be conducted by the UP Police.

headline: Gujarat CM lays SOUL foundation to train future leaders in politics, social and public policy
description: Chairman Emeritus of the Torrent Group Sudhir Mehta has been appointed as the chairperson of the board of governors of SOUL.
content:
Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel on Friday laid the foundation for the School of Ultimate Leadership (SOUL) coming up close to Gandhinagar’s GIFT City. The formal launch of the SOUL which will be done by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Delhi on February 21.
SOUL, formed with the aim of training aspiring youth who wish to enter politics and empowering them to create new opportunities by addressing the “systemic challenges of governance” in India, will be dedicated to leadership development in three key areas – political, social and public policy, a government release said.
Chairman Emeritus of the Torrent Group Sudhir Mehta has been appointed as the chairperson of the board of governors of SOUL, while former finance secretary Hasmukh Adhia is the chairperson of the SOUL Executive Committee. Adhia is also the chairman of GIFT City.
Spread over 22 acre, the institute will come up on GIFT City road next to the Gujarat Biotechnology University in two years’ time and will be built at a cost of Rs 150 crore, said the statement.

“SOUL is an independent and non-partisan organization established by a group of eminent individuals from the private sector. It has no affiliation with any government agency or university,” the statement said.
At the inauguration of the Ramakrishna Math in Ahmedabad last December, Prime Minister Modi had said, “There will be a roadmap to make youth join politics. It is our resolve to bring one lakh talented and energetic youth into politics in the coming years. And these youth will be the new face of 21st century India and the future of the country.”
In the initial phase, SOUL will offer tailored programmes for public service professionals.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Formal programmes will begin at the campus from March 2027, including medium term study programmes from one to three months to long term programmes from nine months to a year. Until the campus is ready, the institute will organise short term programmes of up to a week and seminars.
“The SOUL will provide a suitable platform for leadership training to candidates and youth who aim to contribute to the public sector, health, education, rural development and sanitation, along with opportunities for developing capable leadership that prioritises the interests of the people. For this purpose, individuals with a strong commitment to public service will be selected for admission to SOUL on the basis of merit through a letter of intent and panel interview,” the statement further said.
The faculty at SOUL will be drawn from various fields, including industry, government and global leaders.  A “token fee” will be charged from the young candidates to ensure “commitment” while training will be free of cost for elected representatives and public service officials.
“SOUL has successfully organised various pre-launch programmes. These include a two-day leadership workshop in collaboration with the Ministry of Education to facilitate the effective implementation of NEP, a one-day brainstorming session for the staff of the Chief Minister’s Office… a workshop was also organized to provide a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the state budget to all elected MLAs,” the statement said.

headline: War of words deepens: Jathedar Giani Raghbir Singh makes differences with SGPC public, takes stand for Giani Harpreet Singh
description: Raghbir Singh posted a statement on Facebook during his foreign tour: “The reasons and manner in which Singh Sahib Giani Harpreet Singh has been removed from the position of Jathedar of Takht Sri Damdama Sahib are completely inappropriate.”
content:
Slamming the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee’s (SGPC) decision to remove Giani Harpreet Singh as the Jathedar of Takht Damdama Sahib, Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Raghbir Singh said that the move was “completely inappropriate”.
Expressing that the recent statements by SGPC have saddened him, Raghbir Singh posted a statement on Facebook during his foreign tour: “In recent days, I have been observing the sequence of events with great seriousness from all perspectives. These developments have deeply saddened me. The reasons and manner in which Singh Sahib Giani Harpreet Singh has been removed from the position of Jathedar of Takht Sri Damdama Sahib are completely inappropriate.”

headline: From tomorrow, take direct Metro from Ahmedabad to Gandhinagar’s Sector-1, GIFT City
description: The Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation (GMRC) on Thursday said February 15 onwards, it would start direct Metro rides from APMC in Ahmedabad to the two key locations in the capital city.
content:
From Saturday, commuters wishing to go from Ahmedabad to Sector-1 or GIFT City in Gandhinagar will no longer have to change Metro trains at Motera stadium or Gujarat National Law University (GNLU) to reach their destination.
The Gujarat Metro Rail Corporation (GMRC) on Thursday said February 15 onwards, it would start direct Metro rides from APMC in Ahmedabad to the two key locations in the capital city. In a statement, the GMRC said that it had received permission from the Commissioner of Metro Rail Safety to increase the frequency of Metro trains between Ahmedabad and Gandhinagar. Earlier, those going from Ahmedabad to Gandhinagar would have to change metro trains at Motera. Similarly, those travelling from GIFT City to Ahmedabad would have to change Metro trains at GNLU.
The GMRC further said that bus services will also be available between GNLU station and Gift City offices every 30 minutes, and will make a stoppage at Pandit Deendayal Energy University (PDEU). Six trains each, back and forth, will ply on the APMC-Motera-GNLU-GIFT City route.
On the other hand, 14 trains will run on the APMC-Motera-GNLU-Sector-1 route while 15 of them will ply on the reverse route.

headline: BMC to complete concretisation of 132.75 KM stretch by June first week
description: The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has stated that by the first week of June, the civic authorities intend to complete concretisation of 132.75 KM of road length in Mumbai, that are currently dug up for ongoing works. The BMC’s move comes in wake of rising pollution woes in Mumbai, and civic officials have stated that […]
content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has stated that by the first week of June, the civic authorities intend to complete concretisation of 132.75 KM of road length in Mumbai, that are currently dug up for ongoing works. The BMC’s move comes in wake of rising pollution woes in Mumbai, and civic officials have stated that no additional digging of roads for the ongoing road concretisation project will be taken up by civic authorities, unless the existing works are completed.
“We have mandated that no new roads will be dug up till the monsoon for road concretisation works as our key focus is to complete the ongoing pending work at all existing roads that have been taken for concretisation and are currently dug up. This decision has been taken to mitigate the ongoing pollution woes but also to ensure that our sole focus is to ensure quality is maintained in the work,” Abhijit Bangar, additional municipal commissioner (Projects) told the Indian Express.
The volume of concurrent roadworks in Mumbai has led to displacement of dust particles in the city which as a result has intensified pollution in Mumbai.
According to the BMC’s data, 372 roads having a total length of 221.76 KM have been taken up  for concretisation in the first phase and 759 different roads with a total length of 218.24 KM were taken up for concretising in the second phase. The concretising work in both the phases are currently ongoing and of the total road length, 132.75 KM or 30% of the total road length that have been taken for repair pre-monsoon.

headline: 23rd Pune International Film Festival begins with a grand opening
description: Maharashtra govt announces Centre of Excellence for film industry
content:
The 23rd Pune International Film Festival (PIFF) was inaugurated in a grand ceremony on Thursday at the Ganesh Kala Krida Manch. The festival, jointly organised by the Pune Film Foundation and the Maharashtra government, will conclude on February 20.
Speaking during the inauguration, state Cultural Affairs Minister Ashish Shelar announced that the government will set up a Centre of Excellence for the film and entertainment industry in Mumbai’s Film City.
“The Maharashtra government is a leader in IT and film industry. We have allotted 10 acres of land in Film City to establish a one-of-a-kind Centre of Excellence. This centre, named AVGC (Animation, Visual, Gaming and Comic), will bring in global experts to train people in advanced technologies and developments in films and entertainment,” said Shelar.
The inauguration was attended by several distinguished guests, including Vikas Kharge, principal secretary, cultural affairs; Swati Mhase Patil, MD, Film City; and filmmaker Shaji Karun. Renowned playback singer Kavita Krishnamurthy and veteran actress Shubha Khote were also present at the event. Others included Dr Jabbar Patel, director of PIFF; Ravi Gupta, secretary, Pune Film Foundation; Satish Alekar, trustee, Pune Film Foundation; Samar Nakhate, creative director of PIFF; Abhijeet Randive, member, PIFF Selection Committee; and Dr Mohan Agashe, trustee, PIFF. The ceremony was hosted by actors Shreya Bugade and Kshitish Date and began with the unveiling of the official PIFF catalogue.

As part of the festival’s theme, ‘Celebrating the Showman’, which marks the birth centenary of Raj Kapoor, veteran actress Shubha Khote was honoured with the PIFF Distinguished Award for her outstanding contribution to Indian cinema. Kavita Krishnamurthy received the prestigious SD Burman International Award for creative music and sound.
After receiving her award, Krishnamurthy expressed her gratitude towards her mentors and colleagues. She then delighted the audience by performing her celebrated song “Pyar Hua Chupkese”. Khote also shared her gratitude and reminisced about her journey in cinema, reflecting on how she transitioned into comedy instead of becoming a lead actress.
Speaking at the event, Kharge emphasised PIFF’s growing importance. “PIFF has become a brand now in Maharashtra. The government considers the film industry a crucial sector. Films are not just about entertainment; they also spread important social messages. The film industry contributes 2% to the national GDP, and the entertainment industry has a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 8%. Hence, the Maharashtra government is committed to supporting both regional and international films,” said Kharge. “Maharashtra has all the necessary infrastructure, locations, and facilities for filmmaking. I appeal to national and international filmmakers to explore Maharashtra for their film projects,” he added.

We received 1,500 film entries, out of which 150 films from 81 countries have been selected for screening. The festival includes categories such as World Competition, Marathi Competition, Global Cinema, Marathi Cinema, and Indian Cinema,” he said.
He also addressed concerns regarding the state of Marathi cinema. “Marathi cinema is facing challenges due to the rise of OTT platforms. This is an important issue that will be discussed during the festival.”

headline: Tickets were sold for Samay Raina event in Vadodara, now civic body sends notice to BookMyShow: ‘Didn’t seek nod to book our venue’
description: Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay auditorium, where the show was announced to be held April 18, is run by Vadodara Municipal Corporation; shows in Ahmedabad, Surat also cancelled
content:
Even as comedian Samay Raina’s Gujarat tour seems to have been
called off, with ticketing platform BookMyShow allegedly “pulling down” the ticket sales to the shows scheduled in April, authorities in Gujarat say neither the organisers nor the ticketing platform had applied for permissions for the show in Vadodara.
The tourism department of Vadodara Municipal Corporation (VMC) said it was issuing a notice to BookMyShow and All Events — the two online ticketing platforms where the event venue had been listed as the VMC-run Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay auditorium.
BookMyShow had put up tickets for sale for Raina’s show – India’s Got Latent Unfiltered Tour – informing that it would be held at Sanjeev Kumar Auditorium in Surat on April 17, Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay auditorium on April 18, and at the AUDA Auditorium in Shela, Ahmedabad, on April 19 and 20. The shows were “pulled down” from the platform on Wednesday, sources said, adding that as of Tuesday, the tickets had been sold out.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
VMC officials said that although the organisers and BookMyShow “appeared to have sold tickets” for the Vadodara event, no bookings had been made for it in the auditorium mentioned.
VMC Tourist Officer Ankush Garud, in fact, told The Indian Express that the bookings for the financial year 2025-26 for the town hall had commenced only on Tuesday, February 11.
Raina and his YouTube show India’s Got Latent ended up in a controversy earlier this week when a conversation between the comedian and podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia went viral, prompting strong reactions, and multiple FIRs, for their allegedly objectionable remarks.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In the notice to BookMyShow for “unauthorised announcement of a programme and ticket sale”, the VMC said, “It has come to our notice that you have initiated ticket bookings…at the VMC-run Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Nagar Gruh…As per our records, no booking has been made for the venue on the scheduled date for such an event. Despite this, you have been taking advance bookings on your application. You can only put up tickets for advance booking for the venues which have been booked after making due payments.”
Commissioner of Police, Vadodara, Narasimha Komar told The Indian Express, “We have not received an application from the organisers seeking permission.”
What happened in Surat?
In Surat city, a local event management firm run by one Jayesh Bapodaraiya had booked the Sanjeev Kumar auditorium for the April 17 show. Officials said the organisers contacted the auditorium Wednesday evening and cancelled the event. Sanjeev Kumar auditorium official Bhavesh Gandhi said, “Bapodaraiya conducts regular shows in our auditorium. On December 10, 2024, he had made an auditorium booking for Raina’s show and deposited the fees. On Wednesday, he turned up and told us to cancel the booking due to the ongoing controversy. We have cancelled the show in Surat.”
Surat city police, too, said they did not receive an application for police permission.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Speaking to The Indian Express, Surat Commissioner of Police Anupamsinh Gahlaut said, “We have not received an application seeking police permission so far but we do know that they had scheduled an indoor event in April… Since it was supposed to be an indoor event at an auditorium run by the civic body, the organisers did not need to apply for fire NOCs and other such mandatory permissions. Generally, for indoor events, organisers approach the police for permission about three or four days in advance. We do look into the background to decide whether the police permission can be granted or not, once the application is received.”
Status in Ahmedabad
Raina was set to perform two shows in Ahmedabad, on February 19 and 20, for which, officials said, his team had booked the AUDA auditorium. However, these bookings, too, now stand cancelled after the controversy.
DP Desai, the CEO of Ahmedabad Urban Development Authority (AUDA), said, “They had given an application to book the AUDA auditorium on February 19 and 20. The permission was earlier granted. However, it stands cancelled as of February 12.”
Superintendent of Police (SP) Om Prakash Jat of Ahmedabad Rural Police said, “No (police) permission was sought.”

When contacted, a spokesperson for BookMyShow refused to confirm if the ticketing platform was refunding patrons. It also declined to comment on the allegations of the Gujarat authorities regarding the sale of tickets without requisite permissions.

headline: Iron ore smuggling: Karnataka HC asks special court whether 23 witnesses can be tried as accused
description: As per the case, mining baron and MLA G Janardhana Reddy had allegedly forged permits to transfer iron ore in connivance with the 23 officers, who had purportedly handed over blank permits with signatures.
content:
The Karnataka High Court has directed a special court trying a case of alleged iron ore smuggling to ascertain whether 23 prosecution witnesses who are forest officers could be tried as accused. The order was passed by a single-judge bench consisting of Justice M Nagaprasanna on February 7 based on the petition of S Muthaiah, a retired forest officer and co-accused in the 2011 case.
Muthaiah had also filed a petition before the special court arguing that the witnesses should be treated as accused in the case.
As per the case, mining baron and BJP MLA G Janardhana Reddy had allegedly forged permits to transfer iron ore in connivance with the 23 officers, who had purportedly handed over blank permits with signatures. The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Reddy in 2011 for his alleged role in the illegal mining in Ballari, two months after the Karnataka Lokayukta submitted a report on the issue that rocked the state. The CBI probe found that Reddy’s mining mafia sold the illegally excavated iron ore to traders who exported it without forest clearances and taxes.
The petitioner’s counsel argued that these witnesses had admitted in cross-examination that they had signed blank permits and were treated as witnesses despite being guilty of the offence. He further argued that the procedure under Section 319 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) should have been followed. Section 319 enables courts to proceed against people who appear to be guilty of an offence.

The bench stated, “An accused can seek pardon and become an approver and depose against the other accused. It is ununderstandable as to how prosecution witnesses can seek pardon and depose against the other accused. But, in the case at hand, they are witnesses who are participants in the crime. Participants in the crime to some extent, as they have admitted signing blank documents. If they admit signing blank documents, then they become accomplices, along with other accused who could be charged with some of the offences”. The court observed that “it is rudimentary that an accused cannot be a witness on behalf of the prosecution, and a person who is admittedly guilty cannot run away from punishment, merely because he has been arrayed as a witness”.
The bench directed the special court to answer the application under Section 319 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) “in accordance with law” to determine whether the witnesses would be treated as accused. Until this exercise was completed, they would not be examined as witnesses.

headline: Waqf Board case: Delhi HC seeks response from MLA Amanatullah Khan, wife on ED plea
description: AAP MLA Amanatullah Khan has been accused of misusing his position as chairperson of the Delhi Wakf Board and illegally leasing out Waqf properties.
content:
The Delhi High Court on Thursday issued notice to AAP MLA Amanatullah Khan and his wife Maryam Siddiqui in an Enforcement Directorate (ED) plea challenging a trial court’s refusal to take cognisance of the central agency’s chargesheet against the two in the Delhi Waqf Board money laundering case.
Justice Vikas Mahajan sought a response from the couple and also directed the trial court, the special court hearing Prevention of Money Laundering Act cases, to defer hearing the other co-accused till March 21. The Delhi High Court also sought the accused’s response by then.
On November 14, 2024, citing a lack of prior prosecution sanction against Khan, the trial court had released Khan, who an MLA then, on bail. Khan and Siddiqui were implicated in a supplementary prosecution complaint, which is equivalent to a supplementary chargesheet, by the ED on October 29, 2024.
Khan has been accused of misusing his position as chairperson of the Delhi Wakf Board, including illegally leasing out Waqf properties and allegedly making appointments in exchange for illegal gratification.
The ED, through special counsel Zoheb Hossain, has challenged the trial court’s decision primarily on three aspects. Apart from the special trial court refusing to take cognisance in the absence of requisite prior sanction to prosecute, the ED is also challenging Khan’s release on bail by the trial court after the court concluded that the same is necessary in light of the absent sanction. The ED has also challenged one of the trial court’s grounds of refusal to take cognisance – that the central agency’s chargesheet fails to establish that Siddiqui had prior culpable knowledge or mens rea (intention) of the scheduled offence or the proceeds of the crime.
Hossain argued on Tuesday that the offences Khan has been accused of cannot be said to have been done in discharge of official duty, and thus, the prior prosecution sanction was not required. Hossain also added that prior to filing the supplementary prosecution complaint implicating Khan and Siddiqui as accused, the ED had earlier filed the main complaint on which cognisance has already been taken, and thus the trial court ought to have issued summons to Khan and Siddiqui when the supplementary chargesheet was filed, “as cognisance is to be taken of the offence and not the offenders”.
Hossain also added that the ED was not given an opportunity to address arguments on the aspect of requirement of prior sanction to prosecute, and the trial court “failed to appreciate that it is not a case of complete absence of sanction, in fact the sanction was already there in a predicate offence and had the opportunity been afforded to (ED) the said sanction could have been placed before the special judge”.

headline: Indians deported from US: 2 more FIRs registered against travel agents, tally touches 10
description: A US military aircraft carrying the first batch of 104 illegal Indian immigrants, including 30 from Punjab, landed at the Amritsar airport on February 5.
content:
A Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the illegal human trafficking following the deportation of Indian citizens from the US registered two more FIRs against fraudulent immigration consultants, taking the number of such FIRs to 10, the Punjab Police said on Wednesday.
A US military aircraft carrying the first batch of 104 illegal Indian immigrants, including 30 from Punjab, landed at the Amritsar airport on February 5.
According to a Punjab Police statement, both FIRs were registered on Tuesday. The first FIR was registered against Jaskaran Singh, Mahinder Singh, Hardev Kaur and Sujan Singh, all residents of Tahli village in Tanda, Hoshiarpur district, while the second FIR was registered against Happy of Tanda in Hoshiarpur and Gill of Tarn Taran (both agents), under relevant sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Emigration Act at the NRI police station in Hoshiarpur.
The accused allegedly deceived people with false promises of facilitating illegal entry into the United States, resulting in their deportation, the statement said.

Police sources said the SIT, led by ADGP (NRI Affairs) Praveen Sinha, was looking into the complaints lodged against travel agents duping people on the false promise of illegal entry into the US. The team has recorded statements of deportees and registered FIRs against fraudulent travel agents, they said.
Punjab Director General of Police (DGP) Gaurav Yadav reaffirmed the Punjab Police’s commitment to “act against the chain of fraudulent immigration networks and end the exploitation of vulnerable individuals”.
The DGP urged the citizens to come forward with information leading to the arrest of culprits. “Public cooperation is essential in dismantling these fraudulent networks. Awareness among people will help prevent them from falling prey to such fraudulent immigration consultants,” he said.

ADGP Sinha said, “The NRI Affairs Wing and the district police are working in close coordination to ensure quick and strong action against those named in the FIRs. All linkages will be examined to cripple and demolish the whole network.”
The Punjab Police, meanwhile, has advised individuals seeking immigration services “to take the legal route, only opt for licensed agents, and verify their credentials before making any commitments.”
In late 2024, Punjab Police’s NRI Affairs Wing and Cyber Crime Wing, in coordination with the Protectorate of Emigrants, Chandigarh, had booked 43 travel agencies for allegedly illegally advertising jobs abroad on social media without the requisite licence.
Meanwhile, the Chandigarh Police carried out a special drive on Wednesday against immigration companies and consultants illegally operating in the city.

headline: 1984 anti-Sikh riots case: Former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar convicted for killing father, son in Delhi
description: Sajjan Kumar is serving a life sentence handed down by the Delhi High Court in a case related to the killing of five Sikhs and the burning down of a gurdwara in Palam Colony during the 1984 anti-Sikh riots.
content:
A Delhi court on Wednesday convicted former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar in a case related to the killings of two men in Delhi’s Saraswati Vihar on November 1, 1984, during the anti-Sikh riots. Arguments on the quantum of sentence in this case will take place on February 18.
The Special Investigation Team (SIT), which was probing this case, alleges that Kumar, who was then the Congress MP for Outer Delhi, led a mob that burnt alive the two Sikh men—Jaswant Singh and his son Tarundeep Singh—and destroyed and looted their houses acting on his directions. The SIT was represented in the court by Additional Public Prosecutor Manish Rawat.
Kumar’s counsel Anil Kumar Sharma, Anuj Sharma and Apoorav Sharma argued that the complainants, the wife and the mother of the victims, had claimed to be an eyewitness in the case after a long delay of seven years and that their testimonies were therefore unreliable. The complainants were represented by senior advocate H S Phoolka and advocates Kamna Vohra and Gurbaksh Singh.
Widespread riots broke out in Delhi and other parts of the country after then prime minister Indira Gandhi was murdered by two Sikh bodyguards in retaliation for her order for the Army to storm the Golden Temple at Amritsar in June 1984 to flush out militants.

The FIR in this case was registered in 1991 on the basis of an affidavit dated September 9, 1985, given by the complainant before the Justice Ranganath Mishra Commission, which was appointed in 1985 by then prime minister Rajiv Gandhi “to inquire into the organised violence that took place in Delhi and also the disturbances in the Bokaro Tehsil and Chas Tehsil (both in present-day Jharkhand) and at Kanpur, and to recommend measures that may be adopted for prevention of recurrence of such incidents.”
He is already in Tihar Jail; was handed a life term in 2018
On December 4, 2021, the Rouse Avenue Court of Special Judge M K Nagpal framed charges against the accused for the offences of murder, rioting with a deadly weapon, unlawful assembly and attempt to commit culpable homicide, among others.
Kumar is currently lodged in Tihar Jail serving a life sentence handed down by the Delhi High Court in 2018 in a case related to the killing of five Sikhs at Raj Nagar Part I in Palam Colony on November 1-2, 1984, and the burning down of a gurdwara in Raj Nagar Part II.

In September 2023, a Delhi court acquitted Kumar in a case related to the murder of seven people from the Sikh community in Sultanpuri during the 1984 riots. One case is pending against Kumar in the Rouse Avenue court, two appeals against his acquittals are pending in the high court, and an appeal against his conviction in one case is pending in the Supreme Court.

headline: Pre-arrest bail denied to 3 booked over unauthorised streaming of IPL matches
description: The ED had registered ECIR based on an FIR registered by Nodal Cyber Police station, Mumbai under offences of cheating, criminal conspiracy of IPC and various provisions of  Information Technology Act.
content:
A special court designated under Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) on Tuesday rejected anticipatory bail pleas of three partners of a firm booked by Enforcement Directorate (ED) for receiving proceeds of crime generated from unauthorised streaming of IPL cricket matches and contents from Viacom 18’s OTT platform Voot .
The court noted that there was “ample material on record showing Rs. 13 crore proceeds of crime had been transferred to the account of partnership firm Maa Sharda Sales run by pre-arrest bail applicants Santosh Singh, Mukesh Kumar and Monu Kanskar.
The ED had registered ECIR based on an FIR registered by Nodal Cyber Police station, Mumbai under offences of cheating, criminal conspiracy of IPC and various provisions of  Information Technology Act.
The central agency had claimed that in October, 2021, Viacom’s anti-piracy technical team had gathered information that most of its paid content was being shown unauthorisedly on various applications.The Viacom 18 had the digital (internet) rights for broadcasting live the Tata IPL 2023 cricket matches. However, owners of various applications, without having any official license from the company had illegally put up hoardings at various places in Mumbai and broadcasted and the same for free through their platforms. Due to the same, Viacom 18 claimed to have suffered a financial loss of over Rs 100 crore.

headline: Bengaluru girl dies by suicide after mother scolds her for using mobile phone ahead of Class 10 exams
description: The Bengaluru police filed a case of unnatural death and sent the 15-year-old girl's body for postmortem.
content:
A 15-year-old girl in Bengaluru allegedly died by suicide Wednesday after her mother scolded her for spending too much time on her mobile phone and not preparing adequately for her Class 10 exams, said the police.
The deceased was identified as Avantika Chaurasia, a resident of Assetz Marq on the Whitefield-Hoskote Road. The police said Chaurasia studied at Delhi Public School in Whitefield.
Shivakumar Gunare, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Whitefield), said, “We are investigating further to ascertain other reasons, if any.”

headline: Clash over ‘control of illegal sand mine’ injures 2 in West Bengal, 10 held
description: Residents have long complained about the alleged illegal sand extraction from the Ajay river, accusing “local TMC goons” of the activity
content:
A violent clash involving throwing of crude bombs between two groups —allegedly backed by rival Trinamool Congress (TMC) factions — over control of illegal sand mining operations broke out on Tuesday in Birbhum’s Kankartala area.
The clash allegedly stemmed from a struggle for control over the proceeds from an illegal sand mine in the Ajay river area of Jamalpur, Kankartala. Local sources alleged the fight was also about “establishing dominance” in sand extraction from the river.
A man, identified as Sheikh Saktar Ali, sustained serious injuries in the incident, with administration officials confirming the amputation of his right leg. Ten people have been arrested, including Saktar, who is undergoing treatment. The others are in police custody.
The police said another person was also injured in the clash.

content:
The Delhi Police said Wednesday they arrested three men for an alleged burglary at Kalyan Jewellers showroom in Lajpat Nagar in the last week of January and recovered jewellery worth Rs 1 crore from their possession. The main accused has been identified as Shoib alias Lalla, 31, and the two receivers of the stolen jewellery as Sumit Soni, 30, and Manik Kadam, 42.
“A total of 100 grams of stolen diamonds, a gold chain (10 gm) purchased using stolen funds and 57 grams of fine quality gold, extracted by melting stolen jewellery, were recovered from their possession,” said Ravi Kumar Singh, Deputy Commissioner of Police, South East.
On January 29, the showroom manager of Kalyan Jewellers reported a burglary at night. Upon arriving at Kalyan Jewellers, the police team discovered broken glass displays and approximately Rs 1.5 crore worth of diamond jewellery missing. An analysis of the CCTV footage revealed an unidentified burglar, with a concealed face and gloved hands, who entered through the back by breaking the glass in the washroom.
The footage also captured an attempted entry into Kalyan Jewellers via the roof on January 15, but the burglar was unsuccessful. Instead, he allegedly targeted a nearby shop by breaking the bolt on the roof door. The police said cash worth Rs 26,200 was stolen from that shop between 3 and 5 am on January 15.
