headline: Mumbai police files FIR against BMC officials and police personnel for carrying out demolition at Powai’s Jai Bhim Nagar last year
description: The demolition drive had taken a violent turn with as many as 35 people, including 20 police personnel, injured after alleged stone-pelting and clashes between the residents and municipal personnel
content:
Four months after informing the Bombay High Court that it would register a case against the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) and police personnel, the Mumbai police has booked senior civic and police personnel for carrying out a demolition drive at Powai’s Jai Bhim Nagar during the monsoon — without necessary clearances.
The FIR, filed against nine persons, follows a Bombay HC directive after a Special Investigation Team (SIT) of the Mumbai police informed the court that the demolition was carried out without a specific order.
On June 6, 2024, the BMC demolished nearly 500 allegedly unauthorised structures in Jai Bhim Nagar. While the civic body claimed the action was based on directives from the State Human Rights Commission (SHRC), activists pointed out that a government resolution prohibits demolitions during the monsoon (June 1-September 30).
The demolition drive had taken a violent turn with as many as 35 people, including 20 police personnel, injured after alleged stone-pelting and clashes between the residents and municipal personnel. Nearly 60 people have been arrested on charges of assaulting the police.

Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
The move sparked criticism, leading affected residents to file a petition in the HC, demanding an explanation for the eviction. Subsequently an SIT was set up on the directive of the HC to look into the case.
In September 2024, the SIT told the division bench of Justices Revati Mohite-Dere and Prithviraj K. Chavan that the BMC had conducted the demolitions without a specific SHRC order. The SIT assured the court that officials involved would be booked. Four months later, the FIR has now been registered.
According to police, the FIR was filed based on a complaint by resident Minabai Govind Limbole under IPC sections 323, 324, 143, 504, and 34.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Limbole, a resident of Jai Bhim Nagar since 2000, stated in her complaint that despite submitting applications for water and electricity connections, residents received no response from authorities. While their petition was pending in the HC, a BMC notice was posted in the area on June 3, 2024, ordering residents to vacate their homes within 48 hours.
On June 5, residents were called to a meeting at a local police outpost, where they were urged to leave. The next morning, at around 8:30 am, police personnel, BMC officials, workers, five JCBs and approximately 500 employees of the builder arrived for the demolition.
“Despite pleading for more time, they did not listen. While we were speaking with the authorities, some employees of the builder began throwing stones. The police, assuming we were responsible, started beating us,” Limbole stated in her complaint.
She further alleged that residents were detained at the police station. Upon her release, she returned to find all homes demolished, with her daughter sitting on the footpath.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The petitioners claimed they had been living in Jai Bhim Nagar for nearly 30 years and possessed documents such as electricity bills, Aadhaar cards, and gas connections to prove their residence.

headline: From assisting male cops, Patna’s women are now manning city’s traffic during the day
description: Since January 26, women traffic cops have been fully in-charge of all of the city's 54 checkpoints during the day. For many women officers, this is a step towards empowerment.
content:
For Pushpa Kumari, seeing a chief minister from close quarters was a childhood dream. “Now, I am in charge of the entire VIP traffic movement in and around Patna airport. Facilitating the passage of the CM’s convoy without any hassle gives me a great sense of pride. I feel empowered,” said Kumari, the sub-inspector in charge of traffic around the airport and VIP area.
Since January 26, all traffic control in Patna has been in the hands of women personnel of the traffic police in the first shift – between 7 am and 3 pm – which sees the most traffic flow due to school, office, and business hours. In the second shift – 3 pm to 10 pm – the city traffic is managed by both women and men personnel.
“We handed over Patna’s traffic in the daytime to our women force. But we have kept it mixed for the second shift, considering their important roles as mothers and homemakers as well,” Bihar Additional Director General of Police (Traffic) Sudhanshu Kumar told The Indian Express.
While it is common to see women officers and constables at checkpoints in Patna, since January 26, all 54 checkpoints in the city have been managed by women personnel during the day.

SI Kumari, a 2018 batch officer from Purnia, said she is the first woman police officer from her family. “Before January 26, my job was to assist male officers in managing traffic. But now, there is a great sense of responsibility and empowerment since I am in charge of traffic at the airport and have 14 checkpoints under me,” she said.
Traffic ADG Sudhanshu Kumar said this initiative could be replicated in other major Bihar towns once the number of women officers and constables increases. “It has been over a fortnight now, and we have been getting good feedback on the women traffic police initiative for Patna,” he said.
He also said the initial period of the initiative showed the need for more washrooms and sitting areas near traffic checkpoints. “We have planned several pink toilets for police women near checkposts. These washrooms would have sitting areas,” he said.

Currently, there are toilets near only 32 out of 54 Patna checkpoints. In the first shift, 53 women officers, 179 constables, and 17 Bihar Home Guards are deployed. In the second shift, 63 women constables and seven Bihar Home Guards (women) are deployed along with male officers and constables.
In Patna Traffic Police, among 385 officers, 66 (17%) are women. Among 798 constables, 311 (38%) are women, and out of 269 Bihar Home Guards, 26 (9%) are women.

headline: Giani Harpreet Singh interview: ‘Someone within the party wants to damage Sukhbir Badal’
description: In an interview with The Indian Express Tuesday, Harpreet Singh talked about the controversy over the December 2, 2024, decision on the atonement of SAD president Sukhbir Badal and others who were declared religiously guilty, the process of the decision taken and his plans.
content:
The Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) executive committee has sacked Giani Harpreet Singh based on a report of its three-member panel probing allegations of misconduct against the Takht Damdama Sahib Jathedar.
SGPC had earlier suspended Harpreet Singh from his post. He has, however, denied the allegations, which were levelled by one of his relatives.
In an interview with The Indian Express Tuesday, Harpreet Singh talked about the controversy over the December 2, 2024, decision on the atonement of SAD president Sukhbir Badal and others who were declared religiously guilty, the process of the decision taken and his plans.
Edited excerpts:
Q. What is your defence on the allegations against you apart from denying them?
Giani Harpreet Singh: The allegations were made to assassinate my character. The most important thing is that SGPC conducted a probe into these allegations in 2008 as well. A probe committee was formed, and questioned not only me but also my neighbours, relatives, friends, and colleagues. I was absolved from these allegations. Then I was made Takht Damdama Sahib Jathedar and given charge as acting Jathedar of Akal Takht Sahib. Would SGPC have offered me such posts if they found even an iota of truth in these allegations? SGPC denied these allegations in the first place. These fake allegations are not the reasons but an excuse to remove me.

Q. What is your conflict with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and SGPC about?
Giani Harpreet Singh: What I have understood so far is that someone from within the SAD wants to damage Sukhbir Singh Badal. There has not been a single decision that has been taken for the good of the party in recent times. I don’t know if Sukhbir Singh Badal is unable to understand it or if he can’t do much about it. Who told the party that it should go against the Akal Takht Sahib? Can you explain how my removal or not running the membership drive according to Akal Takht Sahib’s directions benefits the party or Sukhbir Singh Badal?

Some leaders claiming to be in favour of Sukhbir Singh Badal built a narrative in advance that decisions from the Akal Takht would end Sukhbir politically. Were they making ground for the political assassination of Sukhbir? Were they trying to put ideas into the people’s minds that Sukhbir would be finished politically with whatever decision Akal Takht would take?
Q. But the allegation against you is that the December 2 pronouncement from Sri Akal Takht Sahib was to damage Sukhbir Singh Badal.
Giani Harpreet Singh: What Sukhbir Singh Badal and other leaders confessed before Sri Akal Takht Sahib should have been done long ago. But they tried to avoid it and contested many elections. In every election, their vote percentage went down. The party came to a point where some senior leaders rebelled. What Sukhbir Singh Badal and others confessed to Sri Akal Takht Sahib was already known. There was nothing new. But the community forgives when someone confesses with pure heart and following Akal Takht Sahib’s orders would have benefited the party. It was to revive the party and not to destroy it.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A majority of the members in the seven-member committee that Akal Takht formed to start a membership drive were from the SAD itself. These members were not from Pakistan. Only one of the members was a rebel. If they don’t trust SGPC president Harjinder Singh Dhami, one of its two MLAs Manpreet Singh Ayali, Iqbal Singh Jhunda who was party candidate in Sangrur, former SGPC president and Parkash Singh Badal’s close confidant Kirpal Singh Bandugar then how can they blame anyone else? All these committee members are those who worked for the SAD all their lives — except a woman member who comes from a respected family in the community. The party has now committed a grave mistake by standing against Akal Takht Sahib’s directions. Akal Takht never takes decisions with a vendetta. It is always for reconciliation and in good faith.
Q. Giani Raghbir Singh is Akal Takht Jathedar. But the allegations are that you were the architect of the pronouncement.
Giani Harpreet Singh: Decisions at Akal Takht Sahib are always taken unanimously. It was not just me or Giani Raghbir Singh. There is always a jury of five at the Akal Takht and if even one of them objects, a decision cannot be reached. All the other four members of the jury have high integrity and credibility. At the end of the day, we all were technically employees of SGPC. The SAD controls SGPC. But at that time, we were serving the almighty and we only fear the Guru. So, calling me the architect of the decision taken on December 2 is childish.
Q. If all jury members took this decision, why are you the only one who is being targeted?
Giani Harpreet Singh: I enjoyed very good relations with the former SGPC president Kirpal Singh Bandugar, Gobind Singh Longowal, and Bibi Jagir Kaur. The change in the relationship came when Harjinder Singh Dhami became the president in 2022. I used to write letters to the SGPC president on various issues. When Dhami came, Akal Takht was asked to not write letters directly to Dhami but to his PA. Slowly, SGPC stopped replying to communication. In the meantime, the coordination with SAD was also spoiled by some people. I don’t know what happened, and a few people in SAD started targeting me. I think the current developments are also in the same league.
Q. Has Sukhbir Singh Badal ever called you and asked to do something and you declined?
Giani Harpreet Singh: Yes, it happened on two or three occasions that he called me to do something and I declined. But every time, at a later stage, Sukhbir Singh Badal admitted that I was right in not doing what he had asked. Sukhbir wanted me to summon Delhi Gurdwara Parbhandak Committee President Harmeet Singh Kalka over his political dispute with the SAD. I told Sukhbir Singh Badal that it wouldn’t be right for Akal Takht to summon one faction over a political dispute. Sukhbir Singh Badal later told me that it was right for me to not summon Kalka. I had better coordination with Sukhbir Singh Badal before Dhami became president. Earlier, he used to take my advice on religious matters.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Q. You have alleged that Jathedars are often removed unceremoniously. But you were also made Akal Takht Jathedar through the same system.
Giani Harpreet Singh: Initially, I was made Takht Damdama Sahib Jathedar. I had declined when it was announced that I would have charge as acting Jathedar of Akal Takht in 2018. I immediately called then-president Gobind Singh Longowal that I was not ready for this. Because nobody wanted to take charge at Akal Takht Sahib in those circumstances. I knew that SGPC had offered many big personalities and scholars to become Jathedar but all had declined due to harm former Jatehdar Gurbachan Singh caused to the post.
The Akal Takht can never be harmed but the position of Jathedar was badly harmed at that time because of the manners in which Dera Sirsa’s head was pardoned. So, I was also not ready. But then many SGPC members came to me and requested me to accept the post. When I took charge, people were sending bangles in post to Jathedar. This was how bad the situation was. Many Jathedars were removed before me. Because as a Jatehdar, you have to work for the community and not for a leader. I gave the statement that SAD has become the party of landlords. It was a party of poor, working class, farmers, and labourers. Maybe such statements went against me.
Q. So were you, too, made a Jatehdar without any criteria?
Giani Harpreet Singh: There is no criteria. Former Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Joginder Singh Vedanti had made a draft on making criteria for the selection of Jathedars, and submitted it to SGPC in 2008. Immediately after taking over charge of Akal Takht Jatehdar, I sent a reminder to SGPC and asked it to act on the draft to make a rule. I sent the second reminder in 2022. But someone wants to keep all the powers of appointments in their pocket.
Q. When did you last talk to Giani Raghbir Singh? He rejected the SGPC probe against you and accepted your clarification. Do you think he will stand by that?
Giani Harpreet Singh: I talked to him today. I can understand that he must be under immense pressure and I don’t want to put Jathedar Sahib in a tight spot by making any comment. I can understand his position as I also worked on the same post. He was also threatened. All parties have IT wings. But the kind of abusive language that the SAD IT wing used against Jathedar has no parallels. If the SAD will not respect Jathedars then should we expect the Congress, BJP or AAP to do that? Sikh politics was based on ethics. But those ethics are not there in Sikh politicians any more. Personal interests are more important for politicians than the community.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Q. You attended the weddings of Raghav Chaddha and former CM Charanjit Singh Channi’s son. You met Union Home Minister Amit Shah. It was taken as an offence by the SAD.
Giani Harpreet Singh: Not just the SAD but a few people started objecting to my meetings with leaders of other parties. AAP leader and Punjabi Hindu Raghav’s family organised a religious function for his wedding so I must attend. Women recited the Sukhmani Sahib (Sikh scripture) at the wedding. There was nothing wrong with it. If Akali leaders can attend the wedding ceremonies of Congress and BJP leaders then what is wrong in attending the wedding of Charanjit Singh Channi’s son? I met Amit Shah to discuss community issues. They made an issue out of it.
Q. Don’t you think, amid this war between Sikh personalities and Sikh institutions, the community would suffer?
Giani Harpreet Singh: It is true. In my initial years, I restored the credibility of a Jathedar’s post. Many Sikh organisations had stopped reaching out to Jathedars. After I took charge, slowly almost all the organisations restored their connection with Jathedar. During my foreign tours, it also helped Akali leaders reconnect with people. Then we worked on many things including the idea of establishing a Sikh Education Board, a Sikh bank, and Khalsa currency. We were working on many things and then I was removed.
Q. Are you going to join politics?
Giani Harpreet Singh: Politics is not my subject. My subject is religion and I will work in that direction. I have completed my PhD work. I have learned how to conduct research and have published research papers. I will not complete the formalities to submit it at Punjabi University… But I will definitely publish my work.

headline: Ranveer Allahbadia row: Influencer Apoorva Mukhija appears before Mumbai police, faces inquiry
description: As part of its inquiry into podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia’s controversial question on the show ‘India’s Got Latent’, the police have recorded the statement of content creator Ashish Chanchlani.
content:
Social media influencer Apoorva Mukhija appeared before the Mumbai police on Wednesday as part of an inquiry into podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia’s controversial question on standup comedian Samay Raina’s YouTube show ‘India’s Got Latent’.
Responding to police summons, Mukhija reached Khar police station, where her statement was recorded, following which she was allowed to leave. Mukhija, wearing a mask, refused to comment.
Popular as ‘the rebel kid’, Mukhija was among the four judges on Raina’s show along with Allahbadia and content creators Ashish Chanchlani and Jaspreet Singh. All five have been summoned by the police.
On Tuesday, Chanchlani visited the Khar police station with his lawyer and faced an inquiry for over 30 minutes, following which his statement was recorded.

headline: 8 cases of cheating in Pune division on day 1 of HSC exams, 42 across Maharashtra
description: Maharashtra HSC exams: Seven of the eight cheating cases in the Pune division were recorded in the Solapur district, while one was recorded in the Ahilyanagar district
content:
On the first day of the Maharashtra State Board of Secondary and Higher Secondary Education (MSBSHSE) Class 12 examinations Tuesday, the Pune division reported eight cases of cheating. Overall, 42 cheating cases were recorded across Maharashtra, as per MSBSHSE.
Audumbar Ukirde, secretary of the Pune Division of MSBSHSE, told The Indian Express that seven of the eight cases in the Pune division were recorded in the Solapur district, while one was recorded in the Ahilyanagar district. Ukirde said no cases of cheating were recorded in the Pune district.
Ukirde said these were individual cases of cheating, with students hiding copying materials in their clothing at the exam centre. He mentioned that no mass copying incidents were reported in the Pune division.
Out of the 42 cases recorded in the state, the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar division reported the highest number with 26 cases. This was followed by the Pune division with eight cases, the Nashik division with three cases, and the Nagpur and Amravati divisions with two cases each. The Latur division had one case. The remaining three divisions—Mumbai, Konkan, and Kolhapur—reported no cases of cheating.

headline: ‘Probe revealed negligence in hiring, training driver’: Mumbai police files chargesheet in Kurla BEST bus accident case
description: The BEST bus travelling from Kurla station to Andheri lost control and crashed into 22 vehicles on December 9, 2024, killing nine people.
content:
The Mumbai police, which is investigating the accident case involving a BEST bus that killed nine people and injured 49 in a crowded area in Kurla, filed a chargesheet of over 1,000 pages against the driver Sanjay More before the metropolitan magistrate court on Tuesday.
The police also named the CEO of the wet lease company that hired the driver as well as the director of the firm that supplied the electric bus to Brihanmumbai Electricity Supply and Transport (BEST).
“The director of EveyTrans Private Limited and the CEO of Morya Trans India Limited have also been named as accused in the chargesheet because our investigation revealed negligence in hiring and training the driver, which played a role in causing the mishap,” said an officer.
According to the police, around 9.30 pm on December 9, 2024, the BEST bus travelling from Kurla station to Andheri lost control near Anjuman-E-Islam school in Kurla West and crashed into 22 vehicles, including a police van, cars, two-wheelers and hand carts. Four people died on the spot while five succumbed to injuries at the hospital.

Additionally, adequate training was not provided to him and evidence showed that it was a human error on the driver’s part as he lost control over the vehicle.
The police have included CCTV footage of the incident, the driver’s blood sample, other forensic test reports, the statements of over 40 witnesses and the death certificates of the victims in the chargesheet.

headline: JEE Main 2025 result: How Harsh Jha cracked one of toughest exams with back-to-back classes and hours of self-study
description: A resident of Bihar, Harsh Jha says after scoring a perfect JEE score he now wants to focus on his Class 12 board exams.
content:
When Harsh Jha first arrived in Delhi two years ago, he was just another teenager with a dream. At 15, he left his home in Begusarai, Bihar, with one goal: to secure a seat in the prestigious Computer Science programme at IIT Bombay.
On Tuesday, that dream moved closer to reality as the 17-year-old scored a perfect 100 in Paper 1 of the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) Main, catapulting him into the ranks of the country’s top engineering aspirants. “I decided in Class 10 that I wanted to study Computer Science at IIT Bombay,” he said.
His goal was ambitious, but Harsh’s performance in academics hinted at his potential — he scored a stellar 99 per cent in his CBSE Class 10 Board exams.
To pursue his IIT dream, Harsh made the bold decision to move to Delhi. He enrolled in FIITJEE’s coaching programme in Kalu Sarai, known for its rigorous preparation for JEE aspirants while attending a “dummy school” for formalities. “I can’t reveal the name of the school. It’s a dummy school,” he said, referring to institutions designed to support students prioritising competitive exams over regular schooling.

Adjusting to life in Delhi was no easy feat. Away from the comfort of home, Harsh lived in a hostel in Jia Sarai, a bustling hub for IIT aspirants. Days began early, with back-to-back classes and hours of self-study. Despite the pressure, Harsh found moments of solace in small pleasures — watching English movies was one of them. “Will Smith is my favourite actor. His movies always lift my spirits,” he said.
His father, a teacher in neighbouring Jharkhand, and his mother, a homemaker, always emphasised the importance of education. Amidst the grind, Harsh found unwavering support from his mother. “Whenever I felt stressed or overwhelmed, I would call her. She always knew the right words to say to keep me motivated,” he says.

headline: Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd expects order book to reach Rs 2.5 lakh crore in six months
description: The production of light combat aircraft and helicopters have taken Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) to new heights, its chief says at Aero India 2025 in Bengaluru.
content:
Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), India’s largest aerospace and defence manufacturer, said on Tuesday that it would have an order book of Rs 2.5 lakh crore in the next six months, driven by expectations of two major orders.
Addressing a press meet on the sidelines of the biennial Aero India 2025 show at Bengaluru’s Yelahanka Air Force Station, D K Sunil, Chairman and Managing Director, HAL, said the order book growth would make the company one of the leading players in South Asia.
“The company has received orders worth Rs 55,000 crore in the first nine months of the fiscal year and is expecting to close orders worth another Rs 1.2 lakh crore in the next five to six months. Including the present orders, the total orders will be worth Rs 2.5 lakh crore and the production will continue for the next 5-6 years,” he said.
“We are actively pursuing two major contracts. One is for 97 light combat aircraft (Tejas) and 156 light combat helicopters (Prachanda). Both are in the advanced stages of negotiations. We are hoping to close them in the next 5-6 months,” he added.

headline: BJP chief issues show-cause notices to 20 ‘rebel’ leaders
description: The election of the local bodies of 66 municipalities, three taluka panchayats, and Junagadh Municipal Corporation in the state is scheduled for February 16.
content:
Valsad district BJP president Hemant Kansara issued show-cause notices to 20 rebel leaders and active members of the party who are contesting the local body elections of Valsad, Dharampur and Pardi Municipalities from rival political parties or as independent candidates.
Valsad BJP president Hemant Kansara said, “We have issued show-cause notices to 20 BJP active members and leaders who acted against the party mandate or those leaders who pushed their family members to contest the elections. We have started receiving replies to the show-cause notices. We will go through the details, and if the reply is unsatisfactory, we will suspend them from the party for six years.”
The election of the local bodies of 66 municipalities, three taluka panchayats, and Junagadh Municipal Corporation in the state is scheduled for February 16.
Leaders from the BJP, Congress, AAP, and independent candidates are in the poll fray.

headline: Pune: Revenue dept clerk held for taking Rs 1.6L bribe for land allotment to 8 project affected families
description: Pune ACB had received a complaint from a man whose joint family was slated to receive compensatory land from the government because theirs had been acquired for the Temghar dam project
content:
THE PUNE unit of the State Anti Corruption Bureau (ACB) arrested a 50-year-old clerk from a divisional office of the revenue department in Pune district and another person on charges of accepting a bribe of Rs 1.6 lakh for alloting land in eight projects to families affected by the Temghar dam project in Pune district. The ACB was probing if any senior officials were involved in the graft.
A team from Pune ACB on Monday arrested Sujata Badade (50), posted as a senior clerk in the office of the Pune City – Shirur subdivisional officer of the Revenue Department and a private person identified as Tanaji Marne (46), a resident of Bibwewadi, who allegedly accepted the bribe on Badade’s behest.
Pune ACB had received a complaint from a man whose joint family was slated to receive compensatory land from the government because theirs had been acquired for the Temghar dam project. The eight members of this joint family are to receive two gunthas (a guntha is one fortieth of an acre) of land. The proposal for the final allotment of the said order was pending before the said office of the revenue department.
The complainant had approached the ACB earlier this month after Badade allegedly demanded a bribe of Rs 4 lakh — Rs 50,000 for each of the eight families for the final allotment. The bribe demand was verified by the ACB on February 7. The bribe amount was negotiated to Rs 3.2 lakh and a trap was set up at the office of Pune City – Shirur sub divisional officer on Monday. Marne was caught red handed accepting Rs 1.6 lakh from the total bribe amount. He was placed under arrest subsequently.

headline: IIT Bombay stopped collecting caste category information for placements from year 2024
description: This was revealed in IIT Bombay's response to the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) where a complaint of caste discrimination was filed in November alleging that IIT Bombay mandatorily asked students participating in placements to fill in their caste category.
content:
The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay’s Placement Office used to collect caste category information of students participating in the placements in order to provide it to Public Sector Unit (PSUs) companies coming on campus for recruitment. tThe practice, however,  ended in 2024 according to the premier institution.
This was revealed in IIT Bombay’s response to the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) where a complaint of caste discrimination was filed in November alleging that IIT Bombay mandatorily asked students participating in placements to fill in their caste category.
The complaint was filed by Dheeraj Singh, Founder of Global IIT alumni Support Group which has been helping SC/ST students in the placement process. In his complaint Singh had alleged that the placement Office at IIT Bombay was directly involved in carrying out discriminatory practices against students belonging to SC backgrounds who were participating in the campus placement; by making it mandatory to fill their caste-category and category rank in JEE exams.
Taking cognisance of the complaint, the NCSC, as per the procedure; had asked the IIT to submit an action taken report. IIT Bombay’s response to the NCSC states, “In the past, IIT Bombay Placement office used to collect category information of the students to give it to PSUs when they ask for the category information. The placement office stopped collecting this information from the year 2024 onwards. When PSUs recruit students, their personnel verify the birth category documents for positions reserved for certain birth categories. The placement office is not involved in collecting this data.”

headline: Sena ministers skip budget meetings chaired by Deputy CM Ajit Pawar
description: On Monday, the finance minister held a meeting of the Konkan and Nashik division. However, the meetings of Raigad and Nashik districts were not held.
content:
Shiv Sena ministers from Raigad and Nashik on Tuesday did not attend the district annual plan meetings for the 2025-26 financial year, citing prior commitments.
Deputy Chief Minister and finance minister Ajit Pawar on Monday did not hold the district annual plan meetings of Raigad and Nashik for the 2025-26 fiscal as both the districts do not have a guardian minister due to the ongoing tiff within the ruling Mahayuti alliance. The meetings were scheduled on Tuesday.
As part of the preparations for the upcoming state budget, Pawar has been holding a series of meetings with departments. He has also been meeting district administrations to discuss the annual plan for the next fiscal. On Monday, the finance minister held a meeting of the Konkan and Nashik division. However, the meetings of Raigad and Nashik districts were not held.
On Tuesday, Maharashtra Women and Child Development minister and NCP leader Aditi Tatkare attended the meeting called by Pawar. Sena minister Bharat Gogawale who also hails from the same district was however absent. Gogawale claimed that he had a prior commitment at Raigad fort, where an organisation of Hindutva ideologue Sambhaji Bhide arranged a program. “More than 40,000 to 50,000 workers of his organisation were to come to Raigad and I had informed about the same to the Chief Minister,” he said.

headline: Dhankhar expresses desire to deliver speech in Bengal Assembly, Speaker examines provisions
description: After getting bail, he filed an appeal in the Assembly to reimburse his salary during his jail custody period.
content:
Vice President Jagdeep Dhankhar on Tuesday sent a special messenger to West Bengal Speaker Biman Banerjee expressing his desire to deliver a speech in the Legislative Assembly, officials said.
Dhankhar, who remained West Bengal governor from 2019 to 2022 before he was appointed Vice President, sent as his messenger Sunil Gupta, a senior IAS officer, who met Speaker Banerjee in the Assembly.
However, both Banerjee and Gupta did not divulge anything to the media. A senior Assembly official said, “Gupta put forth the Vice President’s proposal before the Speaker but he has not taken any decision as yet.”
“There is no precedent of a vice president delivering a speech in an Assembly. Therefore, the Speaker did not take a decision right away. For this, he will have to call a special session and then take a decision,” he added.

headline: With 4% drop in Bengaluru Metro ridership, BMRCL to plug fare hike anomalies after public backlash
description: BMRCL managing director Maheshwara Rao said the corporation was bound by the recommendations of the Fare Fixation Committee; BJP MP PC Mohan asked BMRCL to increase non-fare box revenues.
content:
A day after the Bengaluru’s Namma Metro’s fares were hiked, the Bengaluru Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) on Monday, February 10, recorded a 4 per cent drop in ridership with 8.29 lakh passengers, compared to a usual Monday.
BMRCL officials attributed the decline in ridership trend to the opening of the mega aero show ‘Aero India 2025’, but the dip has raised eyebrows when Bengaluru Metro has positioned itself as the costliest Metro in India, with its maximum fare touching Rs 90. According to BMRCL’s previous data, the ridership is over 8.6 lakh on Mondays.
After revision, the minimum fare stands at Rs 10, while the maximum ticket fare has been hiked by 50 per cent from Rs 60 to Rs 90.
Following public backlash and staunch protest from BJP leaders at Metro stations, BMRCL managing director Maheshwara Rao told The Indian Express on Tuesday that the corporation would review the fare hike and plug anomalies, if any.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
“We are aware of the public feedback on the revised Metro fares. We are taking in the criticisms constructively. Since certain fare slabs have seen a significant increase, we will review them and plug the anomalies, if any,” said Rao.
He also said the Fare Fixation Committee (FFC) is a statutory body responsible for recommending Metro fare revisions, and BMRCL was bound by its recommendations. “The final decision is made based on the committee’s recommendations as BMRCL has to implement them as per the Metro Railway Act,” he pointed out.
BMRCL had written to the Centre on the constitution of FFC in 2020. However, it was constituted only in 2024 headed by a retired high court judge, and a representative each from the Central and state governments. The overall hike in Metro prices by 46 per cent and in some cases more than 50 per cent has caused significant outcry among passengers.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Some commuters also pointed out to a 100 per cent increase in fares at certain sections. For example, Akshay Phadnis, taking to X, said that his ticket fare has increased from Rs 23 in January 2025 to Rs 50 in February 2025. “How can someone increase fares by 100%? This is my office route and I need double money for that route. Which is equivalent to almost 1 litre of petrol in which I can ride 45k. Why would I choose the Metro?”
However, BMRCL, defending the fare hike, stated that the hike was necessary to cover significant financial obligations, particularly loan repayments, which amount to Rs 500-800 crore annually. These payments include interest on borrowed funds and investments made to expand and upgrade the Metro network. The revised project costs and ongoing infrastructure developments, such as additional trains and station improvements, further contribute to these financial commitments, BMRCL said on Tuesday.
For instance, an estimated Rs 6 crore per station, totalling around Rs 300 crore, is incurred for certain upgrades. Additionally, BMRCL’s financial projections indicate an operational profit of Rs 200 crore in 2025-26. But the net profit is expected to be only Rs 20 crore due to debt servicing and other expenditures.
“The 2020 Fare Fixation Committee considered various factors before recommending fare adjustments, including debt repayment obligations (60-70% of revenues), maintenance costs, staff salaries (including dearness allowance (DA) revisions), and electricity expenses. Unlike Delhi Metro, which balances operational costs differently, BMRCL faces constraints due to initial capital expenditures and project financing agreements,” said a BMRCL officer.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The officer pointed out that there are additional financial challenges, such as land acquisition costs and project cost overruns, which have escalated by 30 per cent in some cases.
According to the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Centre and the state, the Karnataka government is responsible for partial funding of such overruns. BMRCL expects to spend Rs 1,600-2,000 crore on new trains for upcoming Metro lines, with each train costing approximately Rs 40 crore and the total fleet expansion estimated at Rs 3,000 crore.
“Regarding infrastructure enhancements, the demand for platform screen doors and other amenities for the public will be covered in revenue generated through the new fares,” said an official.
Slamming the Congress government for causing trouble to commuters, P C Mohan, Bengaluru Central MP, said, “BMRCL sought Rs 9,919 crore for the second phase of Bengaluru Namma Metro in September 2024. But the Karnataka Cabinet deferred a decision on December 6. Why? They are saying ‘no funds’ as it got drained by freebies and the flawed pursuit of an unscientific Tunnel Road. Now, Metro fares are hiked after 7 years, burdening commuters”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He also advised BMRCL to increase non-fare box revenues. “Public transport must be affordable. Cities like Singapore and Hong Kong understand this—they incentivise Metro use. But after visiting and studying their models, BMRCL, under the Karnataka Congress government, proposes a 105 per cent fare hike to repay Rs 10,422 crore in loans. This goes against global best practices. Instead of raising fares, BMRCL should focus on tapping non-fare revenues. Leasing station air rights (property interest in the “space” above Metro stations) alone could generate over Rs 1,000 crore annually. For instance, building above and leasing space at MG Road and Trinity stations, Bengaluru, if properly utilized, could have made the Purple Line profitable—just like BMRCL has built office space above Deepanjali Nagar station to save on rent. BMRCL should have learned from them, not the opposite,” Mohan explained.
Satya Arikutharam, urban mobility expert, has called for urgent reforms in fare fixation to ensure a fair, scientific, and commuter-friendly approach. “Last December, the fare fixation committee submitted its recommendations to BMRCL on fare hikes apparently based on “studying” other metros. And this included a visit to Singapore and Hong Kong! It raised concerns over its independent functioning, as BMRCL officials accompanied them during the foreign tour. The hikes, exceeding 60 per cent on some routes, drive commuters back to two-wheelers, undermining public transport. Instead of a balanced fare policy, BMRCL’s decision could reduce ridership and revenue. Holding BMRCL accountable is difficult without an independent regulator like Bengaluru Metropolitan Land Transport Authority (BMLTA), whose functioning was stalled for decades by bureaucracy and political indifference,” Arikutharam said.
As of the 2023-2024 financial year, the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) reported an operational profit of Rs 29.3 crore, marking its highest-ever profit and the second consecutive year of profitability. This achievement was driven by fare revenue of Rs 735.48 crore against expenditure of Rs 606.18 crore. In the previous fiscal, 2022-2023, BMRCL recorded an operational surplus of Rs 108 crore, with revenues of Rs 594.01 crore and expenditures of Rs 486.61 crore.

headline: Ranveer Allahbadia’s ‘joke’ on Samay Raina show invites outrage, plaints, summons: What we know so far
description: Two days after the video clip featuring Allahbadia's remarks drew considerable flak, the episode of the show, which was shot in November and was premiered last week, was removed from Youtube.
content:
While your Twitter feed gets loaded with memes, visuals and debates on podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia’s “obscene” “joke” on comedian Samay Raina’s YouTube show ‘India’s Got Latent’, the Mumbai police Tuesday summoned the two panelists for an inquiry into the matter.
Two days after the video clip featuring Allahbadia’s remarks drew considerable flak, the episode of the show, which was shot in November and was premiered last week, was removed from Youtube. Initially available to members only, the episode is now unavailable in India following a government directive.
The comment triggered a row after it went viral on social media on Sunday, following which the Assam Police registered an FIR against five people, including the duo on the panel. The Mumbai police also began a probe into the matter, following a written complaint filed by Mumbai lawyers on Monday who claimed obscene comments were made against parents, women, and their body parts.
Opinion | Ranveer Allahbadia was crass, but he shouldn’t be banned
What has happened in the case so far? We break it all down for you:
Where did it all begin?

Samay Raina’s online show ‘India’s Got Latent,’ known for its dark humour, is at the centre of the controversy where content creators Ashish Chanchlani, Jaspreet Singh, Apoorva Mukhija, along with Youtuber-podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia, were invited as panelists. Notably, the comedy show has provoked uproar on social media earlier on multiple occasions.
During one of the latest episodes of the show, Allahbadia, who has over a crore subscribers on YouTube, asked a question from a contestant: “Would you rather watch your parents have sex every day for the rest of your life or join in once and stop it forever,” he asked.
Also Read | Ranveer Allahbadia faces fresh embarrassment as netizens discover controversial joke he cracked on Samay Raina’s show was taken from elsewhere
A clip of his joke caused a stir on social media on Sunday, with several prominent figures criticising Allahbadia and the other panelists.
Complaint and FIR filed
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Following the controversial question, two Mumbai lawyers, Ashish Rai and Pankaj Mishra, submitted a written complaint to the Mumbai police early Monday, claiming obscene comments were made against parents, women, and their body parts.
According to sources, a police team Monday afternoon also reached Khar’s Habitat building, where the show’s shoot was conducted. As reported by The Indian Express, Dikshit Gedam, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Zone 9, Mumbai police, said, “An inquiry is going on (in the matter).”
Moreover, Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, following the uproar, took to social media to announce that an FIR in the matter had been filed. The FIR in Assam was registered on the basis of a complaint by Alok Boruah from Guwahati. Boruah complained that the remarks caused “serious harm to public decency”. The case was filed with the Guwahati Crime Branch under sections of the IT Act and Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986 as well as section of the BNS pertaining to insulting a woman’s modesty and “obscene acts”.
The Congress’s student wing, National Students Union of India member Nikhil Ruparel, has also approached the Bandra magistrate court with a complaint seeking criminal investigation against Allahabadia, Raina, and the show’s organisers.
What Ranveer said in his apology
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Sharing a video over his social media, Allahbadia said: “My comment wasn’t just inappropriate. It wasn’t even funny. Comedy is not my forte. I am just here to say sorry. Many of you asked if this is how I’m gonna use my platform, and obviously, this is not how I’m gonna use it. I am not going to give any context or justification or reasoning for whatever happened, I am just here to offer an apology.”
The podcaster, popular as BeerBiceps, also said: “I personally had a lapse in judgment, which wasn’t cool on my part. The podcast is watched by people of all ages. Don’t wanna be the kind of person who takes that responsibility lightly. And family is the last thing I would ever disrespect. Need to use this platform better, that’s been my learning from my whole experience. I promise to just get better.”
“I have asked the makers of the video to remove the insensitive sections from the video. All I can say at the end is I am sorry. I hope you can forgive me as a human being,” Allahbadia added.
What politicians said on the controversy
Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis addressed the controversy, following the backlash. He stated, as quoted by The Indian Express: “I have come to know about it. I have not seen it yet. Things have been said and presented in a wrong way. Everyone has freedom of speech, but our freedom ends when we encroach upon the freedom of others. In our society, we have made some rules, and if someone violates them, it is absolutely wrong and action should be taken against them.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Shiv Sena (UBT) Rajya Sabha MP Priyanka Chaturvedi, meanwhile, said that she will raise the issue as a member in the standing committee of IT and Communication. “I will raise the issue regarding the show called ‘India’s Got Latent’ as a member in the standing committee of IT and Communication for the kind of vulgar, blasphemous content that is passed off as comedy. We need to set boundaries since these platforms influence young minds and they are passing off absolute rubbish as content. The language used by Ranveer Allahabadia, which was also actively encouraged by others on that ‘comedy panel’, is unacceptable,” Chaturvedi said.
What artists have to say
While Allahbadia offered an apology for his derogatory remarks, the controversy Tuesday took a fresh turn, with singer B Praak announcing that he has now canceled his participation in the podcaster’s Youtube show, strongly condemning the former’s comment and calling it “pathetic.”
Praak posted a video message on Instagram where he said in Hindi, “I was supposed to appear on a podcast, on BeerBiceps, and we cancelled that. Why? Since we are all seeing how pathetic his thinking is. The choice of words that he has used on Samay Raina’s show.”

He added, “This is not our Indian culture. What story are you telling about your parents? What are you even talking about them? Is this comedy? You are abusing people, teaching them how to abuse… I fail to understand this generation.”
Summons issued to panelists
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In the most recent development, the Mumbai Police said they have contacted Allahbadia and Raina, and called them for an inquiry over the controversial comment.
What action Youtube took
Following two days of heavy backlash, the entire episode of Samay Raina’s show was removed from Youtube on Tuesday. Initially exclusive to members only, the episode is now unavailable in India following a government directive.
The controversial segment was first edited out after Allahbadia had apologized for his remark on social media and also requested the show’s makers to take it down. However, YouTube has now removed the entire episode.
Kanchan Gupta, Senior Advisor at the Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, confirmed the removal and wrote on X, “The ‘India Has Latent’ episode on @YouTube with obscene and perverse comments by Ranveer Allahbadia has been blocked following Government of India orders.”

headline: As Kejriwal meets party’s Punjab MLAs in Delhi, Congress leaders predict defections and a mid-term poll
description: Several Punjab Congress leaders attacked Kejriwal over the meeting, and said he should have brainstormed with AAP leaders from Delhi instead.
content:
Leaders of the Punjab Congress Tuesday criticised Arvind Kejriwal over his meeting with the Aam Aadmi Party’s state unit MLAs in the national capital, following the AAP’s defeat in the Delhi Assembly elections, and hinted that the party would soon split.
Congress MP from Gurdaspur Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa said while the meeting is an internal matter of the AAP, it reflects the confusion within the party after the Delhi Assembly elections were declared on February 8.
“Calling a meeting so soon shows that the party will break soon. There will be mid-term polls in Punjab. When a party loses, there is a discussion within the state, and MLAs of other states are not called. They are worried that what happened in Delhi may be repeated in Punjab,” he said. “Many are in touch with Congress over the past several days,” he added.
Randhawa said the meeting should have taken place in Punjab. “Only one person (Kejriwal) would have needed to go come here. The chopper and the chartered plane of Punjab would have been used to get him here. The people of Punjab would also have been able to see him,” he said.

Randhawa also said he raised the issue of terrorism and repeated grenade attacks in Punjab in Parliament, and pointed out what he called the apathy of the state government — including Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann. “The CM of Punjab did not show courage against the terror acts of Khalistanis. Pakistan is sending in drones with grenades and drugs deep inside Punjab. Why is the BSF, which has a mandate to act up to 50 km from the international border, not doing anything? I have twice written to the Home Minister for an NIA investigation into the grenade blasts on police establishments close to the Indo-Pak border but nothing has been done,“ he said.
Meanwhile, senior Congress leader Partap Singh Bajwa also claimed that over 30 AAP MLAs are in touch with his party, predicting potential defections and a possible mid-term poll in Punjab. Bajwa, who is also the Leader of Opposition, said Kejriwal might contest from Ludhiana to replace Bhagwant Mann, indicating the internal power struggles within AAP.
Congress MP Gurjit Singh Aujla said, “It is his party, he should hold a meeting, but if he is holding a meeting immediately after the defeat then it has a different meaning. He has lost Delhi, so he should call Delhi leaders and brainstorm, but Punjab MLAs have been called. Both his models, Punjab and Delhi, have failed”.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Gurjit Singh Aujla, who represents Amritsar in Lok Sabha, said Arvind Kejriwal wants to become the chief minister or wants to bring about some changes in the leadership of his party’s Punjab unit. “The people of Punjab are fed up with him, no matter how many meetings he holds, it will not make any difference,” he said, adding that 24-30 AAP MLAs were in contact with the Congress.
Punjab will not tolerate a CM from outside the state, and the AAP has already appointed many outsiders in the state, he said.
Speaking to media persons in New Delhi, Congress MP from Chandigarh Manish Tewari said it’s a “tragedy” that “Delhi has never understood Punjab”. “Unfortunately, Delhi will never understand Punjab because the state has a different ethos, a different culture, a different syncretism, and it ticks to a different beat,” he added.
He also pointed out that Punjab, as a border state, needs to be handled very carefully and the Centre needs to have a ‘border policy’ for such states. “Any political instability in Punjab will have very severe national repercussions. Punjab is a border state. Our western neighbour is always hyperactive in trying to subvert and destroy the peace of Punjab. Therefore, there are certain border states which need to be handled very carefully. The situation in the Northeast, Manipur, is far from stabilising and so the Government of India should really concentrate on having a border policy for the border states,” Tewari said.

headline: Crowd gathers at Mysuru police station after controversial post on Delhi polls, leading to lathi charge; 1 detained

headline: Children’s zone turns a hit at World Book Fair at New Delhi’s Bharat Mandapam
description: School children made a beeline to ‘Kidzkingdom’ at the recently concluded World Book Fair in New Delhi.
content:
“Today was the last day of school for Class X. We wanted to party. So we came here to buy some books,” says 14-year-old Shwetan Panga, who was at the World Book Fair at Bharat Mandapam, still in his school uniform. His favourite authors are J K Rowling and Robert Frost — he enjoys the rush that fantasy gives him; bravery is the aspiration. Running his fingers over the strap of his bag back and forth, and eyes fixed on the ground, he says he has read the Harry Potter series cover to cover.
At the nine-day-long book fair that concluded on Sunday, February 9, Hall No. 6 was dedicated to children’s books. In the ever-expansive space, with ceilings so high, one has to crane their neck to get a full view, the scores of children appear smaller than they are.
Panga was accompanied by his friend D K Anshuman Rohit, 14, who gets through maybe two books a year, outside of curriculum. But he says superhero comics have him coming around now.

At the children’s pavilion or the ‘Kidzkingdom’, one has to look before they step every few minutes, for a dash or a crash happens almost on schedule. It was crowded by groups of 20-30 students from different schools all in their respective uniforms and their teachers. As the children, sporting blue, brown, red and green uniforms, scattered to different corners, there came instructions: “Kids! Please stick together!”
Inside one of the stalls, Archit Bangwal, 10, was holding two Tom Gates and explaining to his mother why both needed to be purchased. He is a die-hard fan of comics. His mother Neeru Bangwal says, “I was not very fond of reading books. But I wanted to make sure that I inculcate the habit in my kids early on. His teachers also asked me to ensure he reads — you need that to even excel in mathematics, they had said.”

Neeru started with a National Geographic magazine subscription and her children got attracted to it due to the images. Now, RobinAge, a kid’s newsletter, is a mainstay in the home. Rabindranath Tagore and Sudha Murthy also feature heavily. “I love the humour,” says Archit who loves watching TV too. He reads over 25 books a month and thanks his teachers and school library for it.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The school library and the teachers who draw kids into them seem to be the unsung heroes of this story. Apart from Archit, two nervous girls from an Air Force school, another pair of loud, bespectacled students, and two university students at the book fair credit the library and the librarians for discovering their love for stories they enjoy today.
But in language, there is a rift. Neeru will sign her younger son up for Sanskrit, not French: “What is the point of it? They don’t understand it enough to do anything with it, and then in Class 10, Hindi suffers.”
An older woman, perusing the shelves next to her, agrees, “Haina? Time ki barbaadi hai. (It’s a waste of time) My granddaughter’s teachers want her to opt for it, too,” she says with a grimace. Archit, who stands by, doesn’t say anything. After a while, he just opens Tom Gates and starts reading.

Richa Jha, author and publisher at Pickle Yolk Books, leaning over a pile of books she has written, says with a lightness in her voice, “I think kids love to read. The thought of being with a book comes very naturally to a child. The experience goes off track when the parents come in as gatekeepers. ‘This is too advanced’, ‘this is the wrong kind of book’, ‘this is not moral enough’ — adult sensibilities spoil the fun,” she says.

About the brouhaha over screens too, she adds, “We can’t shun it. But if a child knows that, yes, there is space for this and for that, the child will take to both things and then seamlessly switch between them.”
All around, there is evidence for the case Jha makes. Another dash and crash, and books in the hands of the culprit are all over the floor. He picks himself up – and the books – and starts making his way to the purchase counter, this time slower.

headline: Pune likely to witness hotter-than-usual February this year
description: The high temperature in Pune is primarily due to the absence of northerly cold winds in the region, an IMD scientist said.
content:
After a hotter-than-usual January, February promises to sizzle in Pune. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has attributed the high temperature the city is currently experiencing to the absence of northerly winds and lack of moisture in the air.
At present, maximum temperatures in Pune are around the 32-34°C mark, which is higher than usual for this time of the year. “The month (February) will see higher-than-usual temperatures,” S D Sanap, scientist, IMD, Pune, said.
Sanap said the high temperature is primarily due to the absence of northerly cold winds in the region. “These winds have been absent, and thus central India and Maharashtra have been reporting higher-than-usual temperatures,” he explained. Moisture is present in the air but not enough to cause rainfall, Sanap added.
Pune witnessed an unusually hot January this year, with the city recording an all-time high temperature of 35.9°C on January 29. In fact, the first month of the year was one of the hottest Januaries for Pune, with the city reporting higher-than-usual temperatures from January 26 onwards, as per IMD data. An anticyclone earlier in the year had stopped the entry of the northern winds, leading to the spike in temperature in January.

headline: MCD commissioner to present Budget Estimates on February 13 during special meeting
description: As per the Delhi Municipal Corporation (DMC) Act, the MCD Budget has to be presented after approval from the standing committee.
content:
Days after the Aam Aadmi Party was routed in Delhi, the AAP and the BJP will witness their first face-off. Ashwani Kumar, Commissioner, Municipal Corporation of Delhi, will present the revised Budget Estimates Budget for 2024-25 and Budget Estimates for 2025-26 during a Special Budget meeting to be held on Thursday.
According to the Delhi Municipal Corporation (DMC) Act, the MCD Budget is supposed to be presented after approval from the standing committee. This will be the second term when the MCD Budget will be presented without the crucial committee’s proposal, given the non-formation of the standing committee due to an ongoing tussle between the AAP and the BJP.
The Bharatiya Janata Party has a chance of toppling the AAP’s hold on MCD before its elections take place in April, with just six seats short of the Arvind Kejriwal-led party, needing only four more councillors to shift allegiance to dominate the civic body.
The AAP secured a majority by winning 134 seats in the 2022 MCD elections, and the BJP got 104 seats in the 250-member House. The Congress secured nine seats, and there were three Independent councillors. With the BJP and AAP engaging in aggressive poaching of each other’s councillors, MCD’s tenure has been stormy since then.

headline: Rama Rajya plot: 5 more arrested in attack on Hyderabad temple priest; recruits promised Rs 20,000 salary
description: To establish Rama Rajya, Kovvuri Veera Raghava Reddy recruited youth via social media with a promised monthly salary of Rs 20,000.
content:
The Cyberabad Police Monday arrested five more people in connection with the attack on the chief priest of Chilkur Balaji temple on February 7. The main accused, Kovvuri Veera Raghava Reddy, was arrested on Sunday and remanded in judicial custody.
On Monday, Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy spoke to chief priest C S Rangarajan to enquire about his well-being. “Such attacks will not be tolerated,” he said, directing the police to take strict action against those involved in the attack.
Besides Raghava Reddy, who is a native of East Godavari district in Andhra Pradesh and a resident of Manikonda in Hyderabad, the five arrested include two women from Khammam and Nizamabad districts. They were remanded in judicial custody.
According to Ch Srinivas, Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP), Rajendranagar, Raghava Reddy started ‘Rama Rajyam’ in 2022 on social media platforms, including Facebook, and operated a YouTube channel. “He posted Bhagavad Gita slokas and motivated people to join the Army to protect Hindu Dharma. He also announced that individuals registering between September 1, 2024, and December 31, 2024, would be recruited into the ‘Rama Rajyam Army’ with a salary of Rs 20,000,” the DCP said in a statement.

Responding to this social media post, 25 people first met the accused on January 24, 2025, at Tanuku. “After four days of stay, they travelled to Kotappakonda, where they contributed Rs 2,000 each and had uniforms stitched by a local tailor. On 06.02.2025, after receiving the uniforms, they gathered in an independent house in Yapral, Hyderabad, and took photos and videos in uniform with the organisation’s logo in the backdrop. On 07.02.2025, they travelled to Chilkur in three vehicles and committed the above crime,” the DCP added.
On February 8, at around 8 pm, about 25 people clad in black uniform barged into the residence of C S Rangarajan, the chief priest of the famous Chilkur Balaji temple. They demanded his support financially and also asked him to recruit people into the ‘Rama Rajyam Army’.
In his complaint, Rangarajan said the main accused, Veera Raghava Reddy, called himself the incarnation of Mukkanti (Lord Shiva) and landed strong blows on his face and body as three to four of his followers joined him. “They recorded the whole thing with cell phone cameras… They threatened me with dire consequences if I did not listen to them, and the result would be dangerous… They also asked me to recruit people for his Sainyam (army) and support his causes monetarily,” Rangarajan further said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He said his disciples found out that in many videos on social media, the accused was claiming that he could go to any extent and even take people’s lives if required. “If such persons are allowed to create a parallel army like Naxals in the name of Rama Sena it will be dangerous,” Rangarajan added in the complaint.
The alleged attack occurred on February 7 and came to light on Sunday after the chief priest’s father and Temples Protection Movement convenor M V Soundararajan reached out to the media.
He said a group claiming to establish its “version of Rama Rajya by forming private armies to punish those who do not accept their mission or agenda” was behind the attack.
Moinabad police inspector G Pavan Kumar Reddy told indianexpress.com that the main accused calls himself the ruler of the sainyam (army) spread across Andhra Pradesh and Telangana and that his word alone should be followed. “The group has warned Rangarajan to accept their mission before the Ugadi festival or face consequences,” the inspector further said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He added that the main accused allegedly wanted Rangarajan to spread the message of “dharma rakshana” (protection of religion) just like priests of other religions do.
The accused have been booked under Sections 189(2) (unlawful assembly), 333 (house trespass), 308(5) (extortion), 115(2) (causing hurt), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace), 351(3) (threat involving death, grievous injury or destruction of property) and 190 (applicable to every member of the group) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

headline: High on hype: How investment announcements at Karnataka Global Investors Meet fared?
description: Karnataka is all set to host the next GIM from February 12-14.
content:
Though the biennial Global Investors Meet (GIM) in Karnataka has grabbed headlines for the Memorandum of Understandings (MoUs) signed during the event, data shows that only a fraction of the investment promised was realised. The same was the case with investment proposals cleared by the State High Level Clearance Committee (SHLCC) and State Level Single Window Clearance Committee (SLSWCC), according to data.
Karnataka is all set to host the GIM from February 12-14, eyeing investment proposals worth Rs 10 lakh crore. The last GIM was held from November 2 to 4, 2022, in Bengaluru, after its previous edition in 2020 was postponed due to the Covid-19 pandemic. Following the event that cost the state exchequer Rs 74.99 crore, then Industries Minister Murugesh Nirani had said that Karnataka had received investment proposals worth Rs 9.81 lakh crore during the three-day summit.
However, in a response to an unstarred question by JD(S) MLC S L Bhojegowda in the Legislative Council in February 2024, the Industries Department said that the total value of the 57 MoUs signed by the government at GIM-2022 was 5.41 lakh crore. The total number of jobs projected to be generated due to the investment was 2.81 lakh.
The reply also revealed that 14-months since the investments were announced, only two projects worth around Rs 22,000 crore – 4 per cent of the value of MoUs signed – had received clearance from SHLCC and SLSWCC. While SHLCC clears projects valued over Rs 500 crore, SLSWCC approves investment projects costing Rs 15 crore to Rs 500 crore.

Of the remaining, 18 projects had applied for clearance while 37 companies that signed MoUs with the government had not applied for approval from the two Committees. Though the companies have three years after signing MoUs to set up industries, the data reflected allegations that only a small portion of the investment was realised.
The issue was highlighted during a discussion in the Council over GIM expenditure in the 2022 winter session of the legislature. Congress MLC U B Venkatesh had noted that during the first GIM in 2010, the government claimed to have signed MoUs worth Rs 3.94 lakh crore. “But in reality, only 14 per cent of the proposals were realised,” he had said. The Congress, which was in the Opposition then, had also flagged the massive expenditure for the three-day event.
For the current edition of GIM scheduled from February 12 to 14, the Karnataka government cleared an expenditure of Rs 75 crore in a Cabinet meeting held in June 2024.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Other clearances
The trend of big-ticket investment announcements remaining on paper is also seen among projects cleared by SHLCC and SLSWCC.
Data shows that between 2013-14 to 2024-25, the SHLCC cleared 260 projects worth Rs 6.45 lakh crore. As of November 2024, less than half of these projects valued at a quarter of the total investment promised – 106 worth Rs 1.65 lakh crore – was implemented. While 34 projects were dropped, 120 were ‘under implementation’.
Even the projects cleared by SHLCC in 2013-14 were under implementation, according to data. In the said year, 46 projects worth Rs 39,450 crore were cleared, of which 20 with an investment of Rs 22,210 crore were implemented, 10 (Rs 5,023 crore) were under implementation and 16 projects (Rs 12,216 crore) were dropped. Similarly of the 36 projects worth Rs 52,148 crore cleared in 2014-15, 17 worth Rs 4,803 crore were realised, 12 (Rs 44,507 crore) were under implementation and seven (Rs 2,837 crore) were dropped.
A similar trend is also seen in projects approved by SLSWCC. In the period between 2013-14 to 2024-25, the Committee cleared 3,681 projects worth Rs two lakh crore. As of November 2024, only 579 projects worth Rs 42,808 crore were implemented, while 2,759 proposals worth Rs 1.42 lakh crore were ‘under implementation’. The number of projects dropped was 343, valued at Rs 15,449 crore.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
For GIM 2025, Karnataka Industries Minister M B Patil has said that investment to the tune of Rs 10 lakh crore was expected across key sectors. The minister said recently that the government had set a target of realising “at least 70 per cent” of these commitments.

headline: Car crash kills 2, leaves children orphaned in Ahmedabad

headline: Mumbai-Pune Expressway’s Panvel exit to be shut for 6 months from tomorrow
description: The restriction on the Mumbai carriageway of the Mumbai-Pune Expressway is due to the ongoing construction of a flyover and an underpass at Kalamboli Circle, said the Navi Mumbai traffic police.
content:
Vehicles will not be allowed to take the Panvel exit route on the Mumbai carriageway of the Mumbai-Pune Expressway from Tuesday for the next six months, said the Navi Mumbai traffic police.
The Navi Mumbai traffic police’s Kalamboli unit announced alternative routes to manage traffic flow during this period. “The restriction is due to the ongoing construction of a flyover and an underpass at Kalamboli Circle by the Maharashtra State Infrastructure Development Corporation,” said Tirupati Kakde, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Traffic), Navi Mumbai Police, who issued the notification.
The restriction applies to vehicles travelling towards Panvel, Mumbra, and JNPT via Kalamboli Circle. It also affects those heading towards Taloja, Kalyan, and Shilphata.
Vehicles on the Mumbai-Pune Expressway heading towards Panvel, Goa, and JNPT will be diverted 9.6 km before the Panvel exit at Kon Phata. From there, they will take a left turn to reach Palaspe Circle and connect to National Highway 48 (Delhi-Chennai Highway) to continue their journey.

Bittu said, “I request Maharaja Satauj (Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann) to spare people such as Rajiv Raja — my friend. He is a reputed industrialist, who is now being accused of extortion. The Punjab Police has also been raiding the houses of several other associates of mine, who are BJP supporters. All this is being done to revenge the AAP’s defeat in New Delhi. I request Mann to spare these small workers and arrest me if he has guts.”

headline: Bengal: Polls a year away, welfare schemes to get Budget push
description: The Budget Session of the Assembly is set to begin on Monday with Minister of State for Finance Chandrima Bhattacharya set to table the Budget on February 12.
content:
With the Assembly elections in West Bengal due early next year, the TMC government in the state is planning to allocate more money in social security and welfare schemes in this year’s Budget – the last one before the end of the five-year term of the government.
The Budget Session of the Assembly is set to begin on Monday with Minister of State for Finance Chandrima Bhattacharya set to table the Budget on February 12.
Officials told The Indian Express that two schemes —Banglar Bari, a housing scheme; and Lakshmir Bhandar, a financial assistance scheme for women — will be the government’s thrust areas.
“Banglar Bari will be the one of the key thrust areas in this year’s budget along with other welfare schemes like Lakshmir Bhandar, Kanyasree, Sabuj Sathi, and Rupasree. The revenue deficit may increase in the budget, but then government will not decrease the allocation in the social security schemes,” a senior official in the state Finance Department said.
Last year, the government had announced the launch of ‘Banglar Bari’ housing scheme, citing the Centre’s blocking the funds to the state under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY).
Announcing the launch of the housing scheme last December, Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee handed over the first installment for housing construction to nearly 12 lakh people belonging to the marginal sections of the society. She also announced that 16 lakh more beneficiaries will be given housing funds before the 2026 Assembly elections.
Fully funded by the state government, the funds are allotted to the beneficiaries of the scheme in two phases.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In the 2024-25 Budget, the state government alloted an additional Rs 12,000 crore to Lakshmir Bhandar schemeas it doubled the monthly allowance to beneficiaries of the scheme to Rs 1,000 for the general category, and Rs 1,000 to Rs 1200 for the SCs/ST communities.
TMC leaders said that the hike helped the party to win over women voters in the last year’s Lok Sabha election. Sources said that with women playing a crucial role in the elections, the Finance Department may further increase the amount.
Even as West Bengal’s fiscal deficit increased to Rs 68,250 crore in the 2024-25 Budget, an increase of nearly 37 per cent from 2022-23 when the fiscal deficit was Rs 49,966 crore, the TMC government had announced new welfare schemes and hiked incentives of existing schemes to benefit women, youth and different sections of the society.
The state government had also announced Samudra Sathi schem to extend financial assistance to fishermen and a scheme of one-time grant of upto Rs 1 lakh for artisans, including traditional crafts and trades.

headline: Man killed brutally after he spills food onboard bus in Delhi; 1 held
description: Delhi Police have launched a manhunt for the remaining suspects after arresting one.
content:
An abandoned body, a missing person’s complaint, and a post-mortem report led to the unfolding of the brutal killing of a 35-year-old cook inside a bus last week following an alleged fight over spilled food in Delhi’s Outer North district, police said on Sunday.
While one suspect has been arrested, a search is on for the other two.
The victim, identified as Manoj, was killed in an RTV bus in Bawana on the night of February 1 after he and his colleague Dinesh had catered an event in Sultanpur Dabas. “After finishing their work that night, they packed some leftover food and carried it with them. They boarded an RTV bus in which three people were already present, including the driver. While they were about to reach the Bawana Chowk, Manoj accidentally spilled some food which soiled the bus seats and floor,” said DCP (Outer North) Nidhin Valsan.
“This infuriated the driver and his friends. They allowed Dinesh to deboard at Bawana Chowk but stopped Manoj from getting down and drove ahead. They asked Manoj to clean the curry with his shirt. They then started abusing Manoj and thrashing him. Ashish, the driver, took out a rod and shoved it into Manoj’s private parts. After a while, Manoj fell unconscious. The driver, along with his accomplices, threw his body near the Bawana flyover and left the spot in their bus,” Valsan added.

According to officials, a PCR call was received on February 2 to report that an unidentified male body was lying by the roadside near the Bawana flyover. A police team rushed to the scene and found the body had no visible injuries. It was subsequently preserved at BSA hospital in Rohini, and an initial inquiry was launched, said police.
A day later, the victim was identified as Manoj, a resident of Gautam Colony in Narela, through his brother Jitendra. The family reported that Manoj had been missing since the morning of February 2. Initially, there were no allegations of foul play. However, a post-mortem examination conducted on February 5 revealed multiple internal injuries, including severe trauma to his “private parts”, said police.
Police inquiries established that Manoj and Dinesh worked as cooks at weddings.

Following the post-mortem report, a case was registered under sections 103(1) and 3(5) of BNSS at Bawana Police Station. Special teams were formed to crack the case and CCTV footage was analysed to trace the suspects.
One of the accused, 24-year-old Sushant Sharma, a resident of Karala, has been arrested, confirmed police on Sunday.
The two remaining suspects, including the driver, are absconding. Police teams are conducting raids to track them down, and further investigations are ongoing.

headline: Aero India begins today, Rajnath says will be biggest ever: ‘Showcases strength of new India’
description: Rajnath, who will inaugurate the defence exposition at the Yelahanka Air Force Station on Monday, said at a press conference in Bengaluru that defence ministers or representatives from at least 30 nations will attend the event.
content:
A day ahead of the opening of Aero India in Bengaluru, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said Sunday that the 15th edition of the premier air show will be its biggest yet and showcase the strength of a “new India”.
Rajnath, who will inaugurate the defence exposition at the Yelahanka Air Force Station on Monday, said at a press conference in Bengaluru that defence ministers or representatives from at least 30 nations will attend the event.
Over 900 exhibitors, including 150 foreign companies, and 90 countries will participate.
He described Aero India as a crucial platform that will drive the government’s vision of a strong, secure and self-reliant India. “Aero India is a platform that showcases the strength, resilience, and self-reliance of new India. It is not just crucial for India’s defence preparedness, but it also plays a pivotal role in shaping the future of our nation. It will demonstrate our defence capabilities and forge global partnerships,” he said.
“Our goal is to enhance collaboration in areas of common interest with our friendly nations, fostering deeper cooperation and shared progress. The event is not just a showcase of technology and innovation, but will also serve as a source of inspiration for our youth, fostering scientific temperament and a spirit of innovation,” he said.

According to a Defence Ministry statement, the exhibition spread over 42,000 sq m, will go on till February 14.
Rajnath termed the participation of more than 90 countries as a testament to a growing global confidence in India’s aerospace and defence capabilities. “Defence ministers or representatives from about 30 countries have come to participate in this event. The presence of Air Chiefs and Secretaries from 43 countries highlights the significance of this event — not just for India, but for the entire international defence community,” he said.
The Defence Minister said that India is now capable of indigenously designing and developing major platforms and equipment, and has also established a vast supply chain within the country.

“Advanced platforms like Light Combat Aircraft Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter Prachand and C-295 Transport Aircraft are now being produced in India. We have also taken a firm resolve to manufacture fifth-generation fighter aircraft within the country. From the advanced variants of the Agni missile, the Astra missile system, and the Pinaka missile system to the cutting-edge Hypersonic missile system and the Akash air defence system, we have built numerous success stories. These achievements have played a crucial role in strengthening our defence sector, making India more self-reliant and secure,” he said.
Rajnath said that defence exports, which touched a record figure of Rs 21,000 crore, would surpass Rs 30,000 crore.
