Gujarat government had granted its sanction to prosecute Sharma, a government official, in February 2012 which is mandatory under the criminal law.
The accused were facing charges of wrongful confinement, voluntarily causing hurt and criminal intimidation under the provisions of the Indian Penal Code.
The case witnessed multiple litigations on various legal points and eventually, the Supreme Court ordered to expeditiously decide the matter in November last year.
Gadhvi said that the two have been convicted for wrongful confinement.

headline: Pune Metro to launch rental e-bike service as feeder service for first and last mile connectivity
description: The vehicle battery is compatible with plug-in and swapping models, with a range per charge up to 80 km and will have live tracking and geo-fencing.
content:
To enhance passenger convenience and strengthen first-and last-mile connectivity, the Pune Metro has joined hands with private rental e-bike service provider that would provide service at the rate of Rs 1.5 per minute.
The Pune Metro has signed an MoU with TS Switch E-Ride Pvt Ltd with the hope to increase the Metro ridership. To start with, TS Switch E-Ride Pvt Ltd will introduce the service at 10 selected Metro stations which include PCMC, Sant Tukaram Nagar, Nashik Phata, Dapodi, Shivajinagar, Mandai, Swargate, Ruby Hall Clinic, Anand Nagar and Vanaz. There will be 50 e-bikes in the beginning.
“In the initial phase, the service will operate between Metro stations and locations where secure docking stations can be set up such as educational institutions, corporate/IT parks, SEZs, large residential societies, and government offices,” said a Pune Metro official.
The e-bike speed will be maximum of 25 km per hour with a capacity of two persons. The vehicle battery is compatible with plug-in and swapping models, with a range per charge up to 80 km and will have live tracking and geo-fencing.

headline: Four police teams formed to find 21-year-old who attacked five people in Bengaluru upscale locality on weekend
description: The Bengaluru knife attacker Kadamba and his associates are used to ambushing bikers on the streets late at night and robbing them, according to police sources.
content:
The 21-year-old man accused of serial knife attacks in the upscale Indiranagar area has six cases of robbery and assault registered against him in east Bengaluru, according to police sources. Kadamba S has allegedly been involved in crimes since 2022, when he turned 18, with cases in Indiranagar and Ulsoor police limits. In all the cases, chargesheets have been filed and Kadamba was released either on bail or anticipatory bail.
Meanwhile, the Bengaluru police have formed four teams to nab the accused who went on a slashing spree on the intervening night of February 8 and 9. The Indiranagar police have filed five separate FIRs against Kadamba over these knife attacks which injured five people.
“We are making all efforts to find the accused. We are confident he will be found soon. The deputy commissioner of police (east) is supervising this investigation,” said Bengaluru Police Commissioner B Dayanand during a press conference Tuesday.
Police sources said Kadamba’s father Suresh was also a history-sheeter in east Bengaluru, while his elder brother Vishnu S has had six cases of robbery and assault against him in various police stations in Bengaluru from 2018. The police said the family lives in the Binnamangala slum near Byappanahalli in east Bengaluru.

The modus operandi in the robbery cases filed against Kadamba in the past is one where he and one or two of his associates ambush bikers on the streets late at night and rob them, as per the police. The several cases registered against Kadamba in east Bengaluru include a mobile phone robbery in 2024, a motorbike robbery in the same year, another motorbike theft in 2023, two separate assault cases, and a house burglary in 2022. Notably, several members of his family, including his mother, brother, and sister, are also accused in the house burglary case.
In the series of five slashings, Kadamba, allegedly in an inebriated condition, attacked two pani puri vendors, a security guard, a delivery agent and a 19-year-old man who refused to give him a ride after he forcibly sat on the scooter by brandishing a knife.
The victims were slashed either on their necks or hands in the knife attacks that began at around 9.30 pm on Saturday and culminated with the robbery of a scooter and a mobile phone from a delivery agent at around 2.30 am on Sunday.

The news of the slashings spread rapidly on Sunday and Monday among the resident welfare groups in Indiranagar, leading some to suggest the possibility of a serial killer.

headline: Cheese Chor: ‘Customer’ dupes Mumbai dairy dealer, steals cheese worth Rs 43,000
description: The police said their teams are examining the call data records and CCTV footage to identify the suspect.
content:
The Mumbai police have launched a probe into the incident where an unidentified person, posing as a buyer, stole 84 kg of Amul cheese worth around Rs 43,000 from a wholesale dealer in Lower Parel on February 6, officers said.
The police said their teams are examining the call data records and CCTV footage to identify the suspect.
According to the police, the fraudster rang up the businessman, who was in his office on Delisle Road in Lower Parel at 2.11 pm on February 5, and placed an order for 84 kg Amul cheese and 48 litres of Amul cream and asked the complainant to get them delivered at his alleged shop named Global Dairy Products, near KEM Hospital, in Parel.
“I calculated the total cost of the goods and told him it would cost Rs 52,764, after which the caller informed me that he would confirm the order shortly,” the complainant stated in his complaint.

The man contacted the businessman the next morning, confirmed the order, and claimed he would pay the bill in cash after delivery. The man sent the order via WhatsApp to gain his trust.
“As I trusted him, I loaded the goods, which included 84 kg of Amul cheese in seven boxes of 12 kg each and 48 litres of Amul cream in four boxes of 12 litres each, into a tempo and sent them with my worker to Global Dairy Products around 11 am,” the complainant told the police.
Subsequently, the businessman called the suspect to inform him when the order was dispatched and reminded him to hand over the cash to his worker.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
However, as the worker could not locate the shop, he contacted the businessman, who in turn called the “client”. The suspect allegedly instructed them to stop near the ITC Hotel, where a man would come to collect the delivery.
“The man took the worker to Global Hospital and asked him to leave all the seven boxes of cheese in front of a Chinese hotel on the footpath. The worker followed his instructions and went with the man to deliver the remaining 48 litres of Amul cream. The stranger promised the worker that they would be handed over the cash at the shop,” a police officer said.
However, at the shop, the suspect claimed he had forgotten the keys and left to get them. As the suspect did not return, the worker began to sense something was wrong and informed his employer, who then attempted to contact the caller.
“As the phone was switched off, the businessman instructed his workers to return to the location where they had dropped off the cheese. They discovered that the products were missing,” said an officer.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The dairy dealer later visited the spot in person and made enquiries with the local residents and shop vendors, but did not find any lead. He then approached the NM Joshi Marg police station and filed a complaint.
The police have recorded a cheating case under Section 318(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

headline: Tiger which attacked forest guard held after 12 hours’ search in Sunderbans
description: Around 3.30 am on Tuesday, forest guards were able to tranquilise the tiger in Maipith in the Sunderbans.
content:
After more than 12 hours of search, the West Bengal Forest department finally managed to catch the Royal Bengal Tiger which attacked and injured a forest guard in the Sunderbans on Monday.
Around 3.30 am on Tuesday, forest guards were able to tranquilise the tiger, which is now under observation by the Forest department.
A forest officer said, “It is a male tiger. It is doing well and has no injury.”

headline: Know Your City: In a new audio tour, Bengaluru author Zac O’Yeah explores some literary landmarks
description: Zac O'Yeah wishes his audio tour of Bengaluru's literary heritage would nudge writers in other cities to come up with similar tours.
content:
Bengaluru is a city of books, bookstores, and readers. And if you pay attention to your surroundings, you will start noticing the marks that writers have left on the city for decades and even centuries. One of Bengaluru’s well-known authors Zac O’Yeah has curated an audio tour exploring some of these places on an app.
In the audio tour, O’Yeah — who is originally from Sweden and came to Bengaluru over three decades ago — explores the “book bazaar in the petes, the libraries in Cubbon Park, various literary landmarks related to famous writers who have lived in the city, and so on”.
The audio tour, which covers a walk of around six hours, introduces listeners to places around Avenue Road, the Mythic Society, and State Central Library, and figures such as B L Rice, the scholar who famously translated the ancient inscriptions of the region in the Epigraphia Carnatica. The narration provides context to the stops on the tour alongside recommendations for places where a tired walker can grab a bite or buy a book.
The history of the city is also brought to vivid life through O’Yeah’s voice — from the battles that were once fought here, to the immigrants who settled in the city centuries ago alongside the residents of the pete.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Jack the Ripper: Has a DNA breakthrough finally unmasked the murderer who terrorised Victorian London?
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
In an email interaction, O’Yeah talked to The Indian Express about how the audio tour came to be.
“After the pandemic lockdowns ended, I and some writer friends organised a book love weekend in Church Street, kind of a Back to the Bookstores festivity to help the bookshops that had suffered much during the lockdowns, and to bring people back to browsing in real shops rather than just online. I realised then what a great resource the Bengaluru bookshops are. They could become like a tourist destination for people visiting town,” said the author of the Majestic Trilogy of detective novels.
“Some younger people who attended the events told me they had no idea that Bengaluru had such lovely bookshops… So when the people who design these apps approached me about a collaboration, I thought it would be great to have an app that people can use to explore the literary heritage of Bengaluru… The book bazaar in the petes, the libraries in Cubbon Park, various literary landmarks related to famous writers who have lived in the city, and so on…”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
For O’Yeah, his audio tour is a guide he would have enjoyed as a new visitor to the city, and wishes writers in other cities come up with similar tours.
“When I first came to Bengaluru 33 years ago, I would have loved to have an app like this… Even a printed simple guide to the literary sides of the city would have been handy. So, for me, it has taken 33 years to learn about the rich heritage of Bengaluru, and the process was then very much about how to organise it into an enjoyable walk structure. So, people who download the app can visit various literary landmarks, browse in some library or bookshop they may not have known about previously, then stop for coffee at some cafe where they might actually see writers having an adda, and it is a very interactive app where people can decide themselves how long they’d like to linger on at any place,” said O’Yeah, who is also a travel writer.
On possible additions to the audio tour concept, the author said, “If people enjoy the idea, I’m thinking that there should be more apps like this. Maybe the next project would be to explore South Bengaluru where many legendary authors have lived around Gandhi Bazaar and Jayanagar and those areas. Or North, for that matter. R K Narayan wrote his first novel while living in Malleswaram, and so the Mal in Malgudi comes from there. Hopefully, writers living in other towns in India will also create apps for literary walks in their hometowns.”
The tour, comprising over 20 minutes of narrated audio in several sections, can be accessed on the Tourific App on Android and iOS for Rs 330.

headline: ‘Won’t let a single home stand here’: Ahead of ward election in Vadodara, BJP leader’s ‘warning’ to voters
description: The remarks were allegedly made when Patel, accompanied by BJP's City Unit President Vijay Shah, who is in-charge of the Karjan municipality polls, was campaigning in Ward 7 on Sunday.
content:
During an election campaign in a minority dominated neighbourhood in Vadodara, BJP’s district President Satish Patel kicked up a row after he was heard saying, in a purported video that has now gone viral, that if the party’s panel of four contestants fails to win in the area, “homes will be demolished”.
“If you ensure the victory of the BJP panel, I guarantee you that no homes will be demolished…but if anyone betrays us here and the BJP does not win, I also guarantee you that I won’t let even a single homes stand here…,” Patel could purportedly be heard speaking in Gujarati.
The remarks were allegedly made when Patel, accompanied by BJP’s City Unit President Vijay Shah, who is in-charge of the Karjan municipality polls, was campaigning in Ward 7 on Sunday.
Here, the party faces its one-time stalwart and sitting three-term corporator, Mohammad Yusuf Sindhi, as a rebel candidate from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP). The BJP, too, has included a Muslim candidate — Mumtaz Hussain Multani — in its panel of four.
The municipality will go to polls on February 16.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Express View on Himanta Sarma's allegations against Gaurav Gogoi: Self-defeating strategy
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Sindhi, who has been the Vice President of the Karjan Municipality in the past, is known to have much influence in the area, as per local leaders.
On Sunday night, BJP leaders campaigning for the four candidates, including Multani, could purportedly be heard warning voters about a possible demolition of about 500 homes, allegedly constructed during a previous tenure of Sindhi, on two government plots. The settlements — known as Mohammad Nagri and Wali Nagri – have been at the centre of the campaign in the area.
In his address, while warning the voters to “not go astray”, Patel purportedly said from the stage, “It is time to shake out the people who have looted the citizens in the name of the BJP… Ravan had so many boons but…Lord Ram annihilated him… There is only this much expectation from you that without fearing anyone, you should come out… Whatever he (Sindhi) has done, I will be with you and ensure that we will bring him out and punish him (Ene bahar lavi ne, tamara saathe rahine, hoon pote saza karwanu chu)…”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In his speech, Patel also alleged that Sindhi, who has been suspended for rebelling and filing nominations from AAP for the upcoming polls last week, had been “extorting” money from several residents in the area.
Patel’s comments were seconded by Shah, who could be heard saying in his speech, “It is okay if we do not have power, but dishonest people sitting in the seat of power is not tolerable for the BJP… There are lots of people here, who are from the Muslim community and the Dalit community… we trust you that you will choose the BJP’s symbol of lotus and ensure that our panel wins… We have to…set an example of victory of trust over betrayal.”
Shah also accused Sindhi of running gambling and bootlegging dens in the area.
When contacted by the The Indian Express, Shah refused to comment on the purported statements by Patel but said that the party had decided against fielding Sindhi owing to the complaints received against him. Shah said, “Last time, Sindhi was given a ticket from the party and over a period of time, we identified that he was indulging in wrongdoings. Local people brought several complaints against him before the party. It was decided that he should not be given a ticket this time… (In my speech), I have only mentioned working by the principles of justice as Lord Ram did…”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A senior BJP leader told The Indian Express that it was, in fact, Sindhi who had been threatening the residents that the BJP will demolish the homes if he did not win the upcoming polls. The senior leader said, “Mohammad Nagri and Wali Nagri have come up on government lands, bearing survey number 236 and 237, some time during Sindhi’s 15-year tenure in the municipality… These are illegal structures on government land. The residents are fearful that if the BJP is voted to power without Sindhi, the homes will be demolished. Patel’s comments were made in the context that if the BJP wins, it will regularise the homes and not demolish them, as has been the case in many other cities having encroachments in government lands.”
The Ward 7 in Karjan will see a contest between BJP’s panel, comprising Jyoti Vasava, Tarun Parmar and Pranavrajsinh Atalia along with Multani, and AAP candidates including BJP rebels Sindhi and Bharat Atalia along with Priyanka Machhi and Vinita Vasava.
While Sindhi could not be contacted, Gujarat AAP leader Gopal Italia said, “What do you expect from goons (gundas) of the BJP? Right from the top to the bottom, they have leaders issuing threats to voters, opponents, people and anyone who displeases them… It is not the first time that a BJP leader has threatened anyone…”
The elections to the Junagadh Municipal Corporation along with 66 municipalities, three taluka panchayats (Kathlal, Kapadvanj and Gandhinagar), and mid-term polls to Botad and Wankaner municipalities apart from other seats, which fell vacant due to various reasons, will take place on February 16.

headline: ‘AAP lost credibility because it didn’t do what it promised’: BJP MLA Satish Upadhyay
description: A former councillor in the erstwhile South MCD, Satish was also chairman of the Standing Committee. In an interview with Gayathri Mani, he talks about why AAP lost, why people chose the BJP, and his priorities for the constituency.
content:
Satish Upadhyay, former BJP state president and ex-vice-chairman of the New Delhi Municipal Council, has re-entered the Capital’s political arena with a bang — he defeated three-time AAP MLA Somnath Bharti in Malviya Nagar in the recently concluded Assembly polls. A former councillor in the erstwhile South MCD, he was also chairman of the Standing Committee. In an interview with Gayathri Mani, he talks about why AAP lost, why people chose the BJP, and his priorities for the constituency.
You defeated a three-time MLA. Was it a tough fight?
Any election is a struggle. Somnath Bharti was a three-time MLA from Malviya Nagar and it is not easy to defeat a person who has won for three consecutive terms. But our coordination was good and we were successful in convincing Delhiites that these people (AAP) did nothing in the last 10 years. See the state of Malviya Nagar constituency… People voted for change…
Malviya Nagar’s residents have raised the issue of a water crisis among other things… We will definitely address the water issue. But, along with this, there are other major issues such as roads in need of re-carpeting, sanitation, maintenance of parks… the sewage system has collapsed… These are some of the local issues and grievances of people, which I will take up after taking oath… It is my priority that we have to change the whole system. We will resolve all grievances of the people…
The BJP is going to form a government in Delhi after 27 years? Will the party ensure the representation of minorities and women in its Cabinet?
… I am not the right person to answer this question. It is the decision of the top leadership… It is important that everyone is equally represented and the party will keep this in mind and take care of everyone.

Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Rahul insulted Shivaji Maharaj with post offering ‘sraddhanjali’: Shinde
Why do you think AAP lost?
Because of lies and corruption… all their MLAs were criminals… The CM, former Deputy CM, and MLAs were arrested and jailed… They only abused the central government, the Prime Minister and Lieutenant Governor… The AAP’s credibility was completely gone because it didn’t do what it promised. It focused on everything — from politics to blame game — except governance. During the Covid pandemic, instead of caring about the people and fulfilling his duties as CM, he (Kejriwal) built a ‘Sheesh Mahal’ for himself. So, if a party loses its credibility, people will vote you out of power.

We believe in working for the people… Like Modi ji says, sabka saath, sabka vikas, sabka vishwas, sabka prayas… Modi ji’s guarantees are popular not only across the country but the world… People realised the truth and chose a double-engine sarkarthis time. They want a vision for Delhi and development.
You were NDMC vice-chairman and Arvind Kejriwal was a member of the Council. How was the equation between the two of you?
He never came to meetings and even if he did, he used to leave immediately… He never did anything in the New Delhi area or NDMC… Neither Delhi nor the NDMC were his priority… that is why he never attended any meetings…
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
With your administrative experience, do you think you will be the new CM?
Not at all… You should not ask me this question… Iski mujhe koi discussion ki bhi jarurat nahi hai…
What will the BJP’s first 100 days be like?
Shandaar hoga… The government will be formed and MLAs will take oath… After that, as the Prime Minister said, cleaning the Yamuna and welfare schemes for people will be our priority.
The BJP manifesto promised to deploy Anti-Romeo squads to check sexual harassment. Do you think this is good for a city like Delhi?
Our sankalp patra (manifesto) talks about every issue… When the government is formed… issues to be prioritised will be decided and we will implement them accordingly.

headline: Of 30 Punjabis deported from US, 14 reveal names of their agents; only two deportees are graduates: Prelim data
description: From Pakistan’s ‘Doctor’ to Dubai’s Sabi, some deportees have revealed nicknames of their agents who allegedly took lakhs to send them to the US via illegal ‘Dunki route’.
content:
Only two of the 30 Punjab residents deported by the US last week had studied till graduation, a preliminary database prepared by Punjab officials has revealed.
According to the data accessed by The Indian Express, fifteen others had cleared class 12 and six had cleared class-10 pass. Further, three deportees studied till class-11 and three others till class-8, while another deportee did not reveal his academic qualification, as per the data compiled by the officials based on the statements of the deportees.
A US military aircraft — an IC-17 Globemaster — carrying 104 deported Indians landed at the Amritsar airport on February 5. Those deported included 30 adults and a 10-year-old child from Punjab.
According to the database, at least 14 deportees have revealed the names or nicknames of their travel agents, while two said that they did not know the names of their agents. Another deportee has claimed that he himself had applied for tourist visa for Spain.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'

Of 14 travel agents named by the deportees, five are from Dubai, one each from Spain and Delhi, and others from Punjab including Tanda, Patiala, Ludhiana, Attari, Nawanshahr etc. Some deportees revealed nicknames of their agents such as Sabu, Doctor (from Pakistan), Happy, Rocky, Sandhu but have said that they are unaware of their full names or addresses.
Academic qualification of those deported
According to the data, at least 16 deportees mentioned Spain as a destination en route US, while nearly all had first travelled to Dubai.
Speaking to The Indian Express, a senior Punjab official said: “We compiled the data after deportees had landed at Amritsar airport. Some of them were reluctant to share names of their travel agents who took lakhs from them while others revealed nicknames and claim they do not know their full names or addresses. We are encouraging more deportees to reveal names of their agents so that formal FIRs can be registered for further investigation. Dubai and Spain have emerged as the common destinations in the journeys undertaken by nearly all 30 deportees while a few also travelled via UK and Italy.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Also read | Deportees from US reluctant to complain against travel agents, but have one request for Punjab Police
An SIT formed by the Punjab Police to probe into human trafficking Monday said it has registered 8 FIRs based on the statements of the deportees.
With a dream to settle in the US, thousands of youths from Punjab, Haryana and other Indian states take to illegal “Dunki route” via South American countries before reaching Mexico to cross the US border. For the journey that spans across months and via at least 14 countries, while some reach South America via European countries such as Spain, others take South Africa route. They finally reach Mexico by crossing dense Panama jungles on foot. This illegal journey to the US costs lakhs and even crores which aspirants pay to illegal travel agents who promise them a “safe entry in the US”. The families in Punjab end up selling their home, land, vehicles, buffaloes and other assets to send their children to the US via dunki route.
Details of journeys
The data has also revealed the startling details of the journeys that these deportees undertook for months with a hope to reach the US. From Italy to Spain, Malta to Armenia, Serbia to Bahamas and Vienna to France, the deportees have shared their journeys via several countries to reach US-Mexico border.
For instance, a 20-year-old from Punjab shared that his agent from Dubai first sent him to Italy, from where he went to Spain and then Mexico. However, after he was denied entry in Mexico due to some issue, he again went to Spain and then reached El Salvador, from where he went to Guatemala before reaching Mexico and the US border.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A woman deportee shared that she left from India after her fiancé had arranged multiple tourist visa to Spain for the journey ahead.
An Amritsar-based deportee shared that his agent Lio from Dubai and another local agent Satnam Singh made him reach Mexico via Brazil.
Yet another shared that his agent from Spain took Rs 27 lakh in 2022 and sent him to UK. Then in July 2024, he went from UK to Spain and then to Brazil before reaching Mexican city Tijuana to cross the border.
A deportee from Tarn Taran shared that he first went to Dubai on tourist visa, then ahead to Armenia, Serbia and Vienna (Austria), then to Spain, Bolivia and entered Mexico via other countries to reach the border.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A deportee from Jalandhar went to Italy in 2011, and later to UK, then to Spain, Guatemala and Mexico. He claimed he does not know the name of his agent.
Another one from Jalandhar shared that his agent from Nawanshahr took Rs 45 lakh to arrange Schengen visa to Spain, then El Salvador and he was further taken to Tijuana. Another Jalandhar deportee said that his Dubai-based agent Sabi made him cross dense Panama jungles on foot to reach the US border.
A deportee from Gurdaspur said that he went on his own to Europe in 2018 but later engaged a Pakistani agent named “Doctor” to reach Mexico.
A woman deportee from Ludhiana’s Jagraon revealed to authorities that she reached UK on study visa in January last year and later reached Mexico via Bahamas through an agent.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Another deportee said he paid Rs 15 lakh to an agent to reach Spain via Malta and then Mexico. Another woman deportee also said she went via Malta. Another deportee shared he paid Rs 43 lakh to a Delhi-based agent to travel to Mexico via Spain and Vienna.
Another Patiala deportee revealed to authorities that he traveled via Paris and Spain to reach Guatemala and finally reached the US-Mexico border.
One deportee from Patiala said that he lived in UK for ten months, then reached Spain in November 2024 and further traveled via El Salvador to reach Mexico.

headline: ‘Onerous duty’ on courts to be a watchdog, prevent abuse of sexual assault provisions: Delhi HC
description: According to the accused, the two met at their workplace. After he found out that the woman was with another man, she broke off the relationship with the accused.
content:
Granting bail to a man accused of sexual assault, the Delhi High Court Monday observed that an “onerous duty lies on the courts to be a watchdog” to prevent the abuse of the law.
Justice Neena Bansal Krishna was dealing with the bail plea of a man, accused of sexual assault by a woman, aged 24, with whom he was in a relationship for over a year.
According to the accused, the two met at their workplace. After he found out that the woman was with another man, she broke off the relationship with the accused.
While granting bail to the man, who had been in jail since May 30, 2024, Justice Krishna observed, “In the changing times, when women are emerging and becoming a relevant part of the workforce, it becomes the responsibility of the Legislature as well as the Executive to enact laws and implement them to ensure their safety and well-being… The courts have an equal corresponding responsibility to interpret and apply the laws pragmatically to given situations to ensure that the protection of law is a reality and not merely a paper protection.”
“However, a more onerous duty lies on the courts to also be a watchdog to apply an even hand and deal with a given situation in a manner to prevent its abuse and misuse by any person… In the present times… close proximity at the workplace results in consensual relationships which, on turning sour, get reported as crimes, making it pertinent to be conscious of the distinction between the offence of rape and consensual sex between two adults.”
While granting bail, the court imposed the condition that the accused man would not go “even in the vicinity of the house and workplace of the prosecutrix”.

headline: ‘Evade outside pressure like a batsman concentrating on the ball’: PM Modi at ‘Pariksha Pe Charcha’ event
description: Highlighting the importance of nutrition, Modi underscored India’s leadership in promoting millets globally.
content:
Nutrition, wellness, time management, and handling exam pressure: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed a range of topics with students during the 8th edition of ‘Pariksha Pe Charcha’ at Sunder Nursery on Monday.
Highlighting the importance of nutrition, Modi underscored India’s leadership in promoting millets globally. “The United Nations declared 2023 as the ‘International Year of Millets,’ and we promoted it worldwide,” he said, adding that proper nutrition helps prevent many diseases.
He described millets as a “superfood” linked to India’s heritage, explaining that festivals often celebrate new crops and seasonal produce. “Children should eat seasonal fruits and avoid junk food, oily food, and products made of maida,” he advised.
Encouraging mindful eating, Modi remarked, “Chew your food at least 32 times before swallowing and savour small sips of water.” He emphasised the importance of eating at the right time, citing farmers who start their day with a hearty breakfast and finish supper before sunset.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
‘Great friend of India’: PM Modi meets former UK PM Rishi Sunak
On the topic of wellness, he cautioned against equating it with the absence of illness. “Right sleep is essential for fitness and wellness,” he said, highlighting ongoing research on sleep’s impact on health. Stressing the value of sunlight, he advised students to soak in the morning rays and take deep breaths under a tree after sunrise. “Nutrition lies in what, when, how, and why we eat,” he said.
Addressing exam-related stress, Modi noted, “It is unfortunate how society has ingrained the idea that not scoring high marks in exams like in 10th or 12th means life is ruined.” Drawing a cricket analogy, he encouraged students to “evade outside pressure like a batsman concentrating on the ball” and focus solely on their studies.
Pushing back against the overemphasis on academics, the Prime Minister said “students are not robots”. He urged parents and teachers to create an open environment that fosters hobbies and personal growth. “Exams are not everything in life. Knowledge and exams are two different things,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Modi also urged students to embrace self-reflection and challenge themselves. “Many people do not fight their own battles against themselves,” he said. “Leadership is not imposed but accepted by those around you,” he added, stressing that behaviour, not words, earns respect.
Emphasising positivity, Modi said, “Identify the good qualities in others, such as singing well or dressing neatly, and discuss these traits.” He encouraged students to develop the habit of writing to better capture their thoughts.
On time management, the Prime Minister observed, “Everyone has 24 hours in a day, yet some accomplish much while others feel nothing is achieved.” He advised prioritising challenging subjects first and practicing exam papers to improve speed and accuracy. “Distractions, including phones, hinder focus,” he noted.
Offering a perspective on failure, Modi said, “Even if 30-40% of students fail in class 10th or 12th, life does not come to an end.” He encouraged students to view failure as a teacher and highlighted the importance of developing one’s strengths.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Prime Minister also addressed climate change and environmental responsibility. “Development has led to a culture of exploitation,” he remarked, promoting Mission LIFE (Lifestyle for Environment) and initiatives like planting trees in memory of loved ones.
At the end of the session, Modi reminded students, “The present moment is the most valuable thing. Live it fully, and it becomes a part of your life.”

headline: Retired foresters write to PM Modi seeking scrapping of Aravalli Zoo safari project
description: The retired officers said the Aravalli mountain range has been damaged beyond repair over the last few decades due to mining and construction activities.
content:
A group of 37 retired principal chief conservators of forests and other former Indian Forest Service (IFS) officers from across the country have recently written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, opposing the proposed 10,000-acre Aravalli Zoo safari project in Gurugram and Nuh districts of Haryana.
The foresters have also urged immediate conservation efforts for the ancient mountain range, citing the devastating impact of mining, real estate development, and deforestation.
Spread over an area of 692 km, the Aravallis extend from Gujarat to Delhi, spanning the states of Rajasthan and Haryana. In 2022, then-Haryana chief minister Manohar Lal Khattar stated that the first phase of the proposed Aravalli Zoo safari project would be completed within two years.
Calling for the scrapping of the Zoo safari project, the letter reads: “The aim of the Aravalli Zoo safari project is to increase tourist footfall in the state of Haryana and to increase government and private investment in the tourism sector. Conservation of the Aravallis is not the goal.”
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

‘Great friend of India’: PM Modi meets former UK PM Rishi Sunak
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
The former foresters further wrote, “Apart from increasing human footfall, vehicular traffic and construction in the ecologically sensitive area, the proposed safari park will also disturb the aquifers under the Aravalli hills that are critical reserves for the water-starved districts of Gurugram and Nuh.”
Also See | What will a jungle safari in Gurgaon’s Aravallis look like?
The aquifers are linked, so any changes can impact groundwater. The zoo safari project’s planned “underwater zone” might change water levels in the water-scarce area, as per the letter.
“The primary purpose of any intervention in the eco-sensitive Aravalli region must be ‘conservation and restoration’ and not destruction that projects like the zoo safari will bring… For Haryana state having the lowest forest cover in India at around 3.6%, the Aravalli range is the only saving grace, providing the major portion of its forest cover. If left untouched, the Aravalli range would be enough to bring back humidity and sufficient rainfall in this dry region,” Dr Arvind Jha, retired PCCF from Maharashtra, said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The retired officers said the Aravalli mountain range has been damaged beyond repair over the last few decades due to mining and construction activities.
“The mining mafia carries out the illegal quarrying of rocks with complete disregard to environmental norms for obtaining building materials to feed the hungry ever-expanding real estate industry in the National Capital Region of Delhi, Gurugram, Noida, Faridabad and Ghaziabad. We understand that the mining fetches Rs 5000 crore annually as royalty from mining companies but this revenue generation is at the cost of destruction of our rivers, mountains, forests. During 1972-75, the Aravalli districts in Rajasthan recorded 10,462 sq. km of area under various categories of forest. By 1981-84, the forest cover reduced to 6,116 sq. km,” the letter states.
“…Destruction of this fragile ecosystem is causing significant irreversible biodiversity losses, land degradation and decline in vegetation cover negatively impacting communities, cattle and wildlife living in the lap of the Aravallis,” stated Dr R P Balwan, retired conservator of forest, South Circle, Haryana.

headline: ‘Security transcends borders, there is no peace in isolation’: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh inaugurates Aero India 2025
description: The allocation of Rs 6.81 lakh crore to the Defence Ministry in the 2025-26 Union Budget is proof that the Centre considers it a top-priority sector, Rajnath Singh said.
content:
Highlighting the importance of modernisation in defence sector and the armed forces and expressing concerns over global uncertainties, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said Monday that “peace cannot be achieved in a weak state of security”.
He was speaking after inaugurating the 15th edition of Aero India, the biennial air show and aviation exhibition at Yelahanka Air base in Bengaluru which will be held till February 14.
“We often interact as buyers and sellers, where our relations are at a transactional level. However, at another level, we forge our partnership beyond the buyer-seller relationship to the level of industrial collaboration. We have many successful examples of co-production and co-development with like-minded countries. For us, there is no Indian security or Indian peace in isolation. Security, stability and peace are shared constructs that transcend national borders. The presence of our foreign friends is a testimony to the fact that our partners share our vision of one earth, one family, one future,” Singh said.
Citing global uncertainties, the minister said that India has never attacked any country nor has it been involved in any great power rivalry. “We have always been an advocate of peace and stability. It is part of our fundamental ideals,” he added.

'Very unfair' to US if Elon Musk builds Tesla factory in India, says Donald Trump
Speaking about the allocation for defence in the recently announced Union Budget 2025-26, Singh said that the provision of Rs 6.81 lakh crore to the Ministry of Defence, including Rs 1.80 lakh crore for capital acquisition, is proof that the government considers defence a top-priority sector.
He added that like the previous budget, 75 per cent of the modernisation allocation has been reserved for procurement through domestic sources with an aim to widen and deepen the capabilities of India’s Defence Industrial Complex.
Singh said defence manufacturers are working with a collaborative approach to strengthen the sector, terming the joint venture between Tata Advanced Systems Limited and Airbus for the production of C-295 transport aircraft in Gujarat as a shining example of this cooperation. He added that today India has become a Globally Preferred Destination for Aerospace Components and Complex System Assembly and the public sector and private industries are playing an important role in this transformation.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Shedding light on the accomplishments achieved at the last Aero India, Rajnath Singh stated that a number of high-tech products such as Astra missile, new generation Akash missile, autonomous underwater vehicle, unmanned surface vessel, Pinaka guided rocket, etc are being manufactured within the country.
He voiced the Government’s unwavering resolve to surpass the Rs 1.27 lakh crore defence production and Rs 21,000 crore defence exports figures in the coming times, and ensure that the defence sector moves ahead at an unprecedented pace.
During the curtain raiser press conference of Aero India 2025 on Sunday evening, Singh had expressed confidence that defence production will exceed Rs 1.60 lakh crore by the end of 2025-26 and exports will surpass Rs 30,000 crore.
In his speech, Rajnath Singh also compared Aero India to the Mahakumbh Mela which is currently underway in Prayagraj. “While Mahakumbh is the Kumbh of introspection, Aero India is the Kumbh of research. While Mahakumbh is focusing on internal strength, Aero India will centre on external strength. While Mahakumbh showcases the culture of India, Aero India will display the power of India,” he added.

headline: Free bijli-paani to Mahila Samman Yojana: Why AAP’s welfare formula failed in Delhi this time
description: This has been AAP’s go-to formula in the previous two elections, which it won by a massive mandate — it bagged 67 seats in 2015 and 62 in 2020.
content:
“Vote for AAP if you want to save Rs 25,000 every month”. AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal emphasised this message in nearly all his speeches in the run-up to the Delhi Assembly polls, explaining how every household in Delhi benefits from the government’s welfare initiatives — free electricity, free bus rides for women, healthcare through mohalla clinics, and free education.
This has been AAP’s go-to formula in the previous two elections, which it won by a massive mandate — it bagged 67 seats in 2015 and 62 in 2020. This time, the formula failed to resonate on the ground.
While the BJP made a stunning return to the Capital after 27 years, the AAP has been reduced to a mere 22 seats.
On the face of it, the party seems to have done everything right to beat rising anti-incumbency among the public. It launched its poll campaign last September, with a Janta ki Adalat at Jantar Mantar. This was Kejriwal’s first public meeting after he was released from jail in the liquor policy case. The party was also the first to declare candidates for all 70 Assembly seats. From September till February 3, it held different types of campaigns, public meetings, jansabhas and rallies.
What went wrong

What former Delhi CMs Arvind Kejriwal, Atishi said as Rekha Gupta to take Delhi’s reins
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
First, the AAP’s poll manifesto, except for a few schemes, had few new things on offer. For instance, the Mahila Samman Rashi Yojana was announced during the Budget last year and promised Rs 1,000 to eligible women but it wasn’t implemented. In December, Kejriwal announced that the monthly allowance would be increased to Rs 2,100 if the AAP returned to power. Two days later, the Rs 1,000 scheme announced in the Budget was cleared by the Delhi Cabinet but it was too late.
According to an AAP leader, the delivery of Rs 1,000 could have been a game changer. “Kejriwal being in jail for months meant the scheme could not be implemented earlier. By the time it was cleared by the Cabinet, it was too late to implement as the registration portal was not ready. This proved to be the difference between loss and victory,” the leader said.
The party’s ‘employment for all’ guarantee was similar to the one in the 2022 ‘Rozgar’ Budget, in which the AAP government promised 20 lakh jobs in five years. The scheme remained on paper.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Its promise to waive inflated water bills was also something it said before the 2024 Lok Sabha polls.
Other promises — 24×7 clean drinking water in all households in Delhi; cleaning the Yamuna; maintaining roads as per European standards; and replacing blocked and old sewer lines — have all been mentioned in previous elections and budgets.
Second, several of these subsidies were largely seen as benefitting the poor — JJ colony and lower middle-class households — who have been traditional voters of AAP.
This was reflected in the results on Saturday. Of the 22 constituencies that the AAP has won, 14 are dominated by Dalits and Muslims. Of the 12 reserved seats, the AAP won 8. Despite its defeat, the party has a 44% vote share — showing it has largely retained its support base among the city’s poor.
On the flip side, it lost out on the middle- and upper-middle-class voters who shifted to the BJP. Several residents had flagged issues over the lack of basic infrastructure development such as water, broken roads, pollution, waterlogging, and hiked electricity bills.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Third, issues in the delivery of welfare schemes caused anger among the public.
– Under its power subsidy, the government offered free electricity for up to 200 units and a 50% subsidy for up to 400 units. But between May and July last summer, several households complained of receiving inflated electricity bills — an increase of 6-8% — after the discoms revised the power purchase adjustment charges (PPAC) between 6.75% and 8.75%.
– Under its water subsidy, it offered 20,000 litres of free water. But in the past year, the public — from slums to upscale societies like Vasant Kunj — complained of scarcity, even in winter months, and dirty water. In the weeks leading up to the election, the AAP and BJP engaged in a slugfest with the former alleging the Haryana government was releasing “poisonous” water into the Yamuna.
– The AAP’s flagship mohalla clinics, Delhi government-run hospitals, and dispensaries faced a shortage of medicines and drugs owing to a government-bureaucracy tussle.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Following the party’s loss, a senior AAP leader said: “There was increased anti-incumbency because the AAP was in power for 10 years… For any party, there will be anti-incumbency… even for the BJP at the Centre… Our campaign went well but the lack of infrastructure work and the corruption that the BJP accused us of — like the liquor scam and Sheesh Mahal charge — worked in their favour.”
The leader added, “If you look at the percentage of votes, AAP has not lost its traditional base… But definitely, the BJP managed to sway the middle-class voters… We have a strong opposition and the AAP will continue to raise issues (in the House).”

headline: ‘Didn’t sleep for months, the scene kept playing in my head’: 15 years later, owner recalls how German Bakery blast changed her life
description: Snehal Kharose was 19 when a blast ripped through the iconic German Bakery in Pune’s Koregaon Park, killing 17 people. But that evening, she grew up, maturing with every hour as she took over the reins of the family restaurant.
content:
On February 13, 2010, Smita Kharose, the owner of the iconic German Bakery in Koregaon Park, went to the restaurant with her 19-year-old daughter Snehal and was there till 5.30 pm. They came home and Snehal slumped in front of the TV. A few minutes later, the restaurant manager called and said that there had been a blast.
“Stop trying to fool me. This is not something to joke about,” shot back Snehal. “And he said, ‘You turn on the news, I’m not joking’. He was all panicked and when I turned on the news, I saw that there was a cylinder blast at German Bakery,” she adds.
It was not a cylinder blast, as the family found out on their way to the restaurant. “When we were informed that it was a terror attack, we were like, ‘How do we go about this now?’” says Snehal.
The terror attack that changed Pune forever killed 17 people and injured 58. Fifteen years have passed and Snehal remembers that she and her cousin had to walk about 2 km from Le Meridien to German Bakery because the roads were shut. She can still vividly see the scene at what used to be one of the coolest places in the city. German Bakery was reduced to rubble, there were bloodstains and a kind of horrible stench.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
MP’s Hawk Force gun down four Maoists in Balaghat encounter
Also Read | 15 years of German Bakery blast | Rising from the ashes: As wounds heal, memories of a bitter past linger strong
“I didn’t sleep for two to three months after that because the scene kept playing in my head. Nothing prepares one for something like this – the noise of the ambulance, the chaos of people, being pulled to one side and being told, ‘You can’t go there. There is something there’. I was taken to the police station to give my statement. I had to go to the hospital to identify people,” recalls Snehal.
Her father, Dnyaneshwar Kharose had set up the restaurant with German national Woody Klaus in 1988 so that foreign nationals could find food and a vibe that would feel like home. Dnyaneshwar had no background in the hotel industry or any concept in mind for the restaurant but he was full of passion to get new things done.
Far from its present chic and fancy avatar, the original German Bakery was shack-like but filled with people reading, playing guitars, relaxing over games, food and music or just catching up. Snehal would run to the tables and the guests would pamper her, calling her Nanu’s daughter after her father. Dnyaneshwar passed away in 1999 and Smita, who was a homemaker, began to take care of the three children as well as the business. “She struggled after my dad passed away,” says Snehal.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
A regular teenager, Snehal was an average student who wanted to study law and go abroad. She did not have any kind of aspirations in the hotel industry. But on the evening of the blast, she grew up, maturing with every hour as she took over the reins of the restaurant. “I look back at how I did it and I think everything just happened. When things fall on you, you somehow tend to manage it. That’s a miracle,” she adds.
Snehal, who is the eldest child in the family, soon became the face of German Bakery. She gave interviews to the media, choosing her words wisely as the site was part of a terror investigation. She dealt with the property being sealed by the Anti-Terror Squad (ATS) and “just kept going with the flow”. What helped was that her mother trusted her and said that she could do it. “I am here because of my mother,” she underlines.
It took three years for German Bakery to reopen. “I know the struggle that I had to go through to start it. We didn’t have the finances. The restaurant was the only source of income for the family and when it shut, we faced a challenge. There was my younger sister’s education and care for my brother, who is a special child,” Snehal says.
Today, German Bakery has a classy ambience where people can have meetings, a get-together or a date. There are also 30 cameras, a metal detector and security at the gate. “We have to take precautions. At the back of your mind, a fear lingers,” says Snehal. There are, however, more German Bakery outlets, in Hinjewadi, Lonavala and the Expressway, and another is in the pipeline. The two old trees that stood like an umbrella over the diners at the old bakery, however, still stand guard on a new generation.

headline: 15 years of German Bakery blast | Rising from the ashes: As wounds heal, memories of a bitter past linger strong
description: 15 years ago a bomb ripped through the iconic German Bakery in Koregaon Park killing 17 youngsters on February 13,the eve of Valentine Day. A decade and a half later Indian Express revisits that difficult time that changed Pune forever.
content:
The aroma of freshly baked cookies still wafts through the air at German Bakery in Pune’s Koregaon Park, much like it did fifteen years ago. But for those who remember February 13, 2010, the sweet scent carries with it a hint of bittersweet memories.
February 13, 2010, began like any other Saturday at German Bakery. The winter evening air was crisp, and the bakery hummed with its usual weekend energy. Foreign tourists from the nearby Osho International Meditation Resort lounged at corner tables, while college students clustered around their favourite spots, the aroma of fresh pastries and coffee creating the familiar, cosy atmosphere the establishment was known for.
The blast claimed 17 lives, including five foreign nationals and a staff member and injured over 50 others.
“It was one of those typically busy weekends. The tables were full, and there was a constant flow of people coming in and out. Through the steady stream of customers, a person entered, seemingly unremarkable among the diverse clientele that typically frequented the bakery. He carried a bag and placed it under one of the tables. In a busy place like ours, with so many tourists often temporarily leaving their bags while ordering, it didn’t immediately raise alarms. However, the person left, blending into the crowd outside without taking the bag. Our staff noticed the unattended bag after some time and intended to check for identification while attempting to open it, the package exploded. It was around 7.15 pm, “ explained Snehal Kharose, founder of the German Bakery.
The German Bakery blast, also known as the 2010 Pune bombing, was a terror attack, which shook the city to its core, it happens to be the first major terror attack in India since the 2008 Mumbai attacks. The blast claimed 17 lives, including five foreign nationals and a staff member and injured over 50 others.

Islamist groups, Lashkar-e-Taiba and the Indian Mujahideen claimed responsibility for the bombing. Mirza Himayat Baig, a resident of Maharashtra, was arrested after investigators found explosives at his home and Abdul Samad, a resident of Bhatkal, a coastal town in the Uttar Kannada district of Karnataka, was identified as the prime suspect.
The three-year closure following the blast left many wondering if the establishment would ever return. “We were initially hesitant to start again, would people visit us after such a traumatizing incident? But to our surprise, we have witnessed rising footfalls over the years after reopening in 2013,” said Kharose.
“While the demographic has shifted with fewer foreign tourists compared to its pre-2010 heyday, the bakery has found a new identity. Our clientele now includes college students, young professionals, and families. They visit not just for the culinary experience but also for the story of resilience this place represents,” said Kunal Udane, current owner of the German Bakery. “To avoid repetition of any untoward incident we have weekly Police checks, monthly bomb squad visits and regular checking is done by our private security agency.”

“Every morning when I unlock the eatery’s doors, I’m reminded of how far we’ve come,” says Tukaram Bhekane, manager at the German Bakery. “The spirit of this place is different now, but somewhat stronger.”
“The eatery stands as a testament to resilience, having risen from the ashes of what was Pune’s first brush with terror. This place represents Pune’s unbreakable spirit. Every time I visit with my friends here, I tell them – this is where we choose hope over fear,’ said Payal Sharma, who has been visiting the place since its reopening in 2013.

headline: Medical aid to Dallewal stopped as doctors unable to find veins for drip, say farmer bodies
description: Convenor of SKM (Non-Political), Dhallewal has been on a fast-unto-death on the Khanauri border point since November 26 last year, seeking legal guarantee of minimum support price for crops, among other demands.
content:
Two prominent farmer bodies on Sunday claimed that medical aid to fasting farmer leader Jagjit Singh Dallewal has been stopped for the past six days as doctors are unable to find his veins for administering intravenous drip.
“Dallewal’s medical aid has been stopped for the past six days because his veins are blocked and doctors are unable to find his veins to insert (intravenous) drip,” the Samyukta Kisan Morcha (Non-Political) and the Kisan Mazdoor Morcha (KMM) said in a joint statement.
Convenor of SKM (Non-Political), Dhallewal has been on a fast-unto-death on the Khanauri border point since November 26 last year, seeking legal guarantee of minimum support price for crops, among other demands.
He started getting medical aid after a Centre government delegation led by joint secretary (agriculture) Priya Ranjan on January 18 invited SKM (Non-Political) and KMM for talks to discuss their demands in Chandigarh on February 14.

However, Dallewal did not end his fast and was being given intravenous fluids.
A team of government doctors has been deputed at the Khanauri protest site. Dallewal earlier said that he would not end his fast- unto-death till the Centre accepted the farmers’ demands, including a legal guarantee of MSP for crops.
Meanwhile, both the SKM (Non-Political) and KMM are preparing to hold ‘Kisan Mahapanchayats’ at Ratanpura in Rajasthan (February 11), Khanauri border (February 12), and Shambhu border (February 13) to mark the completion of one year of the ongoing protest.

headline: Maharashtra: Financial stress shows, funds for ‘populist’ schemes delayed
description: In 2024-25, the government allocated Rs 30 crore, of which Rs 20 crore has already been spent. The Social Justice Department required an additional Rs 25 crore to complete the pilgrimages planned for the year.
content:
With state finances getting stretched, the Devendra Fadnavis government in Maharashtra has held back funds for the ‘Mukhyamantri Teerth Darshan Yojana’, a programme that sponsors senior citizens to visit pilgrim spots. The scheme was launched in June-end, about five months months before the 2024 Assembly elections.
In a Cabinet meeting last week, the government also discussed discontinuing two other schemes, the Shiv Bhojan Thali (cooked food including chapati, rice, daal and sabji) for the poor, and Anandacha Shidha (a kit of grocery items such as sugar, edible oil, chanadaal, sooji, distributed during festive occasions), also for the poor. Together, the state spent Rs 1,300 crore so far in the current financial year.
Between July and October last year, 6,424 senior citizens participated in nine tours to Ayodhya’s Shriram Temple under the Teerth Darshan Yojana. But after the elections, only one trip, with 800 beneficiaries from Nagpur, went to Gaya, Bihar. There are 13 more tours planned to Ayodhya, and one to Puri, Odisha; these have been held back for now.

“We are focusing on cutting expenses as much as possible. Several decisions were made ahead of the elections, and this is one of them. We are reviewing the program and may put it on hold for a while,” a senior Finance Department official told The Indian Express.

The delay is on account of the Finance Department’s inability to release a Rs 25-crore tranche to facilitate 13 pilgrimages to the Ram temple in Ayodhya.
When contacted, Om Prakash Bakoria, the state’s Social Welfare Commissioner, overseeing the pilgrimage program, denied finances were an issue. “The ongoing Mahakumbh has caused delays in the 13 trips to Ayodhya. We will finalise the dates once the Mahakumbh concludes.” He said plans for the Puri trip were also underway.
In the run-up to the Assembly elections, the state government rolled out a series of schemes, including the Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana, the Annapurna Yojana, free professional education for girls, the Teerth Darshan Yojana, and a power bill waiver for farmers. Cumulatively, these initiatives are estimated to cost the state exchequer over ?1 lakh crore, which the Ladki Bahin Yojana (Rs 1,500 per month to women below the poverty line) itself entails payout of Rs 46,000 crore.

These programmes have started exerting pressure on the government’s deficit and debt burden. In the budget for 2024-25, the fiscal deficit was estimated at Rs ?1.10 lakh crore. After the announcement of the schemes, including Ladki Bahin, the Finance Department officials said it was estimated to cross Rs 2 lakh crore.
The Mukhya Mantri Teerth Darshan Yojana, a pilgrimage scheme for senior citizens of all religions, was first announced by former Chief Minister Eknath Shinde on June 28, 2024.
Under the scheme, Rs 30,000 is provided to a senior citizen over 60 years with a family income under Rs 2.5 lakh to visit 161 pilgrimage sites in Maharashtra and 88 across India.
In 2024-25, the government allocated Rs 30 crore, of which Rs 20 crore has already been spent. The Social Justice Department required an additional Rs 25 crore to complete the pilgrimages planned for the year.

Recently, the state recently decided to strike off five lakh ineligible women from the Ladki Bahin scheme. Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister Ajit Pawar has emphasised the need for fiscal discipline. “As Finance Minister, I must make tough decisions. Last year, some concessions were made due to the elections, but for the next five years, we need to maintain financial discipline,” he said.

headline: After Delhi victory, BJP eyes its next goal — winning MCD Mayoral polls
description: The mayoral elections are expected to be held in April, and the BJP is working to consolidate its numbers and wrest control of the MCD from the AAP
content:
After securing a huge win in the Assembly elections on Saturday, the BJP has now set its sights on the upcoming mayoral elections of the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) to extend its reach from a metaphorical “double engine”, at the Centre and city-state level, to a “triple engine”.
With a victory in 48 of 70 Assembly seats, the BJP has ended the AAP’s 11-year rule and reduced the party’s tally from 62 to 22.
The mayoral elections are expected to be held in April, and the BJP is working to consolidate its numbers and wrest control of the MCD from the AAP, which party insiders said, is not going to be an uphill task.
In the 2022 MCD elections, AAP secured a majority by winning 134 seats in the 250-member House while the BJP won 104 seats. The Congress managed to secure nine seats, and three councillors were independents. However, the MCD’s tenure since then has been tumultuous, with both the BJP and AAP engaging in aggressive poaching of each other’s councillors.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Together at Shivneri, alone at padyatra: Fadnavis walks alone as Ajit Pawar, Shinde give BJP function a miss
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
As per the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, the MCD is required to elect a new mayor and deputy mayor for which elections are supposed to be held in April every year.
Apart from the councillor, 14 MLAs (nominated from parties in proportion to their representation in the Delhi Assembly), seven Lok Sabha MPs (all BJP) and three Rajya Sabha MPs (at the moment, all of them are from AAP) are going to be a part of the mayoral electorate.
In the previous mayoral elections, the BJP had only one nominated MLA. Given that their numbers in the Delhi Assembly have now increased, the number of elected MLAs who will be a part of the electorate during the upcoming mayoral elections will also see an increase.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The 2023 mayoral polls had seen a delay for eight months due to the non-appointment of a presiding officer by L-G V K Saxena. When the elections were finally held in November last year, AAP’s Mahesh Kumar Khichi had won by a razor-thin margin of just three votes. The results had also exposed friction within AAP as eight of its votes went to the BJP, which had signalled potential vulnerability within the AAP.
To be sure, the anti-defection law does not apply to the MCD councillors leading to constant defections, which have significantly altered the composition of the House. Ahead of the Assembly polls, the BJP’s numbers had climbed to 120 while AAP’s tally had dropped to 121.
The Assembly polls further impacted these figures as AAP has now lost three of its councillors who have successfully transitioned into MLAs — Punardeep Singh Sawhney (Chandni Chowk), Prem Chauhan (Deoli), and Aaley Iqbal (Matia Mahal). This has reduced its total to 118.
On the other hand, the BJP saw eight of its MCD councillors enter the Assembly — Ravinder Singh Negi (Patparganj), Shikha Roy (Greater Kailash), Chandan Chaudhary (Sangam Vihar), Gajender Daral (Mundka), Neelam Pehelwan (Najafgarh), Poonam Sharma (Wazirpur), Umang Bajaj (Rajender Nagar), and Rekha Gupta (Shalimar Bagh). Additionally, Rajkumar Bhatia, an L-G-appointed MCD alderman, won the Adarsh Nagar seat. These developments brought the BJP’s tally in the MCD down to 112.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
With just six seats short of AAP, the BJP needs only four more councillors to dominate the civic body.

headline: Bombay High Court grants bail to 2 men arrested for plotting attack on Salman Khan near Panvel farmhouse
description: The Panvel Town police in Navi Mumbai had claimed that the gang planned to use sophisticated weapons, including AK-47, from Pakistan for the attack.
content:
The Bombay High Court Thursday granted bail to two men arrested in 2024 for an alleged conspiracy to attack Bollywood actor Salman Khan near his Panvel farmhouse. The Navi Mumbai police alleged that a contract of Rs 25 lakh was given by jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi to his gang members to attack the actor while he was leaving a film shoot.
It was believed to be a ‘second’ plot to attack the actor, the first being firing outside his Bandra residence in Mumbai on April 14 last year. The police had claimed that nearly 16-17 people were involved in conducting a recce at Panvel in February last year.
A single-judge bench of Justice Nitin R Borkar on February 6 granted bail to Vaspi Mehmud Khan alias Vasim Chikna and Gaurav Vinod Bhatia alias Sandeep Bishnoi. The plea was argued through advocates Tanveer Aziz Patel and Anil Yashwant Chaware. The detailed order will be made available in due course.
The HC noted that beyond the accused being part of WhatsApp group on which the alleged conspiracy was discussed, no sufficient incriminating evidence was produced against them. The Panvel Town police in Navi Mumbai, in its chargesheet, had claimed that the gang planned to use sophisticated weapons, including AK-47, from Pakistan for the attack.

The lawyers for bail applicants argued that the accused were falsely implicated in the case and the sessions court had rejected their bail pleas due to media attention. They argued that as the co-accused Deepak Gogalia was granted bail earlier and as their clients were not part of Lawrence Bishnoi Gang to hatch any conspiracy, they should be released on bail.
However, the lawyer representing the police opposed the bail pleas, arguing that the accused were part of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang and the offences involved were serious. Therefore, they should not be released on bail, the lawyer argued.
The judge allowed the bail pleas, noting that except for their presence in concerned WhatsApp groups and chats being vague in nature, no other incriminating material was recovered by the prosecution. It directed the two not to leave the Greater Mumbai area till the conclusion of the trial.

headline: Guillain-Barré Syndrome: Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation takes strict action against unauthorized RO water bottling plants
description: The decision was taken in a recent municipal meeting in which it was revealed that several private RO water bottling plants in the city were drawing water from borewells and open wells
content:
In a decisive move to protect public health, the Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) has ordered the immediate shutdown of all unauthorized RO water bottling plants operating within the city limits starting Saturday, February 8. The action follows growing concerns over the presence of contaminated groundwater in bottled water, which has been linked to the cases of Guillain-Barré Syndrome (GBS) and other waterborne diseases.
The decision was taken in a recent municipal meeting in which it was revealed that several private RO water bottling plants in the city were drawing water from borewells and open wells, potentially exposing residents to harmful contaminants. These plants, which supply water in bottles and plastic cans, were found to be operating without proper licenses and failing to meet safety standards.
Under the new directive, all unauthorized RO bottling plants have been ordered to shut down indefinitely until a thorough review and quality assessment are conducted. The PCMC Water Supply Department, in coordination with the Health and Medical Department, has been tasked with implementing the crackdown. Officials, including engineers, inspectors, and security personnel, will carry out immediate inspections and enforcement actions to seal non-compliant facilities, officials said.

PCMC Commissioner Shekhar Singh emphasizing the urgency of the situation, said, “The safety and well-being of our citizens are of utmost priority. The consumption of contaminated water can lead to serious health hazards, including GBS and other waterborne illnesses. These unauthorized RO plants are operating without proper licenses and using unsafe water sources. We cannot allow such a risk to persist.”

All operators of illegal RO bottling plants have been instructed to comply with the shutdown orders immediately, failing which legal action will be initiated. The ban will remain in effect until further notice, subject to a detailed assessment of groundwater quality and compliance with safety regulations.
Further, PCMC has urged residents to remain vigilant and avoid consuming bottled water from unauthorized sources. The administration reassured citizens that official municipal water supply remains safe and is regularly monitored for quality and safety.
PCMC chief engineer Pramod Ombhase, said, “This is a necessary step to prevent further health risks. The municipal corporation will not tolerate any unauthorized activity that endangers public health.”

headline: Vadodara: In separate cases, two women die by suicide; police look for motive in absence of ‘note’
description: Police Inspector MR Sangada of Bapod police station told this newspaper, “According to the family's statement, the deceased prepared an omelette and ate it at noon before locking herself in the bedroom"
content:
Two similar cases of alleged suicides in a single day on Friday, with no suicide notes left behind, had the Bapod police station looking for the triggers that could have pushed two women to end their lives in their respective residences.
A 19-year-old student of Home Science in MS University on Friday allegedly died by suicide due to hanging at her residence at Ajwa road while her family members were home. In the absence of a suicide note, the family of the deceased, Umera Campwala, is “at a loss”, police said.
Police Inspector MR Sangada of Bapod police station told this newspaper, “According to the family’s statement, the deceased prepared an omelette and ate it at noon before locking herself in the bedroom. Her family assumed she was resting but when she did not respond, they knocked down the door and found her hanging. She was declared dead on arrival at the hospital.”
The police, which has registered a case of accidental death, said that Umera’s parents had earlier assumed that she was “fast asleep” and therefore, not responding to them knocking at the door.

“Since she has not left behind a note, we have seized her phone and sent it for forensic examination… Her family has also said that she was a bright student and had no such (academic) pressure. We are trying to ascertain the motive,” Sangada said.
‘Was set to get married this month’
Meanwhile, the police station received another case of alleged suicide of a 25-year-old woman, Diksha Shama. Sangada said that the woman was to be married on February 25. He said, “No suicide note has been left behind in this case too. The family says they are not aware of what must have triggered the deceased to take such a drastic step while preparations were on for her marriage…”

headline: Delhi elections 2025: ‘Accept people’s mandate, AAP will play role of constructive opposition’: Arvind Kejriwal after party loss
description: Outgoing CM Atishi says this is time for war, fight against dictatorship and hooliganism of the BJP will continue.
content:
With his party staring at a massive defeat in Delhi, after two back-to-back wins with a huge mandate in 2015 and 2020, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) chief Arvind Kejriwal said the party will play the role of a constructive opposition and will continue serving the people.
In a video message, the former Delhi Chief Minister said: “We accept the people’s mandate with humility and I congratulate the BJP for its victory and also hope that it will fulfill the expectations of the people of Delhi.”
He also congratulated his workers for “fighting very well”. Reaffirming the party’s commitment, he revisited the party’s roots of serving the people being the way forward. “Now that the people have given their verdict, we will not only play the role of a constructive opposition but also continue serving society… We did not enter politics for a position of power but we see politics as a way to work for the public and stand with the people,” he said.
The party’s two foundational leaders. Kejriwal and former Deputy Chief Minister Manish Sisodia, started with an NGO, Parivartan, only to rise to national prominence through the 2011 anti-corruption movement.

“We will stand with the people in their joys and sorrows… We did not enter politics for power; we see politics as a medium to serve the people… We will continue this work, and in the future as well, we will remain committed to serving the people,” Kejriwal promised.
The AAP’s top-tier leadership, including Kejriwal, Sisodia, Saurabh Bharadwaj, and Satyendar Jain, lost to the BJP’s candidates. Three party heavyweights and ministers — Atishi (Kalkaji), Gopal Rai (Babarpur), and Imran Husain (Ballimaran) — emerged victorious.
As of 4 pm, trends of the Election Commission website showed the BJP leading with 48 seats in the 70-member Assembly and the AAP securing 22.

Atishi, who retained the Kalkaji seat by defeating BJP’s Ramesh Bidhuri by a thin margin of 3,521 votes, in a video message on X, said: “I thank the people of Kalkaji for reposing their faith in me. I congratulate my team which worked against muscle power, hooliganism and violence… We accept the mandate of the people of Delhi.”
‘Time for war’
Calling the overall results a setback, she said: “This is the time for war and our fight against the dictatorship and hooliganism of the BJP will continue. This is definitely a setback but the struggle by the Aam Aadmi Party for its people will not stop.”
Durgesh Pathak, who lost to BJP’s Umang Bajaj by a margin of 1,231 votes in Rajinder Nagar, took to social media to share an emotional note. “You allowed a layman like me to serve you for two years. I learnt a lot from you in these two years. I want to thank all the voters and supporters… If there is anything wrong with whatever I did, I apologise. I congratulate BJP workers on their victory and hope they will meet people’s expectations… I am always available for help.”
In the Patparganj constituency, AAP’s new entrant, UPSC educator Avadh Ojha, lost to BJP’s Ravinder Singh Negi by 28,072 votes. Conceding defeat he wrote on X, “This is my personal defeat. The war starts again tomorrow. Heartfelt thanks to all. May your family be happy and children become kings. Jai Hind.”

headline: Outside Kejriwal residence: ‘Never imagined he could lose in Delhi’
description: Party paid the price for favouring defectors over loyalists, rue AAP loyalists
content:
As AAP’s defeat became undeniable, leaders began making their way to party national convenor Arvind Kejriwal’s residence on Firozeshah Road. One by one, cars pulled up, while a throng of journalists gathered near the gate.
In the afternoon, a man draped in a saffron BJP scarf arrived in front of Kejriwal’s residence, carrying samosas and jalebis. He held them before him, an offering laced with derision. “The way Kejriwal has spread muck in Delhi is why the lotus has bloomed today,” he declared to the cameras before him.
Two figures stood apart. Dressed in blue and yellow, their AAP badges catching the dim sunlight of the evening, they watched in solemn silence. Khurshid Alam, an elderly man in a cardigan, said: “We never imagined Kejriwal could lose in Delhi.”

His companion, Pramod Kumar Sharma, added: “I hate to say this, but the party lost because it abandoned its own workers. They favored defectors over loyalists, and this is the price we have paid.” His words were heavy with foreboding. “Mark my words, if they continue like this, Punjab will be next.”

Before the counting for the Delhi Assembly polls began, AAP’s Delhi spokesperson, Jasmine Shah, stepped outside to address the press. Exuding confidence, he said, “We believe the AAP is going to form the government with a huge majority.”
However, as the day progressed, the party office’s gates remained shut, with no ministers, senior leaders, MLAs, or even municipal councillors in sight.
