headline: Slope direction plays a crucial role in determining tree cover and canopy height in the Western Ghats: Study
description: The research paper highlights the importance of considering slope direction when planning biodiversity assessments, protecting endemic species, or increasing tree cover in the Western Ghats.
content:
In a recent paper, the researchers and collaborators at Indian Institute of Science Education and Research (IISER), Pune, examined vegetation in 25 protected areas along the Western Ghats and found a link between the direction of the slopes, tree cover, and canopy height. The authors included PhD student Devi Maheshwori and faculty member Dr Shreyas Managave from IISER Pune, Dr Girish Jathar from Srushti Conservation Foundation and independent GIS consultant Sham Davande, an official statement issued on Tuesday said.
The research revealed two main patterns: north-facing slopes have higher tree cover and taller canopy height compared to south-facing slopes; similarly, west-facing slopes have more tree cover and taller canopies than east-facing slopes. As a result, the northwest-facing slopes tend to have the highest tree cover and tallest canopy height, while southeast-facing slopes have the lowest.
The authors found these differences to be more pronounced on steeper slopes. Understanding the factors that influence tree growth in the Western Ghats is critical for both academic research and successful conservation and afforestation efforts, said Managave. While regional rainfall patterns are known to impact vegetation distribution at a regional scale, this study is the first to demonstrate significant influence of slope direction at the landscape scale.
The study suggests that uneven solar heating of slopes facing different directions creates better conditions for tree growth on north-and north-west-facing slopes, and less favourable on south-and south-east-facing slopes in the Western Ghats. The paper highlights the importance of considering slope direction when planning biodiversity assessments, protecting endemic species, or increasing tree cover in the Western Ghats. This research received funding from the Science Education and Research Board (SERB), DST, Government of India.

headline: After complaints over pending home sales, MahaRERA orders developers to refund buyers

Many have approached the Maharashtra Real Estate Regulatory Authority (MahaRERA) with complaints against developers. Pune has emerged as one of the most affected regions in Maharashtra’s real estate sector, accounting for around 20 per cent of all complaints registered with MahaRERA. With Rs 177.40 crore still to be recovered from developers in the city, homebuyers continue to suffer from prolonged delays and financial uncertainty.
According to MahaRERA’s latest report, Pune has recorded 274 complaints linked to 140 projects, making up 26 per cent of all disputed projects in Maharashtra. The total financial liability of these projects stand at Rs 219.71 crore, 22 per cent of the total disputed amount in the state. While MahaRERA has successfully recovered Rs 42.31 crore from 37 projects involving 62 complaints, a significant portion remains unpaid.
As per MahaRERA’s data, the top three developers in Pune with the highest pending refunds are Marvel Group and Developers (Rs 67 crore), Exerbia Chakan Developers (Rs 10.61 crore), and D S Kulkarni (Rs 18.31 crore), totalling Rs 96 crore. headline: In the offing: Six new barrages, state’s first rubber weir in Ahmedabad
description: Six new barrages, estimated to be built at a cost of Rs 1,500 crore, have been proposed at Chhelpura, Techava, Fudeda, Falu and Ged in Mehsana district, and Rajpur in Gandhinagar district. The barrage at Acher in Ahmedabad will be a rubber barrage.
content:
To rejuvenate the Sabarmati, which cuts through Ahmedabad city, and recharge the groundwater table, the Gujarat government has planned six new barrages on the river. Besides, three barrages are already under construction, including a rubber weir that will be a first in the state. The rubber structure, which is being built within the city limits, will have a cantilever bridge over it that will be “iconic”, according to officials.
This will take the number of bridges over the Sabarmati river in Ahmedabad city to 11, which includes the Atal Bridge, a foot-over bridge that has become a tourist destination for Ahmedabad.
The six new barrages will be built at an estimated cost of Rs 1,500 crore and will take the total number of barrages on the river between Dharoi dam (in Mehsana) and Vasna Barrage (in Ahmedabad) to 14 by the next three years. While five barrages are completed, three are under construction.
In the long run, some of these barrages are also expected to help retain the surface water in the riverfront portion of Ahmedabad, which the state government is planning to extend up to GIFT City in Gandhinagar. In 2002, the government diverted the waters of the Narmada river into the Sabarmati to keep it rejuvenated throughout the year.

Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Also Read | 20 yrs after ‘rebuilding’ their lives, over 280 homes in Bakramandi face eviction; to move High court again
Currently, the water level is maintained in the riverfront by releasing Narmada water into the Sabarmati by closing the gates of the barrage at Vasna from where the water is released for irrigation in downstream villages.
The new barrages planned on the Sabarmati river are between the existing Dharoi dam in Mehsana district and Vasna Barrage in Ahmedabad city – within a total distance of 148 kilometre. The total length of Sabarmati river – from its origin in Aravalli hills in Rajasthan to outfall into the Arabian Sea near Gulf of Khambhat – is 371 km.
Union Minister for Home and Cooperation and Gandhinagar MP Amit Shah laid the foundation stone of one of the barrages at Ambod village of Mansa tehsil in Gandhinagar district on January 14 where he had mentioned the “14 dams (barrages)” coming up on the Sabarmati river.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Apart from Ambod, work is in progress to build two barrages at Fatepara village of Mehsana district and at Acher in Ahmedabad city.
The five barrages already existing are in the villages or location of Valasana and Hirpura of Mehsana district, Lakroda and Sant Sarovar in Gandhinagar district and city, and Vasna barrage in Ahmedabad city.
Six new barrages have been proposed at Chhelpura, Techava, Fudeda, Falu and Ged in Mehsana district, and Rajpur in Gandhinagar district.
Sharing details of the nine proposed or under-progress barrages on the Sabarmati, a senior officer of the Water Resources Department of Gujarat government said that they are moving ahead with a target of completing the task in the next three years.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Elaborating on the objectives behind the plan to have the barrages, the officer said, “The main objective is to improve the groundwater levels in the villages around the river while replenishing it with maximum available water. And the second objective is to rejuvenate the Sabarmati river so that it can have surface water for the maximum part of the year.”
The officer added, “Currently, the Sabarmati river gets dried up in the months of October-November. Once the barrages are built, we expect the river to have surface water at least till February. As the ground water levels improve, the period of the river having surface water may get further extended. This will also provide water security to the region while decreasing the rate of depletion (of groundwater level).”
The officer further said, “The water will also prove to be an alternate source of Narmada water on which the region is heavily dependent.”
As per the latest report of the Central Ground Water Board — National Compilation on Dynamic Ground Water Resources of India, 2024 — out of the total 252 tehsils of Gujarat, 56 are categorised as Semi-Critical, Critical or Over-Exploited units in terms of annual groundwater extraction.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Out of the 56 such tehsils, 18 are from the districts of Ahmedabad, Mehsana and Gandhinagar.
Over-exploited units indicate tehsils where ground water extraction is exceeding the annual ground water recharge.
The critical units are tehsils where the stage of ground water extraction is between 90-100 per cent of the replenished groundwater. And the semi-critical units are those units where the stage of ground water extraction is between 70 per cent and 90 per cent of the replenished groundwater.
While eight of the nine proposed or under-progress barrages are being built by the Water Resources Department, the one at Acher in Ahmedabad city is being built by the Sabarmati Riverfront Development Corporation Limited (SRFDCL). The barrage at Acher will be a rubber barrage.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD

A senior officer of SRFDCL said, “The rubber barrage will be built at the cost of Rs 55 crore. It will be part of a bridge-cum-barrage project of SRFDCL with a total estimated cost of Rs 290 crore. The bridge will be one more iconic bridge on the Sabarmati river in the city.”
The rubber barrage will be made of air-filled flexible rubber membrane which can be put to use by inflating and deflating to store or release the water in the river.
The officer added, “This barrage will be helpful in getting water for Riverfront, which the government is planning to extend right up to Gandhinagar. It will also be useful in providing water during crisis situations.”

headline: Amid reports of US deporting migrants to India, Punjab NRI Affairs minister says ‘govt is with them’
description: Punjab NRI Affairs Minister Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal said they are yet to find out how many people have been deported by the US.
content:
Amid reports of a United States military plane carrying illegal migrants to India Monday, Punjab NRI Affairs Minister Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal said it was better to “send them back home rather than putting them in jail in the US.”
Reuters said a US military C-17 aircraft had left for India with migrants, and cited an official saying the plane “would not arrive for at least 24 hours”.
Talking to The Indian Express on Tuesday, Dhaliwal said, “We have not got any information yet as to how many from Punjab are being deported. However, I want to say that it is a relief. It is better that they are coming back home. I had been living in the US before I came back to India. I know the jails there. Jails will be a huge punishment for them. Our youths will be shattered if they are put in the jails there. It is better that they come back home.”
Dhaliwal said he would write to the Ministry of External Affairs on Tuesday urging the government to take up the issue with the US so that illegal immigrants are sent back home rather than put in jails.

“I want to convey a message to these Punjabis that the government is with them. I will take it up with Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann in the Cabinet meeting on February 10 that we should take it up with the banks to waive off the interest of those who took loans to go to the US”.
“Some have taken loans of Rs 25 to Rs 30 lakh to go to the US. It will be difficult for them to pay the loan back when they are back. I will also hold a meeting with the banks. There should be a moratorium on the interest as the youths would have to settle down first, look for jobs and then pay back. I am a farmer myself. I know how difficult it is to pay back if one is unable to pay an instalment.”
The minister also said they recognise that the deportation would be a huge problem for the youth and their parents. “We will not leave any stone unturned to rehabilitate them. We will help them as much as we can. We will formulate a policy. Those returning would have to start working.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He said the work would start on Tuesday itself. “We have been busy with the Delhi elections all this while. We have returned only last evening. We will start taking stock of the situation from today.”
The minister also said the details of the flight are awaited. “We will know how many Punjabis are on board. I am just seeking the details. We will have to work hard to help these people. We are on the job.”
Punjab Chief Minister Mann, who had also been campaigning in Delhi for the last several days, is back in Chandigarh, and called a meeting of senior superintendents of Police (SSPs) at noon.

headline: Gujarat BJP legislator Karshanbhai Solanki passes away at 68
description: Karshanbhai Solanki was elected from the Kadi constituency for the first time in 2017, and again in 2022.
content:
Karshanbhai Solanki, the BJP MLA from the Kadi constituency in North Gujarat, passed away following a prolonged illness at his residence early Tuesday. He was 68.

Solanki, who belonged to the Scheduled Caste, was elected from the Kadi constituency for the first time in 2017, and again in 2022. He was probably the only MLA who regularly commuted on state-run buses.

headline: Punjab Police to install 2,300 CCTV cameras in border districts: DGP
description: Move aims to strengthen surveillance from Pathankot to Fazilka, enhancing security along the border
content:
In a bid to bolster border security and improve surveillance, Punjab Police will install 2,300 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras at 703 strategic locations across border districts, stretching from Pathankot to Fazilka.
“We are strengthening the second line of defence with 2,300 CCTV cameras being installed at 703 strategic locations from Pathankot to Fazilka, with a cost of Rs 45 crores,” Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav said in a statement issued today.
During a visit to Pathankot, the DGP inaugurated several police infrastructure projects, including a new Cyber Crime Police Station located on the second floor of Police Station Division-1 in the district. The station is equipped with advanced technology to handle complex cybercrimes and provide swift solutions to victims of online fraud. Citizens can report cybercrimes at the station or via the toll-free helpline number 1930.
Additionally, the DGP inaugurated an overhauled Police Command and Control Centre to enhance security in Pathankot. The centre features 344 HD cameras, including Auto Number Plate Reader (ANPR) cameras, offering live coverage of key areas, including the Second Line of Defence, rural regions, and the entire city. Another 357 cameras are being added to further strengthen the district’s security.

headline: BEST plans new bus route on Coastal Road from Marine Drive to Worli by May
description: On January 26, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis inaugurated the northbound carriageway of the bowstring arch bridge, which links the coastal road to the Bandra Worli Sea Link (BSWL).
content:
With nearly the entire first phase of the Mumbai Coastal Road Project (MCRP) now operational, the Brihanmumbai Electric Supply and Transport (BEST) is looking at starting a bus service linking the entire Worli to Marine Drive stretch by May.
On January 26, Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis inaugurated the northbound carriageway of the bowstring arch bridge, which links the coastal road to the Bandra Worli Sea Link (BSWL). The bridge – now entirely operational – enables motorists from South Mumbai to flow into the BSWL and vice versa, without exiting the coastal road. A bus service till Bandra however is unlikely to materialise soon.
“In the upcoming three months, we are aiming to introduce a new route which will ferry between Marine Drive and Worli, from where the bus will exit/ enter the coastal road. From Worli, the route will extend into the suburbs. Depending on the demand, we are looking at plying the buses on coastal roads at a frequency of 20 – 30 minutes. We are examining the catchment and we are eyeing to launch a new bus route in the upcoming three months,” a senior official told Express.
However, the BEST official maintained that the route will be curtailed at Worli, with no immediate plans for routes upto Bandra.

Officials, privy to the development, added, “While initially there were plans to ferry buses through the entire coastal road between Marine Drive to Bandra via the connector and BSWL, we are not planning any routes immediately. Firstly, the BEST buses are not exempt from the BSWL toll, making the operations of bus services at nominal rates difficult and expensive. Secondly, we want to gauge the response to the new bus route till Worli. If we see good demand, we will consider planning a new route which extends till Bandra.” While the BEST had started ferrying buses on the Sea Link in 2009, its buses no longer ply on this route.
Nearly one year since the MCRP was first launched, the coastal road currently hosts only one BEST route — number A-78 — which ferries passengers between NCPA and Byculla (West). The existing route, however, is also grappling with feeble responses from commuters.
The delay in the deployment of BEST buses on the coastal road – which has earmarked a dedicated lane for buses – has come much to the grouse of citizens and activists.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Its depleting bus fleet, according to senior officials from BEST, is amongst the key reasons for the delayed deployment of buses on the MCRP.
“Currently, the BEST is dealing with a depleting fleet and buses are also being scrapped owing to which services along the existing bus routes are also getting hampered. It is owing to this lack of adequate buses that the introduction of buses on coastal roads has been delayed. As we are able to augment our bus on the western route, we will divert buses on the coastal road,” said the official, adding that there are also concerns over the demand of commuters along the coastal stretch.
According to officials, the BEST’s fleet has currently dwindled below 2,900 buses.
The ongoing works along the coastal road on projects like bus bays, officials said, have induced further delays in the opening. The BMC is developing 10 bus bays along the 10.58 km stretch of the coastal road. To enable users to cross from the landward to the seaside, 20 pedestrian underpasses (PUPs) have also been charted beneath the arterial road. However, the amenities are yet to be opened for public use. Of the 20 PUPs, only one underpass at Haji Ali is currently open for public use with the BMC stating that remaining pedestrian pathways are likely to be opened by May 2025. headline: Pune Crime Files: When a cab driver’s relentless stalking culminated in acid attack on BPO employee
description: The Bombay High Court considered the trial court's punishment of seven years of imprisonment for the cab driver a “miscarriage of justice” and sentenced him to life in prison.
content:
In 2005, a 22-year-old woman from Pune became a victim of stalking when a cab driver threw acid on her after she repeatedly rejected his advances. In 2007, the convict jumped parole while serving his seven-year prison sentence. It took the police nine years to apprehend him for the second time. In between, the Bombay High Court increased his sentence to life imprisonment.
Meanwhile, the woman returned to her job in business process outsourcing (BPO) just a few months after the attack. It has been 20 years since the crime that shocked the residents of Pune.
Cab driver attempts to get close to woman despite refusals
According to police and court records, the woman initially worked as a customer care associate at a prominent company in Pune. The convict, Kailas Sitaram Adagale, aged 25 then, worked as a driver for a company cab provided to her.
As per the police, Adagale, a resident of Thergaon, attempted to become close with her, but she rebuffed his advances. She left the company on December 17, 2004, and started a new job at a well-known BPO firm in Kalyani Nagar in January 2005. In addition, she was pursuing a BCom degree at a college in Pune.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Even after she changed her workplace, Adagale continued to call her frequently, as per the police. He also attempted to meet her on her way to college and her new job. Despite ignoring him, she received a phone call from Adagale around 5.30 pm on January 31, 2005, while she was on her way to Kalyani Nagar in another cab.
He wanted to meet her, but she refused and hung up. Nevertheless, he confronted her on the BPO firm’s campus, threatening to create a scene if she did not speak with him. As a new employee, she wanted to avoid any troubles in the company, so she reluctantly agreed to talk with him in his cab, according to the police.
After Adagale told her she wanted to marry her, she questioned how he dared to say that. An angry Adagale opened a bottle containing acid and splashed it on her face. Hearing her screams, people gathered, two of them caught Adagale, and handed him over to the police, who recorded his arrest. The police filed a First Information Report (FIR) against him under Section 307 (attempt to murder) of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The woman, who was admitted to a hospital, did not suffer acid burns on her face and eyes, but on her hands, legs and other body parts. She underwent multiple surgeries before rejoining the job.
Case reaches Bombay High Court, convict jumps parole
A trial court in Pune convicted Adagale and awarded him seven years of rigorous imprisonment. He moved the Bombay High Court to challenge the conviction while the Maharashtra government filed an appeal in the high court to enhance his sentence.
In August 2007, he was released from jail on parole for 14 days, but he did not return and escaped. A fresh offence for jumping parole was lodged against him at the Hinjewadi police station.
The police launched a search for him but were unable to trace his location even as hearings in the acid attack case continued in the high court. On February 18, 2016, the high court awarded him life imprisonment and fined him Rs 2 lakh as compensation to the woman.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Bombay High Court observed that a mere seven years of imprisonment for this “inhuman and cruel” act of acid attack was a “miscarriage of justice”. It stated that one of the objectives of punishing the convict is to create a “deterrent effect” so that others do not dare to indulge in such acts or offences.
As Adagale continued to be on the run, the police intensified the search for him. Finally, acting on a tip-off to Constable Feroz Bagwan, a team led by the then Crime Branch assistant inspector Sunil Gawali nabbed Adagale from J M Road in Pune on November 24, 2016.
The police probe revealed that after jumping parole, Adagale kept changing his location. He was in Nagpur for some days and then moved to states outside Maharashtra. He then returned to Pune and started working as a cab driver again while residing in the Dhanori area, the police said.

description: Suman Sardar, Farzam Sheikh, and Sheikh Hashibur, from Nazhat in Murshidabad, were allegedly hired byAlimuddin Sheikh to clean an underground sewage line
content:
A contractor, Alimuddin Sheikh, was arrested on Monday in connection with the deaths of three wage laborers at the Kolkata Leather Complex on Sunday.
The laborers, Suman Sardar, Farzam Sheikh, and Sheikh Hashibur, from Nazhat in Murshidabad, were allegedly hired by Sheikh to clean an underground sewage line. The incident occurred when one worker fell ill after entering a 10-foot-deep manhole, and the other two went in to rescue him. Rescue workers in diving gear recovered the bodies.
Kolkata Mayor Firhad Hakim visited the site on Sunday and ordered an inquiry, leading to a case being registered at the Bantala police station.
He claimed that the deaths were likely caused by chemical waste from tanneries flowing through the drainage line, which “should have been directed to the effluent treatment plant”. Hakim said that the police investigation would focus on why the men were sent into the manhole without pumps.

headline: Delhi High Court summons Shashi Tharoor in civil defamation suit by BJP leader Rajeev Chandrasekhar
description: Rajeev Chandrasekhar said Shashi Tharoor had accused him of bribing people for votes ahead of Lok Sabha elections 2024.
content:
The Delhi High Court on Monday issued a summons to Congress MP Shashi Tharoor in a civil defamation suit by BJP leader and former MP Rajeev Chandrashekhar.
Chandrasekhar, represented by advocate Vaibhav Gaggar, has accused Tharoor of defaming and damaging his reputation. This accusation follows Tharoor’s alleged statement during a TV interview ahead of Lok Sabha elections 2024 that Chandrasekhar had bribed people for votes.
Chandrasekhar is seeking damages for the loss of his reputation in society and a permanent injunction against Tharoor. He alleged that Tharoor’s remarks contributed to his defeat in the Lok Sabha elections from the Thiruvananthapuram constituency in Kerala. Tharoor won the seat for the fourth consecutive time, with a margin of over 16,000 votes against Chandrasekhar.
Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav issued a summons and directed that the defamation plaint be registered as a suit and listed the matter for consideration before the joint registrar on April 28.

In August 2024, the Delhi High Court transferred the criminal defamation suit filed by Chandrasekhar against Tharoor from the Patiala district court to the district sessions judge of Rouse Avenue court while directing the parties to “appear in person” later that month. The Rouse Avenue court holds jurisdiction over conducting trials involving cases pertaining to sitting MPs/MLAs. The suit was initially filed before the Patiala court as both the complainant and the accused reside in Delhi under the North Avenue police station.

headline: Cash-strapped Karnataka govt eyes asset monetisation under new PPP policy
description: The revision saw the inclusion of asset monetisation in the PPP policy, which outlined the various methods to generate revenue from infrastructure assets.
content:
Asset monetisation has become the buzzword for the cash-strapped Congress government in Karnataka, with the state Cabinet recently clearing a policy to generate revenue from public infrastructure assets.
The State Public Private Partnership (PPP) Policy for Infrastructure Projects-2025 cleared last Thursday also looks to increase private participation in infrastructure projects. Several key changes are effected in the 2025 version of the policy, which was last revised seven years ago in 2018.
The revision saw the inclusion of asset monetisation in the PPP policy, which outlined the various methods to generate revenue from infrastructure assets. Among the assets that could be monetised include roads, ports, tourist destinations, and agri-processing plants, among others.
Speaking to the Indian Express, Dr N Manjula, Secretary to Government, Infrastructure Development, Ports and Inland Water Transport Department, which is the nodal agency for all infrastructure projects undertaken through PPP mode or asset monetisation, said that the income generated by asset monetisation will be based on the number of projects taken up. “We have not estimated it yet. But PPP has huge potential to generate revenue,” she said.

The new policy is in tune with the Centre’s policy on PPP projects. The asset monetisation guidelines included in the Central policy were also added. The 2025 policy simplifies various procedures required to implement PPP projects, Manjula further said.
Among other changes are the introduction of operational guidelines which provide a road map on the lifecycle of a PPP project, its process flow, and action required at each stage of implementation. Sector-specific incentives, which allow infrastructure projects to avail incentives from policies of a particular sector, are also part of the 2025 policy.
Individual departments will also have to formulate a strategy to develop a multi-year roadmap and create an annual action plan for PPP infrastructure projects. The policy mandates that 90 per cent of the required land should be available for a project at the time of tendering. However, exceptions may be granted on a case-by-case basis by the State Level Single Window Agency or the State High-Level Clearance Committee, it said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The cash-strapped Siddaramaiah government has been exploring various asset monetisation options since assuming power in May 2023. Last year, the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj department started work on a policy to monetise assets owned by gram panchayats in Karnataka. In September, the government set up an expert committee under retired IAS officer K P Krishnan to analyse the potential for asset monetisation, particularly by leveraging the land in and around Bengaluru.

trainThe railway police in Bandra arrested a porter for allegedly sexually assaulting a 55-year-old woman who had come to the city from Haridwar in a train on Saturday night. The accused was produced before a court and remanded to police custody.

headline: Passenger from Brazil held at Mumbai airport for smuggling cocaine
description: An official said that on the night of January 27, customs officers intercepted a passenger arriving from Sao Paulo (Brazil) via Paris, based on profiling and specific input.
content:
A passenger from Brazil was arrested at the Mumbai airport on Saturday in connection with the seizure of cocaine weighing 1.64 kg. The cocaine, seized by the customs offcers, had an illicit market value of nearly Rs 16.49 crore.
An official said that on the night of January 27, customs officers intercepted a passenger arriving from Sao Paulo (Brazil) via Paris, based on profiling and specific input. He was identified as Fernando Da Silva (24).
During this five-day operation, 170 capsules, purported to be cocaine of net weight 1.6 kg having illicit market value of nearly Rs 16.49 crore, were seized.
The said contraband was concealed in the body cavity as well as ingested by the passenger. The passenger, Da Silva, was arrested under the provisions of the NDPS Act, 1985.

headline: 2 criminals attack police during weapon recovery in Punjab, get injured as cops fire back
description: The two accused had been arrested in a case of firing at a shopkeeper at the Main Bazar in Dera Baba Nanak last month.
content:
Two individuals in police custody were injured in cross-firing after they allegedly attacked accompanying policemen during a weapon recovery exercise on the outskirts of Shahpur Jajan village in Punjab’s Dera Baba Nanak on Sunday.
The accused, Sarbjeet Singh and Sunil Masih, had been arrested in a case of firing at a shopkeeper at the Main Bazar in Dera Baba Nanak last month. The trader had allegedly received extortion calls from gangster Jeewan Fauji before the attack.
“Upon interrogation, the arrested accused led the police to a location for weapon recovery. However, during the operation, they opened fire on the police. In the ensuing retaliatory action, both accused sustained gunshot injuries to their legs. Both were referred to Amritsar and both are stable,” said a statement released by the police.
Following the firing incident last month, an FIR was registered under Sections 109, and 111(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, and Section 25 of the Arms Act at Dera Baba Nanak police station.

headline: Better roads, sewers that don’t overflow, proper drinking water: What voters want in East Delhi’s Trilokpuri this election

content:
As a thick layer of fog engulfs the national capital, Rajni and her family of six huddle around a chulha (stove), seeking warmth, in their small 350 sq ft home in East Delhi’s Trilokpuri. Working as a domestic help in apartment complexes in nearby Mayur Vihar, the 30-year-old lists what she thinks is the biggest problem in the area: no proper piped water connection and the “ganda paani (dirty water)” as a result.
She is also reluctant to sign up for the AAP government’s Mahila Samman Yojana which promises a monthly allowance of Rs 2,100 for women if it comes back to power because of “issues” with the registration process. “Par Kejriwal ji sahi hai (But Kejriwal is alright),” she concludes.

Trilokpuri, predominantly a Dalit and Muslim area bordering Uttar Pradesh, is a reserved constituency for SCs. For three consecutive elections, people here have voted for the AAP. In the 2020 polls, AAP’s Rohit Kumar defeated BJP’s Kiran Vaidya by 12,486 votes.

For the upcoming elections on February 5, Kumar has been replaced by Anjana Parcha who previously served as a ward councillor in Trilokpuri. The BJP has fielded local leader Ravikant Ujjain while the Congress candidate is Amardeep.
Incidentally, Kumar, along with six other MLAs, quit the AAP on Friday citing “corruption” within the party.
Change vs second chances
Across the constituency, several residents The Indian Express speaks to have a list of complaints — overflowing sewers, poor maintenance of public parks, lack of drinking water, bad roads, safety issues, and drug addictions among young children to name a few.

“We have given Kejriwal a chance for 10 years… There are more fundamental issues such as jobs, which the Narendra Modi government can give,” says Subhash, 42, a cleaner at the MCD office.
His 18-year-old son Karan, who has dropped out of college and is learning to do “options trading”, agrees with his father. “Ye saare schemes bekaar hai (all these welfare schemes are useless),” he says.
In nearby Block 22, where a majority of Tamil-speaking people reside, the buildings are old — the paint is peeling and the iron gates are rusted. For residents of this locality, this is among the least of their concerns; it is outweighed by civic issues.
Swamidurai, a homemaker from Tamil Nadu’s Dindigul, says they often have to call private contractors to clean the sewers as the “discharge mixes with our drinking water”. She says each house pools in Rs 50 for this.
For Papathi D, even Rs 50 is a big amount. “My husband is paralysed. His medicines are so expensive, I can’t give money every month to clean the roads or the sewer,” she says.

She also complains that the mohalla clinics neither have facilities for treatment nor medicines for her husband. “I had to start selling vada and sambar outside my house to bring in some income… It does not matter who I vote for, nothing will change,” she adds.
At a cart selling South Indian food, Ashok, 59, a retired employee of a private company, complains about the state of the local park. “We are not sure if we want this party (AAP). They keep saying there is no money, so we will vote for someone who has the money. BJP has it,” he smiles.
Two other men, waiting for their turn at the cart, join the conversation. “Boys aged 12 to 13 years are addicted to drugs,” says one of them. “We do not know how they get it or who is selling it to them, but it is ruining their lives. To get money, they now resort to snatching and stealing.”
Kilometres away in Block 15, a few stray dogs bark near the meat shops. A few men are busy listening to political debates on their phones, the sound of which reaches Sanjida’s house.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Pulling a black dupatta over her head, the 60-year-old steps out to chat. Her main worry is her elder son — he is unemployed even after completing his graduation. When talk turns to the election, she is clear about who to support.
“All the government does is instigate fights among Hindus and Muslims. Aafat macha rakha hai har jagha, humko AAP hi chahiye. (They have created chaos everywhere, we only want AAP),” she says.
Her neighbours believe that AAP has made some positive changes in terms of education and by offering free bus rides to women, but none of this has directly helped the Muslim community.
“Our business is finished because of inflation… The price of flour is now equivalent to the price of a cylinder; what will a poor man buy, flour or a cylinder,” asks Zubair Ahmad, 65, an owner of a tea stall.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Ahmad says for the last 25 years, the drains in the area have not been cleared. “If the government had provided any facility to us, then we would have believed them. But there is no hope,” he says.
The constituency is also home to members of the Sikh community.
Kawaljeet Singh Sandhu, 45, an auto driver, says several Punjabi families used to stay here till 1984. “But in the riots that year, a lot of people were killed including my two brothers. After that, many of us moved to areas like Kondli and Tilak Nagar.”
The area saw the worst episodes of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots. It also saw a communal clash in 2014.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Among the community too, there are several complaints on the state of affairs. Amanpreet Singh, who sells electronic parts, says the problem of encroachment has increased. “If you take your vehicle out, you will not be able to move even a few metres in the evening.”
Dharmajeet Kaur, 55, says everything has become worse since the AAP came to power. “Before this government, things were fine. I have been living here for the last 30 years. This park near my house has no gate. We complained so many times but to no avail. In the end, we decided that we would use our money to place a gate at the entrance… but someone stole the gate.”
“Our sewers are clogged. There are piles of garbage on the road. When we ask the sanitation workers to clean it, they say they are temporary employees and are already burdened with work. In the end, we hire private workers to clean it. The government has not given anything to the Sikh community,” she alleges.
Others maintain their support for the AAP.
“(PM Narendra) Modi used to say Kejriwal is giving freebies but he is doing the same this election, so what is the difference? We will vote for Kejriwal because I know he tries. He is not an evil man. He tried to make things better. We will give him another chance,” says Sandhu.

Addressing a jansabha at Trilokpuri last month, AAP chief Arvind Kejriwal drew a comparison between AAP-ruled Delhi and other BJP-ruled states. “If you choose the lotus symbol on election day, electricity will go by the time you come back home… Look at the state of schools in Uttar Pradesh, and look at the state of schools in Delhi. If you choose the wrong button, schools will get spoiled. Choose the right button, and ensure employment for your family.”
Countering Kejriwal, BJP candidate Ujjain says this time, the “tide will turn”. “The lanes in Tilokpuri are choking with garbage. The sewer water overflows. The mohalla clinic they (AAP) talk about is lying empty. We are sure we will win,” he says.

headline: Gujarat CM terms Budget as visionary; Opp calls it disappointing, election-specific
description: CM Patel hailed the "visionary budget" of Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led NDA III government as one that "paves the way for holistic development of the states" and "empowers" them to contribute to the Viksit Bharat 2047 mission.
content:
Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel on Saturday said that the Union Budget presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman embodied the principle of ‘citizen first’ to “fulfill the aspirations” of the middle class and the underprivileged even as Opposition leaders termed the budget as a “disappointment” for Gujarat, aimed for the upcoming elections in Bihar and Delhi.
CM Patel hailed the “visionary budget” of Prime Minister Narendra Modi-led NDA III government as one that “paves the way for holistic development of the states” and “empowers” them to contribute to the Viksit Bharat 2047 mission. Patel said, “Topics that drive the four key engines — agriculture, MSMEs, investment, and exports — have been comprehensively addressed.  Gujarat will gain significantly from the Maritime Development Fund and Mission for Cotton Productivity. Enhanced incentives for MSMEs will further accelerate the growth and expansion of Gujarat’s MSME sector.” Patel also thanked PM Modi for “extending key provisions, including exemptions for financial entities in the IFSC at GIFT City, until March 31, 2030”.
Patel said that the “exceptional tax benefits”, announced in the Union budget would lead to “increased savings, boost business growth, and attract more investment, ultimately creating additional employment opportunities and benefiting the nation as a whole”. The CM said in a release, “The new income tax slabs would provide substantial relief to the middle and upper-middle classes … The budget prioritizes the welfare of farmers, focusing on improving agricultural productivity and boosting farmers’ income. The mission for cotton productivity will particularly benefit Gujarat’s farmers. The improved credit limits under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme will provide much-needed support to farmers, fishermen, and animal husbandry farmers.”
CM Patel added that the PM Dhan Dhanya Yojana for approximately 100 districts with low agricultural productivity across the country will benefit 1.7 crore farmers and promote rural development to help “curb migration”. He also praised establishment of a Rs 25,000 crore Maritime Development Fund to provide long-term credit for the maritime industry, a move especially relevant for Gujarat, given its extensive coastline. Patel stated that the creation of the Rs 1 lakh crore Urban Challenge Fund, aimed at developing prosperous urban centres, would “enhance the infrastructure of Gujarat’s cities”.

Milind Rege, his love for Mumbai cricket and why I won’t be there at his funeral: Sunil Gavaskar
Gujarat Pradesh Congress Committee president Shakitsinh Gohil, however, said that the budget had nothing to offer for Gujarat and did not address local issues of the crisis in the cumin trade industry or the textile industry. Gohil said, “As a Gujarati, I had expectations like all others that there would be special schemes for Gujarat but there was nothing for the state. Just because Bihar elections are approaching, there is a Makhana Board and SOPs for Patna airport with repeated mention of Bihar. In Gujarat, the cumin spice trade is in trouble and several people, who are employed in this trade are staring at a bleak future. There is no mention of any assistance … Nylon yarn is getting expensive and the textile industry of Surat was hopeful, but there was no mention of it in the budget. Asia’s biggest ship-breaking yard is in Alang, Gujarat but there is no mention of it. There is a weak mention of
ship-building, but not ship-breaking.”
Gohil also said that the “drum-roll announcement” of income tax exemptions upto Rs 12 lakh was an “eyewash” as the “terms and conditions” would be known post the Delhi elections. He said, “This announcement is not an exemption from Income Tax. There is a fine print and T&C applies… It is when you read that fine print you will know that there is no profit but only cheating. The Finance Minister said that persons earning Rs 12 lakh do not have to pay tax but the 31st amendment in Income Tax Act will be brought out next week after the gullible people in Delhi cast their votes. So people can beat the drums that Income Tax has been exempted but it is not the case. The Income Tax amendment will be applicable to these announcements… If you had to grant exemptions it should be unconditional.”
Gohil added that the budget had no mention of employment generation or reduction in the GST burden in times when people are paying upto 28% tax on items purchased.  “There was need for definite steps to beat the inflation but no mention has been made… Gujarat has problems with railways, port, coast and no mention has been made for development. Rising prices of fertiliser and the GST applicable has not been discussed in the budget.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Gujarat Aam Aadmi Party president Isudan Gadhvi also put out a reaction to the budget, stating that the “half-hearted tax exemption” was of no help for the middle class, while claiming that issues pertaining to Gujarat-specific industries were ignored. Gadhvi said, “So, we have come to a point where the government will release only election-specific budgets. This time it is only about Bihar. What wrong has Gujarat done by giving them votes that it has been completely ignored? There is nothing for the farmers or labourers. For the middle class, which is fighting inflation, they should have announced complete income tax exemption (for people earning) upto Rs 18 lakh…The current exemption is not even enough to beat inflation. Fuel has not been included under GST nor has there been any consideration for the Morbi ceramic industry, Gujarat’s textile industry or the MSME sector. All in all, it is a disappointing election-specific budget only for Bihar.”
The Minority Coordination Committee of Gujarat said that the budget had been “disappointing and discriminatory” with 0.0661% allocation for a population of 19.3%.
Muhajid Nafees, Convenor of the Minority Coordination Committee, said, “Compared to earlier budgets, a decline of Rs 130.46 crore has been effected in pre-matric scholarships, Rs 731 crore reduction in post-matric scholarships and the merit-cum-means scheme has been slashed by Rs 26.46 crore. There have been budget cuts even in the Maulana Azad Scholarship Scheme… There have also been cuts in the schemes for Madrassas… Several minority schemes have also been shut down. It shows the discrimination… As per the population ratio, at least Rs 1 lakh crore should be allocated for the
minorities.”

headline: Fire breaks out in Kurla scrap market; one injured
description: The Mumbai Fire Brigade (MFB) deployed four engines, six jumbo tankers and two fire tankers.
content:
A fire broke out in Kurla West scrap market on Saturday that spread to nearly eleven shops in the area. While no casualties were reported, a 25-year-old fireman was injured during the course of operations.
The fireman was identified as Suraj Tanaki Nakashe (25) and was taken to Kurla’s Bhabha hospital after sustaining injuries to his left knee.
The incident was reported at 4.19 pm at the scrap market near the Equinox building along Kurla Khadi. The fire was declared level 2 at 4.45 pm.
According to senior civic officials, the fire was confined to the electric installations, wiring, plastic material, stock of chemical drums and other miscellaneous items stored in nearly 11 shops in an area spanning 100X200 square feet of the market.

headline: Education sector appreciates Budget 2025: ‘Forward-looking strategy that aligns seamlessly with the vision of a Viksit Bharat’
description: Dr Vidya Yeravdekar, Pro Chancellor of Symbiosis International University, said “The establishment of AI Centres of Excellence and the expansion of IITs mark a significant step toward positioning India as a global leader in technology and innovation."
content:
Authorities from Symbiosis International University and Sri Balaji University in Pune highlighted the positives for the education sector after the announcement of the Union budget 2025. This included topics like Artificial Intelligence, fellowships in IITs and IISCs, Atal Tinkering Labs, Indian Knowledge System repository, and conservation of India’s manuscripts.
Dr Vidya Yeravdekar, Pro Chancellor of Symbiosis International University, said “The establishment of AI Centres of Excellence and the expansion of IITs mark a significant step toward positioning India as a global leader in technology and innovation. These initiatives, coupled with 10,000 fellowships for technological research in IITs and IISc, will not only strengthen India’s academic and research ecosystem but also equip students with cutting-edge skills required for emerging industries. Additionally, the expansion of medical education with 75,000 new seats will play a crucial role in addressing the growing demand for healthcare professionals and strengthening the country’s healthcare infrastructure.”
She added, “The launch of five National Centres for Excellence in Skilling, in collaboration with global partners, will ensure India’s youth are equipped with industry-relevant expertise. The rollout of 50,000 Atal Tinkering Labs and initiatives like the Bharatiya Bhasha Pustak scheme further exemplify a forward-looking strategy that aligns seamlessly with the vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat.”
Dr Preeti Joshi, Principal, School of Liberal Arts at Sri Balaji University, Pune, said, “Indian Knowledge System (IKS) is an integral part of the National Education Policy (NEP). Thus, an announcement made by the FM in today’s budget regarding setting up a National Digital Repository of Indian Knowledge Systems is a significant one. This will facilitate faster knowledge sharing and will help the research work which is focused on integrating India’s ancient wisdom with modern education and technology. Moreover, an announcement to survey and undertake documentation and conservation of India’s manuscript heritage in collaboration with academic institutions, museums, libraries, and private collectors is an important step in this regard.”

headline: Union Budget 2025-26 will make Haryana self-reliant, says CM Nayab Singh Saini
description: Nayab Singh Saini said the Haryana government will ensure the effective implementation of the schemes announced in the budget to reap maximum benefits for the state.
content:
Haryana BJP Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini Saturday said the Union Budget 2025-26 will boost the country’s development and lay a “strong foundation for Viksit Bharat”, besides making Haryana self-reliant.
“The budget has been designed to benefit all sections of society. Haryana will also receive substantial benefits from the budget’s provisions, which will aid in the state’s continued progress and development,” the chief minister further said.
Saini added that the budget will further empower the poor, youth, women, and farmers – which the Narendra Modi-led Centre has “identified… as the pillars of a developed India”.
“The Finance Minister’s budget includes several key announcements for farmers. The loan limit on the Kisan Credit Card has been increased from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh. In addition, 100 districts with low agricultural productivity will be prioritised under the Dhan Dhanya Krishi Yojana. As Haryana is an agriculture-based state, it will greatly benefit from this budget. It is a significant step towards improving the living standards of farmers and strengthening the agricultural sector.

headline: Karnataka sets up SIT to probe landgrab allegations against Union minister Kumaraswamy and others
description: The SIT was set up following a contempt petition over the government’s failure to comply with an undertaking it gave the Karnataka HC five years ago to clear encroachments allegedly made by JD(S) leader H D Kumaraswamy and others.
content:
The Congress government in Karnataka has ordered the constitution of a Special Investigation Team to probe alleged landgrab by several prominent people—including Union Minister and JD(S) leader H D Kumaraswamy—in the Ramanagara region, which borders Bengaluru.
The government informed the Karnataka High Court on January 29 about the issuance of an order on January 28 for the creation of an SIT to investigate the alleged landgrab in Ramanagara district. The state made the submission during a hearing of a contempt plea filed against it by an NGO over the failure to recover land identified as being encroached.
Among the land identified based on findings from local authorities as being government property for want of documents of original grants is land reportedly owned by Union Minister for Heavy Industries H D Kumaraswamy, also a former chief minister, in the Bidadi taluk of the district.
In 2020, following a petition filed by the NGO Samaj Parivartana Samudaya, the government gave an undertaking to the court to recover public land that was allegedly encroached on in Kethiganahalli by influential people. The NGO filed a contempt petition after the state government failed to report compliance with its undertaking to recover the land.

On January 29, a division bench noted during a physical appearance in court by Rajendra Kumar Kataria, principal secretary of the revenue department that “the State Government vide Government Order dated 28.01.2025 has constituted a Special Investigation Team consisting of five members to conduct a comprehensive and impartial investigation into the removal of unauthorized encroachments on Government lands in Survey Nos. 8, 9, 10, 16, 17 and 79 of Bidadi Hobli, Ramanagara District, Ramanagara Taluk”.
The court, however, observed that the SIT was being constituted five years after it was informed that the state would facilitate the removal of encroachments.
“The writ petition was disposed of on 14.01.2020 and almost five years have been completed. But there is no proper progress made by the concerned authorities for compliance with the order passed in the writ petition relating to the aforesaid properties,” the court observed on Friday.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The state submitted that the matter involved intricate policy issues that need to be validated at various levels of the government and that the court must provide time for the process ahead of a compliance report.
While adjourning the case for further hearing on February 21, the court ruled that the state must submit a compliance report in two weeks. “Government order dated 28.01.2025 shall not come in the way of the respondents/accused submitting a compliance report in this contempt proceeding,” it said.
Lokayukta’s 2014 order
On the basis of a complaint of land grabbing filed by the former Mandya MP G Madegowda, the Karnataka Lokayukta sought a report in 2014 from local authorities in the then Bengaluru Rural region on the land records in Kethiganahalli village of Bidadi.
Kumaraswamy, his close relative and former MLA D C Thamanna, and an aunt of Kumaraswamy were named in the complaint for allegedly encroaching on government land with a market value of over Rs 130 crore at the time.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In an order dated August 5, 2014, the Lokayukta ordered the recovery of government land if there were no records of grants in favour of private individuals.
“The Tahsildar himself is one of the persons who has submitted this joint report. It is an admitted fact that these lands bearing ‘sy.nos. 7, 8, 9, 10, 16, 17 and 19 are the Government lands i.e., gomala. The persons who are found to be in possession of these lands mentioned in Annexure-6 with sketch no. 6 claim that they have purchased these lands from private persons and that some of these lands were gifted to them,” the Lokayukta said in 2014.
The Lokayukta directed a full investigation by revenue officials and stated that “if it is found that such grants of land were not there, then necessary legal steps should be taken for the recovery of the possession of the Government land from the encroachers and also to initiate criminal action against the persons found trespassing the land and against the guilty officers/officials of the government”.
After the state government delayed the implementation of the Lokayukta directions of 2014, the Samaj Parivartana Samuday approached the high court with a writ petition. In an order on January 14, 2020, the court noted a submission from the state advocate-general “that the state will comply with and implement the order dated August 5, 2014, passed by the Karnataka Lokayukta within a period of three months” to dispose of the petition.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
In December 2020, the NGO filed a civil contempt of court petition against state government officials over their failure to comply with the August 5, 2014, directions of the Lokayukta, despite the assurances given earlier in the high court.

headline: Union Budget 2025: In Pune, research body BAIF welcomes gene bank announcement
description: Hailing the budget announcement on setting up a second gene bank, Bharat Kakade, the president of BAIF Development Research Foundation, said preservation of native species was important.
content:
Bharat Kakade, the president and managing trustee of Pune- based BAIF Development Research Foundation, popularly known as BAIF, welcomed Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman’s announcement of setting up the 2nd Gene Bank for future food and nutritional security.
“Native species are part of the agricultural biodiversity of the area. So if they are not preserved, they will cause irrevocable damage,” Kakade said. Preservation of native species, he added, was important “given the manner in which they are being lost due to commercialisation of agriculture”.
The institution has two ex-situ gene banks – one at the Urali Kanchan facility in Pune and the other at its Jawahar campus in Palghar district.
In her Union Budget 2025 speech, Sitharaman said, “The 2nd Gene Bank with 10 lakh germplasm lines will be set up for future food and nutritional security. This will provide conservation support to both public and private sectors for genetic resources.”
For several years now, BAIF has been maintaining both in-situ and ex-situ gene banks with over 700 varieties of rice, millets and vegetables. Ex-situ conservation results in conservation off fields while in-situ conservation means farmers cultivate the varieties on field. The institution has two ex-situ gene banks – one at the Urali Kanchan facility in Pune and the other at its Jawahar campus in Palghar district.

Native species, Kakade said, have huge potential in terms of health benefits. “These species have traits like being drought-resistant which are yet to be tapped,” he added.
Kakade said native species are increasingly being sidelined as commercial agriculture is dependent on hybrid seeds. Given the drought-resistant nature of native seeds, Kakade said a mix and match of these seeds with the commercial varieties would help farmers drought-proof their crops.

headline: ‘Big relief, can plan many things now’: Kolkata’s salaried class reacts positively to Union Budget 2025
description: Reacting to the announcements made by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in her Budget speech, working professionals in Kolkata welcome the high income tax rebate and hope their medical costs will fall.
content:
Bijo Abraham, who works in the fast-moving consumer goods industry, eagerly awaited the Budget 2025, wondering how much tax would be imposed on his salary. As a father of two daughters, he needs to plan for their future, and the announcement of the income tax rebate has brought him joy.
“I am happy about the tax rebate. No tax for up to Rs 12.75 lakh. It will help me a lot as I can save a bit more for my daughters’ higher education. Also, with the rising cost of living, this will help the middle class a lot,” he said sitting at his home in Rashbehari, Kolkata.
Kinshuk Sanyal, 37, a Lake Town resident working in the IT sector, welcomed the Budget but raised a concern about tax fairness. “This time the government has thought of the middle class and the salaried class. But this should not be called income tax; it should be called salaried tax because it’s the salaried class who is paying it. The government should ensure that all those who earn pay taxes. Then only can it be called income tax.”

Sharmistha Chakraborty, a 65-year-old resident of Tollygunge and a housewife suffering from breast cancer, expressed concerns about healthcare costs. “Cancer treatment is very expensive, with medication, surgery, chemotherapy and radiation. Though it is a common disease now, it is not affordable for lower- or middle-income groups. I am a widow and a lot of my savings go towards treatment expenses. The monthly cost is around Rs 60,000-70,000. This reduction in the price of medicines is welcome, but we need to see when the medicine companies will implement it.”

headline: TMC worker shot dead in broad daylight in Naihati: Police; party suspect BJP hand
description: An investigation is underway and a manhunt has been launched to track the culprits, the police officer added. Following the incident, the TMC blamed the BJP for the murder of Yadav.
content:
A TMC worker, Santosh Yadav, was shot dead in broad daylight in the Gauripur area of Naihati police station in North 24 Parganas district on Friday afternoon.
According to the police, the incident occurred around 3:55 pm when Yadav was allegedly surrounded and was shot repeatedly at close range.
“Santosh Yadav was passing by the Gauripur area when the crime took place. He managed to snatch away the revolver from the first attacker after the initial incident of firing. However, he could not save himself as the other miscreants fired at him four times. One bullet hit him in the head,” a police officer said.
Yadav was declared “brought dead” when taken to the Naihati State General Hospital, he said.

An investigation is underway and a manhunt has been launched to track the culprits, the police officer added.
Following the incident, the TMC blamed the BJP for the murder of Yadav.
Naihati MLA Sanat Dey alleged that it was a murder by the BJP-backed criminals.
“Santosh Yadav, an active worker of our party was surrounded by 8-10 people. These were hooligans of Arjun Singh, Rajesh Shaw, Chintu Singh, total ten persons are behind his murder. They fired four rounds. He received one bullet on forehead, one on nose and one near collar bone. After Arjun Singh lost in Lok Sabha he had tried his best to kill Yadav,” Dey alleged.

headline: Dahisar case: Victim’s uncertainty over injuries among grounds for boyfriend’s acquittal by court
description: The victim’s own uncertainty about how she sustained critical injuries were among the grounds on which a sessions court cleared a 27-year-old man arrested in 2022 on charges of attempting to murder his girlfriend. The Dindoshi sessions court had on Thursday acquitted Amey Darekar of charges that he had pushed his then girlfriend, 24-year-old Priyangi […]
content:
The victim’s own uncertainty about how she sustained critical injuries were among the grounds on which a sessions court cleared a 27-year-old man arrested in 2022 on charges of attempting to murder his girlfriend.
The Dindoshi sessions court had on Thursday acquitted Amey Darekar of charges that he had pushed his then girlfriend, 24-year-old Priyangi Singh, from an 18-foot water tank of a high-rise in the northern suburbs of Dahisar on November 13, 2022. The detailed order was made available on Friday.
The court said that the evidence was contradictory as the victim herself has said that the accused did not push her and that she might have fallen on her own.
Among the other reasons for clearing Darekar of the charges, the court has said the police had not produced any evidence to prove that he had the intention to kill Singh. The court said that he was present at the scene but intent, essential to prove section 307 (attempt to murder) of the Indian Penal Code, was missing from the police’s case.
“The foundational fact has not been proved by the prosecution. There is no evidence of prior enmity, provocation or motive for the accused to have committed such an act against the victim. The prosecution has not established any motive as to why the accused would attempt to kill the victim. The nature of the injuries sustained by the victim is fatal to life but in absence of involvement of accused to commit injuries, the accused cannot be held liable,” additional sessions judge D G Dhoble said in the order.
According to the complaint filed before the Dahisar police by Singh’s father, his daughter, who worked in a BPO, had left for work around 4.30 pm on November 12, 2022. The court records say that when the family tried to contact her subsequently, she did not respond. Expecting her to be busy at work, Singh’s parents went for a morning walk the next day. When they returned, the victim was lying in bed in an injured condition. Their domestic help informed them that Darekar’s mother had dropped the victim in a cab, in an injured condition. They rushed her to a hospital, where she underwent treatment for severe injuries. Her family filed a complaint against Darekar, claiming that he had pushed her from the water tank.
Singh in her deposition before the court said that she and the accused were drinking with a friend at the high-rise on the intervening night of November 12 and 13, 2022. She remembered that the friend had left and Darekar and she were watching videos about leopard sightings in the area. But she did not recollect what had happened next and that she gained consciousness at a hospital, she told the court. “The victim’s own uncertainty about how she sustained injuries creates reasonable doubt about whether any intentional act was committed by the accused at all,” the court said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The prosecution had said that the victim was found in a critically injured condition and that CCTV footage showed the accused carrying the victim, rather than seeking immediate medical help. It also said that Darekar had not given any plausible explanation for how Singh got injured, since he was with her. The court, however, said that Darekar has ‘satisfactorily explained’ the injuries sustained by the victim, stating that she accidentally fell from the terrace.
The police had also earlier dropped the charge against Darekar’s mother for lack of evidence. Darekar, who was in custody since November 2022, was ordered to be released. Singh has been bedridden due to the injuries.

headline: Delhi Assembly elections | In Kejriwal citadel, buzz of unease: ‘Not all promises fulfilled’
description: Over the past week, The Indian Express crisscrossed this high-profile block of 1.09 lakh voters in the heart of Delhi, where slum clusters jostle with upscale hotspots, and found that while many are willing to give the AAP founder another chance, there is also a sense of disillusionment.
content:
Pushpa Sharma (44), a housewife from a slum cluster, says she “was a staunch supporter” of Arvind Kejriwal “but he is giving us the same old promises now”.
Jaikesh Mishra (41) says some promises that Kejriwal made to auto drivers like him “have not been fulfilled” and “some have changed their opinions (about the ex-CM)”.
Sushil Arora (42), a tour operator, says AAP’s offers are “very tempting” but “Delhi’s financial situation is worsening so how can we be sure they will fulfill their promises”.
In the last three Assembly elections spanning nearly 12 years, the majority of voters in the New Delhi constituency spoke in one voice, echoing the name of Arvind Kejriwal — and that showed in the results: 53.46% in 2013, 64.14% in 2015 and 61.1% in 2020. This time, as voting looms on February 5, those voices don’t have the same echo.

Over the past week, The Indian Express crisscrossed this high-profile block of 1.09 lakh voters in the heart of Delhi, where slum clusters jostle with upscale hotspots, and found that while many are willing to give the AAP founder another chance, there is also a sense of disillusionment.

“He is giving us the same old promises. He is himself living in a villa, and only visits us from election to election. When it rains here, the roads become waterlogged,” says Pushpa Verma, who stays in the Sangam Mess JJ cluster near Mandi House.
“We were all staunch supporters of Kejriwal ji,” says Jaikesh Mishra, the auto driver. But today, most of the WhatsApp groups on his phone have a BJP tilt. “There are no parking spaces for us… the middle man asks us Rs 1,000 for a permit sometimes,” Mishra adds while listing his grievances.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Kejriwal has helped poor people a lot, but now every other party is following his policy. They are all promising the same freebies,” says Chattar Singh (50), who clicks photos for a living at India Gate, amid a busy afternoon. “The BJP has also promised free electricity and water this time, and they improve the infrastructure too. People want change sometimes,” he says.
Pointing to arrangements made at Kartavya Path for Republic Day, Singh, who lives in a JJ cluster nearby, adds, “The BJP has done all this. They can change the state of Delhi’s roads as well.”
Also Read | If you press jhaadu, you could save Rs 35k a month: AAP chief
In 2015 and 2020, Kejriwal pushed the BJP to a distant second, with Nupur Sharma managing just 28.73% of votes and Sunil Kumar Yadav 32.75% five years later. Meanwhile, the AAP consolidated its hold across the National Capital with close to 15% of Delhi’s total budget dedicated to subsidies, including free bus rides, free electricity and water. The AAP government also spent close to 40% of its budget on health and education, among  the highest for any state.
And yet, it’s not an open and shut case this time in Kejriwal’s fort.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
One reason, of course, is that among the 22 other candidates in the fray here are the sons of two former Delhi CMs: BJP’s Parvesh Verma, son of Sahib Singh Verma, and Congress’s Sandeep Dikshit, son of Sheila Dikshit. In fact, it was here in 2013 that Kejriwal himself dethroned Sheila Dikshit, ending her 15-year rule.
“All the parties are offering the same things… Even if 15% vote for the Congress in New Delhi, BJP could win,” says Mishra, the auto driver, adding that “if Congress was not there, Kejriwal would have won easily”.
“I still think AAP is reliable but our cluster is very divided this time,” says a resident of Sangli Mess, where voters are split between AAP and BJP. For Darshana (65), another resident, health is a major issue. “I am a sugar patient and have to travel all the way to Vinod Nagar in East Delhi to get medicines… sometimes, there are no medicines available there either. We need more Mohalla clinics throughout Delhi,” she says.
Express Explained | Kejriwal vs Haryana government: Why Yamuna in Delhi has high ammonia levels
The nearly 3 lakh households in Delhi’s 675 slums and 1,700 JJ clusters make up almost 10% of the electorate and form one of the most crucial vote banks in the National Capital. Of these households, close to a fifth are situated in the New Delhi Parliamentary constituency, which includes the New Delhi Assembly seat along with nine others.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Even in Connaught Place, nearly 2 km from Sangli Mess, voters seem divided. “I think cleanliness and pollution should be an issue this time…for how long can we rely on freebies?” says Sushil Arora, the tour operator.
This time around, with New Delhi seeing a drop of 25.3% (36,800) in its percent of voters from 2020 to 2025, partly owing to migrating government employees, AAP is also trying to reach out to middle class voters. Last Wednesday, the party came out with a “budget for the middle class” in an attempt to regain the voter base which rallied behind it during the India Against Corruption movement that led to its formation.
The 2022 People Research on India’s Consumer Economy (PRICE) survey pegs Delhi’s middle-class households — defined as those that earn between Rs 5 lakh and Rs 30 lakh per year — at 67.17%, among the highest in the country.
And in 2020, according to a post poll survey conducted by Lokniti-CSDS, an independent research institute, the AAP registered a 2-percentage point gain among middle-class voters, securing 53% of the votes.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Lokniti survey also showed, however, that the BJP had narrowed sizable gaps with AAP among the poor, lower-income and middle-income voters between the 2015 and 2020 polls.
But then, there are still strong echoes from the last three elections, from those who continue to stand behind their “favourite” leader.
“Health, education, electricity and water… earlier governments didn’t pay attention to this. Only AAP has worked to improve the state of Delhi on the following parameters,” says Rakesh Singh (44), who resides near Gole Market. “What will happen to healthcare and education when the BJP is voted in? I don’t think I can trust them… AAP is more reliable to me,” he says.

headline: Cop assaulted in road rage incident, 4 arrested
description: The officer, currently posted at Bhajanpura police station and working with the Static Surveillance Team (SST) in connection with election duties, was allegedly manhandled by four individuals after his two-wheeler got stuck behind a car on a narrow bridge.
content:
Four men have been arrested after a Delhi Police sub-inspector, who has been deployed on election duty, was allegedly assaulted and injured in a road rage incident in the early hours of Friday. According to the police, the incident occurred around 12:30 am when the officer was returning home from duty.
“A video of an assault of a police officer by 4-5 persons in the area of Bhajanpura is being circulated on social media platforms. A case has been registered at Bhajanpura police station. All four accused involved in the incident were identified and arrested within hours. Further investigation in the matter is in progress,” said DCP North East, Ashish Mishra. The accused were identified as Harsh (24), Avnit (25), Himanshu (29), and Mayank (28).
The officer, currently posted at Bhajanpura police station and working with the Static Surveillance Team (SST) in connection with election duties, was allegedly manhandled by four individuals after his two-wheeler got stuck behind a car on a narrow bridge. According to a police official, the police officer was returning from duty on his bike when he saw a car blocking the road. “Four people were standing outside the car and were talking and eating. He asked them to move the vehicle aside, upon which the four started arguing with him,” the police official said. Following the attack, a case under sections 115(2), 126(2), and 3(5) was registered.

headline: What do Delhi’s youngest and oldest poll candidates want for their city
description: According to the Election Commission’s guidelines, the minimum age for contesting elections is 25.
content:
They may be on opposite ends of the age spectrum but the welfare of the Capital’s youth is the core objective of both the oldest and youngest candidates contesting the upcoming Delhi Assembly polls.
Meet Kumari Bhawana (25) contesting as an independent candidate from the New Delhi constituency and Jagdish Chand, 83, who is a CPI(M) candidate from Badarpur.
“My issues are genuine and I hope to win…,” Bhawana tells The Indian Express. For Chand, age is just a number. “What if I am old? People respect me a lot. They love me and I know they will vote for me for change.”
According to the Election Commission’s guidelines, the minimum age for contesting elections is 25.

Bhawana, a resident of Nand Nagri in Northeast Delhi, is one of four candidates aged 25 contesting the elections in Delhi. She is up against high-profile candidates in a high-profile seat — AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, former BJP MP Parvesh Verma and Congress’ Sandeep Dikshit.
The constituency has a total of 1,08,574 voters — 58,381 are male, 50,192 are female and there is one transgender person.
Bhawana’s father, Devender, is as a wage labourer. The family lives in a one-room house, paying a rent of Rs 8,000 per month. She is the eldest of her two siblings — a 23-year-old sister and a 21-year-old brother.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
After completing BCom   from Delhi University’s School of Open Learning, she helped out her father financially by doing part-time jobs. “The idea of contesting elections came to my mind after I lost my job last year, says Bhawana. “I was employed as an associate administrator at a bank. After working there for a few months, they asked me to leave without providing a valid reason. I protested a lot, but it was to no avail. After facing this setback and seeing the condition of my family, I decided to contest.”
“I’ve borrowed Rs 10,000 from my relatives to contest the election. With the help of my brother, I designed the pamphlet on my mobile phone and published it in sets of 50 or 100 from a separate printing press to save money,” she says.
What are the issues she’s focusing on? She says it’s on “issues related to our youth”. “I want to end the practice of contractual jobs, provide free medical and healthcare facilities, and offer free education,” she adds.
On why she decided to challenge the stalwarts in the New Delhi constituency, she says that since it is a “hot seat”, people might listen to her more. “I don’t have a vehicle so I’ll be focusing on door-to-door campaigning.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Chand, meanwhile, is no stranger to elections — this is the third time he’s contesting. “I have been associated with the CPI(M) since 1979. The party has provided me with logistical support to contest the election,” he says.
Lying vacant after its former legislator, Ramvir Singh Bidhuri, was elected as the South Delhi BJP MP last year, Badarpur has an electorate of 3,64,721 voters including 2,03,185 male, 1,61,484 female and 52 transgender voters.
The AAP has fielded Ram Singh Netaji, the BJP has given a ticket to Narayan Dutt Sharma and the Congress to Arjun Bhadana from the seat.
Chand flags several problems in the constituency. Listing them out, he says, “Water is being contaminated due to several illegal jeans factories that use chemicals. There’s petty crime, land grabbing, corruption, and no proper sewage system.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
While campaigning door to door, Chand promises the people that he will make Badarpur free from illegal jeans factories, build a college and a hospital, raise the height of high-tension wires, and reclaim government land from the possession of the land mafia.
Chand, who retired from the NTPC as a supervisor, lives with his wife and two sons, who are in the property business in Meethapur village, Badarpur.
In 2012, he contested the MCD polls from Meethapur ward but lost by a margin of just 41 votes. In the 2020 Assembly polls, he had contested from Badarpur and finished fourth.
“Jeet haar to chalti rahegi, lekin hame bharosa hai ek din yahan ke logon ka bhala hoga. (Winning or losing will continue, but I trust that one day, people of this area will have a better life),” he says.
