“The state health team is working closely with local, divisional and municipal corporations and other departments of water supply and animal husbandry,” Dr Vinayak told The Indian Express. The Indian Council of Medical Research- National Institute of Virology has tested 155 samples and analysis is underway. The campylobacter jejuni and noro virus have been found in many samples.
“We are monioring the case trend and a rigorous surveillance has been undertaken. Among the patients with GBS, we found that 34 per cent had prior history of loose motions, diarrhoea and 14 per cent had symptoms of acute respiratory illness. Close to 49 per cent had not reported any prior symptoms,” said Dr Vinayak.
On hospital preparedness, Dr Vinayak added that there are 2,168 ICU beds, 1,356 ventilators and 1,416 intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) vials . The Food and Drug Administration has also inspected more than 50 places.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The state health secretary added that GBS is a rare neurological disorder and the autoimmune reactions can occur four to six weeks after an illness. He pointed out that as per scientific literature, it is often difficult to pinpoint the trigger in 40 per cent of the GBS cases.
Dr Vinayak also referred to the poultry link to GBS cases and said bio-security measures have to be ensured by poultry farms. “Biosecurity measures have to be ensured as C.jejuni bacteria are known to be present in poultry without causing infection. The animal husbandry department has been advised to consults veterinarians,” Dr Vinayak added.
Eye on poultry farms
Officials from the animal husbandry department visited 11 poultry farms located around the Khadkwasala dam. A total of 106 samples of cloacal swab (89)and poultry faeces (17) were submitted to the National Institute of Virology. A total of 24 samples tested positive for C.jejuni bacteria. Five samples were positive for norovirus from one farm. Meanwhile, 26 water samples (from the farms) tested negative for C. jejuni
Out of the 11 farms, six belong to a single group specializing in rearing layers, while the remaining five are owned by individual poultry farmers who rear broilers. The group farms have maintained biosecurity and two farms have their own sewage treatment facility. Other farms also have litter disposal pits. Litter produced is sold as manure for farming as organic fertilizer.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Individual broiler poultry farmers rear their birds using the deep-litter system, following an “all-in, all-out” approach. After approximately 45 days, the entire batch is sold as manure. Following proper disinfection, a new batch is introduced.
The visiting team found no evidence of spills or drainage from these farms reaching the Khadakwasla dam. Officers from the animal husbandry department in nearby institutes have been advised to carry out a special disinfection activity on these farms within the next two days.

headline: Maharashtra: Meet the numismatist whose collection boasts 1,000 Shivaji Maharaj era coins
description: Parag’s fascination with numismatics began in 2008 when his uncle gifted him a coin from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s era
content:
Katraj resident Parag Suresh Jagtap, 36, has spent years building an extraordinary collection of historical coins. His collection includes over 1,000 copper coins featuring Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, specifically the Shivrai currency, which was introduced during the Maratha king’s coronation in 1674.
Parag’s fascination with numismatics began in 2008 when his uncle gifted him a coin from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s era. That single coin sparked his interest, leading him on a journey to uncover and preserve the legacy of the Shivrai currency. “The attraction towards collecting coins started around 2008 when my uncle gave me a Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj era coin. This fascinated me about the legacy and uniqueness of the coins manufactured then,” he said.
To build his collection, Parag explored Pune’s Juna Bazaar, various forts associated with Maharaj, nearby villages, and even old foundries across Maharashtra. Through years of dedicated searching, he was able to gather a wide range of Shivrai copper coins, each bearing distinct patterns and historical significance.
“During Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s Rajyabhishek (coronation ceremony) in 1674, a limited number of gold and copper coins were issued to mark the historic event. But over time, people melted the gold coins for ornaments, making them rare, while copper coins survived. So, I focused on collecting copper coins and have found over 1,000 with different patterns so far,” he said.
To deepen his understanding of the coins, Parag refers to Maharashtra State Board history books and other literature on Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. He studies the nuances of coinage from that era, such as weight, shape, and purpose of each coin. “Gold coins were mostly traded by sardars, while copper coins were used by common people. The coins were mostly circular, and a Shivrai would weigh about 2.75 grams. Earlier, the value of a coin was equal to its metal worth, and people used to logically weigh them on their palms to determine their value. It took one lakh Gold Hon (a gold coin that had been minted minted on the occasion of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s coronation) to build Sindhudurg Fort in Malvan,” said Parag.
Beyond the Shivrai coins, Parag has expanded his collection to include over 3,000 coins from different parts of the world, rare postcards, stamps, books, and matchboxes related to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s era. “Despite years of effort, I am still unaware of many historical facts, so research and study remain a daily affair,” he added.
His collection includes various Shivrai coins spanning from Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj’s coronation in the 17th century to the 19th century. He said “Among these, I have coins minted during Maharaj’s coronation, which bear the inscription ‘Shri Raja Shiva’ on one side and ‘Chhatrapati’ on the other. Additionally, my collection features coins issued by the successors of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj who ascended the throne after him.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Shivrai currency is a symbol of the self-respecting Marathi empire. Unlike other coins of that time, which had inscriptions in Persian, Urdu, and English, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj ensured that Shivrai coins were inscribed in the Marathi Devanagari script. The design of these coins was influenced by the Vijayanagar Empire’s currency and evolved over time, incorporating symbols like the sun, moon, various weapons, the Shivling, and Bel leaves. “These coins are round, approximately 2.7 cm in diameter, and weigh around 11 to 12 grams. They are made of pure copper and typically feature ‘Chhatrapati’ on one side and the ruler’s name on the other,” Parag said.
Apart from Shivrai, Parag has also collected rare and unique coins from across the world. “I possess rare coins such as a set from Somaliland featuring the 12 zodiac signs, India’s first-ever plastic coin, and commemorative coins of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in denominations of Rs 100, Rs 50, and Rs 2. My collection also includes individually minted coins issued by various Maratha chieftains in their respective regions. Additionally, I own coins from the reign of Hindu emperor Prithviraj Chauhan, coins from the Satavahana period, rare postal covers, Maharashtra-themed postage stamps, and a collection of rare books,” he shared.

headline: In Pocso case against Yediyurappa, court peruses victim’s statement in fresh cognisance process
description: Former Karnataka CM Yediyurappa is alleged to have subjected a minor girl to sexually inappropriate behaviour at his house on February 2, 2024.
content:
A special court for Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act cases on Tuesday perused a statement of a minor victim—recorded by a magistrate under Criminal Procedure Code section 164—in a case filed against former Karnataka chief minister B S Yediyurappa.
The special court is re-examining a chargesheet filed by the CID and evidence contained in it in the wake of the Karnataka High Court’s February 7 order directing the case to proceed from the stage of taking cognisance of the chargesheet.
The special court posted the matter for further perusal on February 24.
The special court, which was earlier scheduled to hear the case against the former chief minister on February 28, advanced the hearing to February 12, as sought by the public prosecutor in light of the high court order.

The special public prosecutor filed an application stating that section 35 of the Pocso Act 2012 mandates that the evidence of the child should be recorded within 30 days and that the trial must be completed within a year—from the date of the court taking cognisance of the case.
The high court, while rejecting a plea filed by Yediyurappa to quash the entire Pocso case against him, ruled that the special court judge had erred in application of mind while taking cognisance of the chargesheet earlier in July 2024, since no reasons were given for it.
“The Writ Petition is allowed in part. The order of taking cognizance by the concerned court dated July 4, 2024 qua accused number one stands obliterated,” Justice M Nagaprasanna said in his February 7 order. “The crime, the investigation and the final report all remain intact. The matter is remitted back to the concerned court to pass appropriate orders on the final report so placed before it by the CID bearing in mind the observations made in the course of the order.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The high court said the special court must make a reasoned order for taking cognisance of the chargesheet. “Though the reasons need not be so elaborate when it records framing of charges or conviction, nonetheless, it must bear application of mind to set further proceedings in motion, as taking of cognizance or issuance of process has some judicial sanctity,” the court said.
The high court also granted conditional anticipatory bail to Yediyurappa stating that no investigation was pending against him. Since Yediyurappa “is an octogenarian and has held the position of the Chief Minister of the State of Karnataka and there can be no apprehension that he would not cooperate with the trial on its ensuing”, the court said.
FIR and chargesheet
An FIR was filed on March 14, 2024, against Yediyurappa, 81, by the Bengaluru police on the basis of a complaint by the mother of a teenager stating that her daughter had been subjected to sexually inappropriate behaviour by the former chief minister during a visit to his house on February 2 that year.
The CID unit of the police filed a chargesheet against the BJP veteran and three others on June 27, 2024, under Pocso Act section 8 (sexual assault) and Indian Penal Code section 354 A (sexual harassment), 204 (destroying evidence) and 214 (offering gifts to silence the victim).
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The Pocso court took cognisance of the chargesheet on July 4, 2024, and issued summonses for the former chief minister and others.
Yediyurappa approached the high court for the quashing of the case during the CID investigations and the court ruled on June 14, 2024, that the former chief minister should not be arrested and later, on July 12, exempted him and three others from appearing in the special court in response to the summonses.
Although the high court issued no stay against the proceedings in the special court, they had been stalled since July 4, 2024, on account of Yediyurappa moving the high court to quash the chargesheet.

headline: Maharashtra CM directs cyber police to get objectionable content on Sambhaji Maharaj removed from Wikipedia
description: The objection regarding highly revered King Sambhaji Maharaj came in the wake of the recently released film titled Chhaava.
content:
Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Tuesday said he has directed the state cyber police to reach out to Wikipedia and get objectionable content related to Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj removed from the online platform.
Fadnavis, talking to media persons in Mumbai, said, “Historical facts should be properly projected. Any distortion will not be tolerated on any open platform like Wikipedia or social media.”
“I have asked the inspector general of cyber cell to contact Wikipedia and bring it to their notice objectionable writing on Sambhaji Maharaj. They should be told to immediately delete these factually incorrect aspects,” he said.
The objection regarding highly revered King Sambhaji Maharaj came in the wake of the recently released film titled Chhaava. The film, based on the life of Sambhaji Maharaj, had a dance sequence which created an uproar. The film makers removed the sequence.

However, some social organisations raised objection over incorrect material on Sambhaji Maharaj on Wikipedia. The followers of Sambhaji Maharaj warned that if the content is not removed, they would protest.
Sambhaji Maharaj is the son of great warrior King Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. Both Shivaji Maharaj and Sambhaji Maharaj are highly revered in Maharashtra and across country.
The chief minister said, “The Wikipedia is not managed or controlled by India. In India, its volunteers hold editorial rights. We can ask them to bring some regulations to avoid controversial and factually incorrect writings on their platform.”

headline: Srinagar MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi accuses BJP of creating ‘anti-Muslim’ theatre: ‘Kashmir its biggest scene’

“BJP has created a theatre, they show this theatre to people who give them applause, and in return, the BJP gets votes. That audience is hardcore Hindutva and the theatre that has been made for them is the condition of the Muslims…,” Mehdi said at a talk on ‘Political Representation and Citizenship in Post-370 Jammu and Kashmir’, organised by National Students’ Union of India-JNU.
“…the biggest scene in this theatre is Kashmir because Kashmir has a Muslim population …because these Muslims have power in their hands, they should be snatched off this power and brought to their knees. What more can be a bigger theatre than this?” Mehdi added.

headline: Blast at house of cop’s relative in Punjab’s Gurdaspur; ‘law and order worsening,’ says MP Sukhjinder Randhawa
description: The incident took place at postman Sukhdev Singh’s house. A social media post claimed that Sukhdev’s relative, Jatinder, a policeman, was the original target.
content:
An explosion occurred at the house of a Punjab police official’s relative in Raimal village in Gurdaspur district on Monday night, sparking panic in the area. The police confirmed the incident and said that no injuries were reported.
The incident took place at postman Sukhdev Singh’s house. While the sound of the explosion was heard across the village, the windows of the house were shattered due to the impact. Sukhdev is a relative of policeman Jatinder Singh, whose house is situated a few metres away from where the blast took place, leading to speculation that Jatinder was the original target.
“Around 8 pm, Kotli Surat Mallian police station received information that a blast sound was heard at the residence of Sukhdev Singh in Raimal village. After visiting the residence, the police have begun their investigation. No damage or harm has been reported,” Riputapan Singh Sandhu, Deputy Superintendent of Police, Gurdaspur, said.
CCTV footage of the incident purportedly shows motorbike-riding accused carrying out the attack.

As per unconfirmed reports, gangster Happy Passia has claimed responsibility for the attack in a Facebook post, saying that Jatinder had raided his house two months ago and mistreated his family. Passia had previously been booked for allegedly targeting police stations and outposts in Punjab.
A social media post, allegedly on behalf of Babbar Khalsa International, warned police officers “with a similar mindset to think about their own families before engaging in such actions”. The post accused the police of conducting fake encounters and harassing innocent families and warned of retaliatory action targeting police officials.
While 11 explosions have been reported in the state in the last four months, this is the first such incident near a police official’s house.

Sukhdev said that he and his family had finished eating dinner on Monday and were getting ready to sleep when the explosion took place. Sukhdev alleged that the attackers may have mistaken his house to be that of his nephew. Jatinder’s house was located close to his house but the family has not been living there for a while now, Sukhdev said. He also claimed that a few months ago, there had been an attempt to fire at him, which he had reported to the police at the time.
Gurdaspur Congress MP Sukhjinder Randhawa visited the family and hit out at Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann for the “worsening law and order situation in the state”. “Last night, a grenade attack took place at the home of my fellow police officer’s uncle in Rai Mal village in my constituency, Dera Baba Nanak. Before your police administration tries to pass it off as a ‘tire or compressor explosion,’ I am sharing pictures of this dangerous incident,” Randhawa said.
“The ongoing explosions in border areas and the chief minister’s silence are worsening Punjab’s law and order situation day by day. CM Sahib, the people of Punjab are living in fear because they have lost trust in you and your administration. If you continue to ignore the law and order situation in the region, you will be held responsible for any worsening circumstances. Thankfully, no one was injured,” Randhawa added.

headline: Asked to remove all our clothes including turbans… mentally tortured: US deportee from Punjab
description: Close to midnight on Saturday, Jaswinder was among the second batch of Indian nationals deported by the US. It was only when he reached Amritsar airport that he was able to wear his turban again.
content:
Jaswinder Singh, 21, from Pandori Arian village of Dharamkot in Moga district, started his illegal journey to the US after selling his family’s 1.5 kila of land and mortgaging their two-room house. The family even had to sell their buffaloes to raise Rs 44 lakh, which they paid to an agent to get Jaswinder to the US.
Close to midnight on Saturday, Jaswinder was among the second batch of Indian nationals deported by the US. It was only when he reached Amritsar airport that he was able to wear his turban again—nearly 20 days after being detained by US authorities upon crossing the US-Mexico border illegally on January 27.
Speaking to The Indian Express, Jaswinder said, “As soon as I was detained on January 27 and taken to the detention centre, they asked me to remove all my clothes, including my turban. We were allowed to wear only a T-shirt, a lower, socks, and shoes. They also removed our shoelaces. I and other Sikh youths asked them to at least return our turbans, but they refused. They said, ‘Who will be responsible if any of you hangs self to death?’ For all the days we were at the detention centre, we were not allowed to wear a turban. It was only after reaching Amritsar airport that I got my luggage back and wrapped my head with a parna (a cloth worn by Sikh men to cover their heads).”
Jaswinder Singh was among the second batch of Indian nationals deported by the US. (Express Photo)
Jaswinder said he wanted to go to the US to support his family, as his father was a heart patient and could no longer work. “Now we are under a debt of Rs 44 lakh and have no idea how we will repay it. We even mortgaged our house,” said Jaswinder, a Class 10 pass, who left home in December last year and first landed in Prague, Czech Republic, from Delhi before reaching the US-Mexico border via Spain, El Salvador, Guatemala, and Mexico.

My agent had also promised that once I was detained, he would bail me out of the detention centre, but he never fulfilled this promise. Now I want my money back. The Punjab government should make him return it,” he said.
Alleging “mental torture” in the detention centre and on the US military plane that ferried them back to Amritsar, Jaswinder said, “On the flight, our hands and feet were chained. We boarded the plane on January 13, and for nearly three days, we were inside without knowing where we were being taken. If anyone stood up even for a minute to stretch, the US authorities on board would reprimand us and order us to sit down. We shivered in the cold, as we were given only plastic sheets, which were not enough in the biting cold.”
“Now I don’t have any money to go abroad again, either to the US or anywhere else. I want my money back from the agent,” said Jaswinder, who has four siblings to support.

headline: Switch to clean fuel by July 8, BMC directs eateries, bakeries
description: The BMC move comes after the city consistently recorded poor and bad air quality ever since the monsoon got over in October 2024.
content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) on Monday directed all the eateries, bakeries, hotels and roadside vendors to switch to clean, natural and eco-friendly fuel by July 8.
The BMC move comes after the city consistently recorded poor and bad air quality ever since the monsoon got over in October 2024. The BMC also attributed to the Bombay High Court (HC) order, which on January 9, gave the civic body a six-month period for making the commercial entities to switch to eco-friendly fuel.
“Strict action will be taken for non-compliance. Establishments must adopt CNG or PNG instead of polluting fuels,” the BMC’s statement issued on Monday read.
“Wood and coal burning releases hazardous emissions, worsening air quality and increasing respiratory diseases. Businesses must shift to cleaner fuels or face legal action,” the statement added.

“We held meetings with bakery associations and hotel owners. The civic body will provide single-window clearance system when it comes to taking permission for switching to alternate fuels, so that as many of them can switch their system at the earliest,” an official said.

headline: Mumbai surgeon’s team screens thousands for diabetes and eye disorders at Kumbh
description: The screening camp is set up at Sector 23 of Arail Ghat, where the team is conducting free blood sugar tests, vision tests, and refraction checks to determine prescription needs.
content:
At the Maha Kumbh in Prayagraj, where millions gather for spiritual reflection, a team of 100 volunteers led by Mumbai-based eye surgeon Dr Nishant Kumar is providing free eye and diabetes screenings to thousands of pilgrims and frontline personnel. Through the Eyebetes Foundation, the initiative aims to screen 20,000 to 30,000 pilgrims and 5,000 uniformed personnel for diabetes and preventable blindness.
Founded in 2016, the Eyebetes Foundation combines its focus on diabetes and eye health, conducting screenings and providing prescription glasses to those in need. The foundation regularly carries out similar efforts in Mumbai, particularly during the Ganpati festival, where more than 30,000 people receive free screenings annually. The Maha Kumbh offers an opportunity to expand these efforts to a much larger and more diverse group of people.
“We saw the Maha Kumbh as a chance to reach people who might otherwise never get an eye check-up,” said Dr. Kumar. “Many people avoid medical tests unless it’s urgent, but here, they have travelled long distances for spiritual reasons. This is an opportunity to address their health concerns while they are here.”
The screening camp is set up at Sector 23 of Arail Ghat, where the team is conducting free blood sugar tests, vision tests, and refraction checks to determine prescription needs. AI-enabled eye cameras are also being used to screen for conditions like glaucoma, cataracts, and diabetic retinopathy. Since pilgrims may not have time to wait for glasses, they receive prescriptions to get them made locally, while police personnel will have their prescription glasses delivered to their homes.

Dr. Kumar, who practices at P D Hinduja Hospital in Mumbai, highlighted the growing burden of diabetes and vision impairment in India. “Diabetes is increasing rapidly, and half of those affected may not even know they have it,” he said. “Similarly, uncorrected refractive errors are a major cause of visual impairment, yet they are often overlooked.”
One of the awareness campaigns at the Kumbh involves using the backs of Naga Sadhus as vision charts to draw attention to eye health. With countless advertisements and messages competing for attention at the Kumbh, this approach has sparked curiosity and encouraged more people to get screened.

headline: Yamuna water-poisoning remark: Former Delhi CM Kejriwal did not appear in Sonipat court, next date of hearing on March 20
description: ‘Proofs’ were handed over to Arvind Kejriwal’s counsel Bhuvesh Malik in a pen drive.
content:
Former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal did not appear in the Sonipat court in Haryana on Monday. The Sonipat court had issued a notice asking Kejriwal to appear before it in connection with a criminal complaint filed against him for his ‘Yamuna river poisoning’ remark.
In his place, Kejriwal’s lawyer Bhuvesh Malik appeared in the court. Advocate Malik apprised the court that the prosecution did not supply them with the proof and evidence based on which the criminal complaint was filed against Kejriwal. On his submission, the ‘proofs’ of Kejriwal’s remarks and other related evidence were handed over to advocate Malik in a pen drive.
Haryana Irrigation Department’s executive engineer Ashish Kaushik had filed the criminal complaint against Kejriwal in Sonipat court on the basis of social media clips in which the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor can be seen accusing Haryana of “poisoning Yamuna river waters”. Kejriwal’s remarks sparked off a political furore ahead of the Delhi Assembly polls.
The case has now been listed for March 20.
On February 4, a day before the Delhi polls, the Haryana Police had also registered an FIR against Kejriwal under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) Act. The FIR was registered in Kurukshetra based on a complaint by Shahbad resident Jagmohan Manchanda.

headline: TISS files FIR after drugs found in a room of girls’ hostel
description: TISS’s campus is home to six hostels, accommodating 976 students pursuing various higher education courses at the renowned social science institution.
content:
The Tata Institute of Social Science (TISS) has filed an FIR with Trombay Police Station after drugs were found in one of the rooms of the girls’ hostels on campus. While the FIR has been filed against an unknown person, the institute administration has expelled one of the two occupants of the where the drugs were found.
TISS’s campus is home to six hostels, accommodating 976 students pursuing various higher education courses at the renowned social science institution. Drugs were found in a room of one of the three girls’ hostels, shared by two occupants. According to the FIR, hostel warden along with others carried out a search of the said hostel-room in the evening of February 3, 2025, following a complaint by one of the two occupants of the room. This search led to the discovery of drugs in a bag belonging to the other occupant of the room.
The complainant, as mentioned in the FIR had stated that her room remains untidy and has a foul smell because of the mess by her roommate who smokes inside the room. Following the complaint, the hostel authority paid a visit to the said hostel-room. During the process, various items were found such as cigarette packets, cigarette butts. Whereas in an open bag on the bed, a transparent plastic bag was found which contained material that resembled cannabis and rolling paper. The FIR mentions that after the search, items were kept as it is and the room was locked from the outside by the authorities conducting the search, and the whole exercise was shot on video by the search team.

headline: ‘Aftershock of 1.2 magnitude natural, will heal it’: National Centre of Seismology director on Delhi earthquake
description: Shallow earthquakes, originating five or ten km below the surface, tend to cause more damage than those originating deep below the surface.
content:
The Director of the National Centre for Seismology (NCS), Dr OP Mishra, speaking to news agency ANI, assured the residents that there is nothing to worry about as the aftershocks of lesser magnitude are “natural” and will heal the earthquake of magnitude 4.0 that had struck Delhi early Monday.
Strong tremors were felt in Delhi and its surrounding areas at 5.36 a.m. Monday after a 4.0-magnitude earthquake jolted the national capital. It originated just 5 km below the earth’s surface. Shallow earthquakes, originating five or ten km below the surface, tend to cause more damage than those originating deep below the surface.
Speaking to reporters, Mishra stated: “Delhi keeps experiencing such minor earthquakes. This earthquake occurred in Dhaula Kuan. And in 2007, an earthquake of 4.7 magnitude had occurred there… There is nothing to worry about. It is a seismic zone there.”
Elaborating on the cause of the earthquake, the Director said: “The earthquake occurred due to in-situ material heterogeneity… After 4.0 magnitude, the aftershock will be less by 1.2 magnitude, it is natural as it will heal it.”

headline: Chef Ablu’s journey, from kitchen helper to culinary maestro in Chandigarh
description: Find out what went into the making of this oriental cuisine specialist who has a menu to his name
content:
In the heart of Chandigarh, where flavours blend seamlessly into culinary masterpieces, one chef’s journey stands out as a tale of perseverance, passion, and hard work. Meet Chef Ablu Bhaumik, a man who carved his path from the humble beginnings of a kitchen service trainee to a respected culinary expert at Shichang, Hyatt Regency. The story of the man, who now has a menu to his name, is not just about cooking — it’s about grit, determination, and an unyielding love for food.
Humble beginnings in the kitchen
Born in a small town near Kolkata, chef Bhaumik’s entry into the hospitality industry was anything but glamorous. He started as a kitchen service staff worker in Bengaluru, tasked with cleaning kitchens, cutting vegetables, and assisting senior chefs. While many saw it as a stepping stone, Bhaumik saw it as a classroom where he could absorb the nuances of professional cooking.
Through sheer dedication, he quickly rose through the ranks, proving that skill and hard work outweigh any formal designations. He moved from a KST worker to a commis chef, working across 3-star, 4-star, and even 5-star hotels in Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Kolkata. Eventually, his passion took him to Chandigarh, where he continues his culinary journey, creating innovative dishes and redefining flavours.
Education: A balancing act between work & studies
Despite starting his career early, Bhaumik never let go of his education. He completed his 10th-grade studies under the West Bengal Board and later pursued his 12th-grade through correspondence from the UP Board. His thirst for knowledge pushed him further — he enrolled at Garden City University, Bengaluru, to study hospitality administration.

Juggling long work shifts with studies was no easy feat. Morning classes were followed by grueling kitchen shifts, leaving little time for rest. Yet, the commitment to both his academic and professional life proved that perseverance can turn dreams into reality.
Culinary inspirations and the art cooking
Bhaumik’s culinary expertise is deeply influenced by some of the finest chefs in the industry. He looks up to chef Zhang of Zuma, New York, a master of Asian cuisine, and chef Mayo, a specialist in Japanese food. Closer to home, he admires celebrity chefs like Vikas Khanna and Vineet Bhatia, whose work has redefined Indian gastronomy on a global scale.
Though he specialises in Chinese cuisine, Bhaumik’s cooking style is versatile. He believes in adapting flavours to suit local palates while maintaining authenticity. The chef mastered the art of improvising his dishes by incorporating people’s feedback and opinions. He also enjoys channa kulcha — popular Indian street food from time to time.

Behind the scenes: The reality of a chef’s life
Running a kitchen isn’t just about cooking — it involves meticulous planning, sourcing quality ingredients, and managing a team. Bhaumik sheds light on the procurement process, explaining that hotels rely on contracted vendors who supply the ingredients.
Beyond the kitchen: A chef with many interests
When he’s not in the kitchen, Bhaumik enjoys the thrill of bike rides, exploring new destinations, and indulging in diverse cuisines. Despite his expertise in gourmet cooking, he finds comfort in simple meals like dal chawal or a perfectly grilled chicken. However, his personal favorite cuisine remains Japanese, a reflection of his admiration for its precision and technique.
A message to aspiring chefs
Bhaumik’s journey is an inspiration for young culinary enthusiasts. His advice? Never stop learning, embrace challenges, and let passion be the driving force. In a profession where long hours and high-pressure environments are the norm, only true passion can keep the fire burning.
As our conversation draws to a close, one thing becomes clear — Bhaumik’s story isn’t just about food. It’s about resilience, passion, and the relentless pursuit of excellence. headline: Within hours of stampede, mourning kin handed Rs 10 lakh in cash as compensation
description: A senior official of the Ministry of Railways said ex-gratia is an immediate relief and is different from “compensation”
content:

“They also told me in case I required security to carry this money home, they would depute an RPF constable. I told them I don’t need any security because I live in Delhi,” said Jha, adding that those who were from outside Delhi took security personnel along.
Manju Kushwaha, who lost her husband Manoj Kushwaha, 47, said, “We got Rs 10 lakh. It was all given in cash. It will help but it can never bring him back.”
In a statement, the Ministry of Railways said, “Earlier in the day, the Indian Railways gave ex-gratia of Rs 10 lakh to the kin of all the 18 deceased. An amount of Rs 2.5 lakh to grievously injured passengers and a compensation of Rs 1 lakh for passengers with minor injuries were distributed to the 15 injured during the day. Further, Indian Railways personnel assisted the families of each of the deceased by accompanying them to their homes and took part in their final rites.”
A senior official of the Ministry of Railways said ex-gratia is an immediate relief and is different from “compensation”. “That is why cash was given to the family members of the victims,” the official added.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“It is not an unusual thing. The ex-gratia was distributed in cash during the Balasore accident too. It is given in cash because… the families usually do not have bank details in hand or some of the victims do not have bank accounts. So the ex-gratia was distributed after identifying them (family members of the victims) by their Aadhaar cards. The station master has the power to order the withdrawal of money (from the official account) and it is then disbursed by the commercial department,” the official said.
Dheeraj Mishra

headline: My pension was not enough to raise two kids: ex-serviceman deported from US
description: A strict vegetarian, Jatinder had to taste chicken to survive on the way to the US.
content:
On August 14 last year, an ex-serviceman left India in search of financial independence, an American tryst with destiny. Five months later, however, he is back home poorer than ever before having blown Rs 40 lakh on the ‘dunki route’.
“I had no skill and my pension was not enough to raise two kids. So, I decided to try my luck in the US. I burnt all my savings on the dunki route. Now I am left with nothing,” Mandeep Singh, 38, told The Indian Express soon after returning on the US Army aircraft that deported Indians on Saturday night.
Mandeep served the Indian Army for more than 17 years. “I hoped that I would support my family after reaching the US. But I was not that lucky,” he said.
Returning along with Mandeep was ex-serviceman Gurcharan Singh’s son Jatinder Singh, a 23-year-old resident of Butala village in Jandiala area. He also went on ‘dunki route’. His father had paid Rs 50 lakh to an agent who promised comfortable travel to the US.

A strict vegetarian, Jatinder had to taste chicken to survive on the way to the US.
“The agent kept us in a house for nearly 52 days, where I had to compromise on my vegetarian diet. Being a baptised Sikh, I had never eaten non-vegetarian food. We were given only rice mixed with chicken at the house where we were kept. I had only two options: either to eat meat or die,” said Jatinder, who after completing his high school in 2019, had tried in vain to move abroad legally.
Throughout the journey, Jatinder faced one problem after another, including life-threatening challenges. “I almost drowned in a river after falling from the boat. They put us in a container where it was difficult to breathe. We remained locked in that container for 15 hours. We peed into bottles during the journey in the container,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“It was a translator from Pakistan who broke the news to us after we were aboard the aircraft. Neither we were given any clue that we will be deported nor did we get any chance to present our case,” said Jatinder.

headline: ‘Where is Tara?’: Man scours hospitals, returns to New Delhi railway station in search of his missing wife after stampede
description: The stampede turned what was meant to be the family’s pilgrimage to Kumbh, on board the Swatantrata Senani Express, into a night of devastation. At least 18 people died in the chaos.
content:
Gupteshwar Yadav’s fingers tremble as he holds up his phone. On the screen is a photo of his wife, Tara Devi (50), captured in a moment of calm — her blue saree draped neatly over her shoulder, red sindoor bright against her forehead, her wrists adorned with bangles.
“I lost sight of her in the crowd,” the 52-year-old murmurs, standing on platform 14 at New Delhi Railway Station on Sunday, where the stampede had unfolded the night before.
“I waited for her, but she never came.”
Must Read | Delhi railway station stampede: Behind 10-minute chaos, delay of two trains, and an announcement
The stampede turned what was meant to be the family’s pilgrimage to Kumbh into a night of devastation. At least 18 people died in the chaos.
Gupteshwar and brother Chhiteshwar (in photo) spent the night combing through hospitals, searching through the rows of bodies, and clinging onto a sliver of hope that Tara survived. (Express Photo)
“It was impossible to move on your own,” Gupteshwar says, recalling the events that unfolded on Saturday. “I was just being pushed along.”
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
MP’s Hawk Force gun down four Maoists in Balaghat encounter
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Karnataka government stops distribution of chikkis in midday meals
As the crowd swelled, he had turned back, searching for his wife, but the sea of bodies made it impossible to see beyond a few feet.
“Everyone was just trying to survive, but there was no space, no air, nothing to hold onto,” he says.
In the frenzy, he felt himself shoved sideways, stumbling toward the platform and all he could think was, “Where is Tara?”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
He and his brother Chhiteshwar spent the night combing through hospitals, searching through rows of bodies, and clinging onto a sliver of hope that Tara survived.
“I think she is no more. But we can’t give up,” says Chhiteshwar.
A few feet away from where Gupteshwar now stood, 40-year-old Digamber Mandal watched it all unfold.
Also Read | ‘Climbed up the iron grille and clung to it… people died in front of me’: Woman recounts New Delhi Railway Station horror
For 12 years, Mandal has been running the small Geeta Press bookstall on platform 14. He has seen crowds swell during Diwali and Holi, watched impatient travelers argue with ticket collectors, and even witnessed the occasional scuffle over a reserved seat. But nothing prepared him for Saturday night’s horror.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“At first, it was just another busy evening,” he recounts. “Devotees heading to the Kumbh Mela filled the platform, their bags heavy with belongings, their voices raised in excitement. Then came several announcements of trains being shifted to different platforms.”
“That’s when it started,” he says. “People panicked. No one knew which way to go. The foot overbridge was already packed, but suddenly, everyone was rushing towards it. It was so crowded that people like me could not even go forward after a point.”
Mandal watched helplessly as the crowd got swept into the narrow staircase. “I wanted to help,” he says. “But I couldn’t move amid the sea of bodies.”
As the minutes stretched, station staff arrived — too late to prevent the tragedy, but in time to carry the dead away.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Mandal says he saw bodies being pulled from the stairway and couldn’t bring himself to look at them. “I didn’t want to see,” he admits. “That’s why I didn’t take the stairs when I closed my shop later in the night. I crossed the tracks instead, just so I wouldn’t have to step over the dead.”
By Sunday morning, the platform has been cleared. Ropes now sectioned off the areas where the worst had occurred and guards stood at every corner. The crowd is more orderly. But for Gupteshwar and Chhiteshwar, and for families still searching for their loved ones, normalcy would not return so easily.
“We woke up again at 7 am and started searching for Tara,” Chhiteshwar says. “But we just can’t find her.”
During the day, a high-level committee from the Railway arrives to begin the investigation. “We have secured all CCTV footage,” says Narsingh Deo, Principal Chief Commercial Manager (PCCM), Northern Railways. “We are looking into all possible angles. Once the investigation is complete, action will be taken accordingly.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
As trains arrive and depart, Gupteshwar continues staring at the sea of faces, searching for the only one that matters. He then heads to platform number 16 and files a complaint with the Railway Protection Force.

headline: Mumbai: Man held for throwing infant daughter on the floor, killing her
description: According to police, the accused got angry after his wife allegedly slapped their eldest daughter for not eating
content:
A 34-year-old man was arrested late Saturday for forcefully throwing his three-month-old daughter on the floor, killing her, at their residence in Kurla.
According to police, the accused got angry after his wife allegedly slapped their eldest daughter for not eating, following which he allegedly picked up their infant from her lap and threw her on the floor.
The accused, identified as Parvez Siddiqui, lived with his wife Saba, their three daughters — aged five years, two-and-a-half years, and three months — his parents, three brothers, and their wives at LIG Colony in Kurla (West), police said.
They added that Parvez was unemployed, and was depending on the income of his three brothers, who work in a pharmaceutical company.

Man held for raping 12-year-old girl on way to school in UP’s Bulandshahr, search on for his mother
On February 14, after the brothers left for work, around noon, Saba was feeding their eldest daughter Daniya in their bedroom. “Parvez was also in the room as she held their three-month-old daughter Afiya on her lap,” said an officer.
When Daniya refused to eat, Saba lightly tapped her head, which angered her husband. An argument ensued and Parvez allegedly verbally abused and physically assaulted his wife.
“The couple later went to the living room, where the rest of the family was present. He kept abusing and assaulting the woman, after which he snatched Afiya from her lap, forcefully threw her on the floor, and left the house,” an officer said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
The accused’s mother picked up the infant when they noticed that she was unresponsive. The family rushed her to a private hospital, where she was declared dead on arrival.
The hospital authorities then reported the matter to police, after which Saba’s statement was recorded and a case of murder was registered.
A senior police officer said, “Parvez was traced and arrested from Kurla.”

headline: ‘Had told her not to go’: Amidst tears and anguish, families mourn victims of stampede at New Delhi Railway Station
description: At Delhi's Lok Nayak hospital, senior leaders, including Delhi’s Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena and former Chief Minister Atishi, arrived to take stock of the situation.
content:
PUSHING A stretcher towards the mortuary at Lok Nayak Jai Prakash Hospital, a weeping Aman Giri, 22, uttered one thing over and over again: “Maine mana kiya tha, mat jao (I told her we should not go). But we still planned the trip.”
On the stretcher lay the body of his mother, Sheela Giri, 47.
Sheela was among the 18 people who died in the stampede at the New Delhi Railway Station Saturday night. Her husband, Umesh Giri, suffered a leg injury.
“From our family, 37 people were supposed to go to the Kumbh Mela but only six managed to get Tatkaal tickets. Before the stampede, she said there was a massive rush on the stairs,” said Meena, Sheela’s sister-in-law.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
MP’s Hawk Force gun down four Maoists in Balaghat encounter
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Inside the hospital, doctors were overwhelmed. Medical Director Dr Suresh Kumar, along with senior physicians, was rushing between wards, trying to manage the sudden influx of injured patients. (Express photo by Gajendra Yadav)
Describing the incident, Aman said, “My mother was a bit heavy so she couldn’t climb the steps, even as everyone ran towards the stairs to escape the stampede. Some of our relatives were also on their way to the station but they were in the Metro when the incident happened.”
Outside the emergency ward at the hospital in central Delhi, anguished family members gathered in search of answers, waiting in uncertainty for news about their loved ones caught in the stampede.
Santosh Mahto, a resident of Panipat, Haryana, rushed to the hospital after learning that his wife, Lalita Devi, 35, had perished in the crush. “Main Panipat mein tha (I was in Panipat),” he explained, waiting outside the mortuary for the release of her body.
Of the 18 who died — 11 women, three men and four children — nine were from Delhi, seven from Bihar and two from Haryana.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Amid heavy police presence, the hospital saw families despair as the dead were being identified and the injured rushed to the emergency ward.
“Koi facilities nahi hain, kuch nahi hain (There are no facilities, no help),” alleged Virender, his voice choking with tears. “Kabse bhaag rahe hain, aur koi kuch bata nahi raha (We have been running around for a long time but no one’s telling us anything).”
His wife, Poonam Rohilla, was among the dead. He found out about her death after hours of agonising search. Poonam, like many others, was on her way to the Kumbh Mela with her friends.
Sheela, who had been traveling to the Kumbh Mela with her husband and son, did not survive the stampede, though her husband, Umesh, was hospitalised with leg injuries.
The families of the dead and injured were handed over the ex gratia amount, in cash, on Saturday and Sunday. Wads of cash were handed over to the next of kin when the bodies were handed over for last rites. A police personnel was deputed to accompany each family so that they reach their homes with the cash safely.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Anubhav Sahay, who lost his mother Asha Devi, 70, from Buxar in Bihar, said, “After post mortem was completed at Lok Nayak Hospital this morning, when I was handed over my mother’s body, the railway and police officials also gave me Rs 10 lakh in cash. Unhone ne bola yeh muaavaza diya ja raha hai (they said, it is compensation),” said Anubhav. “Paisa koyi maayne nahi rakhta (Money has no meaning)… I am living in Noida and have completed the last rites here.”
Last photo of Poonam along with her grandson at the railway station. Her son-in-law Pappu showed it to The Indian Express on while he sat outside the emergency ward.
A senior official of the Ministry of Railways said ex gratia is an immediate relief, which is why cash was given.
“It is not unusual. Ex gratia was distributed in cash during the Balasore accident also. Ex gratia is given in cash because in such a moment the victims do not usually have bank details at hand. Some victims did not have bank accounts, so the ex gratia was distributed after identifying them by Aadhaar card. The Station Master has the power to order withdrawal of money. The money is disbursed by the commercial department,” said the official.
In a statement, the Ministry of Railways said, “Earlier in the day, Indian Railways gave an ex gratia of Rs 10 lakh to the kin of all the 18 deceased. An amount of Rs 2.5 lakh to grievously injured passengers and a compensation of Rs 1 lakh for passengers with minor injury were distributed to the 15 injured during the day. Further, Indian Railway personnel assisted the families of each deceased by accompanying them to their homes and took part in their final rites.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
At the hospital, doctors scrambled to handle the sudden influx of patients. Medical Director Dr Suresh Kumar, along with senior physicians, rushed between wards, trying to handle the situation. The dead were sent, one by one, to the hospital’s mortuary for autopsy, while the injured were moved to the intensive care unit and later, the orthopedics department, as families anxiously followed stretchers and medical staff.
For Manoj Shah, Saturday brought devastation. The Delhi resident lost his 11-year-old daughter, Suruchi, along with his father-in-law Vijay Shah and mother-in-law Krishna Devi, who were from Bihar’s Samastipur.
Manoj recalled the frantic phone call from his brother-in-law, Mukesh. “Bhagdad ho gayi, log ek dusre pe chad gaye (There has been a stampede and people are trampling over one another),” he was told. Mukesh survived, but sustained serious injuries.
Manoj’s wife was also admitted to the hospital. “She is in no condition to even walk out of the emergency ward,” he said.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
“Log ek dusre par toot pade (People were falling on each other),” recounted Pappu, who was with his wife, Pammi, when the crowd rushed toward the stairs. Pammi’s mother, Poonam, died in the stampede.
Hailing from Sonpur in Bihar, Poonam had come to Delhi to stay with her daughter. When she decided to return, Pappu and Pammi decided to accompany her. Hoping to board the Magadh Express Saturday night, they reached the station but tried to retreat after seeing the crowd. It was too late by then.
“I saw the rush and decided to head back but by that time the crowd had swelled. If the authorities had reached on time, probably she (Poonam) would have been alive today. It took 30-35 Q to get to the ambulance,” Pappu alleged.

headline: Kolkata: As 10 buildings tilt, panel reconstituted to examine unauthorised construction
description: According to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, there are over 30 such buildings within its municipal limits
content:
After at least 10 buildings in and around Kolkata were found tilted in the last one month, the state Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Department has reconstituted the State Level Building Committee (SLBC) with the task of examining “minor unauthorised” construction and give technical opinion on such issues.
The committee will be headed by Additional Secretary of Urban development and Municipal Affairs Department, Arup Ratan Mukhopadhyay. Superintending Engineer, Planning Circle (South), Municipal Engineering Directorate will be the member-convenor of the committee. The other members of the committee will be Chief Engineer (North)/ Chief Engineer (South), Municipal Engineering Directorate as per the jurisdiction of case, Law Officer, Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Department, Chief Town Planner, Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Department.
The other three members are Biplab Kanti Sengupta, former HoD of the Department of Architecture and Regional Planning, IIT Kharagpur; and architects Subir Kumar Basu and Anjan Ukil. “The SLBC shall examine the cases of minor unauthorised erection, or execution of any minor work without sanction under these rules, or minor deviation from the sanctioned plan or execution of any minor erection or work in contravention of any sanctioned plan under the provisions of the West Bengal Municipal (Building) Rules, 2007, as and when the Board of Councillors deem fit to refer such cases and also for reviewing the issue of regularization of such cases to the State Level Building Committee,” a notification issued by the government said.
“The SLBC is also entrusted to give technical opinion on such other issues as may be referred to by the Department. It may invite Commissioner/Executive Officer and the Technical Officials of the concerned Urban Local Bodies in its meetings as and when the committee sits to examine the building plans of the respective Urban Local Body,” it added.

headline: 2021 Jaggadal bomb blast: 2 sentenced to 10 yrs in jail
description: The agency had chargesheeted the accused in December 2021
content:
A special NIA court in Kolkata has sentenced two men to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment for their involvement in the 2021 Jaggadal bomb blast case, an official statement said Sunday.
The court sent Chand alias Arif Akhtar and Rahul Pasi to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment and slapped a fine of Rs 5,000 on each offender, the NIA said in a statement.
The duo, along with one juvenile, had hurled three bombs in quick succession at the gate next to ex-MP Arjun Singh’s office-cum-residence — Majdoor Bhawan — at Jaggadal in North 24 Parganas district on September 8, 2021, the statement said.
While Akhtar and the juvenile were apprehended by the local police, the NIA, which took over the case on September 14, 2021, arrested Pasi later.

headline: Karnataka man hires contract killers to murder younger brother, visits Mahakumbh to divert police attention
description: The elder brother was arrested after he returned to Karnataka from Prayagraj recently.
content:
A Karnataka man who allegedly hired contract killers to murder his younger brother and left for the Mahakumbh Mela in Prayagraj to prevent the police from suspecting him was arrested on Saturday. He was arrested after he returned to the southern state.
On February 11, Krishne Gowda, 45, a farmer was killed in the Maddur taluk of Mandya district. During the probe, it emerged that Shivananje Gowda, elder brother of Krishne Gowda, had hired contract killers for Rs 5 lakh.
A police officer said, “Krishne Gowda had run into huge debts which were cleared by his brother. In return, Krishne Gowda was supposed to transfer his property to his elder brother’s wife. However, Krishne Gowda refused to hand over the property and filed a case in court. Also, he was speaking ill about Shivananje Gowda’s wife.”
“Thereafter, Shivananje Gowda hired contract killers Chandrashekar, Sunil, Ullas, Pratap, Abhishek, Srinivas, and Hanumegowda to kill his brother,” he added.

headline: Jewellery worth Rs 24 crore of former CM Jayalalithaa handed over to Tamil Nadu govt
description: The Tamil Nadu government could either deposit the gold with the Reserve Bank of India or auction it after evaluation.
content:
After two decades, former Tamil Nadu chief minister J Jayalalithaa’s movable assets worth Rs 24 crore including several gold ornaments were handed over by a special court in Bengaluru to the Tamil Nadu government on Saturday.
Following a court order directing the return of Jayalalithaa’s seized assets to the Tamil Nadu government, the transfer process began on Friday. An armed police contingent was assigned to escort six sealed boxes carrying the valuables – more than eight years after the former chief minister passed away. The convoy, led by an SP-ranked officer, included 40 police personnel in six vehicles, with the ‘gold truck’ securely positioned in the middle.
ALSO READ | A year later, the golden saga of Jayalalithaa assets continues
Among the gold ornaments were a gold-coated sword, a crown, a plate, a waist belt, and a figurine resembling Jayalalithaa, along with gold watches, pens, bangles, and earrings. Some pieces were even studded with diamonds. These items, along with silver articles and land documents, were seized from Jayalalithaa’s Poes Garden residence in Chennai and brought to Bengaluru in 2004. This followed the establishment of a special court in Bengaluru to hear the disproportionate assets case against Jayalalithaa and her associates – Sasikala Natarajan, V N Sudhakaran, and J Ilavarasi.
In 2014, Special Judge John Michael D’Cunha convicted all four, sentencing them to four years in prison. Jayalalithaa was fined Rs 100 crore, while the others received fines of Rs 10 crore each.

headline: Don’t make our holy city deport centre, Govt should not defame Punjabis: CM Bhagwant Mann on deported Indians
description: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann targeted the BJP-led Centre and questioned how the saffron party would face the people of Punjab in the 2027 Assembly elections.
content:
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann Saturday continued to attack the Centre over the landing of US aircraft carrying deported Indians at Amritsar airport and asked it not to make the holy city a “deport centre”.
“Will anyone be allowed to land a plane (deportation flight) at Vatican City, if they (deportees) hail from there? Amritsar is a holy city. Do not make our holy city a deport centre. The BJP is intentionally defaming Amritsar by (allowing) such planes to land here,” Mann said.
“The Centre should not defame Punjab or Punjabis or vent out their anger on Punjabis just because they do not make the BJP win elections in the state,” he said.
Talking to reporters at Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport where he had reached to receive the deported Indians, Mann said there are many airbases in the country and the flight could have been diverted to any one of them. He said Amritsar is known for the Golden Temple, Durgiana Mandir, Ram Tirath temple, Jallianwala Bagh, and Gobindgarh Fort and holds a great significance for Punjab and Punjabis.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE
Nita Ambani chooses Ranbir Kapoor over Ranveer Singh and Bill Gates, says, ‘He’s my son Akash’s best friend’. Watch
US deportee files case against Punjab farm union leader Sukhwinder Singh for duping him of Rs 45 lakh
Sagarika Ghatge reveals Zaheer Khan wouldn’t even talk to her, kept his distance till Angad Bedi stepped in: ‘He was told, she’s that kind of girl’
A second US flight carrying 119 illegal Indian immigrants landed in Amritsar Saturday night.
Mann claimed that landing a military aircraft at a civil airport in the border state is wrong and could pose a danger to the country’s security.
Replying to a question about BJP national spokesperson R P Singh’s remarks that Amritsar is the closest international airport for flights entering India from the US, Mann said, “If flights carrying deportees from America cannot land at Delhi because it is farther away from the US than Amritsar, then central government should consider launching direct flights from Amritsar to the US as well as Canada to save on fuel.”
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Earlier, taking a dig at Mann, R P Singh said that Amritsar is the closest international airport for flights entering India from the US. “That’s why the plane carrying illegal immigrants is landing there. Stop politicising the issue and promoting conspiracy theories due to your lack of knowledge,” RP Singh said on X while tagging Mann.
Continuing to attack the Centre, Mann asked how the BJP would face the people of Punjab in the 2027 Assembly elections after “defaming” the holy city of Amritsar. “In every village, they will face these deportees. When (PM Narendra) Modi was hugging (US President Donald) Trump, that very same time the US was sending a plane carrying the immigrants,” he added.
Mann also said his government will provide opportunities to the deported Punjabis. “They are our people… If they can pass a competitive exam for a job, then it can be given.”

headline: Over 1,800 seats in local bodies across Gujarat to go to vote today
description: According to a release from the State Election Commission (SEC), candidates of 213 seats across bodies had been declared uncontested
content:
OVER 1,800 seats across local self-government bodies will witness elections – both regular and bypolls – on Sunday. Besides, Junagadh municipal corporation will see a regular election while Surat, Bhavnagar, and Ahmedabad civic bodies will witness byelections on one seat each.
According to a release from the State Election Commission (SEC), candidates of 213 seats across bodies had been declared uncontested. On February 4, the last day of withdrawing nominations, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) had claimed that it had won 215 seats uncontested, largely because Congress candidates withdrew from the race.
Thus, 1,832 seats will see elections while there will be no by-elections on three taluka panchayat seats — one each in Harij (Patan district) along with Bagasara and Babra in Amreli district after no candidate filed nominations to the first two panchayat seats, and one candidate filed for Babra, which was cancelled by the SEC. In all, 5,084 candidates across parties will be contesting in the elections to be held from 7 am to 6 pm.

headline: Antilia bomb scare case: Special court rejects former cop Pradeep Sharma’s discharge plea
description: The NIA alleged that he was part of the conspiracy to murder Thane resident Hiran, who was linked to the SUV parked outside Antilia, the residence of industrialist Mukesh Ambani on February 25, 2021
content:
A special court designated under the National Investigation Agency (NIA) Act on Saturday rejected the discharge plea of retired ACP Pradeep Sharma booked in the Antilia terror scare and Mansukh Hiran murder case. The court said that at this stage, it cannot accept contention that Sharma was falsely implicated in the case and it will be ascertained during the trial.
Sharma was arrested by NIA in June 2021 and booked for charges, including murder, criminal conspiracy, kidnapping, causing disappearance, and destruction of evidence under relevant sections of the IPC, Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, and the Arms Act.
The NIA alleged that he was part of the conspiracy to murder Thane resident Hiran, who was linked to the SUV parked outside Antilia, the residence of industrialist Mukesh Ambani on February 25, 2021. It was allegedly parked by the main accused and dismissed policeman Sachin Waze.
In January 2023, the Bombay High Court dismissed Sharma’s bail plea and expressed anguish about NIA probe in the case as well as Sharma’s presence in the office of the then Mumbai police commissioner Param Bir Singh in March 2021. It questioned NIA’s probe of conspiracy on parking of the Scorpio vehicle near the Ambani’s residence and planting gelatin sticks in the said vehicle between February 24 and 25, 2021.
Thereafter, Sharma approached the Supreme Court in appeal, which granted him bail in August, 2023.

Sharma, in his discharge application before the special court, argued that there was no case made out to frame charges against him and mere suspicion raised by the investigating agency was not sufficient, therefore, he should be discharged from the case.
However, the prosecution opposed the plea and said that the entire chain of events in the matter and evidence collected by NIA proved Sharma’s role, who had connived with the co-accused. Therefore, the prosecution said witnesses need to be examined in the trial to ascertain if there is a case against the accused and he cannot be discharged from the case.
Special NIA judge AM Patil perused material on record, including call data records between Sharma and Waze, and noted that the entire case of prosecution against Sharma was based on circumstantial evidence and the two were in contact with each other even prior to laying of gelatin sticks. The court said it will have to consider possibilities in the case and total effect of the material produced by prosecution during the trial.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
It said that in the present case, prima facie it is true that the larger conspiracy is hatched by the accused in secrecy, but the prosecution has to independently prove it. The special court, while rejecting the plea, found that at present stage, the witnesses and documentary evidence did not look fabricated and their truthfulness and acceptability can be considered only at the stage of trial.

headline: How a daylight drive-by shooting in Rajkot had police on their toes
description: The police have recovered the spent cartridge of the bullet fired in the incident.
content:
A drive-by shooting by an alleged gang against a member of another in broad daylight in Rajkot had the police department on high alert, leading to several teams being deployed to apprehend the four men involved in the incident that took place in Punitnagar area of the city Saturday.
Rajkot City Commissioner of Police (CP) Brajesh Kumar Jha visited the spot in person and gave instructions to the personnel to curb such criminal activities.
By the end of the day, three of the accused were detained while search continued for the fourth.
According to Zone-2 DCP Jagdish Bangarwa, who termed the case an “attempt to murder”, “Parikshit alias Paresh Balda was standing with his friends in a bylane around 5.30 pm. At that time, a white colour Hyundai Verna with four occupants drove by. One of the occupants of this vehicle fired a shot from a pistol, injuring Balda on his left leg.”

An FIR was filed at Rajkot Taluka police station under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) sections 109(1) (attempt to murder), 3(5) (offence committed by several persons in furtherance of common goal), as well as under Arms Act sections 25(1-B)(a) and 27.
DCP Bangarwa said that three of the four accused had been identified as Sohail Bhana, Sameer aka Mrugo and his brother Nawaz, while the identity of the fourth is under investigation.
The police also recovered the spent cartridge of the bullet fired in the incident. The officials suspect that it was Sameer who had fired the weapon.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
Rajkot City Police deployed four teams, one each from the Rajkot Taluka police station D-staff, the Local Crime Branch (LCB) of Zone-2, the Detection of Crime Branch (DCB), and Special Operations Group (SOG) to identify and apprehend the other three accused involved in the shooting.
DCP Jagdish Bangarwa told The Indian Express, “On January 14, there had been a physical altercation between Balda and Bhana, at the house of two of the latter’s friends. Subsequently, one of them filed a complaint at Malviya Nagar police station against Balda for harassing her and assaulting Bhana. We have primarily learnt that this shooting incident was revenge for the same.”
Notably, both the complainant and the accused have criminal records.
Sameer, who is believed to have carried out the shooting in this case, had earlier been booked under liquor prohibition and anti-gambling laws. He had also been in jail under PASA (Prevention of Anti-Social Activities), said police officials.

Meanwhile, Balda had earlier been booked in 10 cases including serious crimes like attempt to murder, liquor prohibition, assault and abduction.

headline: Foreign currency smuggling racket busted at Bengaluru airport, 2 Sri Lankans apprehended
description: Three passengers including two Sri Lankans and one Indian national were attempting to smuggle foreign currencies worth Rs 2.12 crore at the Kempegowda International Airport.
content:
Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) personnel stationed at Kempegowda International Airport Friday apprehended three passengers attempting to smuggle foreign currencies worth Rs 2.12 crore.
The suspects have been identified as Sri Lankan nationals Vimalraj Thuraisingam and Thileepan Jayanthikumar, along with Indian national Veera Kumar. According to officials, Vishal Kumar from the CISF’s Crime and Intelligence Wing noticed the suspicious behaviour of the three and initiated an investigation.
Upon further probe, a substantial amount of foreign currency, including Euros, US Dollars, Rials, and other denominations, was seized from their possession. Following the seizure, Enforcement Directorate officials took the accused into custody for further investigation.
Authorities are now probing the source of the currency and trying to find out if the accused were part of a larger smuggling network.

headline: Karnataka gets proposals worth Rs 10.27 lakh crore at investors’ meet
description: Announcing the figures at the end of the summit, Karnataka’s Minister for Large and Medium Scale Industries, MB Patil, said that the state is determined to convert at least 70% of these investment commitments into reality over the next two years.
content:
Karnataka received investment proposals worth Rs 10.27 lakh crore during the three-day Invest Karnataka summit, which concluded in Bengaluru on Friday. The ambitious commitments are expected to generate over six lakh jobs, boosting employment opportunities across the state.
Announcing the figures at the end of the summit, Karnataka’s Minister for Large and Medium Scale Industries, MB Patil, said that the state is determined to convert at least 70% of these investment commitments into reality over the next two years. More than 45% of the proposed investments is directed towards North Karnataka, reinforcing the government’s push for regional economic balance.
Breaking down the numbers, Patil said that Rs 4.03 lakh crore of the total investment proposals comprise recognized or publicly announced commitments, while Rs 6.23 lakh crore stems from MoUs signed during the event. Notably, nearly 75% of the proposed investments are outside Bengaluru district, with a strong focus on “Beyond Bengaluru” clusters. The state’s push to expand industrialization beyond the capital city aligns with its vision for decentralized growth and development.

Manufacturing followed with a combined share of 25%, while sunrise sectors, infrastructure, logistics, and startup capital made up the rest. Investment commitments in specific sectors include Rs 1.38 lakh crore for industries such as aerospace, electric vehicles, and R&D, while core manufacturing — covering steel and cement — secured Rs 1.59 lakh crore.

headline: Gujarat CM: Tried to swiftly allay issues faced by startups

The CM made these remarks as the chief guest on Friday while addressing a conference titled ‘Gujarat Start-Ups – Fueling Innovation and Economic Growth’ organised by The Indian Express in Ahmedabad.
Patel said, “As a government we are so much positive that it has been our attempt to ensure… how expeditiously the difficulties faced by you (youths) are allayed. headline: 3 men arrested for stealing cash, jewellery worth lakhs from Vasant Kunj flat
description: Police were informed of the incident when they received a PCR call regarding the burglary.
content:
Three men were arrested on Friday in connection with a burglary at a flat in Southwest Delhi’s Vasant Kunj.
Police said the accused, Virender Kumar (35), Vedpal (36), and Mukesh Kumar Mishra (33), stole cash totaling Rs 10 lakh and high-value gold, diamond, platinum, and silver jewellery worth around Rs 30 lakh from the house on the night of February 9.
Police were informed of the incident when they received a PCR call regarding the burglary. According to police sources, the burglars had managed to find their way into the society from a hole formed by a broken iron grill and partly-crumbled wall towards the back of the society’s compound walls. Police added that the apartment’s owner was on a pilgrimage to Kumbh when he received a call from his neighbour on Monday morning that his house had been burgled.
The complainant, Karan Sachdeva, a relative of the apartment’s owner, reported that the burglary had occurred the previous night. Despite a thorough examination by the crime team, no fingerprints were found at the scene, said police. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under sections 305(a) and 331(4) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

headline: Bombay HC permits woman to terminate 25-week pregnancy at private hospital despite 24-week bar
description: The petitioner had approached the HC stating that she was unable to terminate pregnancy at her chosen private hospital in the city due to the said rules.
content:
The Bombay High Court on Thursday allowed 35-year-old woman to terminate her 25-week pregnancy at a private hospital of her choice. The court granted the relief citing “utmost urgency” despite present Medical Termination of Pregnancy (MTP) Rules provide that private institutions can terminate pregnancies only up to 24 weeks.
The petitioner had approached the HC stating that she was unable to terminate pregnancy at her chosen private hospital in the city due to the said rules.
“Conscious of the right of the Petitioner to reproductive freedom, her autonomy over the body and her right to choice, the medical condition of the Petitioner and having considered the findings and opinion of the Medical Board, we permit the Petitioner to medically terminate the pregnancy,” a bench of Justices Revati Mohite-Dere and Neela K Gokhale noted in the order.
“The Petitioner has indicated her desire that the delivery procedure, etc., has to be done in a hospital of her own choice. We permit her to do the same. However, the Medical institution so chosen by her shall have the requisite approval of Rule 5 of the MTP Rules,” it added.
STORIES YOU MAY LIKE

Snatched my script from Abhishek Bachchan's hand and left his house, recalls Apoorva Lakhia: 'Told him he wasted six months of my life'
Gold medallist female power-lifter dies after 270-kg barbell falls on neck during practice in Bikaner
The petitioner, through advocates Meenaz Kakalia and Shruti Kumar, had approached the HC, after which the medical board of doctors from state-run JJ Hospital examined her case. It recommended termination of pregnancy, stating that the foetus had skeletal dysplasia and other conditions, and the same has high post-natal morbidity. It said the multiple corrective surgeries would be required for severe deformities.
The panel opined that there were potential risks of infertility for the child in future and hypogonadism. The panel also said the petitioner was physically fit for termination of pregnancy.
Kakalia submitted that there was a lacunae in form A to be submitted for approval for termination as same comprises of two categories, including termination of pregnancy up to 12 weeks and that up to 24 weeks.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
She added that there was no third category for termination of pregnancy beyond 24 weeks, therefore, the private hospital was unable to go on with the same, and therefore it requires HC’s approval.
She further argued that the petitioner must be allowed to undergo termination procedure of her choice as per guidance notes issued by the central government.
The private hospital also submitted an affidavit stating that it complied with the required criteria under MTP Rules and has required facilities for the same. It said it has the required approval of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation to conduct termination of pregnancy.
The court allowed the plea and also permitted that petitioner’s chosen medical practitioner to perform the procedure as per guidance notes of central government.
STORY CONTINUES BELOW THIS AD
It left the larger issue related to lacunae in form A under Rule 5 (2) of the MTP open, which will be deliberated upon during the next hearing on March 10.

headline: Maharashtra sailor missing from merchant ship on way to India from Saudi
description: A native of Deur village in Dhule, Yash joined the merchant navy last year.
content:
A 21-year-old sailor from Dhule district in Maharashtra, Yash Avinash Deore, has been missing from a merchant ship sailing from Saudi Arabia to India.
A native of Deur village in Dhule, Yash joined the merchant navy last year. His family said he went on a merchant ship as an “Ordinary Seaman (OS)” through Swaraj Marines Pvt Ltd in Thane in June 2024. But on January 30 this year, Yash’s father got a call from the company that he was missing and a search operation was on.
His father immediately contacted his elder son Nayan Deore, who works at a private company in Pune. “I rushed to Thane to meet the company officials. But I did not get satisfactory information. So I contacted the Directorate General (DG) of Shipping in Mumbai. They asked the company to provide full information about my brother. We have got the ship captain’s report about the rescue operation and other details. But, till today, we have not received any concrete information about Yash,” said Nayan.
Further, on February 2, Nayan also filed an application at the Naupada police station in Thane city seeking help in tracing his brother. It stated that Yash was deployed on “MT Athina I” on the Oman to Alang (India) route. Yash last spoke to his family on January 28. Two days later, the family was told by the company that his was a case of “man overboard (fallen off the ship into the sea)” and that it happened on January 29.

headline: Denied to use sound box at Bhagwat meet for Board exams, RSS moves HC
description: The petitioner claimed that the Sub-Divisional Officer of the area had denied permission citing the ongoing secondary examinations by the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education (WBBSE) being underway.
content:
The West Bengal unit of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) on Thursday approached a single judge bench of Justice Amrita Sinha of the Calcutta High Court alleging that they were denied permission to use sound boxes in a meeting to be addressed by the RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at Talit Burdwan’s Sai Complex on February 16.
The meeting in question is for Karyakartas of the RSS as part of Bhagwat’s 10-day tour in West Bengal.
The petitioner claimed that the Sub-Divisional Officer of the area had denied permission citing the ongoing secondary examinations by the West Bengal Board of Secondary Education (WBBSE) being underway.
However, the petitioner countered that since the event was scheduled for a Sunday, the use of sound boxes would not disrupt any exams.
The matter is expected to be heard on Friday.
